Prepare Your Deployment Against Ransomware Attacks
In a ransomware attack, attackers focus on compromising privileged accounts with weak authentication mechanisms to gain complete access to the cluster and eventually, data.
You can eliminate these risks by preparing your cluster for ransomware attacks. The preparation includes:
l Ensure the Cohesity cluster is upgraded to the latest release and updated with latest patches. You can find the latest version at the Cohesity Downloads portal.
l Change default passwords for each user account such as UI Admin, Support, Intelligent Platform Management Interface (IPMI) admin, and cohesity_console and applying the required password policies. For more information, see Users and Groups and Configure Account Security Settings.
l Maintain separate Active Directory (AD) or SSO protection groups for primary and disaster recovery cluster credentials
l Store privileged credentials securely in credential vaults.
l Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) or multi-factor authentication.
l Disable sudo access for the support user account.
l Ensure users are assigned roles with the least privilege to perform their jobs through role-based access control.
l Enable DataLock on Protection Policies applied to critical data.
l Enable centralized logging and auditing (External Syslog Server).
l Enable offsite backups such as replication or archival in an operationally independent environment.
l Enable firewall policy to restrict network access and manage inbound traffic on Cohesity cluster. Refer to the topic Manage Application-Based Firewall Rules to learn more about firewall rules.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 3: Data Protection Key Concepts

Cohesity Security Features

l Protect your Active Directory. Ransomware attacks often target Active Directories to gain control over identity management systems associated with your cluster. You can refer to Active Directory to learn more about prerequisites, best practices, and recovery workflows.
Detect Anomalies
You can connect your Cohesity cluster to Cohesity Data Cloud and keep track of anomalous snapshots in your cluster. Ransomware detection in Helios is based on machine learning and statistical anomaly detection techniques to identify sudden changes in the data across snapshots over time. When these changes are detected, it might be indicative of ransomware compromising the data. Cohesity Data Cloud constantly monitors the metrics, such as how many modified snapshots, and detects any anomalies. In addition, it uses machine learning algorithms to monitor change rates in the backup data continuously. Cohesity's ransomware detection techniques can analyze changes in: 1. The volume of data read or written over time - noticing whether the volume of data protected from one protection job run to the next changed dramatically. 2. Analyzing changes in data entropy - very good for detecting when the contents of files may have changed dramatically due to encryption or compression 3. Changes in the nature of the file system - identifying when a large number of files has been added, deleted, or modified If the rate is out of the normal range -- based on daily and historical rates -- Cohesity flags it as a potential ransomware attack. Refer to Detect Ransomware Attacks to learn more about how Cohesity Data Cloud detects anomalies.
Respond to Ransomware Attacks
In response to ransomware attacks, it's important to immediately take the required measures and limit the potential damage to your organization's digital assets. You can integrate Helios Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) platforms to receive alerts when ransomware has attacked your cluster. You can refer to the View the Alert section in the Anti-ransomware topic to learn about how to check the alerts in your cluster. As a first step to limit the exposure of your cluster to the ransomware attack, you should:
1. Reset Passwords. For more information, see Users and Groups.
Note: For 6.6.0d and earlier, and 6.5.1 releases, you have to change the password of Linux users.
2. Disable accounts that are not configured with multi-factor authentication. 3. Inform your Technical Account Manager and the Cohesity account team.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 3: Data Protection Key Concepts

Cohesity Security Features

4. Enable Legal Hold for critical workloads. It ensures that snapshots of protection groups will not be deleted until the Legal Hold is removed or disabled. For more information, see Add or Remove a Legal Hold to a Snapshot.
5. Stop the cluster through a CLI command cluster stop.
After limiting exposure to the ransomware, you have to start recovery from a clean snapshot, recover active directory objects, and initiate mass restoration of your critical workloads such as VMware virtual machines and network-attached storage backups. For more information, see the Cohesity white paper: Cohesity Ransomware Protection -- Prepare and Recover.
Key Management
A Key Management Service (KMS) helps you manage the keys that encrypt data and secures it from unauthorized access. A Cohesity cluster has a built-in key manager or can be configured to use external key managers - KMIP-compliant or Amazon Web Services (AWS) KMS - to manage encryption keys. Cohesity uses two types of keys for encryption.
l Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) - these keys are used to encrypt the data. l Key Encryption Keys (KEKs) - these keys are used to encrypt the DEKs.
Data on the Cohesity cluster is encrypted using a FIPS-validated implementation of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) in Galois/Counter Mode using a 256-bit DEK. A unique DEK is created for the following entities in your Cohesity cluster.
l Encryption-enabled Storage Domains l External targets, such as
l CloudArchive l CloudArchive Direct
Regardless of the entity type, DEKs are encrypted using a KEK and persisted on the cluster in an encrypted format as Encrypted DEKs (EDEKs). DEKs are never stored or exposed in a plain text format. If the external targets are CloudArchive and CloudArchive Direct, then the EDEKs are also stored alongside the data in the cloud. The encryption and decryption process is performed within the Cohesity cluster and is transparent to all inbound or outbound protocols and applications such as backup, archiving, and file services.
Security Measures
Cohesity prioritizes security and access control to ensure that customer data remains protected at all times. A key concern is whether Cohesity administrators can access customer Key Management Systems (KMS) or encryption keys, potentially exposing

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 3: Data Protection Key Concepts

Cohesity Security Features

protected data. These Security measures clarify why such access is not a risk within the Cohesity Cloud Services (CCS) Backup-as-a-Service (BaaS) solution.
l Restricted Production Environment Access: Cohesity enforces strict access controls, access to the production environment is limited to authorized personnel.
l Encryption and Decryption Controls: Cohesity does not provide any mechanism to decrypt customer data outside of normal product operations. Encryption and decryption occur within the secure system framework, adhering to strict security protocols.
l Key Management and Secure Storage: Key Encryption Keys (KEKs) are securely stored in a Key Management System (KMS), purpose-built for secure key storage and management. This ensures that keys are not exposed or accessible beyond their intended use.
l Customer-Controlled Key Management: Customers can configure an external KMS, ensuring full control over their encryption keys. In this case, Cohesity does not retain direct access to KEKs but only invokes them to decrypt Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) when required for standard operations.
l Risk Mitigation: In the unlikely event of a security breach, Customers utilizing an external KMS can revoke Cohesity's access to the KEK, preventing further decryption operations.
Internal Key Management Service
Cohesity provides an internal key management service (KMS) to generate Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) and Key Encryption Keys (KEKs) on your Cohesity cluster.
l Cohesity stores data in Storage Domains.
l For each Storage Domain, the internal KMS generates a new KEK and DEK.
l At the end of this window, if additional data needs to be written to the Storage Domain, a new DEK is created.
When a new Storage Domain is added to the cluster, the internal KMS creates a new DEK and encrypts it with a KEK. Cohesity securely stores this DEK internally within the cluster's key store as an Encrypted DEK (EDEK).
To keep the encryption keys safe, Cohesity restricts the following actions:
l Exporting keys from your cluster
l Exposing keys in plain text format through any API or user interface
Key Rotation Policy
By default, the KEK rotation interval is 90 days, and you can configure this interval as needed. For more information, see Set Key Rotation Policy.
DEKs are created and managed as described in Internal Key Management Service.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 3: Data Protection Key Concepts

Cohesity Security Features

External Key Management Service
Cohesity supports Amazon Web Services-based KMS and Key Management Interoperability Protocol (KMIP) compliant KMS as external key management services. KMIP is used to facilitate communication between the Cohesity cluster and the key server of the external KMS. You can register multiple key management services. When the Cohesity cluster is configured to use an external KMS, KEKs are generated and stored in the external KMS, though a KEK ID, a reference to the KEK, is maintained on the cluster. The cluster never persists a copy of the KEK, though the Cohesity cluster will persist the KEK ID as an identifier to fetch the KEK from the external KMS periodically.
Note: The KEK ID does not contain any key material.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 3: Data Protection Key Concepts

Cohesity Security Features

KMIP-based External KMS
When a KMIP-based external KMS is enabled, the Cohesity cluster will store both the EDEK and KEK ID locally. The external KMS will manage the KEK. A Cohesity cluster interacts with an external KMS when a service on the cluster requests access to the encrypted data. After receiving this request, the Cohesity cluster sends a request to the external KMS for the KEK referenced using the KEK ID. When the external KMS responds with KEK, the Cohesity cluster uses it to decrypt the EDEK and derive the DEK. This DEK is sent to the service that requires the key to decrypt or encrypt the data for any read or write operations. Cohesity allows caching of keys and it is implemented within various cluster services to ensure cluster throughput and minimize load on the external KMS. This allows the DEK to be cached in-memory on the cluster node for four hours before a call to external KMS must be made again to fetch the KEK and decrypt the EDEK.
Note: If the external KMS is unavailable or unable to deliver the KEKs due to any reason, the data in the Storage Domains remains in an encrypted state and inaccessible.
By default, the key rotation interval is 90 days, though this is configurable.
Create a KMS Cluster
You can add multiple KMS and create a KMS cluster to ensure high availability of keys. A KMS cluster can include up to four key management services. In a KMS cluster, every KMS node should share the same CA certificate and each Cohesity cluster node's certificate is shared internally. This means the additional KMS that is added must be connected to the same Cohesity cluster. Follow the steps below to add a new KMS.

AWS KMS
When a AWS KMS is enabled, the Cohesity cluster will store the KEK ID locally while the EDEK will be stored both on the cluster as well as alongside the data (in the case of CloudArchive and CloudArchive Direct). A Cohesity cluster interacts with AWS KMS when a service on the cluster requests access to the encrypted data. After receiving this request, the Cohesity cluster will send a request to the AWS KMS for the Customer Managed Key (CMK). When you're using AWS KMS, the CMK acts as the KEK. When AWS KMS responds with the CMK, the Cohesity cluster uses it to decrypt EDEK and derive the DEK. This DEK is sent to the service that requires the key to decrypt or encrypt the data for any read or write operations. If you are using AWS KMS as an external KMS, then
l DEKs are rotated every four hours l KEKs, which is an AWS CMK, is rotated once every year by AWS
Caching of keys is implemented within various cluster services to ensure cluster throughput and minimize load on the external KMS. This allows the DEK to be cached in-memory on the cluster node for a limited period of time before a call to AWS KMS must be made again to fetch the KEK and decrypt the EDEK.
Note: You can configure a HTTPS proxy on the Cohesity cluster and use it for communication with AWS KMS. This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.

1. Customer Managed Key ARN: You can choose to have an Amazon CMK ID or Amazon Resource Name (ARN). You should not enter key aliases in this field.
2. Access Key ID: Amazon access key ID. 3. Secret Access Key: AWS secret access key.
7. Enable or disable SSL verification of the connection to the AWS KMS server. By default, SSL verification is enabled.

You have configured AWS KMS as your cluster's external key management service.
Azure KMS
When Azure KMS is enabled, the Cohesity cluster stores the Key Encryption Key (KEK) ID locally. The Encrypted DEK (EDEK) is stored both on the cluster and alongside the data (for services like CloudArchive and CloudArchive Direct). The Cohesity cluster interacts with Azure KMS when a service requests access to encrypted data. Upon receiving the request, the cluster uses the Azure C++ SDK to authenticate via Managed Identity and fetch the private key from Azure Key Vault. This private key acts as the KEK. The cluster then uses it to decrypt the EDEK and derive the DEK. The DEK is passed to the requesting service to perform encryption or decryption operations. If you are using Azure KMS as an external KMS:
l DEKs are generated locally on the cluster and rotated periodically (similar to internal KMS behavior).
l KEKs (RSA-HSM keys in Azure Key Vault) are rotated every 365 days for Cohesitymanaged keys.
l Key caching is implemented across cluster services to optimize performance and reduce load on Azure KMS. DEKs are cached in memory for a limited time before the cluster re-authenticates and re-fetches the KEK to decrypt the EDEK.
You can now configure an HTTP or HTTPS proxy for both new and existing Azure KMS configurations on a Cohesity cluster. This allows Azure KMS operations to run through the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 3: Data Protection Key Concepts

Cohesity Security Features

web proxy already set up on the cluster. Contact Cohesity Support to configure proxy for Azure KMS.
Manage Key Management Service
After you have configured a key management service (KMS) for your Cohesity cluster, you can do the following to manage KMS.
l Restart the Cohesity Keychain Service: The keychain service creates and manages encryption keys in a Cohesity cluster. Restarting it is required after you have updated the KMS configuration.
l Set Key Rotation Policy: You can set the lifetime of encryption keys on the Cohesity cluster. By default, it is set to 90 days.
l Delete an External Key Management System: You can delete an external KMS that is configured to manage encryption keys on the Cohesity cluster.
l Add a Secondary External KMS: If you're using an external key management system, then you can add more than one KMS to your Cohesity cluster to ensure high availability of keys.
Restart the Cohesity Keychain Service
If you update the KMS configuration on the Cohesity cluster, you must restart the Cohesity keychain service on the Cohesity cluster for the configuration changes to take effect. If you configure KMS for the first time, you do not need to restart the keychain service. To restart the keychain service on the Cohesity cluster:
1. Start the Cohesity CLI remotely or locally as described in the Cohesity CLI Reference Guide.
2. Specify the static IPv4 or IPv6 address of one of the Cohesity nodes. For example, if the CLI was downloaded to a Linux system, you might use the following command.
3. Provide a Cohesity cluster username and password.
./iris_cli -server 172.16.3.101 -username=admin
4. Run the following command to restart the Cohesity keychain service:
cluster restart service-names="keychain"
Example: admin> cluster restart service-names="keychain"
Success: Restarting the cluster services [keychain] ...
Set Key Rotation Policy
After the Cohesity cluster is created, the key rotation policy, by default, is set to 90 days. This means that the Cohesity cluster uses new encryption keys every 90 days. After the time period has been reached, all the old encryption keys used by the Cohesity cluster are

Chapter 3: Data Protection Key Concepts

Cohesity Security Features

replaced by a new set of keys and the data on the Cohesity cluster remains as it was originally encrypted. You can change the period of time that new keys are generated by the Cohesity cluster using the CLI command listed below. Specify the time period in seconds. To change the default key rotation period:
1. Start the Cohesity CLI remotely or locally as described in the Cohesity CLI Reference Guide. Specify the static IPv4 or IPv6 address of one of the Cohesity nodes. For example, if the CLI was downloaded to a Linux system, you might use the following command. Provide a Cohesity cluster username and password. ./iris_cli -server 172.16.3.101 -username=admin
2. Change the Key Rotation period. Specify the time period in seconds. For example to change the key rotation period to 30 days, enter the following CLI command: admin>cluster edit enc-key-rotation-period-secs=2592000

MegaFile
Storage of large volumes of data such as large file systems can be challenging because they are often stored in a single storage container, delaying backup and recovery. The MegaFile feature alleviates this delay by dividing large files into smaller parts and distributing the smaller parts across multiple nodes of a Cohesity cluster, allowing parallel and hence faster backup and recovery.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 3: Data Protection Key Concepts

MegaFile

The following example helps to understand the impact of MegaFile. In a four-node cluster, the data ingest of a 2 TB VMDK is split into four parts, each of which is 512 GB, reducing the ingest time by a factor of four. In an eight-node cluster, the data ingest of a 2 TB VMDK is split into eight parts, each of which is 256 GB, reducing the ingest time by a factor of eight. As the number of nodes in a Cohesity Cluster grows, the time to ingest decreases significantly.

.
Note: The size of the smaller parts is determined by MegaFile and varies depending on many factors such as the size of the larger file, the number of nodes in the Cohesity cluster, and so on.

Note: The MegaFile feature is built in a Cohesity Cluster and is enabled by default.

Example using MegaFile
In the example below, two sub-tasks are created by MegaFile and it splits the VMDK to a sub-task for every 256 GB offset:

<date, time> Requesting permit for sub-task 0

<date, time> Requesting permit for sub-task 1

Data Retention for Audits
In planning for audits, keep in mind that the Cohesity cluster retains metadata for Protection Groups and Objects (VMs, physical servers, databases, etc.) differently, as described below.
Data Retention for Backup
Backup auditors need to verify that your organization's assets are backed up at regular intervals and that backups are available for recovery. For example, you might be asked to show evidence of successful backups for the past three months or more.
Protection Group Metadata
Protection Group metadata requires minimal overhead in the Cluster and is retained forever for reporting and compliance purposes, unless the Protection Group is deleted. There is no set retention period for this information. The information includes:
l the Protection Group name l the protection run start and end date and time l the names of the backed up Objects l the total number of bytes read and written l whether the protection run succeeded or failed

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 3: Data Protection Key Concepts

Data Retention for Audits

Note that the protection run is considered successful only if all its Objects are backed up successfully. For example, if a Protection Group is configured to back up 100 VMs, but one of the VMs gets deleted in vCenter, the protection run status indicates failure. The more VMs included in a Protection Group, the greater the probability of the protection run reporting a failure. As a result, it may be desirable to capture more granular success/failure metadata at the Object level.
Object Metadata
Object metadata is not retained forever in the Cluster. A single protection run can back up hundreds or thousands of Objects and the metadata can grow quickly and require overhead. Therefore the Object metadata is retained only for the retention period specified in the Protection Group's Policy. After that period, the Object metadata is permanently deleted from the Cluster and is no longer available. You can guard against gaps in the Object backup history by collecting the Object information on a regular basis and storing it outside the Cluster.
Getting Audit Data
You can get Protection Group and Object information by running the following reports in the Cohesity cluster:
l Backup Summary report l Protection Details Per Object report l Protection Summary by Object Type report l Failed Objects report
You can customize the reports with filters including a date range, Protection Group names and object names. You can run the reports as needed, on a recurring schedule, download them as CSV files or email them to backup administrators to review and keep for auditors.
Data Retention for Recovery
Recovery metadata requires minimal overhead in the cluster and is retained forever for reporting and compliance purposes. There is no set retention period for this information.
Recovery Metadata Retention
The following information is retained:
l Recovery Task l Start Time l Status l Duration
Object Metadata Retention
The following information is retained:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 3: Data Protection Key Concepts

Data Retention for Audits

l Object name l Recovered From l Recovery Point l Options For recovery tasks performed in the last month, the following information is retained: l Object name l Recovered From l Recovery Point l Recovery Task l Start Time l Duration l Options Getting Audit Data You can get recovery task and object information for VMs by running the Clone and Recover VM Tasks Summary report in the Cohesity cluster.
Data Retention for Clone
Clone metadata requires minimal overhead in the cluster and is retained forever for reporting and compliance purposes, unless the clone is deleted. There is no set retention period for this information. Clone Metadata Retention The following information is retained:
l Task Name l Objects Cloned l Start Time l Task Duration l Status Object Metadata Retention The following information is retained: l Clone Options l Object l Snapshot Cloned

Dynamic Disk Support
This topic describes what dynamic disks are and captures details of the supported and unsupported workflows of the Dynamic Disk use case in ESXi VMs.
What are Dynamic Disks?
Dynamic disks provide features such as the ability to create volumes that span multiple disks (spanned and striped volumes) and the ability to create fault-tolerant volumes (mirrored and RAID-5 volumes). Like basic disks, dynamic disks can use the MBR or GPT partition styles on systems that support both styles. All volumes on dynamic disks are known as dynamic volumes. Dynamic disks offer greater flexibility for volume management because they use a database to track information about dynamic volumes on the disk and about other dynamic disks in the computer. Because each dynamic disk in a computer stores a replica of the dynamic disk database, for example, a corrupted dynamic disk database can repair one dynamic disk by using the database on another dynamic disk. The location of the database is determined by the partition style of the disk. On MBR partitions, the database is contained in the last 1 megabyte (MB) of the disk. On GPT partitions, the database is contained in a 1-MB reserved (hidden) partition. Dynamic disks are a separate form of volume management that allows volumes to have non-contiguous extents on one or more physical disks. Dynamic disks and volumes rely on the Logical Disk Manager (LDM) and Virtual Disk Service (VDS) and their associated features. These features enable you to perform tasks such as converting basic disks into dynamic disks and creating fault-tolerant volumes. To encourage the use of dynamic disks,

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 3: Data Protection Key Concepts

Dynamic Disk Support

multi-partition volume support was removed from basic disks and is now exclusively supported on dynamic disks. The following operations can be performed on dynamic disks:
l Create and delete simple, spanned, striped, mirrored, and RAID-5 volumes. l Extend a simple or spanned volume. l Remove a mirror from a mirrored volume or break the mirrored volume into two
volumes. l Repair mirrored or RAID-5 volumes. l Reactivate a missing or offline disk.

Are Dynamic Disks Recommended?
Cohesity supports dynamic disks while recommending against them as they complicate the disaster recovery process. Cohesity also advises against using dynamic disks as a system disk.
Physical Windows workflows back up at the volume level and create one VHD / VHDX file with one volume. Thus, there is no issue with supporting dynamic disks if the VM is treated as a physical server.

Limitations
l Recovery to an alternate location is supported with the following restrictions: l The volume should be a simple volume. Dynamic disks may be created unintentionally after some P2V workflows.
l The alternate machine should ideally not have any other dynamic disks. If there are any other disks already, then manual intervention is required to clean up the missing dynamic disks that result from the disks attached during restores.
l Quiesced VM snapshots fail with missing dynamic disks. Thus, if the alternate machine has dynamic disks and is part of a job that takes quiesced snapshots of the VM, then the cleanup becomes mandatory.
l Indexing (and hence search and download) will work for Simple, Spanned, Striped and Mirrored volumes. It will not work for RAID-5 volumes. So, File Level Recoveries are not supported for RAID-5 volumes.
l Instant Volume mounts on Hyper-V are not supported for Dynamic Disks.
l VM with SQL DB will have the same behaviors as above.

Throttling Background System Activities
The activities, such as garbage collection, system checks, post-process storage optimization, and other system activities, run in the background on the Cohesity cluster. These system activities utilize the Cohesity cluster resources and impact the workloads, such as file shares and backups.
Schedule the throttling of the system activities to reduce the utilization of the Cohesity cluster resources.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Configure Settings

Settings

Description

Background System Activity

Enable this option to schedule the throttling of the system activities running in the background. Time Zone Settings To change the time zone for throttling schedules, click Change Time Zone and select a time zone from the drop-down menu. By default, your current time zone is displayed. Add Throttling Schedules

Important: Cohesity recommends that you schedule the throttling in such a way that, on average, the background system activities utilize at least 50% of Cohesity resources in a week.

To add schedules:
1. In the Days column, select one or more weekdays from the drop-down menu. You can also select Everyday to schedule throttling to run daily.
2. In the Time column, enter the time duration for throttling.
3. In the Activity Level column, select a level of throttling from the drop-down menu.
l No restriction: The background system activities will run without any restriction.
l Moderate: The background activities will utilize 66% of the Cohesity resources. This is the default option.
l Low: The background activities will utilize 33% of the Cohesity resources. l No activity: Other than critical processes, all other background system
activities will be completely stopped. The background activities will not utilize any of the Cohesity resources. 4. Click Add.
5. Optional. To configure multiple schedules for throttling the background system activities, repeat steps a to d.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Configure Settings

Settings

Description

Note:
l

If there is an overlap between the schedules added, then the latest added schedule will take precedence over other schedules. For example, you have added a schedule (say S1) for running the background activities on every Monday between 9.00 am to 5.00 pm with Activity Level set to Low. Later, you added another schedule (say S2) for running the background activities every day between 1.00 am to 3.00 pm with Activity Level set to Moderate. In this scenario, on Monday from 1.00 am to 3.00 pm, there is an overlap between these two schedules. In such cases, the recently added schedule, S2, will take precedence during the overlap time.

l Cohesity will perform throttling of the system activities running in the background only for the days and duration for which you have configured the throttling.

Saving the Cohesity cluster configuration with this option disabled will clear all the existing throttling schedules. When you save the Cohesity cluster configuration, the following error message appears if the Cohesity resources utilization by the background system activities is less than 50%:
Error occurred while configuring background activity schedule. Background activity has been excessively throttled. Please relax the throttling conditions.
Delete an Existing Throttling Schedule To delete a throttling schedule, click the delete icon against the schedule.

3. Click Save.

Manage the Support Channel
The Cohesity Support Channel is a secure, simple, and effective way for Cohesity employees to provide on-demand assistance to customers. When the channel is enabled, a qualified Cohesity employee can log in to the Cohesity cluster to troubleshoot issues in a remote session. The following diagram illustrates how the Support Channel works.
The Support Channel server is located in the public cloud and has a secure login mechanism. The server is configured with a public key and accepts connections from the Cohesity cluster. The Cohesity cluster selects a master Node, which then establishes an SSH reverse tunnel with the Support Channel server on a TCP port. (For information on ports,

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Configure Settings

see Firewall Ports for Support Channel.) This setup ensures that all communication is encrypted between the Support Team and the Cohesity cluster. The server configuration is limited to only certain Cohesity employees, and there are strict rules for user registration that are checked regularly. Only a limited set of Cohesity employees can configure the Support Channel server, and a strict user registration policy is enforced and audited regularly.
Firewall Ports for Support Channel
The primary node in the Cohesity cluster initiates an SSH reverse tunnel with the Support Channel server on TCP port 443. To use the Support Channel server server, you need to configure the ports listed in the Cohesity Support Channel section in the Manage Firewall Ports topic before you enable the Support Channel server.
Note: Make sure your network team has unblocked and is not monitoring the Cohesity support channel sites or ports for seamless connectivity and effective communication.
Enable Support Channels
Cohesity recommends that you enable the Support Channel when you need assistance from Cohesity employees. You can enable the Support Channel using the Cohesity Dashboard or the Cohesity CLI. When you enable the Support Channel, you must specify how long you want the Support Channel enabled. When the period you specified expires, the Support Channel turns off. You can also manually disable the Support Channel before the specified period expires.
Note: Support Channels are disabled by default in Cohesity clusters.
Enable or Disable the Support Channel To enable or disable the Support Channel:
1. Navigate to Settings > Summary.
2. Next to the Support Channel at the bottom of the page, click the edit icon ( ). 3. Select one of the following from the list:
l Off--Disables the channel. l Temporarily On--Lets you enable the channel temporarily. Enter a number (1
to 30) and then select hours or days from the drop-down. If the support channel is in use and about to expire within 7 days, the support channel duration will be automatically extended for the next 7 days.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Configure Settings

Note: You can toggle off the automatic extension if it is not required.
4. Click Save.
You can also manage the Support Channel with the Cohesity CLI. See the iris_cli support support-channel command.
Support Channel Tokens
Once the Support Channel is enabled, a Support Channel token is autogenerated. Cohesity employees require the Support Channel token to remotely log in to your Cohesity cluster using SSH. Copy the Support Channel Token and share it with the Cohesity employee. Support Channel tokens provide a more secure and hassle-free method than sharing the password with Cohesity employees. Support Channel tokens are encrypted and are longer than the tokens in the previous Cohesity versions. Because encryption appends a random number, an encrypted token may appear different every time it is fetched. However, the token is still valid until the Support Channel expires or is disabled. Support Channel tokens expire when the set time duration for the Support Channel expires, as a security enhancement. A new token is generated when you re-enable the Support Channel. Cohesity employees logging into Cohesity clusters require the new Support Channel token every time the Support Channel is enabled.
Note: If you extend the Support Channel duration before it expires, the existing Support Channel token is retained. However, if you manually disable the Support Channel before its session expires, the Support Channel token also expires.

Copy the Support Channel Token
To copy the Support Channel token: 1. Navigate to Settings > Summary. 2. From the Support Channel token field, copy the Support Channel token using the copy icon.
Or, from the Cohesity CLI, run the following iris_cli command to copy the Support Channel token: iris_cli user linux-bash-access
The following is a sample output of the command: admin@127.0.0.1> user linux-bash-access

supportUserToken

Support UI User
When you enable a Support Channel, a Support UI user role (cohesity_ui_support_ <clusterid>) is created by default and displayed along with the other user roles under the Users & Groups tab on the Access Management page. Cohesity employees remotely logging into the Cohesity cluster use this user role. By default, this user role will have viewer permissions and a secure password. The user role is automatically disabled and deleted if the Support Channel expires or if the Support Channel is manually disabled.

Migrate from Internal KMS to External KMS
This section describes the procedure to migrate the storage domain or metadata encryption from Internal KMS to External KMS.

Note: Once you migrate from Internal KMS to External KMS, the change is irreversible. Migration from External back to Internal KMS is not supported.

Migrate Storage Domain Encryption from Internal KMS to External KMS If encryption is already enabled and the storage domain uses Internal KMS, you can migrate from Internal KMS to AWS KMS or any KMIP-compliant KMS. To migrate the storage domain encryption from Internal KMS, complete the following steps:
1. Go to Settings > Summary. 2. Click the Storage Domains tab.

3. In the Storage Domains page, hover over the storage domain, click Edit.

and select

4. In the Encryption section, from the Key Management Service Type drop-down list, select AWS or KMIP Compliant.

5. Click Update Storage Domain.

Migrate Metadata Encryption from Internal KMS to External KMS

If you enable encryption when creating a Cohesity cluster, by default, Cohesity uses Internal KMS for cluster-level encryption. After the Cohesity cluster is created, you can migrate from Internal KMS to AWS KMS or any KMIP-compliant KMS.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Configure Settings

Note: If encryption was not enabled when you created the Cohesity cluster, the Encryption option does not appear.
To migrate metadata encryption from Internal KMS, complete the following steps: 1. Go to Settings > Summary. 2. Click Configure. 3. In the Encryption drop-down list, select AWS or KMIP Compliant. 4. Click Save.
Set Key Rotation Policy for Encryption
After the Cohesity cluster is created, the key rotation policy, by default, is set 90 days. This means that the Cohesity cluster automatically creates and uses new encryption keys every 90 days. After the time period has been reached, all the old encryption keys used by the Cohesity cluster are replaced by a new set of keys and the data on the Cohesity cluster remains as it was originally encrypted. You can change the period of time that new keys are generated by the Cohesity cluster using the CLI command listed below. Specify the time period in seconds. To change the default key rotation period:
1. Start the Cohesity CLI remotely or locally as described in the Cohesity CLI Reference Guide. Specify the static IPv4 or IPv6 address of one of the Cohesity nodes. For example, if the CLI was downloaded to a Linux system, you might use the following command. Provide a Cohesity cluster username and password.
./iris_cli -server 172.16.3.101 -username=admin
2. Change the Key Rotation period. Specify the time period in seconds. For example to change the key rotation period to 30 days, enter the following CLI command:
admin>cluster edit enc-key-rotation-period-secs=2592000
Update SSL Certificates Using Cohesity CA or Customer CA certificate for Agent to Cluster Communication
Cohesity software packages ship with an auto-generated self-signed certificate. You must accept the self-signed certificate to access the Cohesity clusters. This topic describes the following ways to update or manage the cluster certificate from the Cohesity cluster (User Interface):

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Configure Settings

l Load a Certificate Authority (CA) signed certificate.
l Refresh the factory shipped (Cohesity signed) certificate if it expires.
l Configure CA integration with Venafi.
Important Notes on SSL Certificates
l Cohesity does not recommend using self-signed certificates.
l Cohesity cluster supports X.509 certificates in PEM format only.
l The certificate must have the "Common Name" field set to the server's hostname (for example, a VIP's DNS name). The Common Name must be the same as the name you plan to use to access the Cohesity cluster.
l Private Key Files must not be encrypted.
l If the certificate admin provides a single file, ensure to separate the file to obtain the certificate and key files.
l By default, OCSP validation is disabled. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
l Cohesity does not support ECDSA certificates.

Configuring Cohesity Cluster with a CA Signed Certificate
A Certificate Authority (CA) signed certificate is a digital certificate issued by a trusted organization called Certificate Authority. It authenticates the identity of the entity (certificate holder) before digitally signing the certificate, thereby assuring users that they are interacting with a legitimate and secure entity.
You can replace the Cohesity cluster's self-signed certificate with a Certificate Authority (CA) signed certificate. Optionally you can use the Subject Alternative Name (SAN) field to specify additional host names (such as sites, IP addresses, and common names) to be protected by a single SSL certificate, such as a Multi-Domain or Extend Validation MultiDomain Certificate.
This procedure applies to configuring the Cohesity cluster using SHA256 and SHA384 cryptographic hash algorithms. When configuring, update the default_md parameter in step 3 accordingly. To configure a Cohesity cluster with a CA certificate using SHA256 or SHA384:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Configure Settings

1. Copy the following template to a text editor, replace the sample values in red color with actual values, and save the file in your local directory. Sample

#REQ FILE: cert_req.conf

#---------------------------

[ req ]

default_bits = 2048

default_md

= sha384 (or sha256)

prompt

= no

encrypt_key

= no

distinguished_name = req_distinguished_name

req_extensions

= req_ext

[ req_distinguished_name ]

countryName

= "US"

stateOrProvinceName = "CA"

localityName

= "San Jose"

organizationName = "Data Protection"

organizationalUnitName = "example Organization Name"

commonName

= "cluster1.example-domain.com"

[ req_ext ] subjectAltName = @alt_names

[alt_names] DNS.1 = cluster1.example-domain.com DNS.2 = cluster1-vip.example-domain.com IP.1 = 10.1.1.1 IP.2 = 10.1.1.3 IP.3 = 10.1.1.5 #---------------------------
2. Run the following command to the SCP file saved in the local directory to support user:
scp "/path_to_file/filename" user@ip_address:"/Path to destination/"
Example
scp cert_req.conf support@111.1.1.1:/var/tmp/
3. Get the IP address for any Cohesity Cluster node (You can get the list of IP addresses by selecting Settings > Summary and then opening the Nodes tab). Use the IP

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Configure Settings

address to log in to that node using a support user account that has the admin role. Command ssh support@<node IP address> Example ssh support@111.1.1.1 When prompted, enter the password of the support user account. [support@111.1.1.1's password: Once your password is successfully authenticated, the prompt changes to the Secure Shell prompt. [support@restricted-8888222f444 ~]\> 4. Generate the private key and certificate signing request files using cert_req.conf file: openssl req -out cert_req.csr -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout cert_ key.key -config <path to file>/cert_req.conf Example openssl req -out cert_req.csr -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout cert_ key.key -config /var/tmp/cert_req.conf
Note: Private key must not be encrypted.
5. Convert the cert_key.key to a PEM private key using the following command: openssl rsa -in cert_key.key -out /var/tmp/key.pem
6. Configure Certificate Authority Integration with Venafi
In addition to using the Cohesity CA or manually uploading CA-signed certificates, you can configure the cluster to obtain certificates from an external Certificate Authority using Venafi Trust Protection Platform (TPP).
With this integration, the cluster retrieves certificates from Venafi based on your organization's policy and automatically distributes them to all registered Cohesity Agents. This removes the need to manually install Cohesity Agent certificates.
Prerequisites
Before integrating with Venafi, ensure that:
l The Venafi Trust Protection Platform (TPP) server is deployed and reachable from all cluster nodes, with network connectivity, DNS resolution, and firewall access configured.
l A policy directory (Policy DN) exists in Venafi TPP. The policy must define certificate attributes, be associated with a certificate authority template, and you must have the Policy DN value.
l An OAuth application (Client ID) is configured in Venafi TPP with the required scope to request and retrieve certificates. You must also have a service account username and password with access to the application and policy.
l The certificate values you provide follow the rules defined in the Venafi policy.
l No other external CA is already configured on the cluster. If one is already configured, remove or update the existing configuration before proceeding. Contact Cohesity Support to remove an existing CA configuration.
l You have administrative access to run certificate management commands using the CLI on the cluster.
l You have the following details from your Venafi setup. These values are required when running the configuration command.

Parameter ca-type
ca-url

Description
Type of customer managed CA provider. Set this value to VENAFI.
Base URL of the customer managed CA provider API endpoint.

Required
Yes
Yes

Disable AES-128 Ciphers Using the CLI
You can disable AES-128 cipher suites on the cluster's web services and S3-compatible object store endpoints. Disable AES-128 Ciphers on Port 443 Perform the following steps to disable AES-128 Ciphers on Port 443:
1. Open the Cohesity CLI. 2. To view the ciphers currently enabled on the cluster, run the following command:
iris_cli -username=<username> -password=<password> -skip_password_ prompt=true cipher list The command output displays the list of ENABLED CIPHERS and DISABLED CIPHERS. 3. Run the following command to disable the AES-128 ciphers on port 443: cipher update enable=false ciphers=<AES_128 cipher1>,<AES_128 cipher2> 4. Restart the Iris service to apply the change: cluster restart-services service-names=iris 5. After the service restarts, run cipher list once again to confirm that AES-128 cipher suites are disabled. Disable AES-128 Ciphers on Ports 3000 and 3001 Perform the following steps to disable AES-128 and other legacy Ciphers on ports 3000 and 3001:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Configure Settings

1. Open the Cohesity CLI. 2. Run the following command to disable the AES-128 TLS 1.3 cipher suites on the S3-
compatible object store on ports 3000 and 3001:
Note: The naming scheme for the ciphers in the command below is different from the scheme used for port 443.
iris_cli -username=username -password=password -skip_password_ prompt=true cluster update-gflag service-name=bridge reason=disable_ aes_128 gflag-name=bridge_s3_disabled_cipher gflag-value= TLS_AES_128_ GCM_SHA256,AES128-GCM-SHA256,AES256-GCM-SHA384,AES128-SHA,AES256-SHA effective-now=true Following is the list of ciphers used by port 3000 and 3001:
l TLS 1.2: o "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256" o "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384" o "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-SHA" o "ECDHE-ECDSA-AES256-SHA" o "ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256" o "ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384" o "ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA" o "ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA" o "AES128-GCM-SHA256" o "AES256-GCM-SHA384" o "AES128-SHA" o "AES256-SHA"
l TLS 1.3: o "TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256" o "TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384" o "TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256"
3. Restart the Bridge service to apply the changes: cluster restart-services service-names=bridge
Disabling AES-128 ciphers lets organizations that require AES-256-only encryption policies restrict the cluster to stronger cipher suites.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Customize Preferences

Note: Before disabling any ciphers, verify that your clients and backup agents support AES-256 cipher suites. Disabling AES-128 ciphers on a cluster that has clients or agents that only support AES-128 will prevent those clients from connecting.

Enable File Modification Detection
The Enable File Modification Detection feature sends notifications to the user if a shared file or folder is modified. To enable this feature, contact Cohesity Support.
Update the Change Notification Events Limit
This feature enables you to update the number of events generated per file object within a given time interval. The default limit is 5 events in one minute (60000000 usecs). To update the events notification, contact Cohesity Support.
Customize Preferences
The Customization page in the Cohesity cluster allows you to customize various settings and options to tailor your experience according to your personal preferences. You can modify settings related to your account, user interface, and interactions with the Cohesity cluster. For example, you can hide the options on the left navigation that are not relevant to your environment, hide the options from the Data Protection menu, or select a favorite dashboard. You can customize the preferences both at the cluster level and user level.
Note: The Customization feature is not available for tenant users.
Customize Preferences at the User Level
User-level customization of the Cohesity cluster applies to the logged-in user. Perform the following steps for user-level customization:

Cohesity Cluster Services
A Cohesity cluster consists of multiple internal services that work together to deliver core cluster operations like data protection, storage management, monitoring, security, and overall cluster operations. Each service performs a specific function, such as orchestrating backup and recovery workflows, managing cluster health, handling I/O operations, or enabling indexing and search. This topic provides a consolidated overview of the cluster services that support core cluster operations. It includes:
l Internal service names: The service identifier as it appears in logs, alerts, support bundles, and diagnostic outputs. You may encounter this name during troubleshooting or when working with Cohesity Support.
l External service names: A simplified, descriptive name that represents the service's function. Use this name when discussing system behavior at a high level.
l Description: A brief explanation of what the service does and the responsibilities it handles within the cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Cohesity Cluster Services

l Primary function: A concise summary of the service's main role, such as backup orchestration, monitoring, indexing, or cluster management.
l Functional category: A high-level grouping that indicates the functional area to which the service belongs, such as Data Protection, Base Infrastructure, Monitoring, Networking, or Agent services. Categories help you quickly identify related services and understand how they fit into overall cluster operations.

Software Update
Cohesity provides a comprehensive solution for managing software upgrades and patch installations within your cluster. The new design streamlines the update process, enabling you to upload and apply both upgrade and patch packages, perform necessary pre-checks, and initiate the upgrade or patch on all cluster nodes. When you download an upgrade package, you also have the option to download a corresponding patch, ensuring your cluster is fully updated. Additionally, Cohesity provides real-time tracking for both upgrades and

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Software Update

patches, allowing you to monitor the status of each node, track completion times, and resolve any issues that may occur during the process. Cohesity ensures a seamless and efficient way to maintain your cluster with the following key functions:
l Download Package l Upgrade Cluster l Apply Patch l Upgrade with Patch
Before you begin, it is important to familiarize yourself with the following upgrade paths, prerequisites, and considerations to ensure a smooth upgrade and patching process.

Upgrading to 7.4
You can upgrade your Cohesity cluster from previous releases to 7.4.1. The following table provides details on supported upgrade paths.

Your Current Release
l 7.4 l 7.3.2 l 7.3.1 l 7.3 l 7.2.2_u2 l 7.2.2_u1 l 7.2.2 l 7.2.1 l 7.2 l 7.1.2_u6 l 7.1.2_u4 l 7.1.2_u3 l 7.1.2_u2 l 7.1.2_u1 l 7.1.2 l 7.1.1 l 7.1

Upgrade Path to 7.4.1 7.4.1 directly

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Software Update

Note: Direct upgrades from 6.8.x to 7.4.1 are not supported. If your cluster is running any 6.8.x release (such as 6.8.1, 6.8.1_u1, or 6.8.2), a step upgrade is necessary. First, upgrade to 7.1.2_u6, and then proceed to 7.4.1.

Release Upgrade Policy

Policy

Example

Cohesity will support upgrades from the latest release of the prior LTS release branch, which includes all LTS designated releases within the branch, to the most recent release of the current LTS branch.

6.6.0d+ (LTS designated releases: 6.6.0d_u3, 6.6.0d_u4, 6.6.0d_u5, 6.6.0d_u6) to 6.8.2 LTS designated release will be supported.

Cohesity will not allow upgrades by default to any release that is older in time irrespective of the release branch. Exceptions are to be managed on a case-bycase basis.

6.5.1f_release-20210825_596bb917 is released after 6.6.0c_release-20210822_ 0d731348. Therefore, an upgrade from the 6.5.1f version to the 6.6.0c version is not supported.
This policy is also applicable to patches. If you have upgraded your Cohesity cluster to a patch released after the LTS release, upgrading to that LTS release is not supported. However, you can upgrade to any LTS version released after the patch. For example, your Cohesity clusters were upgraded to 6.6.0d_u5 in July 2022. Cohesity released 6.8.1_u1 on Nov 2022 and the 6.6.0d-p32 patch on March 2023. If you've applied 6.6.0d-p32, you cannot upgrade to 6.8.1_u1. However, you can upgrade to the upcoming 6.8.1_u2 release.

Cohesity will support the release N-1 upgrade without an intermediate step. (N is defined as the current release branch).

7.2.x to 7.4.1 is supported. 7.4.1 is the current release branch.

Cohesity will support the release N-2 upgrade without an intermediate step. (N is defined as the current release branch).

7.1.x to 7.4.1 is supported. 7.4.1 is the current release branch.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Software Update

Policy

Example

When a specific release is declared LTS, Cohesity will support upgrading from the open LTS releases to the new LTS release. This will include the three most recent releases on the LTS branch to the new LTS release.

6.8.1, 6.8.1_u1, 6.8.1_u2, 6.8.1_u3, 6.8.1_u4, 6.8.1_u5, 6.8.1_u6, 6.8.1_u7 to 6.8.2.

Upgrade Considerations
Note the following about upgrading the Cohesity cluster to 7.4.1:
l Cohesity does not support rolling back to older versions.
l To upgrade the Cohesity cluster from a version that is no longer supported, Cohesity recommends you to upgrade to any of the supported versions mentioned in the Upgrade Paths, and then perform an upgrade to the latest release version. For information on Cohesity Products that have reached the end of support, see Cohesity Products End of Support.
l See Cohesity Feature Deprecation to review the list of features marked for deprecation for Cohesity 7.4.1 and later releases.
l Before performing the upgrade, ensure that the cluster data space and metadata space utilized is less than 85%. After the cluster upgrade, the Garbage Collection algorithms take 3 to 4 days to trigger. Hence, ensure that the cluster has enough space during this period. Space constraints may lead to backup and replication failures on the Cohesity cluster.
l If you are running remote adapter jobs and the cluster is upgraded, the jobs will be disrupted during the upgrade process. The jobs will be killed and restarted multiple times during the upgrade.
l Starting 6.8.2 and 7.1.2, the Cohesity indexing service is optimized to automatically identify and delete stale directories at regular intervals, which were created for indexing. After upgrading from a version without this optimization, the cluster indexing service will remove any stale directories identified, which may result in cluster-free space increase.
l Cohesity recommends upgrading the Cohesity Agent on Physical Servers and the Cohesity installed Agent on VMs to the latest release version of the Cohesity cluster.
l Cohesity recommends upgrading the Cohesity cluster first, followed by the Cohesity Agent. Upgrading an agent before the cluster is likely to impact the existing functionality and disruptions may be observed due to agent being on a higher version

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Software Update

than the cluster. Cohesity also recommends the agents be on the same, latest major version as the Cohesity cluster to get the latest security fixes and benefit from newer features.
l After upgrading to the latest version, if there is an IP subnet conflict, the Enable Apps Management toggle in Marketplace > My Apps is turned off. Navigate to Settings > Summary > click Configure and specify a different IP address in the Configure Apps management network field and then turn on the Enable Apps Management option.
l If you are on a Cohesity Cloud Edition cluster and using Marketplace Apps, then when you upgrade the Cohesity Cloud Edition cluster to 7.4.1, connectivity among the Marketplace Apps could be impacted* due to Flannel moving to etcd v3 APIs. It is recommended to pause any Marketplace Apps before the upgrade and resume them once the upgrade is complete.
*Impact: Running workloads, Protection Groups, or scans related to the Marketplace App might see network disruption during the upgrade.
l For pure PXG clusters, before upgrading from version 6.6 to 6.8.1 or above, make sure that your cluster usage is below 95%. After the upgrade, there is a known issue where the available data space may decrease. Even clusters that are using only 88% of disk space before the upgrade have experienced out-of-space errors afterward, which can lead to backup failures. To avoid disruptions, Cohesity strongly recommends reducing disk usage well below 95% before starting the upgrade process.
l Cohesity is working to qualify the Windows agent for Japanese Windows version that uses Shift-JIS encoding. Wait to upgrade agent to version 7.4.1 until Cohesity releases a version that supports Japanese language (Shift_JIS) based Windows OS.
l Manual disk-space verification on nodes is not required. During the upgrade, the system performs pre-upgrade checks and automatically cleans up disk space when possible. If sufficient space is still unavailable, the upgrade stops immediately and provides a clear error message indicating the specific node and path that require additional space.
l If you are leveraging storage snapshots for VMware VM backups in releases prior to 7.2 and plan to upgrade the Cohesity cluster to release 7.2 or later, ensure that SAN connectivity between Cohesity nodes and the Storage Array (Pure, HPE Alletra, Nimble, and IBM) is in place before the upgrade to prevent VM backup failures.
l Starting with Cohesity version 7.2.2, the Cohesity BaseOS transitioned from RHEL 7.x to RHEL 9.x, and the time synchronization service changed from ntpd to chronyd. Due to this architectural change, Windows-based NTP sources (Windows Time Service / W32Time) are not supported for Cohesity clusters running version 7.2.2 or later. Configure Linux-based NTP sources for time synchronization before upgrading to ensure cluster stability and supportability.

Databases
l The addition of the new Postgres database could cause UI slowness until the ETL process completes. The bootstrap run of the ETL process pulls the entire data set to populate the database. The initial run has a slight performance impact. In the case of upgrades, data population happens in the post-upgrade step. Subsequent upgrades will not be affected.
l After upgrading to the latest version, to display SAP HANA log backups in the Cohesity cluster, you need to modify the existing registered source and set the et-log-backup source registration parameter to true. Only the log backups triggered after enabling et-log-backup will be shown on the Cohesity cluster.
Note: After modifying the source configuration (with-et-logbackup=true), a full backup is mandatory. The initial full backup must be completed before any log backups appear on the Cohesity user interface.
l If you are upgrading to version 7.4.1 or later, you need to update the existing SAP HANA source configuration to enable auto-discovery and entity hierarchy. Set the -entity-hierarchy source registration parameter to "true." After updating the source configuration (with --entity-hierarchy=true), a full backup is mandatory.
l For SQL log backups, if you are upgrading the cluster to version 7.2 and above, ensure that the Cohesity cluster bridge node VIPs on port 11117 are reachable from the SQL source. In case of the multitenant environment, ensure that the Hybrid Extender IPs on port 11117 are reachable from the SQL Source.
Note: The SQL log backup will fail post-upgrade if the above-mentioned port requirement is not satisfied.
l If you have upgraded your cluster to Cohesity 7.4.1 from an earlier version and already have an AWS account registered, you must add new permissions to protect the newly supported AWS workloads: l Amazon RDS (Ingest-based protection) l Amazon Redshift l Amazon DocumentDB l Amazon DynamoDB

Microsoft 365

Single Node Cluster Upgrades
Single node cluster upgrades must be run when the upgrade will have the least impact. During the upgrade of a single node cluster, the node is rebooted and during the reboot, the cluster is unable to process Protection Groups, recover tasks, or any other workflow.
Virtual Edition Deployment
The following are the requirements for the Virtual Edition deployment for 6.8 and later versions:
l small (8 TB) configuration supports Virtual Machines with 12 vCPUs, 32 GB of memory, and 64 GB virtual disk to store the operating system.
l large (16 TB) configuration supports Virtual Machines with 24 vCPUs, 64 GB of memory, and 64 GB virtual disk to store the operating system.
For more information, see Virtual Edition for VMware Setup Guide and Virtual Edition for Clustered VMware Setup Guide.
Replication Environments
l If the cluster replication is configured, verify that the network connectivity is functioning properly during the upgrade to ensure the cluster replication relationship is successfully upgraded to use AES-256-GCM for encryption.
l In a replication setup, when you upgrade your Cohesity cluster to Cohesity 6.6 or later and you use the default System Admin password, you will be prompted to change the password. After changing the password, you must update the new password on the replication partner cluster.
l For information about using replication between Cohesity clusters running different versions, see Replication Compatibility. For the latest notes about replication compatibility, prerequisites and limitations, see the Release Notes.

Upgrade and Patch Workflows
If the Cohesity cluster is not running the newest software version, upgrade the Cohesity cluster. Only upgrade packages that are newer than the current version can be installed.
You can upgrade the software using the Cohesity cluster as described in the procedures below. You can use the same procedure and upgrade package to upgrade any Cohesity cluster, regardless of whether the Cohesity cluster is hosted on on-premises hardware, Cloud Edition or Virtual Edition.
Download Package
To download an upgrade or patch package, you can select the desired package type from either a URL or your local machine. Once the package is chosen, you can proceed with downloading, or opt to apply the upgrade or patch immediately.
Perform the following steps to download the package:
1. Go to Settings > Software Update and click Get New Package.

A dialog appears with the following package options: 1. Upgrade Package 2. Patch Package 3. Upgrade and Patch Packages

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration
2. Select the required package and click Continue. A Get New Upgrade Package dialog appears.

3. Choose one of the following options to download the package.

Option

Field

Description

From URL

Enter the download URL

Provide the package's URL

Repository credentials for package (Optional)

Repository credentials can be used to download packages from secure repositories that require authentication to access the files.
Choose one of the following options from the drop-down:
Basic - Select this if your repository requires HTTP basic authentication. Enter the Username and Password.
Custom - Select this if your repository requires custom authentication schemes and requires you to pass credentials as HTTP headers. Enter Key and Value. Key is the HTTP header name and Value is the HTTP header value.

From Local Machine

Select File

Browse and select the downloaded package from your local machine.

Note: When you select the Upgrade and Patch Package option, you can either specify the download URLs of both upgrade and patch packages or you can upload the downloaded packages from your local machine to cluster.

4. Depending on your package selection, you can click: 1. Get Only to download the package. 2. Get and Upgrade to download and immediately upgrade the package. 3. Get and Apply to download and apply the patch.

Once the package is downloaded, you can perform the following actions by clicking

on

the package:

l Upload CRL for Signed Package - To upload Certificate Revocation List (CRL) for signed packages. CRLs are used to validate whether the certificate used for signing the package has been revoked after the package was downloaded to the Cohesity cluster.
l View Checksum - To view and verify the checksum of the package.
l Delete - To delete the package.
Run Pre-check
The pre-check option is available after the package download. It is important to run the prechecks once the packages have been downloaded. Doing so in advance allows you to identify and resolve any issues, ensuring a smooth upgrade and patching process without any interruptions.
To run the pre-check on the downloaded package, click Run.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Software Update

The pre-check will start and you can see the pre-check details by clicking View Details.
Note: The cluster can host only one patch package and one upgrade package.
Upgrade Cluster To upgrade the cluster, you can select the upgrade package and initiate the upgrade process after performing the pre-check. You can track the upgrade progress for all nodes until the operation is completed. Perform the following steps to upgrade the cluster:
1. On the Software Update page, click Upgrade.

The Upgrade Review dialog appears.

Software Update

2. After reviewing the upgrade information, click Start Upgrade. The Ok to Upgrade? dialog appears.

Proceed with the upgrade by ignoring pre-check failure to continue the upgrade process despite the pre-check failure.
4. Enter Yes in the text field and click Upgrade to confirm and start upgrading.
The upgrading process will begin. You can observe the upgrading progress for all the available nodes in the cluster.

3. Enter Yes in the text field and click Apply to confirm and start applying the patch.
You can observe the patching progress for all the available nodes in the cluster. The patching process will begin after the pre-checks are completed on all nodes, starting with the node having the lowest ID.

4. If the pre-check fails, you can either: 1. Stop immediately to stop the upgrade process (recommended). This allows you to review and address the pre-check failures before retrying the upgrade. 2. Proceed with the upgrade by ignoring pre-check failure to continue the upgrade process despite the pre-check failure.
5. Enter Yes in the text field and click Upgrade to confirm and start upgrading.
The upgrading process will begin. You can observe the upgrading progress for all the available nodes in the cluster.

Cancel Upgrade
Cancel Upgrade in a Single Node Cluster Run the following command to cancel the upgrade in a single node Cohesity cluster: iris_cli cluster upgrade cancel=true Sample Output Username: admin 'admin' Password:password123 Success: Aborted upgrade. When running the CLI command to cancel the upgrade of a Single Node Cohesity Cluster, all upgrades, including ongoing upgrades on its nodes, are canceled. Cancel Upgrade in a Multinode Cluster Run the following command to cancel the upgrade in a multinode Cohesity cluster: iris_cli cluster upgrade cancel=true Sample Output Username: admin 'admin' Password:password123 Success: upgrade cancellation is requested. If upgrade cancellation is requested when an upgrade is in progress on one of its nodes, the Cohesity cluster allows the upgrade to complete on that node. Once the ongoing upgrade is completed, subsequent upgrades on its remaining nodes are aborted. While the approach improves cluster stability, it may lead to nodes on different versions. You can resolve this by upgrading the remaining nodes to ensure all the nodes are of the same version.

Search the Cluster and Take Action
You can search the Cohesity cluster for objects, such as VMs, storage volumes and databases, refine the search results and then perform actions on the objects. You can find and protect unprotected objects, investigate failed Protection Groups, or recover or clone snapshots, all from the search results page. The actions launch the same familiar Cohesity workflow pages, but help is available for each page if you need it.
Example: Find and Protect with a Job
The following example demonstrates how to find unprotected VMs and protect them by creating a Protection Group.
1. Type vm in the search box at the top of the dashboard and press enter. You can search for any partial name or type an asterisk * wildcard.

The Search page displays a list of objects that contain vm in the name.
2. Optionally, refine the list by selecting checkboxes in the left pane. a. Under Type, select the Virtual Infrastructure checkbox. Additional options are displayed based on the infrastructure you select. b. Under Virtual Infrastructure Type, select the VMware checkbox. c. Under Status, select the Unprotected checkbox.
The list of objects automatically updates to display only unprotected VMware VMs. 3. Select a VM in the center pane.
Details about the VM display in the right pane. 4. Click Protect and select Protection Group. 5. Click New Job. 6. The New Job page is displayed and you can create a job to protect the VM.

Manage Storage Domains
From the Manage Storage Domains page, you can view, add and manage the Storage Domains that have been created on the Cohesity cluster. For detailed instructions, see Create or Edit Storage Domains.
The columns for the table displayed on the Manage Storage Domains page are described below.

Column Name

Description / Action

Storage Domain Name

Drill-down on this link to view the details and statics about the Storage Domain. You can also edit the Storage Domain from the linked page.

Organization

Drill-down on this link to get details of the organization that is associated with the Protection Group.

Physical Used

The size of the data physically stored on the Cohesity cluster, after the data has been reduced by change block tracking, compression and deduplication, including the disk space used for data resiliency (fault tolerance and erasure coding).

Physical Quota

The maximum physical capacity of the Storage Domain if its Physical Quota option is on. If the option is off, the field indicates n/a.

Logical Managed

The logical data managed, as computed by the Cohesity cluster without reduction by change-block tracking, compression and deduplication.

Redundancy

The Storage Domain's redundancy, either Redundancy Factor (RF2 or RF3) or Erasure Coding (EC) and the number of data stripes : number of failures to tolerate.

Deduplication

Indicates if Deduplication is on for the Storage Domain and when the deduplication occurs. If Deduplication is on, the Cohesity cluster eliminates duplicate blocks of repeating data stored on the Cohesity cluster, thus reducing the amount of storage space needed to store data. If Inline Deduplication is on, deduplication occurs when the Cohesity cluster writes the data to the Cohesity View. If Inline Deduplication is off, deduplication occurs after the Cohesity cluster writes the data to the Cohesity View.

Create or Edit Storage Domains
A Storage Domain, formerly known as a View Box, is a named storage location on a Cluster. A Storage Domain defines the policy and frequency for deduplication among other configurations such as Compression, Erasure Coding, and Replication Factor. A Storage Domain contains Views. When you configure a Protection Group, you specify a Storage Domain, and during a Protection Group Run, the Cohesity cluster stores the Snapshots in that Storage Domain.
To create or edit a Storage Domain:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Manage Storage Domains

1. Navigate to Settings > Summary and select the Storage Domains tab. 2. On the Storage Domains page, complete one of the following actions:
l Click Add Storage Domain located at the top right of the page.
l Edit an existing Storage Domain by clicking the Actions Menu ( ) and
selecting Edit ( ).
3. Storage Domain Name: Enter a name for the Storage Domain.
4. Associated External Target: Select the external target to be associated with the Storage Domain. This associated external target stores all the data landing on this Storage Domain. Each Storage Domain can only be associated with one external target and vice versa. Once set, the associated external target cannot be changed.
NOTE: This field is only available for GCP Next-Gen Cloud Edition.
5. Authentication Provider: You can map the Storage Domain to an AD domain if the Cohesity cluster, version 6.5.1d or higher, is AD domain-joined. Mapping to a specific AD domain means that users from only that AD domain have permission to view the Storage Domain's contents when accessing through SMB. By default, a Storage Domain is accessible to users from all joined AD domains.
6. Deduplication: Optionally toggle on. If Deduplication is on, the Cohesity cluster eliminates duplicate blocks of repeating data stored on the Cohesity cluster, thus reducing the amount of storage space needed to store data.
Note: Toggling Deduplication on for a non-Deduplication Storage Domain that uses Cloud Tier may result in a large number of reads from the Cloud Tier if Storage Domain data has already been sent to the Cloud Tier.
Inline Deduplication: Optionally toggle on. If Inline Deduplication is on, deduplication occurs when the Cohesity cluster writes the data to the Cohesity View. If Inline Deduplication is off, deduplication occurs after the Cohesity cluster writes the data to the Cohesity View.
7. Compression: Optionally toggle on. If Compression is on, the Cohesity cluster compresses all the data stored in the Storage Domain, thus reducing the amount of storage space needed to store the data. If Compression is on and then turned off later, the current data on the Storage Domain is not decompressed, but any new data stored on the Storage Domain is not compressed.
Inline Compression: Optionally toggle on. If Inline Compression is on, compression occurs when the Cohesity cluster saves the blocks to the Cluster. If Inline Compression is off, compression occurs after the Cohesity cluster writes the data to the Cohesity cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Manage Storage Domains

Note: If both Compression and Inline Deduplication are on, Cohesity recommends you turn Inline Compression on.
8. Encryption: Toggle to enable encryption for the Storage Domain. Encryption can be enabled only when you are creating the Storage Domain. Once the Storage Domain is created, the options to enable encryption or modify its encryption settings are disabled in the Cohesity cluster. By default, Cohesity uses Internal KMS for encryption. If encryption is enabled at the cluster level, then data within the Storage Domains is also encrypted, and you don't have to enable encryption for each Storage Domain. You can register an external KMS and select one of the following from the drop-down list: l AWS l KMIP Compliant For more information, see External Key Management Service.
9. Expand Show Advanced Settings to see the list of additional View settings. 10. Physical Quota: Optionally toggle on to limit the Storage Domain's physical capacity
and then set the capacity. The capacity must be a whole number. Toggle Alert on to trigger an Alert when the Storage Domain reaches the specified threshold. 11. Logical Quota: Optionally toggle on to set a default logical capacity limit for Views created in this Storage Domain and set the capacity. Logical data is fully hydrated and expanded. Toggle Alert on to trigger an Alert when the View reaches the specified threshold. 12. Cloud Tier: Optionally toggle on. If Cloud Tier is on, the Cohesity cluster moves cold (rarely accessed) data to the designated External Target. Once Cloud Tier is on, it cannot be turned off. To turn Cloud Tier off, contact Cohesity Support to disable the feature. If Cloud Tier is on, select an External Target or register a new External Target. Set the coldness of data to tier.
Note: If the Physical Quota toggle is off, the cluster's default capacity and space utilization threshold are used for tiering.
Optionally, toggle on Override Cluster Threshold and set the Space Utilization Threshold to activate cloud tiering for the Storage Domain.
