Secure Login
Secure Login provides additional layers of security that enable the verification of the identity of a user, restricting unauthorized access and malicious activity in the cluster environment. Secure Login includes,
l Multi-factor Authentication (MFA)
l Split Key
For enhanced security, Cohesity strongly recommends that you enable MFA for all users and groups. After MFA is enabled by the administrator, users are prompted for an additional authentication factor along with the Cohesity cluster user credentials during the sign-in process.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

Note: A user must have a user account in the Cohesity Data Cloud (Selfmanaged) to use MFA provided by Cohesity.
Cohesity supports multi-factor authentication for the following types of users and groups: l Local user l Active Directory users with user accounts created in Cohesity l SSO users and groups l Support user
Cohesity supports split key for the following types of users: l Cohesity Console user l Support user
Important: If you are using SSO for authentication, then Cohesity recommends that you enable MFA in your SSO system.
By default, MFA is enabled for Active Directory users with user accounts created in the Cohesity. You can enable MFA for local users and the support user account in the Cohesity. For more information, see:
l Multi-factor Authentication for Local and Active Directory Users l Multi-factor Authentication for the Support User Account l Enable Split Key Multi-factor Authentication for Local and Active Directory Users Multi-factor Authentication (MFA) is an additional layer of security used to verify the identity of a user. Cohesity supports MFA for local users. MFA enforces users to provide an additional authentication factor to access the Cohesity GUI or Cohesity CLI. By default, MFA is enabled for Active Directory users with user accounts created in Cohesity. Administrators can enable MFA so that all or specific local users are prompted during the sign-in process for an additional authentication factor along with the local user credentials that they use to log in to the Cohesity cluster. Cohesity supports the following authentication methods: l Authenticator App--Users must enter the verification code generated by a TOTP
authenticator app such as Okta Verify.

Access Management

Note: For Active Directory users, the Authenticator App is the only supported MFA method.
l Email--Users must enter the verification code sent to their email address. After MFA is enabled by the administrator, an additional authentication factor is enforced for all users on their next login.

Frequently Asked Questions
1. How can I log in to the Cohesity cluster if I lose my device? If the authenticator app is the primary MFA method and if you lose your device, you can use the alternative verification method. For more information, see Click Use Alternative Verification Method: Cohesity recommends that administrators enable both authentication methods for local users:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

l Authenticator app l Email If email is not enabled as an authentication method, users can contact the administrator to reset MFA for their account. 2. How do I connect the authenticator app to my new device? If you are changing your device, check whether the authenticator app allows transferring accounts to your new device. For example, Google Authenticator supports transferring accounts to your new device. For more information, see the Transfer Google Authenticator codes to a new phone section on this page. As a best practice, Cohesity recommends that you check the authenticator app that you are using and confirm whether you can transfer accounts to your new device as different authenticator apps handle this in different ways. Users can also contact the administrator to reset MFA for their account. 3. How can the administrator reset the MFA for a user? If the authenticator app does not support transferring accounts or if a user does not have access to their old device, the administrator or users with the Manage Users privilege can reset MFA for users.
Note: MFA can be disabled only for local users and not Active Directory user with user accounts created in the Cohesity.
To reset MFA: a. Navigate to Settings > Access Management > Users & Groups tab. b. Turn off the toggle and disable MFA for the user. c. Turn on the toggle and reenable MFA for the user. d. The user must install and set up the authenticator app on their new device.
4. How can the administrator reset MFA for all local users? Administrators or users with the Manage MFA privilege can reset MFA for all local users. To reset MFA: 1. Navigate to Settings > Access Management > Secure Login tab. 2. Turn off the MFA toggle and disable MFA at the cluster level. 3. Turn on the MFA toggle and re-enable MFA at the cluster level. MFA is reset for all local users. Users must set up MFA again. For more information, see Set Up MFA for Local and Active Directory Users.
5. What should I do if my email-based verification code expires?

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

If email is the primary MFA method and if there is a delay in receiving the email, the verification code expires. Users can request a new verification code. Cohesity recommends that you use the authenticator app method instead. An authenticator app can generate verification codes even if the device has no connectivity. 6. What should I do if I am locked out of my account? A login attempt may fail if users enter an incorrect password or verification code. User accounts are locked out after three consecutive failed attempts. If the user account is locked out because of an incorrect verification code, retry after one minute. If the user account is locked out because of an incorrect password, retry after 15 minutes or contact the administrator and request to unlock the user account. If an administrator is locked out, contact the peer administrator to reset MFA. 7. Can the default MFA be disabled for AD accounts? Yes, the default MFA can be disabled for the AD accounts through Cohesity CLI. Contact the Cohesity Support to disable the default MFA.

Certificates
The Certificates page lists all the certificates available in the certificate store. Certificates in this store are used to authenticate Cohesity to registered sources, enabling Cohesity to protect your workloads. You can generate a new certificate or import a certificate in the Personal Information Exchange (PFX) format. You can also add, edit, and delete the certificates.
Note: l This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature. l The Certificates page is used to manage the certificate store for workload authentication. Generate Cohesity Managed Certificate To generate a Cohesity Managed Certificate:
1. Navigate to Settings > Access Management > Certificates. 2. Click on the Certificates drop-down and select Generate. 3. In the Generate Cohesity Managed Certificate window, enter the following
details: l Given Name - A name for the certificate that is easy to recall. This can be edited later.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

l Common Name (CN) - Domain name or the entity for which the certificate is issued.
l Cluster/Region - Cluster/Region for which the certificate is generated. Only required when accessing from global mode or Data Protect mode.
l Valid Till - Validity of the certificate. The default validity is one year. l Organization Issued To - [Optional] Organization to which the certificate is
issued. The default value is Cohesity Inc. l Department Issued To - [Optional] Department to which the certificate is
issued. The default value is Cohesity Inc. 4. Click Generate. 5. The new certificate will be generated and displayed on the Certificates page. Guidelines to Generate Custom Certificate using OpenSSL To generate a custom certificate using OpenSSL: 1. To generate a private key:
#openssl genrsa -out tls.key 2048 2. To generate a CSR:
#openssl req -new -key tls.key -out tls.csr 3. To self sign the certificate:
#openssl x509 -req -in tls.csr -signkey tls.key -out tls.crt -days 365 If you require a password protected certificate, then instead of command 4 run command 5.
4. To export the certificate and the private key to PFX: #openssl pkcs12 -export -out tls.pfx -inkey tls.key -in tls.crt certfile ca-chain.crt
5. To generate a password protected certificate. #openssl pkcs12 -export -out tls.pfx -inkey tls.key -in tls.crt certfile ca-chain.crt -passout pass:MyStrongPassword
If you already have the certificate and private key in PEM format and only require the PFX file, then only run the commands in steps 4 or 5. Import Custom Certificate
Note: Certificates only in the Personal Information Exchange (PFX) format are supported.

Certificate Alert Threshold Configuration
Certificates generated by Cohesity are valid for one year by default. Default severity thresholds for non-auto-renewed certificates are 15% / 10% / 5% remaining validity (Info / Warning / Critical). You can perform a retrieval of certificate inventory and configure alert thresholds using the API and CLI. A retrieval is faster than relying on scheduled inventory scans. It allows you to fetch certificate details on demand and proactively manage certificate expiry alerts. The CLI commands internally invoke the same REST APIs for threshold configuration. Run the following command from a node to enable the certificate_inventory_api_and_alerts feature:
iris_cli cluster update-feature-flag name=certificate_inventory_api_and_ alerts is-approved=true reason="enable cert inventory"
Ensure the threshold values meet the following requirements: l Values must be in the range 1-50. l criticalPercent < warningPercent < infoPercent.
View Certificate Inventory using API
Endpoints
GET /v2/cert-manager/cert-inventory
Perform the following steps to retrieve certificate inventory using API: 1. Authenticate using POST /irisservices/api/v1/public/accessTokens 2. Call GET /v2/cert-manager/cert-inventory
Parameters

Parameter maxStaleness nodeIp pageSize

Type string string integer

Required No No No

Description Controls freshness of certificate inventory data Retrieves inventory for a specific node Reserved for future batching/pagination

Configure Certificate Alert Threshold using CLI To view the stored override configuration, run: iris_cli cert-manager inventory-alert-threshold-get | jq . You can update threshold configurations using either a JSON file or CLI flags.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

To update thresholds using a JSON file, run: iris_cli cert-manager inventory-alert-threshold-set threshold-json-filee=/tmp/threshold-by-cert.json | jq .
The JSON file supports the following structure: { "byCertId": { "<cert_id>": { "infoPercent": , "warningPercent": , "criticalPercent": } }, "byCategory": { "": { "infoPercent": , "warningPercent": , "criticalPercent": } }, "global": { "infoPercent": , "warningPercent": , "criticalPercent": } }
To update thresholds using flags, run: iris_cli cert-manager inventory-alert-threshold-set
global-info-percent= global-warning-percent= global-critical-percent= | jq .
Example: iris_cli cert-manager inventory-alert-threshold-set
global-info-percent=28 global-warning-percent=17 global-critical-percent=9 | jq .

Required No No No

Perform the following steps to retrieve stored threshold configuration using API: 1. Authenticate using POST /irisservices/api/v1/public/accessTokens 2. Call GET /v2/cert-manager/cert-inventory/alert-threshold
Perform the following steps to configure thresholds using API:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

1. Authenticate using POST /irisservices/api/v1/public/accessTokens
2. Call PUT /v2/cert-manager/cert-inventory/alert-threshold
Request Body
The request body for PUT /v2/cert-manager/cert-inventory/alert-threshold should include a JSON object with the following structure:
{ "byCertId": { "<cert_id>": { "infoPercent": <int>, "warningPercent": <int>, "criticalPercent": <int> } }, "byCategory": { "<category>": { "infoPercent": <int>, "warningPercent": <int>, "criticalPercent": <int> } }, "global": { "infoPercent": <int>, "warningPercent": <int>, "criticalPercent": <int> }
}

Request Body Schema

Field byCertId byCategory global

Type Object Object Object

Required No No No

Description
Map of certificate IDs to threshold configurations. If omitted, the existing byCertId configuration is preserved.
Map of certificate categories to threshold configurations. If omitted, the existing byCategory configuration is preserved.
Global threshold configuration. If omitted, the existing global configuration is preserved.

Configure Account Security Settings
The Account Security page on a Cohesity cluster allows you to secure your Cohesity cluster through policy-driven user settings for managing passwords, user sessions, user inactivity, and locking the user account after multiple wrong password attempts. You can refer to the sections below to learn more about using and configuring these policies.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

l View the Default Password Policy l Define the Account Lockout Policy l Define the Account Session Policy
View the Default Password Policy
On the Cohesity cluster, by default, a password policy is assigned to the local users. For added security, you can edit and customize the password policy based on your organization's requirements. It's important to change the passwords immediately as a response to ransomware attacks. This helps in minimizing the impact of the attack while keeping the data secured. In the default password policy, you can update:
l Password strength l Restrict the reuse of recently used passwords l Set the password lifetime
From the Cohesity Dashboard, you can view the password policy that is applied by default to the local user account in the Cohesity cluster. To view the default password policy:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Settings > Account Security. 2. From the Password Policy tab, you can view the configuration of the default
password policy.
Update the Password Strength
The strength of a password depends on its length, complexity, and unpredictability. You can make the local user access to your Cohesity cluster more secure by changing the default password strength defined in the password policy. To update the password strength:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Settings > Account Security. 2. On the Password Policy tab, click the Edit icon. 3. In the Strength section, based on your requirement, set the following values:
1. In the Minimum Length field, enter the length of the password. By default, the length of the password is set to eight characters.
Note: Ensure that you select any one of the following options.
2. Select At least one uppercase letter to mandate, including one uppercase letter in the password.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

3. Select At least one lowercase letter to mandate, including one lowercase letter in the password.
4. Select At least one number to mandate, including one numerical digit in the password
5. Select At least one special character to mandate, including one special character in the password. For more details on what special characters are allowed in the local user password, see the Users and Groups section.

4. Click Save.
Restrict Reuse of Passwords
You can prevent local users from reusing a specified number of previous passwords. By default, the password policy is set to restrict five previously used passwords. To update the password reuse limit:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Settings > Account Security. 2. On the Password Policy tab, click the Edit icon. 3. Under the Reuse section, do the following:
l In the Minimum Characters Different field, set the minimum character that must be different than the characters used in the previous password.
l In the Minimum Reuse Difference field, set the password reuse limit. 4. Click Save.
Set Password Lifetime
In the password policy, you can restrict the local user from resetting the password for a certain number of days. Also, you can set the local user password to expire after a specific number of days. By default, passwords are set to expire in 60 days. You can set the minimum and maximum number of days for the password lifetime.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

The minimum number of days defines the number of days the local user is restricted to reset the password. For example, if the minimum number of days is set to five, the local user cannot reset his password for five days after the password is set for the local user. The maximum number of days defines the number of days the local user password is valid. After the defined number of days, the password expires, and the local user is automatically prompted to change the password. To set the password lifetime:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Settings > Account Security. 2. On the Password Policy tab, click the Edit icon. 3. In the Lifetime section, based on your requirement, set the following values:
1. In the Minimum Password Reset Duration field, enter the minimum number of days to restrict the local user from resetting the password.
2. In the Password Expiry field, enter the maximum number of days after which the local user password must expire.
4. Click Save.
Note: The password lifetime can be set to a maximum value of 365.
Define the Account Lockout Policy The Account Lockout policy in your password policy enables you to automatically lock the local user account if an attempt has been made to brute-force a local user password.
Note: Users with the admin role are exempt from lockouts even after the failed login attempts.
In the Account Lockout policy, you can define: l The number of consecutive failed login attempts causes a local user account to be locked. l The time duration within which the consecutive failed login attempts cause a local user account to be locked. l The inactivity timeout period for the user account. If the local user account is inactive for the configured inactivity timeout period, the local user account is automatically locked.
Once a user account is locked, the System Admin can unlock the account from the Settings > Account Security page in the Cohesity Dashboard.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

To define the account lockout policy:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Settings > Account Security. 2. On the Password Policy tab, click the Edit icon. 3. In the Account Lockout Policy section, based on your requirement, set the
following values: 1. In the Lockout Time Duration field, enter the time duration within which the consecutive failed login attempts must cause a local user account to be locked. By default, the time duration is set to 15 minutes. 2. In the Inactivity Time field, enter the inactivity timeout period for the user account after which the account is automatically locked. By default, the inactivity timeout period is set to 35 days. 3. In the Failed Login Attempts field, enter the number of consecutive failed login attempts that must cause a local user account to be locked. By default, the number of failed attempts is set to 3.
4. Click Save.
Define the Account Session Policy
The Session policy enables you to define the session timeout for various interfaces such as UI, CLI, and SSH. In the Account Session policy, you can define:
l The maximum time limit after which the user is logged out from Cohesity UI and Cohesity CLI.
l The time limit after which any user on the Cohesity cluster is logged out from Cohesity Dashboard.
l The time limit after which any user on the Cohesity cluster is logged out when the user accesses the Cohesity through an SSH tunnel.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

To define the account session policy:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Settings > Account Security. 2. On the Password Policy tab, click the Edit icon. 3. In the Session Management Policy section, based on your requirement, set the
following values: 1. In the Maximum Absolute Timeout for UI and CLI, enter the maximum time duration for UI and CLI after which the user account will be logged out irrespective of the status of the session. The default value is set to 1440 minutes, i.e. 24 hours. The minimum value can be 1 hour and the maximum value can be 24 hours. 2. In the Inactivity Timeout for Cluster UI field, enter the inactivity time limit on Cluster UI for the user account to get logged out. The default value is set to 30 minutes. The minimum value can be 1 minute and the maximum value can be 12 hours. 3. In the Inactivity Timeout for SSH, enter the inactivity timeout limit on SSH sessions for the user account to get logged out. The default value is set to 5 minutes. The minimum value can be 1 minute and the maximum value can be 24 hours.
4. Click Save.

Best Practices for Managing Helios Users
Firstly, Cohesity recommends that you decide the primary authentication mechanism you wish to use. You have two options:
l Helios (SaaS) authentication l Your own SSO provider
For more information about configuring Cohesity Data Cloud to use an Identity Provider (IdP), see Add a Single Sign-on Provider.
Cohesity does not recommend one over the other. However, regardless of which authentication mechanism you choose, there are a few things you should do right away to avoid any access issues in the future:
l Create custom roles to provide access to individuals/groups in your organization. Cohesity recommends following the principle of least privilege.
l Cohesity recommends that you create a custom role with privileges equivalent to the built-in Super Admin role as you cannot modify the privileges of the built-in account. For more information about roles and privileges, see Custom Roles and Privileges.
l You must have multiple system administrator level users. Cohesity recommends that you have at least three users assigned with the built-in Super Admin role or custom role that you created with equivalent permissions.
Note: Cohesity recommends assigning the custom role.
Warning: If you have only one user with the Super Admin role or the equivalent custom role and if this user leaves your organization, you may experience issues, so ensure that you create additional users with the Super Admin role or the equivalent custom role.
l Enable MFA for all users: l To enable MFA for Cohesity Data Cloud local accounts, you should follow the steps mentioned in Multi-factor Authentication. l To enable MFA for SSO users, you must set up MFA in your SSO provider's system. For example, if you use Okta as the Identity Provider, you must set up and enable MFA in Okta.
Shared User Accounts
Cohesity does not recommend using a shared user account for any administration of our platform. If you use a shared user account, you will not be able to determine who made changes within your Cohesity Data Cloud account as audit logs are recorded for actions performed at the user account level.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

Warning: A shared user account is considered insecure and Cohesity strongly recommends you to not use a shared user account.
If you decide to use the shared user account method, Cohesity strongly recommends that you enable MFA by following the steps outlined below.
Enable Multi-factor Authentication for Cohesity Data Cloud Users
Multi-factor Authentication (MFA) provides a two-step verification method to authenticate and access Cohesity Data Cloud (SaaS). Setting up the MFA requires users to provide an additional verification factor along with the password credentials to log in to Cohesity Data Cloud. You can use codes from any authenticator app to log into Cohesity Data Cloud. After you enable MFA, access to your Cohesity Data Cloud is secured. MFA prevents unauthorized access and protects your data from ransomware attacks. For more information, see Multifactor Authentication.
SSO Usage Notes
If you enable SSO to maintain your organization's users within Cohesity Data Cloud, then Cohesity recommends that you maintain two native accounts in case of an outage or impact to your SSO provider.
If you choose to use your own SSO provider, after all SSO users are created, you can remove the initial Helios/MyCohesity account from the Cohesity Data Cloud portal. Subsequently, only users from your SSO organization can access the Cohesity Data Cloud portal. However, note that SSO users cannot access MyCohesity, so you need MyCohesity user accounts to manage support tickets and download software updates.
If you need additional users strictly for MyCohesity, you can create them in the Cohesity Data Cloud portal and once the user logs in for the first time, you can remove the application access. These users would still maintain MyCohesity access. Cohesity strongly recommends that you enable MFA for MyCohesity user accounts as well. For more information, see this knowledge base article.
Summary
l If you have followed the guidelines outlined in the Manage Helios (SaaS) Users section, you should have multiple Cohesity Data Cloud and MyCohesity users with elevated permissions to perform additional functions.
l Create custom roles based on your operational requirements. You can then create additional users and assign custom role(s) based on your requirement. For more information about roles and privileges, see Custom Roles and Privileges.
l Periodically evaluate your three elevated users to ensure that as people change roles, you are maintaining a minimum of three active users with elevated permissions.

About Cohesity Cluster Local Users
You can add local users to a Cohesity cluster. By default, when a new cluster is created, default built-in local users and groups are also created. The first user created is assigned the built-in Local Admin role. You have multiple options to add users in the Cohesity cluster:
l Local users and groups (GUI and iris_cli) l SSO users (GUI only) l Active Directory (GUI and iris_cli) l Generic LDAP (GUI and iris_cli)
Local users have direct access to the cluster if the Cohesity Data Cloud application is unavailable for cloud-based multi-cluster management. The support user can be used to access the bash shell of the Cohesity cluster using SSH. Cohesity does not recommend one over the other. However, regardless of which authentication mechanism you choose, there are a few things you should do right away to avoid any access issues in the future. SSO users cannot execute iris_cli commands. If you decide to use SSO on the local cluster and if you want to avoid using the initial admin user and local user accounts, you can import users from Active Directory or any other domain for executing iris_cli commands.
Best Practices for Managing Local Cohesity Cluster Users
l Create custom roles to provide access to individuals/groups in your organization. Cohesity recommends following the principle of least privilege.
l Cohesity recommends that you create a custom role with privileges equivalent to the built-in Admin role as you cannot modify the privileges of the built-in account.
l You must have multiple system administrator level users. Cohesity recommends that you have at least three users assigned with the built-in Admin role or custom role that you created with equivalent permissions.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

Note: Cohesity recommends assigning the custom role.
Warning: If you have only one user with the Admin role or the equivalent custom role and if this user leaves your organization, you may experience issues, so ensure that you create additional users with the Admin role or the equivalent custom role.
l Leverage named local users such as Active Directory users so that you can track iris_cli usage through audit logs.
l Enable MFA for all users: l To enable MFA for SSO users, you must set up MFA in your SSO provider's system. For example, if you use Okta as the Identity Provider, you must set up and enable MFA in Okta.

Summary
l If you have followed the guidelines outlined in the Manage Users Locally on the Cohesity Cluster section, you should have multiple local users with elevated permissions to perform additional functions.
l Create custom roles based on your operational requirements. You can then create additional users and assign custom role(s) based on your requirements.
l Periodically evaluate your three elevated users to ensure that as people change roles, you are maintaining a minimum of three active users with elevated permissions.
Open ID Connect Support for Cluster APIs
You can integrate your identity provider solution with Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-managed) to access Cohesity REST APIs through single sign-on.
Note: OpenID Connect is supported only for cluster APIs, and is not available for Single Sign-On (SSO) login via the UI.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

Prerequisites
1. You should get the JSON Web Token from your identity server. To create JWT, enter the following parameters: l alg - The type of algorithm used to generate JWT. For example, RS256. l typ - The type should be JSON Web Token and the value for it is JWT. l x5t - This is X509 Thumbprint. It's a Base64 encoded string. l exp - This is a Timestamp. l aud - The audience ID of the client application on the identity server. l upn - The username or email address of the user.
Note: The validity of JWT is defined on the Open ID Connect server.
2. You should create an Open ID user on Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-managed) to access Cohesity REST APIs through SSO. For more information, see Create an Open ID User.
3. You should register Cohesity as an application on your identity server. 4. You should create a public key and get the URL to it. Refer to the sample key below,
{ "n": "<Modulus_of_Public_Key_in_Base64>", "e": ["<Exponent_of_Public_Key_in_Base64>"] "x5t": "<Certificate_Thumbprint_of_Public_Key_in_Base64>" }
How it works
You can use Cohesity REST APIs to run cluster operations. To use Cohesity REST APIs, you can use your credentials or configure single sign-on (SSO) to authenticate without credentials. Cohesity uses OAuth 2.0 authorization framework to allow access to its REST APIs.
Configure SSO
When you configure SSO, Cohesity fetches the public key from the identity server based on the time defined for the parameter pollingFrequencyMins.
Access Cohesity REST APIs
The API request is sent from a client application to Cohesity. As a prerequisite, the client application should have the access token in JSON Web Token (JWT) format. This token consists of information about the user's claims, the algorithm used for encoding, and the public and private keys. The client application fetches this token from the identity server such as the Open ID Connect server. Once the client application receives the token, it sends an API request to the Cohesity REST API endpoint with the JWT in its headers. Cohesity decodes the JWT from the API request

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

and matches the information against the public key. If the public key matches, then Cohesity allows the user mentioned in the JWT to access its REST APIs.
Configure Identity Provider
This API endpoint allows you to configure your identity provider on Cohesity. As a result, Cohesity requests the public key from the identity server regularly and uses it to authenticate users. API URL
https://<IP_Address>/v2/identity-provider

Important: Make sure to use the POST method.
Sample Body
{ "id": 1, "domain": "<Domain_Name>", "isEnabled": true, "identityProviderType": "OpenIdConnect" "openIdConnectParams": { "audienceIds": [ "<Audience_ID1>" "<Audience_ID2>" ] "publicKeyURL": "<URL>", "pollingFrequencyMins": 1 }
Parameters

Parameter id domain
isEnabled
identityProviderType

Description
Enter the value.
Enter the domain name of the identity server. The domain should be the same as available in the JWT.
If this is set to False, then the OAuth access is disabled. If no value is entered by default, it is set to True.
Enter the value "OpenIdConnect".

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Access Management

Parameter audienceIds publicKeyUrl pollingFrequencyMins

Description
The audience ID of the client application on the identity server.
The URL to the public key on the identity server.
The rate at which Cohesity sends the request for the public key to the identity server. The minimum value is one minute and the maximum value is one week. By default, it is set to one day.

Response The status code 200 is returned. Create an Open ID User API URL https://<IP_Address>/irisservices/api/v1/public/idps/principals

Important: Make sure to use the POST method.
Sample Body
[ { "principalName": "<Email_Address>", "objectClass": "kUser", "Roles": [ "COHESITY_ADMIN" ], "domain": "<Domain_Name>" "restricted": false } ]
Parameters

Parameter principalName objectClass

Description Enter the username or email address of the user. This should match the value of `upn' in JWT. You should enter the value "kUser" to create a user.

restricted

Description Enter the roles you want to define for the user. Enter the domain name of the identity server. The domain should be the same as available in the JWT. Enter the value "false".

Response The status code 200 is returned. Refresh Public Key This API endpoint allows you to fetch the public key from the identity server. API URL https://<IP_Address>/v2/identity-providers/actions

Important: Make sure to use the GET method.
Sample Body
[ { "identityProviderType": "OpenIdConnect", "openIdConnectParams": { "action": "RefreshPublicKeys" } } ]

Web Server Certificates

Web Server Certificates
The Web Server Certificates page displays the SSL Certificate used by the Cluster UI, along with common name, certificate issue date, and validity period. From this tab, you can perform the following actions:
l View Details l Show Certificate l Update Certificate You can hover over next to a certificate to view the function of that specific certificate.
View Details
From the Web Server Certificates page, click a certificate or click Actions menu ( ) > View Certificate to view the complete web server certificate details. The page displays certificate attributes and the certificate trust chain. In the trust chain section, the details of the intermediate CA certificates and the root CA certificate are shown. The following details for the default certificate and trust chain certificates are displayed:
l Issued To l Issued By l Issued On l Valid Till l SHA Fingerprint
Note: If the issuing CA certificates are not uploaded, the application displays a message indicating that the certificate chain is incomplete.
To view the certificate or any certificate in the trust chain, click Show Certificate available in that particular certificate section. Click Back to Web Server Certificates to return to the Web Server Certificates page.
Show Certificate
From the Web Server Certificates page, click Actions menu ( ) > Show Certificate to view the cluster certificate.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Support Toolbox Overview

Update Certificate
The Update Certificate option allows you to update the cluster certificates. Perform the following steps to update the certificate:
1. From the Web Server Certificates tab, select Actions menu ( ) > Update Certificate. The Update Certificate pop-up appears.
2. Click Select File under Cluster Web Server Certificate, browse to the file location, and select the cluster certificate file.
3. Click Select File under Private Key, browse to the file location, and select the private key file.
4. Choose one of the following options to update the certificate: l Update & Restart Later - Updates the certificate once you restart the cluster later. l Update & Restart Now - Updates the certificate immediately. A Restart Services pop-up appears to confirm the restart of the cluster services. Enter YES in the pop-up and click Proceed to restart the cluster immediately.
Support Toolbox Overview
The Support Toolbox is a utility provided by Cohesity that assists you with various support and maintenance tasks on Cohesity clusters. The key features of the Support Toolbox are as follows:
l Health Checks: The toolbox can run various health checks to diagnose issues within the cluster. For instance, it can check network node reachability and other critical parameters before an upgrade.
l Diagnostics: It provides tools for diagnosing and troubleshooting issues within the cluster, helping you to identify and resolve problems quickly.
l Reporting: The toolbox can generate reports on the health and status of the cluster, which can be useful for both support and maintenance purposes.
You can use Support Toolbox using one of the following options:
l CLI l Siren Web UI
Access Support Toolbox from CLI
To use Support Toolbox through CLI, you must download the Support Toolbox from the Cohesity downloads portal and then install it on one of the nodes of the cluster. This version of the Support Toolbox is supported on the Cohesity 6.8.1 and above versions.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Support Toolbox Overview

Prerequisites Before you can install the Support Toolbox to your Cohesity cluster, you must enable Host shell access. To enable host shell access:
1. Log on to the node's secured shell using the support user: $ ssh support@<node_IP>
Where node_IP is the IP address of the node in your Cohesity cluster. 2. Log on to the iris_cli and generate a support token using the following command:
$ iris_cli support host-access-token
By default, the support token is only valid for an hour. You can extend the support token validity for up to 12 hours using the following command: $ iris_cli support host-access-token validity-in-hours=12
3. Obtain the Cohesity cluster information using the following command: $ iris_cli cluster info
4. Share the following details with Cohesity Support to generate an access code: l Support Token l Cluster ID l Cohesity Software Version l The number of hours you require the host shell access
5. After you receive the access code with Cohesity Support, enable host shell access using the following command in iris_cli: $ iris_cli support host-access ssh-enable=true
access-code=<access_code>
Where access_code is the access code you received from Cohesity Support. Ensure you enable host shell access before the support access token you generated in Step 2 expires. 6. Access the host shell of the node on port 2222 using the support user. Use the following command: $ ssh support@<node_IP> -p 2222

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Support Toolbox Overview

Note: Sudo access is disabled by default. For support channel access, you need to enable sudo access for the support user to the host shell using the following command:
$ iris_cli user linux-sudo-access enable=true duration-in-hours=12
Install Support Toolbox Perform the following steps to download and install the Support Toolbox:
1. Go to the Cohesity download page, and select Cohesity Tools tab. 2. Select the fast link for support-toolbox-installer and download to your local computer. 3. Use WinSCP or SCP command to upload the support-toolbox-installer file from your
local computer to the Cohesity node. 4. SSH to the Cohesity node where you uploaded the package and navigate to the folder
where the package was uploaded to. 5. Unpack the tar file:
tar -xzvf support-toolbox-installer.tgz
The following files will be present in the package. l st-utilities-20241024-aff631b3.x86_64.rpm l Toolbox utilities l st-signatures-20241024-aff631b3.x86_64.rpm l Toolbox health checks l st-brigidServer-20241024-aff631b3.x86_64.rpm l Backend API Server l st-dart-20241024-aff631b3.x86_64.rpm l Detect and resolve tool l st-upgradeSignatures-20241024-aff631b3.x86_64.rpm l Pre and post upgrade checks l st-framework-3.1.0-20240731-cfdadf52.x86_64.rpm l Framework package l st-sirenui-2.0.0-cfdadf52.x86_64.rpm l Siren UI upgrade package
6. Install the package by running the following command: ./install

Support Toolbox CLI Execution Options
The Support Toolbox uses its command-line interface, hc_cli to perform health checks and diagnostics on Cohesity clusters. You can run the health checks by logging into one of the Cohesity cluster nodes. The Support Toolbox supports the following CLI execution options with hc_cli:
l hc_cli run l hc_cli show l hc_cli debug l hc_cli version

Available Service Health Checks

Important: Cohesity continuously develops and refines this tool. While these tests are set for release on X date, they may be updated and improved over time with subsequent upgrade packages.
hc_cli run
The hc_cli run command executes all available health checks for all the modules on the Cohesity cluster, across all nodes. The modules on the Cohesity cluster are as follows:
l Services l Thirdparty l Backup l Vendor l Software l Networking l Hardware l Archival l Performance l Fingerprint l Upgrade l Patch
Services
This module verifies the health of all Cohesity services and checks that best practices were adhered to during the cluster configuration process. If required, you can run the following command to perform only the health check of the services on the Cohesity cluster: hc_cli run -m services
Available Service Health Checks
Following are the health checks that will be performed for the Service module: l Alerts uptime check l Apollo uptime check l Athena uptime check l Bifrost Broker uptime check

Results
The Results page allows you to review the most recent health check results, as well as a limited history of past runs. You can:
l Sort results (ascending or descending) by Severity, Node Name, or Test Name. l Download the results in JSON format to attach to a support case.
Result Categories
Health check results are organized into the following categories: l Passed - No failures detected. l Warning - An issue was found, but it has not reached a full failure state. Consider it an early indication of a potential failure. l Fail - The test has failed and remediation is required. l Skip - The test is irrelevant to the current platform, hardware, or codebase. l Error - The test itself encountered an error.
Severity Levels
Each test is assigned a severity level from 1 (Imminently Critical) to 4 (Informational). A Severity 1 Failure is the most urgent and must be addressed immediately. A Severity 4 Failure is the least critical and primarily informational.
Result Details
Expanding an individual test result displays the following details: Result - Human-readable description of the issue. Test Name - The command or script executed. State - The outcome of the test (Pass, Fail, or Warning). Severity - The criticality of the issue, from 1 (Most Critical) to 4 (Least Critical). Node IP - IP address of the reporting node. Node ID - Cohesity Cluster Config ID of the reporting node. Node Name - Hostname of the reporting node. Test KB Link - Link to a Cohesity Support KB article explaining the test and possible resolutions.

Environment Setup
This section provides information about setting up environments that interface with the Cohesity cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Environment Setup

Backup Manager Service Replica
A Cohesity multi-node cluster consists of a primary instance of the Backup Manager Service. The Backup Manager Service is responsible for handling all the requests from the Cohesity and APIs. A multi-node cluster environment with a large amount of data increases the load on the primary instance of the Backup Manager Service. Heavy workloads on the primary instance of the Backup Manager Service increase the response time of Cohesity and API calls. Enabling the Backup Manager Service Replica allows the primary instance of the Backup Manager Service to serve a high volume of traffic. Each Cohesity cluster can have only one Backup Manager Service Replica. Benefits of enabling Backup Manager Service Replica on a multi-node Cohesity cluster are:
l Offloads the read requests on the primary instance of the Backup Manager Service.
l Improves performance of Cohesity.
l Lower API latency.
Cohesity recommends enabling Backup Manager Service Replica on a multi-node cluster only.
Note: Backup Manager Service Replica reads the primary instance of the Backup Manager Service once in 15 seconds.

Ensure Adequate Privileges for Cohesity on the Source
The Cohesity cluster must perform various actions on the source. For the Cohesity cluster to perform these actions, the user specified to connect to the source (the one used to register the source) must have adequate privileges. For information about each source type, refer to the appropriate section:
l VMware vCenter l Standalone ESXi l Microsoft Hyper-V l vCloud Director l Nutanix Acropolis l NetApp l Dell EMC Isilon l Storage Snapshot Integration l Active Directory

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Environment Setup

l Linux Servers l Windows Servers
Create a Role with Necessary vCenter Server Privileges
The Cohesity cluster performs various VMware actions such as creating VMware snapshots, restoring VMware snapshots to ESXi hosts using vSphere Storage vMotion and creating new VMs by mounting the new VMDKs. For the Cohesity cluster to have adequate vCenter server privileges, the VirtualCenter user specified to connect to the source (vCenter Server ) must have the role privileges listed in Role Privileges for vCenter Server and that VirtualCenter user must be associated with vCenter objects that the Cohesity cluster interfaces with.
Note: By default, the VMware Consolidated Backup user (sample) role does not have adequate privileges for the VMware activities performed by the Cohesity cluster.
Create a Role with adequate vCenter Server Privileges
1. Using the vSphere Web Client, log in to the vCenter server that contains the VM to protect.
2. Create a new role. 3. Select the appropriate privileges for the new role as listed below. 4. Assign this role to the vCenter users that will access the Cohesity cluster. Assign this
role to users at the top vCenter object level and enable Propagate to children check box. 5. When registering a source on the Cohesity cluster, specify a VirtualCenter user assigned to a role with the required Cohesity privileges (defined below).
For more information on VMware vCenter permissions, refer the knowledge base article, Required Cohesity Permissions for VMware vCenter Environments.

l *restoreFilesUtil.exe (the * represents the variable task ID used as a file name prefix)

Access Cohesity Host OS
You can access the host OS on a node through the Intelligent Platform Management Interface (IPMI) remote console and Secure Shell by using cohesity_console and support user accounts respectively. Cohesity restricts the access to host OS through multi-layer of security that requires login credentials, and a challenge and response workflow.
About Challenge and Response Text
A challenge is an alphanumeric text that is displayed after you attempt to log in to the Cohesity host OS with your credentials through an IPMI remote console or a VE node's console. The challenge appears in the following format. -----Challenge String------<Alphanumeric_Value> -----Challenge String End-------

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 4: Cluster Administration

Hardware Replacement

This challenge is an 81-character text. It is valid for 60 minutes if you have accessed the Cohesity Platform through an IPMI console. To proceed further, you have to copy this challenge and share it with Cohesity Support. The Support team verifies the request and shares a 16-character alphanumeric response. On the IPMI remote console or the Secure Shell, a prefix is also displayed along with the challenge. The prefix should be combined with the response you have received from the Cohesity Support team to generate the login password and give you access to the host OS.
Note: The prefix should not be shared with Cohesity.

Access Host OS through IPMI remote console
Follow the steps below to access the host OS on a node via IPMI.
1. Create a support ticket to access the host OS. For more information, see Cohesity Support.
2. Launch your preferred IPMI utility tool IPMI remote console.
3. Enter the IP address of the node with the required command. For more information on using Secure Shell and IPMI remote console, see Using the Secure Shell and Using the Cohesity CLI.
The message Welcome to Cohesity OS! is displayed with details about accessing the host OS. Towards the end of the message, a challenge text is displayed in the format mentioned in the About Challenge and Response Text topic.
4. Copy the challenge text and share it with Cohesity Support through the support ticket.
5. After receiving the challenge, Cohesity Support verifies the request and shares the response text.
6. Enter the Prefix followed by the response text from Cohesity Support together as the password.
The console should now display a live session to the host OS on the node.

Hardware Replacement
Hardware replacement procedures (PDFs) are available at: Hardware Universe.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 5: FortKnox Self-Managed
FortKnox Self-Managed enables you to vault a copy of your backup data in a securely isolated Cohesity cluster using pull based method. It allows you to maintain an isolated, immutable copy of your data within your own self-managed infrastructure. This also ensures protection against cyber threats or primary cluster failures while enabling full control, security, and compliance over the vaulted data.
Key Concepts
Vault Cluster
A vault cluster stores another copy of data from the Cohesity cluster and recovers data to the original or a new location. You can convert a Cohesity cluster into a vault cluster to vault the data. The vault cluster provides isolated copy, immutable, WORM (Write Once, Read Many) storage, ensuring protection against unauthorized modifications, deletions or a cyber event.
Air Gapping
The Cohesity vault cluster operates on a pull-based model, leveraging outbound-only connections from an isolated network and ensuring no unauthorized external access. Connections are strictly established during designated vaulting windows, reinforcing airgapped data protection.
Storage Immutability & WORM Support
The vaulted data is stored with Write Once, Read Many (WORM), ensuring immutability and protection against unauthorized modifications or deletions.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 5: FortKnox Self-Managed

Supported Workloads

Quorum-Based Access Control
Helios Self-Managed, running within the secure Vault network, enforces quorum control, requiring multiple approvals for any critical vault operations, enhancing security and governance.
Multi-Tenancy Support
FortKnox Self-Managed supports multi-tenancy, allowing the service provider to manage the mapping of storage domains and vaulting windows for the tenants in a secure infrastructure.
Low Recovery Time Objective (RTO)
FortKnox Self-Managed is optimized for fast data recovery by maintaining a local copy within your premises, minimizing downtime in the event of a cyber-attack.
Vaulting Window
The Vaulting Window in FortKnox Self-Managed is an air-gapping mechanism that defines when the vault cluster can connect to the primary cluster. During the configured time window, connections are opened to pull data. Once the window closes, connections are dropped and active jobs are paused. These jobs automatically resume when the window opens again.
Supported Workloads
FortKnox Self-Managed supports the vaulting workflow for all workloads that are currently qualified for the Replication workflow. The workloads listed in the table below have been qualified for vaulting, while qualification for the remaining workloads is in progress. This list will be updated periodically as additional workloads are qualified.
Qualified Workload Name
VMware ESXi VM Servers
VMware vCloud Director
Physical Files

Get Started
The following topics provide guidance that helps you to get started with FortKnox SelfManaged.
Prerequisites
Ensure the following prerequisites are met before enabling FortKnox Self-Managed: l Encrypt Storage Domains l Enable Cluster Level Encryption l Enable Node to Node Encryption l Configure Firewall l Enable MFA l Disable Archival and Replication l Disable Support Channel

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 5: FortKnox Self-Managed

Get Started

Encrypt Storage Domains Storage Domains must be encryption enabled. Delete the unencrypted storage domains before converting the cluster to the vault cluster. Encryption can be enabled only when you are creating the Storage Domain. Once the Storage Domain is created, the options to enable encryption or modify its encryption settings are disabled in the Cohesity cluster. To create a storage domain and enable encryption, see Create or Edit Storage Domains. Enable Cluster Level Encryption Enable the software encryption at the cluster level to convert the cluster to vault cluster.
Note: Cluster-level encryption can be enabled only during the cluster creation, and it cannot be disabled or modified later.
To enable the encryption, 1. Navigate to Settings > Summary and click Configure. 2. Turn on the Encryption toggle. 3. Scroll down to the end of the page and click Save.
Note: Once encryption is enabled for a cluster, it cannot be disabled. Additionally, any storage domains created without encryption before cluster-level encryption was enabled must be deleted for this pre-requisite to succeed.
Enable Node to Node Encryption Enable Node-to-node encryption for all services. Node-to-node encryption is enabled by default starting from, 7.1.X and later for Physical Clusters For Clusters upgraded from earlier versions, run the following command to enable node-tonode encryption manually, $ iris_cli cluster tpenc enable-encryption=true After enabling, run the following command to restart all services to stabilize the cluster, $ iris_cli cluster restart-services all-services=true Configure Firewall You need to configure firewall, before converting a Cohesity cluster to a vault cluster. To configure the firewall:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 5: FortKnox Self-Managed

Get Started

1. Navigate to Settings > Networking and select the Firewall tab.
2. Click edit icon ( ) to edit the incoming firewall rules. 3. Select Allow action for Management. 4. Select Deny action for all other applications.
1. To deny SSH, users must manually select each interface group individually from the drop-down when configuring the deny rule.
2. To deny other applications, no selection is required from the drop-down, the rule automatically applies to all interface groups by default.
5. After configuring the firewall to deny all firewall rules except management, follow these steps to add a single trusted IP address to the Management firewall rule to enforce least security measure. 1. Select Custom IP/Subnet from the Source drop-down menu. 2. Enter any one IP address to access the vault cluster.
Important: Deny action should be set for all applications other than the Management inbound traffic.
Manage Firewall Ports

The Refresh API Key option allows the vault administrators to re-establish communication between paired clusters when API keys expire. Prevent Duplicate Cluster Pairing
FortKnox Self-Managed now validates cluster registrations during pairing and blocks any attempt to pair a cluster that is already registered as a remote or vault-paired cluster. A clear error message is displayed when a duplicate pairing is attempted, and the operation does not proceed. This validation prevents accidental duplicate registrations in environments where the same cluster may be visible under multiple roles. Error Behavior
l The pairing operation is blocked before any changes are made. l An error message is displayed indicating that the cluster has already been registered. l To pair the cluster in a new role, remove the existing pairing or registration first, then
initiate the new pairing.
Note: This validation applies to all pairing attempts, including attempts to register the same cluster as both a remote cluster and a vault-paired cluster.

Create Protection Policy for Vault Cluster from Primary Cluster

1. On the primary cluster, navigate to Data Protection > Policies. 2. Click Create Policy located at the top right of the page. 3. Policy Name: Specify a protection policy name. The name can contain the
alphanumerics, underscores, hyphens, periods, and spaces. This field is required and can be changed later. 4. Specify when backups are captured:
1. Backup every xx: Specify the minutes, hours, weeks, months, or years to set the frequency for how often backups are captured by the Protection Group. This defines the protection schedule for capturing backups. The policy schedule can be configured to run on specific days. From the Every drop-down, select Week and in the On field, select the days of the week you want to run the backup. For example, you can schedule a backup to run on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, and not on Tuesday and Thursday. The policy schedule can be configured to run on specific dates as well (calendarbased scheduling). From the Every drop-down, select Month, and in the On field, select the Date. You can then choose the date of the month you want to run the backup. For example, you can schedule a backup to run on the 5th of every month.
5. Under Primary Copy, specify the following: 1. Keep On: Select Local from the drop-down to keep the primary copy data on the Cohesity cluster. If you are selecting any external targets, then this policy can be only used for performing CloudArchive Direct wherein the primary copy of the data is stored on the external targets. For more information, see CloudArchive Direct. 2. Retain for: Specify how many days, weeks, months, or years backups are retained on the Cohesity cluster before they are deleted. 1. The Retain option can be set to a maximum value of 365000. 2. Retentions at 7-day boundaries turn into weeks. 3. Lock: Specify how many days, weeks, months, or years the retained log backups should be locked. You cannot delete the snapshots during the specified period.
Note: This option is available only if you have enabled the DataLock option at the policy level.
6. Click More Options to configure the additional policy settings.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 5: FortKnox Self-Managed

Create Protection Policy for Vault Cluster from Primary Cluster

7. DataLock: Toggle on to lock the policy and any snapshots that belong to Protection Groups associated with the policy. DataLock is typically used for compliance and regulatory purposes. For more information, see DataLock. If you have enabled the DataLock option at the policy level, then you have the option to lock the backup retained on the Cohesity cluster. In the Lock option field available in the Primary Copy pane, specify how many days, weeks, months, or years the retained backups must be locked. You cannot delete the snapshots during the specified lock period.
8. Select Add Vault to add the vault cluster for the backups to the protection policy. Specify the following: 1. Transfer to: Select the Vault cluster from the dropdown menu to transfer the data from the source cluster. 2. Every: Specify the frequency of data transfer to the vault. 3. Retain for: Specify the duration of the vaulted copy to be retained on the vault cluster. The default minimum retention is set to the primary copy retention value. The vault retention value can be greater than or equal to the primary copy retention.
Note: Data transferred from the source cluster to the vault cluster is automatically locked using DataLock. This lock is permanently applied to vaulted snapshots, cannot be disabled, and remains active throughout the retention period. DataLock ensures immutability and compliance by preventing any modification or deletion of data during its lifecycle in the vault cluster.
9. Optional: Enable Transfer only successful runs if required. Transfer only successful runs: With this option, the data from the source cluster is transferred to the vault cluster only after the successful protection run.
10. If required, you can add additional policy settings. For more information, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.

Flexible Vault Retention Configuration
The vault retention period in a protection policy can now be set to any value, including a value lower than the primary backup retention. Previously, the system enforced a minimum retention equal to the primary copy retention and prevented saving the policy if the vault retention was set lower. This change supports use cases where a shorter retention period is appropriate for vaulted copies, such as cost optimization or regulatory requirements that call for a reduced vault retention independent of the primary backup timeline.
Note: Removing the minimum retention restriction does not affect DataLock. Data transferred to the vault cluster is automatically locked and cannot be modified or deleted during the retention period.
Set Vault Retention in a Protection Policy To configure vault retention during policy creation:
1. On the primary cluster, navigate to Data Protection > Policies and click Create Policy.
2. Click Add Vault to add the vault cluster to the policy. 3. In the Retain for field under the vault configuration, specify the desired retention
period.
Note: You can now enter a value lower than the primary copy retention.
4. Complete the remaining policy settings and click Create.
Exclude Paired Clusters from Replication Targets
When creating a protection policy on the vault cluster, clusters that are already paired to the vault cluster as primary clusters are no longer displayed in the replication target dropdown. Only clusters registered as independent remote clusters appear in the list. Previously, vault-paired primary clusters appeared in the same replication target list as independent remote clusters, which could lead to unintended selection and misconfiguration. To view the paired clusters that are excluded from replication targets:
1. On the vault cluster, navigate to Data Protection > Policies and click Create Policy.
2. Under the replication configuration, click Replicate to drop down and select Remote Cluster.

Supported Vaulting and Recovery Configurations
FortKnox Self-Managed supports multiple configurations for both vaulting and recovery workflows to enable deployment flexibility. Configuration 1 The primary cluster vaults data to a designated vault cluster. All recovery operations are performed directly from the vault cluster.

To vault the backup data directly from the primary cluster to the vault cluster:
1. From the vault cluster, initiate pairing with the primary cluster. 2. On the primary cluster,
1. Create a vaulting policy. For more information, see Vaulting Policy. 2. Configure a protection job and assign the vaulting policy to it. For more
information, see Protection Group.
Configuration 2
The primary cluster vaults data to a designated vault cluster. The vault cluster then performs policy-based replication to a secondary Cohesity cluster, which is used for

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 5: FortKnox Self-Managed

Recover from Vault Cluster

recovery operations. This workflow is supported through APIs. Data protection policies configured on the primary cluster control both vaulting and replication.

To vault and recover the backup data:
1. From the vault cluster, initiate remote cluster pairing with the secondary Cohesity cluster.
2. On the primary cluster, 1. Use the API to configure a cascading policy that vaults the data to the vault cluster and then replicates from the vault cluster to the secondary Cohesity cluster. 2. Provide the cluster ID and name for both the vault cluster and the secondary Cohesity cluster in the cascading policy. 3. Create and assign a protection job that uses this cascading policy.
For more information, see Cascaded Replication, Archival, and Vaulting Policy.
Configuration 3
The Primary cluster vaults data to a designated vault cluster. When recovery is needed, snapshots are manually replicated from the vault cluster to a secondary Cohesity cluster. This secondary cluster is used to perform recovery operations.

To perform just-in-time replication of snapshots to secondary Cohesity cluster:

Clean Room Recovery using FortKnox Self-Managed
FortKnox Self-Managed enables you to vault a copy of your backup data in a securely isolated Cohesity cluster within your own infrastructure. The Clean Room Recovery workflow for FortKnox Self-Managed provides a secure mechanism to recover data

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 5: FortKnox Self-Managed

Clean Room Recovery using FortKnox Self-Managed

Snapshots and the Digital Jump Bag from the Vault Cohesity to an Isolated Clean Room environment using Just-In-Time replication, governed by Quorum approval. The vault cluster does not accept any inbound connection from the Clean Room environment during this process.
Digital Jump Bag
A Digital Jump Bag is a secure software repository that stores the critical assets you need to rebuild your infrastructure during a cyberattack, including OS images, software packages, configuration files, and documentation templates for dial-tone workloads such as Active Directory, DNS, security tools, contact lists, and recovery procedures. With Cohesity, you create a Digital Jump Bag using a SmartFiles View with data lock and object lock enabled and secure it using policy-based replication and FortKnox vaulting so that a trusted, immutable copy is always available when you need it.
Goals
l Securely recover the Digital Jump Bag and data Snapshots from the FortKnox Vault Cluster to the Isolated Clean Room environment.
l Maintain WORM and immutability SLAs for all backup data stored in the FortKnox Vault Cluster throughout the recovery process.
l Ensure no inbound communication is established into the FortKnox Vault Cluster during the CyberAttack Recovery process.
Non-Goals
l Setting up the Clean Room environment, network isolation, or micro-segmentation configuration.
l Performing forensic analysis on the data recovered from the vault cluster to the Clean Room.
l Recovering sanitized data from the Clean Room to an isolated Sandbox environment after forensic analysis is complete.
l Restoring data from the Sandbox environment to the Production environment, or reconfiguring primary backup, replication, and vaulting.
Assumptions
l The Digital Jump Bag, which contains essential OS images, configuration templates, and installers, is stored in a SmartFiles View on the Primary Cohesity Cluster and vaulted to the FortKnox Self-Managed Vault Cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 5: FortKnox Self-Managed

Clean Room Recovery using FortKnox Self-Managed

l All Primary Cohesity clusters are inaccessible. The FortKnox Vault Cluster is the sole source for data Snapshots and the Digital Jump Bag during Clean Room Recovery.
l Your Active Directory servers and all online identity providers are compromised and cannot be trusted as part of the attack.
Note: The Intermediate Cluster must reside in a dedicated, isolated network segment (for example, a VLAN with firewall rules) during the replication phase. This prevents lateral movement and preserves the integrity of the FortKnox Vault Cluster.

Prerequisites
Ensure the following are configured before a cyber-recovery event occurs. All prerequisite tasks must be completed before a cyber-attack occurs. These tasks cannot be performed after primary clusters become inaccessible.
l Set Up a Quorum Group in Helios Self-Managed l Configure Vault Pairing l Set Up the Digital Jump Bag l Configure Vaulting to the FortKnox Vault Cluster
Set Up a Quorum Group in Helios Self-Managed
In Helios Self-Managed, deployed in the isolated Vault network, set up a Quorum Group for the following Cluster Operation: Update runs for a Protection Group on the FortKnox Vault Cluster. For more information, see Set Up a Quorum Group.
Configure Vault Pairing
Set up Vault pairing between the Primary Cluster and the FortKnox Vault Cluster. For more information, see Pair Primary Cluster to Vault cluster.
Set Up the Digital Jump Bag
To set up the Digital Jump Bag: 1. Create a SmartFiles View on the Primary Cohesity Cluster. 2. Copy all Digital Jump Bag contents (OS images, configuration templates, and installers) into the View. 3. Configure a local backup policy for the View.

Clean Room Recovery using FortKnox Self-Managed

Configure Vaulting to the FortKnox Vault Cluster
To configure vaulting: 1. Create a protection policy that targets the FortKnox Vault Cluster. 2. Create Protection Groups for both the data Snapshots and the Digital Jump Bag SmartFiles View, and assign the vaulting policy to each.
For more information, see Create a Protection Group on Primary Cluster.
Recovering to the Clean Room
Complete the following steps in order during a cyber-attack recovery event: l Close the Vaulting Window on the FortKnox Vault Cluster l Pair the Intermediate Cluster to the FortKnox Vault Cluster l Trigger Just-In-Time Replication l Un-pair the Intermediate Cluster and Recover Data Snapshots
Close the Vaulting Window on the FortKnox Vault Cluster
Close the Vaulting Window to stop all active and scheduled vaulting from Primary Clusters to the Vault Cluster. This prevents any compromised cluster from writing to the Vault Cluster during the recovery process. To close the Vaulting Window:
1. On the FortKnox Vault Cluster, navigate to Vault > Paired Clusters. 2. Click the action icon next to the paired Primary Cluster and select Edit Pairing. 3. Set the Vaulting Window to Closed and click Save. 4. Repeat for all paired Primary Clusters.
Note: Closing the Vaulting Window drops active vaulting connections and pauses in-progress jobs. Any paused jobs will not resume because the window remains closed.
Pair the Intermediate Cluster to the FortKnox Vault Cluster
Pair a new Cohesity cluster to the FortKnox Vault Cluster. This Intermediate Cluster serves as the staging target for all data and is used for recovery into the Clean Room environment. To pair the Intermediate Cluster:
1. On the FortKnox Vault Cluster, navigate to Vault > Paired Clusters and click Pair Cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 5: FortKnox Self-Managed

Clean Room Recovery using FortKnox Self-Managed

2. Enter the Virtual IPs or Node IP addresses of the Intermediate Cluster in the VIP or Node IP Addresses field.
3. Enter the username and password of a user with the FortKnox Self-Managed Vault Admin role on the Intermediate Cluster.
4. Select the required Interface Group and click Continue: Storage Domain Pairing. 5. Select the source and destination storage domains for the pairing. 6. Click Complete Pairing.
Note: Do not configure a Vaulting Window for this pairing. The Intermediate Cluster connection is used for Just-In-Time replication only and should not receive recurring vaulting jobs.
Trigger Just-In-Time Replication
Initiate a one-time, Quorum-gated replication of the required data Snapshots and the Digital Jump Bag from the FortKnox Vault Cluster to the Intermediate Cluster.
Note: Just-In-Time replication is triggered through the API only. This operation is not available from the Cohesity UI.
To trigger Just-In-Time replication: 1. Using the Cohesity API, send an Update Protection Group Run request for the Protection Groups containing the desired data Snapshots, targeted at the Intermediate Cluster. 2. Send a second Update Protection Group Run request for the Digital Jump Bag SmartFiles View Protection Group, targeted at the Intermediate Cluster. 3. A Quorum request is generated automatically for each operation. 4. Notify the designated Quorum Group members to review and approve each request in Helios Self-Managed. 5. After Quorum approval, monitor the replication jobs until they complete. 6. Verify that all required Snapshots and the Digital Jump Bag are present on the Intermediate Cluster.
Un-pair the Intermediate Cluster and Recover Data Snapshots
After replication is complete, un-pair the Intermediate Cluster from the FortKnox Vault Cluster to sever all network connections, connect it to the Clean Room environment, and recover the required data Snapshots to the Recovery Targets. To un-pair the Intermediate Cluster, bootstrap the Clean Room environment, and recover data Snapshots:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 5: FortKnox Self-Managed

Vaulting Scenario for Organizations

1. On the FortKnox Vault Cluster, navigate to Vault > Paired Clusters. 2. Click the action icon next to the Intermediate Cluster and select Unpair. 3. Confirm the unpairing when prompted. 4. Verify that the Intermediate Cluster no longer appears in the Paired Clusters list.
Important: Do not connect the Intermediate Cluster to the Clean Room environment until the unpairing is confirmed. Connecting before unpairing could expose the Vault Cluster's network path to the Clean Room environment.
5. Connect the Intermediate Cluster to the Clean Room network. 6. Mount the replicated Digital Jump Bag SmartFiles View on the Intermediate Cluster. 7. Deploy the required OS images, apply configuration templates, and install the
required software from the Digital Jump Bag to bootstrap the Clean Room environment. 8. Trigger the recovery of the desired data Snapshots from the Intermediate Cluster, specifying the Recovery Targets in the Clean Room environment. 9. Monitor the recovery job until it completes and verify that all data Snapshots are available on the specified Recovery Targets.
Note: After completing recovery, all data Snapshots and the Digital Jump Bag are available in the Clean Room environment, with the FortKnox Vault Cluster remaining fully isolated and its WORM data intact. Proceed with forensic analysis on the recovered data.

Considerations

Vaulting Window
Cohesity limits the number of parallel tasks using a slot allocation algorithm. With the current implementation, vault replication slots are not released if vaulting does not finish before the vaulting window closes. The paused vaulting task holds the slot until the vaulting window opens again. This can lead to slot starvation for new vaulting or regular replication tasks, preventing them from running, and impacting cluster scalability. As a workaround, Cohesity recommends that the vaulting window duration be long enough to allow vaulting to complete.
Agent-Based Recovery from Vault Cluster
To recover agented data sources from a vault cluster, perform a manual registration. Follow the procedure documented in Generate and Upload Cluster Certificates to register the source with the vault. This process enables successful recovery without requiring a Cohesity Agent reinstallation.
Inbound Connection Requirements for Certain Recoveries
Certain recovery operations require the recovery target to establish inbound connections to the vault cluster. Modify firewall configurations to allow the required inbound traffic.
Important: l For vCenter VM recoveries, set the inbound NFS firewall rule to Allow in the vault cluster firewall settings. l For MongoDB recoveries, set the inbound Data Protection firewall rule to Allow in the vault cluster firewall settings.

Node Addition and Removal
When a new node added or the existing node removed from the primary cluster, make sure to update the vault pairing configuration. To update the pairing configuration:
1. On the vault cluster, navigate to Vault > Paired Clusters.
2. Click the Actions menu ( ) next to the paired cluster and select Edit. 3. Add/Remove the Node IP/VIP that was added/removed from the primary cluster. 4. Complete the cluster pairing procedure.

Best Practices

If a node is removed from the vault cluster, the vaulting process will get stuck and will need a restart of services on the primary cluster. Contact Cohesity Support for details.
Best Practices
This page outlines best practices for deploying and managing a Cohesity vault, focusing on physical and logical isolation, access control, firewall configuration, foundational services, and recovery strategies. Refer to the Prerequisites before configuring FortKnox SelfManaged.
Vault Deployment

Follow these best practices when deploying the vault. Physical Isolation
l Deploy the vault in a physically isolated environment, separate from production systems.
l Use dedicated, locked cages or racks to enhance physical security. l Avoid sharing physical hardware with production infrastructure. Logical Isolation l Place the vault in an isolated network protected by a firewall. l Use separate network interfaces for management and vaulting traffic to prevent
cross-contamination.
Vault Access and Management
l Limit access to a minimal number of authorized users. l Enforce Least Privilege Access and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). l Allow management access only via a secure jump host within the isolated network.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 5: FortKnox Self-Managed

Best Practices

l Physically disconnect IPMI ports to prevent out-of-band access. l Do not register the vault with Cohesity managed Helios.

Block all inbound traffic to the vault network except for controlled access to the jump host. Allow only the following outbound traffic from the vault:

Foundational Services
Do not share foundational services (e.g., NTP, DNS, AD/LDAP, MFA) between vault, production, and recovery zones.

Data Recovery Options
l While recovery directly from the vault is supported, it is not recommended. l Replicate data from the vault to a Cohesity cluster in a Trusted Recovery Zone. l Perform recovery from the Recovery Zone cluster back to production using one of the
approved recovery patterns.
