Frequently Asked Questions

Additional Best Practices
l Use physical clusters for all production vault deployments. l Avoid using the vault as a Primary backup cluster, even though it is technically
supported. l Implement quorum-based approval via Helios Self-Managed for critical operations
(e.g., recovery, firewall changes). l Use a dedicated Helios Self-Managed instance for vault operations.
Frequently Asked Questions
1. Can previously replicated data still be used for restore? Yes. Data replicated before switching to a vault remains fully available for restore operations. However, the cluster cannot be converted to a vault cluster unless storage domain encryption or software encryption at the cluster level is enabled.
2. Does existing replicated data expire? Yes. Replicated snapshots will expire according to their original retention policies.
3. Does transitioning to a vault policy or protection group require a new full backup? No. Once the replication cluster is converted to a vault target (removed as a replica and added as a vault target, and policies updated accordingly), the next vaulting run will transfer incremental data.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 5: FortKnox Self-Managed

Frequently Asked Questions

Note: Existing replicated snapshots are immutable if they were data-locked. If they were not data-locked, they are not immutable.
4. Are there version compatibility requirements between the primary backup cluster and FortKnox Self-Managed? Yes. The primary backup cluster must be running version 7.2.2_u2 or later to be compatible with FortKnox Self-Managed.
5. Does Proof of Concept (POC) require Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)? Yes. MFA is required. You can use either email-based MFA or an authenticator app for verification.
6. Can data be vaulted from a FortKnox Self-Managed cluster to FortKnox SaaS? No. Vaulting from FortKnox Self-Managed to FortKnox SaaS is not supported.
7. Can CloudArchive be used for workloads in a FortKnox Self-Managed cluster? No. CloudArchive is not supported for workloads in FortKnox Self-Managed clusters.
8. Can the vault cluster also be used as a replication target? No. The vault cluster cannot be used as a replication target.
9. Does Helios Self-Managed require managing the vault cluster? No. Helios Self-Managed is optional and needed only for quorum controls. Vault cluster does not support SaaS.
10. What are the requirements when converting a primary cluster to a vault cluster? Before converting a primary cluster to a vault cluster, 1. Enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for local users. 2. Encrypt either the entire cluster or all storage domains. 3. Enable node-to-node encryption across the cluster. 4. Configure the firewall to deny all traffic except for the "Application Management" rule. 5. Remove any active policies for replication or cloud archival. After conversion, you can change the firewall settings as they are no longer enforced.
11. Is Cloud Edition/NGCE supported as a FortKnox Self-Managed cluster? No. Cloud Edition/NGCE is not supported as a FortKnox Self-Managed cluster. For production deployments, any physical hardware supported for Cohesity DataProtect is also supported for FortKnox Self-Managed. For Proof of Concept (POC) purposes, Cohesity Virtual Edition can be used.

Chapter 6: Cohesity Data Cloud for NetBackup
Cohesity Data Cloud for NetBackup is Cohesity's unified data protection solution that modernizes NetBackup by bringing it onto a single, scalable Cohesity Data Platform. It simplifies operations by replacing fragmented architectures with a streamlined, hyper-converged design that delivers faster recovery, seamless upgrades, and uninterrupted protection.
With centralized management through Cohesity Helios and cyber resilience built in, Cohesity Data Cloud for NetBackup helps organizations protect mission-critical workloads while reducing complexity and operational overhead. The solution is designed to support long-term growth, security, and innovation with a consistent, future-ready data protection experience.
Data Cloud for NetBackup leverages Cohesity cluster to run NetBackup applications. You can manage Data Cloud for NetBackup clusters directly from Helios. For more information on managing Data Cloud for NetBackup clusters directly from Helios, see Manage Data Cloud for NetBackup Clusters from Helios.
Deployment Modes
When you set up a cluster, you choose one of two deployment modes. Your choice determines which services are installed on the cluster nodes and what steps are required during configuration.
l With media servers: Media server services are installed on the cluster nodes. The cluster is registered as a storage server with the NetBackup primary server during setup, and NetBackup assigns backup and restore jobs directly to the media servers running on the cluster. This mode follows the standard Data Cloud for NetBackup configuration workflow.
l Without media servers:Media server services are not installed on the cluster nodes. The cluster operates as a DirectIO storage target and uses external media servers that are registered with the NetBackup primary server. Storage server registration and logical storage unit creation are not performed during initial configuration.

Deployment Overview

Deployment Overview
Stage 2 - Assemble the nodes Carefully evaluate all the software and hardware requirements. The requirements cover high level areas such as power and cooling needs, networking infrastructure, and rack sizing, to more specific needs such as system requirements, IP addresses, storage, and security. It is critical that your IT environment meets all the required infrastructure needs to ensure a smoother deployment and operational experience. At a high level, deploying the cluster involves the following stages: Stage 1 - Verify the deployment requirements Assemble the supported hardware and mount the nodes on to a rack in your data center. Connect all the power and network cables as per the instructions provided. After setting up the target systems, procure the installation media and install the softtware on all the nodes. Stage 3 - Configure the NetBackup network Configure the NetBackup external primary server and media servers.
Note: This step has to be performed only if you have opted to build the cluster with media servers.
Stage 4 - Configure the cluster From a web browser, connect to one of the nodes using a public IP address and run the cluster configuration workflow to configure all the nodes into a cluster. During the cluster configuration, you will configure the infrastructure components as well as the core NetBackup services. Stage 5 - Sign in to the NetBackup UI Once the configuration is successful, you sign in to the NetBackup web UI and create protection plans and start protecting desired workloads. You can also monitor the infrastructure components and the general health of all the configured services.

Limitations

Network Requirements
You require a minimum of three nodes to configure a cluster. Verify the following cluster network requirements for a three-node cluster.
l Reserve IP addresses for the nodes in the cluster on a single subnet (the cluster subnet).
l Reserve two sets of virtual IP addresses (VIPs). One set should resolve to a single fully qualified domain name (FQDN) for the storage server. The other set should resolve to different FQDNs for media server containers.
Note: If you plan to deploy without media servers, only one set of VIPs (for the storage server FQDN) is required.
l Open firewall ports to allow the cluster to transmit and receive data and to allow communication between the client, primary server, and data servers on the cluster.
l Verify that the cluster subnet can communicate with the source's subnet. l Reserve high speed ports (one for each node) on one switch. Minimum of 10GbE
required. l Reserve high speed ports (one for each node) on another switch. Minimum of 10GbE
required. l Reserve IP addresses for the IPMI interfaces. Most hardware platforms require one IP
address for each node. All the IPMI IP addresses must be in the same subnet, either in the IPMI subnet or the cluster subnet. l Reserve 1GbE ports (one for each node) for the IPMI on a switch. l Enable multicast traffic on your network (required for Cohesity's auto-discovery function). l The cluster supports bonding mode 1 ( active-backup) and bonding mode 4 (LACP 802.3ad). By default, bonding mode 1 is configured on the cluster bond interfaces.
Limitations
Operational Considerations
l To successfully collect logs, initiate log collection using a job ID. When a job ID is used, the system automatically selects a resolvable host name and collects the logs successfully. When you initiate log collection without a job ID, you can select a media host and client host manually. For Data Cloud with NetBackup clusters, the cluster ID is

Manually adding media hosts or client hosts is not supported in this release. l Collecting specific debug logs is not supported for Data Cloud with NetBackup media servers.

DNS Servers Domain Name Search Domains

Specify a unique name for the cluster. Only alphanumeric characters and hyphens are allowed. A hyphen cannot be the first or last character. Length cannot exceed 32 characters. No other characters are allowed.

Deactivate Media Server

In the Deactivate Media Server window, type YES to confirm that you want to deactivate and select Deactivate.
Note: Deactivating the media server will prevent NetBackup from assigning new backup or restore jobs to it. Running jobs will continue until completion. Policies and schedules using this server may queue or be redirected based on availability. Existing data and configuration will not be affected.
The selected media server is deactivated.
Stop Media Server
To stop a media server: 1. Navigate to Summary > Services. 2. Locate the media server that you want to stop and click the Actions menu on the right side of the row. Click Stop. 3. In the Stop Media Server window, type YES to confirm that you want to stop and select Stop.
Note: Stopping the media server will immediately terminate all running backup and restore jobs on this server. Active jobs may fail and require manual retry. New jobs will not be processed until the server is started again. Connected clients may experience interruptions.
The selected media server is stopped.
Restart Media Server
To restart a media server: 1. Navigate to Summary > Services. 2. Locate the media server that you want to restart and click the Actions menu on the right side of the row. Click Restart.

Manage Storage Domains
From the Manage Storage Domains page, you can view, add and manage the storage domains that have been created on the cluster. A storage domain is a named storage location on a cluster. A storage domain defines the policy and frequency for deduplication among other configurations such as compression, erasure coding, and replication factor. A storage domain contains views. You can perform the following operations:
l Create Storage Domain l Delete Storage Domain l Edit Storage Domain

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 6: Cohesity Data Cloud for NetBackup

Manage Storage Domains

Create Storage Domain
To create a storage domain:
1. Navigate to Settings > Storage Management and select the Storage Domains tab.
2. Select Create Storage Domain located at the right side of the page. Fill all the required details in the Create Storage Domain window.
3. Storage Domain Name: Enter a name for the storage domain. 4. Authentication Provider: You can map the storage domain to an AD or LDAP
domain. Mapping to a specific domain means that users from only that domain have permission to view the storage domain's contents when accessing through SMB. By default, a storage domain is accessible to users from all joined domains. 5. Deduplication: To enable deduplication, turn it on. If deduplication is enabled, the cluster eliminates duplicate blocks of repeating data stored on the cluster thus reducing the amount of storage space needed to store data. Deduplication can be:
l Inline (Recommended): Deduplication occurs as the cluster saves blocks to the partition.
l Post Process: Deduplication occurs after the cluster writes data to the partition. 6. Compression: To enable compression, turn it on. If compression is enabled,the
cluster compresses all the data stored in the storage domain thus reducing the amount of storage space needed to store the data. If compression is on and then turned off later, the current data on the storage domain is not decompressed but any new data stored on the storage domain is not compressed. Compression can be:
l Inline (Recommended): Compression occurs as the cluster saves blocks to the partition.
l Post Process: Compression occurs after the cluster writes data to the partition.
Note: If both compression and inline deduplication are on, Cohesity recommends you turn Inline Compression on.
7. Encryption: To enable encryption for the storage domain, turn it on. This option is enabled only if cluster level encryption is not enabled.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 6: Cohesity Data Cloud for NetBackup

Manage Storage Domains

Note: Encryption can be enabled only when you are creating the storage domain. Once the storage domain is created, the options to enable encryption or modify its encryption settings are disabled in the cluster.

Note: If encryption is enabled at the cluster level, then data within the storage domains are also encrypted and this option is not enabled for each storage domain.

By default, Cohesity uses Internal KMS for encryption.

You can register an external KMS and select one of the following from the drop-down list:

l AWS

l KMIP Compliant

For more information, see External Key Management Service.

8. Expand More Options to see the list of additional settings.

9. Physical Quota & Alerts: Turn it on to set the total quota for the storage domain. Includes space on the cluster as well as cloud tier. The capacity must be a whole number.

Alert Threshold: Turn it on to trigger an alert when the storage domain reaches the specified threshold.

10. Default View Quota & Alerts: Turn it on to set a default logical capacity limit for the storage domain and set the capacity. Logical data is fully hydrated and expanded.

Alert Threshold: Turn it on to trigger an alert when the view reaches the specified threshold.

11. Fault Tolerance & Redundancy: Select the number of hard drive, node, chassis, or rack failures that can occur before a cluster health alert is triggered. The available choices are determined by the number of nodes, chassis, racks in the cluster. The cluster's global custom failure domain setting determines the failure domain (node, chassis or rack) and the number of failures tolerated at the storage domain level.

1D:1N

Tolerate failure of 1 drive or 1 node. The available options to select are RF2 or EC x:1.
Tolerate failure of 2 drives or at least 1 node. The available options to select include RF3 and EC x:2.

2D:1N

This option is available only if the Cluster has three or more nodes.

Cohesity will always make the best effort to place each EC stripe unit to be on separate nodes when sufficient nodes are available. Only

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 6: Cohesity Data Cloud for NetBackup

Manage Storage Domains

2D:2N

when sufficient nodes are not present the EC stripe units will be placed within the same node but on separate disks. Tolerate failure of 2 drives or 2 nodes. This setting is only available if there are at least four nodes. With this setting, the available options are RF3 or EC x:2. Cohesity will always try to place each EC stripe unit on separate nodes when sufficient nodes are available.
Note: You cannot change the fault tolerance setting to 2D:2N if the metadata usage is >=50% of the available storage.

Note: This Erasure Coding (EC) setting is not recommended for clusters with fewer than five nodes because the data cannot be healed after one node failure. Your data will be at risk until the failed node is replaced.

3D:1N 3D:2N

Tolerate failure of 3 drives or 1 node. This setting is only available if there are at least three nodes. With this setting, the available options are RF4, EC x:3, or EC x:4.
Tolerate failure of 3 drives or 2 nodes.
This setting is only available if there are at least seven nodes. With this setting, the available options are RF4, EC x:3, or EC x:4.

12. Erasure Coding: Turn it on for better fault tolerance and capacity utilization. You can also select an Erasure Coding setting from the drop-down list. The available choices are determined by the Fault Tolerance setting and the number of nodes, chassis, or racks in the cluster. The settings indicate the ratio of the data stripes to the code stripes, expressed as x:y. For example, 2:1, 2:2, 3:1, 3.2, 4:1, 4:2, 4:3, 5:1, 5:2, or 5.3.

13. Select Create.

Add Nodes to the Cluster

Add Nodes to the Cluster
Before you begin:
l Ensure connectivity to all the existing sources on the newly added nodes.
l VLAN virtual IPs need to be provisioned first before adding the nodes. Typically, one virtual IP per node should be provisioned in each VLAN. VLAN virtual IPs need not be added for the primary interface VLAN.
l If cluster usage is above 85%, Cohesity recommends adding additional nodes to the cluster.
To add nodes to the cluster:
1. Navigate to Settings > Summary and select the Nodes tab.
2. Select Add Node. The cluster looks for free nodes in the same subnet which are discoverable from the node from where add node option is being done to add to the cluster. The node list is displayed on the Dashboard.
3. Select the node(s) you want to add to the cluster. The cluster can accommodate a maximum of 8 nodes when adding them at the same time. Select Continue.
4. Configure the node IP addresses. Specify IP addresses for each of the new nodes. You can use first node's IP to auto-fill remaining IP and IPMI addresses. Select Continue.
5. (If you have opted to build the cluster with media servers) In clusters on which multiple VLANs are configured, add virtual IPs for the new node if the number of virtual IPs previously assigned to the VLAN is less than the total number of nodes currently in the cluster. This ensures better workload balancing. Add a media server VLAN IP and FQDN for the new node.
6. (If you have opted to build the cluster with media servers) Configure IP addresses and FQDN for each of the media servers. You can use the first node's IP to auto-fill the remaining media server IP addresses.
7. (If you have opted to build the cluster with media servers) Under Storage Server Registration, provide this cluster's credentials to add new media servers to the storage server already registered with the NetBackup Primary server.
8. Select Add. You can see the progress of the add node progress using alerts.
Note: If a node's software version is different from the cluster's software version, the node's software is automatically updated to the cluster's version when you add the node. The IPMI configuration is optional. You can configure IPMI after adding nodes to the cluster using the CLI or Dashboard.

The node addition continues in the background even if progress is no longer visible. If progress details disappear, do not retry the operation or attempt additional configuration actions. Wait for the operation to complete in the background.

Service Providers (SPs)
As a service provider, you can use the Cohesity cluster to provide storage-related, data backup, data management services, etc. to your customers. Cohesity Platform allows tenants to manage their organizations based on the privileges provided by you as a service provider. This allows organizations (tenants) to perform routine tasks without depending on you as the service provider. You can provide the following services as a service provider:
l Backup as a Service (BaaS) l Disaster Recovery as a Service (DRaaS) l Filer as a Service (FaaS)
For more information on solutions, see the following documents:
l Backup as a Service Solution Guide l Disaster Recovery as a Service (DRaaS) Solution Guide

Large Enterprises
Multitenancy is not just for service providers; it's also useful for large enterprises. Large enterprises can use multitenancy to isolate departments or business units as an individual tenant from each other for security and compliance reasons.

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Organization User Types

Organization User Types
In the Organization environment, we define the following user types for clarity of communication and understanding only. These user types may be different from jargon used elsewhere in the Cohesity documentation.
Note: The following user types are used in Cohesity's Organizations (multitenancy) environment. These user types are not defined in the Cohesity Dashboard (UI).

Service Provider Administrator
A service provider is a company that provides IT services to its customers using the Cohesity cluster. A service provider administrator is typically a user with the default Administrator role.
Note: Technically, the service provider administrator is the same as the Cluster administrator. We use the term service provider administrator in the context of the Organization feature, where the service provider manages multiple Organizations.

Organization Users
An Organization on the Cohesity cluster can have users and groups. An Organization user with the Admin privilege is called the Organization administrator and users without the Admin privilege are called Organization users.
Organization Administrator
An Organization administrator can manage its own Organization in a multitenant environment. The Organization administrator role and its privileges are defined by the service provider administrator. The Organization administrator can create an Organization user or group. However, the Organization administrator cannot create or modify roles.
Note: To add Active Directory as an Organization Admin, the AD domain's IP must be part of your assigned VLAN. Otherwise, please contact the Service Provider admin to add the AD domain to the cluster and assign it to your Organization. For Service Provider use cases, see Privileges for Service Provider Admin and Organization Admin.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Organizations Subfeatures

Organization Users
An Organization user or group is created by the Organization administrator or it can be assigned to the Organization by a service provider administrator. The Organization administrator can only assign the inherited roles to a new Organization user or group. The roles can be Viewer, Operator, or other custom roles.
Organizations Subfeatures
The following are some key subfeatures of the Organizations feature.
l A Service Provider Administrator can add Organizations and assign them the following Cohesity resources: l Storage Domain l View l AD, LDAP, SSO, or Keystone l Add Organization administrator, users, or groups l Objects l Policies and protection groups l VLAN(s)
l Organization users can log in to the Cohesity GUI for self-service access to their assets and services, in a manner that is securely isolated from other tenants. Clusterlevel administrative capabilities are not available to Organization users.
l Organization administrators can configure Role-Based Access Control to control what is visible to tenant users.
l For data protection, each Organization owns private sources, protection jobs.
Storage efficiency
l As a service provider, you can also isolate data in Organizations from each other logically by assigning each Organization a storage domain, which creates separate, independent deduplication domains and encryption keys.
l As a service provider, you can alternatively configure Organizations to use the same storage domain for storage efficiency, which acts as a single deduplication domain. However, access is still secure and limited to each Organization. For more information, see Infrastructure for Organizations.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Organizations Subfeatures

Network Isolation
l Service provider admins can isolate Organizations from each other by assigning VLAN.
l On each VLAN, service providers can assign cluster virtual IP addresses to each tenant.
l Alternatively, you can use Cohesity's Hybrid Extender to overcome IP address conflicts across the tenants. For more information, see Configure Network Settings for an Organization and Hybrid Extender
Impersonate Organizations
l Service providers can impersonate Organizations to preview and verify what their Organization administrator sees and helps Organizations diagnose and debug issues. l The Service provider administrator acquires tenant administrator privileges during impersonation. l The Service provider operator acquires tenant operator privileges during impersonation. l Service provider viewers will get tenant viewer privileges during impersonation.
l All actions performed during impersonation are audit-logged for security reasons. The audit logs are available to both service providers and Organizations. For more information. For more information, see Impersonate an Organization.
Backup and Restore
Cohesity provides efficient backup and restore workflows for service providers and Organizations and helps in managing large environments with multiple workloads using a single pane of glass. For more information, see Data Protection for Organizations.
Encryption
l Cohesity has a built-in key manager that generates keys and stores them internally on the SSDs in encrypted form.
l Data on the cluster is encrypted using a Data Encryption Key (DEK) and the DEK is in turn encrypted using a Key.
l Key Encryption Key (KEK). The encryption and decryption process is done within the Cohesity cluster and is transparent to all inbound and outbound protocols and applications, such as backup, archiving, and file services. Also, the keys are stored in a distributed fashion to be resilient in the rare event of a hardware failure.
l The default key rotation policy for KEK is 90 days, but the administrator can configure a different value.

Prerequisites and Considerations for Organizations

Third-party Integration
Cohesity is based on an API-first architecture, valuing automation, consumable APIs, and self-service capabilities from the get-go. Users can enjoy error-free consistency and selfservice manageability that extends the capabilities of individual applications and enables IT to spend less time with management, and more time with ambitious, value-oriented projects. Supported automation frameworks include:
l VMware vCloud Director l VMware vRealize Automation (vRA) and Orchestration (vRO) l ServiceNow l Python/Powershell SDK
Reports
l All Organizations can view their storage consumption report. l As a service provider, you can view storage consumption reports by each tenant and
generate custom reports. For more information, see Reports and Chargeback for Organizations.
Prerequisites and Considerations for Organizations
As a Cohesity cluster Administrator, you can enable multi-tenancy permanently for a cluster, add Organizations to the cluster, and assign resources and local users to the organization.
Prerequisites
l You must enable the Organizations feature to support multi-tenancy. l Use VLANs to segregate traffic across different tenants. A VLAN should be assigned to
each tenant. If it's not assigned, then the views in the tenant may become visible but not accessible to other tenants.
Considerations
l Once the Organizations feature is enabled on a cluster, you cannot disable it. l Once an organization is created with a particular name/OrgID, the name/OrgID
cannot be reused even after the org is deleted.

Privileges for Service Provider Admin and Organization Admin

l If a single-tenant cluster is configured with remote access to a multi-tenant-enabled cluster, the Organizations page will not be available when accessing the multi-tenant cluster. The workaround is to enable multi-tenancy on the single tenancy cluster (it is not necessary to add any organizations.)
l Storage Consumed by Storage Domains: The Storage Consumed by Storage Domains report is available to the organization only if Storage Domain Sharing is disabled.
l View names must be unique. Two Organizations or service providers admin, or tenant cannot have two same view names.
l Users are assigned to the organization with specific roles by the service administrator. Cohesity does not allow an organization user to create a new user with a different role other than the organization's inherited roles.
l For example, the service provider administrator creates two users with the "Viewer" and "Admin" roles and assigns them to the Organization. The organization administrator can now create a new user with either a "Viewer" or "Admin" role but cannot create a new user with a different role.
l No DNS per tenant. Global DNS must have stub zones for all tenant DNS.
l No multi-tenancy support for Marketplace Apps.
l If the Enable for all Organizations option is selected for a VLAN and the VLAN is assigned to an Organization in the OpenStack environment, the Swift clients cannot access Cohesity Swift Service through this shared VLAN.
l Organizations (tenants) do not have access to the Dashboard in the Cohesity UI.
l Replication to a source or remote cluster fails if the source or remote cluster has multi-tenancy enabled and VLAN assigned to the tenant. For more information, see the Replication stops sending data after upgrade to Cohesity release 6.4.1c and later KB article.
l To create a SmartFiles S3 View in a multi-tenant environment, log in to the Cohesity cluster as an Organization user. If you create the S3 View while impersonating an organization, the Service Provider administrator becomes the owner of the S3 View.

Best Practices for Organizations
The following are best practices you can implement in Cohesity's Organizations (multitenancy) environment.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Enable Organizations (Multitenancy) on a Cluster

l To get better performance for VMware backups, use VMkernel ports (usually 10G) for backup instead of ESXi management (usually 1G) ports. For more information, see How to determine which vmkernel port is being used in a Cohesity VMware VM Backup in the Cohesity Knowledge Base.
l For a Hosted Backup solution with a shared, multitenant hypervisor, as a service provider, you should make sure the VLAN carrying the backup traffic has the Enable For All Organizations option enabled. This ensures the same backup network can be used for backing up different tenants' data.
l Use VLANs to segregate traffic across different tenants. Each tenant can be assigned a VLAN.
l Use different VPN tunnels for different tenants if the tenants are remote and accessing the Cohesity cluster over the Internet. This is important for secure self-service restores.
l Naming conventions in a multitenancy environment: l Create your naming convention for the Organization ID to work with 10 characters. l The Organization ID cannot be edited later. If the organization is deleted later, the Organization ID cannot be reused. l Use the same Organization ID across clusters.
l Follow the same practice when using CloudRetrieve; the same Organization ID and Storage Domains must exist on both clusters prior to running a CloudRetrieve download task.
l For service providers who are implementing a BaaS solution using Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-managed), Cohesity recommends that you segregate replication and backup traffic on the source cluster to avoid bandwidth issues. For more information, see Disaster Recovery as a Service (DRaaS) Solution Guide.
l Cohesity also recommends having a VPN connection between the source and DR clusters to set up replication across the clusters if the clusters are not using public IPs for replication communication.
l Alternatively, you can replicate over WAN without the need for a VPN connection.

Hybrid Extender
As a service provider, if you are serving multiple tenants (customers) in isolated networks with the same IP address ranges and subnets on the same Cohesity cluster, you may need to enable the Hybrid Extender.
Once the service provider administrator or cluster administrator enables the Hybrid Extender, the Organization (tenant) administrator can deploy and configure the Hybrid Extender.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Infrastructure for Organizations

Note: If you are upgrading the Cohesity cluster from one maintenance release to another maintenance release, you need not upgrade the Hybrid Extender. For example, if you are upgrading the Cohesity cluster from 7.2.1 to 7.2.2, you need not upgrade the Hybrid Extender. However, Cohesity recommends that the version of Cohesity cluster and the Hybrid Extender should be the same.
In a multitenant environment, if organizations are controlling the IP addressing for their virtualization hosts, virtual machines, physical servers, NAS servers, Active Directories, and other servers (collectively "tenant entities"), there is a possibility that the tenant entities' IP addresses overlap with each other. As a result, the Cohesity cluster will be unable to uniquely identify a given tenant entity using its IP address (Example: tenant A and tenant B might both have SQL Server VMs with identically the same IP address on their respective tenant private networks). To resolve this issue, you can deploy a Hybrid Extender VM on each organization to uniquely identify the virtual entities using the tuple of organization ID and virtual entity's IP address. The Hybrid Extender acts as a proxy VM between the organization and the Cohesity cluster and also provides source-side deduplication.
Hybrid Extender Support
Communication between the Hybrid Extender VM and the Cohesity cluster is over-secure gRPC and encrypted using mutual TLS. The Hybrid Extender VM handles all the outbound traffic from the Cohesity cluster to supported platforms (VMware vCenter, VMware ESXi, and to the "physical server", and the inbound traffic of VMware backup ingest traffic from VMware ESXi (or physical server) to Cohesity cluster.
For more information about the supported workflows, see Supported Multitenancy Workflows for Hybrid Extender.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Infrastructure for Organizations

Prerequisites
l Ensure that the Hybrid Extender option is enabled while creating the organization.
l (Default) Ensure port 29994 is open on the Hybrid Extender VM, and ports 11117 and 29991 are open on the Cohesity cluster.
l DNS configuration--The DNS configuration on your Hybrid Extender is used for general name resolution and to look up the domain controller to join the Cohesity cluster to the tenant AD. This is used during source registration for name resolution and mount-based restores/clones for data protection of MS-SQL server, Oracle, and so on.
The following are the considerations for DNS configuration on Hybrid Extender:
l When you assign an IP address using DHCP, the Hybrid Extender automatically gets the DNS configuration.
l When you assign a static IP address, you must add the DNS in the Hybrid Extender VM by accessing the VM using SSH. You can access the Hybrid Extender VM and add your DNS in the /etc/resolv.conf file. For more information on the steps to edit the /etc/resolv.conf file, see Editing for Hybrid Extender VM. For any assistance, you may contact the Cohesity Technical Support team.
l Register the AD domain of the tenant and on the DNS server of the tenant, create DNS entries for the registered AD machine accounts with Hybrid Extender IPs. This ensures that the clients connected to the tenant network are able to access the views.
l Ensure that Network Time Protocol (NTP) is set up on the Hybrid Extender. For more information, see Set Up NTP Servers.
If NTP is not setup:
l RPC requests between the Hybrid Extender and the cluster can timeout.
l If the time skew between the AD server and the Hybrid Extender is greater than five minutes, Kerberos authentication may fail.
l Hybrid Extender may not be able to connect if the time lag between the Hybrid Extender and the cluster is extensive enough to invalidate TLS certificates.
Authentication
NFS--Hybrid Extender supports only LDAP group membership lookups.
SMB--Hybrid Extender supports the following authentication methods:
l NTLM authentication--Tenants can mount their shares using the server IP address or FQDN. The tenant must be registered with only one AD domain.
l Local user account--The Service Provider can create a local user account and assign this user to a tenant.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Infrastructure for Organizations

l Kerberos authentication. l Anonymous users.
Considerations
l Hybrid extender supports source registration and backup only for Windows and Linux physical sources. AIX, HPUX, Solaris physical sources are not supported with hybrid extender.
l Currently, Cohesity does not support the auto-upgrade of the Hybrid Extender. Therefore, you must upgrade the Hybrid Extender after upgrading the Cohesity cluster from one major release to another major release. For example, if you are upgrading the Cohesity cluster from 6.5.1 to 6.6, use the Hybrid Extender version provided with 6.6.
l When you're upgrading to maintenance releases such as 6.5.1e, you need not upgrade the Hybrid Extender. However, Cohesity recommends that the version of Cohesity cluster and the Hybrid Extender to be same.
l If a tenant deploys multiple Hybrid Extender VMs, SMB and NFS sessions do not failover to the next available Hybrid Extender VM. Cohesity depends on the hypervisor that is hosting the Hybrid Extender VM to ensure high availability. If the hypervisor does not support high availability, I/O requests fail.
l Hybrid Extender does not support the following features: l S3 l SMB Multichannel l Keystone l Kerberos client for NFS l SSO l NFS authentication

l Memory: 4GB RAM l Processor: 4 vCPU

Support Two Interfaces on Hybrid Extender
Hybrid Extender can be configured with two interfaces so that it can simultaneously talk to a tenant's private network and an entity (Cohesity) outside of the private network. This feature eliminates the need for making network configuration changes (such as NAT mappings or changing firewall rules) for the Hybrid Extender interface to reach the Cohesity. Following are the two network interfaces:
l Primary interface (ens160) l Secondary interface (ens192)
Configuring Two Interfaces
You can configure the Hybrid Extender using one or two network interfaces. Each network interface can be configured with DHCP or static IPs. DHCP is the default. Static IPs will be used only if you configure a static IP.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Infrastructure for Organizations

To use Hybrid Extender with one network interface: 1. Configure the first network interface with DHCP or static IPs. 2. Do not specify any configuration for the second network interface. This unused secondary interface will not affect user functionality.
To use Hybrid Extender with two network interfaces: l Configure both network interfaces as required (using either DHCP or static IPs)
Note: l By default, the primary interface is used to communicate with the Cohesity cluster
and the secondary interface is used to communicate with entities in the tenant's internal network. l If the Network IP Address field value for an interface is left empty, Cohesity uses a DHCP server to configure the interface. l If network field values are provided as input, Cohesity uses those static values to configure the interface and fall back to DHCP if there is an issue with the values. l After deployment, you can remove the second interface manually from the VM if required.
Network Interfaces Combinations
l If you specify the network fields for both interfaces, the interfaces will come up with the specified static IP addresses.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Infrastructure for Organizations

l If you do not specify the network fields for both the interfaces, the interfaces will be automatically configured as DHCP.
l If you specify the network field only for the primary interface, the primary interface will come up with the static IP and the secondary interface is automatically configured as DHCP.
l If you specify the network field only for the secondary interface, the secondary interface will come up with the static IP and the primary interface is automatically configured as DHCP.
Use Cases
Use only Primary Interface
1. In the primary interface, provide an IP address if you want to use a static IP address or leave it blank to use DHCP.
2. Leave the secondary interface blank.
Note: The secondary interface comes up with DHCP as you left the field blank. Remove the interface from the VM configuration or use the following command to bring down the secondary interface:
ip link set dev ens192 down
Use the Secondary Interface to communicate with Cohesity Cluster
1. Configure both interfaces as required. For more details, see Network Interfaces Combinations.
2. Once the VM is up, create a customer_settings.json file in the data/bifrost directory. This file is used to override default interface behavior.
3. Explicitly mention the interface to be used for communication with the cluster and the interface to be used for internal tenant side communication (Note that explicitly mentioning both of these is important. If only one is mentioned, we will still use the default interfaces).
Sample customer_settings.json file:
{
"tenant_source_side_interface_name": "ens160",
"cohesity_side_interface_name": "ens192"
}

Deploy Hybrid Extender VM
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Settings > Access Management.
2. In the Organizations tab, click for required organization, and select Edit. 3. In the Network Segments section of the Edit Organization page, click Add Hyx. 4. On the How to configure Hybrid Extender? page, click the download button under
step 1(Download and provision the HyX) to download the .ova file. You can also download the .ova file from MyCohesity portal. 5. Deploy this OVA file in your ESXi hypervisor as a virtual machine by following the instructions given on the ESXi console. 6. Go back to the How to configure Hybrid Extender? page and click the download button under step 2 (Download the configuration file). 7. Go to http://<ip_address>:29994/upload and upload the configuration file you downloaded.
Note: Where <ip_address> is the IP address of the Hybrid Extender VM.
8. Refresh the Hybrid Extender page. The Hybrid extender VM will connect.
You can deploy more than one Hybrid Extender for each organization. If the backup adapter supports multi-streaming, then having multiple Hybrid Extenders per organization improves high availability, load balancing, and yields faster backups and restores.
l High availability--If one Hybrid Extender instance fails, the Cohesity cluster will retry backup, recovery, and clone workflows using a surviving Hybrid Extender.
l Load-balancing and throughput--When multi-streaming a backup or restore, different network flows may traverse different Hybrid Extenders to parallelize the task and speed the overall operation.
The configuration file you upload (steps 6 and 7) on each Hybrid Extender VM should be unique for each organization. It is recommended to use a different config file for every Hybrid Extender but you may choose to reuse the same config file for deploying Hybrid Extenders of the same organization. However, for different organizations, use a different configuration file on different Hybrid Extender VMs.

ntpdate -u <ntpserver> Example: ntpdate -u ntp.for.mydomain

1. bifrost.sh stop> 2. bifrost.sh start --magneto_grpc_timeout_msecs=300000 --tcp_proxy_
connector_ports=445:445,2049:2049,80:80,443:443,11117:11117,11113:11113 3. sudo firewall-cmd --add-port=11113/tcp --zone=public --permanent &&
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
Recommendations
l Deploy multiple Hybrid Extender VMs to distribute client traffic and achieve high availability and increased throughput.
l Download a new configuration file from Cohesity Cluster every time you deploy a new Hybrid Extender VM.
l Cohesity recommends that you use the Hybrid Extender version provided with the Cohesity version to get access to the supported sources. For example, use the Hybrid Extender version provided with Cohesity 6.6.0a.
l Once the Hybrid Extender is connected, the backup and recovery communication between cluster and source will be proxied through the Hybrid Extender VM.
l If you are upgrading the Cohesity cluster, you must upgrade the Hybrid Extender. To upgrade the Hybrid Extender, you should first redeploy the new version and then decommission the existing version of the Hybrid Extender. After you upgrade a cluster, then the version of Hybrid Extender should be either the same as Cohesity cluster or it can remain in the previous version. Network Realms for Multi-tenant Environments
Cohesity introduces Network Realms for multi-tenant environments. Network Realm ensures source-level selection in a multi-tenant environment, and allows you to create and manage multiple isolated networks within a tenant. On a Cohesity cluster, a source and a hybrid extender can be associated with a Network Realm to create an isolated network.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Infrastructure for Organizations

How it works?
When a backup task is initiated on a Cohesity cluster, it reaches out to the Hybrid Extender associated with the Network Realm for the source IP address. You can associate the source with the Network Realm during its registration and each source can be associated with only one Network Realm. However, you can associate multiple Hybrid Extenders with a Network Realm. The Network Realm maintains the list of registered sources on a Cohesity cluster to create isolated networks. An isolated network ensures that a task on a Cohesity cluster doesn't fail due to a mismatch of IP addresses from multiple sources.
Note: You must have an Admin or Super Admin role or similar privileges in a custom role to create and manage Network Realms.

Technical Support for Hybrid Extender VM
Hybrid Extender now has a support channel that can be enabled to let Cohesity Technical Support engineers access it for troubleshooting. The login credentials for the Hybrid Extender will be needed for accessing it. The support channel can be enabled or disabled as an Organization admin or service provider admin impersonating the tenant. Contact the Cohesity Technical Support team for assistance.

Data Source Connection
In a Service Provider (SP) multi-tenant environment, tenants often operate in isolated networks and may use overlapping IP address ranges and subnets. When multiple

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Infrastructure for Organizations

organizations use identical IP ranges on the same Cohesity cluster, the cluster cannot uniquely identify tenant workloads based on IP address alone.
To address this, Cohesity provides Data Source Connections.
A Data Source Connection consists of one or more Data Source Connectors (virtual machines) that act as secure data movers between a tenant organization and the Cohesity cluster. These connectors enable backup and recovery of workloads that are not directly reachable from the cluster or that exist in overlapping IP environments.
In earlier releases, this functionality was provided by the Hybrid Extender (HyX). Starting with release 7.4, you can also use Data Source Connections.
Why Use Data Source Connection
Data Source Connections provide significant improvements in manageability, scalability, security, and user experience for both Service Providers and their tenants.
Following are the key benefits of Data Source Connection:
l Improved Lifecycle Management: Data Source Connectors can be securely claimed using a token-based workflow. They support in-place upgrades and controlled patching, eliminating the need for redeployment during version changes and reducing operational overhead.
l Connection-Based Traffic Segmentation: Data Source Connections let you group connectors logically and configure VIPs per connection. This gives you better control over how backup traffic flows, making it easier to manage routing, balance load across nodes, and isolate network traffic when needed.
l Improved Monitoring and Visibility: Data Source Connections provides visibility into connector health, CPU/memory, along with proactive alerts.
How Data Source Connection Works
In a multi-tenant deployment, tenant organizations may independently control IP addressing for their virtualization hosts, virtual machines, physical servers, and other infrastructure components (collectively referred to as "tenant entities").
Because tenants operate in isolated private networks, overlapping IP addresses are common. For example:
l Tenant A may have a SQL Server VM with IP address 10.0.0.15
l Tenant B may also have a SQL Server VM with IP address 10.0.0.15
Without network isolation, the Cohesity cluster cannot uniquely identify these workloads using IP address alone.
Data Source Connections resolve this by logically isolating traffic per organization. Workloads are uniquely identified using a combination of:
l Organization ID
l Workload IP address

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Infrastructure for Organizations

Each Data Source Connector acts as a proxy VM between the tenant environment and the Cohesity cluster. The connector:
l Handles outbound traffic from the cluster to protected sources l Handles inbound backup ingest traffic (for example, VMware backups) from the
tenant environment to the cluster l Supports source-side deduplication l Ensures tenant-level network isolation
Secure Communication Model
Communication between the Data Source Connector and the Cohesity cluster uses: l Secure gRPC channels l Mutual TLS (mTLS) encryption l Certificate-based authentication
All data and control traffic between the connector and cluster is encrypted in transit. The connector maintains secure, outbound connections to the cluster, minimizing firewall and inbound exposure requirements within tenant environments. Data Source Connector Requirements Before deploying the Data Source Connector, review and understand the following requirements.
Supported Sources
You can protect the following sources in an organization using the Data Source Connection: l VMware vCenter l Physical Servers (Windows - File and Block Based) l Physical Servers (Linux - File and Block Based) l MS SQL VM, FCI, AG (Volume-based, and File-based, Native backup) l MS SQL Native l Oracle Standalone l Oracle RAC
Required User Role
Service Provider Administrator The Service Provider (SP) Administrator role is required to:
l Enable Data Source Connections for Organizations in a multitenant cluster l Upgrade Data Source Connections for Organizations in a multitenant cluster

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Infrastructure for Organizations

This role ensures centralized control over connector enablement and lifecycle management across tenant organizations. Organization Administrator or Organization User An Organization Administrator or a user with the following privileges is responsible for managing Data Source Connections within their own Organization.
l Modify data-source connections l View data-source connections
l Modify data-source connectors l View data-source connectors
This role is required to: l Deploy Data Source Connectors for their Organization l Manage Data Source Connections
Supported Data Source Connection
Cohesity supports the following Data Source Connection: l VMware Data Source Connection l Hyper-V Data Source Connection
System Prerequisites
Ensure that the Data Source Connector virtual machine (VM) meets the following system requirements before deployment:
l Compute Requirements l 4 vCPUs l 10 GB RAM
l Disk Requirements l The required disk size depends on the hypervisor platform: l 171 GB for VMware deployments l 166.6 GB for Hyper-V deployments
l Network Requirements l Outbound Internet connectivity is required for secure communication, updates, and patch downloads. l Data Source Connectors require IPv4 network connectivity to communicate with the Cohesity cluster. IPv6-only network environments are not supported for Data Source Connector deployments.

Data Source Connector Sizing Recommendations
We recommend that you have one Data Source Connector for each 160 VMs or 16 TB of source data. If you have more data, we recommend that you stagger their first full backups.
Note: These requirements are subject to change.
Check Firewall Ports
A Data Source Connector communicates with both: l The cluster l The protected data sources (for example, VMware vCenter, physical servers, and other workloads)
To ensure proper connectivity, the required firewall ports must be open between the Data Source Connector, the cluster, and the relevant data sources. These firewall rules allow outgoing traffic from a Data Source Connector to the Cohesity cluster endpoint. The Data Source Connector opens a secure encrypted gRPC tunnel to the endpoint and uses it for both backup and recovery traffic. For more information, see Data Source Connector. Deploy VMware Data Source Connectors
The organization administrator can deploy the VMware Data Source Connection using the installer OVA. The installer OVA can be obtained either from the service provider administrator or from the Cohesity Downloads Portal. Deploy the OVA in your VMware environment on:
l A vCenter Server, or l A Standalone ESXi host The selected host must: l Have network access to your protected data sources. l Meet the system requirements. l Meet the required firewall and port configurations. After deployment, each Data Source Connector runs as a virtual machine within your data center. Best Practice Recommendation For improved performance and redundancy, Cohesity recommends deploying at least two Data Source Connectors for each Data Source Connection in your data center. Cohesity can concurrently back up individual VM disks using multiple Data Source Connectors, leading to faster backups. Cohesity determines the concurrency based on various factors, such as disk size and the workload of the Data Source Connectors. All the data that a Data Source Connection handles, from your sources to the cluster, is encrypted in flight and at rest.
Create VMware Data Source Connection
To create a VMware Data Source Connection, you must perform the following steps: 1. Deploy Data Source Connector OVA. 2. Obtain the Connection Token from the Cohesity cluster UI. 3. Authenticate the Data Source Connector with Cohesity using the Connection Token. 4. Verify the Connection.

Manage Data Source Connectors
Important: This action can be performed only by the Organization administrator.
To optimize performance, we recommend that you use at least two Data Source Connectors in each Data Source Connection you create, and that you have one Data Source Connector for each 160 VMs or 16 TB of source data. (If you have more VMs, we recommend that you stagger their first full backups.) Cohesity clusters can concurrently back up individual VM disks using multiple Data Source Connectors, leading to faster backups. Cohesity clusters determine the concurrency based on various factors, such as disk size and the workload of the Data Source Connectors. Cohesity clusters cannot recover individual VM disks using multiple Data Source Connectors because VMware and HyperV do not support it.

The pre-check option is available after the package download. It is important to run the prechecks once the packages have been downloaded. Doing so in advance allows you to identify and resolve any issues, ensuring a smooth upgrade and patching process without any interruptions. To run the pre-check on the downloaded package, click Run. The pre-check will start and you can see the pre-check details by clicking View Details.
Upgrade Data Source Connectors
To upgrade the Data Source Connectors, you can select the upgrade package and initiate the upgrade process after performing the pre-check. You can track the upgrade progress for all connectors until the operation is completed. To upgrade the Data Source Connector:

2. After reviewing the upgrade information, click Start Upgrade. The Ok to Upgrade? dialog appears.
3. If the pre-check fails, you can either: 1. Stop immediately to stop the upgrade process (recommended). This allows you to review and address the pre-check failures before retrying the upgrade. 2. Proceed with the upgrade by ignoring pre-check failure to continue the upgrade process despite the pre-check failure.
4. Enter Yes in the text field and click Upgrade to confirm and start upgrading.
The upgrading process begins. You can observe the upgrading progress for all the available connectors.

To apply a patch, select the patch package and begin the process after performing the precheck. The patch will be applied across all connectors, with progress tracked until completion. Perform the following steps to apply a patch:
1. On the Software Update page, click Apply. The OK to apply? dialog appears.
2. If the pre-check fails, you can either: 1. Stop immediately to stop the patching process (recommended). This allows you to review and address the pre-check failures before retrying the patch.

2. Proceed with the patch by ignoring pre-check failure to continue applying the patch despite the pre-check failure.
3. Enter Yes in the text field and click Apply to confirm and start applying the patch.

To cancel the patching, click Cancel. The Cancel Patching? dialog appears. Enter Cancel Patching in the text field and click Yes to cancel the patching or No to continue the patching.

Single Sign-On for Organizations
An Organization in a multitenancy cluster can register an IDP and use it for single sign-on authorization within the Organization.
For information on SSO, see Single Sign-On (SSO).
You can configure Single Sign-On at two different levels on a Cohesity cluster with the Organizations feature is enabled:
l Single Sign-On at a Service Provider level. l Single Sign-On at an Organization level.
To successfully sign in to the Cohesity cluster, after successful validation at IDP, at least one of the following must be true:
1. The user is registered as an SSO user on the Cohesity cluster.
2. The user is part of an SSO group that is registered on the Cohesity cluster.
3. A default role is available in the SSO configuration.
1. If a default role is added to the SSO, then the user needn't be added to the cluster and all users will have default access to the cluster using the default role.
2. If no default role is added to the cluster, then the user has to be added to the cluster with a particular role, and then only the user login to the cluster.
Single Sign-On at a Service Provider Level
When a Service Provider Administrator registers an SSO (IDP), the SSO is configured at the cluster level and it is not assigned to a specific Organization.
The following are a few points you should consider for Service Provider-level SSO:
l The Service Provider Administrator can create new SSO users and groups and assign roles in multiple Organizations.
l The Service Provider Administrator can configure multiple SSOs (IDPs) on the cluster. However, one SSO per tenant and one per service provider admin.
l The users and groups that are part of the SSO (IDP) configured on the cluster are authenticated through the same SSO (IDP).
l If a default role is assigned to the SSO, the role is applicable to all the SSO users and groups that are part of the SSO.
l If no default role is assigned to the SSO, the role that is assigned to the individual group or user is applicable.
l An SSO group can be assigned to multiple Organizations. If an SSO user is part of a group and that group is part of multiple Organizations, the user can access other Organizations by using the Switch Organization option in the Cohesity Dashboard and then manage more than one Organization based on the roles assigned to the group.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Access Management for Organizations

l A user who is a part of a group and the group is assigned to multiple Organizations can have different roles inside different Organizations.
For example, In the following configuration:
l IDP: Okta is configured at the Cohesity cluster level. l SSO Groups: Group 1 with Admin role and Group 2 with Operator role are created on
the Cohesity cluster and the same groups are present on the Okta IDP. l SSO User on Okta: User1 is part of both Group 1 and Group 2 on the Okta IDP. l Organizations: Org 1, Org 2, and Org 3 are created on the Cohesity cluster. l Group 1 with the Admin role is assigned to Org 1 and Org 2. l Group 2 with the Operator role is assigned to Org 3.
Now, when the User1 accesses the Cohesity cluster, the user can switch among Org1, Org2, and Org3. User1 inherits the role assigned to the group. In this scenario, the User1 plays the role of the Admin for Org1 and Org2 and for Org 3 as an Operator.
l All the existing SSO users in the SSO of an Organization can be quickly onboard to Cohesity by configuring the SSO and registering groups on the Cohesity cluster.
l An Organization Admin can switch among multiple Organizations. The Service provider/tenant admin can only see the entities that belong to a logged-in Organization.
Single Sign-On at an Organization Level
When an Organization Administrator registers an SSO (IDP), the SSO is configured at the Organization level and is applicable only to that Organization. The following are a few points you should consider for the Organization-level SSO:
l To manage the SSO configured at the Organization level, you must sign in to the Organization.
l When you sign in to the Organization with SSO configured at the Organization level, you are authenticated through the SSO installed on the Organization and you cannot switch to any other Organization.
l As an Organization user or administrator, depending on the role assigned, you can create new SSO users and groups, and assign roles to them within the Organization.
l All the existing SSO users in the SSO of an Organization can be quickly onboard to Cohesity by configuring the SSO and registering groups on the Cohesity cluster.
Configure SSO at an Organization Level
As an Organization Admin, you can sign in to the Organization and register an SSO specific to your Organization. Prerequisites

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Access Management for Organizations

l As the Organization admin, you must have the Admin role assigned or you should be part of an SSO group with the Admin role assigned.
l Add the Cohesity cluster as an application on your IDP. l Get the SSO URL and certificate file.
To configure SSO at an Organization level, complete the following steps:
1. Access the Cohesity Dashboard. 2. On the Sign in page, click Sign in with SSO and click Sign In. 3. Slide the Sign in to Organization toggle button. 4. Type your Organization ID and click Sign In. 5. On the IDP login page, provide your username and password. 6. Click Sign in. 7. After signing in, click Settings > Access Management. 8. to become part of multiple Organizations. l Add SSO group(s) on the cluster the same as the IDP group. l Assign groups to multiple Organizations. For more information, see the Assign an SSO
Group to Organizations. l Add the Cohesity cluster as an application on your IDP

Access Management for Organizations

Assign an SSO Group to Organizations
Currently, a Cohesity user can be part of only one Organization. However, you can assign an SSO group to multiple Organizations. When you assign the group to multiple Organizations, a user that's part of the group can switch among the Organizations. However, the user inherits the role assigned to the group.
Note: After assigning a group to multiple Organizations, users within that group can sign in to the Cohesity Dashboard and switch among the Organizations. All users have the same privileges that are assigned to the group.
To assign an SSO user or group to Organizations, complete the following steps:
1. Click Settings > Organizations. 2. On the Organizations page, click the button and select Edit. 3. On the Edit Organization page, click Assign Users/Groups of the Users/Groups
section. 4. Select a required IDP domain from the drop-down list at the top of the page. 5. In the Assign Users/Groups window, select the groups from the list and click
Assign. 6. Click Save. 7. Repeat steps 1 to 6 to assign the same group to a different Organization.
Sign in Using an Organization ID
Users of an Organization with SSO assigned can sign in using the Organization ID. When a user signs in using an Organization ID, the sign-in goes through the SSO assigned to the Organization. The user can access only the objects assigned to the Organization and the role assigned to the user/group. The user cannot switch to any other Organization. Prerequisites
l Users must be part of the IDP. l Add the Cohesity cluster as an application on your IDP. l A default role must be assigned for the user/group that is signing in to the Cohesity
cluster. l You must know the Organization ID. Cohesity Admin or Service provider can provide
the Organization ID.
To sign in using the Organization ID, complete the following steps:
1. Access the Cohesity Dashboard. 2. On the Sign in page, click Sign in with SSO. 3. On the Single Sign-On page, click Sign in to Organization.

Multi-factor Authentication for Organizations
Multi-factor Authentication (MFA) is an additional layer of security used to verify the identity of a user. In a multitenant environment, the Cohesity supports MFA for local users. For more information about organization users, see Organization User Types.
A service provider administrator can enable or disable MFA at the cluster level. An Organization administrator can enable or disable MFA for user(s) in their organization.
To enable and set up MFA, follow the instructions in the Multi-factor Authentication for Local and Active Directory Users section.

Delete an Organization
When you delete an Organization, all the resources and users for the Organization are permanently deleted from the Cohesity cluster. Deleting an Organization deletes all the entities of the Organization, such as protection groups, protection sources, LDAP, remote targets, users, groups, and recovery targets. Once deleted the above entities will be completely lost. However, service providers can still impersonate a deleted Organization. This allows the service providers to remove any entity (that gets stuck while deletion) manually.
Note: l Policies and Storage Domains of the Organization will retain their association with the tenant even if the tenant is deleted.
l The Organization ID and name cannot be reused after the Organization is deleted.
To delete an Organization, complete the following steps:

for the

CloudArchive and CloudTier for Organizations

CloudArchive
Using the Cohesity, you can quickly archive data to multiple external targets such as:
l Public clouds l Private clouds - S3-compatible device l Any NAS-NFSv3 from storage vendors l QStar managed tape libraries
As a service provider, you can register an external target and add the target to a policy that you can assign to an Organization for CloudArchive. If you want your Organization Administrator to perform the Cloud Archive, you should create a protection policy with CloudArchive and assign the protection policy to the required Organization.

CloudTier
Cohesity CloudTier enables an additional storage tier where cold data can be stored. After you register supported existing cloud storage as a CloudTier target with the Cohesity cluster, you can enable CloudTier to move rarely used and inactive data to the cloud when HDD used capacity exceeds a set threshold (typically 80%). As a service provider, you can enable the CloudTier setting in a storage domain.
Note: If you plan to allow any CloudTier functionality, do not share a storage domain among Organizations. If you enable CloudTier, Cohesity recommends mapping each storage domain to a single Organization.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Replication for Organizations

Replication for Organizations
The Replication feature in Cohesity enables the service providers to provide Disaster Recovery as a Service (DRaaS) solution to their tenants.
For more information about replication, see: About Replication.
Prerequisites
l The Organizations feature must be enabled on the source cluster or target cluster to use the replication feature in the Organizations (multitenancy) environment.
l The source and target cluster must be running Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-managed) version 6.1 or later for Organizations to use the replication feature.
l When replicating data between multitenancy-enabled Clusters, the same Organization ID and matching storage domain(s) must exist on both the transmitting and receiving Clusters prior to running replication tasks.
l When using replication, the same org ID should exist on the primary and DR clusters for the Organization.
Disaster Recovery for Organizations (Multitenancy)
As a service provider, you can implement replication in the Organizations (multitenancy) environment using your Cohesity cluster for your Organizations (tenants) and provide Disaster Recovery as a Service (DRaaS). You can implement DRaaS depending on the backup network topology implemented. DRaaS service enables Organizations (tenants) to recover data in the event of data loss.
Replication is the fundamental operation that makes any Disaster Recovery as a Service (DRaaS) solution possible. Cohesity's DRaaS refers to the approach of maintaining a regularly updated replica of Organizational backup data in another Cohesity cluster in the same or different locations for data retention and offsite storage. Cohesity leverages service providers' multi-tenant infrastructure wherein they replicate data from multiple customers on shared but logically isolated infrastructure.
For more information on implementing Disaster Recovery as a Service (DRaaS), see the solution document: Use Cohesity Multi-tenancy to Offer Disaster Recovery as a Service (DRaaS).

l Some of the UI labels in different reports have different UI label names for the same attribute. So, consider them as synonyms. The Cohesity admin can either assign the entire VMware source or the components of the VMware source to an organization.
The following table lists different granularity at which VMware components can be assigned as a source to an organization (especially applicable for service providers that provide hosted IaaS).

Source

Components

l Entire VC l VMware DC l ESXi cluster l ESXi host l Folders l Resource
pools l VMs

l Entire vCD l vCD Org l Org vDC l vApp l VMs

Tenant-Level View Allowlist
In a multitenant environment, a tenant can add subnets to the allowlist and only the IP addresses within this subnet can access all the views of the tenant. This feature enables the tenant to manage all endpoints that have access to their views seamlessly.
Points to Note
l Tenant-level allowlist complements global allowlist and view-level allowlist. l The tenant administrator must have the Manage Cohesity Views privilege. For
more information, see Privileges for Service Provider Admin and Organization Admin. To allowlist views at the tenant level, complete the following steps:

Key Management Service (KMS) in Multitenancy
In a multitenancy (Organizations) environment, each tenant must use its own Key Management Service (KMS). This topic describes the required KMS configuration for tenants and the configuration that is not supported.
A KMS manages the encryption keys used to protect tenant data. In a multitenancy environment, every tenant is linked to a single vault, and that vault is linked to a unique KMS server. This one-to-one mapping keeps each tenant's encryption keys separate from every other tenant's keys.
This model applies to any external KMS, including cloud KMS such as GCP, Azure, or AWS.

Assign a Unique KMS Server to Each Tenant
Attach each tenant to its own KMS server and vault. Assigning a separate KMS server per tenant is a strict requirement. It allows tenant-level data partitioning and supports migrating a tenant in the future.
l When a tenant is provisioned, a new KMS server is created for that tenant, a new vault is attached to the KMS server, and both are assigned to the tenant.
l When you register a new tenant, attach it to a new KMS server. Do not reuse an existing tenant's KMS server for a new tenant.
l Each tenant's vault is linked to exactly one KMS server, and each KMS server serves exactly one tenant.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 7: Organizations (Multitenancy)

Key Management Service (KMS) in Multitenancy

Important: Attaching multiple tenants to the same KMS server is not a supported configuration. It is unsupported both from a security perspective and from a migration and availability perspective.

Chapter 8: Manage Protection Policy
A protection policy is a reusable set of settings that define how and when objects are protected, replicated and archived. You can select a standard policy to use when configuring a Protection Group. A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, archived or replicated. For instructions on creating and managing policies, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy. Some settings are defined in the Protection Group and some settings are defined in the policy. For example, for a Protection Group that protects servers, the schedule is defined at the policy level but indexing is defined at the Protection Group level as shown in the following figure. Policies are reusable. You can define a single policy that is used by different Protection Groups as shown in the following figure.

10. Continuous Data Protection: (Applies only for VMware) To achieve near zero RPO, click the Continuous Data Protection option floating menu and specify the time unit (hours) to capture and retain logs on the Cohesity cluster. This value defines the CDP schedule for capturing logs from the VMs.
You can use this option to restore the VM applications to a point-in-time as opposed to periodic snapshots available with regular backups. For more information, see Cohesity CDP for VMware.
11. Quiet Times: Select this option from the Backup Options floating menu to add a quiet time. Quiet Times define time periods when new protection runs are not started. For example, you may want to configure hourly backups that run during weekdays but not on Saturday or Sunday. Quiet Times only prevent new protection runs from starting during the specified time period. Protection runs that started before the quiet time period are not affected and will continue to run. For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time period that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet times. Similarly, for jobs set on an interval basis, such as incremental jobs running every 6 hours, the job will start immediately after the Quiet Time ends. If the quiet time window ends 6 or more hours after the start time of a protection job, that run is skipped. For example, if jobs are scheduled at 6 AM, 12 PM, 6 PM, and 12 AM, and a Quiet Time is set from 11:30 AM to 1:30 PM, the job originally planned for noon will instead commence at 1:31 PM. Once the run commences at 1:31 PM, the next run will take place at 7:30 PM and not 6 PM (6 hours difference).

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 8: Manage Protection Policy

Create or Edit a Standard Policy

You can add multiple quiet times. For example, you could define a quiet time period for Saturday and Sunday and another quiet time period every morning from 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM. The quiet time window is considered based on the timezone specified in the protection group to which the protection policy is applied. For example, consider a policy defining a quiet time from 9 AM to 11 AM. There are two protection jobs: one in the IST timezone and the other in the PST timezone having the same policy. For the first job (in IST), protection runs will not be triggered during the 9 AM to 11 AM IST window. However, for the second job (in PST), protection runs can still be triggered because the 9 AM to 11 AM quiet time does not overlap with the same hours in the PST timezone, despite both jobs having the same policy.
Note: If you update the Quiet Time periods in a policy for a running Protection Group, only new protection runs using the policy are affected and any existing Protection runs that have already started will use the original Quiet Time periods.
12. Retry Options: Select Customize Retries from the Backup Options floating menu to customize the retry settings for capturing snapshots. By default, the Cohesity cluster attempts to capture Snapshots three times before the protection run fails. The default time between retries is five minutes. You can optionally customize the number of retries and how long to wait between each attempt.

l Wait for snapshots to expire, then delete and recreate the Protection Group.
l Delete the Protection Group and all associated snapshots (if no longer needed).
