OpenStack Swift Storage Protocol

OpenStack Swift Storage Protocol
Cohesity supports the OpenStack Swift Storage protocol. Cohesity Swift services function as a third-party Swift implementation for the OpenStack environments. You can create a Cohesity view, assign it to the Swift Only protocol, and then authenticated Swift clients can use Swift APIs to access the view as they would use an OpenStack container. The OpenStack Keystone identity service is used to authenticate and authorize the Swift clients.
Note: Cohesity cluster communicates with the Keystone Server using the identity API v3. So, the Keystone server must support the identity API v3. For more information, see OpenStack API Documentation.
You must add a Keystone server and configure default Swift options to use the Swift protocol when the Organizations feature is disabled.
Note: You can manually add the Cohesity Swift service endpoint in the Keystone server for clients using the OpenStack command line to discover the Cohesity Swift service.

OpenStack Project and Domain Concepts
Project
Projects are an equivalent concept of tenancy in the Openstack environment. From Swift perspective, Containers tagged with the project ID can be given ownership to Users / User groups using the concept of roles. When you create a Swift Only view, you create a Swift container and tag that view to a Project in your Openstack environment. The view that you created is associated with the Project that you defined when creating the Swift Only view.
Domain
A Domain is a namespace within the Openstack environment. All the entities such as Projects, Users, and Roles belong to a namespace by default. In the OpenStack environment, a domain isolates one business entity from other business entities.
Swift Authentication and Authorization
Swift protocol authentication and authorization go through a Keystone server. All users are created and managed independently in the external Keystone server. Each user has at least one proper role and project assigned under some domain to operate on the Cohesity

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

OpenStack Swift Storage Protocol

Swift service. A user who is a Swift operator can create Swift Only View using cURL. All authorized Swift users can provide access to other users using Access Control Lists (ACL) based on the container owned by the Swift user. ACLs allow access to Swift containers/objects. For example, a Swift user who owns a container A, can provide access to container A using ACL.
Note: l Cohesity supports only Container level ACLs. For more info, see OpenStack Access Control Lists (ACLs). l Cohesity Swift service grants access to the users based on the ACL setting on the container when the user does not have the required roles assigned. A Swift container owner can provide access to the container to other authorized Swift users using ACL.
Keystone uses token-based authentication. Before doing any operation on Swift, a user must request a token from the Keystone server by providing its user credentials. If verification of user credentials succeeds, the user is assigned a token. Then the user could use the token to send a request to Swift service. The Swift service authenticates itself with a Keystone server and obtains a token. To authenticate the user's token, Swift service sends the user token to the Keystone server. After the Keystone server verifies the user's token, Swift service will be able to grant authorization based on the information returned by the Keystone server.
Multitenancy Support (Organizations)
Cohesity Swift implementation supports multitenancy by assigning a Keystone config to each tenant. For a multi-tenant Cohesity cluster (with the Organizations feature enabled), consider the following:
l You must add a Keystone server and complete Swift config to use the Swift protocol in both organizations and single tenancy environments.
l Assign the Keystone server to the Cohesity cluster and Swift user. l If the Organization feature is enabled on the Cohesity cluster, you can have multiple
Keystone servers and can be assigned to multiple tenants.
Note: You cannot disable the Organizations feature once it is enabled.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

OpenStack Swift Storage Protocol

l If the Organizations feature is not enabled on the Cohesity cluster, you can have only one Keystone server.
l You can assign only one Keystone configuration per organization.
l You must choose an existing Keystone config and complete Swift config for the required tenant if you want to use Swift service in the tenant.

Add a Keystone Server
The Keystone Server in the OpenStack environment provides secure controlled access to all of the OpenStack services. To create a Swift Only view, you must add a Keystone config for authentication and access management. Prerequisites:
l Keystone Authentication URL l Keystone admin credentials To add a Keystone Server: 1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Settings > Access Management. 2. Click the Keystone tab. 3. On the Keystone page, click Add Keystone Server. 4. In the Edit Keystone Server page, complete the following:
1. Type Keystone configuration name. 2. Type or copy-paste the Keystone Authentication URL. 3. Provide Admin Credentials.
1. Admin Domain 2. User name 3. Password 4. Provide Admin Scope, type Project name and Domain name.
Note: Admin scope is a configuration that defines Cohesity to get the admin token
5. Click Add Keystone Server.
Manage Swift Roles for the Single Tenancy
You can manage Swift roles for a single-tenant(default tenant) by adding or updating the Swift roles. Swift roles are already defined roles on the Keystone server. These roles are used by Swift clients to send requests to a Cohesity cluster. When you add a Swift role, the Cohesity Swift service verifies that the role exists on the Keystone server. To add or modify Swift roles:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Settings > Access Management. 2. Click the Keystone tab.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

OpenStack Swift Storage Protocol

3. In the Default Swift Options section of the Keystone page, click the edit icon. 4. In the Edit Default Swift Options screen, add or delete Swift roles. 5. Click Save.
Register Cohesity Swift Service on OpenStack
Prerequisites l You must add a KeyStone server and assign the Keystone server to the organization. l Swift configuration must be complete for the organization.
You can register Cohesity Swift Service on the Keystone server for better integration of the OpenStack system. To register the Swift Service on the Keystone server:
1. Log in to the Cohesity cluster. 2. Run the following command:
iris_cli 3. Run the following command:
swift register tenant-id=<tenant_id>
Note: If the Organizations feature is not enabled on the Cohesity cluster, to register the swift service, use the following command:
swift register tenant-id=''
As part of the registration process the following steps are performed on the Keystone server:
l The Cohesity cluster sends a request to the Keystone server to create a Region for the tenant. The Region name is a combination of the cluster-id and tenant-id.
l Ensure a Service Id is available for the Swift service on the Keystone server. If a Service Id is not available, then the Cohesity cluster sends a request to the Keystone server to create a Service Id.
l The Cohesity cluster sends a request to the Keystone server to create Endpoints for the Service Id in the created Region.
Unregister Cohesity Swift Service on OpenStack
You can unregister Cohesity Swift Service on the Keystone server.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

OpenStack Swift Storage Protocol

To unregister the Swift Service on the Keystone server: 1. Log in to the Cohesity cluster. 2. Run the following command: iris_cli 3. Run the following command: swift unregister tenant-id=<tenant_id>
Note: If the Organizations feature is not enabled on the Cohesity cluster, to unregister the swift service, use the following command: swift unregister tenant-id='
As part of the unregistration process, the Cohesity cluster deletes the Endpoints, Service Id, and Region on the Keystone server.
Create a Swift-Only View
A Swift Only view provides storage space for authorized Keystone users. The Swift Only view is tagged to a Project within a Domain. Only authorized Keystone users can access Swift Only views.
Note: You cannot convert a view created with other protocols to Swift Only view later. Nor can you convert a Swift Only view to another protocol.
After creating a Swift Only view (container), you can use a Swift API compatible client or cURL to send requests to a Cohesity cluster. You must use the 3001 port to perform any operations supported by the Swift APIs. For example, the Swift client can be OpenStack CLI, Swift CLI, or cURL. You must log in to the Keystone server to use the Swift CLI and OpenStack CLI.
Note: You must have OpenStack Object Storage Framework installed to send requests to the Cohesity cluster when using OpenStack and Swift command lines.
Prerequisites: l Keystone Config and Swift config are configured before creating a Swift Only view. l Project and Domain already exist on the Keystone server.

regulatory purposes.

Note: The File DataLock option is only applicable for NFS and SMB View types.

l File DataLock Mode: Select one of the following modes:
Compliance: Once File DataLock is enabled for the view, it cannot be disabled by anyone. However, a Cohesity user with Data Security privileges can edit the other DataLock settings. Compliance mode means the view complies with SEC Rule 17a-4.
Enterprise: A Cohesity user with Admin privileges or Data Security privileges can rename the view, delete the view, switch to Compliance mode, and edit the File DataLock settings. This mode is useful for giving storage administrators additional control over the view.

Note: Enterprise mode is supported on 6.4.1 and later Cohesity clusters. If the view is replicated to a pre-6.4.1 Cohesity cluster, Enterprise mode is automatically changed to Compliance mode. If the view is then replicated back to a 6.4.1 or later Cohesity cluster, it retains the Compliance mode setting.

l Default Retention: Indicate the default time period that locked files remain locked if a user or application does not specify a retention default. When the time period ends, files can be deleted but not changed.

l Autolock Files: Indicate whether files are automatically locked after the specified period of I/O inactivity (based on the last modified time stamp).

l Manually Lock Using: By default, manual file locking occurs when a user or

application sets the file's read-only attribute. Click the edit icon following:

to set the

Optionally set a Minimum Retention and/or a Maximum Retention period to ensure that a file's last access time cannot be set outside this period. A request to do so results in a permission denied error if manual locking mode is

This setting is typically used for legal hold purposes. Files in a lock expired state cannot be deleted until this date. In Compliance mode, a user with Data Security privileges can extend the override date into the future, but no one can shorten the date. NAS Tiering
In primary storage devices such as NAS, there is unused or infrequently used data that remains relevant to the organization or must be retained for future reference or regulatory compliance reasons. As a result, the growing data takes more space in primary storage, which has a higher cost than secondary storage. Cohesity supports the tiering of unused or infrequently used data from NAS primary storage to the Cohesity cluster. The process of moving unused data from the primary NAS storage to the Cohesity cluster is called downtiering. Based on a tiering policy the administrator sets while creating a data tiering task, the data from the NAS primary storage that is unused or infrequently used is periodically moved to the Cohesity cluster. When creating a data tiering task, the administrator determines how frequently the data tiering task runs and sets a tiering policy based on various parameters, such as:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

NAS Tiering

l The last time the file was accessed l The last time the file was modified l The size of the file l The file type to be allowed or denied for downtiering
Note: - Cohesity does not support updating last access time (atime) on files belonging to a Cohesity view. Use caution when tiering data from a Cohesity View. - Data tiering is supported only for NAS storage that is registered as mount points of type SMB or NFS. - Mac clients are not supported to access files via symbolic links. - You must add all sources as Generic NAS only.
Important: Uptiering is not supported. By default, orphan data deletion is disabled.

SmartFiles MTIME/CTIME Support for NAS Tiering
l Tiering Policy Inputs. NAS tiering jobs can use the last modified time of the file (MTIME), with other attributes such as file size and type, in the policy that determines the files to downtier from primary NAS to SmartFiles.
l Change Detection. SmartFiles file walkers and backup logic check both MTIME and CTIME to detect if the changes are made to file data or metadata. This ensures that updates affecting only attributes such as permissions or ownership are not missed in cases where MTIME remains unchanged.
l Preservation of Tiered Copies. During data tiering, the Cohesity filesystem (SnapFS) preserves the file metadata, including MTIME and CTIME, on the tiered copy. These timestamps are then used in the subsequent scans to avoid re-tiering or skipping modified data. Backups and tiering share this change-detection logic.
When data is tiered from the primary storage, a symbolic link is created for the original file. The name of this symbolic link is the same as that of the original file, ensuring that users and applications continue to access the data as before. On a Windows server, local-to-local symbolic links and local-to-remote symbolic links are enabled. However, remote-to-local symbolic links and remote-to-remote symbolic links are disabled by default. Therefore you must run the following commands on the Windows server to enable the symbolic link access:
C:\Windows\system32>fsutil behavior set SymlinkEvaluation R2R:1

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

NAS Tiering

C:\Windows\system32>fsutil behavior query SymlinkEvaluation
If you are permanently moving the unused data to the Cohesity cluster, you can choose not to create this symbolic link after tiering while creating a tiering task.
For NFS shares, for the user or applications to access the data that was tiered to the Cohesity View, the View needs to be mounted on the NFS client. The mount path where the Cohesity View will be mounted on the host must be provided when you create the data tiering task. This mount path cannot be changed later. All the NFS clients should use this mount path to mount the Cohesity View. For more information on mounting a view using NFS, see Mount a View Using NFS.
Once the data is tiered to the Cohesity cluster, the subsequent read and write operations of the tiered data are performed on the Cohesity server hosting the data.
A user with an admin role also can restore the tiered data back to the primary storage by mounting the Cohesity target (server hosting the data) view on a Windows client and then copying the data.

Backups and Access to Older Versions of Tiered Files
NAS downtiering is not a replacement for backing up primary NAS storage. Changes made to files in the target are not visible to the primary storage. Consequently, Cohesity recommends taking snapshots of the target storage and replicating them, similar to the backup process for any SmartFiles content on Cohesity. You cannot restore these files from snapshots on the primary storage but can recover them by mounting the target view.
Prevent Unintentional Access to the Target View
For symlinks to work, there needs to be a connection from the user's systems to the target. To facilitate backup and restore, the target view is available in SmartFiles. You must choose a view name that indicates its purpose is solely for file recovery. If users mount the target and delete files, the symlinks on the source will become inactive.
Considerations
l Cohesity does not support downtiering of junction points present on the NAS source. l If the downtiering task was created in a version prior to 7.0 and if the Cohesity cluster
is upgraded to 7.0, the downtiering task is based on the old policy. You cannot edit the downtiering task. If you want to edit the downtiering task, Cohesity recommends doing the following:
l Delete the previously created downtiering task l Create a new downtiering task l If the downtiering task was created in a version prior to 7.0 and if the Cohesity cluster is upgraded to 7.0, the downtiering task is based on the old policy. You cannot edit the grouping of this downtiering task. If you want to edit the grouping, Cohesity recommends doing the following:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

NAS Tiering

l Delete the previously created downtiering task
l Create a new downtiering task and edit the grouping
l If SMB permissions are modified on the original source, these changes are not fetched and applied to the data tiered on Cohesity.
l Avoid utilizing NAS downtiering for home directories or datasets with active user modifications. If used for such cases, consider the following:
l When using Save As within certain applications after accessing the symlink, the new file is automatically written to the target instead of the source by default. Consequently, when searching for such files later, you must check the target location.
l Installer programs that delete themselves upon completion may erase the file in the target, rather than removing the symbolic link on the primary. This results in a non-functional link remaining on the primary system.
l Users with an older version of Windows 10 that does not support long path names might encounter difficulties when mass copying files from the downtiered target for tasks such as restoring older versions. To address this, a newer system that supports long path names may be necessary to easily copy the files back.
l Deleting the symbolic link will not automatically free up space on Cohesity.
Contact Cohesity Support to free up space.
l Before 6.8.1_u7, commands existed to uptier and delete orphaned files -- files whose symlinks were deleted or renamed by the user. If a user moves or renames one of the Cohesity-created symlinks, the delete orphaned command removes the file from Cohesity, and the uptier command restores the file under its old name, potentially overwriting a new file that reuses the original symlink name. To mitigate this risk, uptier and delete orphaned commands were removed in 6.8.1_u7 or later versions. If link alterations may have occurred, contact Cohesity Support to run diagnostics to identify and address such issues.
l Cohesity does not recommend downtiering of nested shares.
l Downtiering symlink source files without the stub option may result in dangling symlinks.
l NAS Tiering is not supported in multitenant environments, and organization administrators do not have the ability to configure NAS Tiering.
l You cannot modify the File Level DataLock on the tiering target view.
l The File Level DataLock configuration will be removed from the destination cluster's view when replicating a tiering target view.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

NAS Tiering

l The Tiering Audit option is enabled by default starting from version 7.2.2, and audit logs for tiering jobs will be recorded. For clusters running version 7.2.1 or earlier, you must manually enable tiering audit logs.
l You cannot configure Lifecycle Management on a tiering target view. l If the source is Dell EMC Isilon, orphan data deletion (ODD) is not supported. l If a directory is deleted on the source and ODD is enabled, the corresponding
directory on the target is deleted once it is empty. This process may take multiple runs to complete. l Deletes and renames require multiple runs to complete. l Cohesity atime is not updated each time a file is accessed; it is updated based on the file modification time.

Tiering Audit
The Tiering Audit option at the cluster level and the Audit Logging option in the downtiering task record details about the downtiered data. This includes logs for created symlinks and files that have been renamed or deleted during the downtiering process. The audit log file is stored in the `tiering_audit` directory within the `COHESITY_AUDIT_ VIEW` View. Mount the View as an NFS share at `<cluster_ip>:/COHESITY_AUDIT_VIEW` to access this file. The following is an example audit log of a file that was down-tiered:
{"Timestamp" : "2024-07-23T06:10:04.314Z", "TieringAction" : "DownTier", "RemoteShare" : "10.14.59.185:/source_view", "ViewName" : "target_view", "EntityPath" : "/err.txt", "EntityModifyTimestamp" : "2024-07-23T06:09:50.491Z", "EntityAccessTimestamp" : "2024-07-23T06:09:50.535Z", "EntityMode" : 33152, "EntityUserID" : 0, "EntityGroupID" : 0, "EntitySize" : 3, "EntityInode" : 154514, "JobName" : "tier"}

File Services Audit Logs
The File Services Audit Logs feature enables you to record and monitor events occurring on your SMB and NFS views. Unlike the cluster-level audit logs, the logs for views are not displayed in the Cohesity GUI. The file services audit logs are saved in an internal view called filesystem_audit. You can access these views by mounting the path COHESITY_AUDIT_VIEW\filesystem_audit. The File Services tab in the Audit Log page provides two mount paths for NFS and SMB. You can mount these paths to access and view the audit logs. You can set permissions for the view and restrict access only to required subnets or users. Only the subnet's IP addresses in the allowlist can access and view the audit logs.
Note: By default, when you create a view, the Audit Log option is disabled. You must manually enable it when creating the view or after creation.

Antivirus Software to Protect Cluster Data
You can enable antivirus software to protect your data on the Cohesity cluster from viruses. Once an antivirus software scans a file and detects a threat, the Cohesity cluster reports the threat on the Cohesity Dashboard. The administrators can either quarantine, unquarantine, reset, or delete the infected file.
Perform the following steps to enable antivirus scanning and manage threats:
1. Add an Antivirus Provider 2. Enable Antivirus Scan on a View 3. View and Manage Threats

Add an Antivirus Provider
To perform an antivirus scanning on your data in the Cohesity cluster, you must first add the antivirus software to the Cohesity cluster. You can add the software in one of the following ways:
l Register External Antivirus Software l Install the Antivirus App from the Cohesity Marketplace
Register External Antivirus Software
1. Navigate to SmartFiles > Antivirus and click the Providers tab. 2. Click Add External Provider in the upper-right corner of the page. 3. In the New External Provider field, enter the name of the antivirus software
provider of your choice. 4. (Optional) Describe the provider. 5. Enter the ICAP Server URL in the following format: icap://<server>:<port>/<uri>

Description
Indicates the required protocol identifier that enables communication with external servers hosting third-party antivirus software.

Antivirus Software to Protect Cluster Data

Enable Antivirus Scan on a View
Once you install the antivirus software on the Cohesity cluster, you can enable the antivirus scan on a View. To enable antivirus scan on a view:
1. Navigate to SmartFiles > Antivirus and click the Secured Views tab. 2. Click Add a View at the top right of the page. 3. From the View drop-down list, select a view for which you want to perform the
scanning of files. Antivirus scanning is supported only on Views with SMB protocol. Therefore, the dropdown list displays the Views which support SMB protocol. 4. Provide the following details either by clicking Edit All or by clicking the Edit option for each scan settings option:

Option Scan on

Description
Antivirus scans can be configured to send the files for scanning when they are closed, opened, or both. In each case, all the files to be scanned are added in a queue and sent to the antivirus provider(s) for scanning, as per the queue order.
l Close: Files are scanned after they are closed (Default) With this configuration, you can access the files without any delay as file scanning is done after the user's file operation. This type of scanning is faster but less secure.
l Open: Files are scanned before they are opened. With this configuration, you can access the files once they are scanned. You must wait for the file scan to complete. This type of scanning is slower but more secure.
l Open and Close: Scans the files before they are opened and after they are closed. This type of scanning is the slowest and most secure, as the scanning queue includes all the live files (opened and closed).
Cohesity recommends scanning the file after they are closed as this configuration ensures that the files are accessible even if the antivirus provider(s) or scanning network is down, unavailable or unreachable.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

Antivirus Software to Protect Cluster Data

Option

Description

Files to Scan

l All Files: Select this option to scan all the files in the View.
l All Files Except: Select this option to exclude files in the view from scanning. You can specify the file extensions (comma-separated) to be excluded in the File extensions to skip field.
l Only These Files: Select this option to scan only the selected files. You can specify the file extensions (Comma-separated) to be included in the File extensions to scan field.

Exclude files based on file size: Enable this option to exclude files based on the file size.
In the Max File Size field, you can specify the file size limit for scanning. The default file size limit is 50 MB. The maximum file size limit is 125 MB.

Scan Timeout Set the maximum amount of time (in seconds) that a scan can take before timing out.

If Scan Cannot Be Completed

Blocks file access if the antivirus servers are unavailable or are unable to scan the file due to any issue. This option is disabled by default to ensure that the files stay accessible even if the antivirus provider(s) or scanning network is down, unavailable, or unreachable.

5. Click Add. You can also enable antivirus scan while creating a View or by editing an existing View.

Access Management

Active Directory (AD)
Active Directory (AD) in Cohesity Access Management is a directory service implemented by Microsoft that provides several services such as LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol), Kerberos, and DNS. It is used for user and group identity management and authentication within a Cohesity cluster. You can join the Cohesity cluster to one or more Active Directory (AD) domains. Joining to AD allows the following:
l Existing AD users and groups can be assigned Cohesity roles l SMB shares created by the Cohesity cluster can be authenticated based on AD
credentials
Cohesity Roles
Once the Cohesity cluster is joined to an AD domain, existing AD principals can be added assigned different roles so they can access the Cohesity Dashboard. For example, you can assign the View role to the AD group "ITGroup." This gives all group members read-only access to the Cohesity Dashboard. You can also assign the Admin role to the AD user "ITManager."
Cohesity SMB Share Access
The action steps in the following procedure are represented in the figure below with blue
numbered time squares: . The procedure assumes the Cohesity cluster is already joined to an Active Directory domain. Client access to an Active Directory-joined Cohesity cluster SMB share consists of the following actions:
T1) A client requests access to a Cohesity cluster SMB share. T2) The client attempts to perform an operation on the Cohesity cluster SMB share. T3) Active Directory authenticates the client's membership within a group that can
perform the requested operations on the Cohesity cluster SMB share.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

Access Management

Join to Active Directory Domain
For detailed instructions, see Join to Active Directory.
Join Active Directory
This topic explains how to configure a Cohesity cluster to use Active Directory (AD) credentials for SMB access to views and to access the Cohesity Dashboard. (For information about protecting Active Directory domain controllers, see About Active Directory Data Protection.) Joining the Cohesity cluster to an AD domain is optional. You can join the Cohesity cluster to one or more AD domains to enable:
l existing AD users can access Cohesity cluster SMB shares based on their AD credentials
l existing AD users and groups can be assigned Cohesity roles and access the Cohesity Dashboard
On Cohesity clusters that are not joined to AD, all views are accessible as SMB shares and there is no authentication. If the AD administrator blocks NTLM, the shares on the Cohesity cluster are not accessible. All accounts and Cohesity cluster SMB share privileges for users in AD are managed through Active Directory or where the SMB shares are mounted. Non-admin AD users must be granted backup and restore privileges on Windows clients explicitly. This is in addition to backup and restore privileges for the Cohesity cluster.
Migrated AD Users and Groups with Historical SIDs
Cohesity supports migrated AD users and groups with historical SIDs and grants access accordingly in Active Directory domains. The SID history retains user and group membership and access rights during Active Directory domain migration. Considerations Review the following considerations of migrated AD users and groups with historical SIDs:
l Historical SIDs with multiprotocol access is not supported. l Historical SIDs user quota accounting is not supported. l Privilege assignment for Historical SIDs is not supported.
Prerequisites and Considerations
For information about the required firewall ports for AD, see Manage Firewall Ports.

Guidelines for Joining Multiple AD Domains
A cluster can join multiple Active Directory domains even if there are trust relationships between the AD domains. After the Cohesity cluster joins the AD domain, you can add trusted domains to the allowlist or denylist. By default, all trusted domains are used for authentication unless added to the denylist. For more information, see Trusted Domains. Only Kerberos authentication is supported for SMB shares when multiple AD domains are joined to the Cohesity cluster. NTLM authentication is disabled.

Trusted Domains
After the Cohesity cluster joins the Active Directory domain, you can add trusted domains to the allowlist or denylist. By default, all trusted domains are used for authentication unless added to the denylist. You can add trusted domains to the allowlist so that only trusted domains added to the allowlist are used for authentication.
Note: If the domain controller is not functioning correctly, the discovery of trusted domains may take a relatively long period of time or may provide inconsistent results. Therefore, a trusted domain might not be discovered at all. You must manually enter such domains in the allowlist or denylist.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

Access Management

A trusted domain forest can have multiple trusted domains. To provide optimized access, you can use a subset of trusted domains so that the Cohesity cluster does not send group membership queries to all trusted domains. You can choose a subset of trusted domains by using one of the following modes:
l Denylist--Ignores specified trusted domains. For example, if there are three trusted domains T1, T2, and T3 and if T2 is added to the denylist, T1 and T3 are the trusted domains used for authentication.
l Allowlist--Allows only specified trusted domains. For example, if there are three trusted domains T1, T2, and T3 and if T1 and T2 are added to the allowlist, T1 and T2 are the trusted domains used for authentication.
Add Trusted Domains to the Allowlist
To add a trusted domain to the allowlist:
1. Navigate to Settings > Access Management and click the Active Directory tab. 2. Click the domain name to navigate to the AD domain details page. 3. Click the edit icon in the Denied Trusted Domains section. 4. Click Allowlist and add the domain name in the Allowed Trusted Domains field.
Click + to add another domain. Cohesity recommends adding at least one domain or switching to a denylist. 5. Click Save. The trusted domain is added to the allowlist.
Add Trusted Domains to the Denylist
If you want Cohesity to ignore specific trusted domains so that their principals are not assigned roles and denied access to Cohesity SMB shares, you can add the desired domains to the denylist. To add a trusted domain to the denylist:
1. Navigate to Settings > Access Management and click the Active Directory tab. 2. Click the domain name to navigate to the AD domain details page. 3. Click the edit icon in the Denied Trusted Domains section. 4. Click Denylist and add the domain name in the Denied Trusted Domains field.
Click + to add another domain. 5. Click Save.
The trusted domain is added to the denylist.

One-Way Trust
A one-way trust is a unidirectional authentication path created between two AD domains. In a one-way trust, the trust relationship is only one way. The following is an illustration of one-way trust and the direction of access:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

Access Management

As shown in the above figure:
l domain2.ad.local has a one-way trust with domain1.ad.local. domain1.ad.local does not have a trust relationship with domain2.ad.local. Users in domain2.ad.local can access resources in domain1.ad.local. However, users in domain1.ad.local cannot access resources in domain2.ad.local.
l domain3.ad.local has a one-way trust with domain2.ad.local. domain2.ad.local does not have a trust relationship with domain3.ad.local. Users in domain3.ad.local can access resources in domain2.ad.local. However, users in domain2.ad.local cannot access resources in domain3.ad.local.
In a one-way trust, the direction of trust is the opposite of the direction of access. An outgoing trust allows incoming access and an incoming trust allows outgoing access.
If one-way trust is enabled on the AD domain, trusted domains are listed in the following way in the Cohesity cluster:
l If the Cohesity cluster joins domain2.ad.local and if trusted domains are enabled:
l domain1.ad.local is displayed as a trusted domain because domain1.ad.local trusts domain2.ad.local

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

Access Management

l domain3.ad.local is not displayed as a trusted domain because domain3.ad.local does not trust domain2.ad.local
l If the Cohesity cluster joins domain3.ad.local, both domain2.ad.local and domain1.ad.local are displayed as trusted domains because domain2.ad.local trusts domain3.ad.local and domain1.ad.local trusts domain2.ad.local.
l If the Cohesity cluster joins domain1.ad.local, no domain is displayed as a trusted domain because domain1.ad.local does not have a trust relationship with domain2.ad.local or domain3.ad.local.

When a user has access to an Object, that user also has access to all previous Snapshots of that Object and any Objects added to the selected Source folder in the future. For example, if a user has access to an ESX host, they will also have access to VMs added to the host later.
Users that have access restricted to specific Objects cannot modify users or Sources even if their role grants them these privileges.
Object permissions are replicated for Virtual Machine Objects but not currently for physical Server and View Objects.
The Object permissions for a local user or group are not replicated to the remote Cohesity cluster.
Local users inherit the permissions of the Restricted Objects provided to the Restricted Groups to which the users belong.
Users that have access restricted to specific objects cannot update the Protection Group created by an admin user even if the restricted user has access to all the objects in the Protection Group.
Enable this option for the user to access file services. From the Primary Group drop-down list, select a group as a Primary group. The user can be a part of one or more groups and the SMB/NFS protocol requires a primary group to access the files.

Add a Local Administrator Group Using the CLI
You can use local administrator groups to grant SMB access to views and/or administrative access to the Cohesity cluster.
The Cohesity cluster has a built-in local administrators group called Administrators. By default, the group has only SMB Security privileges and the standard Windows administrator Security ID (SID) S-1-5-32-544. You can use and modify the Administrators group, or create your own local administrator groups and assign roles and SIDs by using the Cohesity CLI.

Change Local User Password

Using the Cohesity Dashboard, you can change your local user password. By default, the new password must replace at least eight characters with the current password.
Using the following Cohesity CLI command, you can define the number of characters you have to replace in your existing local user password:

iris_cli security-config update num-diff-chars=<number_of_characters>

For example:
If you want to restrict those six characters in your existing local user password must be replaced while changing the password, then use the following command:

iris_cli security-config update num-diff-chars=6

Manage LDAP Providers
A Unix user belonging to a primary group can also be a member of many other groups defined in the database. Because of an NFS protocol limitation, NFS users who belong to

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

Access Management

more than 16 groups have access issues. You can add an LDAP provider to the Cohesity cluster to provide access to NFS exports for Unix users belonging to more than 16 groups. The LDAP server provides a central repository to store user identities in a network security system. The Unix group information (GIDs) is stored on the LDAP server. When a Unix user accesses data through NFS on Cohesity, the GIDs corresponding to the users are fetched from the configured LDAP server using the credentials configured by the administrator from the Cohesity GUI.
Note: Cohesity does not support user authentication to the Cohesity Dashboard through LDAP.
If the Cohesity cluster is joined to an Active Directory domain, you can map the AD domain to an LDAP provider across SMB and NFS protocols so users can access the same files on the Cohesity cluster from both Windows and Linux systems. Mapping happens based on the user name in Windows and the user ID in Unix.
Note: Cohesity supports SASL over LDAP by default. If you are seeking stronger security, we recommend you to refer Secure LDAP for LDAP over SSL.
Prerequisites l Cohesity supports LDAP version 3. l The port that the LDAP provider listens on must be open. The default port is 389 (outgoing, TCP/UDP). l Only administrators or users who have the Manage AD and LDAP role assigned can add or modify the LDAP provider.
Add an LDAP Provider to the Cohesity cluster 1. Navigate to Settings > Access Management and select the LDAP tab. 2. Click Add LDAP Provider. 3. Specify the name of the LDAP provider. You can change the name later. 4. LDAP Servers--Identify the LDAP server to use. l IP or FQDN--The IP addresses or fully qualified domain names for the LDAP server. l Domain Name--The domain name to use when querying LDAP from DNS. l Port--The port on which the LDAP server is listening. The default port is 389. l Base Distinguished Name--The base distinguished name to use for the LDAP server. 5. Authentication Type--Select the authentication type to use:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

Access Management

l Simple--The Bind Distinguished Name and bind password to use for authentication to the LDAP server. Indicate whether to use SSL for LDAP connections.
l Anonymous--There is no username and password provided to bind to an LDAP server. The bind session has no user associated with it.
6. Mapped AD Domain--Select the Active Directory domain to which you want to map the LDAP server.
7. Click More Options. 8. Additional Attributes--Default values are populated for the following attributes. If
required, you can modify the attributes: l Common Name Attribute l UID Attribute l GID Attribute l Member of Attribute l Username Attribute
9. Group Query--A default value is populated. If required, you can modify the Group Object Class.
10. User Query--A default value is populated. If required, you can modify the User Object Class.
11. Click Add. The LDAP provider is added and the status is displayed on the Access Management > LDAP page.

Secure LDAP
Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) is a protocol used for interacting with Active Directory servers. By default, LDAP traffic is not encrypted. The Cohesity cluster uses the LDAP service to:
l Search users and groups l Get the group membership of users and groups l Get the SID of a user or group
Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
This document describes how to enable LDAPS after the Cohesity cluster is joined to AD, including certificate installation and LDAP bind credential configuration. Ports for LDAP Port 389 uses LDAP with Simple Authentication and Security Layer (SASL), which encrypts user and group data within LDAP messages. For security policies, this provides protection comparable to Lightweight Directory Access Protocol over SSL/TLS (LDAPS). Port 636 is the standard network port used for LDAPS. Ensure to enable LDAPS on Cohesity only when your security policy specifically requires LDAP over SSL on port 636.

Method

Port

LDAP with

SASL

LDAPS

Role Always required. AD and the Cohesity cluster use this port during normal operation.
Uses TLS from the start of the connection. After LDAPS is enabled, most Cohesity user and group lookups use this port.

Considerations
l Port 389 must remain open at all times between the Cohesity cluster and the AD domain controllers. Do not block port 389 and open it only for occasional AD changes.
l Windows AD and Cohesity continue to use port 389 during normal operation. If port 389 is closed, Cohesity cannot bypass the restrictions enforced by Windows AD.
l After you enable LDAPS, most Cohesity LDAP lookups (like SMB session setup) use port 636. Some LDAP traffic continues to use port 389. Ensure not to force all LDAP traffic to port 636 in firewalls or AD, since it can break the functionality.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

Access Management

l AD operations like joining AD, changing AD settings, and leaving AD requires port 389. Other ongoing cluster and Windows AD communication also uses port 389.
l LDAPS uses simple bind with LDAP bind credentials. Kerberos bind and NTLM bind are not supported on port 636.
l LDAPS port settings are global per cluster. You cannot configure one AD to use port 389 and another AD to use port 636.
l Ensure to install an SSL certificate on every cluster node. LDAP Bind Credentials Bind operations authenticate the Cohesity cluster to AD when opening an LDAPS connection. LDAP bind credentials are stored in the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) format in the Cohesity cluster. They are used when the cluster needs to create a new LDAP connection to AD. LDAP bind credentials must be the same for all trusted domains. Use the following CLI to update bind credentials periodically: iris_cli ad update-ldap-bind-credentials domain-name=<example> user-name=<test> password=<test123>
After you update the bind credentials, you must restart the I/O Operations service using the following command: admin@198.51.100.12>cluster restart service-names=bridge
Use the following CLI to clear LDAP bind credentials: iris_cli ad update-ldap-bind-credentials domain-name=<example> clear-credentials={}
Install SSL Certificates To enable LDAPS, you must install an SSL certificate on every node in the Cohesity cluster.
Important: Use the Host Shell to perform the steps to install the SSL certificate on every node in the Cohesity cluster.
Note: Ensure to upload the root CA certificate for your Active Directory domain. Do not use individual Domain Controller (DC) certificates. Using the root CA certificate ensures that Secure LDAP continues to work when domain controllers are added, removed, or replaced.
To install the certificate:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 9: SmartFiles (File and Object Services)

Access Management

1. Create a .pem file from the certificate file imported from the Active Directory domain controller (not an individual DC certificate). You can perform this step on any Linux system on which the OpenSSL tool is available. The filename must be in lowercase letters and be the same as the AD domain FQDN:
$ openssl x509 -text -in <certificate>.cer -out <example>.pem
2. If the following directories do not exist, create these directories on the Cohesity cluster node(s):
/home/cohesity/data/bridge/openldap/certs /home/cohesity/data/bridge/openldap/cacerts
3. Copy the .pem file to the /home/cohesity/data/bridge/openldap/certs directory. 4. Generate the certificate hash from the .pem file:
$ openssl x509 -in <example>.pem -hash -noout
For example, the certificate hash can be 75b8ef63. 5. Use the certificate hash to create symbolic links in the cacerts directory and point it
to the certs directory:
$ ln -s /home/cohesity/data/bridge/openldap/certs/<example>.pem /home/cohesity/data/bridge/openldap/cacerts/75b8ef63.0
Note: .0 indicates the version number of the certificate. Each hash is identified by the subject hash. You can install multiple certificates from the same or different AD. The OpenLDAP library picks the correct certificate file for verification using this hash.

AWS
Cohesity provides a simple and fast backup, recovery, and data management solution for Amazon Web Service (AWS) workloads.
Cohesity supports the following solutions on AWS:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

AWS

l Cloud Edition Deploy Cohesity clusters in AWS to backup workloads to AWS.
l Backup and Recovery Back up and recover Amazon services, such as Amazon EC2, Amazon S3, and Amazon RDS, using Cohesity clusters.
l Disaster Recovery Disaster recovery failover and failback of VMware VMs backed up using the on-prem Cohesity cluster to AWS using Cloud Edition.
l Replication Replicate data from on-premise Cohesity cluster to Cloud Edition in AWS.
l Clone VMs Using CloudSpin Convert VMware VMs backed up using on-premises Cohesity cluster to Amazon EC2 instances.
l CloudArchive Archive data backed up using Cohesity cluster to Amazon S3 for long-term retention.
This chapter includes the following topics:
Supported AWS Regions
Cohesity supports the backup and recovery of AWS workloads (such as Amazon EC2, S3, RDS, and Aurora) across all AWS regions, including AWS GovCloud. For the list of supported regions. For more details on these regions, see Regions, Availability Zones, and Local Zones.
AWS Permissions
This topic provides information on the permissions required to backup, recover and to perform other supported workflows for AWS workloads:
l Minimum Permissions for Individual Workloads and Workflows l Comprehensive Permissions List for AWS Source Protection l Assign AWS Permissions Minimum Permissions for Individual Workloads and Workflows This topic lists the minimum permissions required for protecting individual workload. If you intend to protect only a specific workload, then you can choose to remove the permissions related to other workloads in the policy.

s3:GetBucketLocation s3:GetBucketNotification s3:GetBucketOwnershipControls s3:GetBucketTagging s3:GetBucketVersioning s3:GetInventoryConfiguration s3:GetObject s3:GetObjectAcl s3:GetObjectTagging s3:GetObjectVersion s3:GetObjectVersionAcl s3:GetObjectVersionTagging s3:ListAllMyBuckets s3:ListBucket s3:PutBucketNotification s3:PutInventoryConfiguration s3:PutObject s3:PutObjectAcl s3:PutObjectTagging s3:PutObjectVersionAcl s3:PutObjectVersionTagging
iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy
kms:CreateGrant kms:DescribeKey kms:ListAliases kms:GenerateDataKey

Reason These permissions are required for the backup and recovery of S3 objects.
SimulatePrincipalPolicy is needed to ensure that the required actions are allowed on the IAM role we created as part of the Cloud Formation template. KMS permissions are needed to read data of an encrypted database at the time of backup, as well as write encrypted data to the recovered database. Describe permissions are needed so we can list & identify keys associated with database instances.

Permissions for Amazon RDS for MySQL Protection Permissions for AWS Snapshot-based Protection

Resource rds

Permissions
rds:AddTagsToResource rds:CopyDBClusterSnapshot rds:CopyDBSnapshot rds:CreateDBClusterSnapshot rds:CreateDBInstance rds:CreateDBSnapshot rds:DeleteDBClusterSnapshot rds:DeleteDBSnapshot rds:DescribeDBClusterSnapshots rds:DescribeDBClusters rds:DescribeDBInstances rds:DescribeDBParameterGroups rds:DescribeDBSnapshots rds:DescribeDBSubnetGroups rds:DescribeOptionGroups rds:DescribeSourceRegions rds:ModifyDBClusterSnapshotAttribute rds:ModifyDBSnapshotAttribute rds:RestoreDBClusterFromSnapshot rds:RestoreDBInstanceFromDBSnapshot rds:RestoreDBInstanceToPointInTime

Purpose
These permissions are required to register the AWS account on Cohesity with the IAM role which got created by the Cloud Formation template.
Once the source is registered with Cohesity, described permissions are needed so Cohesity can identify resources present in the account, which will be used for backups as well as at the time of recovery we use this information to provide a list of options to choose from.
Cohesity creates snapshots of the Amazon RDS instances while backing up and storing the different database instance attributes and tags.
While recovering the database instance, Cohesity creates DB instance/cluster, it also attaches the original tags.
Cohesity requires the delete snapshots permissions to delete the expired/old snapshots it creates during the backup.
The modify snapshot attributes permissions are required for sharing the snapshot across accounts if cross-account recovery is attempted.
RestoreDBInstanceToPointInTime and RestoreDBClusterToPointInTime is needed to do the point in time recoveries.

Assign AWS Permissions
AWS permissions are required to use Cohesity cloud services such as CloudArchive and CloudSpin. Cohesity recommends that you create an AWS policy with permissions and then attach it to IAM users. For example, you can create a policy that grants permissions for back up and recovery and attach it to users.
The permissions are available as JSON in Minimum Permissions for Individual Workloads and Workflows. You can copy the JSON and paste it into the policy, as described below.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

AWS

Create a Policy with Permissions
1. Log in to the Amazon AWS console using your AWS account with admin privileges. 2. In the top left of the menu bar, select Services. 3. Under Security, Identity & Compliance, select IAM. 4. In the left frame, click Policies. 5. Click Create policy. 6. In the Create policy page, select the JSON tab. 7. Create the JSON code with the required permissions and paste it in the JSON tab. 8. Click Next: Tags. Adding tags is optional.

9. Click Next: Review. 10. Enter a name for the policy and an optional description and click Create Policy.

Register AWS Source
To protect your AWS workloads, you must register AWS as a source on the Cohesity cluster. Cohesity supports registering AWS environments at both the Organization level and the account level, providing flexibility in how you onboard and manage AWS resources for protection. You can register an AWS Organization and its member accounts as separate AWS sources in the same Cohesity cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

AWS

Organization-Level Registration With organization-level registration, you can register an AWS Organization to enable centralized onboarding and management of multiple AWS accounts.
Note: Organization-level registration is only supported on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS.
Account-Level Registration With account-level registration, you can register and manage individual AWS accounts independently. AWS Organization-Level Registration Use organization-level registration to onboard and manage multiple AWS accounts through AWS Organizations. This method enables centralized management of AWS environments from a single registration workflow. During registration, you can optionally specify Organizational Unit (OU) IDs to limit the discovery of AWS accounts within those OUs. This allows you to control the scope of resource discovery and protection. Organization-level registration is useful when:
l You want centralized onboarding of multiple AWS accounts l Your environment is structured using AWS Organizations
AWS Organization Registration Methods
To protect AWS source in your organization with Cohesity, you must register your AWS Organization as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. You can register AWS Organization using one of the following options:
l Register AWS Organization using Preconfigured IAM roles l Register AWS Organization Using CloudFormation Template
Comparison At a Glance

Registration Method

Description

Using preconfigured IAM roles

Registers an AWS Organization using the delegated admin IAM role and IAM member role that are already configured with the required permissions to discover the AWS resources.

Using Cohesity-provided CloudFormation template

Registers an AWS Organization using a Cohesity-provided CloudFormation template to automatically create required IAM roles and policies to discover the AWS resources.

Register AWS Organization using Preconfigured IAM roles
You can register an AWS Organization using the delegated admin IAM role and IAM member role that are already configured with the required permissions to discover the AWS resources.
Pre-requisites
Before registering AWS at the Organization level, ensure that the following prerequisites are met:
l The Cohesity cluster is deployed in one of the member accounts of your AWS Organization. We recommend you deploy the Cohesity cluster in the delegated administrator account of your AWS Organization.
l AWS Organizations is enabled in your environment. l Delegated administrator account ID:
A delegated administrator is an AWS member account authorized by the management account to perform AWS Backup administrative tasks across all accounts in your organization. To configure a delegated administrator account, run the following commands from your management account:
1. Enable trusted access for AWS Backup:
aws organizations enable-aws-service-access --service-principal backup.amazonaws.com
2. Register the member account as delegated administrator:
aws organizations register-delegated-administrator --account-id <MEMBER_ACCOUNT_ID> --service-principal backup.amazonaws.com
Where, <MEMBER_ACCOUNT_ID> is the AWS account ID of the member account you want to designate as delegated administrator . l Delegated administrator IAM role: The IAM role in the delegated admin account that has the required permissions to discover the AWS Organizational Units (OUs) and member accounts within the organization. For more information on permissions, see Comprehensive Permissions List for AWS Source Protection. l Member account IAM role: An IAM role that is present in all member accounts within the AWS Organization and is configured with the permissions required to discover and protect the AWS services you want to protect. Cohesity assumes this role to perform resource-level discovery and protection for AWS workloads within each member account. For more information on permissions, see Comprehensive Permissions List for AWS Source Protection.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

AWS

Note: Cohesity will not discover member accounts that do not have this role configured.
Register AWS Organization
To register AWS at Org-level using preconfigured IAM roles: 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click Register at the top-right of the page and then select Cloud Platforms > AWS. The Register AWS Source dialog box appears. 3. In Source Type, select AWS Organization. 4. In Delegated Admin Account ID, enter the AWS account ID of the delegated administrator. 5. Turn on Specify Pre-configured IAM Roles. 6. In Delegated Admin Role Name, enter the IAM role in the delegated admin account. Ensure that IAM role has the required permissions for discovering the OUs and member accounts. 7. In Member Account Role Name, enter the IAM role used in all member accounts. Ensure the IAM role has the permissions required to discover the AWS workloads you want to protect. 8. (Optional) To restrict discovery to AWS accounts within specific OUs, turn on Specify Organizational Unit ID, and then enter the OU IDs.
Note: If you specify OU IDs, Cohesity discovers only the accounts that belong to those OUs. Accounts that are directly attached to the organization root (management account) are not discovered. To discover all accounts in the organization, including those attached directly to the organization root, skip this step.
9. From the list of AWS Services, review the services selected for protection. All services are selected by default. Clear any services that you do not want to protect: l EC2 l S3 l DynamoDB l RDS l Redshift Serverless

10. (Applies only for Amazon S3 buckets protection) Cohesity utilizes the Amazon S3 inventory report to protect the Amazon S3 bucket. Under Inventory Report Location, provide the following information to create the inventory report:
a. AWS Account ID: Enter the AWS member account ID in your organization where you want to create the inventory report.
b. S3 buckets ARN: Enter the ARN of the Amazon S3 bucket where you want to create the inventory report. The ARN you provide must be of only those Amazon S3 buckets that are in the same cloud region as the Amazon S3 you want to protect.
c. Prefix: Add a prefix value to the name of the inventory report that will be created.
l The prefix can contain any character, including white spaces.
l For example, Report-Source Bucket.
l The prefix should not begin or end with a forward slash (/) .
l The prefix should not contain consecutive forward slashes.
l You must not upload any files in the prefix of the inventory report.
l The inventory report will be created at <Prefix>/<Path_to_ inventory_report> when you initiate the protection. Cohesity creates the path to the inventory report configuration on AWS based on the Cohesity cluster, Amazon S3 bucket, and protection.
11. Click Register.
The AWS Organization is registered as a source on the Cohesity cluster, and all member accounts within the organization or the specified OUs are discovered. For more information, see What Happens After Registering AWS Organization.
Attach Trust Relationship
The delegated administrator IAM role and the member account IAM role contain the permissions to allow Cohesity to discover AWS workloads in the entity hierarchy within the product UI. However, to enable full discovery, backup, and recovery operations, you must establish the following trust relationships:
l Between the delegated administrator IAM role and the IAM role attached to Cohesity cluster node (CohesityInstanceRole): This trust relationship allows the CohesityInstanceRole to assume the delegated administrator role, enabling discovery of resources across the AWS organization.
l Between the member account IAM role and the IAM role attached to Cohesity cluster node (CohesityInstanceRole): This trust relationship allows the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

AWS

CohesityInstanceRole to assume the member account IAM role in each member account, enabling backup, restore, and discovery of account-level resources. These trust relationships use AWS Security Token Service (STS) to allow the CohesityInstanceRole to assume the appropriate roles as needed for each operation.
Configure the Trust Relationship
Update the trust policy of both the delegated administrator IAM role and member account IAM role to allow the CohesityInstanceRole to assume them:
1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console. 2. Open AWS IAM Console. 3. Navigate to Roles. 4. Select the IAM role. 5. Open the Trust relationships tab. 6. Choose Edit trust policy. 7. Add the CohesityInstanceRole ARN to the trust policy. 8. Save the changes. Example for adding CohesityInstanceRole ARN to the delegated admin role trust policy:
{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::<cluster_account_id>:root" }, "Action": "sts:AssumeRole", "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:iam::<cluster_account_id>:role/CohesityInstanceRole" } } } ]
}

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

AWS

Example for adding CohesityInstanceRole ARN to the member account role trust policy:
{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::<cluster_account_id>:role/CohesityInstanceRole", "Service": [ "glue.amazonaws.com", "redshift.amazonaws.com" ] }, "Action": "sts:AssumeRole" } ]
}
Replace <cluster_account_id> with the AWS account ID where Cohesity cluster is deployed.
Register AWS Organization Using CloudFormation Template
You can register an AWS Organization using a Cohesity-provided CloudFormation template to automatically create required IAM roles and policies to discover the AWS resources.
Pre-requisites
Before registering AWS at the Organization level using CFT, ensure that the following prerequisites are met:
l AWS Organizations is enabled in your environment.
l The Cohesity cluster is deployed in one of the member accounts of your AWS Organization. We recommend you deploy the Cohesity cluster in the delegated administrator account of your AWS Organization.
l Choose one of the following AWS CloudFormation StackSet deployment methods:
l Deploy from the delegated administrator account: The user or the IAM role performing the StackSet deployment must have the required permissions to deploy AWS CloudFormation StackSet.
l Deploy from the organization management account: Use the organization management account to deploy the StackSet. No additional delegated-administrator permissions are required. The CloudFormation template automatically identifies the delegated administrator account.
For information on the permissions required, see the Permissions Required for Deploying the CloudFormation StackSet from the Delegated Administrator Account topic below.
l If you are deploying the AWS CloudFormation StackSet from the delegated administrator account, you must:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

AWS

l Register that account as a delegated administrator for CloudFormation StackSets in AWS Organizations. Perform the following steps from the management account: a. Verify that the delegated administrator account is registered:
aws organizations list-delegated-administrators --serviceprincipal member.org.stacksets.cloudformation.amazonaws.com
b. If the delegated administrator account is not listed in the output, register it:
aws organizations register-delegated-administrator --accountid <delegated_admin_account_id> --service-principal member.org.stacksets.cloudformation.amazonaws.com
l Enable trusted access between AWS CloudFormation StackSets and AWS Organizations from the delegated administrator account: a. Log in to the AWS Management Console of the delegated administrator account. b. Navigate to AWS Organizations > Services > CloudFormation StackSets > Enable trusted access.
Permissions Required for Deploying the CloudFormation StackSet from the Delegated Administrator Account
If you deploy the CloudFormation StackSet from the delegated administrator account, ensure that the user or role performing the deployment has the permissions required to create and manage AWS CloudFormation StackSets. The required CloudFormation permissions include:
l cloudformation:CreateStackSet l cloudformation:UpdateStackSet l cloudformation:DeleteStackSet l cloudformation:DescribeStackSet l cloudformation:DescribeStackSetOperation l cloudformation:ListStackSets l cloudformation:ListStackInstance

Run CFT Template
To complete the registration of AWS Organization with the Cohesity cluster, you must run the Cohesity's CloudFormation Template (CFT) either from the delegated administrator account you use for registering or from the management account. Running the CFT will create the IAM roles required for discovering the AWS OUs and member accounts. For more information on registering AWS Organization, see Register AWS Organization Using CloudFormation Template.
Before you begin, ensure you have met the Pre-requisites.
To run the CFT:
1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console of the Delegated administrator AWS account or management account.
2. Open the AWS CloudFormation console.
3. In the CloudFormation console navigation pane, choose StackSets.
4. Choose Create StackSet.
5. On the Choose a template page, configure the following options, and then click Next:
1. Under Permissions, select Service-managed permissions. By selecting this option, AWS CloudFormation automatically manages deployment roles across the AWS Organization. The delegated administrator account must have the permissions required to manage StackSets and access AWS Organizations.
2. Under Prerequisite - Prepare template, select Template is ready.
3. Under Specify template, choose Upload a template file as the Template source.
4. Choose Choose file and select the CloudFormation Template you downloaded from the Cohesity cluster UI.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

AWS

6. On the Specify stack set details page, configure the following options, and then click Next:
1. Stack set name: enter a name (for example, test-stackset). The name must contain only letters, numbers, and hyphens, and must start with a letter.
2. Stack set description - optional: optionally describe the StackSet's purpose.
3. Under Parameters, fill in the values:
1. ClusterAccountId: the AWS account ID, where the Cohesity cluster is deployed.
2. DelegatedAdminAccountId: The AWS account ID where the delegated administrator role exist for organization discovery and StackSet operations.
3. Workflow: Select one of the following based in your requirement:
l source_registration: Select this option are if you are creating IAM role for registration AWS source.
l external_target: Select this option if you are creating IAM role for cloud tiering or cloud archiving purposes.
l both: Select this option if you are rcreating IAM role for both of the above purposes.
7. On the Configure stack set options page, configure the following options, and then click Next:
1. Tags - optional: Choose Add new tag to apply key-value metadata to the resources (up to 50 tags per stack). Leave empty if no tags are needed.
2. Execution configuration Managed execution: Choose how StackSets handles operations.
1. Inactive: StackSets performs one operation at a time.
2. Active: StackSets runs non-conflicting operations concurrently and queues conflicting ones, starting queued operations in the requested order once conflicts clear.
3. Capabilities: Select the checkbox I acknowledge that AWS CloudFormation might create IAM resources with customized names. This acknowledgment is required to continue.
8. On the Set deployment options page, configure the following options, and then click Next:
1. Add stacks to stack set: Choose Deploy new stacks.
2. Under Accounts > Deployment locations, choose the targeting method:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

AWS

1. Deploy stacks in accounts: Enter the target accounts directly. In Account numbers, type the 12-digit account numbers separated by commas, or choose Upload .csv file to populate them from a file. Deploy stacks in organisational units: target all accounts in one or more OUs.
3. Under Specify Regions, select each Region to deploy to from the dropdown. Stacks are deployed in the order listed; use the up/down arrows to reorder, Remove to drop one, or Add all regions / Remove all regions to bulk-edit.
4. Under Deployment options, set the operation preferences: 1. Maximum concurrent accounts - optional: Number of accounts per Region to deploy to simultaneously. A higher number speeds up the operation. (Default 1.) 2. Failure tolerance - optional: Number of accounts per Region where a deployment can fail before the operation stops. If stopped in one Region, the operation will not continue in other Regions; a lower number is safer. (Default 0.) 3. Region concurrency: 1. Sequential: Deploy into one Region at a time, following the specified Region order. 2. Parallel: Deploy simultaneously across all specified Regions.
Note: Maximum concurrent accounts must not exceed failure tolerance + 1.
4. Concurrency mode: Specifies how the concurrency level behaves during operation execution.
9. On the Review page: 1. Review all selections from the previous steps. 2. Re-confirm the IAM capabilities acknowledgment if prompted. 3. Choose Submit to create the StackSet.
CloudFormation begins creating the StackSet and the stack instances in the targeted accounts and Regions. The StackSet details page opens, where you can monitor the progress and status of each stack instance. The CFT provisions the following IAM roles and profiles:
l CohesityInstanceRole: Attached to Cohesity cluster EC2 nodes; used as the base identity for assuming other roles.

Troubleshooting

l CohesityInstanceProfile: EC2 instance profile that wraps CohesityInstanceRole; must be attached to all cluster nodes.
l CohesitySourceRegistrationRole: Grants permissions for source registration operations.
l CohesityDelegatedAdminRole: Created in the delegated administrator account; allows Cohesity to discover OUs and member accounts across the organization.
l CohesityBackupS3StagingRole: Grants permissions for S3 staging operations during backup and recovery.
Note: The trust relationship to enable full discovery, backup, and recovery operations are configured by default when the organization is registered using the CFT template. No additional steps are required.

If the StackSet creation fails with an AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationRole error when deploying from the delegated administrator account, this indicates one of the following:
l The delegated administrator account is not registered for CloudFormation StackSets. l Service-managed permissions was not selected as the permission model while
running te CFT.
What Happens After Registering AWS Organization
Once the AWS Organization is registered as a source on the Cohesity cluster, Cohesity initiates discovery of the AWS Organization hierarchy. Member account and resource discovery is performed asynchronously in the background and may take time depending on the size and complexity of the organization. As member accounts are discovered, resources in those accounts become available for protection based on the workloads selected during source registration. Any new AWS accounts added to the registered organization or selected OUs are automatically discovered. You can view the registered source by navigating to Data Protection > Sources in the cluster UI.
Note: If discovery fails for a member account due to permission issues, connectivity problems, or other errors, Cohesity skips that account and continues discovery for the remaining accounts. You can review the failure details in the UI and take corrective action as needed.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Troubleshooting

AWS Organization Level Registration Considerations

Consider the following limitations and behaviors when registering AWS at the Organization level:

l Cohesity performs automatic refresh of AWS Organization every 24 hours.
l You must perform a manual refresh to discover the latest account and resource changes.
l The Tags option on the entity hierarchy of the cluster UI displays resources and instances across all those accounts which are discovered as a part of the source registration.
l When the Native Backup option is enabled for EC2 instance protection, backups use AWS EBS Direct APIs.
l Fleet instances are not supported for AWS Organization-level registration.
l The CloudSpin feature is not supported for AWS Organization-level registration.
l Backup and restore operations are supported within the same account and across different accounts belonging to the same AWS Organization.
l Cohesity does not support protection of DocumentDB Elastic Clusters when AWS is registered at the organization level.
l Cohesity uses AWS APIs to perform discovery and protection. Ensure that the AWS endpoints for the workloads you want to protect are reachable from all Cohesity cluster nodes.

AWS Account-Level Registration

Use account-level registration to onboard and manage an individual AWS account for protection. This method allows you to register a single AWS account by providing the required credentials and permissions.
Account-level registration is useful when:

l You want granular control over a specific AWS account l AWS accounts are managed independently l You do not use AWS Organizations

After registration, Cohesity discovers resources within the account and enables you to configure protection workflows.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Troubleshooting

Note: Cohesity uses AWS APIs to perform discovery and protection. Ensure that the AWS endpoints for the workloads you want to protect are reachable from all Cohesity cluster nodes.

Create an AWS Policy
To restrict Cohesity's access to your AWS resources, Cohesity recommends creating an IAM policy with only the permissions required for backup and recovery. To create a new policy with permissions to create the cluster:
1. Log in to the Amazon AWS console using your AWS account with admin privileges. 2. In the top left of the menu bar, select Services. 3. Under Security, Identity & Compliance, select IAM. 4. In the left frame, click Policies. 5. Click Create policy. 6. In the Create policy page, select the JSON tab. 7. Update the default JSON code with the permissions required for the workloads your
want to protect. For information on the permissions required, see Minimum Permissions for Individual Workloads and Workflows. 8. Click Review policy. 9. In the Name field, enter a name of this policy, such as CohesityPolicy and click Create policy.
Create an IAM User
Once you create a policy with the required permissions, you can create a new IAM user and attach the policy that you created previously. To create an IAM user:
1. Log in to the Amazon AWS console using your AWS account with admin privileges. 2. In the top left of the menu bar, select Services. 3. Under Security, Identity & Compliance, select IAM. 4. In the left frame, click Users.

created previously and select that policy. 9. Click Next: Tags. 10. Optionally, enter tags for the policy and then click Next: Review. 11. Review your choices and then click Create User. 12.
