Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud Instances
Cohesity provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective backup, recovery, and data management solution for Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) instances in your AWS account. Plan and Prepare for AWS EC2 Protection
Prerequisites
Required AWS Service Endpoints

AWS Resource Type IAM CloudFormation EC2 KMS S3
SSM EBS RDS

Service Endpoints iam.amazonaws.com cloudformation.<regionId>.amazonaws.com ec2.<regionId>.amazonaws.com kms.<region>.amazonaws.com s3.<region>.amazonaws.com s3fips.<region>.amazonaws.com ssm.<region>.amazonaws.com ebs.<region>.amazonaws.com rds.<region>.amazonaws.com

Recovery Prerequisites
Same Account, Same Region: No prerequisites. Different Account, Same Region:
l Target AWS account should be registered as a data source in the same destination cloud region.
l If you have enabled Encryption Settings for an EC2 instance that is already

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

encrypted, then the EC2 instance will be recovered with the encryption provided in the Encryption Settings.
Different Account, Different Region:
l Target AWS account should be registered as a data source in the same destination cloud region.
l If you have enabled Encryption Settings for an EC2 instance that is already encrypted, then the EC2 instance will be recovered with the encryption provided in the Encryption Settings.
Considerations
General Considerations
l When recovering an AWS EC2 instance running Microsoft Windows OS with UEFI Preferred boot mode, the process will utilize a base AMI based on the 'Current Instance Boot Mode' of the source EC2. For example, if the source EC2 was configured as UEFI-preferred, the recovery will automatically use an AMI that supports UEFI boot mode.
l Cohesity does not support recovery of EC2 instances to a different availability zone. l Backups for ARM-based Amazon EC2 instances from the marketplace are only
supported using the EBS diff API-based backup method. l You cannot exclude EBS volumes at the object-level (manual volume exclusion) for
auto-protected EC2 instances. To exclude EBS volume for auto-protect VMs, you must use the Volume Exclusion Settings option in the Additional Settings.
File-Level Recovery (FLR) Considerations
l File-level recovery is not supported if EC2 instances are backed up using Snapshot Manager as the protection type.
l File-level recovery is not supported for EC2 instances using the XFSv5 file system. l You can perform file and folder recovery to a Linux EC2 instance only if it uses x86_64
architecture. When browsing files or folders for recovery, Cohesity does not display files or folders with an absolute path length exceeding approximately 3,500 characters. To recover these files or folders, select the parent directory.
AWS C2S Considerations
l Amazon EC2 Simple Systems Manager (SSM) is not available in C2S. You must install the Cohesity Agent on the target machine for FLR.
l AWS diff APIs are not available in C2S. l All VM restores are fleet-based.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

Networking and Configuration Issues
Issue: The backup of the AWS VMs will fail with the following error if you have configured to launch the fleet instance in the VPC and subnet of a region different from the protected VM's region: VPC and Subnet are not specified for the fleet instance. Please specify the same by editing the source. Workaround: Update the registered AWS source to launch the fleet instance in the same subnet as protected VMs.
Support for HTTP Proxy Server
HTTP Proxy is used if the cluster using the proxy server is behind a private network and cannot reach the internet to go through the proxy. Cohesity cluster supports HTTP proxy for AWS sources for performing the following workflows:
l On-demand CloudSpin l Policy-based CloudSpin l Cloud-native backup and recovery l Disaster recovery failback workflows
To enable HTTP proxy, contact Cohesity Support.
Protect AWS EC2 Instances
In Cohesity, AWS EC2 instances are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, archived, or replicated. A Protection Policy is a reusable set of settings that define how and when objects are protected and replicated. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.
Note: l Backup and recovery of AWS EC2 requires a proxy VM to be launched on the cloud
source. For enhanced security, after creating the proxy VM on the cloud source, Cohesity now automatically deploys an X.509 certificate .
l Cohesity preserves the Instance Metadata Service v2 (IMDSv2) configuration of Amazon EC2 instances during protection.
To protect AWS EC2 instances:
1. Select Data Protection > Protection. 2. Click Protect on the top-right of the page and then click Protect > Virtual
Machines. The New Protection page appears.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

3. Click Add Objects, and from the Registered Source drop-down list, select the AWS source you want to protect. You can also register a new source with the Cohesity cluster by clicking the Register Source option.
4. From the objects list, select the EC2 instances you want to protect. Optionally, you can:
l Click the icon to enable Auto Protect at various hierarchy levels (account, AWS region, or Availability zone levels). When this option is enabled at a particular level, all the EC2 instances that are added to that level in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run.
l Click the Tags icon on the right and select tags to:
l Auto Protect ( ) the VMs having these tags.
l Exclude ( ) the auto protection of VMs having these tags. If a VM has multiple tags with Auto Protect and Exclude applied, exclusion takes precedence. These excluded VMs are also excluded even if a parent object is auto protected. The Tags button will not be displayed if the Cohesity cluster detects that no sources have tags assigned to them. l Exclude any volumes of the EC2 instance from protection. To exclude a volume:
l Click the edit icon displayed next to the EC2 instance of which you want to exclude the volume. Unselect the volume which you want to exclude from protection.
Note: l You cannot exclude the root volume from protection.
l You cannot exclude EBS volumes at the object level (manual volume exclusion) for auto-protected EC2 instances. To exclude EBS volume for auto-protect VMs, you must use the Volume Exclusion Settings option in the Additional Settings.
For more information, see Exclude EBS Volumes from EC2 Instance Backup. 5. Click Continue to go back to the New Protection page. 6. In the Protection Group field, enter a name for the Protection Group. The name can contain alphanumeric characters, underscores, dashes, and periods.

l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental protection run to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last protection run.
l Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup protection run to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).

Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A Protection Group run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.

Note: Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.
l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Protection Groups.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve a similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
This option is toggled on by default to index the data of the Protection Group. Indexing improves files and folders search. Cohesity performs incremental indexing where only the data that has changed since the previous snapshot is scanned and indexed.

Exclude EBS Volumes from EC2 Instance Backup
Cohesity supports excluding EBS volumes from EC2 instance backup. The following are important points to note:
l By default, all volumes are included as part of the EC2 instance backup. l You cannot exclude the root volume. l You cannot exclude EBS volumes at the object level (manual volume exclusion) for
auto-protected EC2 instances. To exclude EBS volume for auto-protect VMs, you must use the Volume Exclusion Settings option in the Additional Settings. l If you exclude a volume from the EC2 instance backup and if any system information is stored on the excluded volume, recovering the EC2 instance fails. For example, in the /etc/fstab file, if you do not specify the nofail option for the excluded volume, recovering the Linux instance fails.
You can exclude EBS volumes from EC2 instance backup using the following two methods:

AWS Backup Use Cases
The following are the use cases for backing up Amazon EC2 instances:
Backup On-prem Data Using Cloud Edition
Cloud Edition supports the backup and recovery of Virtual Machines (such as a VM in a vCenter server) to a Cohesity cluster Cloud Edition running in AWS Cloud Service.VMs can be recovered to a new location or back to the original location.
Backup Amazon EC2 to On-Premises or Cloud Edition Cluster using Native Snapshot
Cohesity cluster supports backing up virtual servers using the native snapshot of the cloud service. For example, a virtual server Protection Group backs up Amazon EC2 instances from AWS Cloud service to an on-premises Cohesity cluster. The result of this backup is a snapshot on the on-premises Cohesity cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

Cohesity Cloud Edition also supports backing up Amazon EC2 instances using the native snapshot of the Cloud Service. For example, a Virtual Server Protection Group backs up Amazon EC2 instances to a Cloud Edition Cohesity cluster running in the same Cloud service. The result of this backup is Snapshots on the Cloud Edition cluster.

Backup Amazon EC2 Using Snapshot Management
Cohesity uses Snapshot Management APIs to create AWS snapshots for the services such as Amazon EC2 and Amazon RDS. When a Protection Group with Snapshot Manager enabled is

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

executed, only the metadata is stored on the Cohesity cluster. All snapshot data gets stored in AWS itself. To enable this feature, you must select Snapshot Manager as the Protection Group Type while creating the Protection Group for protecting AWS service. By default, the snapshots are stored on the same region and account as the AWS source. You can recover these snapshots to a different region and account. Additionally, the snapshots stored in the same AWS region and account as the source can be replicated to a different AWS account or region. For more information, see Use AWS Snapshot Management for Replication.
Use AWS Snapshot Management for Replication
If the policy attached to the Snapshot Manager-enabled Protection Group has replication to AWS enabled, you can replicate the data to different AWS regions or accounts. To replicate the AWS snapshots to another AWS region:
1. Register AWS Source. 2. Create a Policy with replication to AWS enabled. 3. Create a Protection Group:
l Choose Snapshot Manager as the Protection Group Type. l Attach the policy with replication enabled. This type of replication does not require a Cohesity cluster to serve as the destination for the replication of data. The AWS region serves as the destination. Cohesity replicates the snapshots to the EBS bucket in the selected region. Manage Recovery This chapter includes the following topics:

The Cohesity cluster attempts to index all files and folders to a drive on both Windows and Linux systems. If the Cohesity cluster is unable to find mount point information about files or directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories in the lvol_N directory, where N is a unique number such as 1.
On Windows systems, if the Cohesity cluster finds the mount point information about files and directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories with a drive letter such as C:.
On Linux systems, how files and directories are indexed and displayed is dependent on the conditions specified in the following table.

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

Simple Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
UUID="ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc" /mnt ext4 auto 0
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point that was specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

LVM Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
/dev/mapper/VG1-root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
/dev/VG1/root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt. If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Linux Physical

LVM Volume

The Cohesity agent can only return mount data when the volume is mounted on the Linux physical Server. If the volume is mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the volume is not mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

4. Once you select the files and folder to recover, select one of the following options:
l Next: Recover Options: If you select this option, then continue with the step 5 to configure the file recovery options.
l Download Files: If you are recovering a single file, this option downloads the file to your browser's download folder. For all other selections, this creates a recovery task. When the task is completed, from the Recoveries page, click the task name and then click Download Files to download the generated zip file.
Character replacement explanation for : and \ in file and directory names in zip files
If the original file or directory name contains a `:' , it is replaced with `_COLON_' in the archive. Example:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

l The original name is "a:b" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b" l The original name is "a:b:c" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b_
COLON_c" If the original file or directory name contains a `\', it is replaced with '_BACK_ SLASH_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "x\y" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_y" l The original name is "x\y\z" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_
y_BACK_SLASH_z" 5. From the Recover To, select New Server to recover the files or folders to a new
server. 6. Source: From the Source drop-down menu, select a registered server to which you
want to recover the files and folders. You can also register a new source by clicking Register Source. 7. Target: From the Target (for VM and physical server) or Volume (for NAS) drop-down menu, select a VM or volume to which the files and files are to be recovered.
Note: For recovering files and folders of a VMware VM, ensure that VMware Tools are installed and running on the target VM. The target list displayed includes only VMs with VMware Tools installed and running.
8. Recover to: In the Recover to field, change the default location to which the files or folders are recovered. By default, the files and folders are recovered to the /tmp/ directory for VMs. For NAS, an example path on an alternate location could be /tmp/recover. You can recover encrypted files/folders to their original location only. Example for Windows alternate location: l D:\cohesity_restore\1.txt l D:\cohesity_restore\bar User Account Requirements for VM Protection may need to be met to recover files to a Windows VM. If recovering to a standalone Hyper-V host or cluster, you must add the guest VM to the reverse lookup zone in the DNS server to complete the recovery successfully.
9. Optional. Edit the default settings of the following Recovery options: l Overwrite Existing File/Folder: By default, this option is enabled to overwrite the existing files and folders. Disable this option to create the files and folders in the specified location. Any duplicate files are skipped.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

Example for a Windows alternate location with Overwrite Existing File/Folder enabled and the target already exists: Files to be recovered: "C:\foo\1.txt", "C:\foo\test\1.txt", "C:\bar", "C:\foo\bar". Specified alternate location: "C:\restore". At the end of the copy, the target folder looks like this:
l C:\restore\1.txt l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_0\1.txt l C:\restore\bar l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_1\bar If Overwrite Existing File/Folder is enabled, recovering a file to source when the file is in Fuse may cause the open file to be overwritten. Whether overwriting occurs depends on the application using the file. l Preserve File/Folder Attributes: By default, this option is enabled and the ACLs, permissions, and timestamps are preserved for all files and folders. If you disable this option, then ACLs and permissions are not preserved. If recovering both folders and files, then folders will receive the new timestamps, but files retain their original timestamps. If recovering only files, then files will receive the new timestamps. l Continue on Error: Enable this option if you want to continue the recovery even if one of the objects encounters an error. By default, this option is disabled and the recovery operation will fail if one of the objects encounters an error. l Cluster Interface: By default, the Auto Select option is enabled and the recovery task automatically selects the correct VLAN. If you disable this option, then select a configured interface group from the Interface Group drop-down. l Task Name: Change the default name of the recovery task. 10. Click Start Recovery.
The recovery task is initiated. You can monitor the recovery task from the Recoveries page.

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

l The original name is "a:b" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b" l The original name is "a:b:c" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b_
COLON_c"
If the original file or directory name contains a `\', it is replaced with '_BACK_ SLASH_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "x\y" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_y" l The original name is "x\y\z" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_
y_BACK_SLASH_z"
5. From the Recover To, select Original Server to recover the files or folders to the original server.
6. Recover to Original Path: To recover to a different location in the original server, disable the Recover to Original Path option, and then provide the location to which the files or folders are to be recovered in the Recover To field. By default, the files and folders will be recovered to the original location.
7. Optional. Edit the default settings of the following Recovery options:
l Overwrite Existing File/Folder: By default, this option is enabled to overwrite the existing files and folders. Disable this option to create the files and folders in the specified location. Any duplicate files are skipped.
Example for a Windows alternate location with Overwrite Existing File/Folder enabled and the target already exists:
Files to be recovered: "C:\foo\1.txt", "C:\foo\test\1.txt", "C:\bar", "C:\foo\bar". Specified alternate location: "C:\restore". At the end of the copy, the target folder looks like this:
l C:\restore\1.txt
l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_0\1.txt
l C:\restore\bar
l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_1\bar
If Overwrite Existing File/Folder is enabled, recovering a file to source when the file is in Fuse may cause the open file to be overwritten. Whether overwriting occurs depends on the application using the file.
l Preserve File/Folder Attributes: By default, this option is enabled and the ACLs, permissions, and timestamps are preserved for all files and folders. If you disable this option, then ACLs and permissions are not preserved. If recovering both folders and files, then folders will receive the new timestamps, but files retain their original timestamps. If recovering only files, then files will receive the new timestamps.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Execute the CloudFormation Template

l Continue on Error: Enable this option if you want to continue the recovery even if one of the objects encounters an error. By default, this option is disabled and the recovery operation will fail if one of the objects encounters an error.
l Cluster Interface: By default, the Auto Select option is enabled and the recovery task automatically selects the correct VLAN. If you disable this option, then select a configured interface group from the Interface Group drop-down.
l Task Name: Change the default name of the recovery task.
8. Click Start Recovery.
The recovery task is initiated. You can monitor the recovery task from the Recoveries page.

Recover VMs with Disks > 1 TB from AWS Native API Snapshots
When recovering from backups that were captured using AWS native snapshotting and the disks being restored are greater than 1 TB, the Cohesity cluster uses Proxy VMs to upload the data to the AWS cloud similar to how the Cohesity cluster creates Proxy VMs to download the data from the AWS Cloud to an on-premises Cohesity cluster or Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster. Note the following requirements for supporting the recovery of VMs with disks over 1 TB:
l The VPC where the VM will be recovered to, must be reachable from the Cohesity cluster through a VPN. For more information, see VPN Connections.
l Port 50051 must be open in the network security group where the VMs will be recovered to.
Disaster Recovery of VMs Using AWS Cohesity Cloud Edition
To provide disaster recovery failover and failback, Cohesity supports the Cloud Migration of VMs between hypervisor servers (VMware vCenter), cloud services (AWS and Azure) and Cohesity Cloud Edition Cohesity clusters. For Hyper-V, Cohesity supports only failover to Azure. Disaster recovery with Cohesity Cloud Edition consists of the following two use cases:
l Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to AWS Cloud l Back Up AWS Cloud VMs, Replicate to On-Prem and Failback to Hypervisor Server
Cohesity Import and Export for AWS
Cohesity supports an internal import and export feature that is fast and cost-effective. The number of temporary fleet instances created in the user account is limited by limiting the number of import tasks running at a time. Hence, even if other workloads are not present in the cluster, the number of import tasks will remain the same. For details on setting the number of import tasks, contact Cohesity Support.

Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to AWS Cloud
To provide disaster recovery failover and failback, Cohesity supports the Cloud Migration of VMs between hypervisor servers (VMware vCenter), cloud services (AWS and Azure) and Cohesity Cloud Edition Cohesity clusters. For Hyper-V, Cohesity supports only failover to AWS. Cohesity Cohesity Cloud Edition supports the replication of VMs captured on an onpremises Cohesity cluster to Cohesity Cloud Edition as shown by the example figure below. Starting from the left in the following figure, the use case shows how Protection Groups running on the on-premises Cohesity cluster captures Snapshots of VMs and stores these Snapshots on the on-premises Cluster. The Protection Policies associated with these Jobs, are configured to replicate (or copy) Snapshots from the on-premises Cohesity cluster to the Cohesity Cloud EditionCohesity cluster. From the Snapshots stored on the Cohesity Cloud Edition, you can failover VMs. The failover process creates new VMs running in the cloud service (such as AWS or Azure). As part of the Failover process, the VMs are converted and spun up in the cloud service.
Note: Multi-Disk Windows and Linux EC2 instances are supported to failover to AWS and failback from AWS.
Cohesity supports the failover of VMware VMs with UEFI boot mode enabled to AWS. Failover to AWS supports the following UEFI boot mode enabled operating systems:
l Windows Server 2012, 2016, 2019 l Ubuntu 16, 18

The new Inactive Protection Group on the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cohesity cluster has the same name as the Protection Group on the on-premises Cohesity cluster, for example: Win2k12. The VM must be powered on and connected to the network when the Protection Group is running.

Back Up AWS Cloud VMs, Replicate to On-Prem and Failback to Hypervisor Server
To provide disaster recovery failover and failback, Cohesity supports the Cloud Migration of VMs between hypervisor servers (VMware vCenter), cloud services (AWS and Azure) and Cohesity Cloud Edition Cohesity clusters.
Note: l For Hyper-V, Cohesity supports only failover to AWS. Failback is not supported.
l Failover of VMs born in the cloud to an on-premises VMware vCenter is not supported. This topic describes the failback of VMs that were originally backed up from an on-premises VMware vCenter server and subsequently failed over to AWS using the process described in Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to Cloud.
This topic describes the second use case of disaster recovery using Cloud Edition--how to backup cloud VMs to the Cloud Edition cluster, replicate to the on-premise cluster, and then failback to the Hypervisor server. For information on how the VMs are backed up in the AWS cloud service, see the first process of disaster recovery using Cloud Edition documented in Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to AWS Cloud. Cohesity supports the failback of VMware VMs with UEFI boot mode enabled from AWS. Failback from AWS supports the following UEFI boot mode enabled operating systems:
l Windows Server 2012, 2016, 2019 l Ubuntu 16, 18

As illustrated in the figure above, on the Cohesity Cloud Edition running in the Cloud Service, a Protection Group using native snapshots or Cohesity Protection Service backs up the cloud VMs (as indicated by the backup arrow in the figure). The policy associated with the Protection Group specifies that these Snapshots are replicated to the on-premises Cohesity cluster (as indicated by the Replicate arrow). From those Snapshots stored on the on-premises Cohesity cluster, you can failback or recover the VMs back to their original

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

location or a new location in your Hypervisor server such as a vCenter Server (as indicated by the Failback (Recover) arrow).
To back Up Cloud VMs to Cohesity Cloud Edition, replicate to an on-premises Cohesity cluster and failback to a hypervisor server:
Verify the following requirements prior to failback:
l The VMs that are backed up to the Cloud Service must have VMware Tools and Remote Desktop installed before the original Protection Group captures the Snapshots from the VMware vCenter Server as described in the Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to AWS Cloud.
l If you are backing up the Cloud VMs to the Cohesity Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster using the Cohesity Protection Service Protection Group type, the VMs must have the Cohesity agent installed inside the guest operating system. The agent backs up the VM from inside the guest OS (guest-level backup). This is unlike the Native Snapshots type, which operates at the hypervisor level and does not require an agent on the VMs. For installation instructions, see Deploy Cohesity Agent on Virtual Servers.
l For AWS cloud source:
l Configure the VPC and tunnels so that the source VMs are reachable using private IP addresses.
l Cohesity fleet instances must have ports 50051 and 22 open, so that the Cohesity cluster can communicate with fleet instances. Cohesity creates one network security group in each VPC, and attaches to the fleet instance.
Note: By default, the inbound rules at the security group will be configured with the CIDR range of the network where the Cohesity cluster is configured. Contact Cohesity Support if you want to configure the security group with a different CIDR range.
l If you are backing up from an AWS Cloud Source, you must use a AWS Cloud Source that has been granted adequate permissions to back up.
For more on the native snapshot process for creating the Cohesity snapshot, see AWS Backup Use Cases.
Steps:
1. If not already configured, set up replication between the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster and the on-premises Cohesity cluster. For instructions, see Replication and Remote Access Setup.
2. On the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster, create a Policy that replicates from the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster to the on-premises Cohesity cluster as shown in the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

figure. For instructions, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.
3. On the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster, refresh the Object hierarchy for the Source of the VMs that will be backed up:
a. Select Data Protection > Sources.
b. Click the action icon ( ) next to the Source and select Refresh.
4. On the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster, create a Virtual Server Protection Group (such as BackToPrem) with Protection Group Type option as Native Snapshots or Cohesity Protection Service. Associate the Policy created in the previous step with this Protection Group. For detailed instructions, see Add or Edit a Protection Group for Virtual Servers. If Cohesity Protection Service is selected as the Protection Group type, then the VMs that are backed up to the Cloud Service (failovered VMs) must have a Cohesity agent installed.

Clone VMs to AWS Cloud Using CloudSpin
On a Cohesity cluster with a Protection Group that captures Snapshots of VMs with a CloudSpin schedule, the cluster clones VMs to an AWS cloud service. You can then launch the VMs to a running state. What happens during the CloudSpin process is dependent on the cloud service type:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

Full
When you clone to an AWS Cloud using CloudSpin, the Cohesity cluster copies the Snapshot to an S3 bucket in the specified AWS account and then converts the snapshot from VMDK format to an AMI format using the AWS import service.

Incremental
On the first CloudSpin run, the Cohesity cluster copies the full VM snapshot data to EBS volumes. The number of EBS volumes corresponds to the number of backed-up VM disks. Once copying is done, Cohesity uses AWS import service to generate an AMI from the EBS volume corresponding to the root volume and generates the EBS snapshots for all other volumes, if any.
For subsequent runs, only incremental changes are copied between the snapshots.
Incremental CloudSpin to AWS requires a Fleet Instance. The cluster communicates with the Fleet Instance using private IP. Therefore, the onprem cluster must be on a VPN to AWS VPC.

Edit /etc/fstab to use UUID

You must edit the /etc/fstab file and change the (non-LVM) entries to use UUIDs to identify the disk partitions. These changes must be made to the /etc/fstab file before the Protection Group (which captures the Snapshots to be cloned) is run.
For example, the following entry in the /etc/fstab table must be changed to use the UUID to identify the partition instead of the device file name of /dev/sbd1.

/dev/sdb1 /mnt/disk1 ext4 defaults

Note: l Use labels or UUIDs instead of device names, as device names may change when other disks are added or removed.
l Kernel name descriptors must not be used in configuration files as they are not persistent and may change during each boot. UUIDs or PARTUUIDs are preferred over labels.
l Using only the device name in the absence of UUID or label might cause issues as these names are not unique. This can cause overwrites and eventual loss of an entire volume indexing itself.
l Each volume must be uniquely identified by an identifier like UUID or label. A missing unique identifier (UUID/label) can result in dummy volume names being used instead of actual volumes.

You can determine the UUID by running the blkid command, for example:

# blkid /dev/sdb1 /dev/sdb1 UUID="12345cac-77bc-46b1-9f79-cb180e438c12" TYPE="ext4"

Edit the /etc/fstab as root and for this entry replace the device file name with the returned UUID, for example:

12345cac-77bc-46b1-9f79-cb180e438c12 /mnt/disk1 ext4 defaults

Note: LVM volume entries should not be updated. LVM volumes start with the /dev/mapper prefix, for example: /dev/mapper/centos-root and /dev/mapper/centos-swap.
Repeat these steps for all entries in the /etc/fstab that are not LVM volume entries.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

Amazon Elastic Block Store
Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) is a scalable, high-performance block storage service designed for use with Amazon EC2 instances. EBS volumes function as virtual hard disks and provide persistent storage independent of the lifecycle of the EC2 instance. Cohesity uses AWS EBS Direct APIs to provide agentless, block-level backup and recovery for both standalone and attached EBS volumes.
Important: The backup and recovery of Amazon EBS volume is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS.
Why Use EBS Volume Protection?
You can use EBS volume protection when you need to protect and recover storage volumes independently of the EC2 instances to which they are attached. Key benefits include:
l Independent volume protection - Protect EBS volumes without relying solely on EC2 instance backups.
l Faster and more flexible recovery - Recover individual volumes directly when only the volume data is required.
l Avoid full instance recovery - Restore a specific EBS volume without recovering the entire EC2 instance, reducing recovery time and operational overhead.
l Support for standalone volumes - Protect EBS volumes that are not attached to any EC2 instance.
Plan and Prepare for Amazon EBS Volume Protection
To protect Amazon EBS volume with Cohesity, you must register your AWS account as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. Ensure you meet the pre-requisites and understand the considerations before registering the AWS account. For information on registering AWS account, see Register AWS Source.
Supported Amazon EBS Volume Types
Cohesity supports protection of the following Amazon EBS volume types:
l General Purpose SSD (gp2, gp3) l Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1, io2) l Throughput Optimized HDD (st1) l Cold HDD (sc1)
Required Permissions for EBS Volume Data Protection
For information on the permissions required to protect EBS volume, see Minimum Permissions for Individual Workloads and Workflows.

Considerations for EBS Volume Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect EBS volumes:
l If an EBS volume attached to an EC2 instance is protected through both EC2 instance protection and EBS volume protection, each protection is accounted for independently and contributes separately to protected-size calculations.
l Cohesity does not support: l Restoring an EBS volume to an alternate AWS account or AWS Region. l Restoring an EBS volume directly as an attached volume to an EC2 instance. l File-level recovery (FLR) from EBS volume backups. l EBS volume protection when AWS is registered at the organization level.
l Restores create a new EBS volume in a detached state. l If required, you must manually attach the restored volume to an EC2 instance. l AWS supports up to five pending snapshots per EBS volume. AWS regional snapshot
limits may also affect backup and recovery operations. l Cohesity automatically retries AWS API requests when throttling occurs. Backup and
recovery operations may take longer during periods of high AWS API activity.
Backup Amazon EBS Volume
Depending on the services you selected while registering the AWS source, the Cohesity cluster automatically discovers all supported workloads in the specified AWS account ID. The discovered workloads appear under Data Protection > Sources. When you open the registered AWS account source, each workload type is displayed on its own tab. Select the EBS tab to view all discovered EBS volumes. For more information on registering the AWS, see Register AWS Source. Cohesity discovers both standalone EBS volumes and EBS volumes attached to EC2 instances. You can filter discovered volumes by attachment state:
l Detached (standalone volumes) l Attached l All
The EBS tab displays the entity hierarchy for Amazon EBS, allowing you to navigate from the account level down to individual volumes.

Backup Scope by Amazon EBS Volume Hierarchy
The Cohesity cluster allows you to back Amazon EBS volumes at different levels of the entity hierarchy. You can choose to back up:
l AWS Account - Backup all the Amazon EBS volumes within the registered AWS account.
l AWS Region - Backup all the Amazon EBS volumes within a specific region of the registered account.
l Availability Zone - Backup all the Amazon EBS volumes within a specific availability zone.
l EBS Volume - Backup individual Amazon EBS volume.
Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports both full and incremental backup for Amazon EBS volumes:
l Full backup: The first backup of an EBS volume is always a full backup. l Incremental backup: Subsequent backups capture only the blocks that have
changed since the previous backup, reducing backup time and storage consumption.
The backup behavior depends on the AWS snapshot retention setting configured in the Protection Group for the EBS volume:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

Retain Last AWS Snapshot Enabled
Disabled

Backup Behavior
After the initial full backup, subsequent backups are incremental. The most recent AWS snapshot is retained in your AWS account and used to identify changed blocks for subsequent backups.
After the initial full backup, subsequent backups are also full backups. Because no AWS snapshot is retained after the backup completes, Cohesity cannot identify changed blocks for subsequent backups.

A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. Pause Future Runs

Enable Pause Future Run only if you do not want to schedule future runs of the Protection Group.

End Date

Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.

Retain AWS Snapshot

Use the Retain last AWS snapshot option to retain the most recent AWS EBS snapshot in your AWS account after a backup completes.
When enabled, the most recent AWS snapshot is retained and used to identify changed blocks for incremental backups. Only the changed data is transferred to the Cohesity cluster, which can reduce backup duration and data transfer compared to full backups.
When disabled, the AWS snapshot created during the backup is deleted after the backup completes. Because no previous AWS snapshot is available for comparison, each backup is performed as a full backup.

Note: The first backup of an EBS volume is always a full backup, regardless of the Retain AWS Snapshot setting.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, we recommend the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Manage Amazon EBS Volume Backup Configuration
In the Cohesity, a backup configuration includes a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. You can modify the existing Protection Group and the Protection Policy based on your requirements.
Add Object(s) to the Protection Group
Depending on the Protection Type you chose while creating the Protection Group, you can add new EBS volumes to the existing Protection Group for backup. The newly added object is backed up from the next protection run, and it will be a full backup for the newly added object. To add object(s) to the Protection Group:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for the EBS
volume protection.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit. 4. On the Edit Protection page, click in the Objects section. 5. In the Objects section, click the plus icon (+) to enter multiple objects that you plan
to back up. Click Save Selection. 6. Click Save.
Attach New Protection Policy to the Protection Group
A Protection Policy can be attached to multiple Protection Groups, and any changes in the policy settings impact all the Protection Groups that are associated with the Protection Policy. You can create and attach a new Protection Policy with the required policy settings to your Protection Group. The new policy is applied to the Protection Group from the next scheduled protection run. To attach a new Protection Policy to the Protection Group:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for the EBS
volume protection.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit. 4. In the Policy drop-down list, select the new Protection Policy for the Protection
Group. 5. Click Save.

You can delete a Protection Group if you:

l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots: Allows you to delete the Protection Group and all associated local and archived snapshots. Replicated snapshots must be deleted from the remote cluster. Snapshots under DataLock cannot be deleted.

Amazon Simple Storage Service Bucket
Cohesity's software-defined platform provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective data protection solution for the Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) buckets.
To protect the Amazon S3 bucket, Cohesity leverages the Amazon S3 inventory report. The inventory report contains the list of all the objects available on the Amazon S3 bucket you selected for protection. Cohesity uses this report to perform the first full backup. This report

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Execute the CloudFormation Template

is also used to periodically reconcile the list of objects. The subsequent incremental backups are performed by using the AWS EventBridge capability. With this protection approach, Cohesity can back up multi-billion objects at a faster rate.
Note: l This is an Early Access feature on Physical and Virtual Edition clusters. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature. l This feature is not supported on Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS (formerly known as AWS Cloud Edition cluster) l This feature is Generally Available (GA) on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster).
Plan and Prepare for Amazon S3 Bucket Protection Before protecting your Amazon S3 bucket, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Amazon S3 with Cohesity cluster, you must register your AWS as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.
Supported Amazon S3 Storage Class
Cohesity supports the data protection of the following Amazon Simple Storage Service Bucket (S3) storage class:
l Amazon S3 Standard l Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering l Amazon S3 Standard-IA l Amazon S3 One Zone-IA
Permission for AWS S3 Inventory Report
l To write objects to the Amazon S3 bucket, you must add the S3:PutObject permission to the S3 bucket policy attached to the Amazon S3 bucket where you want to create the inventory report. The following is an example of an Amazon S3 bucket policy that allows s3.amazonaws.com to write (Put) objects in the Amazon S3 bucket:

Execute the CloudFormation Template

{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Id": "S3-Console-Auto-Gen-Policy-1698064515475", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "InventoryAndAnalyticsExamplePolicy", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "Service": "s3.amazonaws.com" }, "Action": [ "s3:PutObject" ], "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::<s3bucketname_you_chose_for_inventory>/*", "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:SourceAccount": "<account_Id>", "s3:x-amz-acl": "bucket-owner-full-control" } } } ]

l If you're using Server-Side Encryption with AWS Key Management Service (SSEKMS) for the bucket where you want to create the inventory report, ensure that the KMS key associated with that bucket has the necessary permissions to allow Amazon S3 to access it. To do this, add the following permissions to the KMS key policy:
{ "Sid": "Allow Amazon S3 use of the KMS key", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "Service": "s3.amazonaws.com" }, "Action": "kms:GenerateDataKey", "Resource": "*"
}
Create a Lifecycle Rule on Amazon S3
To delete the older inventory reports from the Amazon S3 bucket, you must create a lifecycle rule on the Amazon S3 bucket. You can delete all the inventory reports older than 30 days. For information on creating a lifecycle rule, see Amazon documentation.
Create AWS IAM Role for Glue Job
Cohesity uses AWS Glue jobs to process and sort Amazon S3 inventory reports during full and baseline incremental backups of AWS S3 buckets.
For these Glue jobs to run successfully, an AWS IAM role named AWSGlueServiceRole must exist in your AWS account with the required permissions and trust relationship.
If the AWS source is registered at the organization level, ensure that the AWSGlueServiceRole IAM role and permissions are configured in each member account containing Amazon S3 buckets to be protected.
If the AWS source is registered at the account level using IAM role, then the role required for Glue job is created by default.

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

Considerations
l Cohesity does not support: l Browse and recover an object in an Amazon S3 bucket. However, you can recover multiple objects by specifying the object prefix in the recovery task under the S3 Prefixes to Recover option. l The backup of older versions of the Amazon S3 versioned bucket. Only the latest version of the versioned Amazon S3 bucket is backed up. l Cross-region backup and recovery, i.e., the backup and recovery of Amazon S3 buckets located in a different cloud region than where your data is backed up.
l The Amazon S3 buckets where you want to create the inventory report and the Amazon S3 bucket you want to protect must be in the same region.
l If the SQS is deleted between backups, all the changes between these backups will be skipped in the next incremental backups.
l Cohesity will skip the backup of Amazon S3 objects that are present in the following access tiers of the Amazon S3 Intelligent Tiering during the protection: l Archive Access Tier l Deep Archive Access Tier
l Cohesity does not support restoring only metadata. The metadata of Amazon S3 objects will be restored only if the object itself is also restored.
l Cohesity does not remove older inventory reports from the Amazon S3 bucket. Therefore, you must create a lifecycle rule to remove these objects from the Amazon S3 bucket to avoid storage issues.
Backup Amazon S3 Bucket
Depending on the services you selected while registering the source, the Cohesity cluster automatically discovers all supported workloads including Amazon S3 associated with the specified AWS Source. The discovered workloads appear under Data Protection > Sources. When you open the registered AWS source, each workload type is displayed on its own tab. Select the S3 tab to view all discovered S3 buckets. Depending on the registration scope, you can navigate from the organization level or account level down to individual S3 buckets. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.
Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy
Based on the registration level of your AWS source, the S3 tab displays the S3 entity hierarchy, allowing navigation from the organization or account level down to individual S3 buckets. The Amazon S3 entity hierarchy in the Cohesity cluster follows this structure:

Description

The S3 bucket within the AWS source.

Backup Scope by Amazon S3 Hierarchy
The Cohesity cluster allows you to back up Amazon S3 at different levels of the entity hierarchy. Depending on the registration level of your AWS source, you can choose to back up:
l AWS Organization - Protect all S3 buckets across all member accounts in the registered AWS organization.
l Organizational Unit (OU) - Protect all S3 buckets within the member accounts that belong to a specific organizational unit.
l Member Account - Protect all S3 buckets within a specific member account in the registered AWS organization.
l AWS Account - Protect all S3 buckets within the registered standalone AWS account.
l AWS Region - Protect all S3 buckets within a specific AWS Region. l S3 Bucket - Protect an individual S3 bucket.
Backup Process
Cohesity utilizes the Amazon S3 inventory report to protect the Amazon S3 bucket. When you register the AWS source, you can specify the Amazon S3 bucket where you want to create the inventory report. The requirements for this bucket depend on how the source is registered:
l Organization-level registered source: The Amazon S3 bucket you specify must be within the same cloud region as the Amazon S3 buckets selected for protection.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

l Account-level registered source: The Amazon S3 bucket you specify must be within the same account and the same cloud region as the Amazon S3 buckets selected for protection.
When you initiate the Amazon S3 buck et protection, AWS will create an inventory report. It may take up to 48 to 72 hours for AWS to create an inventory report. This inventory report will contain the list of all the objects available on the Amazon S3 bucket you selected for protection. Cohesity uses this inventory report to perform the first full backup of the Amazon S3 bucket. Once Cohesity performs the first full backup, Cohesity utilizes Amazon EventBridge and SQS queues to perform incremental backups of the Amazon S3 bucket. With this protection approach, Cohesity can back up multi-billion Amazon S3 objects at a faster rate.
Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports both full and Incremental backups for Amazon S3.
Protect Amazon S3 Bucket
In Cohesity, Amazon S3 buckets are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Policies.
Before you Begin
Before protecting your Amazon S3 buckets, ensure you have met the prerequisites and understood the considerations. For more information, see Plan and Prepare for Amazon S3 Bucket Protection.

After you protect your Amazon S3 buckets, you can recover them to their original location or a new location using Cohesity.

To recover your protected Amazon S3 buckets to their original location:

2. Search for a S3 bucket or Protection Group that contains the snapshots to recover from by entering characters of the S3 bucket name, Protection Group name, or by specifying the wildcard character *. You can optionally filter the search results by source, Protection Group, or date.
3. From the list of search results, select an S3 bucket you want to recover. By default, the latest snapshot is selected for recovery. To recover from a different snapshot, perform the following steps:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

l Selecting the date from the Choose a date drop-down list. Once you select the date, the Edit recovery point page displays the available snapshots on the specified date.
l Clicking the List tab. The List tab displays all the available snapshots of the selected S3 bucket.
c. Select the snapshots to be recovered.

If the target bucket is versioned and the S3 object name of the target and the source match, then a new version of the S3 object will be created.

For example, Finance/statement/document.
You can click the add icon to provide multiple prefixes.

b. Continue on Error: Enable this option if you want to continue the recovery even if one of the S3 objects encounters an error. By default, this option is

disabled and the recovery operation will fail if one of the objects encounters an error. c. Task Name: Change the default name of the recovery task. 9. Click Recover.

Amazon Aurora MySQL
Amazon Aurora MySQL is a fully managed, MySQL-compatible, cloud-based relational database service offered by Amazon Web Services (AWS). Cohesity natively integrates with AWS to provide a simple, fast, and cost-effective solution for backup, recovery, and data management of Amazon Aurora MySQL clusters.
Backup Methods
You can protect your Amazon Aurora MySQL using one of the following backup methods:
l AWS Snapshot methods: Cohesity uses this option to protect Amazon Aurora MySQL clusters. For protecting the Amazon Aurora MySQL clusters, Cohesity leverages the AWS native snapshot and stores them in the same AWS account and region as the source Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster.
l Ingest method: Cohesity uses this option to protect the Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster at the database level by ingesting the backup data to the Cohesity cluster.
Important: l Cohesity supports the protection of Amazon Aurora MySQL only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster) and Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS.
l On Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS, Cohesity supports the protection of Amazon Aurora MySQL at both the cluster level (via AWS snapshot-based protection) and the database level (via ingest-based protection).
l On Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS, Cohesity supports the backup and recovery of Amazon Aurora MySQL only at the cluster level.

Considerations for AWS Aurora MySQL Data Protection
Review and understand the following considerations before you protect Amazon Aurora MySQL:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

l Cohesity performs only full backup of Amazon Aurora MySQL.
l Cohesity protects only the user databases within the Amazon Aurora MySQL. Protection of system databases are not supported.
l The backup and recovery of Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster at database level is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS.
l Point-in-time restore (PITR) is supported when recovering Amazon Aurora MySQL at cluster-level.
l Restoring a backup taken from a higher Amazon Aurora MySQL database version to a lower version is not supported.
l You cannot perform ingest-based and snapshot-based protections within the same Protection Group.
l If the databases of an Aurora cluster are discovered, then to perform snapshot-based protection, you must select all the databases of that Aurora cluster.
l If you select Aurora clusters for which no databases are discovered, then you cannot perform ingest-based protection.
l Cross-account restore of an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster protected using the AWS Snapshot protection type is not supported.
l When recovering encrypted Aurora clusters to the same AWS account but a different AWS region, you must create a KMS encryption key in the target region with the same alias name as the KMS key used to encrypt the source Aurora cluster.
l When performing cross-region cross-account recovery of an Amazon Aurora cluster encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, ensure the following:
l The source account's KMS key alias is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account.
Example:
If A1 is the source account with region R1, and A2 is the destination account with region R2, ensure the KMS key alias from A1 is available in both R1 and R2 of A2.
l The destination account has permission to access the source account's KMS key alias.
l The option group from the source account is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account.

Description

The AWS organization registered with Cohesity for Aurora MySQL protection. Applicable when the AWS source is registered at the organization level.

The individual databases hosted within the Aurora MySQL cluster.

Additional Settings

Pause Future Runs

End Date

Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Alerts

Optional.
Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
Cohesity natively integrates with AWS to provide a simple, fast, and cost-effective solution for backup, recovery, and data management of Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters.
Backup Methods
You can protect your Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL using one of the following backup methods:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

l AWS Snapshot methods: Cohesity uses this option to protect Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters. For protecting the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters, Cohesity leverages the AWS native snapshot and stores them in the same AWS account and region as the source Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster.
l Ingest method: Cohesity uses this option to protect the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster at the database level by ingesting the backup data to the Cohesity cluster.
Important: l Cohesity supports the protection of Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster) and Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS.
l On Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS, Cohesity supports the protection of Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL at both the cluster level (via AWS snapshotbased protection) and the database level (via ingest-based protection).
l On Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS, Cohesity supports the backup and recovery of Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL only at the cluster level.
This topic provides information on how you can protect Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS.
Plan and Prepare for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Protection
Before protecting Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your AWS as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.
Before You Begin
To protect Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your AWS as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.
Authenticate for Ingest-based Protection
When creating a Protection Group to protect Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL using the Ingestbased protection method, you must authenticate the PostgreSQL client running on the Cohesity cluster to discover the databases of the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster. This can be done using one of the following authentication methods:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

l Username and password of the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters. Ensure the user has the following permissions: l psql -h cluster_fqdn -U postgres l CREATE USER dbuser WITH PASSWORD '<password>' CREATEDB; l GRANT rds_superuser TO dbuser;
l IAM-authenticated PostgreSQL user. If you choose the IAM-authenticated PostgreSQL user method, ensure the following: l Enable IAM DB authentication on the DB cluster: i. From the AWS Management Console, go to RDS Console. ii. Select the DB cluster and click Modify. iii. Scroll to the Database Authentication section. iv. Enable Password and IAM database authentication. v. Click Continue. vi. Choose whether to Apply Immediately or during the next maintenance window, and then click ModifyDBcluster. l Create database user using admin login: l CREATE USER <iamuser> WITH LOGIN; l Grant below role to user l GRANT rds_iam TO <iamuser>; l ALTER ROLE <iamuser> WITH LOGIN CREATEDB; l GRANT rds_superuser TO <iamuser>;
For information on the steps to authenticate the Cohesity cluster to the Amazon Aurora for PostgreSQL in the Cohesity cluster UI, see Protect Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Using Ingest Method.
Ports Used for Communication
For information on port numbers required, see AWS Cloud Database Workloads.
Incremental Backup Requirements
Cohesity supports full and differential incremental backups for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL databases. Incremental backups rely on PostgreSQL logical decoding and replication slots. To enable logical decoding in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, configure the rds.logical_ replication server parameter to 1 in a custom DB parameter group. Perform the following steps in the AWS Console:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

1. Create a custom DB cluster parameter group. 2. Set the rds.logical_replication server parameter to 1. 3. Associate the parameter group with the database instance or cluster. 4. Restart the aurora cluster writer instance to apply the changes. 5. Verify the configuration using the following SQL command:
SHOW wal_level;
Permissions Required to Refresh Materialized Views
To refresh materialized views automatically or manually, the database user must have the required schema and object permissions. For materialized view refresh: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA schema_name TO refresh_user; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA schema_name TO refresh_user; GRANT ALL ON materialized_view_name TO refresh_user; For dependency analysis: GRANT SELECT ON pg_class, pg_namespace, pg_depend, pg_rewrite TO refresh_ user; Replace `schema_name` with your actual schema name. Replace `refresh_user` with the database user configured in your Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Replace `materialized_view_name` with each materialized view name.
Note: If the database user does not have the required permissions, use manual refresh after recovery.
Considerations for AWS Aurora PostgreSQL Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL:
Backup Considerations
Cohesity supports full and differential incremental backups for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: l General Backup Considerations l Replica server databases are not supported for full or incremental backups. l If a full backup fails due to temporary objects, delete the temporary objects manually and run the backup again.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

l Incremental Backup Considerations l Incremental backups are not supported in the following scenarios: l Databases containing Large Objects. l The bytea_output server parameter is set to escape. l The backup user is a non-admin user. l Tables owned by other users do not have a primary key.
l Database Rename Considerations for Incremental Backups l Incremental backups rely on PostgreSQL replication slots to track database changes. Before renaming a protected database, identify the replication slot associated with the database:
SELECT slot_name
FROM pg_replication_slots
WHERE database = '<database_name>';
After renaming the database, drop the existing replication slot:
SELECT pg_drop_replication_slot('<replication_slot_name>');
Failure to remove stale replication slots may impact future incremental backup operations.
Restore Considerations
l Restore of Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL to an EC2 instance running PostgreSQL is not supported.
l Restoring a backup taken from a higher Aurora PostgreSQL database version to a lower version is not supported.
l Restoring security privileges is not supported. l Restore does not fail if the owner or role does not exist on the destination. l Post-restore, the database is associated with the role based on the credentials used
for the destination cluster. l ACLs and permissions for a database are restored only if an IAM-authenticated
PostgreSQL user is attached to the cluster. l Users must modify database ownership manually after restore. l Point-in-time restore (PITR) is supported when recovering Amazon Aurora
PostgreSQL at cluster-level. l Cross-account restore of Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL protected using the AWS
Snapshot protection type is not supported.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

Protection Scope and Configuration Considerations
l Cohesity protects only user databases within Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. System databases are not protected.
l You cannot perform ingest-based and snapshot-based protections within the same Protection Group.
l If databases of a cluster are discovered, you must select all databases of that cluster for snapshot-based protection.
l If you select clusters for which no databases are discovered, ingest-based protection cannot be performed.
l If a full backup fails because of temporary objects, delete the temporary objects manually and run the backup again.
Authentication and User Considerations
l Uppercase usernames are not supported for new users added after PostgreSQL server creation.
l SCRAM authentication configured on a database cluster is not supported.
Naming Restrictions
The following characters are not supported in database names during restore workflows: `, @, , [, ], !, #, %, ^, ., ,, &, *, (, ), <, >, ?, /, |, }, {, ~, :, ', ", ;, +, =, -
Encryption Considerations
l PostgreSQL does not natively provide Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) in standard community deployments. However, PostgreSQL supports application-level and column-level encryption through cryptographic extensions and functions (for example, pgcrypto).
l In Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, encryption at rest is typically provided through AWSmanaged storage encryption mechanisms.
l During protection, backup, and recovery operations, encrypted column data is preserved in its encrypted form. After restore, applications can continue to access and decrypt the data using the appropriate encryption keys and application logic.
l Backup and restore operations do not modify or decrypt application-encrypted column data. You are responsible for maintaining access to the required encryption keys after recovery.
l When recovering encrypted Aurora cluster to the same AWS account but a different AWS region, you must create a KMS encryption key in the target region with the same alias name as the KMS key used to encrypt the source Aurora cluster.
l When performing cross-region cross-account recovery of an Amazon Aurora cluster encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, ensure the following:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

l The source account's KMS key alias is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account.
Example:
If A1 is the source account with region R1, and A2 is the destination account with region R2, ensure the KMS key alias from A1 is available in both R1 and R2 of A2.
l The destination account has permission to access the source account's KMS key alias.
l The option group from the source account is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account.
Backup Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
Depending on the services you selected while registering the source, the Cohesity cluster automatically discovers all supported workloads including Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL associated with the specified AWS source. The discovered workloads appear under Data Protection > Sources. When you open the registered AWS source, each workload type is displayed on its own tab. Select the Aurora PostgreSQL tab to view all discovered clusters.
Based on the registration level of your AWS source, the Aurora PostgreSQL tab displays the entity hierarchy for the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL environment, allowing navigation from the organization or account level down to individual databases.
For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Entity Hierarchy
The Aurora PostgreSQL tab displays the entity hierarchy for the Aurora PostgreSQL, allowing you to navigate from the organization or account level down to individual databases.
The Aurora PostgreSQL entity hierarchy in the Cohesity cluster follows this structure:

Structure

Description

AWS Organization

The AWS organization registered with Cohesity for Aurora PostgreSQL protection. Applicable when the AWS source is registered at the organization level.

Organizational Unit (OU)

Organizational Unit (OU) The organizational units within the AWS organization that contain member accounts.

Member Account The AWS member accounts within the organization that contain Aurora PostgreSQL clusters.

AWS Account

The AWS account registered with Cohesity for Aurora protection. Applicable when the AWS source is registered at the account level.

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

Structure AWS Region Availability Zone Aurora Cluster Database

Description
The AWS region where the Aurora resources reside.
The availability zone within the region where the Aurora cluster is deployed.
The specific Aurora PostgreSQL cluster within the selected availability zone.
The individual databases hosted within the Aurora PostgreSQL cluster. The database will be listed in the entity hierarchy only if you have provided credentials to discover the databases of the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster.

Backup Scope by Aurora PostgreSQL Hierarchy
The Cohesity cluster allows you to back up Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL at different levels of the entity hierarchy. The available hierarchy levels depend on whether the AWS source is registered at the organization level or account level. You can choose to back up:
l AWS Organization - Protect all Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters and databases across all member accounts in the registered AWS organization.
l Organizational Unit (OU) - Protect all Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters and databases within the member accounts that belong to a specific organizational unit.
l Member Account - Protect all Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters and databases within a specific member account in the registered AWS organization.
l AWS Account - Protect all Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters and databases within the registered standalone AWS account.
l AWS Region - Protect all Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters and databases within a specific AWS Region.
l Availability Zone - Protect Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters and databases within a specific Availability Zone.
l Cluster - Protect a specific Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster and all databases hosted on it.
l Database - Protect individual databases within an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster by providing the database credentials.
Aurora PostgreSQL Backup Methods
Cohesity provides the following Protection Types for the protecting Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

l AWS Snapshot method: Cohesity uses this option to protect Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters. For protecting the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters, Cohesity leverages the AWS native snapshot and stores them in the same AWS account and region as the source Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster.
l Ingest method: Cohesity uses this option to protect the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster at the database level by ingesting the backup data to the Cohesity cluster.
Supported Backup Types
Cohesity performs full and incremental backup of Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. Incremental backups capture only the data changes since the last successful backup, helping reduce backup windows, optimize storage consumption, and improve backup efficiency.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Amazon S3 Entity Hierarchy

Section
Additional Settings

Setting

Description

Pause Future Runs

Enable Pause Future Run only if you do not want to schedule future runs of the Protection Group.

Batch Count

Enter the number of records to process in a single batch during a protection run. This value helps balance backup performance and resource utilization on the Aurora PostgreSQL. Higher values can improve throughput but may increase memory and database load. The default value is 1024.

End Date

Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, we recommend the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
