Manage Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Backup Configuration
In the Cohesity, a backup configuration includes a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. You can modify the existing Protection Group and the Protection Policy based on your requirements.
Add Object(s) to the Protection Group
Depending on the Protection Type you chose while creating the Protection Group, you can add new Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL clusters or databases to the existing Protection Group for backup. The newly added object is backed up from the next protection run, and it will be a full backup for the newly added object. To add object(s) to the Protection Group:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for Amazon
Aurora PostgreSQL.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit. 4. On the Edit Protection page, click in the Objects section. 5. In the Objects section, click the plus icon (+) to enter multiple objects that you plan
to back up. Click Save Selection. 6. Click Save.
Attach New Protection Policy to the Protection Group
A Protection Policy can be attached to multiple Protection Groups, and any changes in the policy settings impact all the Protection Groups that are associated with the Protection Policy. You can create and attach a new Protection Policy with the required policy settings to your Protection Group. The new policy is applied to the Protection Group from the next scheduled protection run. To attach a new Protection Policy to the Protection Group:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit. 4. In the Policy drop-down list, select the new Protection Policy for the Protection
Group. 5. Click Save.

Delete the Protection Group

You can delete a Protection Group if you:
l Do not want to retain the backups and the local and archived snapshots that are generated by the Protection Group.
l Want to reclaim the storage space utilized by the Protection Group.
Cohesity provides the following ways to delete a Protection Group:
l Delete Protection Group Only: Allows you to delete the Protection Group. All the backups generated by the Protection Group are preserved till the snapshots expire.
l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots: Allows you to delete the Protection Group and all associated local and archived snapshots. Replicated snapshots must be deleted from the remote cluster. Snapshots under DataLock cannot be deleted.

Note: After deleting the Protection Group, the reclaimed storage space details are not displayed immediately. It will take some time to reflect on the product UI.

b. Select the snapshots to be recovered.
c. By default, the snapshot is recovered from the local Cohesity cluster.

Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Materialized View Refresh After Recovery
When recovering Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL databases, materialized views need to be refreshed to reflect the recovered data. This topic explains the available options for refreshing materialized views and how to choose the right approach for your environment.

What are Materialized Views
Materialized views are database objects that contain the results of a query, stored physically like a table. Unlike regular views, they need to be explicitly refreshed to reflect changes in their underlying base tables.

Why Refresh is Needed After Recovery
After a database recovery operation, materialized views contain stale data from the backup point. The views must be rebuilt to work with the newly recovered data. Without refresh, queries against materialized views will return outdated or incorrect results.

Materialized View Refresh Options
You can refresh the materialized views using one of the following options: l Option 1: Automatic Refresh During Recovery l Option 2: Manual Refresh After Recovery

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Option 1: Automatic Refresh During Recovery
During the recovery workflow, you can enable automatic materialized view refresh using the toggle available under Recovery Options. When to Use
l Use this option in the following scenarios: l Smaller databases where refresh completes quickly l Immediate data consistency is critical l Database credentials have required permissions to refresh materialized views l Longer recovery duration is acceptable Permission Verification Before enabling automatic refresh, verify that the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database user has the required permissions: l To check schema usage
SELECT has_schema_privilege('refresh_user', 'schema_name', 'USAGE');
l Check table select permissions SELECT has_table_privilege('refresh_user', 'table_name', 'SELECT');
l Check materialized view permissions SELECT has_table_privilege('refresh_user', 'materialized_view_name', 'INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE');

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Materialized View Refresh Options

How to Enable When initiating recovery from the Cohesity cluster UI, enable the Refresh materialized views automatically after recovery option under Recovery Options.
Option 2: Manual Refresh After Recovery
Skip automatic refresh during recovery and perform the materialized view refresh separately using the script available in the Cohesity UI. When to Use Use this option in the following scenarios:
l Large databases with materialized views that require significant time to refresh. l AWS source credentials do not have sufficient permissions to refresh materialized
views. l Recovery Time Objective (RTO) requirements demand faster database availability. l Materialized view refresh must be scheduled during off-peak hours. Benefits of Manual Post-Recovery Refresh l Faster Recovery Time: Your database becomes available immediately after recovery. l Controlled Timing: Schedule the refresh during off-peak hours. l Better Resource Management: Avoid resource contention during critical recovery
operations. l Flexibility: DB administrators can monitor and manage the refresh process
independently. l Permission Flexibility: Use a different user with appropriate permissions for refresh
operations. Permission Verification Before refreshing the materialized view manually, verify that the Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database user has the required permissions:
l To check schema usage SELECT has_schema_privilege('refresh_user', 'schema_name', 'USAGE');
l Check table select permissions SELECT has_table_privilege('refresh_user', 'table_name', 'SELECT');
l Check materialized view permissions SELECT has_table_privilege('refresh_user', 'materialized_view_name', 'INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE');

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

How to Use 1. During recovery, leave the Refresh Materialized Views option disabled. 2. Complete the database recovery. 3. Download the refresh script from the Cohesity UI. 4. Run the script manually after recovery.
Download the refresh script In the Cohesity UI:
1. Navigate to Recoveries. 2. Select the PostgreSQL recovery task. 3. Open the Options tab. 4. Locate the Materialized View Refresh section. 5. Download the refresh script. Run the Refresh Script 1. Execute the downloaded script on the recovered database 2. The script automatically determines materialized view dependencies. 3. Materialized views are refreshed in dependency order.
Best Practices
l Assess Your Data Size: For databases with materialized views exceeding several GB, consider manual refresh.
l Verify Permissions: Before using automatic refresh, ensure DataProtect source credentials have required permissions.
l Save the Script: Download and save the refresh script from the recovery details page for future use.
l Test in Non-Production: Validate your chosen approach in test/dev environments first.
l Schedule Appropriately: For manual refresh, run during maintenance windows or low-traffic periods
l Monitor Resources: Materialized view refresh can be resource-intensive; ensure adequate system resources.
l Regular Maintenance: Consider implementing periodic refresh schedules (using tools like pg_cron) independent of recovery operations.
l Document Your Views: Maintain documentation of materialized views and their dependencies.

Amazon Relational Database Service for MySQL
Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) for MySQL is a fully managed, cloud-based relational database service offered by Amazon Web Services (AWS). Cohesity natively integrates with AWS to provide a simple, fast, and cost-effective solution for backup, recovery, and data management of Amazon Relational Database Service for MySQL instances.
Backup Methods
You can protect your Amazon RDS for MySQL using one of the following backup methods:
l AWS Snapshot methods: Cohesity uses this option to protect Amazon RDS for MySQL instances. For protecting the Amazon RDS for MySQL instances, Cohesity leverages the AWS native snapshots and stores them in the same AWS account and region as the source Amazon RDS for MySQL instance.
l Ingest method: Cohesity uses this option to protect the Amazon RDS for MySQL instance at the database level by ingesting the backup data to the Cohesity cluster.
Important: l Cohesity supports the protection of Amazon RDS for MySQL only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster) and Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS.
l On Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS, Cohesity supports the protection of Amazon RDS for MySQL at both the instance level (via AWS snapshot-based protection) and the database level (via ingest-based protection).
l On Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS, Cohesity supports the backup and recovery of Amazon RDS for MySQL only at the instance level.
This topic provides information on how you can protect Amazon RDS for MySQL on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS.
Plan and Prepare for Amazon RDS for MySQL Protection
Before protecting Amazon RDS for MySQL with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Amazon RDS for MySQL with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your AWS as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Considerations for AWS RDS for MySQL Data Protection
Review and understand the following considerations before you protect Amazon RDS for MySQL:
l Cohesity performs only full backup of Amazon RDS for MySQL.
l Cohesity protects only the user databases within the Amazon RDS for MySQL. Protection of system databases are not supported.
l The backup and recovery of Amazon RDS for MySQL instance at database level is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS.
l Restoring a backup taken from a higher RDS MySQL database version to a lower version is not supported.
l Point-in-time restore (PITR) is supported when recovering Amazon RDS for MySQL at instance-level.
l You cannot perform ingest-based and snapshot-based protections within the same Protection Group.
l If the databases of an instance are discovered, then to perform snapshot-based protection, you must select all the databases of that instance.
l If you select instances for which no databases are discovered, then you cannot perform ingest-based protection.
l Cross-account restore of Amazon RDS for MySQL instance protected using the AWS Snapshot protection type is not supported.
l When recovering encrypted Amazon RDS instance to the same AWS account but a different AWS region, you must create a KMS encryption key in the target region with the same alias name as the KMS key used to encrypt the source Amazon RDS instance.
l When performing cross-region cross-account recovery of an Amazon RDS instance encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, ensure the following:
l The source account's KMS key alias is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account.
Example:
If A1 is the source account with region R1, and A2 is the destination account with region R2, ensure the KMS key alias from A1 is available in both R1 and R2 of A2.
l The destination account has permission to access the source account's KMS key alias.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

l The option group from the source account is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account.

The RDS MySQL entity hierarchy in the Cohesity cluster follows this structure:

Structure

Description

AWS Organization

The AWS organization registered with Cohesity for protecting Amazon RDS for MySQL. Applicable when the AWS source is registered at the organization level.

Organizational Unit (OU)

The organizational units within the AWS Organization that contain member accounts.

Member Account The AWS member accounts within the organization that contain Amazon RDS for MySQL.

AWS Account

The AWS account registered with Cohesity for RDS protection. Applicable when the AWS source is registered at the account level.

AWS Region

The AWS region where the RDS resources reside.

Availability Zone

The availability zone within the region where the RDS instance is deployed.

RDS Instance

The specific RDS MySQL instance within the selected availability zone.

Database

The individual databases hosted within the RDS MySQL instance.

Backup Scope by RDS MySQL Hierarchy
The Cohesity cluster allows you to back up Amazon RDS for MySQL at different levels of the entity hierarchy. The available hierarchy levels depend on whether the AWS source is registered at the organization level or account level.

Setting

Pause Future Runs

Enable Pause Future Run only if you do not want to schedule future runs of the Protection Group.

End Date

Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Alerts

Optional.
Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Amazon Relational Database Service for PostgreSQL
Cohesity natively integrates with AWS to provide a simple, fast, and cost-effective solution for backup, recovery, and data management of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instances.
Backup Methods
You can protect your Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL using one of the following backup methods:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

l AWS Snapshot methods: Cohesity uses this option to protect Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instances. For protecting the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instances, Cohesity leverages the AWS native snapshot and stores them in the same AWS account and region as the source Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instance.
l Ingest method: Cohesity uses this option to protect the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instance at the database level by ingesting the backup data to the Cohesity cluster.
Important: l Cohesity supports the protection of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster) and Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS.
l On Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS, Cohesity supports the protection of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL at both the instance level (via AWS snapshotbased protection) and the database level (via ingest-based protection).
l On Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS, Cohesity supports the backup and recovery of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL only at the instance level.
This topic provides information on how you can protect Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS.
Plan and Prepare for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Protection
Before protecting Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your AWS as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.
Authenticate for Ingest-based Protection
When creating a Protection Group to protect Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL using the Ingestbased protection method, you must authenticate the PostgreSQL client running on the Cohesity cluster to discover the databases of the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instance. This can be done using one of the following authentication methods:
l Username and password of the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instances. Ensure the user has the following permissions:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

l psql -h instance_fqdn -U postgres l CREATE USER dbuser WITH PASSWORD '<password>' CREATEDB; l GRANT rds_superuser TO dbuser; l IAM-authenticated PostgreSQL user. If you choose the IAM-authenticated PostgreSQL user method, ensure the following: l Enable IAM DB authentication on the RDS DB instance:
i. From the AWS Management Console, go to RDS Console. ii. Select the DB instance and click Modify. iii. Scroll to the Database Authentication section. iv. Enable Password and IAM database authentication. v. Click Continue. vi. Choose Apply Immediately, and then click ModifyDBinstance. l Create database user using admin login:
l CREATE USER <iamuser> WITH LOGIN; l Grant the following role to user:
l GRANT rds_iam TO <iamuser>; l ALTER ROLE <iamuser> WITH LOGIN CREATEDB; l GRANT rds_superuser TO <iamuser>;
Incremental Backup Requirements
Cohesity supports full and differential incremental backups for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databases. Incremental backups rely on PostgreSQL logical decoding and replication slots. To enable logical decoding in Amazon RDS PostgreSQL and Aurora PostgreSQL, configure the rds.logical_replication server parameter to 1 in a custom DB parameter group. Perform the following steps in the AWS Console:
1. Create a custom DB parameter group. 2. Set the rds.logical_replication server parameter to 1. 3. Associate the parameter group with the database instance or cluster. 4. Restart the RDS instance to apply the changes. 5. Verify the configuration using the following SQL command:
SHOW wal_level;

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Permissions Required to Refresh Materialized Views
To refresh materialized views automatically or manually, the database user must have the required schema and object permissions. For materialized view refresh: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA schema_name TO refresh_user; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA schema_name TO refresh_user; GRANT ALL ON materialized_view_name TO refresh_user; For dependency analysis: GRANT SELECT ON pg_class, pg_namespace, pg_depend, pg_rewrite TO refresh_ user; Replace `schema_name` with your actual schema name. Replace `refresh_user` with the database user configured in your Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. Replace `materialized_view_name` with each materialized view name.
Note: If the database user does not have the required permissions, use manual refresh after recovery.
Ports Used for Communication
For information on port numbers required, see AWS Cloud Database Workloads.
Considerations for AWS RDS for PostgreSQL Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL:
Backup Considerations
Cohesity supports full and differential incremental backups for Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databases.
l General Backup Considerations l Replica server databases are not supported for full or incremental backups. l If a full backup fails due to temporary objects, delete the temporary objects manually and run the backup again.
l Incremental Backup Considerations l Incremental backups are not supported in the following scenarios: l Databases containing large objects.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

l The bytea_output server parameter is set to escape. l The backup user is a non-admin user. l Tables owned by other users do not have a primary key. l Database Rename Considerations for Incremental Backups l Incremental backups rely on PostgreSQL replication slots to track database
changes. Before renaming a protected database, identify the replication slot associated with the database:
SELECT slot_name
FROM pg_replication_slots
WHERE database = '<database_name>';
After renaming the database, drop the existing replication slot:
SELECT pg_drop_replication_slot('<replication_slot_name>');
l Failure to remove stale replication slots may impact future incremental backup operations.
Restore Considerations
l After restoring an incremental backup, the last value of the sequence may not be consistent.
l Restore of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to an EC2 instance running PostgreSQL is not supported.
l Restoring a backup taken from a higher RDS PostgreSQL database version to a lower version is not supported.
l Restoring security privileges is not supported. l Point-in-time restore (PITR) is supported when recovering Amazon RDS for
PostgreSQL at instance-level. l Restore does not fail if the owner or role does not exist on the destination. l Post-restore, the database is associated with the role based on the credentials used
for the destination instance. l ACLs and permissions for a database are restored only if an IAM-authenticated
PostgreSQL user is attached to the instance. l Users must modify database ownership manually after restore. l Cross-account restore of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instance protected using the
AWS Snapshot protection type is not supported.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Protection Scope and Configuration Considerations
l Cohesity protects only user databases within Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. System databases are not protected.
l You cannot perform ingest-based and snapshot-based protections within the same Protection Group.
l If databases of an instance are discovered, you must select all databases of that instance for snapshot-based protection.
l If you select instances for which no databases are discovered, ingest-based protection cannot be performed.
Authentication and User Considerations
l Uppercase usernames are not supported for new users added after PostgreSQL server creation.
l SCRAM authentication configured on a database instance is not supported.
Naming Restrictions
The following characters are not supported in database names during restore workflows: `, @, \, [, ], !, #, %, ^, ., ,, &, *, (, ), <, >, ?, /, |, }, {, ~, :, ', ", ;, +, =, -
Encryption Considerations
l PostgreSQL does not natively provide Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) in standard community deployments. However, PostgreSQL supports application-level and column-level encryption through cryptographic extensions and functions (for example, pgcrypto).
l In Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, encryption at rest is typically provided through AWSmanaged storage encryption mechanisms.
l During protection, backup, and recovery operations, encrypted column data is preserved in its encrypted form. After restore, applications can continue to access and decrypt the data using the appropriate encryption keys and application logic.
l Backup and restore operations do not modify or decrypt application-encrypted column data. You are responsible for maintaining access to the required encryption keys after recovery.
l When recovering encrypted RDS intance to the same AWS account but a different AWS region, you must create a KMS encryption key in the target region with the same alias name as the KMS key used to encrypt the source RDS intance .
l When performing cross-region cross-account recovery of an Amazon RDS intance encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, ensure the following: l The source account's KMS key alias is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Example:
If A1 is the source account with region R1, and A2 is the destination account with region R2, ensure the KMS key alias from A1 is available in both R1 and R2 of A2.
l The destination account has permission to access the source account's KMS key alias.
l The option group from the source account is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account.
Backup Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
Depending on the services you selected while registering the source, the Cohesity cluster automatically discovers all supported workloads including Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL associated with the specified AWS source. The discovered workloads appear under Data Protection > Sources. When you open the registered AWS account source, each workload type is displayed on its own tab. Select the RDS PostgreSQL tab to view all discovered instances.
The RDS PostgreSQL tab displays the entity hierarchy for the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL environment, allowing you to navigate from the account level down to individual databases. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.
The RDS PostgreSQL entity hierarchy in the Cohesity cluster follows this structure:

Structure

Description

AWS Organization

The AWS Organization registered with Cohesity for RDS PostgreSQL protection. Applicable when the AWS source is registered at the organization level.

Organization Unit

The organizational units within the AWS Organization that contain member accounts.

Member Account

The AWS member accounts within the Organization that contain RDS PostgreSQL instances.

AWS Account

The AWS account registered with Cohesity for RDS protection. Applicable when the AWS source is registered at the account level.

AWS Region

The AWS region where the RDS resources reside.

Availability Zone The availability zone within the region where the RDS instance is deployed.

RDS Instance

The specific RDS PostgreSQL instance within the selected availability zone.

Database

The individual databases hosted within the RDS PostgreSQL instance. The database will be listed in the entity hierarchy only if you have provided credentials to discover the databases of the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instance.

Best Practices

Backup Scope by RDS PostgreSQL Hierarchy
The Cohesity cluster allows you to back up Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL at different levels of the entity hierarchy. The available hierarchy levels depend on whether the AWS source is registered at the organization level or account level.
You can choose to back up:
l AWS Organization - Protect all RDS for PostgreSQL instances and databases across all member accounts in the registered AWS Organization.
l Organizational Unit (OU) - Protect all RDS for PostgreSQL instances and databases within the member accounts that belong to a specific organizational unit.
l Member Account - Protect all RDS for PostgreSQL instances and databases within a specific member account in the registered AWS organization.
l AWS Account - Protect all RDS for PostgreSQL instances and databases within the registered standalone AWS account.
l AWS Region - Protect all RDS for PostgreSQL instances and databases within a specific AWS region.
l Availability Zone - Protect RDS for PostgreSQL instances and databases within a specific Availability Zone.
l RDS Instance - Protect a specific RDS for PostgreSQL instance and all databases hosted on it.
l Database - Protect individual databases within an RDS for PostgreSQL instance by providing the database credentials.
RDS for PostgreSQL Backup Methods
Cohesity provides the following Protection Types for protecting the Amazon RDS PostgreSQL:
l AWS Snapshot method: Cohesity uses this option to protect Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instances. For protecting the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instances, Cohesity leverages the AWS native snapshot and stores them in the same AWS account and region as the source Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instance.
l Ingest method: Cohesity uses this option to protect the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL instance at the database level by ingesting the backup data to the Cohesity cluster.
Supported Backup Types
Cohesity performs full and incremental backup of Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. Incremental backups capture only the data changes since the last successful backup, helping reduce backup windows, optimize storage consumption, and improve backup efficiency.

Enter the number of records to process in a single batch during a protection run. This value helps balance backup performance and resource utilization on the PostgreSQL instance. Higher values can improve throughput but may increase memory and database load. The default value is 1024.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, we recommend the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

What are Materialized Views

Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Materialized View Refresh After Recovery
When recovering Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databases, materialized views need to be refreshed to reflect the recovered data. This topic explains the available options for refreshing materialized views and how to choose the right approach for your environment.

What are Materialized Views
Materialized views are database objects that contain the results of a query, stored physically like a table. Unlike regular views, they need to be explicitly refreshed to reflect changes in their underlying base tables.

Why Refresh is Needed After Recovery
After a database recovery operation, materialized views contain stale data from the backup point. The views must be rebuilt to work with the newly recovered data. Without refresh, queries against materialized views will return outdated or incorrect results.

Materialized View Refresh Options
You can refresh the materialized views using one of the following options: l Option 1: Automatic Refresh During Recovery l Option 2: Manual Refresh After Recovery

Comparison of Refresh Options

Factor

Automatic Refresh Manual Refresh

Database Size

Small to medium

Large

Refresh Duration

Short

Large

Recovery Time Objective Flexible

Strict

Permissions Available

Yes

Strict

Scheduling Flexibility

Low

High

Administrative Control

Minimal

Greater

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Materialized View Refresh Options

Option 1: Automatic Refresh During Recovery
During the recovery workflow, you can enable automatic materialized view refresh using the toggle available under Recovery Options. When to Use
l Use this option in the following scenarios: l Smaller databases where refresh completes quickly l Immediate data consistency is critical l Database credentials have required permissions to refresh materialized views l Longer recovery duration is acceptable Permission Verification Before enabling automatic refresh, verify that the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database user has the required permissions: l To check schema usage
SELECT has_schema_privilege('refresh_user', 'schema_name', 'USAGE');
l Check table select permissions SELECT has_table_privilege('refresh_user', 'table_name', 'SELECT');
l Check materialized view permissions SELECT has_table_privilege('refresh_user', 'materialized_view_name', 'INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE');
How to Enable When initiating recovery from the Cohesity cluster UI, enable the Refresh materialized views automatically after recovery option under Recovery Options.
Option 2: Manual Refresh After Recovery
Skip automatic refresh during recovery and perform the materialized view refresh separately using the script available in the Cohesity UI. When to Use Use this option in the following scenarios:
l Large databases with materialized views that require significant time to refresh. l AWS source credentials do not have sufficient permissions to refresh materialized
views. l Recovery Time Objective (RTO) requirements demand faster database availability. l Materialized view refresh must be scheduled during off-peak hours.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Materialized View Refresh Options

Benefits of Manual Post-Recovery Refresh l Faster Recovery Time: Your database becomes available immediately after recovery. l Controlled Timing: Schedule the refresh during off-peak hours. l Better Resource Management: Avoid resource contention during critical recovery operations. l Flexibility: DB administrators can monitor and manage the refresh process independently. l Permission Flexibility: Use a different user with appropriate permissions for refresh operations.
Permission Verification Before refreshing the materialized view manually, verify that the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database user has the required permissions:
l To check schema usage SELECT has_schema_privilege('refresh_user', 'schema_name', 'USAGE');
l Check table select permissions SELECT has_table_privilege('refresh_user', 'table_name', 'SELECT');
l Check materialized view permissions SELECT has_table_privilege('refresh_user', 'materialized_view_name', 'INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE');
How to Use 1. During recovery, leave the Refresh Materialized Views option disabled. 2. Complete the database recovery. 3. Download the refresh script from the Cohesity UI. 4. Run the script manually after recovery.
Download the refresh script In the Cohesity UI:
1. Navigate to Recoveries. 2. Select the PostgreSQL recovery task. 3. Open the Options tab. 4. Locate the Materialized View Refresh section. 5. Download the refresh script.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Run the Refresh Script
1. Execute the downloaded script on the recovered database 2. The script automatically determines materialized view dependencies. 3. Materialized views are refreshed in dependency order.
Best Practices
l Assess Your Data Size: For databases with materialized views exceeding several GB, consider manual refresh.
l Verify Permissions: Before using automatic refresh, ensure DataProtect source credentials have required permissions.
l Save the Script: Download and save the refresh script from the recovery details page for future use.
l Test in Non-Production: Validate your chosen approach in test/dev environments first.
l Schedule Appropriately: For manual refresh, run during maintenance windows or low-traffic periods
l Monitor Resources: Materialized view refresh can be resource-intensive; ensure adequate system resources.
l Regular Maintenance: Consider implementing periodic refresh schedules (using tools like pg_cron) independent of recovery operations.
l Document Your Views: Maintain documentation of materialized views and their dependencies.
Amazon Relational Database Service for Oracle
Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) for Oracle is a fully managed service offered by Amazon Web Services (AWS) that simplifies the deployment, operation, and scaling of Oracle Database in the cloud. Cohesity natively integrates with AWS to provide a simple, fast, and cost-effective solution for backup, recovery, and data management of Amazon RDS for Oracle.
Backup Methods
You can protect your Amazon RDS for Oracle using one of the following backup methods:
l AWS Snapshot methods: For protecting the Amazon RDS for Oracle, Cohesity leverages the AWS native snapshot and stores them in the same AWS account and region as the source Amazon RDS for Oracle.
l Ingest method: Cohesity uses this option to protect Amazon RDS for Oracle by ingesting the backup data into the Cohesity cluster. During a restore operation,

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Cohesity does not rely on connectivity to AWS RDS Service. Instead, restoration requires connectivity only to the Cohesity cluster where the backups reside and the EC2 target VM.
Important: l Cohesity supports the protection of Amazon RDS for Oracle only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster) and Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS.
l Cohesity supports both AWS snapshot-based protection and ingest-based protection of Amazon RDS for Oracle on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster).
l On Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS (formerly known as AWS Cloud Edition cluster), Cohesity supports only ingest-based protection of Amazon RDS for Oracle.
l The ingest-based protection of Amazon RDS for Oracle on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
This topic provides information on how you can protect Amazon RDS for Oracle on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS.
Plan and Prepare for Amazon RDS for Oracle Protection
Before protecting Amazon RDS for Oracle with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Amazon RDS for Oracle with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your AWS as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.
Authenticate for Ingest-based Protection
To protect Amazon RDS for Oracle using the Ingest-based protection method, you must authenticate by providing the username and password of an Amazon RDS for Oracle instance user. These credentials are required for Cohesity to connect to the Oracle instance and initiate backup operations. For CDB-enabled databases, Cohesity must connect to one of the PDBs. In this case, the credentials must be provided in the following format: Username: {PDB username}@{PDB name} Password: Corresponding PDBs password

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Example:
l Consider a CDB named CDB that contains two PDBs: PDB1 and PDB2. The credentials for these PDBs are as follows:
l PDB1: pdb1admin/Mynameis1pwd l PDB2: pdb2admin/Mynameis2pwd
When adding credentials for the CDB database (CDB) during protection, you can choose either of the following:
l Pdb1admin@PDB1: In this case use the password Mynameis1pwd l Pdb2admin@PDB2: In this case use the password Mynameis2pwd
For information on the steps to authenticate the Cohesity cluster to the Amazon RDS for Oracle in the Cohesity cluster UI, see Protect Amazon RDS for Oracle Using Ingest Method.
AWS S3 Staging Bucket Requirement
For ingest-based backup of Amazon RDS Oracle, Cohesity uses an Amazon S3 staging bucket as temporary storage.You can either allow Cohesity to automatically create the staging bucket when you initiate a backup or recovery task, or you can manually create the staging bucket in your AWS account before starting the process. You must use the same bucket for both backup and recovery. If you choose to manually create the bucket, ensure to create the AWS S3 bucket of type, S3 Standard in the same AWS region as the database selected for backup and restore. You can specify only one custom bucket name per Protection Group. Because an S3 bucket belongs to a single AWS region, a custom bucket is supported only when all databases in the Protection Group are in the same region. If your Protection Group spans multiple regions, use the Auto Create option instead.
Note: Cohesity supports adding custom tags to S3 staging buckets when the auto-create staging bucket option is selected. Tags are applied Cohesity clusterwide across all AWS registrations on that Cohesity cluster. To configure tags for S3 staging bucket, contact Cohesity Support.
Ports Used for Communication
For information on port numbers required, seeAWS Cloud Database Workloads.
(Optional) Encrypt Data to be Protected
Optionally, if you want to encrypt the data to be protected, you can enable the NNE (Native Network Encryption) option for RDS Oracle.

Considerations for AWS RDS for Oracle Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect Amazon RDS for Oracle:
l Cohesity supports only full backups for Amazon RDS for Oracle instances. Even if you choose an incremental-based policy, Cohesity will always perform a full backup, regardless of the selected policy type.
l Incremental and log backups are not supported.
l Do not select a log-backup-based policy, as log backups are not supported. The backup will fail if you select a log-based policy.
l Tune the section size and the number of parallel streams based on the database size for optimal performance.
l Group databases of similar size into the same Protection Group to improve overall performance.
l Cross-account restore of Amazon RDS for Oracle protected using the AWS Snapshot protection type is not supported.
l When you use the Specify Bucket to Use option, you can specify only one bucket name per Protection Group. Because an S3 bucket resides in a single AWS region, this option is not supported in scenarios where databases from multiple regions or accounts might be protected together, such as:
l Auto-protect at the AWS Account, OU, or Organization level.
l Tag-based auto-protection.
l A Protection Group that includes databases from multiple AWS regions.
l AWS Organization registration spanning multiple accounts with databases.
l For these scenarios, use the Auto Create option to allow Cohesity to automatically create the appropriate staging bucket per region.
l When recovering (snapshot-based) encrypted RDS instance to the same AWS account but a different AWS region, you must create a KMS encryption key in the target region with the same alias name as the KMS key used to encrypt the source RDS instance.
l When performing cross-region cross-account recovery (snapshot-based) of an Amazon RDS instance encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, ensure the following:
l The source account's KMS key alias is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account.
Example:
If A1 is the source account with region R1, and A2 is the destination account with region R2, ensure the KMS key alias from A1 is available in both R1 and R2 of A2.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

l The destination account has permission to access the source account's KMS key alias.
l The option group from the source account is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account.
Backup Amazon RDS for Oracle
Depending on the services you selected while registering the source, the Cohesity cluster automatically discovers all supported workloads including Amazon RDS for Oracle associated with the specified AWS source. The discovered workloads appear under Data Protection > Sources. When you open the registered AWS source, each workload type is displayed on its own tab. Select the RDS Oracle tab to view all discovered instances. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source. Based on the registration level of your AWS source, the RDS Oracle tab displays the entity hierarchy for the Amazon RDS for Oracle, allowing navigation from the organization or account level down to individual instances.

Backup Scope by RDS for Oracle Hierarchy
The Cohesity cluster allows you to back up Amazon RDS for Oracle at different levels of the entity hierarchy. You can choose to back up:
l AWS Organization - Protect all RDS for Oracle instances across all member accounts in the registered AWS organization.
l Organizational Unit (OU) - Protect all RDS for Oracle instances within the member accounts that belong to a specific organizational unit.
l Member Account - Protect all RDS for Oracle instances within a specific member account in the registered AWS organization.
l AWS Account - Backup all the Amazon RDS for Oracle instances within the registered AWS account.
l AWS Region - Backup all the Amazon RDS for Oracle instances within a specific region of the registered account.
l RDS for Oracle instance - Backup individual Amazon RDS for Oracle instance.
Backup Process
AWS Snapshot Method
When you initiate a protection run using the AWS Snapshot method, Cohesity triggers a native AWS RDS snapshot of the selected Amazon RDS for Oracle instance. The snapshot is created and stored directly within the same AWS account and region as the source instance, leveraging AWS's built-in snapshot infrastructure.
Ingest Method
When you initiate a protection run in the Cohesity cluster to back up Amazon RDS for Oracle, Cohesity first exports the selected instance data to an Amazon S3 staging bucket. Once the data is successfully exported to the S3 bucket, Cohesity ingests the staged data from the S3 bucket into the Cohesity cluster. Once the ingestion is successful and the data

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

is fully backed up to the cluster, Cohesity automatically deletes the exported data from the staging bucket to free up storage and minimize S3 costs.
Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports only full backups for Amazon RDS for Oracle instances. Incremental and log backups are not supported.
Protect Amazon RDS for Oracle Using Ingest Method
In Cohesity, Amazon RDS for Oracle instances are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Policies. With the Ingest protection method, Cohesity protects Amazon RDS for Oracle by ingesting the backup data into the Cohesity cluster.
Prerequisites
Choose Staging Bucket
Before initiating a backup of Amazon RDS for Oracle instances, ensure that an Amazon S3 staging bucket is available in the AWS account where the Amazon RDS for Oracle instances reside. This bucket is used to temporarily store exported data during the backup process. You can manually specify a new or existing S3 bucket in your AWS account, or allow Cohesity to automatically create one when the backup process begins.
AWS Source Registered at the Account Level
When creating a Protection Group, you can manually specify an S3 bucket only if all selected RDS for Oracle instances belong to the same AWS account and region. If all selected RDS for Oracle instances are in the same AWS account and region: You can manually specify a newly created or existing S3 bucket, or allow Cohesity to automatically create one. If you are manually specifying an S3 bucket, ensure the S3 bucket is in the same AWS account and region as the selected RDS for Oracle instances.
If the selected RDS for Oracle instances span multiple regions:
You must allow allow Cohesity to automatically create the staging bucket. If you manually specify a newly created or existing S3 bucket, the backup will fail.
AWS Source Registered at the Organization Level
When protecting RDS for Oracle instances across member accounts, you can manually specify an S3 bucket only if all selected RDS for Oracle instances for protection belong to the same member account and region as the specified S3 bucket.

If the selected RDS for Oracle instances span multiple AWS member accounts or regions: You must allow allow Cohesity to automatically create the staging bucket. QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, we recommend the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Manage Amazon RDS for Oracle Backup Configuration
In the Cohesity, a backup configuration includes a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. You can modify the existing Protection Group and the Protection Policy based on your requirements.
Add Object(s) to the Protection Group
Depending on the Protection Type you chose while creating the Protection Group, you can add new Amazon RDS for Oracle instances or databases to the existing Protection Group for backup. The newly added object is backed up from the next protection run, and it will be a full backup for the newly added object. To add object(s) to the Protection Group:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for Amazon
RDS for Oracle.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit. 4. On the Edit Protection page, click in the Objects section. 5. In the Objects section, click the plus icon (+) to enter multiple objects that you plan
to back up. Click Save Selection. 6. Click Save.
Attach New Protection Policy to the Protection Group
A Protection Policy can be attached to multiple Protection Groups, and any changes in the policy settings impact all the Protection Groups that are associated with the Protection Policy. You can create and attach a new Protection Policy with the required policy settings to your Protection Group. The new policy is applied to the Protection Group from the next scheduled protection run. To attach a new Protection Policy to the Protection Group:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for
Amazon RDS for Oracle.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit. 4. In the Policy drop-down list, select the new Protection Policy for the Protection
Group. 5. Click Save.
Pause Future Protection Runs
You can pause future protection runs of the Protection Group from executing. However, if the Protection Group is currently executing a protection run, the current run continues to

Best Practices

execute and only future runs of the Protection Group are paused. To pause future protection run:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for
Amazon RDS for Oracle.

Delete the Protection Group

You can delete a Protection Group if you:
l Do not want to retain the backups and the local and archived snapshots that are generated by the Protection Group.
l Want to reclaim the storage space utilized by the Protection Group.
Cohesity provides the following ways to delete a Protection Group:
l Delete Protection Group Only: Allows you to delete the Protection Group. All the backups generated by the Protection Group are preserved till the snapshots expire.
l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots: Allows you to delete the Protection Group and all associated local and archived snapshots. Replicated snapshots must be deleted from the remote cluster. Snapshots under DataLock cannot be deleted.

Note: After deleting the Protection Group, the reclaimed storage space details are not displayed immediately. It will take some time to reflect on the product UI.

Recover RDS for Oracle
You can recover RDS for Oracle instance using one of the following methods:
l Recover Amazon RDS for Oracle Using Snapshot Method l Recover Amazon RDS for Oracle Using Ingest Method
Recover Amazon RDS for Oracle Using Ingest Method
If you choose to recover the Amazon RDS for Oracle using the ingest method, then you can recover the Amazon RDS for Oracle instance as a standalone instance on an EC2 instance of the same AWS account or a different AWS account.
Prerequisites
Before recovering an Amazon RDS for Oracle instance as a standalone database on an EC2 instance, ensure the following:
l Oracle Software Installation: The target EC2 instance must have Oracle software installed. The Oracle software version must match the version of the source RDS for Oracle instance. l If the target Oracle version matches the source version, no additional configuration is required. l If the target Oracle version is newer than the source, you may need to manually set the COMPATIBLE parameter in the pfile during recovery. The value should match the source database's compatibility version.
l Database Instance: The database instance you are recovering must not already exist on the target EC2 instance.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

l Free Space: The EC2 instance must have sufficient free space to restore the database.
l Cohesity Agent: The Cohesity Agent must be running on the EC2 instance (this applies only to Linux-based Oracle databases).
l OS Authentication: If the Cohesity Agent is running as a non-root, non-oracle user, OS authentication must be enabled for that user.
Recover Amazon RDS for Oracle
To recover Amazon RDS for Oracle:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Recoveries.
2. Click Recover at the top right of the page and then select AWS > RDS Oracle.
3. Select Ingest as the Recovery Task.
4. Search for the instance by entering the instance name or a partial name, or use the wildcard character (*) to view all available instances.
5. From the list of search results, select the instance to recover. By default, the latest snapshot of the instance is selected for recovery. To recover from a different snapshot, perform the following steps depending on the instance selected:
From the selected lists, mouse over the snapshot, and then click the edit icon. The Edit recovery point for <instance_name> page appears. Amazon Relational Database Service for Microsoft SQL Server
Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) for SQL Server is a fully managed relational database service offered by Amazon Web Services (AWS) that simplifies the deployment, operation, and scaling of Microsoft SQL Server databases in the cloud. Cohesity natively integrates with AWS to provide a simple, fast, and cost-effective solution for the backup, recovery, and data management of Amazon Relational Database Service for Microsoft SQL Server (MS SQL) databases, including databases enabled with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE).
Backup Method
Cohesity uses the Ingest method to protect Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server databases. With this approach, Cohesity exports database-level data from Amazon RDS for MS SQL to an Amazon S3 staging bucket, then ingests the data into the Cohesity cluster for backup. In addition to full backups, Cohesity supports cumulative incremental backups, which capture all changes since the most recent full backup. Incremental backups always depend on the last successful full backup.
Important: l Cohesity supports the protection of Amazon RDS for MS SQL only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster) and Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS .
l On Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS, Cohesity supports the protection of Amazon RDS for MS SQL at both the instance level (via AWS snapshotbased protection) and the database level (via ingest-based protection).
l On Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS, Cohesity supports the backup and recovery of Amazon RDS for MS SQL only at the instance level.
Plan and Prepare for Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server Protection
Before protecting Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your AWS as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.
Ports Used for Communication
For information on port numbers required, see AWS Cloud Database Workloads.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Authentication Requirement
When creating a Protection Group to protect the Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server at database level, you must authenticate the Cohesity cluster to discover the databases of the Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server instance using the credentials of the RDS for MS SQL Server instance. You can provide either the credentials of:
l Admin user, or l Custom database user
If you are providing the Custom user credentials of RDS for MS SQL Server instance, then ensure the followings:
l The SQL user has the following permissions on the database:
-- Create a login on the SQL Server CREATE LOGIN dbuser WITH PASSWORD = ''; -- Create a database user mapped to the login CREATE USER [dbuser] FOR LOGIN [dbuser]; -- Add the user to the db_owner role ALTER ROLE [db_owner] ADD MEMBER [dbuser];
l The custom user is not a part of any database deny role such as db_denydatareader, db_denydatawriter. These roles prevent discovery and backup operations.
For information on the steps to authenticate the Cohesity cluster to the Amazon RDS for MS SQL in the Cohesity cluster UI, see Protect Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server Using Ingest Method.
AWS S3 Staging Bucket Requirement
For ingest-based backup and recovery of Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server databases, Cohesity uses an Amazon S3 staging bucket as temporary storage. You can either allow Cohesity to automatically create the staging bucket when you initiate a backup or recovery task, or you can manually create the staging bucket in your AWS account before starting the process. You must use the same bucket for both backup and recovery. If you choose to manually create the bucket, ensure to create the AWS S3 bucket of type, S3 Standard in the same AWS region as the database selected for backup and restore. You can specify only one custom bucket name per Protection Group. Because an S3 bucket belongs to a single AWS region, a custom bucket is supported only when all databases in the Protection Group are in the same region. If your Protection Group spans multiple regions, use the Auto Create option instead.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Best Practices

Note: Cohesity supports adding custom tags to S3 staging buckets when the auto-create staging bucket option is selected. Tags are applied Cohesity clusterwide across all AWS registrations on that Cohesity cluster. To configure tags for S3 staging bucket, contact Cohesity Support.
Configure Option Group
An Option group is required as the RDS for MS SQL Server backup and restore operations use the SQLSERVER_BACKUP_RESTORE option, which enables native backup and restore integration with Amazon S3. Perform the following steps to configure Option Group:

1. From the AWS Management console, open the Option Group created. 2. Click Add Option. 3. Select SQLSERVER_BACKUP_RESTORE.

4. Select CohesityBackupS3StagingRole as IAM role to grant write access to staging S3 bucket.

Considerations for Amazon RDS for MS SQL Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server databases:
Backup Capabilities and Behavior
l Cohesity supports full and cumulative incremental backups for Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server databases.
l Incremental backups are cumulative and depend on the most recent full backup. l If the last full backup is unavailable, incremental restore is not possible. l For Multi-AZ RDS instances, automated backups cannot be disabled and may cause
more frequent fallback to full backups.
Backup Prerequisites and Requirements
l The RDS for MS SQL Server instance must be in an available state for Cohesity to initiate a backup.
l Backups cannot be initiated if the server is offline or unavailable. l The staging buckets used for temporarily storing data during backup and recovery
must be located in the same AWS region as: l The database being protected, and l The selected recovery target.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Protection Policy Constraints
l You cannot perform ingest-based and snapshot-based protections within the same protection group.
l If you select databases for protection, you cannot choose a snapshot-based policy. l If you select instances with no databases discovered, you cannot choose an ingest-
based policy.
Restore Limitations and Scope
l Restoring a backup taken from a higher RDS for MS SQL Server database version to a lower version is not supported.
l Restoring to another AWS region within the same AWS account is supported. l Restoring to a different AWS account is not supported. l Incremental restore is supported only to single-AZ RDS instances. l Point-in-time restore (PITR) is supported when recovering Amazon RDS for MS SQL at
instance-level. l Cross-account restore of Amazon RDS for MS SQL instance protected using the AWS
Snapshot protection type is not supported.
Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) Considerations
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
l Cohesity backs up only databases, not TDE certificates. l You are responsible for managing TDE certificates in Amazon RDS. l To restore a TDE-enabled database to a different MS SQL Server instance:
l First back up the TDE certificate from the source instance. l Then restore the certificate to the target instance before performing the
database restore from the Cohesity cluster UI. For information on the backup and restore of TDE certificate, see the AWS documentation.
KMS Encryption and Cross-Region/Cross-Account Recovery
l When recovering encrypted RDS instances to the same AWS account but a different AWS region, you must create a KMS encryption key in the target region with the same alias name as the KMS key used to encrypt the source RDS instance.
l When performing cross-region cross-account recovery of an Amazon RDS instance encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, ensure the following:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

l The source account's KMS key alias is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account.
Example: If A1 is the source account with region R1, and A2 is the destination account with region R2, ensure the KMS key alias from A1 is available in both R1 and R2 of A2.
l The destination account has permission to access the source account's KMS key alias. l The option group from the source account is available in both the source and
destination regions of the destination account.
Custom Staging Bucket and Multi-Region Considerations
When you use the Specify Bucket to Use option, you can specify only one bucket name per Protection Group. Because an S3 bucket resides in a single AWS region, this option is not supported in scenarios where databases from multiple regions or accounts might be protected together, such as:
l Auto-protect at the AWS Account, OU, or Organization level. l Tag-based auto-protection. l A Protection Group that includes databases from multiple AWS regions. l AWS Organization registration spanning multiple accounts with databases. l For these scenarios, use the Auto Create option to allow Cohesity to automatically
create the appropriate staging bucket per region.

Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server Hierarchy
The Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server entity hierarchy in the Cohesity cluster follows this structure:

Structure

Description

AWS Organization

The AWS organization registered with Cohesity for RDS for MS SQL protection. Applicable when the AWS source is registered at the organization level.

Organizational Unit (OU)

The organizational units within the AWS organization that contain member accounts.

Member Account The AWS member accounts within the organization that contain RDS for MS SQL Server instances.

AWS Account

The AWS account registered with Cohesity for protecting Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server databases. Applicable when the AWS source is registered at the account level.

AWS Region

The AWS region where the RDS resources reside.

Availability Zone

The availability zone within the region where the RDS instance is deployed.

RDS MS SQL Server Instance

The specific RDS for MS SQL Server instance within the selected availability zone.

RDS MS SQL Server Database

The individual databases hosted within the RDS for MS SQL Server instance. The database will be listed in the entity hierarchy only if you have provided credentials to discover the databases of the Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server instance.

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Backup Scope by RDS for Microsoft SQL Server Hierarchy
The Cohesity cluster allows you to back up Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server at different levels of the entity hierarchy. The available hierarchy levels depend on whether the AWS source is registered at the organization level or account level.
l AWS Organization - Protect all RDS for MS SQL Server instances and databases across all member accounts in the registered AWS organization.
l Organizational Unit (OU) - Protect all RDS for MS SQL Server instances and databases within the member accounts that belong to a specific organizational unit.
l Member Account - Protect all RDS for MS SQL Server instances and databases within a specific member account in the registered AWS organization.
l AWS Account - Backup all the Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server databases within the registered AWS account.
l AWS Region - Backup all the Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server databases within a specific region of the registered account.
l Availability Zone - Protect Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server databases within a specific availability zone.
l RDS MS SQL Server Instance - Backup all Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server databases within a specific database instance.
l RDS MS SQL Server Databases - Backup individual Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server database.
Backup Process
AWS Snapshot Method
When you initiate a protection run using the AWS Snapshot method, Cohesity triggers a native AWS RDS snapshot of the selected Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server instance. The snapshot is created and stored directly within the same AWS account and region as the source instance, leveraging AWS's built-in snapshot infrastructure.
Ingest Method
When you initiate a protection run in the Cohesity cluster to back up Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server databases, Cohesity first exports the selected database data to an Amazon S3 staging bucket. Once the data is successfully exported to the S3 bucket, Cohesity ingests the staged data from the S3 bucket into the Cohesity cluster. Once the ingestion is successful and the data is fully backed up to the Cohesity cluster, Cohesity automatically deletes the exported data from the staging bucket to free up storage and minimize S3 costs.
Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports full and cumulative incremental backups. The first protection run after the initial backup configuration or upgrade is always a full backup. The subsequent

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

protection runs perform cumulative incremental (differential) backups. Each incremental backup contains all changes since the most recent full backup. Incremental backups fall back to full backup if:
l An automated full backup or a snapshot (initiated from the MS SQL Server databases) was taken after the last successful full backup initiated by Cohesity.
Note: It is recommended to disable automated backups to prevent frequent fallbacks to full backups.
l No prior full backup exists.
Note: Cumulative incremental backup support is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Protect Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server Using Ingest Method
With the Ingest protection method, Cohesity cluster protects the Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server of your AWS source at the database level. In Cohesity, Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server databases are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Policies.
Note: The backup and recovery of Transparent Data Encryption (TDE)-enabled Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server databases is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Prerequisites
Choose Staging Bucket
Before initiating a backup of Amazon Web Services Amazon RDS for MS SQL Server at database, an Amazon S3 staging bucket must be available in the AWS account where the RDS for MS SQL Server resources reside. This bucket is used to temporarily store exported data during the backup process. You can manually create or select an existing S3 bucket in your AWS account, or allow Cohesity to automatically create one when the backup process begins.

l Auto Create: Cohesity automatically creates a temporary AWS S3 staging bucket in the same region as your RDS for MS SQL Server databases selected for backup. The bucket follows the naming format: cohe-<source-id><region-name>. Where, l source-id is the AWS account ID. l region-name is the AWS region where the database reside.
l Specify Bucket to Use: Enter the name of an existing AWS S3 bucket in the same region and account as the databases being protected. If the Protection Group includes databases from multiple AWS regions, do not use this option, the backup will fail. Use Auto Create instead.
Note: The Specify Bucket to Use option is not supported when the Protection Group includes databases from multiple AWS regions. This includes Protection Groups using auto-protect at the AWS Account, OU, or Organization level, tag-based auto-protection, or manual selection of databases across regions. In these cases, select Auto Create. If you select Specify Bucket to Use in these scenarios, the backup will fail.
If the selected databases span multiple AWS accounts or Regions, the option to manually specify an S3 bucket isn't available. In such cases, Cohesity automatically creates the staging bucket. After each protection run, Cohesity deletes only the temporary data stored in the staging bucket during backup operations. The staging bucket itself is retained and reused for future backup operations to minimize storage costs and avoid cross-region charges. 7. The Ingest-based policy is enabled by default. Pause Future Runs

Enable Pause Future Run only if you do not want to schedule future runs of the Protection Group.

End Date

Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, we recommend the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Alerts

Optional.
Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Recover TDE-Enabled Databases
Before you recover a TDE-enabled database to another Amazon RDS for SQL Server instance using Cohesity, you must:
1. Back up the TDE certificate from the source instance to Amazon S3. 2. Restore the TDE certificate to the target instance. For more information, see the
Amazon Documentation.
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Recovery Process
When you initiate a recovery, Cohesity exports the selected database data from the Cohesity cluster to an Amazon S3 staging bucket. You can manually create or select an existing S3 bucket in your AWS account, or allow Cohesity to automatically create one when the recovery process begins. After the data is successfully exported to the staging bucket, Amazon RDS reads the exported files from the bucket and imports them into the specified Amazon RDS for MS SQL database instance. Once the import completes, Cohesity automatically deletes the exported files from the staging bucket to free up storage and minimize S3 costs. If you choose Auto Create: Cohesity automatically creates a staging bucket in the same AWS account and region as the target RDS for MS SQL Server database instance. If you choose to specify a bucket: You must specify an S3 bucket that you created or that already exists. The S3 bucket must be in the same AWS region as the target RDS for MS SQL database instance.
