Amazon Relational Database Service Custom for Oracle
Cohesity supports protecting Relational Database Service (RDS) Custom for Oracle databases using two methods:
l Ingest method (via Cohesity Oracle Adapter): Performs database-level protection by installing the Cohesity Oracle Adapter directly on the RDS Custom instance. This method enables RMAN-based, application-consistent backups and restores with external storage like EC2 VMs as target storage.
l Snapshot method (via native AWS snapshots): Uses AWS's native snapshot capability to capture and restore the RDS Custom instance at the storage layer.
The setup and workflows differ for each method. Choose the method that best suits your protection strategy and operational requirements.
Cohesity enables protection of Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle databases through two supported approaches -- ingest-based protection using the Cohesity Oracle Adapter and snapshot-based protection using AWS native snapshots.
With the ingest method, you can use a Protection Group to perform database-level protection for Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle instances. The Cohesity Oracle Adapter, installed directly on the RDS Custom instance, integrates natively with Oracle Recovery Manager (RMAN) to deliver application-consistent backup and recovery for single-instance RDS custom oracle databases.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

The snapshot method, on the other hand, leverages AWS native snapshot capabilities to back up and restore the RDS Custom instance at the infrastructure level, offering a fast and storage-efficient alternative for customers preferring snapshot-based workflows.
Note: Cohesity supports the backup and recovery of Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster).
To learn more, see the following topics:
l Plan and Prepare for Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle l Manage Protection Policy l Backup Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle
Plan and Prepare for Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle
This topic provides information on minimum permissions, prerequisites, and considerations to protect Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle using both Ingest and Snapshot methods.
l Ingest method (via Cohesity Oracle Adapter) l Snapshot method (via native AWS snapshots)
Ingest method (via Cohesity Oracle Adapter)
To protect Amazon Custom RDS for Oracle with Cohesity using the Ingest method, you must register your custom RDS EC2 instance as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. Ensure you meet the prerequisites and understand the considerations before registering for the AWS account.
Prerequisite
l The Cohesity Oracle adapter has to be installed on the Custom RDS EC2 instance. l Non-overlapping backup windows: Schedule Amazon RDS Custom backup and
maintenance windows so they do not overlap with Cohesity backup jobs. l Archive log retention: Configure RDS Custom archive log retention to ensure that
archived logs are retained long enough for at least one Cohesity backup cycle to complete successfully. For example, create the following configuration file on your RDS Custom instance:
sudo mkdir -p /opt/aws/rdscustomagent/config sudo vi /opt/aws/rdscustomagent/config/redo_logs_custom_ configuration.json Add the following content: { "archivedLogRetentionHours": "60" }

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

This ensures archived logs are retained for 60 hours, preventing them from being purged before Cohesity backup jobs complete.
For more details, see Configuring archived log retention for Amazon RDS Custom.
l Required service endpoints: The following table lists the service endpoints required for the backup and recovery of AWS Custom RDS databases:

AWS Resource Type

Service Endpoints

IAM

iam.amazonaws.com

KMS

kms.<region>.amazonaws.com

RDS

rds.<region>.amazonaws.com

EC2 (for SBT traffic & agent operations)

ec2.<region>.amazonaws.com

CloudWatch Logs (for monitoring agent activity) logs.<region>.amazonaws.com

Considerations
l Ingest Backup and recovery of Amazon RDS Custom databases are not supported on Physical clusters or Virtual Edition clusters. To back up and recover Amazon RDS Custom databases, the cluster must be a Next-Gen Cloud Edition (NGCE) cluster.
l Cohesity uses the Oracle Adapter installed on the RDS Custom instance to perform database-level ingest backups and restores. Backup and recovery operations are managed through Oracle RMAN, with Cohesity acting as the backup target.
l Cohesity supports full, incremental, and archivelog backups for RDS Custom databases.
l You can restore backups to the original RDS Custom instance or to an alternate location (such as another RDS Custom instance or an on-premises Oracle environment).
l Cohesity does not support recovery to different accounts with different regions, but recovery to different accounts with the same region, the same account with the same region, and the same account with different regions are supported.
l Point-in-time recovery (PITR) is supported for RDS Custom databases if archive log retention is configured to meet Cohesity backup requirements and AWS automated backups are enabled. PITR allows you to select a specific time within the retention period and restore the database to that point in time.
l Cohesity supports full, incremental, and archived log backups via Oracle RMAN using the Cohesity Adapter.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

l Recovery of an RDS Custom database encrypted with the default AWS KMS Customer Managed Key (CMK) to a different account is not supported because AWS does not allow sharing snapshots encrypted with the default KMS key.
l You cannot restore an RDS Custom database to a location (same or alternate) if the target already has a database with the same name. AWS prohibits multiple RDS Custom database instances with identical names.
l Workaround: Assign a unique name to the RDS Custom database instance before performing recovery.
l When creating a protection group for Linux sources, choose either Imagecopy or Backupset (SBT) as the backup type; these types are not interchangeable.
Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Snapshot method (via native AWS snapshots)
To protect Amazon Custom RDS for Oracle with Cohesity, you must register your AWS account as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. Ensure you meet the prerequisites and understand the considerations before registering for the AWS account.
Prerequisites
l Non-overlapping backup windows: Schedule Amazon RDS Custom backup and maintenance windows so they do not overlap with Cohesity backup jobs.
l Archive log retention: Configure RDS Custom archive log retention to ensure that archived logs are retained long enough for at least one Cohesity backup cycle to complete successfully. For example, create the following configuration file on your RDS Custom instance:
sudo mkdir -p /opt/aws/rdscustomagent/config sudo vi /opt/aws/rdscustomagent/config/redo_logs_custom_ configuration.json Add the following content: { "archivedLogRetentionHours": "60" }
This ensures archived logs are retained for 60 hours, preventing them from being purged before Cohesity backup jobs complete. For more details, see Configuring archived log retention for Amazon RDS Custom. l Required Permissions - IAM requires the user permissions listed below to execute.

Before you begin
When you create a Protection Group, you can select an existing source, policy, or storage domain. You can also create them while creating the Protection Group. However, you might

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

find it easier to create them prior to creating the Protection Group, as described in the following topics.

To create a Protection Group for Custom RDS for Oracle:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection and do one of the following: l To create a Protection Group--Click Protect on the top-right of the page and then select the type of Protection Group.
l To edit a Protection Group--Click the action icon ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit.
2. If creating a Protection Group for Custom RDS, select Databases > Oracle Database.
3. Name: Enter a name for the Protection Group. The name can contain alphanumeric characters, underscores, dashes, and periods.
4. Source: Select the database you want to protect. You can also register a new source with the Cohesity cluster so you can protect it.
5. Select the source objects to back up or exclude. By default, all objects in the source are excluded as indicated by the unselected check box. Expand the source objects and select the objects you want to include in the Protection Group. A selected check box indicates the object is selected to be backed up.
6. Click the arrow adjacent to the Object (Expand All) to expand the entire Object hierarchy. Click the arrow again (Collapse All) to collapse the entire Object hierarchy.
7. The graphical representations in the table are described below.
When creating a new Protection Group, a shield next to the Object name indicates the Object has already been protected by another Protection Group.
Click the icon to see details about the object.
If the object name is in red, it is inaccessible, invalid, or orphaned. If the object is in one of the specified states when the Protection Group runs, no snapshot is created. If the object becomes accessible, a snapshot is created the next time the Protection Group runs. 8. Click Save Selection. 9. Policy: Select an existing protection policy or create a new one by selecting New Policy.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

10. Backup Type: When creating a protection group for Linux sources, choose either Imagecopy or Backupset (SBT) as the backup type. Backup type selection is possible while creation of the protection job. They are not interchangeable.
a. Image Copy: Use this option if you prefer NFS-based backups and require forever incremental backup capability. This is selected by Default.
b. Backup Sets: Use this option to enable encryption in transit using gRPC and to avoid NFS client dependencies.
Note: l You must create or select a policy with the Periodic Full Backup option set when using Oracle SBT.
l This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
11. Start Time: Indicates when the Protection Group should run. The current time is displayed by default, but you can change it. Enter the hour and minutes or use the up and down arrows on your keyboard. Verify the AM or PM setting.
The default time zone is the browser's time zone. You can change the time zone by selecting a different time zone.
12. End Date: Optional. Toggle on and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion, even if it completes after this date.
13. Cancel Runs at Quiet Time Start: Available only if the selected policy has at least one quiet time period. Toggle it on to specify that all currently executing protection runs should abort if a quiet time period specified for the Protection Group starts. By default, this toggle is off, which means after a protection run starts, it continues to execute even when a quiet time period specified for this protection run starts. However, a new protection run will not start during a quiet time period.
a. Success: Create an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
b. Failure: Create a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
c. SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
For more information, see Alerts.
14. Priority: Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity supports concurrent backups, but if the number of Protection Groups exceeds the ability to

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

process them, those with High priority are given the highest priority to execute, Medium the second-highest priority, and Low the lowest priority. 15. Email Recipients: You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the Protection Group. The connection to the SMTP Server must be enabled to send email notifications. You can enable the SMTP Server connection in the configuration settings page ( Cohesity UI > Settings > Summary > Configure > Enable SMTP Server). 16. SLA: The service-level agreement (SLA) defines the expected time to complete either a full backup or an incremental backup. The backup completion time depends on the Windows volume size on AD, objects changed between incremental backups, network speed, and other Protection Groups running on the Cohesity cluster.
a. Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental protection run to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last protection run.
b. Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup protection run to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).
17. Description: Optional. Click the plus sign and enter a description for the Protection Group.
18. Click Protect.
The Protection page is displayed and includes the new Protection Group.

If the object becomes accessible, a snapshot is created the next time the Protection Group runs. 6. Click Save Selection. 7. Policy: Select an existing protection policy or create a new one by selecting New Policy.
Note: You must create or select a policy with the Periodic Full Backup option set.
8. Start Time: Indicates when the Protection Group should run. The current time is displayed by default, but you can change it. Enter the hour and minutes or use the up and down arrows on your keyboard. Verify the AM or PM setting. The default time zone is the browser's time zone. You can change the time zone by selecting a different time zone.
9. SLA: The service-level agreement (SLA) defines the expected time to complete either a full backup or an incremental backup. The backup completion time depends on the Windows volume size on AD, objects changed between incremental backups, network speed, and other Protection Groups running on the Cohesity cluster. a. Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental protection run to complete. An incremental backup captures only the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

differences (changed blocks) since the last protection run.
b. Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup protection run to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).
10. From the Backup Options (Optional), configure the following Additional Settings:
a. Pause Future Runs: Toggle on this option to stop protection runs of the Protection Group from executing. Once you enable this option, no protection runs will be scheduled for this Protection Group.
b. End Date: Optional. Toggle on and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion, even if it completes after this date.
c. Alerts: Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
i. Success: Create an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
i. Failure: Create a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
ii. SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created. For more information, see Alerts.
d. Priority: Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity supports concurrent backups, but if the number of Protection Groups exceeds the ability to process them, those with High priority are given the highest priority to execute, Medium the second-highest priority, and Low the lowest priority.
e. Description: Optional. Click the plus sign and enter a description for the Protection Group.
11. Click Protect.
The Protection page is displayed and includes the new Protection Group.

Amazon Relational Database Service Custom for SQL Server
Cohesity supports protecting Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) Custom for Microsoft SQL Server. This managed database service provided by AWS offers a balance between the automation of Amazon RDS and the flexibility of self-managing a database on Amazon EC2.
Note: Cohesity supports the backup and recovery of Amazon RDS Custom for SQL Server on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster).
This chapter includes the following topics:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Planning and Preparation for Amazon RDS Custom for SQL Server
The following topics provide guidance that helps you get ready to implement MS SQL Server:
Requirements to Access Amazon RDS Custom for SQL Server
Cohesity DataProtect SQL Server agent must be installed on the corresponding EC2 instance that has the Amazon RDS Custom instance. You can then perform the backup and recovery operations as you would for a standalone SQL Server instance. You must access Amazon RDS Custom to connect to the underlying EC2 instance and then to the database. Use remote access to the EC2 instance and then client tools to connect to the database.
1. Prepare the EC2 Instance for Remote Desktop: i. Ensure the VPC security group allows inbound RDP traffic (port 3389) from your source IP. ii. Create an RDS instance. For more information, see Creating an Amazon RDS DB Instance. The EC2 instance will also be created.
iii. Configure the Windows firewall on the EC2 instance to allow remote desktop access.
iv. On the EC2 instance, connect with the Session Manager. v. Run the following PowerShell command to open firewall:
Set-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Remote Desktop - User Mode (TCPIn)" -Direction Inbound -LocalAddress Any -Profile Any
vi. Retrieve the administrator password for the EC2 instance from AWS Secrets Manager using the key pair information.
vii. Go to the Secret Manager and click on the required secret name. viii. Under the Secret Value section, select Retrieve Secret Value.
ix. Copy the secret value in plain text. 2. Connect to the EC2 Instance via RDP:
i. Use an RDP client (like Remote Desktop Connection on Windows) to connect to the EC2 instance using its private IP address and the administrator credentials. A jump server in a public subnet is often used for this.
ii. On the EC2 instance, connect with the RDP Client. iii. Select Get Password at the bottom of the page. iv. Paste the secret value into the Private Key Contents field and click Decrypt
Password.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

v. Copy the decrypted password.
vi. Go back to the jump server and RDP into the EC2 instance with the administrator credentials and decrypted password.
3. Connect to SQL Server:
i. From the RDP session on the EC2 instance, use SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) or other SQL client tools to connect to the SQL Server database endpoint.
ii. Use this endpoint to register your Microsoft SQL Server as a source on Cohesity DataProtect.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Requirements for Amazon RDS Custom for SQL Server Protection
Supported Software for Microsoft SQL Server Protection
For more information, see Supported Software.
Agent Minimum Permissions for Microsoft SQL Server Protection
You can use either the host LOCAL SYSTEM account or an account that meets the requirements to install the Cohesity agent. It is recommended to run the Cohesity Agent service with an Active Directory domain user account that is a member of the local administrator of the SQL Server host. The AD domain user account must be a member of the SQL sysadmin server role. The user account must have log-on rights to the SQL Server host in the local security policy of the SQL Server host. If you do not use the LOCAL SYSTEM account, ensure the following for the chosen account:
l The account must be a member of the local Windows Administrators group. For example, qa01\tme-backup is an Active Directory user account in the data center. If the backup admin plans to use this account, qa01\tme-backup must be part of the local Windows Administrators group on the SQL server.
l The account must have Log on as a service in the User Rights Assignment on the MS SQL server to install the Cohesity agent.
l The account must have the sysadmin role in the MS SQL Server instance.
Ports Used for Communication
l On physical servers or VMs with an ephemeral or installed agent, open the ports 445, 11113, 11117, and 50051. For more information, see Manage Firewall Ports.
l If the Windows Firewall is used: l Inbound rules: l Add a rule to accept SQL Server traffic and TCP connections on local port 1433. l Set Remote Port to All Ports. l Outbound rules (for MS SQL Server 2016 running on Windows 2016): Update the "Block network access for R local user accounts in SQL server instance MSSQLSERVER" rule by going to General tab > Action window > select "Allow the connection".

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Prerequisites for Microsoft SQL Server Protection
l Verify MS SQL Server services are running. l The Readable Secondary field in the Availability Group Properties of the SQL Server
Availability Group (AAG) must be set to Yes if you have selected Secondary Only as the Backup Preference setting for AAG. l MS SQL database and instance names must meet the Microsoft SQL Server naming requirements. Names containing illegal Windows file characters, such as double quotes, pipe symbols, greater than and less than signs ( " | > < ), a space at the beginning or end of the database name (applicable only for VDI-based backup) are not supported. For more information, see Naming Files, Paths, and Namespaces. l On the Server's Windows system, Cohesity recommends to set the Power Plan to High performance.
Credentials and Privileges for Microsoft SQL Server Protection
There are three accounts you must consider when installing the Cohesity Agent:
l Installation Account: The account you use to log in to the host and run the installer.
l Service Account: The account under which the Cohesity Agent service runs on the SQL Server host. (Selected at the time of installation.)
l SQL Server login account: The SQL Server account by which the Cohesity Agent has access to the databases. (Configured after installation.)
Installation Account
When installing the Cohesity Agent on a Microsoft Windows host, you must log onto the SQL Server host with an account that has local administrator privileges. This is because the Windows agent installer installs the Cohesity Agent service. Microsoft requires the installation account to have administrator privileges on the host.
Choose the Service Account
The installer gives you the option between two types of service accounts:
l The LocalSystem account. l A user account. Assigning privileges to the service account will differ depending on
which type of account you choose. Cohesity recommends using either the LocalSystem account or an Active Directory Domain User account. See the chart below for a comparison of service account types.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Best Practices

Comparison of Service Account Types

SERVICE ACCOUNT LocalSystem (Default)
User Account

TYPE

DEFINITION

RECOMMENDATION

LocalSystem Account (Built-in Host Account)

The LocalSystem account is a predefined local account on the host computer.

Recommended: The Local System account is a predefined local account used by the service control manager. It has extensive privileges on the local computer, and acts as the computer on the network. Its token includes the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM and BUILTIN\Administrators SIDs; these accounts have access to most system objects.

Domain User Account (Active Directory)

A user whose username and password are stored in Active Directory.

Recommended: A domain user account enables the service to take full advantage of the service security features of Windows and Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services. The service has whatever local and network access is granted to the account, or to any groups of which the account is a member.

Local User Account (Host account)

In Windows, a local user is one whose username and encrypted password are stored locally, only on the computer itself.

Not recommended: When you log in as a local user, the computer checks its own list of users and its own password file to see if you are allowed to log in to the computer. The computer itself then applies all the permissions and restrictions that are assigned to you for that computer.

Note: If you are unsure which account to use, choose the LocalSystem account. This account already has most of the required permissions. The agent service account can be changed later if needed.

Linux OS RHEL 8 and higher versions

Database
Microsoft SQL Server 2019

Notes
l Only VDI-based backups are currently supported on Linux OS.
l High Availability Microsoft SQL Server configurations like FCI and AG are not supported.

Considerations
l Cross-platform database restores between Windows and Linux are currently not supported.
l For VDI-based backups to work, Microsoft requires the backup application account (Cohesity Agent's service account) and the Microsoft SQL Server service account to be added to each other's primary groups using the usermod command. For example: sudo usermod -a -G mssql cohesityagent sudo usermod -a -G cohesityagent mssql where, mssql is the user account of the mssql-server service and cohesityagent is the user account of the Cohesity Agent service. Following this, the Microsoft SQL Server and the Cohesity Agent services must be restarted for the changes to take effect.
Note: The usermod -a -G command may not work for domain accounts.
l Currently, only password-based SQL Server authentication is supported and Active Directory-based authentication is not supported for Linux. For supported features of SQL Server 2019 on Linux, see Editions and supported features of SQL Server 2019 on Linux.

Supported Database Types for Microsoft SQL Server
Before proceeding to deploy the Cohesity agent for SQL data protection, we recommend you correctly identify the type of SQL database you want to protect. Below is a table of SQL database types that are supported by the Cohesity SQL agent, and the recommended protection methods. To understand the concept of each method, see About Microsoft SQL Server Backup.

Database Types

Definition

Stand Alone

A SQL Server User database.

Adapter-based Protection Method

File-based Protection

VDI-based Protection

AG

A database that belongs to an availability group (AG). For each

availability database, the availability group maintains a single

read-write copy (the primary replica) and one to four read-only

copies (secondary replicas).

For details, see Always On availability groups: a high-availability and disaster-recovery solution in the Microsoft documentation.

FCI

A database that belongs to a Failover Cluster Instance (FCI),

which is a single instance of SQL Server that is installed across

Windows Server Failover Clustering (WSFC) nodes.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

Database Types
CDC TDE
Filestream
SQL System

Definition

Adapter-based Protection Method

File-based Protection

VDI-based Protection

A change data capture (CDC) enabled SQL database records activity and is applied to an internal table. This makes the details of the changes available in an easily consumed relational format.
For details, see About Change Data Capture (SQL Server) in the Microsoft documentation.

A Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) enabled SQL database has its data files encrypted, known as encrypting data at rest. TDE performs real-time I/O encryption and decryption of the data and log files.
For details, see Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) in the Microsoft documentation.
NOTE: Cohesity does not manage the keys associated with the TDE database.

A Filestream enabled SQL Database is a database that contains a table that stores its data outside the database on the host file system. SQL Filestream leverages the OS file system's ability to handle large objects like images, PDFs, Binary, Bmp, Docs, and other unstructured data.
For details, see Filestream (SQL Server) in the Microsoft documentation.

SQL Server maintains a set of four system-level databases (master, model, msdb, tempdb), which are essential for the operation of a server instance. System databases must be backed up after every significant update. The system databases that you must always back up include msdb, master, and model.
System databases are not supported for log backups.
For details, see Backup & restore: system databases (SQL Server) in the Microsoft documentation.

Now that you can identify the type of SQL database you want to protect, you can register it as a Cohesity source.

Microsoft SQL Server Dashboard
Access the MS SQL Dashboard by going to Dashboard and from the drop-down, select MS SQL.
The page's upper portion displays information such as metrics, status and recovery history. In the page's lower portion, you can start the different actions from the Hosts tab and the Databases tab. The MS SQL Dashboard displays local MS SQL databases only. To restore or clone replicated or CloudRetrieved databases, use their respective restore or clone workflows.
From the Hosts tab, mouse over the actions menu for the following actions (some actions are available for physical servers only):

l Protect Databases ( )--Create a Protection Group using this server.

l Unregister MS SQL ( )--Unregister the MS SQL application. The server remains registered with the Cohesity cluster.

l Edit ( )--Configure the settings of a registered MS SQL server.

l Unregister ( )--Unregister this server from the Cohesity cluster.

l Refresh ( )--Manually force a refresh of the object hierarchy.

l Upgrade Agents ( available.

)--Upgrade the Cohesity agent on the server if an upgrade is

From the Databases tab, mouse over the actions menu for the following actions (some actions are not available for system databases):

l Protect ( )--Create a Protection Group using this database.

l Run Now ( )--Start a run of this Protection Group. You have the option to back up one or more objects.
If the policy associated with the Protection Group is configured with replication and archive targets, you can select those targets. If the policy supports multiple backup types, you can select an incremental, full or log backup.
VM MS SQL Protection Groups do not support selecting individual databases for run now; only the entire VM is selectable.
l Pause Future Runs/Resume Future Runs ( ) l Select Pause Future Runs to stop new runs of this Protection Group from executing. However, if the job is currently executing a run, the current run continues to execute and only future runs of this job are paused.

l Select Resume Future Runs to restore the Protection Group to a running state. The runs resume as specified in the schedule defined in the policy associated with this job.
l Cancel this Protection Group Run ( )--Cancel the current run of this Protection Group. (This option is only available when a Protection Group run is executing.) This cancellation only affects the current run of the Protection Group and not future runs.
l Clone ( )--Make a copy of the database. The clone database is a unique copy of the original database taken from the backup.

Database Recover and Clone Actions
In the Databases tab click a protected database to display available recover and clone actions. To recover or clone the latest snapshot, click the arrow next to the Protect button at the top right corner and select an action. By default, the latest snapshot is selected. You can optionally choose to restore from a
different snapshot by clicking Edit ( ).
You can also provide a specific time to restore to if transaction logs are available. Click a date on the calendar to select a snapshot from that date. The default point selected will be the latest log transaction or the latest full or incremental, whichever is the latest. The slider also displays available points in time and displays snapshots as circles. Manually select a point on the slider if you want to restore to a specific point in time. Selecting an invalid time from the slider automatically changes to the closest available snapshot. If your manual selection is within 10 minutes of a snapshot, your selection automatically snaps to it. You can also select a specific point in time by entering it in the time fields. After selecting the desired recover point, click Recover. You can choose to clone the selected recover point by clicking the arrow adjacent to recover and selecting Clone. In this workflow, deleted snapshots may be displayed as valid recover points for a brief period until they are removed from the search index by a background process.

Auto-discover Microsoft SQL Server Topology when Registering Microsoft SQL Server
To register an MS SQL Server, MS SQL FCI, or an MS SQL AG of a Windows cluster, you can provide the IP address of the server, FQDN of the server, or VIP of the SQL FCI. The Cohesity cluster discovers the entire MS SQL topology on the Windows cluster and displays the relevant subset based on the MS SQL address you provide while registering. From the topology list, you can select the servers you want to register with the Cohesity cluster. To display the entire MS SQL topology, use the Windows Cluster IP/FQDN.
Prerequisites
Before you register the MS SQL, ensure to meet the following:
l MS SQL prerequisites. For more information, see Requirements for Amazon RDS Custom for SQL Server Protection.
l Download and Install the Agent.
Download and Install the Agent
Install the Cohesity agent on each SQL server that you want Cohesity to protect.
1. Select Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click Download Cohesity Agent. Ensure the agent has been downloaded to the
appropriate server. 3. As an administrator with local system privileges on that server, run the executable
and complete the installation using the following steps: 4. Volume CBT (Changed Block Tracker): Install this component to leverage
Cohesity's built-in CBT technology. Without this component, only full backups can be performed. Installing this component requires a one-time reboot to load the Cohesity CBT driver. Until a reboot, only full backups can be performed. File System CBT (Changed Block Tracker): Install this component to perform MS SQL file-based protection.
Note: Installing the Volume CBT or File System CBT is not necessary for MS SQL VDI-based protection.
5. Service Account Credentials: You can use either the LOCAL SYSTEM account or an account that meets the requirements to install the Cohesity agent. If you do not use the LOCAL SYSTEM account, ensure the following: l The account must be a member of the local Windows Administrators group. For example, qa01\tme-backup is an Active Directory user account in the data center. If the backup admin plans to use this account, qa01\tme-backup must be part of the local Windows Administrators group on the SQL server.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

l The account must have Log on as a service in the User Rights Assignment on the MS SQL server to install the Cohesity agent.
6. Wait for the installation to finish. In the SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), ensure that the account used to install the Cohesity agent has Server Roles: sysadmin in the SQL server instances.
7. The agent starts automatically. 8. Reboot the machine if you have installed the Volume CBT component. 9. Repeat the agent installation process on each SQL server you want to protect. This
includes any standalone MS SQL servers and Microsoft SQL Server nodes with AGs.

Set Up Standalone Microsoft SQL Server or Microsoft SQL Server AGs
This topic describes how to set up standalone MS SQL servers and MS SQL Server Always On Availability Groups (AGs) to be protected by a Cohesity cluster.
Note: The Readable Secondary field in the Availability Group Properties of the SQL Server Availability Group (AG) must be set to "Yes" or "Read-intent only".
The following are the different methods to register your physical or virtual MS SQL Servers allowing you to protect your MS SQL server databases:
l Registering a SQL Server using the Cohesity SQL Agent: This option is the preferred method to protect your MS SQL server databases on physical or virtual hardware. This option can be used to protect any SQL server configurations such as MSQL standalone, FCI, and AG. For more information, see Set Up MS SQL on Virtual or Physical Servers using the Agent. To set up an MS SQL FCI, follow the steps described in Set Up Microsoft SQL Server FCI.
l Registering a Hypervisor for SQL Server: Cohesity provides an additional option to protect your MS SQL server at the hypervisor level. While this option is available, it is not the preferred method to protect your SQL server databases. Following are the two available registration methods: l Persistent Agent--For more information, see Set Up MS SQL on VMs as a VMware vCenter application with the Installed Agent. l Auto-Deployed Agent (non-Persistent)--For more information, see Set Up MS SQL on VMs as a VMware vCenter application with the Auto-deployed Agent.
Ensure Prerequisites are Met
Ensure the prerequisites listed in Prerequisites for Microsoft SQL Server Protection are met.
Set Up MS SQL on Virtual or Physical Servers using the Agent
This option can be used for both physical or virtual servers that are in standalone or AG configurations. Cohesity recommends you use this method to protect the MS SQL Servers with the Cohesity cluster. For more information, see Set Up MS SQL on Virtual or Physical Servers using the Agent.

Set Up Microsoft SQL Server FCI
This topic describes how to set up an MS SQL Failover Cluster Instance (FCI) to be protected by a Cohesity cluster. To set up a standalone MS SQL Server or MS SQL AG, follow the steps described in Set Up Standalone Microsoft SQL Server or Microsoft SQL Server AGs.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

MS SQL FCI - Overview
An MS SQL FCI is an MS SQL instance installed on a Windows server that is part of a Windows Server Failover Cluster (WSFC or simply Windows Cluster for short). The SQL instance physically exists on (and is accessible from) only one node of the WSFC at any given time. If the FCI's current node goes down, the FCI moves to another node in the WSFC. The FCI is addressed by a Virtual IP (VIP) which points to the physical IP of the node on which it currently resides.
Set Up MS SQL FCI Overview
MS SQL FCI setup has the following steps:
1. Ensure Prerequisites Are Met 2. Download and Install the Agent on Each Node 3. Register an MS SQL FCI as a Source 4. Register an MS SQL FCI as MS SQL
Ensure Prerequisites Are Met
Ensure the prerequisites listed in Prerequisites for Microsoft SQL Server Protection are met.
Download and Install the Agent on Each Node
Before registering an MS SQL Server FCI, you must download and install the Cohesity agent on each node within the MS SQL FCI.
1. Select Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click Download Cohesity Agent. Ensure the agent has been downloaded to the
appropriate server. 3. As an administrator with local system privileges on that server, run the executable
and complete the installation using the following steps: 4. Volume CBT (Changed Block Tracker): Install this component to leverage
Cohesity's built-in CBT technology. Without this component, only full backups can be performed. Installing this component requires a one-time reboot to load the Cohesity CBT driver. Until a reboot, only full backups can be performed. File System CBT (Changed Block Tracker): Install this component to perform MS SQL file-based protection.
Note: Installing the Volume CBT or File System CBT is not necessary for MS SQL VDI-based protection.
5. Service Account Credentials: You can use either the LOCAL SYSTEM account or an account that meets the requirements to install the Cohesity agent. If you do not use the LOCAL SYSTEM account, ensure the following:

l The account must have Log on as a service in the User Rights Assignment on the MS SQL server to install the Cohesity agent.
6. Wait for the installation to finish. In the SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), ensure that the account used to install the Cohesity agent has Server Roles: sysadmin in the SQL server instances.

FCI Standalone Multi-Registration
You can register and back up a Windows Server that participates in an MS SQL FCI. You can separately register the FCI clusters and their standalone nodes. This allows you to backup local drives for physical server backups.
Prerequisites
l Ensure that all the SQL agents are upgraded. l Ensure that the following unsupported protection groups are not present:
l A protection group that auto-protects a standalone SQL host participating in a WSFC.
l A protection group that explicitly protects FCI databases on a SQL server participating in an MS SQL FCI.
Error Messages
l The following error message is displayed when unsupported protection groups are present: Error FCI-node multi-registration cannot proceed, please correct the following protection groups:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

l <protectiongroupname1>, <protectiongroupname2> - jobs that autoprotect Windows Cluster node(s).
l <protectiongroupname1>, <protectiongroupname2> - jobs that explicitly back up some FCI databases from Windows Cluster node(s).
Solution
Either delete or fix the protection groups such that they no longer fit the unsupported criteria, and continue the procedure.
l The following error message is displayed when the agent on the Windows cluster node has not been upgraded to a version that supports this feature: Error Agents on the following sources do not support FCI-node multi-registration: <server1>, <server2> Solution Upgrade the agent on the Windows cluster node to a version that supports this feature.
Best Practices for Microsoft SQL Server
Cohesity recommends the following best practices when protecting MS SQL:
l Cohesity recommends triggering a full backup whenever a database file (.mdf, .ndf, .ldf) is added or removed from the database.
l Multiple Cohesity clusters concurrently backing up an MS SQL VM is not recommended because the jobs will interfere with the other's log chain.
l For MS SQL point in time restores, the Full Recovery Model is recommended as a best practice. For more information, see Choosing the Recovery Model for a Database.
l Set MS SQL Server to autostart.
l To accurately report the size of transaction log data read/written during log backups, the Windows local or domain Administrator account that is registered with Cohesity for backup must be added as a user to the 'model' system database. Use the following query: -- Configures accurate reporting of the size of transaction log data read/written during log backup USE [model] GO CREATE USER [HOSTNAME\Administrator] FOR LOGIN [HOSTNAME\Administrator]
GO Where HOSTNAME is the hostname of the SQL server. This assumes that the Administrator account used to register MS SQL is already registered in the SQL server instance's Security Logins and has the "sysadmin" role per documentation. If privileges are not correct, the logical bytes read stat ("Size" column on the Job's details page) for MS SQL log backups will be the same as the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

physical bytes read stat ("Read" column on the Job's details page). If privileges are correct, then the size reported will be the sum of the sizes of all the .ldf files for the database.
Considerations for Microsoft SQL Server
General
l For file-based Protection Group, object-level granularity is not supported for Rolebased access control (RBAC), such as setting access to objects through Active Directory and roles.
l If using native or third-party backup software to back up an application (such as MS SQL), note that the following behavior breaks the differential chain for the application on that server: l Performing an app-consistent backup on a VMware SQL VM. l You are allowed to run a file-based physical server Protection Group with a SQL Protection Group or 3rd party SQL protection tools. This is a Microsoft limitation. For more information, see Various Causes of Log Chains Breaking Issue in SQL Server.
l The SQL Server VDI log backup and restore operations require Sysadmin privileges which is a Microsoft requirement. For more details, see Microsoft Documentation on SQL Server VDI backup.
l Cohesity cluster uses the Encrypted Network Block Device (NBDSSL) transport method for the vSphere Storage APIs for Data Protection (VADP) workflow. NBDSSL uses SSL to encrypt the data. SAN transport mode operation is not supported.
Protection
l Ensure that all AG databases you want to protect are selected from the respective replica.
l For file-based backups, Cohesity operations rely on default MS SQL file extensions (.mdf, .ndf, .ldf).
l SQL Database and logs residing on SMB/NFS can be protected using the MS SQL Native method.
l SQL Database and logs residing on Clustered Shared Volumes (CSV) can be protected using the MS SQL Native and MS SQL VDI methods.
l CBT information does not persist after a reboot for the file-based backup method.
l As per Microsoft requirements, VDI backups executed on secondary replicas are copyonly full backups. Copy-only backups on secondary replicas do not impact the log

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

chain. For more information, see Offload supported backups to secondary replicas of an availability group. l Overwriting Filestream database is not supported; this may prevent the completion of recovery.
Recovery
l Performing a point-in-time restore of an Always On Availability Group replica requires full backups from that replica. Log backups are merged across all replicas; full backups are not. During restore, the user sees multiple results for the same database from different replicas. Each replica shows a set of Snapshots for full backups done on that particular replica. For point in time restore to a specific replica, the user must select a full backup Snapshot from that replica only. If a full backup does not exist, point in time restore is not possible. Restore the database to the desired MS SQL Server instance on a replica that has a full backup.
l Using the "Restore to Original SQL Server instance" option is not supported if any of the following occurs: l The Windows host name changed and you attempt to restore a snapshot that was taken before the host name change. l Granular DB restore performed from a higher SQL Server version to a lower version. This is a Microsoft limitation. You can toggle off "Restore to Original SQL Server Instance" and perform a database restore. For more information, see Rename computer hosting instance - SQL Server. Restoring a snapshot taken after the name change or upgrade is supported.
l Restoring MS SQL Server from backups of dynamic disks to the same machine is not supported.
l Use File-based or VDI-based backup methods to protect TDE databases. Follow the Microsoft TDE best practices for key and cert management.
l If multiple restore tasks are run on the same target host, the restore tasks will be serialized.
l For system database recovery: l Recovering the system database to an alternate instance is not supported. l When recovering to the original database, the original database is deleted before the recovery. Therefore, a recovery failure will also lead to the loss of the original database.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

l If you are recovering the system databases individually, then the recovery of the system database must be in the following order: 1. Master 2. MSDB 3. Model
l You cannot recover a system database along with a user database. l If you are recovering more than one system database in a recovery task, then
the recovery point for the selected system databases must be the same. l For recovering a database to an Amazon RDS Custom SQL Server, the recovery
destination path must be under the D:\rdsdbdata folder.
Clone
l Cloning an MS SQL database and renaming the database via SSMS can leave the cloned database in the "Recovery Pending" state during a clone teardown task. This is because the Cohesity cluster database clone operation assumes the cloned database name and files are associated with the original clone operation. To prevent a disconnect between the Cohesity cluster and SQL Server operation, it is recommended to clone a new database with the intended database name rather than rename a cloned database.
Migration
l Cohesity does not support the migration of MS SQL FILESTREAM databases. l Once a migration task is configured and created, the target SQL Server or database
paths cannot be modified for the existing migration task. l Cohesity does not detect changes/deletions to the target database with a running
migration task. Changes made external to the migration task before finalizing can cause the migration task to fail. l Cohesity does not support the migration of MS SQL databases that are replicated to an alternate Cohesity cluster.

Known Issues that lead to backup failure

Very High transaction rate on databases may occur resulting in backup failure. This is due to Microsoft's VSS system provider not being able to maintain the VSS snapshot on SQL host with very high transactions. This is very rare. Configuring the shadow storage on volume with no/less IO helps to mitigate the issue.

Agent/SQL host may restart during backup.

Known Issues that lead to incremental backup converting to full backup

First backup after SQL server reboot will be a full backup (incremental backup automatically switches to full backup)

If no explicit policy is available for full backup, incremental backup is converted to full backup after 7 days.

About Microsoft SQL Server Backup
Cohesity supports the following MS SQL Server backups: l File-based Backup l VDI-based Backup
Cohesity also supports VM-based Backup and SQL Native Backup.
File-based Backup
A Cohesity cluster MS SQL file-based backup protects only the MS SQL databases you choose. It captures only the database files for those selected databases. The Cohesity cluster captures full database server backups and can optionally back up database transaction logs, so you can roll forward to any point in time. The advantage of a file-based backup is that a smaller amount of data is captured, which allows the Protection Group to run more quickly.
Note: To enable file-based backup, you must install the File System CBT component during Cohesity agent installation.
For information on performing MS SQL file-based backup, see Microsoft SQL Server (Filebased). All configurations are for illustrative purposes only. Cohesity recommends following MS SQL best practices. An example of MS SQL running on a Windows server that contains the following:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms
l Multiple volumes, C, D, E and F in the figure below l Volume D is running two MS SQL databases l Volume E is running three MS SQL databases l Volume F contains database logs

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

The MS SQL file-based backup task consists of the following actions:
1. During SQL database protection run, a VSS snapshot of the specified MS SQL databases is captured using Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS). The VSS snapshot resides on the local drive as a special VSS volume. This VSS snapshot is a full database server backup.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

2. The snapshot is captured and saved on the Cohesity cluster with a date and time stamp. You can optionally choose for the Cohesity cluster to utilize Change Block Tracking (CBT) when backing up the snapshot. VMware VMs leverage VMware CBT to back up the snapshot. Physical servers leverage Cohesity CBT to back up the snapshot.

3. Backups of database transaction logs use MS SQL Server Virtual Device Interface (VDI) and are stored on the Cohesity cluster. The logs allow you to roll back to a specific point in time. MS SQL Server automatically truncates the SQL logs after a successful SQL log backup and marks the Virtual Log Files (VLFs) for reuse.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

VDI-based Backup
A Cohesity cluster MS SQL VDI-based backup captures the native MS SQL server backups. It captures VDI-based backups of a specific database on a SQL Server instance running on a VMware or physical server.
The Virtual Device Interface (VDI) is a Microsoft interface that allows the Cohesity agent to execute SQL Server Native backup and restore commands. This backup type produces a standard SQL Server Native backup of type (.BAK), transaction logs, (.TRN), and differentials, (.DIFF). These backup files are stored on a Cohesity View and take advantage of View compression, deduplication, encryption, replication, and archiving features.
All configurations are for illustrative purposes only. Cohesity recommends following MS SQL best practices.
An example of MS SQL running on a Windows server that contains the following:
l Multiple volumes, C, D and F in the figure below l Volume D is running multiple MS SQL databases l Volume F contains database logs

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

The MS SQL VDI-based backup task consists of the following actions:
1. During an MS SQL protection run, a "BACKUP DATABASE" command for the specified MS SQL databases is initiated using MS SQL Server Virtual Device Interface (VDI). The generated backup file is saved on the Cohesity cluster with a date and time stamp.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

2. If the policy is configured to take incremental database backups, it translates to differential backups in case of VDI-based backup.
3. If transaction log backups are specified in the policy, the database transaction logs are backed up to the Cohesity cluster using MS SQL Server Virtual Device Interface (VDI). The logs allow you to roll back to a specific point in time. MS SQL Server automatically truncates the SQL logs after a successful SQL log backup and marks the Virtual Log Files (VLFs) for reuse.

About Log and Full DB Backup Retention Periods
The retention periods of log files and full database server backups are independent of each other. Consider the following examples to help determine the best retention periods for your database server backups. These retention guidelines also apply to full database server and log replication schedules. Retention periods of log files and full database backups must adhere to Microsoft rules for restoring databases.
1. A point-in-time restore using SQL log backups is dependent on a full backup because a full database server backup must also be available to apply the logs.
When the Cohesity cluster restores to a specific point in time, it must first restore a full database server backup and then apply the appropriate set of logs. If a full database server backup is not available because the retention period of the full database server backup is too short, the Cohesity cluster cannot restore to a point in time within the specified log retention period. For example if the log retention period

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

is three weeks and the full database server backup captures snapshots weekly with a retention period of two weeks, the Cohesity cluster will not be able to restore to any point in time from three weeks ago. In addition, the logs from three weeks ago cannot be utilized and are using disk space.

2. If the log retention period is shorter than the full database server backup retention period, the Cohesity cluster cannot restore to a point in time where the logs are not saved. For example, if the log retention period is two weeks and the full database server backup captures snapshots weekly with a retention period of three weeks, the Cohesity cluster will not be able to restore to any point in time between two and three weeks ago. The Cohesity cluster can, however, restore to the snapshot from three weeks ago.
3. Cohesity recommends specifying a log retention period with extra time to allow for failed full database server backups as demonstrated by the following example. A full database server backup is scheduled weekly with a three-week retention period for both full database server and logs. If the full database server backup failed two weeks ago, the Cohesity cluster can still restore to the point in time from the log indicated by the green arrow.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

The Cohesity cluster restores full database server backup from three weeks ago and applies the appropriate logs to restore the state to a point.
You can restore to a specific transaction in the log.

Note: A full database backup is not a transaction log backup. Ensure that your SQL Server protection policy has transaction log backup for full and bulk-logged recovery model requirements.

Considerations
Consider the following when using the Auto Protect option on the backup job
l If new databases are added to the host, the existing filters are applied to the newly added databases. For example, if the exclude filter matches the newly added databases then these databases will be excluded in the backup job.
l If any system databases are excluded by the filters in an SQL server, it will exclude all the system databases belonging to that SQL server.
l When defining filters to exclude AG databases, ensure that the filters are configured on all the AG hosts. For example, to exclude an AG database and if the AG database has 4 hosts, then ensure that the filters are defined on all the four AG hosts.
l Auto protect functionality is supported only for physical SQL jobs (file-based and native)
l To selectively exclude a SQL database from the protection job, you must upgrade all the cluster nodes to version 6.5.1 and later.

Note: Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.
l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Protection Groups.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
l TestAndDev High: The Cohesity cluster writes the data to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. The I/Os with this QoS policy are given higher priority compared to other QoS policies. Use this policy for workloads that require lower I/O latency.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

19. Cancel Runs at Quiet Time Start: Available only if the selected policy has at least one quiet time period. Toggle it on to specify that all currently executing protection runs should abort if a quiet time period specified for the Protection Group starts. By default this toggle is off, which means after a protection run starts, it continues to execute even when a quiet time period specified for this protection run starts. However, a new protection run will not start during a quiet time period.
20. Pre & Post Scripts: Edit this option to run scripts on the protected server before and/or after a Protection Group runs. If configured, the scripts are run every time an object is backed up by a Protection Group run.
For configuration details, see Configure Pre & Post Scripts.
21. Indexing: Indexing is enabled by default and required for file recovery. The Cohesity cluster will scan all the files in the Protection Group and create an internal index that can be used later by a recover task to locate files by name.
For information about customizing indexing, see Customize Indexing.
Indexing is not supported for file-based Protection Groups. Without indexing, file/folder-level recovery and searching are not supported.
22. Alerts: Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Create an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Create a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
For more information, see Alerts.
23. Priority: Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity supports concurrent backups, but if the number of Protection Groups exceeds the ability to process them, those with High priority are given the highest priority to execute, Medium the second-highest priority, and Low the lowest priority.
24. Email Recipients: You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the Protection Group.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

Note: The connection to the SMTP Server must be enabled to send email notification. You can enable the SMTP Server connection in the configuration settings page ( Cohesity UI > Settings > Summary > Configure > Enable SMTP Server).
25. SLA: The service-level agreement (SLA) defines the expected time to complete either a full backup or incremental backup. The backup completion time depends on the Windows volume size on AD, objects changed between incremental backups, network speed, and other Protection Groups running on the Cohesity cluster.
l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental protection run to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last protection run.
l Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup protection run to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).
26. Click Protect.
The Protection page is displayed and includes the new Protection Group.

If appropriate for your organization, enable Auto Protect.
Click to turn on Auto Protect. By enabling this option: l All the SQL databases that are added to the SQL server in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run. l All the SQL databases that are removed from the SQL server in the future are automatically removed from the Protection Group and are not protected from the next protection run. The existing backup for the user is preserved until the snapshot expires.
For example, you create a Protection Group that backs up a SQL Server. The Protection Group runs for two weeks and then a new database is added to the SQL Server. The next time the Protection Group runs, if the object hierarchy has been refreshed on the Cohesity cluster, the new database is also backed up even though the new database has not been explicitly selected to be included in the Protection Group. The object hierarchy is automatically refreshed every four hours. To manually refresh the object hierarchy, select Data Protection > Sources, find
the source in the list and click . To exclude an object from Auto Protect, click .
l Indicates an Auto Protected object.
l Use this option to exclude SQL databases from the protection group. Excluded objects are not protected. The icon indicates that an ancestor of the object is Auto Protected but this object is explicitly excluded.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

To exclude a database from the protection group, specify the absolute path of the database to be excluded from the backup at a protection job level. You can optionally use:
l Wildcard Exclusion - You can optionally use the Wildcard * in any location in the search string to exclude all the matching databases from the backup at a protection job level.
l Regex Exclusion - You can use the RegEx string name match and manual user selection to exclude DBs from backup at a protection job level.
Note: You can use the exclude SQL database feature only if Auto Protect is enabled for a backup job.
Protection of dismounted databases, recovery database types, and deleted databases are automatically skipped by the Protection Group. After defining the filter click Apply to save the selection. The following table lists the examples for excluding objects in an MS SQL database:

Sample Configuration
10.2.157.20 (Host) * SQL2012 (SQL Server Instance) - UserDB1 - UserDB2 - TestDB1 - TestDB2
Example of Absolute Path

* SQL2014 (SQL Server Instance) - UserDB3 - UserDB4 - TestDB3 - TestDB4

* MSSQLSERVER (SQL Server Instance) - ProdDB1 - ProdDB2

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

Sample Configuration
l 10.2.157.20/SQL2012/UserDB1 - Excludes the database 'UserDB1' from the SQL server instance 'SQL2012' on the host 10.2.157.20.
l 10.2.157.20/SQL2012/ - Excludes the 'SQL2012' from the SQL server instance and its databases.
Note: The absolute instance path must end with '/' and the plain text instance path must contain two or more slashes.
Example of Wildcard Exclusion
l 10.2.157.20/SQL2012/User* - Excludes the databases 'UserDB1' and 'UserDB2' from the SQL server instance 'SQL2012' on the host 10.2.157.20.
l 10.2.157.20/SQL201?/* - Excludes the SQL server instances 'SQL2012' and 'SQL2014' from the host 10.2.157.20.
Example of Regex Exclusion
10.2.157.20/SQL.*/.* - Excludes the SQL server instances 'SQL2012' and 'SQL2014' from the host 10.2.157.20.
Considerations Consider the following when using the Auto Protect option on the backup job
l If new databases are added to the host, the existing filters are applied to the newly added databases. For example, if the exclude filter matches the newly added databases then these databases will be excluded in the backup job.
l If any system databases are excluded by the filters in an SQL server, it will exclude all the system databases belonging to that SQL server.
l When defining filters to exclude AG databases, ensure that the filters are configured on all the AG hosts. For example, to exclude an AG database and if the AG database has 4 hosts, then ensure that the filters are defined on all the four AG hosts.
l Auto protect functionality is supported only for physical SQL jobs (file-based and native)
l To selectively exclude a SQL database from the protection job, you must upgrade all the cluster nodes to version 6.5.1 and later.
If MS SQL belongs to an AG network, selecting that server displays options for protecting the AG.

l Select all servers that belong to this AG network.
Note: If backing up VMs within an AG, protecting the AG databases requires that all servers within the AG are registered with the Cohesity cluster and are selected for protection. Otherwise AG databases are skipped and only local databases will be backed up. New servers added to AG are not automatically protected.
When using this option when there are multiple AGs, only interlinked AG nodes are automatically selected. For example:
l If there are AGs that use only Node1 and Node2 and other AGs that use Node3 and Node4, if you select Node2 as a source, only Node1 is added automatically.
l If AG1 uses Node1 and Node2, AG2 uses Node2 and Node4, AG3 uses Node3 and Node5. If you select Node2, then these nodes are selected: Node1, Node2 and Node4. Node3 and Node5 are not selected.
When adding nodes to an AG that is protected by Cohesity, ensure you register the node with Cohesity and add it to the Protection Group. Otherwise the AG databases will not be protected. When removing nodes from an AG that is protected by Cohesity, you can remove it from the Protection Group or keep it; the AG databases remain protected in either case. If the removed node remains in the Protection Group, only its local databases are backed up. If you do not want to back up the removed node, you can safely remove it. l Select only this server. l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental protection run to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last protection run.

Microsoft SQL Server VDI-based Recovery Recommendations
The Virtual Device Interface (VDI) is a Microsoft interface that allows the Cohesity agent to execute SQL Server Native backup and restore commands. This backup type produces a standard SQL Server Native backup of type (.BAK), transaction logs, (.TRN), and differentials, (.DIFF). These backup files are stored on a Cohesity View and take advantage of View compression, deduplication, encryption, replication, and archiving features. The aim of the SQL DBA is to have a combination of backups so that the database can be restored to any point in time. A good combination of backups consists of having a full backup, differential (in Cohesity, incremental) backups, and log backups. For example, all SQL database restores must begin with a full database backup, secondly, a differential can then be applied to the full, and finally, log backups can be applied in sequence to complete the database restore. When the backups are applied during the database restore process, you are sequentially adding the captured changes to the database: FULL+DIFF+Log1+Log2+Log3 = Restored Database. All Microsoft VDI backups, their differentials, and their logs are dependent on a full backup to perform a database restore. Microsoft requires that in order to restore a SQL database, you must start with a full backup, then its transaction logs can be applied. This means your backup retention policy must keep a full backup along with its log backups in order to successfully restore a database. Simply put, a SQL VDI-based database restore requires a full backup to seed the database, then differential and/or log backups are applied to the specified point in time. We recommend retaining two sets of full backups with their differential and log backups.
Note: A good backup plan always includes a combination of full, differential, and log backups.

SQL Server Maintenance Mode
You can enable maintenance mode for SQL Server instances and databases. Enabling maintenance mode skips any scheduled or manually initiated protection runs. To place a SQL Server instance or database in maintenance mode:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click on the action menu ( ) of the source and select Maintenance. 3. You can initiate the maintenance mode immediately or later.
To initiate the maintenance mode immediately: 1. Select Start Now. The Start Maintenance Now dialog displays the list of Protection Groups available in the source. 2. Review the list of Protection Groups and enter Yes to confirm. 3. Optionally, you can enter a note. 4. Click Confirm.
To schedule the maintenance mode: 1. Select Schedule. 2. On the Schedule Maintenance dialog, enter the start date and time and the end date and time. 3. Optionally, you can enter a note. 4. Click Save.
The SQL Server instance or database will be set in maintenance mode accordingly.
AG in Maintenance Mode
When maintenance mode is enabled for a SQL instance hosting the AG database, the replica hosting the instance is not considered for the AG backup plan. This behavior is common to both legacy (non-first-class citizen) and first-class citizen features. For legacy AG backup, only the replica for which maintenance mode is enabled will be skipped. You must enable maintenance mode on all the replicas to skip the entire backup.
Migrate Microsoft SQL Server
The following topics provide guidance to help you migrate MS SQL databases:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

About Migrating Microsoft SQL Server Databases
You can use MS SQL database migration for the following use cases:
l Back up and migrate a database from a single pane of glass. Leverage database backup to achieve database migration. No more shipping logs across multiple sites or multiple data centers. Upgrade the MS SQL Server version while minimizing application downtime and maintaining the ability to restore to any point in time.
l Staging a database on the target server for faster recovery with Cohesity's database migration. Stage a database on the target SQL server and perform only incremental updates at the file level to improve RPO.
Database migration for file-based MS SQL backups consists of the following actions, which must be initiated manually:
1. Perform the initial copy of database files to the target MS SQL server. 2. Sync forward to the latest incremental/full snapshot available on the cluster. You can
trigger multiple syncs. For each sync, Cohesity performs incremental file updates to database files on the target MS SQL server. Syncs ensure files are up to date. The files are not attached to the database until you complete the finalized workflow. This ensures that the database is up to date when finalization occurs. 3. Finalize the migration. Finalizing is available only if the target database is synced to the latest snapshot. This brings the database online. After the database is online and the finalize step succeeds, the recovery task is completed successfully. You cannot perform syncs after this point because the migration workflow is complete.
Migrate Microsoft SQL Server Databases
Before you migrate an MS SQL database, ensure that a file-based snapshot exists on the cluster.

Amazon Relational Database Service for MariaDB
Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) for MariaDB is a fully managed, cloud-based relational database service offered by Amazon Web Services (AWS). Cohesity natively integrates with AWS to provide a simple, fast, and cost-effective solution for backup, recovery, and data management of Amazon Relational Database Service for MariaDB instances.
Important: Cohesity supports the backup and recovery of Amazon RDS for MariaDB only at the instance level.
This topic provides information on how you can protect Amazon RDS for MariaDB on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS. For information on protecting Amazon RDS for MariaDB on Physical and Virtual Edition clusters, see Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora.
Plan and Prepare for Amazon RDS for MariaDB Protection
To protect Amazon RDS for MariaDB with Cohesity, you must register your AWS as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. Ensure you meet the pre-requisites and understand the considerations before registering the AWS source with the Cohesity cluster.
Ports Used for Communication
For information on port numbers required, see Amazon Elastic Block Store.
Considerations for AWS RDS for MariaDB Data Protection
Review and understand the following considerations before you protect Amazon RDS for MariaDB:
l Cohesity supports only snapshot-based protection of RDS for MariaDB. Ingest-based protection is not supported.
l Cross-account restore of an Amazon RDS for MariaDB protected using the AWS Snapshot protection type is not supported.
l When recovering encrypted RDS instance to the same AWS account but a different AWS region, you must create a KMS encryption key in the target region with the same alias name as the KMS key used to encrypt the source RDS instance.
l When performing cross-region cross-account recovery of an Amazon RDS instance encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, ensure the following: l The source account's KMS key alias is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account. Example:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

If A1 is the source account with region R1, and A2 is the destination account with region R2, ensure the KMS key alias from A1 is available in both R1 and R2 of A2.
l The destination account has permission to access the source account's KMS key alias.
l The option group from the source account is available in both the source and destination regions of the destination account.
