Setting

Description

Pause Future Runs

Enable Pause Future Run only if you do not want to schedule future runs of the Protection Group.

End Date

Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Alerts

Optional.
Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Amazon DocumentDB
Amazon DocumentDB is a fully managed, MongoDB API-compatible document database service. Cohesity natively integrates with AWS to provide simple, fast, and cost-effective backup, recovery, and data management for both Instance-based DocumentDB Clusters and Elastic DocumentDB Clusters in your AWS source.
Important: The backup and recovery of Amazon DocumentDB is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster).
Plan and Prepare for Amazon DocumentDB Protection
Before protecting Amazon DocumentDB with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Amazon DocumentDB with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your AWS as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.

When creating a Protection Group to protect Amazon DocumentDB at the database level, the Cohesity cluster must authenticate to the DocumentDB primary instance using one of the following methods:

l IAM-authenticated DocumentDB User: This option is available only if the AWS account is registered using the IAM Role method.
If you choose the IAM-authenticated DocumentDB user method, ensure the following: l DocumentDB supports the MongoDB AWS authentication mechanism (MONGODBAWS). l The database user must be created inside the Amazon DocumentDB cluster. l The database username must be the ARN of the IAM Role attached to the Cohesity cluster nodes (when registering the AWS account). l The IAM Role must allow the sts:AssumeRole flow for MONGODB-AWS authentication.

Structure

Description

AWS Organization

The AWS Organization registered with Cohesity for Amazon DocumentDB protection. Applicable when the AWS source is registered at the organization level.

Organizational Unit (OU)

The Organizational Units within the AWS Organization that contain member accounts.

Member Account The AWS member accounts within the organization that contain Amazon DocumentDB.

AWS Account

The AWS account registered with Cohesity for DocumentDB protection. Applicable when the AWS source is registered at the account level.

AWS Region

The AWS region where the AWS resources reside.

The specific Amazon DocumentDB cluster within the selected region.

DocumentDB Database

The individual databases hosted within the DocumentDB cluster. The database will be listed in the entity hierarchy only if you have provided credentials to discover the databases of the Amazon DocumentDB cluster.

Backup Scope by Amazon DocumentDB Hierarchy
The Cohesity cluster allows you to back up Amazon DocumentDB databases at different levels of the entity hierarchy. The available hierarchy levels depend on whether the AWS source is registered at the organization level or account level. You can choose to back up:
l AWS Organization - Protect all Amazon DocumentDB clusters and databases across all member accounts in the registered AWS organization.
l Organizational Unit (OU) - Protect all Amazon DocumentDB clusters and databases within the member accounts that belong to a specific organizational unit.
l Member Account - Protect all Amazon DocumentDB clusters and databases within a specific member account in the registered AWS organization.
l AWS Account - Protect all the Amazon DocumentDB clusters and databases within the registered AWS account.
l AWS Region - Protect all the Amazon DocumentDB clusters and databases within a specific region of the registered account.

l DocumentDB Cluster - Protect all Amazon DocumentDB databases within a specific Amazon DocumentDB cluster and all databases hosted on it.
l DocumentDB Databases - Protect individual Amazon DocumentDB database by providing the database credentials.
Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports only full backups for Amazon DocumentDB databases. Incremental backups are not supported.
Protect Amazon DocumentDB
In Cohesity, Amazon DocumentDB databases are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Policies.

Section

Setting QoS Policy

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, we recommend the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Amazon DynamoDB
Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database service provided by AWS, designed for high performance at scale. In DynamoDB, data is stored in tables. Cohesity natively integrates with AWS to provide a simple, fast, and cost-effective solution for the backup, recovery, and data management of both the DynamoDB Standard table class and the DynamoDB Standard-Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class in your AWS source.
Important: The backup and recovery of Amazon DynamoDB is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster). This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Plan and Prepare for Amazon DynamoDB Protection Before protecting Amazon DynamoDB with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Amazon DynamoDB with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your AWS as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.
Ports Used for Communication
For information on port numbers required, seeAWS Cloud Database Workloads.
Considerations for Amazon DynamoDB Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before protecting Amazon DynamoDB tables:
l General Protection Limitations l Tables in Amazon DynamoDB can be protected across all regions in your AWS source. l During recovery, you can restore Amazon DynamoDB tables to their original region. However, the restore operation fails if another table with the same name already exists in that region. l To restore a table using its original name, you must first manually delete the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

existing table. Then, perform the recovery without specifying any prefix or suffix for the table name.
l Restore Method Behavior and Priority
When a restore is initiated, Cohesity attempts recovery using the AWS Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) method first. If PITR is unavailable, Cohesity falls back to the snapshot-based restore method.
Capabilities and limitations differ between the two methods:
l PITR Restore
l By default, restores both Local Secondary Indexes (LSIs) and Global Secondary Indexes (GSIs) within the 35-day PITR window.
l Restore is supported only to the original AWS account where the backups were created.
l Cross-region and cross-account restores are not supported using PITR.
l Snapshot-Based Restore
l Supports restoring Local Secondary Indexes (LSIs) only when the Restore Local Secondary Indexes option is enabled during recovery. Otherwise, Cohesity uses the AWS ImportTable-based restore workflow, which does not restore LSIs.
l Cross-region and cross-account restores are supported.
l Used automatically when PITR is unavailable.
l LSI Restore Considerations
l If Restore Local Secondary Indexes is enabled for snapshot-based restore, but the selected DynamoDB tables do not contain any Local Secondary Index (LSIs), Cohesity automatically switches to the ImportTable-based recovery method to reduce restore cost.
l If you select multiple Amazon DynamoDB tables in a single recovery task, the configured restore settings are applied to all selected tables. Cohesity recommends creating separate recovery tasks for each table when the table sizes differ significantly. This allows you to optimize throughput allocation, restore performance, and cost per hour for individual tables.
l If an LSI-enabled snapshot-based restore fails or is cancelled, Cohesity may not be able to automatically delete the partially created DynamoDB table. In such cases, the table might remain in the AWS account. If the table is provisioned with high write capacity units, AWS billing continues until the table is deleted.
Recommendation: To avoid additional AWS charges, verify and manually delete any partially restored tables after a failed or cancelled recovery operation.
l Global Tables

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

l Global tables are recovered as local tables. l After restore, you must manually reconfigure the table as a global table. l This behavior applies only to EVENTUAL CONSISTENCY Global Tables. l Backup strategy: Perform the backup from any one of the regions
participating in the global table. l Restore strategy: Restore the table to the desired region, then manually
configure the global table. l Index Restore Considerations
l Tables with Global Secondary Indexes (GSIs) may take longer to restore because indexes are recreated during recovery.
l Restore of Local Secondary Indexes (LSIs) is not supported when using snapshot-based protection. This limitation applies only to snapshot restores and not to PITR restores. This is an AWS consideration for importing DynamoDB tables from Amazon S3.
l Large Table Backup and Restore Considerations For DynamoDB tables larger than 2.5 TB: l The default Max task DPUs per account must be increased in the AWS region where the AWS Glue job runs. l The increase is required on: l The AWS side (AWS Glue DPU quota) l The Cohesity side (cluster G-flag configuration) Contact Cohesity Support for assistance with increasing the DPU limits on both the AWS and Cohesity sides. For Large Restores (15 TB or Larger) l AWS does not natively support restores of 15 TB or larger. l Before attempting a restore of this scale, you must contact AWS Support to request an increase to the import size limit.
l AWS Charges For protected DynamoDB tables, the following AWS charges may apply: l AWS Glue job costs: For data transformation and movement during backup or recovery. l Export table costs: For exporting table data to S3. l Egress costs: For data transferred out of AWS.
l Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) Considerations

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

l Cohesity enables PITR for Amazon DynamoDB tables, allowing restoration to any specific point within the past 35 days.
l PITR is available only when restoring to the original AWS account.
l After unprotecting a DynamoDB table, you must manually disable PITR to avoid unnecessary retention and associated AWS costs.
l Manually turning off PITR after a full backup breaks the backup chain. Subsequent incremental backups cannot run until a new full backup is completed.
l DynamoDB Version Limitation
l Restoring a backup taken from a higher DynamoDB version to a lower version is not supported.
l Recovery Cleanup on Failure or Cancellation
If the recovery workflow fails or is cancelled, Cohesity may be unable to automatically delete or roll back the DynamoDB table created during the recovery process, because the configured IAM role has insufficient deletion permissions. In such cases, you must verify the recovered table in AWS and manually delete any incomplete or unwanted tables.

Backup Scope by Amazon DynamoDB Hierarchy
The Cohesity cluster allows you to back up Amazon DynamoDB at different levels of the entity hierarchy. You can choose to back up:
l AWS Organization - Backup all Amazon DynamoDB tables across all member accounts in the registered AWS organization.
l Organizational Unit (OU) - Backup all Amazon DynamoDB tables within the member accounts that belong to a specific organizational unit.
l Member Account - Backup all Amazon DynamoDB tables within a specific member account in the registered AWS organization.
l AWS Account - Backup all the AWS DynamoDB tables within the registered AWS account.
l AWS Region - Backup all AWS DynamoDB tables within a specific region of the registered account.
l DynamoDB Tables - Backup individual DynamoDB tables.
Backup Process
When you initiate a protection run for DynamoDB tables, Cohesity performs a DynamoDB API call to export the table data to a temporary AWS S3 staging bucket . This S3 bucket is created by Cohesity in the same AWS account and region where the DynamoDB table to be backed up resides.
Once the data is successfully exported to the S3 bucket, Cohesity ingests the exported data from the S3 bucket to the Cohesity cluster. Once the data is fully backed up to the Cohesity cluster, the data on the staging bucket is deleted to free up storage space.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

During the first full backup, Cohesity also enables AWS Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR) for the DynamoDB table. This allows you to perform PITR restores, enabling recovery to a specific point in time within the past 35 days by default.
Note: Cohesity supports adding custom tags to S3 staging buckets. Tags are applied Cohesity cluster-wide across all AWS registrations on that Cohesity cluster. To configure tags for S3 staging bucket, contact Cohesity Support.
Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports both full and Incremental backups for Amazon DynamoDB. Although Cohesity does not support log backups for DynamoDB, it enables Amazon DynamoDB Point-In-Time Recovery (PITR) to provide point-in-time restore capability. This allows Cohesity to perform point-in-time recovery of DynamoDB tables back to the original location using AWS-managed PITR snapshots.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Alerts

Optional.

l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Recover Amazon DynamoDB
After protecting your Amazon DynamoDB tables in the Cohesity cluster, you can recover them to either their original region or a different region. Cohesity recovers the table as a new table within the location you choose. When you restore a table, all the tags that were present on the original table at the time of backup are automatically added to the restored table. Additionally, any new tags specified in the custom recovery options are also applied to the restored table. You can also perform PITR when restoring to the original AWS account where the backups were created. Restoring to an alternate AWS account using PITR is not supported.
Note: We recommend that you review the Plan and Prepare for Amazon DynamoDB Protection topic.
Recovery Process
Depending on the target location for recovery, Cohesity supports the following recovery methods for Amazon DynamoDB:
l Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) l Snapshot-based Recovery
Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR)
Cohesity uses Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) when restoring a DynamoDB table within the same AWS account and region as the source table.
l By default, Cohesity attempts PITR method for recovering to the same region and account as the original DynamoDB table.
l PITR uses AWS-native APIs to restore the table directly from DynamoDB-managed backups.
l When PITR is successful, the table is restored with all configurations, including Local Secondary Indexes (LSIs) and Global Secondary Indexes (GSIs).
l PITR is available only when: l The restore point is within the configured PITR retention window (up to 35 days). l The source table exists and PITR was enabled.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

l If PITR is not available or fails, Cohesity automatically falls back to snapshot-based recovery.
Snapshot-based Recovery
Cohesity uses this method when restoring the DynamoDB table to an alternate location (different AWS account or region). Depending on whether Local Secondary Index (LSI) restore is required, Cohesity uses one of the following approaches:
l Snapshot Restore using ImportTable l Snapshot Restore with LSI Support
Snapshot Restore using ImportTable
This is the default snapshot-based recovery method when LSI restore is not required. In this method:
1. Cohesity exports the selected table data from the Cohesity cluster to an Amazon S3 staging bucket. This bucket is created by Cohesity in the same AWS region as the target DynamoDB table.
2. After the data export is complete, Amazon DynamoDB imports the data directly from the S3 staging bucket into the target table. Cohesity invokes the AWS ImportTable API to import the table from the S3 bucket.
3. After the import is complete, Cohesity deletes the exported data from the staging bucket to reduce storage costs.
Snapshot Restore with LSI Support
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
If you have enabled the Restore Local Secondary Indexes option on the Cohesity restore workflow, Cohesity uses an alternative restore method to support LSI restoration. In this method:
1. Cohesity creates a new DynamoDB table using the original table schema, including LSI definitions.
2. Data is read from the Cohesity snapshot and written to DynamoDB using the BatchWriteItem API.
3. Data ingestion is performed in parallel using multiple workers to optimize throughput. 4. After data ingestion completes:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

l Global Secondary Indexes (GSIs) are created and backfilled sequentially using AWS APIs.
l Table settings are reverted to the original configuration.

Amazon Redshift Cluster
Amazon Redshift cluster is a fully managed, petabyte-scale cloud data warehouse service offered by AWS to efficiently analyze large datasets using standard SQL and existing business intelligence (BI) tools. Cohesity natively integrates with AWS to provide solution for the backup, recovery, and data management of Amazon Redshift databases in your AWS source.
Important: The backup and recovery of Amazon Redshift cluster is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster). This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Plan and Prepare for Amazon Redshift Cluster Before protecting Amazon Redshift Cluster with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect AmazonRedshift Cluster with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your AWS as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.
AWS S3 Staging Bucket Requirement
Cohesity uses an Amazon S3 staging bucket as temporary storage during the backup and recovery of Amazon Redshift databases. You can either allow Cohesity to automatically create the staging bucket when you initiate a backup or recovery task, or you can manually create a custom bucket in your AWS account before starting the process. You must use the same bucket for both backup and recovery. If you choose to manually create the bucket, ensure to create the AWS S3 bucket of type, S3 Standard in the same AWS region as the Redshift database selected for backup and restore. You can specify only one custom bucket name per Protection Group. Because an S3 bucket belongs to a single AWS region, a custom bucket is supported only when all Redshift

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

databases in the Protection Group are in the same region. If your Protection Group spans multiple regions, use the Auto Create option instead.
Note: Cohesity supports adding custom tags to S3 staging buckets when the auto-create staging bucket option is selected. Tags are applied Cohesity clusterwide across all AWS registrations on that Cohesity cluster. To configure tags for S3 staging bucket, contact Cohesity Support.
Ports Used for Communication
For information on port numbers required, seeAWS Cloud Database Workloads.
Considerations for Amazon Redshift Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect Amazon Redshift databases:
l Redshift Support Scope: Cohesity supports protection only for provisioned Amazon Redshift clusters. Amazon Redshift Serverless is not supported.
l Restore Scope: does not support restoring Amazon Redshift databases to a different region or account. Restores can only be performed to the original account within the same region.
l FIPS Certification: Backup and recovery operations for Redshift databases using Cohesity are not FIPS-certified.
l Database Coverage: Only user databases are supported for protection. System databases within Redshift are not supported for backup or recovery.
l Cluster State Requirement: The Redshift cluster must be in an available state for Cohesity to initiate a backup. Backups cannot be initiated if the cluster is offline or unavailable.
l Empty Tables: It is not recommended to back up databases that contain empty tables.
l Table Format: Tables with names that use double quotes or are case-sensitive will not be restored.
l Crash-Consistent Backup: Cohesity provides crash-consistent protection for Amazon Redshift databases. Before initiating a backup, review your application's activity and requirements to determine if it is necessary to perform a checkpoint or quiesce the application.
l Tag Restore: Cohesity does not support restoring tags for Amazon Redshift clusters since the protection is at database level.
l Point-in-Time Restore (PITR): Cohesity does not support PITR of Amazon Redshift cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

l AWS S3 Staging Bucket: You must use the same AWS S3 staging bucket for both backup and recovery. Recovery may fail if you do not use the same staging bucket that was used during the backup operation.
l Version Downgrade Not Supported: Restoring a backup taken from a higher Redshift database version to a lower version is not supported.
l External Database Support Limitation: External databases in Amazon Redshift created through AWS Glue Data Catalog registration may appear in the Cohesity cluster entity hierarchy; however, they are not currently supported for backup and recovery.
l IAM Auto-Created User Ownership: Recovery of Redshift cluster database to an alternate cluster can fail if a table is owned by an IAM auto-created database user (for example a user created through Redshift Query Editor v2 using temporary IAM credentials). During recovery, the workflow attempts to restore table ownership using an ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO statement. This statement fails if the referenced IAM user does not already exist on the target cluster, because IAM auto-created users are not restored as part of the recovery process.
To resolve this issue, log in to the target cluster using the same IAM identity (example, using Redshift Query Editor). This automatically creates the corresponding database user on the target cluster. After the user is created, rerun the recovery task. The subsequent recovery task succeeds.
l Custom Staging Bucket and Multi-Region Considerations: When you use the Specify Bucket to Use option, you can specify only one bucket name per Protection Group. Because an S3 bucket resides in a single AWS region, this option is not supported in scenarios where Redshift databases from multiple regions or accounts might be protected together, such as:
l Auto-protect at the AWS Account, OU, or Organization level.
l Tag-based auto-protection.
l A Protection Group that includes Redshift databases from multiple AWS regions.
l AWS Organization registration spanning multiple accounts with Redshift databases.
l For these scenarios, use the Auto Create option to allow Cohesity to automatically create the appropriate staging bucket per region.

Backup Scope by Amazon Redshift Cluster Hierarchy
The Cohesity cluster allows you to back up Amazon Redshift at different levels of the entity hierarchy. You can choose to back up:
l AWS Organization - Protect all Amazon Redshift cluster databases across all member accounts in the registered AWS Organization.
l Organizational Unit (OU) - Backup all Amazon Redshift cluster databases within the member accounts that belong to a specific organizational unit.
l Member Account - Backup all Amazon Redshift cluster databases within a specific member account in the registered AWS organization.
l AWS Account - Backup all the AWS Redshift cluster databases within the registered AWS account.
l AWS Region - Backup all the AWS Redshift cluster databases within a specific region of the registered account.
l Redshift Cluster - Backup all databases within a specific Redshift cluster. l Redshift Database - Backup individual Redshift cluster database.
Backup Process
When you initiate a protection run in the Cohesity cluster to back up Amazon Redshift databases, Cohesity first exports the selected Redshift data to an Amazon S3 staging bucket. Once the data is successfully exported to the S3 bucket, Cohesity ingests the staged data from the S3 bucket into the Cohesity cluster. Once the ingestion is successful and the data is fully backed up to the Cohesity cluster, Cohesity automatically deletes the exported data from the staging bucket to free up storage and minimize S3 costs.
Note: Cohesity supports adding custom tags to S3 staging buckets when the auto-create staging bucket option is selected. Tags are applied Cohesity clusterwide across all AWS registrations on that Cohesity cluster. To configure tags for S3 staging bucket, contact Cohesity Support.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports only full backups for Redshift cluster databases. Incremental backups are not supported.
Protect Amazon Redshift Cluster
In Cohesity, Amazon Redshift databases are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Policies.
Prerequisites
Before initiating a backup of Amazon Redshift cluster databases, an Amazon S3 staging bucket must be available in the AWS account where the Redshift cluster resources reside. This bucket is used to temporarily store exported data during the backup process. You can manually create or select an existing S3 bucket in your AWS account, or allow Cohesityto automatically create one when the backup process begins. When creating a Protection Group, you can choose either option based on your preference.
AWS Source Registered at the Account Level
When creating a Protection Group, you can manually specify an S3 bucket only if all selected databases belong to the same AWS account and region. If all selected databases are in the same AWS account and region: You can manually specify a newly created or existing S3 bucket, or allow Cohesity to automatically create one. If you are manually specifying an S3 bucket, ensure the bucket is in the same account and region as the selected database If the selected databases span multiple regions: You must allow allow Cohesity to automatically create the staging bucket. If you manually specify a newly created or existing S3 bucket, the backup will fail.
AWS Source Registered at the Organization Level
When protecting databases across member accounts, Cohesity supports manual bucket selection only when all selected databases for protection belong to the same member account and region. If all selected databases are in the same AWS member account and region: You can manually specify a newly created or existing S3 bucket, or allow Cohesity to automatically create one. If you are manually specifying an S3 bucket, ensure the bucket is in the same account and region as the selected database

Pause Future Runs

End Date

Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, we recommend the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Alerts

Optional.
Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Recover Amazon Redshift Cluster
Cohesity does not support restoring Amazon Redshift databases to a different region or account. Restores can only be performed to the original account within the same region.
Note: We recommend that you review the Considerations for Amazon Redshift Data Protection.
Recovery Process
When you initiate a recovery, Cohesity exports the selected Redshift data from the Cohesity cluster back into the Amazon S3 staging bucket that was used during the original backup. After the data is successfully exported to the staging bucket, Amazon Redshift reads the exported files from the bucket and imports them into the specified Redshift target location. Once the import completes, Cohesity automatically deletes the exported files from the staging bucket to free up storage and minimize S3 costs.

Amazon Redshift Serverless
Amazon Redshift Serverless is an on-demand, auto-scaling configuration of the Amazon Redshift data warehouse that allows you to run analytics without managing data warehouse infrastructure. Cohesity integrates with AWS to provide a simple, fast, and cost-effective solution for backup, recovery, and data management of databases within the Amazon Redshift Serverless namespace of your AWS source.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

Important: The backup and recovery of Amazon Redshift cluster is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS (formerly known as AWS NGCE cluster). This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Plan and Prepare for Amazon Redshift Serverless
Before protecting Amazon Redshift Serverless with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect AmazonRedshift Serverless with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your AWS as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For information on registering AWS, see Register AWS Source.
Required Permissions for Amazon Redshift Serverless Data Protection
For information on the permissions required to protect Redshift Serverless namespace database, see Minimum Permissions for Individual Workloads and Workflows.
AWS S3 Staging Bucket Requirement
Cohesity uses an Amazon S3 staging bucket as temporary storage during the backup and recovery of databases within a Redshift Serverless namespace. You can either allow Cohesity to automatically create the staging bucket when you initiate a backup or recovery task, or you can manually create the staging bucket in your AWS account before starting the process. You must use the same bucket for both backup and recovery. If you choose to manually create the bucket, ensure to create the AWS S3 bucket of type, S3 Standard in the same AWS region as the Redshift Serverless namespace database selected for backup and restore. You can specify only one custom bucket name per Protection Group. Because an S3 bucket belongs to a single AWS region, a custom bucket is supported only when all Redshift databases in the Protection Group are in the same region. If your Protection Group spans multiple regions, use the Auto Create option instead.
Note: Cohesity supports adding custom tags to S3 staging buckets when the auto-create staging bucket option is selected. Tags are applied Cohesity clusterwide across all AWS registrations on that Cohesity cluster. To configure tags for S3 staging bucket, contact Cohesity Support.
Ports Used for Communication
For information on port numbers required, seeAWS Cloud Database Workloads.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

Admin Password Secret ARN Requirement
For enabling backup and restore operations in Amazon Redshift Serverless, you must configure an admin password secret ARN on the namespace. Backup and recovery workflows require secure access to administrative credentials. Configuring an admin password secret ARN ensures that these credentials are securely stored and retrieved using AWS Secrets Manager, enabling successful data protection operations. This requirement applies to both:
l Newly created namespaces l Existing namespaces that do not already have an associated secret ARN
You can update existing namespaces using the AWS CLI. For more information, see AWS CLI update-namespace command.
Note: Use the --manage-admin-password option to enable management of the admin password via Secrets Manager.
Enabling the admin password secret ARN rotates the existing admin password. As a result, any applications or services using the previous password will fail to connect until they are updated. Ensure that all dependent applications retrieve credentials dynamically from AWS Secrets Manager.
Considerations for Amazon Redshift Serverless Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect Amazon Redshift databases:
l Restore Scope: Cohesity does not support restoring Amazon Redshift databases to a different region or account. Restores can only be performed to the original account within the same region.
l FIPS Certification: Backup and recovery operations for Redshift databases using Cohesity are FIPS-certified.
l Database Coverage: Only user databases are supported for protection. System databases within Redshift are not supported for backup or recovery.
l Namespace and workgroup State Requirement: The Amazon Redshift Serverless Namespace and workgroup must be in an available state for Cohesity to initiate a backup. Backups cannot be initiated if the Namespace and workgroup are offline or unavailable.
l Empty Tables: It is not recommended to back up databases that contain empty tables.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

l Table Format: Tables with names that use double quotes or are case-sensitive will not be restored.
l Crash-Consistent Backup: Cohesity provides crash-consistent protection for databases. Before initiating a backup, review your application's activity and requirements to determine if it is necessary to perform a checkpoint or quiesce the application.
l Tag Restore: Cohesity does not support restoring tags for namespace since the protection is at database level.
l AWS S3 Staging Bucket: You must use the same AWS S3 staging bucket for both backup and recovery. Recovery may fail if you do not use the same staging bucket that was used during the backup operation.
l Custom Staging Bucket and Multi-Region Considerations: When you use the Specify Bucket to Use option, you can specify only one bucket name per Protection Group. Because an S3 bucket resides in a single AWS region, this option is not supported in scenarios where Redshift Serverless namespace databases from multiple regions or accounts might be protected together, such as:
l Auto-protect at the AWS Account, OU, or Organization level.
l Tag-based auto-protection.
l A Protection Group that includes Redshift databases from multiple AWS regions.
l AWS Organization registration spanning multiple accounts with Redshift Serverless namespace databases.
l For these scenarios, use the Auto Create option to allow Cohesity to automatically create the appropriate staging bucket per region.

Note: Cohesity supports adding custom tags to S3 staging buckets when the auto-create staging bucket option is selected. Tags are applied Cohesity clusterwide across all AWS registrations on that Cohesity cluster. To configure tags for S3 staging bucket, contact Cohesity Support.

Section
Additional Settings

Setting

Description

Pause Future Runs

Enable Pause Future Run only if you do not want to schedule future runs of the Protection Group.

End Date

Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, we recommend the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Alerts

Optional.
Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

All the backups generated by the Protection Group are preserved till the snapshots expire. l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots: Allows you to delete the Protection Group and all associated local and archived snapshots. Replicated snapshots must be deleted from the remote cluster. Snapshots under DataLock cannot be deleted.

Recover Amazon Redshift Serverless
Cohesity does not support restoring Amazon Redshift Serverless namespace databases to a different region or account. Restores can only be performed to the original account within the same region.
Note: We recommend that you review the Considerations for Amazon Redshift Serverless Data Protection.
Recovery Process
When you initiate a recovery, Cohesity exports the selected Redshift Serverless data from the Cohesity cluster back into the Amazon S3 staging bucket that was used during the original backup. After the data is successfully exported to the staging bucket, Amazon Redshift Serverless reads the exported files from the bucket and imports them into the specified Redshift Serverless target location. Once the import completes, Cohesity automatically deletes the exported files from the staging bucket to free up storage and minimize S3 costs.
Recover Redshift Serverless Namespace Database
To recover Amazon Redshift Serverless namespace database:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Recoveries. 2. Click Recover at the top right of the page and then select AWS > Redshift
Serverless. 3. Search for the database by entering characters of the database name, or by
specifying the wildcard character *. 4. From the list of search results, select the database to recover.
l By default, the latest snapshot of the database is selected for recovery. l To recover from a different snapshot, hover over the snapshot and click the
Edit icon. The Edit Recovery Point for <database_name> page appears. l By default, snapshots are displayed in the List mode. You can switch to the
Timeline mode by clicking the Timeline tab in the top-right corner of the page. To select a snapshot from the List mode:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Register SQL Server on Linux OS

a. Select the List tab from the top-right corner of the Edit recovery point for <database_name> page. By default, the page displays the snapshots available in the last one month. You can also select a snapshot from a different date range by selecting the date range from the Date drop-down list. The page displays the available snapshots in the specified range.
b. Select the snapshots to be recovered. c. By default, the snapshot is recovered from the local Cohesity cluster. d. Click Select Recovery Point and then go to step 5. To select a snapshot from the Timeline mode: a. From the Choose a date drop-down, select a date. The snapshots available on
the selected date are displayed in blue dots on the timeline bar. b. Select the snapshot to be recovered by clicking the corresponding blue dot. c. By default, the snapshot is recovered from the local Cohesity cluster. d. Click Select Recovery Point and then go to step 5. 5. Click Next: Recover Options. 6. In the Recover To section, select any one of the following options based on where you want to restore the database and then provide the required information:
l Original Location: Restore the database to the original Amazon Redshift Serverless.
Note: Restoring to the original location will overwrite any existing database with the same name.
Type Yes to confirm. l New Location: Restore the database to an Amazon Redshift Serverless within
the same region of the same AWS account. Restoring to different AWS account or to a different region within the same account is not supported. Based on the registration level of the AWS source, select the recovery destination hierarchy:
l If the AWS source is registered at the organization level: l Source: Select the AWS organization that contains the destination Amazon Redshift serverless namespace. You can recover data only within the same AWS Organization as the source. l AWS Account: Select the AWS member account that contains the destination Amazon Redshift serverless namespace.

Setup Azure Cosmos DB - Table Permissions
Prerequisites Ensure the following are available:
l User with Global Administrator role. l Service Principal Object ID (from Enterprise Applications > your app > Object ID). Do
not use the Application (Client) ID. l Cosmos DB Account name, Subscription ID, Resource Group name.
Variables Ensure you replace the values with your actual values. SUBSCRIPTION_ID="<your-subscription-id>" RESOURCE_GROUP="<your-resource-group>" COSMOS_ACCOUNT="<your-cosmosdb-account-name>" PRINCIPAL_ID="<service-principal-object-id>" ACCOUNT_SCOPE="/subscriptions/${SUBSCRIPTION_ID}/resourceGroups/${RESOURCE_ GROUP}/providers/Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/${COSMOS_ACCOUNT}"
Procedure Following are the steps to setup the permissions:
1. Assign Control Plane Role (for Account Discovery)
az role assignment create \ --assignee-object-id "${PRINCIPAL_ID}" \ --assignee-principal-type "ServicePrincipal" \

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

--role "Cosmos DB Account Reader Role" \ --scope "/subscriptions/${SUBSCRIPTION_ID}"
Note: You can skip this step if the Service Principal already has the Contributor role at the resource group level.
2. Assign Cosmos DB Built-in Data Contributor Role (Data Plane)
az cosmosdb sql role assignment create \ --account-name "${COSMOS_ACCOUNT}" \ --resource-group "${RESOURCE_GROUP}" \ --scope "/" \ --principal-id "${PRINCIPAL_ID}" \ --role-definition-id "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002"
Where: --principal-id: The Object ID of the Service Principal (not the Application/Client ID) --role-definition-id: Built-in Data Contributor role ID (00000000-0000-0000-0000000000000002) --scope: Use / for the entire account 3. Create Custom Role for Throughput Settings (Data Plane) The Built-in Data Contributor role does not include the throughputSettings permissions. A custom role is required for table creation during recovery.
cat > /tmp/throughput-role.json << 'ROLEEOF' { "RoleName": "Cohesity Table Throughput Access", "Type": "CustomRole", "AssignableScopes": ["/"], "Permissions": [{ "DataActions": [ "Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/readMetadata", "Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/throughputSettings/*" ] }] } ROLEEOF az cosmosdb sql role definition create \ --account-name "${COSMOS_ACCOUNT}" \ --resource-group "${RESOURCE_GROUP}" \ --body @/tmp/throughput-role.json
4. Assign the Custom Throughput Role

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

ROLE_ID=$(az cosmosdb sql role definition list \ --account-name "${COSMOS_ACCOUNT}" \ --resource-group "${RESOURCE_GROUP}" \ --query "[?roleName=='Cohesity Table Throughput Access'].name" -o tsv)
echo "Custom role GUID: ${ROLE_ID}" az cosmosdb sql role assignment create \ --account-name "${COSMOS_ACCOUNT}" \ --resource-group "${RESOURCE_GROUP}" \ --scope "/" \ --principal-id "${PRINCIPAL_ID}" \ --role-definition-id "${ROLE_ID}"
5. Verify All Assignments
echo "=== Cosmos DB Data Plane Roles ===" az cosmosdb sql role assignment list \ --account-name "${COSMOS_ACCOUNT}" \ --resource-group "${RESOURCE_GROUP}" \ --output table
echo "=== Azure RBAC (Control Plane) Roles ===" az role assignment list \ --assignee "${PRINCIPAL_ID}" \ --scope "${ACCOUNT_SCOPE}" \ --output table
For Azure Cosmos DB - Table, DataProtect intentionally uses two Azure built-in roles and a custom role (for the throughputSettings/*) instead of a single all-in-one custom role. These permissions are Azure actions required by the workflow, and not a role definition. This is due to the following reasons:
l Control-plane vs data-plane separation. Cosmos DB splits permissions into two different RBAC systems. l Action entries (control plane) - managed by Azure RBAC (az role) l DataAction entries (data plane) - managed by the Cosmos DB data-plane RBAC (az cosmosdb sql role). A single Azure RBAC custom role cannot include Cosmos DB DataAction permissions, and a single Cosmos DB data-plane custom role cannot include control-plane Action permissions. A minimum of two role assignments is required.
l Data-plane roles cannot be assigned via Azure portal UI. Cosmos DB dataplane roles must be assigned via Azure CLI. Relying on the existing built-in Data Contributor role keeps the procedure minimal and consistent with the Microsoft pattern.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Microsoft-maintained built-in roles are preferred where they fit. The Cosmos DB Account Reader role and Cosmos DB Built-in Data Contributor role already contain most of the permissions. Using these ensures lesser maintenance, and any further permissions added by Microsoft to these roles will be picked automatically.
l Custom roles only fix the gap. Microsoft. DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/throughputSettings/* is the only permission not supported by the Built-in Data Contributor role. A custom role (step 3) grants only that permission, preserving least-privilege and avoiding a sprawling custom role that duplicates what the built-ins already provide.
l Auditability. The tables remain the source of truth for what and why permissions are used. The setup steps show how those permissions are granted (which built-in role or custom role covers each). Reviewers can map operation > permission > role without re-deriving the role contents.
Points To Remember
l After assigning roles, wait 5-10 minutes for role propagation before performing backup or recovery.
l Always use the Service Principal Object ID (from Enterprise Applications) and not the Application (Client) ID.
l Cosmos DB data plane roles cannot be assigned via the Azure portal UI; Azure CLI is required.
l The Cosmos DB Built-in Data Contributor role does not include throughputSettings permissions; the custom role is mandatory for recovery.
l User Managed Identity (UMI) and System Managed Identity (SMI) require the same permissions, except that you must use the Object ID of the Managed Identity resource instead of the Service Principal, to obtain the Principal ID.

Permissions Required to Refresh Materialized Views in Azure PostgreSQL
To refresh materialized views automatically or manually, the database user must have the required schema and object permissions. For materialized view refresh: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA <schema_name> TO <refresh_user>; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA <schema_name> TO <refresh_user>; GRANT ALL ON <materialized_view_name> TO <refresh_user>;
For dependency analysis: GRANT SELECT ON pg_class, pg_namespace, pg_depend, pg_rewrite TO refresh_ user;
Where you must, l replace <schema_name> with your actual schema name. l replace <refresh_user> with the database user configured in your DataProtect source. l replace <materialized_view_name> with each materialized view name.
Note: Ensure to use manual refresh after recovery if the database user does not have the required permissions.
For manual execution of script: GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE <restore_database_name> TO <refresh_user>; GRANT USAGE, CREATE ON SCHEMA <script_schema> TO <refresh_user>; Where, <script_schema> is the first schema in the search_path (often public). This is required for the script to create and drop temporary helper views. Manual execution of script requires connection to database and usage on the schema to create temporary views. Prerequisites for Source Registration Using Managed Identity
Cohesity DataProtect supports managed identity - User-Assigned Managed Identity (UMI) and System-Assigned Managed Identity (SMI), to access Azure APIs for Azure native data protection.
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Ensure the following when registering an Azure source using the Managed Identity authentication methods:
l Cohesity DataProtect runs on an Azure VM (for example, NGCE node), so that Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) is available for SMI and UMI token acquisition.
l Managed Identity configurations are set for authentication method. l SMI: System-Assigned Managed Identity (SMI) is enabled on the Azure VM where Cohesity runs. l UMI: User-Assigned Managed Identity (UMI) is created and attached to the Azure VM. The Client ID of the managed identity is required during registration. l Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): The managed identity has the required permissions for the specific workload. For more information, see the Plan and Prepare section of the respective Azure workload.

Azure Virtual Machines
Cohesity provides a simple and fast backup, recovery, and data management solution for Microsoft Azure Virtual Machines. This chapter includes the following topics:
Plan and Prepare for Azure Protection Review the following prerequisites and considerations of Azure.
Prerequisites
l Azure agent must be installed on the Windows VMs if you need to CloudSpin the VMs to Azure. For more information, see Windows VM Agent.
l The Cohesity cluster must be able to resolve the following URLs by name: l Login.windows.net l management.azure.com l *.blob.core.windows.net Ensure to whitelist *.blob.storage.azure.net.
l All storage accounts associated with the subscription must have the relevant permissions, not just the account used to register Azure.
Recovery Prerequisites To recover files and folder:
l Firewall port 50051 must be open on the target VM. For more information, see Manage Firewall Ports
l The target VM must be reachable with private IP. l The Cohesity agent must be installed on the target VM.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

Note: You can perform files and folder recovery to an Azure VM Linux instance only if the Azure VM Linux instance is of x86_64 architecture.
Considerations
General Considerations l Cloning is not supported. l App-consistent backup is not supported. l LDM for OS disk is not supported. l VMs with static IP addresses aren't restored with the same static IP. l All disk sizes must be a multiple of 1 MB.
Note: Adjusting disk size may cause failback issues to on-premises vCenter environments.
Independent Disk Considerations l Independent disks aren't converted during snapshot-based operations. l If the boot disk is an independent disk, conversion and cloning aren't supported.
This applies to the following use cases: l Clone VMs from On-Premises to Azure Cloud Service (On Demand CloudSpin) l Replicate and Clone VMs in Azure Cloud Edition l Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to Azure Cloud l Back Up Azure Cloud VMs, Replicate to On-Prem and Failback to Hypervisor Server l Clone VMs to Azure Cloud Using CloudSpin
Tenant-level Registration Considerations l Tenant-level registration of Azure Cloud Source is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure. l This feature is not supported on On-premises hardware clusters, Virtual Edition clusters, or Cohesity Cohesity Cloud Edition (Legacy).
Supported Operating Systems (UEFI Boot) Backup and restore of UEFI-enabled Azure VMs is supported for:
l Windows: 2012, 2016, 2019 l Ubuntu: 14, 16, 18, 20

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l RHEL: 6.x, 7.x, 8.x l CentOS: 6.x, 7.x File-Level Recovery Considerations File-level recovery (FLR) isn't supported in the following scenarios: l Azure VMs using the XFSv5 file system. l Encrypted VMs. l When Life Cycle Management (LCM) is enabled on:
l Azure storage. l External targets (Azure Hot Tier). l End-of-Life (EOL) Linux distributions when required package repositories aren't reachable (for example, YUM repositories for CentOS or RHEL-based distributions). In this scenario: l The Cohesity agent required for FLR can't be installed on the target VM. l File-level recovery fails.
Note: Backup and recovery of VMs continue to work as expected. Only filelevel recovery is affected.
l File/folder recovery to Azure Linux VMs is supported only on x86_64 architecture. l Recovery of Azure files and folders for encrypted VMs isn't supported.
When browsing files or folders for recovery, Cohesity does not display files or folders with an absolute path length exceeding approximately 3,500 characters. To recover these files or folders, select the parent directory. l File download is supported. l Standard_LRS l Premium_LRS l StandardSSD_LRS

Recovery Considerations and Behavior
l Recovery may fail if a disk contains more than 50 Azure tags. l Managed disk VMs in a powered-off state may show as 0 bytes, but backup and
recovery are supported. l Recovery of unmanaged disks depends on the target storage container SKU. l Restore fails if required resources are deleted:
l Resource group l Storage account l Storage container l Blobs l VMs restored to a different location: l Don't retain Availability Set configuration. l Disk-level recovery considerations: l Supported only for VMs protected using native snapshot protection on Cohesity
Cloud Edition on Azure. l For spanned volumes (such as LVM on Linux or Dynamic Disks/Storage Pools on
Windows), Cohesity restores disks individually. To maintain consistency, recover all disks that belong to the volume in the same recovery job. Recovering only some disks can break the configuration and may require manual reassembly inside the guest OS. l If the OS disk of a Linux VM contains /etc/fstab entries for disks that do not use the nofail option, the restored VM may fail to restart
Authentication and Access After Restore
l The restored Azure VM does not support login using username and password present in the backed-up VM. Login using SSH keys is supported. When the restored VM boots up for the first time, Azure images are pre-installed with cloud-init software that locks user accounts as per the default behavior. Workaround: 1. Create an admin user from the Azure portal. Or, log in using the root account (if enabled). 2. Unlock accounts using:
passwd -u <username>
Encryption Considerations

l Azure Storage Service Encryption (SSE): l No such consideration.

Native Snapshot Process for Creating a Snapshot
Creating a Snapshot for Managed Disks
Default method: The following is the default native snapshot process for creating a snapshot:
1. A snapshot of each managed disk is taken. 2. (Applicable only for private endpoint-enabled backup) A disk access resource with a
private endpoint linked is created. 3. (Applicable only for private endpoint-enabled backup) The disk access is then
attached to the snapshot of the managed disk.
Note: The disk access resource can be shared only by five disks. For every backup, depending on the disk access availability, Cohesity creates a new disk access or uses an existing disk access to attach it to the disk snapshot.
4. A SAS URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) is generated for the created snapshot. 5. The snapshot is then copied to the Cohesity cluster.
For managed disks, Azure does not provide APIs to perform incremental backups. The entire data is downloaded onto the Cohesity cluster each time you run a Protection Group. Alternative method: You can also use the following process for creating the snapshot:
Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

1. A snapshot (S1) of each managed disk is taken. 2. (Applicable only for private endpoint-enabled backup) A disk access resource with a
private endpoint linked is created and is then attached to the snapshot (S1).
Note: The disk access resource can be shared by up to five disks. For each backup, depending on disk access availability, Cohesity either creates a new disk access or reuses an existing one to attach to the disk snapshot.
3. A SAS URI is generated for the snapshot (S1). 4. Using the SAS URI, the snapshot (S1) is copied to the Cohesity cluster for the first
backup, which will be a full backup. (Applicable only for private endpoint-enabled backup) The disk access resource attached to the snapshot (S1) is deleted. This snapshot (S1) on Azure is retained after the first protection run. 5. In the next protection run, a new snapshot (S2) of each managed disk is taken. 6. (Applicable only for private endpoint-enabled backup) A disk access resource with a private endpoint linked is created and is then attached to the new and the previous snapshots (S1 and S2).
Note: Since each disk access resource can be shared by only five disks, multiple disk access resources may be created if there are more than five snapshots.
7. A SAS URI is generated for the new and previous snapshots. 8. The changes between the previous snapshot (S1) and the new snapshot (S2) are
calculated and then downloaded to the Cohesity cluster. 9. The SAS URI of both the snapshots is revoked. 10. The previous snapshot (S1) on Azure is deleted. The new snapshot (S2) is retained on
Azure for the next incremental protection run.
Important: Multiple Protection Groups can share disk access. However, if no Protection Group has used it for the past 20 minutes, Cohesity will delete it.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

Creating a Snapshot for Unmanaged Disks
1. A snapshot of an unmanaged disk is stored as a page blob. 2. The incremental changes between the previous and the current snapshot are
calculated and then downloaded to a Cohesity cluster. 3. The previous snapshot is then deleted.
Note: Only one outstanding snapshot (which reflects the latest complete snapshot) is always maintained and therefore to take an incremental backup, the current snapshot is compared with the previous outstanding snapshot and the incremental changes are only considered for backup. The older snapshots are deleted so that the system always maintains only one outstanding snapshot at any time.
Considerations
Review the following considerations of Azure native snapshotting: l App consistent backup is not supported. l Cloning is not supported. l Disks cannot be excluded when using Azure Native Snapshot API.
Back Up Azure Cloud VMs to Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster Using Native Snapshot API
Cohesity Cohesity Cloud Edition supports backing up Virtual Servers using the native snapshot API of the cloud service. For example, a Virtual Server Protection Group backs up VMs in a cloud service to a Cohesity Cloud Edition Cohesity cluster running in the same cloud service. The result of this backup is Snapshots on the Cohesity Cloud Edition cluster. You can recover the VMs from the snapshot on the Cohesity cluster to the cloud service as described in Recover VMs. Review the following considerations of Azure native snapshotting:
l App consistent backup is not supported. l Cloning is not supported. l Disks cannot be excluded when using Azure Native Snapshot API.

Native Snapshot Process for Creating a Snapshot
Note: By default, every backup run is a full backup. Please contact Cohesity Support to enable incremental backup.

Creating a Snapshot for Managed Disks
Default method: The following is the default native snapshot process for creating a snapshot:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

1. A snapshot of each managed disk is taken. 2. (Applicable only for private endpoint-enabled backup) A disk access resource with a
private endpoint linked is created. 3. (Applicable only for private endpoint-enabled backup) The disk access is then
attached to the snapshot of the managed disk. 4. A SAS URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) is generated for the created snapshot. 5. The snapshot is then copied to the Cohesity cluster.
For managed disks, Azure does not provide APIs to perform incremental backups. The entire data is downloaded onto the Cohesity cluster each time you run a Protection Group. Alternative method: You can also use the following process for creating the snapshot:
Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
1. A snapshot (S1) of each managed disk is taken. 2. (Applicable only for private endpoint-enabled backup) A disk access resource with a
private endpoint linked is created and is then attached to the snapshot (S1). 3. A SAS URI is generated for the snapshot (S1). 4. Using the SAS URI, the snapshot (S1) is copied to the Cohesity cluster for the first
backup, which will be a full backup. (Applicable only for private endpoint-enabled backup) The disk access resource attached to the snapshot (S1) is deleted. This snapshot (S1) on Azure is retained after the first protection run. 5. In the next protection run, a new snapshot (S2) of each managed disk is taken. 6. (Applicable only for private endpoint-enabled backup) A disk access resource with a private endpoint linked is created and is then attached to the new and the previous snapshots (S1 and S2) .
Note: Multiple disk access resource may exist if the there are more than five snapshots.
7. A SAS URI is generated for the new and previous snapshots. 8. The changes between the previous snapshot (S1) and the new snapshot (S2) are
calculated and then downloaded to the Cohesity cluster. 9. The SAS URI of both the snapshots are revoked.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

10. The previous snapshot (S1) on Azure is deleted. The new snapshot (S2) is retained on Azure for the next incremental protection run.
Creating a Snapshot for Unmanaged Disks
1. A snapshot of an unmanaged disk is stored as a page blob. 2. The incremental changes between the previous and the current snapshot are
calculated and then downloaded to a Cohesity cluster. 3. The previous snapshot is then deleted.
Note: Only one outstanding snapshot (which reflects the latest complete snapshot) is always maintained and therefore to take an incremental backup, the current snapshot is compared with the previous outstanding snapshot and the incremental changes are only considered for backup. The older snapshots are deleted so that the system always maintains only one outstanding snapshot at any time.
Back Up Azure Cloud VMs Using Cloud Snapshot Management
Cohesity cluster uses Cloud Snapshot Management (CSM) APIs to backup the Azure VMs (Managed VMs) and AWS Cloud services to the same cloud. To enable this feature, you must select the Snapshot Manager as the job type while creating the Virtual Server Protection Group. When this Protection Group is executed, the VMs' snapshots are created on the same cloud service. The CSM snapshots are stored in the same Azure subscription, but can be used to recover to a different subscription.
Cloud Snapshot Management Process for Creating the Snapshot
For Azure Managed Disks: 1. Fetch the information about the VM using the GET API. This API takes subscriptionId, resourceGroupName, and vmName as an argument and returns the information about the VM (such as disks, network interfaces, and so on). 2. After the VM information is fetched, snapshots of the VM's disk is created on the same cloud service using the Snapshots API.
You can also recover these snapshots. For more information, see Recover VMs.
Considerations
l The backup of unmanaged VMs is not supported. l Incremental snapshot of managed disks is not supported

l App consistent backup is not supported. l Cloning is not supported. l File download is not supported.

The Cohesity cluster attempts to index all files and folders to a drive on both Windows and Linux systems. If the Cohesity cluster is unable to find mount point information about files or directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories in the lvol_N directory, where N is a unique number such as 1.
On Windows systems, if the Cohesity cluster finds the mount point information about files and directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories with a drive letter such as C:.
On Linux systems, how files and directories are indexed and displayed is dependent on the conditions specified in the following table.

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

Simple Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
UUID="ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc" /mnt ext4 auto 0
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point that was specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

LVM Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
/dev/mapper/VG1-root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
/dev/VG1/root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt. If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Linux Physical

LVM Volume

The Cohesity agent can only return mount data when the volume is mounted on the Linux physical Server. If the volume is mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the volume is not mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Character replacement explanation for : and \ in file and directory names in zip files
If the original file or directory name contains a `:' , it is replaced with `_COLON_' in the archive. Example:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l The original name is "a:b" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b" l The original name is "a:b:c" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b_
COLON_c"
If the original file or directory name contains a `\', it is replaced with '_BACK_ SLASH_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "x\y" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_y" l The original name is "x\y\z" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_
y_BACK_SLASH_z"

For NAS, an example path on an alternate location could be /tmp/recover. You can recover encrypted files/folders to their original location only.
Example for Windows alternate location:
l D:\cohesity_restore\1.txt
l D:\cohesity_restore\bar
User Account Requirements for VM Protection may need to be met to recover files to a Windows VM.
If recovering to a standalone Hyper-V host or cluster, you must add the guest VM to the reverse lookup zone in the DNS server to complete the recovery successfully.
9. Optional. Edit the default settings of the following Recovery options:
l Overwrite Existing File/Folder: By default, this option is enabled to overwrite the existing files and folders. Disable this option to create the files and folders in the specified location. Any duplicate files are skipped.
Example for a Windows alternate location with Overwrite Existing File/Folder enabled and the target already exists:
Files to be recovered: "C:\foo\1.txt", "C:\foo\test\1.txt", "C:\bar", "C:\foo\bar". Specified alternate location: "C:\restore". At the end of the copy, the target folder looks like this:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

l C:\restore\1.txt l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_0\1.txt l C:\restore\bar l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_1\bar If Overwrite Existing File/Folder is enabled, recovering a file to source when the file is in Fuse may cause the open file to be overwritten. Whether overwriting occurs depends on the application using the file. l Preserve File/Folder Attributes: By default, this option is enabled and the ACLs, permissions, and timestamps are preserved for all files and folders. If you disable this option, then ACLs and permissions are not preserved. If recovering both folders and files, then folders will receive the new timestamps, but files retain their original timestamps. If recovering only files, then files will receive the new timestamps. l Continue on Error: Enable this option if you want to continue the recovery even if one of the objects encounters an error.
