The Cohesity cluster attempts to index all files and folders to a drive on both Windows and Linux systems. If the Cohesity cluster is unable to find mount point information about files or directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories in the lvol_N directory, where N is a unique number such as 1.
On Windows systems, if the Cohesity cluster finds the mount point information about files and directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories with a drive letter such as C:.
On Linux systems, how files and directories are indexed and displayed is dependent on the conditions specified in the following table.

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

Simple Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
UUID="ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc" /mnt ext4 auto 0
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point that was specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

LVM Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
/dev/mapper/VG1-root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
/dev/VG1/root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt. If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Linux Physical

LVM Volume

The Cohesity agent can only return mount data when the volume is mounted on the Linux physical Server. If the volume is mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the volume is not mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

l Download Files: If you are recovering a single file, this option downloads the file to your browser's download folder. For all other selections, this creates a recovery task. When the task completes, from the Recoveries page, click the task name and then click Download Files to download the generated zip file.
Character replacement explanation for : and \ in file and directory names in zip files
If the original file or directory name contains a `:' , it is replaced with `_COLON_' in the archive. Example:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l The original name is "a:b" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b" l The original name is "a:b:c" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b_
COLON_c"
If the original file or directory name contains a `\', it is replaced with '_BACK_ SLASH_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "x\y" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_y" l The original name is "x\y\z" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_
y_BACK_SLASH_z"

7. Optional. Edit the default settings of the following Recovery options:
l Overwrite Existing File/Folder: By default, this option is enabled to overwrite the existing files and folders. Disable this option to create the files and folders in the specified location. Any duplicate files are skipped.
Example for a Windows alternate location with Overwrite Existing File/Folder enabled and the target already exists:
Files to be recovered: "C:\foo\1.txt", "C:\foo\test\1.txt", "C:\bar", "C:\foo\bar". Specified alternate location: "C:\restore". At the end of the copy, the target folder looks like this:
l C:\restore\1.txt
l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_0\1.txt
l C:\restore\bar
l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_1\bar
If Overwrite Existing File/Folder is enabled, recovering a file to source when the file is in Fuse may cause the open file to be overwritten. Whether overwriting occurs depends on the application using the file.
l Preserve File/Folder Attributes: By default, this option is enabled and the ACLs, permissions, and timestamps are preserved for all files and folders. If you disable this option, then ACLs and permissions are not preserved. If recovering both folders and files, then folders will receive the new timestamps, but files retain their original timestamps. If recovering only files, then files will receive the new timestamps.

Disaster Recovery of VMs Using Azure Cohesity Cloud Edition
To provide disaster recovery failover and failback, Cohesity supports the Cloud Migration of VMs between hypervisors servers (VMware vCenter), Azure Cloud Services, and Cohesity Cloud EditionCohesity clusters. For Hyper-V, Cohesity supports only failover to Azure.
Disaster recovery with Cohesity Cloud Edition consists of the following two use cases:
l Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to Azure Cloud
l Back Up Azure Cloud VMs, Replicate to On-Prem and Failback to Hypervisor Server
Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to Azure Cloud
To provide disaster recovery failover and failback, Cohesity supports the Cloud Migration of VMs between hypervisors servers (VMware vCenter), Azure Cloud Services and Cohesity Cloud EditionCohesity clusters. For Hyper-V, Cohesity supports only failover to Azure. Cohesity Cohesity Cloud Edition supports the replication of VMs captured on an on-premises Cohesity cluster to Cohesity Cloud Edition as shown by the example figure below. Back Up Azure Cloud VMs, Replicate to On-Prem and Failback to Hypervisor Server
To provide disaster recovery failover and failback, Cohesity supports the Cloud Migration of VMs between hypervisors servers (VMware vCenter), Azure Cloud Services and Cohesity Cloud EditionCohesity clusters.
Note: l For Hyper-V, Cohesity supports only failover to Azure. Failback is not supported.
l Failover of VMs that originated in Azure (Azure-native VMs) to an on-premises VMware vCenter is not supported. This topic describes the failback of VMs that were originally backed up from an on-premises VMware vCenter server and subsequently failed over to Azure using the process described in Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to Azure Cloud.
This topic describes the second use case of disaster recovery using Cloud Edition--how to backup cloud VMs to the Cloud Edition cluster, replicate to the on-premise cluster, and then failback to the Hypervisor server.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

For information on how the VMs are backed up in the Azure cloud service, see the first process of disaster recovery using Cloud Edition documented in Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to Azure Cloud.

As illustrated in the figure above, on the Cohesity Cloud Edition running in the Cloud Service, a Protection Group using native snapshots or Cohesity Protection Service backs up the cloud VMs (as indicated by the backup arrow in the figure). The policy associated with the Protection Group specifies that these Snapshots are replicated to the on-premises Cohesity cluster (as indicated by the Replicate arrow). From those Snapshots stored on the on-premises Cohesity cluster, you can failback (recover) the VMs to their original onpremises VMware vCenter server or an alternate VMware vCenter server (as indicated by the Failback (Recover) arrow in the figure). This restores the VMs to the on-premises hypervisor environment from which they originally failed over to the Azure Cloud Service.
To back Up Cloud VMs to Cohesity Cloud Edition, replicate to a on-premises Cohesity cluster and failback to a hypervisor server:
Verify the following requirements prior to failback:
l The VMs that are backed up to the Cloud Service must have VMware Tools and Remote Desktop installed before the original Protection Group captures the Snapshots from the VMware vCenter Server as described in the Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to Azure Cloud.
l If you are backing up the Cloud VMs to the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster using the Cohesity Protection Service Protection Group type, then the VMs that are backed up to the Cloud Service must also have Cohesity agent installed.
Steps:
1. If not already configured, set up replication between the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster and the on-premises Cohesity cluster. For instructions, see Replication and Remote Access Setup.
2. On the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster, create a Policy that replicates from the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster to the on-premises Cohesity cluster as shown in the figure. For instructions, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.
3. On the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster, refresh the Object hierarchy for the Source of the VMs that will be backed up:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

a. Select Data Protection > Sources.
b. Click the action icon ( ) next to the Source and select Refresh.
4. On the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster, create a Virtual Server Protection Group (such as BackToPrem) with Protection Group Type option as Native Snapshots or Cohesity Protection Service. Associate the Policy created in the previous step with this Protection Group. For detailed instructions, see Add or Edit a Protection Group for Virtual Servers. If Cohesity Protection Service is selected as the Protection Group type, then the VMs that are backed up to the Cloud Service (VMs that failed over to the cloud) must have Cohesity agent installed.
When selecting Windows VMs to failback (recover), you can only select Snapshots of VMs that had the Cohesity agent installed when they were created with the Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to Azure Cloud process. The VM should be powered on when the Protection Group is running.
When you create a Protection Group on the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster that replicates to an on-premises Cohesity cluster, after the first Snapshot is replicated to the on-premises Cluster, an Inactive copy of the Job is created on the on-premises Cluster that received the Snapshot. The new Inactive Job on the on-premises Cohesity cluster has the same name as the Protection Group on the Cohesity Cloud Edition Cluster, for example: BackToPrem.
5. You can failback (recover) the VMs to the original Hypervisor server or an alternate Hypervisor server:
a. On the on-premises Cohesity cluster that contains the replicated Snapshots, select Data Protection > Protection and browse for the Inactive Job that was automatically created.

b. Click on the inactive Job name. c. Browse for protection run that captured a Snapshot that you want to recover.
d. Click the action icon ( ) next to the Job and select Recover VM. e. Follow the instructions provided in Recover VMs. The VM is created in the Hypervisor server and is powered up if that option was selected. As part of the convert and clone process, the VMware Tools will be uninstalled. You must reinstall the VMware Tools.
Important: Do not change the size of the partition or the disk of the recovered VM.

Disaster Recovery of Views in Azure Cohesity Cloud Edition
Cohesity Cohesity Cloud Edition supports the disaster recovery of Views as shown by the following example figures.
Views can be used to store data such as files and directories. For example, other backup products can store data on a view that is hosted on the Cohesity cluster. To access a view from your system, you must mount the view.
On the left of the first figure, shows systems accessing a View hosted on an on-premises Cohesity cluster using the NFS or SMB protocols. A Protection Group running on the onpremises Cohesity cluster captures Snapshots of the View and stores these Snapshots on the Cluster. The Protection Policy associated with this Job, is configured to replicate (or copy) Snapshots from the on-premises Cohesity cluster to the Cohesity cluster Cohesity Cloud Edition. From these Snapshots stored in the Cohesity Cloud Edition, you can clone a new View that can be accessed by systems using the NFS or SMB protocols as shown on the right of the first figure.

You can backup Views hosted on the Cohesity Cloud Edition as shown on the right of the following figure. A Protection Group captures a Snapshot of a View and stores the Snapshot on the Cohesity cluster Cohesity Cloud Edition. The Protection Policy associated with this Job, is configured to replicate (or copy) Snapshots from the Cohesity cluster Cohesity Cloud Edition to the on-premises Cohesity cluster. From these View Snapshots stored in the onpremises Cohesity cluster, you clone a View and make it available for mounting as shown on the left of the following figure.

Clone VMs to Azure Cloud Using CloudSpin

On a Cohesity cluster with a Protection Group that captures Snapshots of VMs with a CloudSpin schedule, the cluster clones VMs to Azure cloud service. You can then launch the VMs to a running state.
What happens during the CloudSpin process is dependent on the cloud service type:

l Cohesity supports CloudSpin of Hyper-V to Azure.
l Cohesity supports CloudSpin of VMware to Azure.
l During cloning to an Azure Cloud using Cloudspin, the Cohesity cluster converts the snapshot to VHD format and then copies the VHD image to a storage container in the Azure Cloud. Managed disks, including SSD and HDD, are also supported.
l For policy-based CloudSpin to Azure, the Storage Account must support page blobs.

For the list of VMs that supports CloudSpin to Azure, see Supported Software.

l Azure does not support booting UEFI VMs with unmanaged disks.
l The maximum data disk size supported for an Azure VM for CloudSpin is 8191 GiB.
l Cohesity does not support CloudSpin of VMware VMs from VMware Cloud (VMC) to Azure.
l Cohesity supports both on-demand and policy-based CloudSpin for snapshots stored on the Cohesity cluster (primary copy).
l Cohesity does not support on-demand and policy-based CloudSpin for archived or CloudRetrieved snapshots.
l Cohesity supports on-demand CloudSpin for snapshots that are replicated to another Cohesity cluster.

Edit /etc/fstab to use UUID

You must edit the /etc/fstab file and change the (non-LVM) entries to use UUIDs to identify the disk partitions. These changes must be made to the /etc/fstab file before the Protection Group (which captures the Snapshots to be cloned) is run.
For example, the following entry in the /etc/fstab table must be changed to use the UUID to identify the partition instead of the device file name of /dev/sbd1.

/dev/sdb1 /mnt/disk1 ext4 defaults

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

Note: l Use labels or UUIDs instead of device names, as device names may change when other disks are added or removed.
l Kernel name descriptors must not be used in configuration files as they are not persistent and may change during each boot. UUIDs or PARTUUIDs are preferred over labels.
l Using only the device name in the absence of UUID or label might cause issues as these names are not unique. This can cause overwrites and eventual loss of an entire volume indexing itself.
l Each volume must be uniquely identified by an identifier like UUID or label. A missing unique identifier (UUID/label) can result in dummy volume names being used instead of actual volumes.

You can determine the UUID by running the blkid command, for example:

# blkid /dev/sdb1 /dev/sdb1 UUID="12345cac-77bc-46b1-9f79-cb180e438c12" TYPE="ext4"

Edit the /etc/fstab as root and for this entry replace the device file name with the returned UUID, for example:

12345cac-77bc-46b1-9f79-cb180e438c12 /mnt/disk1 ext4 defaults

Note: LVM volume entries should not be updated. LVM volumes start with the /dev/mapper prefix, for example: /dev/mapper/centos-root and /dev/mapper/centos-swap.
Repeat these steps for all entries in the /etc/fstab that are not LVM volume entries. Replicate Azure Virtual Machines This chapter includes the following topics:

Migrate Cloud Edition Azure Nodes to Managed Disks
The nodes (VMs) in a Cohesity Cloud Edition Azure cluster can use Azure-managed disks or unmanaged disks. Managed disks are described in Introduction to Azure Managed Disks. Cohesity recommends that all nodes in a cluster use the same type of disk. You can migrate nodes from unmanaged disks to managed disks as described below.
Before Migrating the Nodes
Do the following before you migrate the nodes to use managed disks. 1. Take a snapshot of every node (VM) in the cluster as a backup precaution. 2. SSH into any node in the cluster. ssh cohesity@<ip_address>
3. Run the following commands and record the command output to verify disk utilization after the migration. df -h
lsblk
Migrate the Nodes
To migrate the nodes to use managed disks, repeat the following steps for each node in the cluster.
1. Make sure there are no outstanding replication, archival or CloudSpin tasks active for the cluster.
2. In the Azure portal, click the Cloud Shell button shown below and activate the PowerShell environment.

For more information, see Quickstart for PowerShell in Azure Cloud Shell. 3. In the PowerShell window, run the following commands to deallocate the node (VM).
Replace myResourceGroup and myVM with the names of the resource group and VM instance name you want to deallocate. $rgName = "myResourceGroup"
$vmName = "myVM"
Stop-AzVM -ResourceGroupName $rgName -Name $vmName -Force
4. After the above commands run successfully, run the following command to initiate the migration.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

ConvertTo-AzVMManagedDisk -ResourceGroupName $rgName -VMName $vmName 5. Repeat the previous steps for each node in the cluster.
Verify the Migration
1. SSH to any node in the cluster. 2. Run the following Cohesity CLI command to verify that all services are up and
running. iris_cli cluster status 3. Run the following commands and compare the results to the same command output that you recorded previously. The disk utilization should be the same as it was before the migration. df -h lsblk
Azure MySQL
Cohesity DataProtect provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective backup, recovery, and data management solution for Microsoft Azure MySQL databases. Azure Database for MySQL is a fully managed relational database service offered by Microsoft Azure. It allows users to deploy, manage, and scale MySQL databases in the cloud without the need to manage the underlying infrastructure.
Important: The backup and recovery of Azure MySQL is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure (formerly known as Azure NGCE cluster).
Plan and Prepare for Azure MySQL Protection Before protecting Azure MySQL with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Azure MySQL with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your Azure as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For more information, see Register an Azure Source at Tenant Level.
Authentication for Azure MySQL Protection
You must authenticate the Cohesity cluster to discover the Azure MySQL databases using one of the following methods:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Username and password of the Azure MySQL instance. l User Managed Identity.
Configure Database User Associated with User Managed Identity
To configure a database user associated with User Managed Identity:
1. Get the client ID for managed identity using the following commands in Azure CLI: # az ad sp list --display-name <managed_identity_name> --query [*].appId --out tsv
2. Login to the MySQL server and create a user using the following commands: # SET aad_auth_validate_oids_in_tenant = OFF; # CREATE AADUSER '<db_user>' IDENTIFIED BY '<Generated_client_id>'; # GRANT <Permissions> ON *.* TO '<db_user>'@'%'
3. Create a normal database user or one associated with the relevant User Managed Identity and grant the required permissions to that user using the following command: GRANT SELECT , INSERT , UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, DROP , RELOAD, PROCESS, REFERENCES, INDEX, ALTER, SHOW DATABASES, LOCK TABLES, CREATE VIEW, SHOW VIEW, CREATE ROUTINE, ALTER ROUTINE, SHOW_ROUTINE, EVENT , TRIGGER, SET_USER_ID ON *.* TO `<dbuser>`@'%' WITH GRANT OPTION;
Note: Replace <dbuser> in the above command with the actual name of the database user.
Firewall Ports for Azure MySQL Protection
l Ensure connectivity from Cohesity DataProtect to the Azure MySQL server on port 3306.
Considerations for Azure MySQL Protection
l Full backup support - Only full backup is supported; incremental backup is not available for Azure MySQL.
l Azure MySQL database size display - The size of the database under Azure MySQL server will only be populated once the credentials are specified for the server entity. Otherwise, it will be reported as 0.
l Attach metadata and credentials - A database instance moved to a different resource group is considered a new entity. Hence, ensure that you attach the new metadata and credentials.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Azure MySQL version compatibility - You can recover an Azure MySQL database to an alternate instance with an Azure MySQL version different than the backup instance, depending on the Azure MySQL version compatibility.
l Database naming convention -Backup and recovery of databases with names containing the characters # and / are not supported. Ensure the database names adhere to the naming conventions suggested by the cloud service.
l Special character in password - Server or database passwords do not support ; (semicolon).
l Database Level Protection - Protection occurs at the database level and not server level; backup and recovery are performed for the databases on the server. Cohesity does not change or create an Azure MySQL server in the workflows. Hence, the properties of the server like tags are not recovered.
Backup Azure MySQL Database
After registering your Azure MySQL source in Cohesity DataProtect, Cohesity uses the cloud credentials provided to authenticate with Azure.
Once authenticated, Cohesity automatically discovers all the subscriptions that the service account can access, as well as all supported workloads such as Azure MySQL databases within those subscriptions. The discovered workloads appear under Data Protection > Sources. You can select the MySQL tab to view all the databases discovered.

Backup Scope by Azure MySQL Hierarchy
Cohesity cluster allows you to backup Azure MySQL databases at different levels of the hierarchy. You can choose to back up:
l Subscription - Protect all Azure MySQL databases within the subscription. l Resource Group - Protect all Azure MySQL databases within the resource group. l Database Server - Protect all Azure MySQL databases within the database server. l Database - Protect individual Azure MySQL database.
Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports only full backups for Azure MySQL. Incremental backups are not supported.
Protect Azure MySQL
Azure MySQL databases are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group enables you to select and group the objects that you want to backup. It uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured and replicated. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy.
Prerequisites to Protect Azure MySQL
Set Azure MySQL Server Credentials
For Backup, the database credentials are used to authenticate and connect to the MySQL server. Once the connection is established, the relevant database can be dumped and protected. For Azure MySQL, you can set credentials at the Azure MySQL Server level. This information is used to connect to the database during backup and recovery. You can also add credentials at any higher level in the hierarchy, such as the subscription. Credentials added at a higher level automatically apply to all objects beneath it. The Cohesity cluster searches for credentials in a bottom-up manner, starting from the specific entity (for example, a server) and moving up the hierarchy until valid credentials are found. When multiple credentials exist, the credentials closest to the MySQL server take precedence. For example:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l If region-1 has a set of credentials and server-1 under that region has its own, the Cohesity cluster uses the credentials on server-1 to authenticate to server-1.
l Another server, server-2, under the same region, the Cohesity cluster uses the region-level credentials for authentication because that is the closest level where credentials are specified.
To set the database credentials:
1. In DataProtect, navigate to Data Protection > Sources, find the registered Azure source, and click on it.
2. Click on the MySQL tab. 3. Select the checkbox next to the required Azure MySQL Server. 4. Click the Database Credentials button. 5. You can select one of the following options:
1. Username and Password - Provide the database admin username and password. These credentials are required for leaf-level databases. The account must have access to all databases within the MySQL server.
2. User Managed Identity (UMI) - Uses authentication automatically managed by Azure. For more information, see Configure Database User Associated with User Managed Identity.
Note: - User Managed Identity must be attached to the Azure VM on which Cohesity DataProtect is deployed. - UMI authentication method does not work across tenants. - Authentication fails if the database credentials provided are incorrect. Ensure that the username/password/UMI ClientID is correct, and/or the UMI associated database user is properly configured.
6. Click Save.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.
l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Object.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Object. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Objects.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve a similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the current running task.

Alerts

Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when an Object completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Object fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the takes longer than the time specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.

Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra
Cohesity provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective backup, recovery, and data management solution for Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra keyspaces. Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra is a fully managed NoSQL database service that enables you to run Cassandra workloads in the cloud with minimal changes to your application code.
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Plan and Prepare for Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra Protection Before protecting Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

Before You Begin
To protect Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your Azure as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For more information, see Register an Azure Source at Tenant Level.
Authentication for Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra Keyspace Protection
You must authenticate to Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra keyspace from Cohesity DataProtect using one of the following methods:
l Username and Password l User Managed Identity (UMI) l System Managed Identity (SMI)
Username and Password
This method uses the credentials of the admin user for the Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra keyspace. This is the user account configured during server creation. For backup, you can create a custom user. In the CLI and run the following commands:
1. To create login user on the server: #CREATE LOGIN [newlogin] WITH PASSWORD = 'somepassword;
2. To create same user under database which should be backed up by user newlogin: User <database>; #CREATE USER [newlogin] FOR LOGIN [newlogin]; ALTER ROLE db_owner ADD MEMBER [newlogin];
3. Run the following command on the master system database: CREATE USER [newlogin] FOR LOGIN [newlogin];
For recovery, the default admin credentials created during server creation are required if the custom user credentials were set for authentication before backup. During recovery, you must change the credentials back to the default admin credentials.
User Managed Identity (UMI)
This method uses a user-assigned managed identity to authenticate to the Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra keyspace. Perform the following to use the UMI authentication:
1. Create a user-assigned managed identity. For more information, see Manage userassigned managed identities using the Azure portal.
2. Assign the Managed Identity Operator role to the UMI identity. For more information, see User-assigned managed identity.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

3. Set the UMI as the identity for all the cluster nodes. Ensure that the UMI is from the same subscription as the one in which the keyspace exists. For more information, see Assign a user-assigned managed identity to an existing VM.
4. Assign this User Managed Identity as Entra ID Admin on the server. For more information, see Set Microsoft Entra admin.
5. Assign the required user managed identity to Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra keyspace under the Identity section - User assigned managed identity on the Azure Portal.
System Managed Identity (SMI)
This method uses a unique identity that is automatically created by Azure when you enable SMI on the node. This identity belongs only to the specific node and is deleted if the node is deleted. Each node in the cluster includes its own SMI (multiple distinct identities). Since the Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra keyspace allows only one Microsoft Entra admin per node, having multiple nodes, each with a different SMI may cause issues. To mitigate this issue, you can perform the following:
1. Create a Microsoft Entra group. 2. Add SMI identities as group members. 3. Assign this group as Microsoft Entra Admin.
This ensures that all the nodes can be authenticated using their respective SMIs through the group.
Note: SMIs are not created separately as a resource. You must enable it on the cluster nodes from the Azure portal.
Perform the following to use the SMI authentication:
1. Enable system-assigned managed identity on all the nodes of the cluster. For more information, see Enable system-assigned managed identity on an existing VM.
2. Create a Microsoft Entra basic group and add SMI's of all the nodes created in previous step as members. The SMI name is the same as the VM (node) name, which can be easily searched for while finding members to include in the group. For more information, see Create a basic group and add members.
3. Assign this Microsoft Entra basic group as Entra ID Admin on the server. For more information, see Set Microsoft Entra admin.
Considerations for Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra Keyspace Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and considerations before you protect Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra Keyspace:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Full back up support - Only full backup is supported; incremental backup is not available for Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra protection.
l Attach metadata and credentials - When you recover a keyspace to a different account, ensure that you attach the metadata and credentials to the destination account.
l Rename keyspace during recovery - Keyspace names can have up to 48 alphanumeric characters and can contain underscores; only letters and numbers are supported as the first character.
l Keyspace-Level Protection - Protection occurs at the keyspace level and not account level; backup and recovery are performed for the keyspaces on the account. Cohesity does not change or create an Azure Cosmos DB-Cassandra account in the workflows. Hence, the properties of the account like tags are not recovered.
l Ingest rate during recovery - Ingest rate during recovery can be changed to a value between 0.1 and 1.0. The default value is 0.4, which is 40% of the maximum theoretical ingest rate capacity. This helps in resolving rate limit errors during recovery.
l Serverless vs provisioned throughput - Keyspace belonging to an account with Serverless mode cannot be recovered to the one with provisioned throughput capacity mode and vice versa.
l SSR (Server Side Retry) - During backup and recovery, SSR must be enabled on the source and destination Cassandra account. This is mandatory for the backup and recovery to be successful.
l TTL (Time-to-live) on recovered tables - When recovering Azure Cosmos DBCassandra tables, the default_time_to_live (TTL) setting is preserved from the source table and applied to the recovered table. As a result, any newly inserted rows in the recovered table will automatically expire after a duration of Row creation time + default_time_to_live (in seconds).
This ensures consistency with the TTL-based data expiration behavior of the original table.
Note: Row-level TTL settings are not retained during backup. When data is recovered, the TTL for those rows is set to the table's default_time_to_live value.
l Index Name on Recovery - Index names are not retained during the backup and recovery of Azure Cosmos DB-Cassandra tables. While index names are accepted syntactically by the service, they are not functionally relevant in Azure Cosmos DBCassandra. To ensure consistency and compatibility, index names are regenerated during the recovery process.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Materialized views support - If the source table includes materialized views, during recovery the destination account must have Materialized Views settings enabled. This is mandatory for successful recovery of materialized views. As per Azure, materialized views are not recommended for production workloads. For more information, see Materialized Views in Azure Cosmos DB for Apache Cassandra.
l Replication regions - To get optimum performance during recovery, it is recommended to disable multi-region replication. After recovery, you can re-enable multi-region replication.
l Version Downgrade not supported: Recovering a backup taken from a higher database version to a lower version is not supported.

Backup Scope by Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra Hierarchy

Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports full backups for Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra. Incremental backups are not supported.
Protect Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra Keyspaces
Azure Cosmos DB - Cassandra keyspaces are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group enables you to select and group the objects that you want to backup. It uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured and replicated. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy.

l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Object.

This policy tries to achieve a similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the current running task.

Azure Cosmos DB - MongoDB
Cohesity provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective backup, recovery, and data management solution for Azure Cosmos DB - MongoDB databases. Azure Cosmos DB offers an API for MongoDB, which allows you to use Azure Cosmos DB like a native MongoDB database. This compatibility allows the use of existing MongoDB applications, tooling, drivers, and SDKs.
Important: The backup and recovery of Azure PostgreSQL is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure (formerly known as Azure NGCE cluster).

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.
l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Object.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Object. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Objects.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve a similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the current running task.

l Success: Creates an informational alert when an Object completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Object fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the takes longer than the time specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.

Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL
Cohesity provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective backup, recovery, and data management solution for Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL databases. Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL is a fully managed, serverless, and globally distributed NoSQL database service offered by Microsoft Azure. It is designed for modern application development, including AI applications and agents, providing high performance, availability, and scalability for handling massive volumes of NoSQL and vector data.
Important: The backup and recovery of Azure PostgreSQL is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure (formerly known as Azure NGCE cluster).
Plan and Prepare for Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL Protection Before protecting Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your Azure as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For more information, see Register an Azure Source at Tenant Level.
Authentication for Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL Database Protection
You must authenticate to Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL database from Cohesity DataProtect using one of the following methods:
l Username and Password l User Managed Identity (UMI) l System Managed Identity (SMI)
Username and Password
This method uses the credentials of the admin user for the Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL database. This is the user account configured during server creation. For backup, you can create a custom user. In the CLI and run the following commands:
1. To create login user on the server: #CREATE LOGIN [newlogin] WITH PASSWORD = 'somepassword;
2. To create same user under database which should be backed up by user newlogin:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

User <database>; #CREATE USER [newlogin] FOR LOGIN [newlogin]; ALTER ROLE db_owner ADD MEMBER [newlogin];
3. Run the following command on the master system database:
CREATE USER [newlogin] FOR LOGIN [newlogin];
For recovery, the default admin credentials created during server creation are required if the custom user credentials were set for authentication before backup. During recovery, you must change the credentials back to the default admin credentials.
User Managed Identity (UMI)
This method uses a user-assigned managed identity to authenticate to the Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL database. Perform the following to use the UMI authentication:
1. Create a user-assigned managed identity. For more information, see Manage userassigned managed identities using the Azure portal.
2. Assign the Managed Identity Operator role to the UMI identity. For more information, see User-assigned managed identity.
3. Set the UMI as the identity for all the cluster nodes. Ensure that the UMI is from the same subscription as the one in which the database exists. For more information, see Assign a user-assigned managed identity to an existing VM.
4. Assign this User Managed Identity as Entra ID Admin on the server. For more information, see Set Microsoft Entra admin.
5. Assign the required user managed identity to Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL database under the Identity section - User assigned managed identity on the Azure Portal.
System Managed Identity (SMI)
This method uses a unique identity that is automatically created by Azure when you enable SMI on the node. This identity belongs only to the specific node and is deleted if the node is deleted. Each node in the cluster includes its own SMI (multiple distinct identities). Since the Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL database allows only one Microsoft Entra admin per node, having multiple nodes, each with a different SMI may cause issues. To mitigate this issue, you can perform the following:
1. Create a Microsoft Entra group. 2. Add SMI identities as group members. 3. Assign this group as Microsoft Entra Admin.
This ensures that all the nodes can be authenticated using their respective SMIs through the group.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

Note: SMIs are not created separately as a resource. You must enable it on the cluster nodes from the Azure portal.
Perform the following to use the SMI authentication:
1. Enable system-assigned managed identity on all the nodes of the cluster. For more information, see Enable system-assigned managed identity on an existing VM.
2. Create a Microsoft Entra basic group and add SMI's of all the nodes created in previous step as members. The SMI name is the same as the VM (node) name, which can be easily searched for while finding members to include in the group. For more information, see Create a basic group and add members.
3. Assign this Microsoft Entra basic group as Entra ID Admin on the server. For more information, see Set Microsoft Entra admin.
Considerations
Review and understand the following limitations and considerations before you protect Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL Database:
l Full backup support - Only full backup is supported; incremental backup is not available for Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL protection.
l Attach metadata and credentials - When you recover a database to a different account, ensure that you attach the metadata and credentials to the destination account.
l Rename database during recovery - Database names can have up to 48 alphanumeric characters and can contain underscores; only letters and numbers are supported as the first character.
l Database-Level Protection - Protection occurs at the database level and not account level; backup and recovery are performed for the databases on the account. Cohesity does not change or create an Azure Cosmos DB-NoSQL account in the workflows. Hence, the properties of the account like tags are not recovered.
l Serverless vs provisioned throughput - Database belonging to an account with Serverless mode cannot be recovered to the one with provisioned throughput capacity mode and vice versa.
l Partition key configuration - During recovery, the partition key configuration of the source container must match the destination. The partition key cannot be changed during recovery operations.
l Indexing policy preservation - The indexing policy from the source container is preserved and applied to the recovered container. Custom indexing policies are maintained during recovery.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Unique key constraints - Unique key constraints defined on the source container are preserved during recovery. Ensure the destination account supports the same unique key configurations.
l TTL (Time-to-live) on recovered containers - When recovering Azure Cosmos DB-NoSQL containers, the default TTL setting is preserved from the source container and applied to the recovered container. As a result, any newly inserted items in the recovered container will automatically expire after a duration of Item creation time + default TTL (in seconds).
This ensures consistency with the TTL-based data expiration behavior of the original container.
Note: Item-level TTL settings are not retained during backup. When data is recovered, the TTL for those items is set to the container's default TTL value.
l Stored procedures, triggers, and UDFs - Stored procedures, triggers, and userdefined functions (UDFs) defined on the source container are backed up and recovered to the destination container. Ensure the destination account has the necessary permissions to execute these server-side logic components.
l Change feed configuration - Change feed settings are not preserved during recovery. After recovery, you may need to reconfigure the change feed processors and their lease containers.
l Analytical store - If the source container has an analytical store enabled, the destination container must also support analytical store. This feature must be enabled at the account level before recovery.
l Replication regions - To get optimum performance during recovery, it is recommended to disable multi-region replication. After recovery, you can re-enable multi-region replication.
l Custom role permissions - For backup and recovery using custom roles, ensure the service principal has the following minimum data plane permissions:
l Backup: readMetadata, sqlDatabases/read, containers/read, items/read, executeQuery, readChangeFeed.
l Recovery: readMetadata, sqlDatabases/read, sqlDatabases/write, containers/read, containers/write, items/create, items/upsert.
l Rate limiting and throttling - During backup and recovery, monitor the HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) responses. Adjust the ingest rate or increase provisioned throughput temporarily to avoid throttling.
l Container throughput - Ensure the destination container has sufficient provisioned throughput (RU/s) to handle recovery. Insufficient throughput will result in throttling and extended recovery times.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Hierarchical partition keys - If the source container uses hierarchical partition keys (multi-level partitioning), the destination account must support this feature. Hierarchical partition keys are preserved during recovery.
l Version Downgrade not supported: Recovering a backup taken from a higher database version to a lower version is not supported.

Supported Backup Types

Protect Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL Databases
Azure Cosmos DB - NoSQL databases are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group enables you to select and group the objects that you want to backup. It uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured and replicated. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy.

Azure Cosmos DB - Table
Cohesity provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective backup, recovery, and data management solution for Azure Cosmos DB - Table. Azure Cosmos DB -Table is a fully managed NoSQL database service that provides a highly scalable and globally distributed store for key-value and tabular data, using the familiar Azure Table storage APIs. It is ideal for applications that require fast, high-performance storage for structured, non-relational data, like device registries, user profiles, or configuration data.
Important: The backup and recovery of Azure PostgreSQL is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure (formerly known as Azure NGCE cluster).
Plan and Prepare for Azure Cosmos DB - Table Protection
Before protecting Azure Cosmos DB - Table with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Azure Cosmos DB - Table with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your Azure as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For more information, see Register an Azure Source at Tenant Level.
Considerations for Azure Cosmos DB - Table Protection
l Recovery Failure from Replicated Cluster - Recovery from a replicated cluster of Azure Cosmos DB-Table may fail with the following error: "kStale: File previously opened with higher session ID: <xxx_yyy>".
l Recovery Validation UI Warning - During recovery validation, the following warning may be displayed in the UI: "Metadata view RecordIO client not available". This warning does not impact the actual recovery process.
l Version Downgrade not supported: Recovering a backup taken from a higher database version to a lower version is not supported.

Azure

Azure SQL Database
Cohesity provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective backup, recovery, and data management solution for Azure SQL databases. Azure SQL database is a fully managed, intelligent, relational database-as-a-service (DBaaS) offered by Microsoft Azure. It provides a cloud-based SQL Server database engine, optimized for modern cloud applications and websites.
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Plan and Prepare for Azure SQL Protection Before protecting Azure SQL databases with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Azure SQL databases with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your Azure as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For more information, see Register an Azure Source at Tenant Level.
Authentication for Azure SQL Database Protection
You must authenticate to Azure SQL database from the Cohesity cluster using one of the following methods:
l Username and Password l User Managed Identity (UMI) l System Managed Identity (SMI)
Username and Password
This method uses the credentials of the admin user for the SQL server. This is the user account configured during server creation. For backup, you can create a custom user. Connect to the SQL server using SQL management studio or SQLCMD and run the following commands:
1. To create login user on the server: #CREATE LOGIN [newlogin] WITH PASSWORD = 'somepassword;
2. To create same user under database which should be backed up by user newlogin: User <database>; #CREATE USER [newlogin] FOR LOGIN [newlogin]; ALTER ROLE db_owner ADD MEMBER [newlogin];

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

3. Run the following command on the master system database:
CREATE USER [newlogin] FOR LOGIN [newlogin];
For recovery, the default admin credentials created during server creation are required if the custom user credentials were set for authentication before backup. During recovery, you must change the credentials back to the default admin credentials.
User Managed Identity (UMI)
This method uses a user-assigned managed identity to authenticate to the Azure SQL database. Perform the following to use the UMI authentication:
1. Create a user-assigned managed identity. For more information, see Manage userassigned managed identities using the Azure portal.
2. Assign the Managed Identity Operator role to the UMI identity. For more information, see User-assigned managed identity.
3. Set the UMI as the identity for all the cluster nodes. Ensure that the UMI is from the same subscription as the one in which the SQL database exists. For more information, see Assign a user-assigned managed identity to an existing VM.
4. Assign this User Managed Identity as Entra ID Admin on the server. For more information, see Set Microsoft Entra admin.
5. Assign the required user managed identity to Azure SQL instance/server under the Identity section - User assigned managed identity on the Azure Portal.
System Managed Identity (SMI)
This method uses a unique identity that is automatically created by Azure when you enable SMI on the node. This identity belongs only to the specific node and is deleted if the node is deleted. Each node in the cluster includes its own SMI (multiple distinct identities). Since the Azure SQL database allows only one Microsoft Entra admin per node, having multiple nodes, each with a different SMI may cause issues. To mitigate this issue, you can perform the following:
1. Create a Microsoft Entra group. 2. Add all the nodes' SMI identities as group members. 3. Assign this group as Microsoft Entra Admin.
This ensures that all the nodes can be authenticated using their respective SMIs through the group.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

Note: SMIs are not created separately as a resource. You must enable it on the cluster nodes from the Azure portal.
Perform the following to use the SMI authentication:
1. Enable system-assigned managed identity on all the nodes of the cluster. For more information, see Enable system-assigned managed identity on an existing VM.
2. Create a Microsoft Entra basic group and add SMI's of all the nodes created in previous step as members. The SMI name is the same as the VM (node) name, which can be easily searched for while finding members to include in the group. For more information, see Create a basic group and add members.
3. Assign this Microsoft Entra basic group as Entra ID Admin on the server. For more information, see Set Microsoft Entra admin.
Considerations for Azure SQL Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and considerations before you protect Azure SQL database:
l Database-level configurations - Configuring credentials at database level is not supported.
l Column-level encryption - Database protection does not support column-level encryption.
l Database Tables - Backup and recovery of the following tables in the databases are not supported: l GRAPH_TABLE, l TEMPORAL_TABLE, l LEDGER_TABLE, l MEMORY_OPTIMIZED_TABLE
l Backup failure with invalid object name error: Subsequent full/incremental backups of an Azure SQL Server backup may fail with the following error: "Invalid object name 'cdc.<schema_name>_<table_name>_CT'" This issue occurs while executing the backup query script with a transfer object in the query (to transfer table from one schema to another). This may cause a mismatch between the user tables and their associated CDC tables. The mismatch typically arises after the schema changes or when database objects are moved between schemas after CDC is enabled. Workaround: Perform the following:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

1. Disable CDC on the database before running the backup. 2. Login to the SQL database using the following command:
sqlcmd -S hostname -U user -d database_name
3. Run the following command on the SQL database:
# EXEC sys.sp_cdc_disable_db
4. Perform a full backup. The CDC will be automatically enabled during the next backup.
l Incremental backup fall back to full backup: Incremental backups fall back to full backup in the following cases: l Schema changes are detected during backup. l The state file from an earlier backup is not available. l CDC is enabled/disabled on the database/tables. l Previous full backup does not exist.
l Insufficient tempDB storage - If a backup fails due to insufficient tempDB storage on the SQL server, perform the following: 1. Login to the Azure portal. 2. Navigate to Protection Group > Additional Setting > CDC processing location > SQLDB server or Client. 3. Select the Client-Side processing for CDC processing.
l VNet settings for Azure SQL - An Azure VM used as a DataProtect node must be present in the same VNet as that of the Azure-managed instance. Alternatively, if the DataProtect node and SQL-managed instance are in different VNet, then both the VNets must peer to access the database instance.
l Backup failure due to Readlock - Backup fails when Readlock is placed on the database or resource group.
l For Azure databases, if a backup is generated by the native backup database workflow, using TDE enabled by Customer-managed Keys or TDE disabled, these types of tables are supported.
l Database diagrams - Database diagrams are not recovered. l Mandatory client certificate - Backup and recovery are not supported for the
databases that mandatorily require client certificates for connection to DataProtect. l Default ports - Only default ports are supported. l Database names with special characters - Backup and recovery of databases
with names containing the characters '#' and '/' are not supported. Also, the database name should adhere to the naming conventions suggested by the cloud vendors.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Passwords with special characters - Semicolon (;) is not supported in server or database passwords.
l Subscriptions of different tenants - Azure Managed Identity is not supported across subscriptions of different tenants.
l Version Downgrade not supported: Recovering a backup taken from a higher database version to a lower version is not supported.
l Duplicate Records: Recovered database may contain duplicate records if the source database does not include primary or foreign keys."
l Incremental Backup Failure: Incremental backup for Azure SQL database fails when the tempdb storage is exhausted due to a large number of CDC transactions on the database. To avoid this, use the batch count to limit the number of transactions being processed at a time.
l CDC Job Cleanup: Full backups can fail during CDC processing if CDC jobs are not cleaned at the SQL database level. This issue occurs when a database is deleted and then recreated with the same name. Workaround: You can manually perform the cleanup and disable CDC on database before backup. For more details, see Cleanup job.
Note: The CDC cleanup job removes all data from the change tracking tables based on the configured retention period.
l CDC Performance: For optimal CDC performance, ensure the following: l Do not use DDL triggers that block schema changes, like CREATE/DROP TABLE, CREATE/DROP FUNCTION. l Ensure that the SQL Server Agent service is running. l Use an account with db_owner or sysadmin privileges for CDC setup. l To avoid capture_instance conflicts, check if the table is already CDC-enabled.
l Database Tables: If the databases contain any of the following types of tables, the backup fails due to CDC limitations: l Graph tables l Temporal tables l Ledger tables (updatable ledger) l Memory optimized table (business critical tier only) l These types of tables are supported for Azure SQL databases, if the backup

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

uses the native backup database workflow, using TDE enabled by CustomerManaged Keys or TDE disabled.
l SqlPackage Utility: Consider the following for the SqlPackage utility:
l SqlPackage may fail to export the following SQL Server objects: Logins, Jobs (SQL Agent Jobs), Linked Servers, Server-level permissions, Server roles, Credentials, Database Mail configuration, Replication settings, SSIS packages, Service Broker objects, CLR assemblies, Data in FILESTREAM/FILETABLE, Encrypted objects (if keys/certs are not exported), Cross-database dependencies, extended stored procedures, and some system objects.
l SqlPackage primarily exports database-level objects and data, but not serverlevel or agent-level configurations. For a complete migration, use additional tools or scripts to handle these objects.

Azure SQL Managed Instance
Cohesity provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective backup, recovery, and data management solution for Microsoft Azure SQL Managed Instance. Azure Database for Azure SQL Managed Instance is a fully managed relational database service offered by Microsoft Azure. It enables users to deploy, manage, and scale Azure SQL Managed Instance in the cloud without the need to manage the underlying infrastructure.
Important: The backup and recovery of Azure SQL Managed Instance is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure (formerly known as Azure NGCE cluster). This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
This topic covers the following:
Plan and Prepare for Azure SQL Managed Instance Protection Before protecting Azure SQL Managed Instances with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Azure SQL Managed Instances with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your Azure as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For more information, see Register an Azure Source at Tenant Level.
Authentication for Azure SQL Managed Instance Protection
You must authenticate to Azure SQL Managed instance with Cohesity cluster for cloud in Azure to perform backup and restore. You can use one of the methods such as Username and Password, User Managed Identity, or System Managed Identity.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Username and Password:
With this method, you need to provide the credentials of the admin user of the SQL Managed Instance. This is the user account configured in your Azure environment during SQL Managed Instance creation. If needed, instead of using the admin user credentials, you can create a custom user and use it for authentication during backups. However, for restoring that backup, the admin user credentials are required. So, if you have used custom user credentials for backup authentication, you must change them back to the admin user credentials at the time of restore. You can use the following commands to create a custom user on the server/Managed Instance:
l To create a custom user on the server/Managed Instance: #CREATE LOGIN [newlogin] WITH PASSWORD = 'somepassword;
l To create same user under database which should be backed up by the custom user you have created: #CREATE USER [newlogin] FOR LOGIN [newlogin];
#ALTER ROLE db_owner ADD MEMBER [newlogin];
l Run the following command on the master system database: #CREATE USER [newlogin] FOR LOGIN [newlogin];
l User Managed Identity (UMI):
It uses a user assigned managed identity to authenticate to the Azure SQL Managed Instance. For this authentication, you must assign the Managed Identity Operator role to the UMI identity. Also, this UMI needs to be from the same subscription as the one in which the SQL Managed instance exists.
A single identity is shared by all nodes in the cluster. This identity should be assigned as the Microsoft Entra admin of the SQL Managed instance. Ensure all cluster nodes have this UMI set as their identity. To use the UMI method for authentication, you must perform the following activities as prerequisite:
l Create a user-assigned managed identity that would be used for authentication. Manage user-assigned managed identities
l Assign the Managed Identity Operator role to the UMI identity. Assign Azure roles to a managed identity
l Set the UMI as identity of the cluster nodes. Assign a user-assigned managed identity
l Assign this User Managed identity as Entra ID Admin on the server. Set Microsoft Entra admin
l Assign the UMI to Azure SQL Managed Instance/server under the Identity section > User assigned managed identity on the Azure Portal.
l System Managed Identity (SMI):

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

It uses a unique identity that is automatically created by Azure when you enable SMI on the node. This identity belongs only to that node and is deleted if the node is deleted. Each node in your cluster will have its own SMI, meaning multiple distinct identities. However, Azure SQL Managed Instance allows only one Microsoft Entra admin per node. This creates a challenge when you have multiple nodes, each with a different SMI. To mitigate this issue, you can do the following:
l Create a Microsoft Entra group. l Add all the nodes' SMI identities as group members. l Assign this group as Microsoft Entra Admin. This way, all nodes can authenticate using their respective SMIs through the group. SMI is not created separately as a resource here. You need to enable it on the cluster nodes from the Azure portal. To use the SMI method for authentication, you must perform the following activities as prerequisite: l Enable system-assigned managed identity on all the nodes of the cluster.
Enable system-assigned managed identity l Create a Microsoft Entra basic group and add SMI's of all the nodes created in
previous step as members. SMI name is the same as the VM (node) name which can be easily searched for while finding member to include in the group. Create a basic group and add members l Assign this Microsoft Entra basic group as Entra ID Admin on the server. Set Microsoft Entra admin
Considerations for Azure SQL Managed Instance Protection
You must review the following considerations before you proceed for registration, backup, or recovery:
l Backup and recovery are not supported for the following: l GRAPH_TABLE, l TEMPORAL_TABLE, l LEDGER_TABLE, l MEMORY_OPTIMIZED_TABLE
l Incremental backups fall back to full backups in the following cases: l Schema changes are detected during backup. l The full backup state file from an earlier backup is not available. l CDC (Change Data Capture) is enabled or disabled on the database/tables. l A previous full backup does not exist.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l If a backup fails due to insufficient tempDB storage on the SQL Managed Instance, you need to select the Client-side processing for CDC. Go to Protection Group > Additional Settings > CDC processing location > select Client.
l Restoring a backup taken from a higher database version to a lower version is not supported.
l If public access to the SQL Managed Instance is not available and a private endpoint is used for connectivity, add the private endpoint mapping in Cohesity Host Mapping, so name resolution works over the private network. Go to Settings > Networking > Host Mapping and add the required endpoints.
l An Azure VM, which is used as a Cohesity cluster node, should be in the same Vnet as that of the Azure-managed instance. Alternatively, if the Cohesity cluster node and SQL-managed instance are in different Vnet, then both the Vnets must peer to access the database instance.
l Backup fails when Readlock is placed on the database or resource group.
l Database diagrams are not restored.
l Backup and restore are not supported for the databases, which makes it mandatory to use client certificates for their connection to Cohesity cluster.
l Only default ports are supported.
l Database names containing the characters '#' and '/' are not supported for backup and restore operations. Also, the database name should adhere to the naming conventions suggested by the cloud vendors.
l ";" is not supported in server or database passwords.
l Restore across subscriptions of different tenants is not supported.
l Backup failure with invalid object name error: Subsequent full/incremental backups of an Azure SQL Managed Instance backup may fail with the following error, "Invalid object name 'cdc.<schema_name>_<table_name>_CT'".
l This issue occurs while executing the backup query script with a transfer object in the query (to transfer table from one schema to another).
l This may cause a mismatch between the user tables and their associated CDC tables. The mismatch typically arises after the schema changes or when database objects are moved between schemas after CDC is enabled. Workaround:
l Disable CDC on the database before running the backup.
l Run the following command: # EXEC sys.sp_cdc_disable_db
l Perform a full backup. The CDC will be automatically enabled during the next backup.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Duplicate Records: Recovered database may contain duplicate records if the source database does not include primary or foreign keys."
l CDC Job Cleanup: Full backups can fail during CDC processing if CDC jobs are not cleaned at the SQL MI level. This issue occurs when a database is deleted and then recreated with the same name.
Workaround:
You can manually perform the cleanup and disable CDC on database before backup. For more details, see Cleanup job.
Note: The CDC cleanup job removes all data from the change tracking tables based on the configured retention period.
l CMK as TDE: For native backups, Cohesity supports only CMK as TDE on the instance. During recovery, ensure that the same key (and version) is associated with the target server's CMK. Since Azure does not allow export of the keys, ensure that the keys are backed up and associated correctly during recovery.
l Recovery Database Encryption: During backup and recovery of Azure SQL MI without CDC, if the source database has encryption disabled but Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) is configured on the SQL server with Service-Managed Keys (SMK) or Customer-Managed Keys (CMK), encryption will be turned on for the recovered database by default.
l Database Tables: If the databases contain any of the following types of tables, the backup fails due to CDC limitations:
l Graph tables
l Temporal tables
l Ledger tables (updatable ledger)
l Memory optimized table (business critical tier only)
l These types of tables are supported for Azure Managed Instance databases, if the backup uses the native backup database workflow, using TDE enabled by Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) or TDE disabled.
l Column-level Encryption: Column-level encryption is supported only for Azure SQL Managed instances where TDE is configured with CMK. Full backups must be performed either in the native BAK format (without CDC data).
l Public Endpoint Support: Public endpoint on Azure SQL MI workload is not supported.
l Incremental Backup Failure: Incremental backup for Azure SQL MI fails when the tempdb storage is exhausted due to a large number of CDC transactions on the database. To avoid this, use the batch count to limit the number of transactions being

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

processed at a time.
l CDC Performance: For optimal CDC performance, ensure the following:
l Do not use DDL triggers that block schema changes, like CREATE/DROP TABLE, CREATE/DROP FUNCTION.
l Ensure that the SQL Server Agent service is running.
l Use an account with db_owner or sysadmin privileges for CDC setup.
l To avoid capture_instance conflicts, check if the table is already CDC-enabled.
l Protection to New Environment: DataProtect can back up and recover databases to new environments, but the identity columns may not retain their original seed values. This can cause new records to receive unexpected identity numbers, especially if rows were deleted before the backup. However, this issue does not affect TDE-enabled Azure SQL Managed Instance databases configured with a CMK and backed up with the native BAK format (without CDC data).
l SqlPackage Utility: Consider the following for the SqlPackage utility:
l SqlPackage may fail to export the following SQL Server objects: Logins, Jobs (SQL Agent Jobs), Linked Servers, Server-level permissions, Server roles, Credentials, Database Mail configuration, Replication settings, SSIS packages, Service Broker objects, CLR assemblies, Data in FILESTREAM/FILETABLE, Encrypted objects (if keys/certs are not exported), Cross-database dependencies, extended stored procedures, and some system objects.
l SqlPackage primarily exports database-level objects and data, but not serverlevel or agent-level configurations. For a complete migration, use additional tools or scripts to handle these objects.

Configure Authentication for Azure SQL Managed Instance
Before performing a backup of Azure SQL Managed Instances that are discovered in Cohesity cluster, you must configure credentials for these Managed Instances. These credentials are essential because they enable secure authentication and connectivity between Cohesity and your Azure SQL Managed Instance. Without valid credentials, the backup process cannot access your Managed Instance or its databases. You need to enter the credentials that you have already configured for the Managed Instances in your Azure environment. Once these credentials are validated and the connection is established, Cohesity can access the databases within the instance to perform operations such as dumping, protecting and restoring in case required. Consider the following points:
1. You can set credentials for the SQL Managed Instance at any object in the entity hierarchy. 1. Tenant 2. Subscription 3. Resource group 4. Instance level
2. The credentials you set are applied to all child objects within the selected object. 3. You cannot set credentials for individual databases. 4. It is recommended to apply credentials at the Managed Instance level. As if you apply
credentials at a higher level in the entity hierarchy (Resource group, Subscription, or Tenant), they will be applied to all child-level Managed Instances. If the credentials do not match any of the Managed Instances at the child-level, the backup of the databases within those Managed Instances will fail. 5. Three authentication methods are supported:
1. Username and Password 2. User Managed Identity 3. System Managed Identity
