Azure PostgreSQL
Cohesity provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective backup, recovery, and data management solution for Microsoft Azure PostgreSQL databases. Azure Database for Azure PostgreSQL is a fully managed relational database service offered by Microsoft Azure. It enables users to deploy, manage, and scale Azure PostgreSQL databases in the cloud without the need to manage the underlying infrastructure.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

Important: The backup and recovery of Azure PostgreSQL is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure (formerly known as Azure NGCE cluster).
This topic covers the following:
Plan and Prepare for Azure PostgreSQL Protection Before protecting Azure PostgreSQL with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Azure PostgreSQL with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your Azure as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For more information, see Register an Azure Source at Tenant Level.
Authentication for Azure PostgreSQL Protection
You must authenticate to Azure PostgreSQL database from the Cohesity cluster using one of the following methods:
l Username and Password l User Managed Identity (UMI) l System Managed Identity (SMI)
Username and Password
This method uses the credentials of the admin user for the PostgreSQL database. This is the user account configured during server creation. For backup, you can create a custom user. In the CLI run the following commands:
1. To create login user on the server: #CREATE LOGIN [newlogin] WITH PASSWORD = 'somepassword;
2. To create same user under database which should be backed up by user newlogin: User <database>; #CREATE USER [newlogin] FOR LOGIN [newlogin]; ALTER ROLE db_owner ADD MEMBER [newlogin];
3. Run the following command on the master system database: CREATE USER [newlogin] FOR LOGIN [newlogin];
For recovery, the default admin credentials created during server creation are required if the custom user credentials were set for authentication before backup. During recovery, you must change the credentials back to the default admin credentials.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

User Managed Identity (UMI)
This method uses a user-assigned managed identity to authenticate to the Azure PostgreSQL database. Perform the following to use the UMI authentication:
1. Create a user-assigned managed identity. For more information, see Manage userassigned managed identities using the Azure portal.
2. Assign the Managed Identity Operator role to the UMI identity. For more information, see User-assigned managed identity.
3. Set the UMI as the identity for all the cluster nodes. Ensure that the UMI is from the same subscription as the one in which the PostgreSQL database exists. For more information, see Assign a user-assigned managed identity to an existing VM.
4. Assign this User Managed Identity as Entra ID Admin on the server. For more information, see Set Microsoft Entra admin.
5. Assign the required user managed identity to Azure PostgreSQLdatabase under the Identity section - User assigned managed identity on the Azure Portal.
System Managed Identity (SMI)
This method uses a unique identity that is automatically created by Azure when you enable SMI on the node. This identity belongs only to the specific node and is deleted if the node is deleted. Each node in the cluster includes its own SMI (multiple distinct identities). Since the Azure PostgreSQL database allows only one Microsoft Entra admin per node, having multiple nodes, each with a different SMI may cause issues. To mitigate this issue, you can perform the following:
1. Create a Microsoft Entra group. 2. Add all the nodes' SMI identities as group members. 3. Assign this group as Microsoft Entra Admin.
This ensures that all the nodes can be authenticated using their respective SMIs through the group.
Note: SMIs are not created separately as a resource. You must enable it on the cluster nodes from the Azure portal.
Perform the following to use the SMI authentication:
1. Enable system-assigned managed identity on all the nodes of the cluster. For more information, see Enable system-assigned managed identity on an existing VM.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

2. Create a Microsoft Entra basic group and add SMI's of all the nodes created in previous step as members. The SMI name is the same as the VM (node) name, which can be easily searched for while finding members to include in the group. For more information, see Create a basic group and add members.
3. Assign this Microsoft Entra basic group as Entra ID Admin on the server. For more information, see Set Microsoft Entra admin.
Considerations for Azure PostgreSQL Protection
You must review the following considerations before you proceed for registration, backup, or recovery:
l Cohesity cluster does not restore accounts and their grants to the destination server. l Restoring a backup taken from a higher PostgreSQL database version to a lower
version is not supported. l Restoring security privileges is not supported. l Use the --no-owner and --no-privileges options during restore.
After restore, metadata captured at the time of backup is shown as the owner/ACL in the progress log restore activity on the web UI. l Restore does not fail if the owner or role does not exist on the destination. l Modify database ownership after restore. l Azure PostgreSQL database restore from a single server to a flexible server or vice versa is not supported. l Unsupported characters in database names during restore: `, @, \, [, ], !, #, %, ^, ., ,, &, *, (, ), <, >, ?, /, |, }, {, ~, :, ', ", ;, +, =, l Uppercase names are not supported for new accounts added after PostgreSQL server creation. l If full backups fail due to temporary objects, delete the temporary objects manually and run the backup again. l When Azure Managed Identity (UMI or SMI) is configured for authentication, Cohesity cluster performs full backups only. Incremental backups are not supported with MI. Use Username and Password authentication to enable incremental backups.
Considerations for Azure PostgreSQL Incremental Backups
l You can protect Azure PostgreSQL sever assets with a protection plan and policy. You can use full and incremental schedules.
l Always set the wal_level server parameter as logical. l The backup user must be an administrator. l The backup user must have the CREATEROLE and REPLICATION permissions. l To backup tables of other users, the tables must have the primary key.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Intelligent groups are supported. l Replica server databases are not supported for full and incremental backups. l Large object data type is not supported for incremental backups. l Incremental backup with the bytea_output server parameter with an escape value is
not supported. l Azure SMI and UMI are not supported for incremental backups. l The last value of the sequence generator may not be consistent after recovery of an
incremental backup. l To rename a database, perform the following:
l Note the name of the replication slot created for the database. SELECT slot_name FROM pg_replication_slots WHERE database = <database name to be renamed>
l Drop the replication slot after renaming the database. SELECT pg_drop_replication_slot('<replication slot name>')
l The default value of the max_replication_slots server parameter is 10. Since each database uses one replication slot, ensure you set this value to a higher number based on the approximate number of databases to be protected.
l Set the azure.enable_temp_tablespaces_on_local_ssd server parameter to OFF when the following error occurs: "psycopg2.errors.DiskFull: could not write to file "pg_tblspc/16386/PG_16_ 202307071/pgsql_tmp/pgsql_tmp449554.119": No space left on device."
l Ensure to check the storage space while incremental backups are running. l Avoid maintenance windows during backup and recovery.
Considerations for Azure PostgreSQL Encryption
l PostgreSQL does not natively provide Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) in standard community deployments. However, PostgreSQL supports application-level and column-level encryption through cryptographic extensions and functions (for example, pgcrypto).
l In Azure PostgreSQL, encryption at rest is typically provided through Azure-managed storage encryption mechanisms.
l During protection, the encrypted column data is preserved in its encrypted form. After recovery, applications can continue to access and decrypt the data using the appropriate encryption keys and application logic.
l Backup and recovery operations do not modify or decrypt application-encrypted column data. You must ensure that the required encryption keys remain accessible after recovery.

Configure Authentication for Azure PostgreSQL
Before performing a backup of Azure PostgreSQLs that are discovered in Cohesity cluster, you must configure credentials for these Managed Instances. These credentials are essential because they enable secure authentication and connectivity between Cohesity and your Azure PostgreSQL. Without valid credentials, the backup process cannot access your Managed Instance or its databases.
You need to enter the credentials that you have already configured for the Managed Instances in your Azure environment. Once these credentials are validated and the connection is established, Cohesity can access the databases within the instance to perform operations such as dumping, protecting and restoring in case required.

1. Tenant

If the credentials do not match any of the Managed Instances at the child-level, the backup of the databases within those Managed Instances will fail.

Recover Azure PostgreSQL Databases
After you protect your Azure PostgreSQL, you can recover them from Cohesity cluster to their original location or a new location.
Note: - If you plan to overwrite an existing database, Cohesity recommends backing up the database first. - To restore to a new location, the destination instance credential validation must be done, and the host mapping of the destination instance must be added in Settings>Networking> Host Mapping.
To recover protected Azure PostgreSQL databases:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Recoveries. Select the required database that is to be recovered.
2. Click Recover > Azure > PostgreSQL. 3. On the New Recovery page,
1. Use the filters and search box to locate the required databases. Wildcards are supported.
2. Select the required database that is to be recovered. 3. Click Next: Recovery Option. 4. In the Recover To section, do one of the following:
1. To restore to the original location: 1. Select the Original Location option to recover the database to its original location. Consider the following points: 1. The existing database at that location with the same name will always be overwritten. 2. You must type Yes to confirm and proceed. 3. To avoid overwriting the database with the same name, enter a new name in the Rename field below. The database will be recovered with the new name you have provided.
2. To restore to a new location: 1. Select the New Location option to recover the database to an alternative PostgreSQL.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

2. Select the registered Azure tenant from the Source drop-down and then select the PostgreSQL server to which you want to recover the database.
3. To overwrite an existing database, toggle on the Overwrite existing database(s) option and type Yes to confirm.
4. If you want to recover the database with a different name, enter a new name in the Rename field below.
5. If you enter a new name, the database will be restored at the selected location with the new name assigned.
6. If you do not enter a new name, the existing database with the same name will be overwritten.
4. Select your Recovery Options:
1. Refresh Materialized Views. Toggle On Refresh materialized views automatically after recovery to automatically refresh the PostgreSQL materialized views post recovery to ensure they reflect the latest recovered data.
Materialized views in PostgreSQL are database objects that physically store the pre-computed results of a query on the disk. Cohesity automatically runs a refresh script after recovery to refresh materialized views and ensure data consistency.
If this option is toggled Off, the recovery time can be reduced, but materialized views can remain outdated until manually refreshed. To manually refresh, download the script from the recovery task details page, and then run it on the recovered PostgreSQL database.
2. Rename. If you have renamed the database, it will be recovered with the new name at either the original or the new location, based on the option you have selected.
3. Task Name. Change the default name of the recovery task.
5. Click Recover.
Refresh Azure PostgreSQL Materialized Views
When recovering Azure PostgreSQL databases, materialized views must be refreshed to reflect the recovered data. This topic explains the available options to refresh the materialized views and recommendations to choose the right approach for your environment.
Materialized views in PostgreSQL are database objects that physically store the precomputed results of a query on the disk. Unlike regular views, they need to be explicitly refreshed to reflect changes in their underlying base tables.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

After a database recovery operation, materialized views contain stale data from the backup point. The views must be rebuilt to work with the newly recovered data. Without refreshing, queries against materialized views return outdated or incorrect results. You can refresh the materialized views using one of the following options:
l Automatic Refresh Materialized Views During Recovery l Manual Refresh Materialized Views After Recover
The following is a comparison between the refresh options:

Factor

Automatic Refresh Manual Refresh

Database Size

Small to medium

Large

Refresh Duration

Size

Large

Recovery Time Objective Flexible

Strict

Permissions Available

Yes

Limited

Scheduling Flexibility

Low

High

Administrative Control

Minimal

Greater

Automatic Refresh Materialized Views During Recovery
Cohesity supports performing automatic materialized view refresh using the recovery options in the Cohesity UI. You can use this option in the following scenarios:
l Smaller databases where refresh completes quickly l Immediate data consistency is critical l Database credentials have the required permissions to refresh materialized views l Longer recovery duration is acceptable
Prerequisites
Before enabling automatic refresh, verify that the Azure PostgreSQL database user has the required permissions using the following commands:
l Check schema usage: SELECT has_schema_privilege('refresh_user', 'schema_name', 'USAGE');
l Check table select permissions:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

SELECT has_table_privilege('refresh_user', 'table_name', 'SELECT');
l Check materialized view permissions:
SELECT has_table_privilege('refresh_user', 'materialized_view_name', 'INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE');
Procedure
To automatically refresh materialized views: 1. During the recovery workflow, navigate to the Refresh Materialized Views option in the Recovery Options section. 2. Toggle On Refresh materialized views automatically after recovery. 3. Complete the database recovery.
Manual Refresh Materialized Views After Recovery
Cohesity supports manually performing materialized view refresh using the script available in the Cohesity UI. You can use this option in the following scenarios:
l Large databases with materialized views require significant time to refresh l DataProtect source credentials do not have sufficient permissions to refresh
materialized views l Recovery Time Objective (RTO) requires faster database availability l Materialized view refresh must be scheduled during off-peak hours The following are the benefits of manual post-recovery refresh: l Faster Recovery Time: Your database becomes available immediately after
recovery. l Controlled Timing: Schedule the refresh during off-peak hours. l Better Resource Management: Avoid resource contention during critical recovery
operations. l Flexibility: Database administrators can monitor and manage the refresh process
independently. l Permission Flexibility: Use a different user with appropriate permissions for refresh
operations.
Prerequisites
Before refreshing the materialized view manually, verify that the Azure PostgreSQL database user has the required permissions using the following commands:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Check schema usage: SELECT has_schema_privilege('refresh_user', 'schema_name', 'USAGE');
l Check table select permissions: SELECT has_table_privilege('refresh_user', 'table_name', 'SELECT');
l Check materialized view permissions: SELECT has_table_privilege('refresh_user', 'materialized_view_name', 'INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE');
Procedure
To manually refresh materialized views after recovery: 1. Disable Automatic Refresh: 1. During recovery, disable the Refresh Materialized Views option. 2. Complete the database recovery. 3. Download the refresh script from the Cohesity UI. 4. Run the script manually after the recovery. 2. Download the refresh script: 1. Navigate to Recoveries. 2. Select the PostgreSQL recovery task. 3. Open the Options tab. 4. Locate the Materialized View Refresh section. 3. Download the refresh script. 1. Run the Refresh Script: 2. Execute the downloaded script on the recovered database 3. The script automatically determines materialized view dependencies. 4. Materialized views are refreshed in dependency order.
Best Practices
l Assess your data size. For databases with materialized views exceeding several GB, consider manual refresh.
l Verify permissions. Before using automatic refresh, ensure dataprotect source credentials have required permissions.
l Save the script. Download and save the refresh script from the recovery details page for future use.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

l Test in non-production. Validate your chosen approach in test/dev environments first.
l Schedule appropriately. For manual refresh, run during maintenance windows or low-traffic periods.
l Monitor resources. Materialized views refresh can be resource-intensive; ensure adequate system resources are available.
l Regular maintenance. Consider implementing periodic refresh schedules (using tools like pg_cron) independent of recovery operations.
l Document your views. Maintain documentation of materialized views and their dependencies.
Azure Blob Storage and Azure Data Lake Storage
Azure Blob Storage and Azure Data Lake Storage are types of storage accounts in Microsoft Azure, designed for storing unstructured data. Within these storage accounts, you can create containers (for Blob Storage) or file systems (for Data Lake Storage) to organize and manage your data. Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS) offers a hierarchical namespace, enabling efficient file system operations and enhanced file-level security, while Azure Blob Storage utilizes a flat namespace for simpler object storage. Cohesity seamlessly integrates with Azure, providing a straightforward, fast, and cost-effective solution for backup, recovery, and data management across both Azure Blob Storage and Azure Data Lake Storage accounts.
Important: The backup and recovery of Azure Blob Storage and Azure Data Lake Storage is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure (formerly known as Azure NGCE cluster).
Plan and Prepare for Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage Protection
Before protecting Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage with the Cohesity cluster, ensure you have met the prerequisites and reviewed the considerations described in this topic.
Before You Begin
To protect Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your Azure as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. For more information, see Register an Azure Source at Tenant Level.
Prerequisites for Registering Azure Source
Before registering Azure with the Cohesity cluster, you must perform the following steps:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

1. Register an application with Microsoft Entra ID and create a service principal. For information, see the Azure documentation.
2. Create an application secret key for setting up authentication for the service principal. For information, see the Azure documentation.
3. Create a custom role at subscription level with the required permissions for backup and recovery.
4. For information about creating a custom role, see the Azure documentation. 5. Assign the custom role to the Microsoft Entra ID application created in step 1.
The Entra ID and application secret key are required when you register the Azure source with the Cohesity cluster.
Considerations for Azure Storage Protection
Review and understand the following considerations before you protect Azure Blob Storage and Data Lake Storage:
l The Microsoft Entra ID you create must have access to the Storage Container you want to protect.
l Protection of Page blobs and blobs in the archive tier is not supported. l Both full and incremental backups are supported. l You cannot recover Blob data to a Data Lake container, or Data Lake data to a Blob
container
Backup Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage
After registering your Azure source, Cohesity uses the cloud credentials provided to authenticate with Azure. Once authenticated, Cohesity automatically discovers all the subscriptions that the service account can access, as well as all supported workloads such as Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage within those subscriptions. The discovered workloads appear under Data Protection > Sources. You can select the Blob and Data Lake Storage tab to view all the Storage Containers discovered. For more information on registering Azure source, see Register an Azure Source at Tenant Level.

displays the entity hierarchy of Azure, allowing you to navigate

from the tenant-level down to individual Storage Container.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: This policy achieves similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy. The data is written to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD.
For best performance, we recommend the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Cohesity provides the following ways to delete a Protection Group: l Delete Protection Group Only: Allows you to delete the Protection Group. All the backups generated by the Protection Group are preserved till the snapshots expire. l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots: Allows you to delete the Protection Group and all the local and archived Snapshots generated by the Protection Group.
Note: After deleting the Protection Group, the reclaimed storage space details are not displayed immediately. It will take some time to reflect on the product UI.
To delete the Protection Group: 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for Storage Container.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Delete. 4. In the Delete Protection Group? dialog box, select any one of the following
options: l Delete Protection Group Only l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots
Recover Azure Blob or Data Lake Storage Account Containers You can restore the Storage Containers of Azure Blob or Data Lake Storage Account either to its original location or to a different location.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

Note: We recommend that you review the Plan and Prepare for Azure Blob and Data Lake Storage Protection.
To recover a Storage Container:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Recoveries.
2. Click Recover at the top right of the page and then select Azure > Blob and DataLake Storage.
3. Search for the Storage Container by entering characters of the Storage Container name, or by specifying the wildcard character *.
4. From the list of search results, select the Storage Container to recover. By default, the latest snapshot of the Storage Container is selected for recovery. To recover from a different snapshot, perform the following steps depending on the object selected:
From the selected lists, mouse over the snapshot, and then click the edit icon. The Edit recovery point for <container_name> page appears. By default, the option to select the snapshot is displayed in the List mode. You can also choose to view the option in the Timeline mode by clicking the Timeline tab in the top-right corner of the page.
l To select a snapshot from the List mode:
a. Select the List tab from the top-right corner of the Edit recovery point for <container_name> page. By default, the page displays the snapshots available in the last one month. You can also select a snapshot from a different date range by selecting the date range from the Date drop-down list. The page displays the available snapshots in the specified range.
b. Select the snapshots to be recovered.
c. By default, the snapshot is recovered from the local Cohesity cluster.
d. Click Select Recovery Point and then go to step 5.
l To select a snapshot from the Timeline mode:
a. From the Choose a date drop-down, select a date. The snapshots available on the selected date are displayed in blue dots on the timeline bar.
b. Select the snapshot to be recovered by clicking the corresponding blue dot.
c. By default, the snapshot is recovered from the local Cohesity cluster.
d. Click Select Recovery Point and then go to step 5.
5. Click Next: Recover Options.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

Azure

6. In the Recover To section, select any one of the following options based on where you want to restore the container and then provide the required information: l Original Location: Restore into the original container. a. Enable Overwrite existing container(s) to recover the Storage Container by overwriting the original container. Type Yes to confirm. If the source and target objects are identical, then the target container will not be updated even if the Overwrite existing container(s) option is enabled. b. Optionally, in the Prefix or file path (optional) field, add a prefix or file path to the files of the containers that are recovered. l New Location: Restore into another container within the same or a different Azure source. a. From the Source drop-down, select a registered Azure source and from the Container drop-down, select the target Storage Container to which you want to restore the object from the source containers. If the source and target objects are identical, then the target container will not be updated even if the Overwrite existing container(s) option is enabled. b. To overwrite any existing Storage Container with the same name, enable Overwrite existing container(s) and type Yes to confirm. If the source and target objects are identical, then the target container will not be updated even if the Overwrite existing container(s) option is enabled. c. Optionally, in the Prefix or file path (optional) field, add a prefix or file path to the files of the containers that are recovered.
Note: If Overwrite existing container(s) is enabled, any existing object in the target container with the same name as a recovered object is overwritten. Cohesity does not delete or replace the Azure Storage Container itself.
7. In the Recovery Options section, configure the following options: a. Granular recovery: To perform granular recovery the Storage Container, toggle on Enable to recover specific prefixes or file paths and provide the prefix of the files to be recovered. For example, Finance/statement/document. You can click the add icon to provide multiple prefixes.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

The maximum number of prefixes that you can provide per recovery task is 100. b. Continue on Error: Enable this option if you want to continue the recovery even if one of the files in the container encounters an error. By default, this option is disabled and the recovery operation will fail if one of the files encounters an error. c. Task Name: Update the default name of the recovery task. 8. Click Recover.

GCP Virtual Machines
Cohesity natively integrates with Google Cloud to provide a simple, fast, and cost-effective solution for backup, recovery, and data management of Google Cloud Services, such as virtual machines. This chapter includes the following topics:
Plan and Prepare for GCP Protection
Review the following prerequisites and considerations of GCP.
Prerequisites
l To add a new node to a Cohesity cluster, both the node and Cohesity cluster must have Cohesity 6.0 or later installed. For more information, see Manage Nodes.
l Make sure googleapis.com is reachable through firewall port 443 when registering the GCP Source.
l You must allowlist the following source FQDNs for registering and backing up the GCP source: l https://accounts.google.com/ l https://www.googleapis.com/ l https://storage.googleapis.com l https://vpcaccess.googleapis.com/ l https://cloudfunctions.googleapis.com/ l https://cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com/
Considerations
Review the following considerations of GCP native snapshotting:
l App consistent backup is not supported. l Recovering files/folders to source is not supported. File download is supported. l Cloning is not supported. l For incremental snapshots, native backup uses source side dedup and not Google API
as Google does not have any APIs for incremental backup. Hence full and incremental

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

backups after the first run takes about the same time to complete. l For backup and recovery of GCP VMs, the service account, the VPC and Subnet where
the fleet instances are launched should be on the same project. l You can perform files and folder recovery to an GCP VM Linux instance only if the GCP
VM Linux instance is of x86_64 architecture. l File-level recovery is not supported for GCP VMs with XFSv5 file system. l You cannot exclude disk at the object-level for auto-protected VMs. To exclude disk
for auto-protect VMs, you must use the Volume Exclusion Settings option in the Additional Settings. l When browsing files or folders for recovery, Cohesity does not display files or folders with an absolute path length exceeding approximately 3,500 characters. To recover these files or folders, select the parent directory.
Create an IAM Custom Role for GCP
You need to create IAM custom roles when registering GCP as a source on the Cohesity cluster.
Prerequisites
Before you begin creating IAM custom roles, ensure the following prerequisites are met:
l Enable IAM API. For more information, see Enable GCP APIs. l Create service accounts. For more information, see Creating and managing service
accounts.
Perform the following steps to create an IAM custom role:
1. In the Google Cloud Platform Console, navigate to IAM & Admin. 2. From the drop-down located at the top of the page, select the project in which you
want to create the custom role.

3. Click Create Role. 4. In the Title field, enter a title for the role. 5. In the Description field, enter a brief description. 6. In the ID field, enter the ID. 7. From the Role launch stage drop-down, select the role launch stage for the role.

Protect GCP VMs
In Cohesity, GCP VMs with their shielded VM properties are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, archived, or replicated.
A Protection Policy is a reusable set of settings that define how and when objects are protected and replicated. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

Note: Backup and recovery of GCP VMs requires a proxy VM (fleet instance) to be launched on the cloud source. For enhanced security, after creating the proxy VM on the cloud source, Cohesity automatically deploys an X.509 certificate. Contact Cohesity Support if you want to launch the proxy VM with its Shielded VM properties enabled.

1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. Click Protect on the top-right of the page and then select Virtual Machines. 3. Click Add Objects and from the Registered Source drop-down list, select the GCP

l Click the Tags icon on the right and select a tag to:
l Auto Protect ( ) the VMs having this tag.
l Exclude ( ) the auto protection of VMs having this tag. If a VM has multiple tags with Auto Protect and Exclude applied, exclusion takes precedence. These excluded VMs are also excluded even if a parent object is auto protected.
The Tags button will not be displayed if the Cohesity cluster detects that no sources have tags assigned to them. l Exclude any disks of the VM from protection. To exclude the disks:
a. Click the edit icon displayed next to the VM of which you want to exclude the disk.

Additional Settings

Additional Settings

Description

Pause Future Runs

Toggle on this option to stop protection runs of the Protection Group from executing. Once you enable this option, no protection runs will be scheduled for this Protection Group.

End Time

Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A Protection Group run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy.

Note: Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.

Indexing

l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Protection Groups.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve a similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
This option is toggled on by default to index the data of the Protection Group. Indexing improves files and folders search. Cohesity performs incremental indexing where only the data that has changed since the previous snapshot is scanned and indexed.

The Cohesity cluster attempts to index all files and folders to a drive on both Windows and Linux systems. If the Cohesity cluster is unable to find mount point information about files or directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories in the lvol_N directory, where N is a unique number such as 1.
On Windows systems, if the Cohesity cluster finds the mount point information about files and directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories with a drive letter such as C:.
On Linux systems, how files and directories are indexed and displayed is dependent on the conditions specified in the following table.

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

Simple Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
UUID="ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc" /mnt ext4 auto 0
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point that was specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

LVM Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
/dev/mapper/VG1-root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
/dev/VG1/root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt. If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

4. Once you select the files and folder to recover, select one of the following options:
l Next: Recover Options: If you select this option, then continue with the step 5 to configure the file recovery options.
l Download Files: If you are recovering a single file, this option downloads the file to your browser's download folder. For all other selections, this creates a recovery task. When the task completes, from the Recoveries page, click the task name and then click Download Files to download the generated zip file.
Character replacement explanation for : and \ in file and directory names in zip files
If the original file or directory name contains a `:' , it is replaced with `_COLON_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "a:b" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b" l The original name is "a:b:c" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b_
COLON_c"
If the original file or directory name contains a `\', it is replaced with '_BACK_ SLASH_' in the archive. Example:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

l The original name is "x\y" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_y" l The original name is "x\y\z" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_
y_BACK_SLASH_z" 5. From the Recover To, select New Server to recover the files or folders to a new
server. 6. Source: From the Source drop-down menu, select a registered server to which you
want to recover the files and folders. You can also register a new source by clicking Register Source. 7. Target: From the Target (for VM and physical server) or Volume (for NAS) drop-down menu, select a VM or volume to which the files and files are to be recovered.
Note: For recovering files and folders of a VMware VM, ensure that VMware Tools are installed and running on the target VM. The target list displayed includes only VMs with VMware Tools installed and running.
8. Recover to: In the Recover to field, change the default location to which the files or folders are recovered. By default, the files and folders are recovered to the /tmp/ directory for VMs. For NAS, an example path on an alternate location could be /tmp/recover. You can recover encrypted files/folders to their original location only. Example for Windows alternate location: l D:\cohesity_restore\1.txt l D:\cohesity_restore\bar User Account Requirements for VM Protection may need to be met to recover files to a Windows VM. If recovering to a standalone Hyper-V host or cluster, you must add the guest VM to the reverse lookup zone in the DNS server to complete the recovery successfully.

Disable this option to create the files and folders in the specified location. Any duplicate files are skipped. l C:\restore\1.txt l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_0\1.txt l C:\restore\bar l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_1\bar If Overwrite Existing File/Folder is enabled, recovering a file to source when the file is in Fuse may cause the open file to be overwritten. Whether overwriting occurs depends on the application using the file. l Preserve File/Folder Attributes: By default, this option is enabled and the ACLs, permissions, and timestamps are preserved for all files and folders. If you disable this option, then ACLs and permissions are not preserved. If recovering both folders and files, then folders will receive the new timestamps, but files retain their original timestamps. If recovering only files, then files will receive the new timestamps. l Continue on Error: Enable this option if you want to continue the recovery even if one of the objects encounters an error. By default, this option is disabled and the recovery operation will fail if one of the objects encounters an error. l Cluster Interface: By default, the Auto Select option is enabled and the recovery task automatically selects the correct VLAN. If you disable this option, then select a configured interface group from the Interface Group drop-down. l Task Name: Change the default name of the recovery task. 10. Click Start Recovery.

Considerations for BigQuery Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect BigQuery objects:
l User permissions are not restored -- Google Cloud project users and their permissions are excluded from restores. The restored dataset owner will be the GCP service principal configured in the Cohesity cluster when you registered the Google Cloud as a source.
l Daily export limit -- Google Cloud imposes a maximum data export limit of 50 TB per project, per day.
l Tags are not restored -- Dataset and table tags are not included in backups or restores.
l Unsupported data types -- A record with the data type: DATETIME in the tables is not supported for backup. This also includes DATETIME fields nested inside a RECORD-type field.
The RANGE data type is also not supported.
l Linked datasets -- Datasets linked from other projects are not discovered, backed up, or restored.
l External datasets -- Datasets that reference external data sources outside BigQuery (for example, data in Cloud Storage or Spanner) are not discovered, backed up, or restored.
l Schema requirements -- Tables without a defined schema or without any columns cannot be backed up. Tables must have a defined schema to be backed up. Empty tables are supported for protection and recovery if the table schema is present.
l Access controls not supported -- Tables that use column-level access control or row-level security cannot be backed up.
l Backup type limitation -- Only full backups are supported; incremental backups are not available for BigQuery objects.
l Cross-region charges -- Cross-region backup and recovery operations will incur additional charges as per Google Cloud Platform (GCP) pricing policies and may result in higher overall costs due to data transfer and storage in multiple regions.
l Unsupported table types -- Views, materialized views, and table snapshots are not supported for backup and restore in this feature. External tables are supported.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

BigQuery Backup Process
When you run a protection job in the Cohesity cluster to back up BigQuery datasets, the datasets specified in the Protection Group are first exported from BigQuery to a staging bucket in Google Cloud Storage. The Cohesity cluster then copies the data from the staging bucket to the cluster. After the backup completes successfully, the contents of the staging bucket are deleted to free up storage.

Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports only full backups for BigQuery datasets or tables. Incremental backups are not supported.
Protect BigQuery
In the Cohesity cluster, Google Cloud BigQuery datasets and tables are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy.
Note: Cohesity supports only full backups for BigQuery datasets and tables. Incremental backups are not supported.
Prerequisites
Before you protect BigQuery objects, ensure that a staging bucket is available in Google Cloud Storage. You can either use an existing bucket or allow Cohesity to automatically create one during the backup configuration.
l If you choose to Auto Create the staging bucket: Cohesity automatically creates a staging bucket in the same region as your dataset(s) or tables when you start a backup operation.
l If you choose to specify an existing bucket: You can specify an existing bucket located in the same region as the datasets or tables being protected. Using a bucket in a different region is supported but may incur additional Google Cloud Storage charges.
Note: After each protection job run, Cohesity deletes only the temporary data stored in the staging bucket during backup operations. The staging bucket itself is retained and reused for future backup operations to minimize storage costs and avoid cross-region charges.

Additional Settings QoS Policy

Priority Description

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.
Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. The Cohesity cluster supports concurrent backups. However, if the number of protection runs exceeds the ability to process runs, this will be the priority of implementation of the protection runs:
a. High-priority protection runs b. Medium-priority protection runs c. Low-priority protection runs

When you run a protection job for Bigtable, the Cohesity cluster performs a full backup specified in the Protection Group. The Cohesity cluster connects to the selected instance using the specified credentials during source registration. Cohesity triggers a Dataflow job to read data from Bigtable tables and transfers to staging bucket. Further, the data is transferred from staging bucket to the Cohesity cluster.

Additional Settings QoS Policy
Alerts

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
l Backup Auto: The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Considerations for Spanner Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect Spanner databases with Cohesity .
l Full Backups Only: Only full backups are supported. Incremental backups and point-in-time recovery (PITR) are not supported.
l Database-Level Operations: Backups and recovery operations are performed at the database level. Table-level operations are not supported.
l Data Format: Backup data is exported in Avro format. Some Spanner-specific data types or extensions may require adjustments before being restored or imported into other SQL databases.
l Edition Compatibility: Backups and restores are supported across all Spanner editions (Standard, Enterprise, and Enterprise+). Cross-edition recovery is allowed but may be limited to features or datatypes common to both editions. For best results, restore to the same edition whenever possible.
l Database-Level Recovery: Recovery of complete Spanner instances is not supported. You can restore only individual databases.
l Overwrite Behavior: Restoring over an existing database with same name in an instance requires deletion of existing conflicting database. If drop protection is enabled , deletion will fail, and manual intervention is required.
l Performance Optimization: Improve backup performance by increasing the number of Dataflow workers and enabling Boost. For large databases, horizontal scaling (adding more workers) is typically more effective than vertical scaling.
l Plan for Cloud Dataflow quotas: Cohesity uses Cloud Dataflow jobs during backup and recovery. Google Cloud projects run up to 25 concurrent Dataflow jobs by default. If your environment triggers more than 25 concurrent backup/recovery operations

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

and they start Dataflow jobs, some jobs can be rejected and the corresponding operations can fail. To avoid this, reduce concurrent operations or request a higher Dataflow job quota in Google Cloud. For more information, see Quotas and limits.
l Cross-region charges: Cross-region backup and recovery operations will incur additional charges as per Google Cloud Platform (GCP) pricing policies and may result in higher overall costs due to data transfer and storage in multiple regions.
Backup Spanner Databases
After registering your Google Cloud source in the Cohesity cluster, it uses the provided service account credentials (JSON key or email and private key) to authenticate with Google Cloud.
Once authenticated, it automatically discovers all projects that the service account can access, as well as all supported workloads such as Spanner databases within those projects. The discovered workloads appear under Data Protection > Sources. When you open the registered Google Cloud source, each workload type is displayed on its own tab. Select the Spanner tab to view all the discovered databases.

Spanner Backup Process
When you run a protection job in the Cohesity cluster, one or more selected Spanner databases are exported to a Google Cloud Storage staging bucket. The staging bucket temporarily stores the exported data before it is ingested into the Cohesity cluster. The Cohesity cluster verifies that the selected bucket meets configuration requirements and ensures that the backup runs efficiently.
During the process, the Spanner databases are securely exported to the staging bucket as full backups. After the export completes, the Cohesity cluster automatically copies the data from the staging bucket to the cluster for retention. Once ingestion is successful, the Cohesity cluster applies the defined retention policies. The contents of the staging bucket are then automatically deleted to free up storage and reduce costs.

Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports only full backups for Spanner databases. Incremental backups are not supported.
Protect Spanner
In the Cohesity cluster, Spanner database are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy.
Note: Cohesity supports only full backups for Spanner databases. Incremental backups are not supported.

l Auto Create: Allow Cohesity to automatically create a temporary staging bucket during protection configuration. l The staging bucket is created in the same region as the database(s). l For multi-region deployments, the bucket is created in the default leader region.

l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Recover Spanner Databases
You can recover Spanner databases either to their original Google Cloud source or to a different source, instance and region.
Spanner Recovery Process
When a recovery job runs on the Cohesity cluster, the selected Spanner database backups are exported to a Google Cloud Storage staging bucket. The Cohesity cluster then recreates the database in the target environment and transfers the exported data to it. After the data transfer and database creation are complete, the Cohesity cluster triggers a Spanner import job. Google Cloud Spanner automatically ingests the database data from the staging bucket into the Spanner deployment. Once the import is successful, the staged backup data is automatically deleted from the bucket to free up storage and minimize costs.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

Note: Under normal conditions, staged backup data in the staging bucket is automatically cleaned up after the import completes. However, in certain failure scenarios, the cleanup may not occur. In such cases, you should manually verify and delete any remaining staged data.
Cleanup may fail in scenarios such as:
l Import job submission failure during recovery. Staged data may remain if the import job could not be triggered.
l Duplicate subtask-related errors during backup or restore. These errors may interrupt cleanup, leaving temporary data in the staging bucket.
Prerequisites
Before you recover Spanner databases, ensure that a staging bucket is available in Google Cloud Storage. You can either use an existing bucket or allow Cohesity to automatically create one during the restore process.
l If you choose to Auto Create the staging bucket: Cohesity automatically creates a staging bucket in the same region as your database(s) when you start the recovery. For multi-region deployments, the bucket is created in the default leader region.
l The recovery operations may take longer if the target instance has lower compute capacity or is already running active workloads. Smaller instances may process data more slowly during recovery.
l If you choose to specify an existing bucket: You can specify an existing bucket located in the same region as the recovery target. Using a staging bucket in a different region than the target instance's default leader region is not supported by default. Contact Cohesity Support if cross-region usage is required.
Note: After each recovery job run, Cohesity deletes only the temporary data stored in the staging bucket. The staging bucket itself is retained and reused for future recovery operations to minimize storage costs and avoid cross-region charges .
Recover Spanner Databases
To recover Spanner databases: 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Recoveries. 2. Click Recover at the top right of the page and then select Google Cloud > Spanner.

Considerations for Firestore Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect Google Cloud Firestore databases.
l Database-Level Protection Only: Backups and restores are performed at the database level. Individual collections cannot be selected for backup or restore.
l Full Backups Only: Incremental and log-based backups are not supported. Each backup creates a full copy of the database.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

l No Snapshot Isolation: Backup consistency is based on the snapshot time. Updates made during export may not be included.
l Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR): PITR is optional and available for up to seven days. It incurs additional Google Cloud costs.
l Quota Limits: Firestore allows a maximum of 20 export/import requests per minute and up to 50 concurrent operations per project. Exceeding limits can result in failures.
l Manual Service Account Configuration: Service accounts must be registered and assigned required IAM roles for Firestore and Cloud Storage operations.
l No Transaction or Log Backups: Firestore does not support log-based backups.
l Overwrite Behavior: Restoring a database with the overwrite option deletes all collections before import. If the restore fails, data loss can occur.
l No Maintenance Mode: Firestore does not support disabling access during recovery. Pause application writes manually to maintain consistency.
l Cross-region charges: Cross-region backup and recovery operations will incur additional charges as per Google Cloud Platform (GCP) pricing policies and may result in higher overall costs due to data transfer and storage in multiple regions.
Backup Firestore Databases
After registering your Google Cloud source in the Cohesity cluster, it uses the provided service account credentials (JSON key or email and private key) to authenticate with Google Cloud.
Once authenticated, it automatically discovers all projects that the service account can access, as well as all supported workloads such as Firestore databases within those projects. The discovered workloads appear under Data Protection > Sources. When you open the registered Google Cloud source, each workload type is displayed on its own tab. Select the Firestore tab to view all the discovered databases.
The Firestore tab displays the entity hierarchy for the Firestore environment, allowing you to navigate from the project level down to individual databases.

GCP

Firestore Backup Process
When you run a protection job in the Cohesity cluster, the selected Firestore database(s) and their collections are exported to a Google Cloud Storage (GCS) staging bucket. The staging bucket temporarily stores the exported data before it is ingested into the Cohesity cluster.
After the export completes, the Cohesity cluster copies the data from the staging bucket into the cluster for retention and applies the defined retention policies.
Once ingestion is complete, Cohesity automatically deletes only the temporary data from the staging bucket to free up storage and reduce Google Cloud Storage costs.

Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports only full backups for Firestore databases. Incremental backups are not supported.
Protect Firestore
In the Cohesity cluster, Google Cloud Firestore databases are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy.
Note: Cohesity supports only full backups for Firestore databases. Incremental backups are not supported.
Prerequisites
Before you protect Firestore databases, ensure that a staging bucket is available in Google Cloud Storage. You can either use an existing bucket or allow Cohesity to automatically create one during the backup configuration.

GCP

l If you choose to specify an existing bucket: You can specify an existing bucket located in the same region as the databases being protected. Using a bucket in a different region is supported but may incur additional Google Cloud Storage charges.
Note: After each protection job run, Cohesity deletes only the temporary data stored in the staging bucket during backup operations. The staging bucket itself is retained and reused for future backup operations to minimize storage costs and avoid cross-region charges.

Priority Description

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Considerations for Cloud SQL for MySQL Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect Cloud SQL for MySQL databases:
l Full Database Backups Only: Incremental backups are not supported. Each backup captures the complete contents of the selected database.
l Database-Level Restores: You can restore individual databases and choose to rename or overwrite them. Restoring an entire MySQL server is not supported.
l Direct Database Connection: Cohesity connects directly to the MySQL server using the database credentials you provide. These credentials are required for performing backup and recovery operations, as well as for retrieving the size of the databases on the server.
l Version Downgrade Not Supported: Restoring a backup taken from a higher Cloud SQL for MySQL database version to a lower version is not supported.
l Cross-region charges: Cross-region backup and recovery operations will incur additional charges as per Google Cloud Platform (GCP) pricing policies and may result in higher overall costs due to data transfer and storage in multiple regions.
Backup Cloud SQL for MySQL Databases
After registering your Google Cloud source in the Cohesity cluster, it uses the provided service account credentials (JSON key or email and private key) to authenticate with Google Cloud.
Once authenticated, it automatically discovers all projects that the service account can access, as well as all supported workloads such as Cloud SQL for MySQL databases within those projects. The discovered workloads appear under Data Protection > Sources. When you open the registered Google Cloud source, each workload type is displayed on its own tab. Select the Cloud SQL for MySQL tab to view all the discovered databases.
The Cloud SQL for MySQL tab displays the entity hierarchy for the Cloud SQL for MySQL environment, allowing you to navigate from the project level down to individual databases.

Backup Scope by Cloud SQL for MySQL Hierarchy
Cohesity cluster allows you to back up Cloud SQL for MySQL databases at different levels of the hierarchy. You can choose to back up:

region. l Region level: Back up all databases within a specific region. l Multiple databases across regions: Back up selected databases from different
regions. l Project level: Back up all databases in all regions within the specified Project ID.
Cloud SQL for MySQL Backup Process
When you run a protection job for Cloud SQL for MySQL, the Cohesity cluster performs a full backup of the databases specified in the Protection Group. The Cohesity cluster connects to the selected Cloud SQL instance using the database credentials you provided during source registration and uses standard MySQL backup utilities, such as mysql and mysqldump, to export the complete database contents to the cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports only full backups for Cloud SQL for MySQL databases. Incremental backups are not supported.
Protect Cloud SQL for MySQL
In the Cohesity cluster, Google Cloud Cloud SQL for MySQL databases are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy.
Prerequisites
Before you protect Cloud SQL for MySQL databases, ensure that you add the database credentials required to authenticate and connect to the MySQL server. These credentials allow the Cohesity cluster to establish a secure connection, perform the database dump, and complete backup and recovery operations.
Add Database Credentials
You must add credentials at least at the Cloud SQL for MySQL server level. You can also add credentials at any higher level in the hierarchy, such as the region. Credentials added at a higher level automatically apply to all objects beneath it. The Cohesity cluster searches for credentials in a bottom-up manner, starting from the specific entity (for example, a server) and moving up the hierarchy until valid credentials are found. When multiple credentials exist, the credentials closest to the MySQL server take precedence. For example:
l If region-1 has a set of credentials and server-1 under that region has its own, the Cohesity cluster uses the credentials on server-1 to authenticate to server-1.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

l Another server, server-2, under the same region, the Cohesity cluster uses the region-level credentials for authentication because that is the closest level where credentials are specified.

l Select the checkbox next to the MySQL server and click Select All Child Objects.

Additional Settings QoS Policy
Alerts
Priority Description

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.
Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. The Cohesity cluster supports concurrent backups. However, if the number of protection runs exceeds the ability to process runs, this will be the priority of implementation of the protection runs:
a. High-priority protection runs b. Medium-priority protection runs c. Low-priority protection runs
Optional. Enter a brief description about the Protection Group.

GRANT cloudsqlsuperuser,pg_read_all_data,pg_write_all_data TO <username>; ALTER USER <username> WITH CREATEDB; ALTER USER <username> WITH BYPASSRLS;

Considerations for Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL databases:
l Security Privileges Not Restored: Restoring database security privileges is not supported.
l Owner and Privilege Options: You can use the -no-owner and -no-privileges options during restore. The metadata captured during backup is displayed as the owner and ACL details in the restore activity logs.
l Missing Roles Do Not Block Restore: The restore operation does not fail if the owner or role from the source does not exist on the destination instance.
l Post-Restore Role Assignment: After restore, the database is assigned to the role configured in the Cohesity cluster for the destination instance.
l Manual Ownership Updates: You must manually update database ownership after the restore, if required.
l Unsupported Characters in Database Names: The restore workflow does not support the following characters in database names: , @, \, [, ], !, #, %, ^, ., ,, &, *, (, ), <, >, ?, /, |, }, {, ~, :, ', ", ;, +, =, -

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

l Uppercase Usernames Not Supported: Uppercase usernames are not supported for users added after the PostgreSQL server is created.
l Temporary Objects May Cause Backup Failures: Full or differential incremental backups may fail if temporary objects exist. Remove temporary objects manually and retry the backup.
l Version Downgrade Not Supported: Restoring a backup taken from a higher Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database version to a lower version is not supported.
l Objects owned by multiple users: PostgreSQL database may contain objects owned by multiple users. Ensure that the backup user has sufficient privileges to access the tables and other objects owned by all users. Otherwise the backup operations may fail or will be incomplete.
l Cross-region charges: Cross-region backup and recovery operations will incur additional charges as per Google Cloud Platform (GCP) pricing policies and may result in higher overall costs due to data transfer and storage in multiple regions.

Additional Settings QoS Policy
Alerts
Priority Description

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.
Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. The Cohesity cluster supports concurrent backups. However, if the number of protection runs exceeds the ability to process runs, this will be the priority of implementation of the protection runs:
a. High-priority protection runs b. Medium-priority protection runs c. Low-priority protection runs
Optional. Enter a brief description about the Protection Group.
