AlloyDB for PostgreSQL
Cohesity natively integrates with Google Cloud to provide a simple, fast, and cost-effective solution for backup, recovery, and data management of Google Cloud databases, including AlloyDB for PostgreSQL.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

Important: The backup and recovery of Google Cloud AlloyDB for PostgreSQL is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP.
This chapter includes the following topics:
Plan and Prepare AlloyDB for PostgreSQL Data Protection To protect AlloyDB for PostgreSQL databases with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your Google Cloud environment as a source in the Cohesity cluster and perform backup and recovery operations. The following table lists the requirements are grouped into those needed only for source registration and those needed for both backup and restore.

Requirement Network Connectivity
Allowlisted Domains

When Needed
Source registration, backup/restore
Source registration, backup/restore

Database User

Backup and restore

Details
Ensure that you open the specified ports in the firewall to allow the Cohesity cluster to transmit and receive data.
Allowlist the following FQDNs for source registration and data protection operations:
l https://accounts.google.com/ l https://www.googleapis.com/ l https://storage.googleapis.com l https://vpcaccess.googleapis.com/ l https://cloudfunctions.googleapis.com/ l https://cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com/
Cohesity requires PostgreSQL user credentials to perform backup and recovery operations on AlloyDB for PostgreSQL databases. You can use the AlloyDB cluster admin user or create a dedicated database user with the required privileges for backup and recovery operations.

Create a Custom Database User
Cohesity requires PostgreSQL user credentials to discover databases in an AlloyDB for PostgreSQL cluster, retrieve database size information, and perform backup and recovery operations. You can use the AlloyDB cluster admin credentials or create a dedicated database user with the required privileges and provide those credentials to the Cohesity cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

These credentials allow the Cohesity cluster to establish a secure connection to the AlloyDB cluster, perform database dumps, and complete backup and recovery operations. To create a custom database user:
1. Log in to the AlloyDB for PostgreSQL cluster using a user with administrative privileges. Create a database user by running the following command:
2. CREATE USER <username> WITH PASSWORD '<password'>; 3. Assign the following permissions to the database user.
GRANT alloydbsuperuser, pg_read_all_data, pg_write_all_data TO <username>; ALTER USER <username> WITH CREATEDB; ALTER USER <username> WITH BYPASSRLS;
Create an IAM Custom Role in GCP
To enable AlloyDB for PostgreSQL data protection, you must create an IAM custom role in Google Cloud and assign it to the service account used by the Cohesity cluster. For detailed instructions, refer to the following topics in the Google Cloud documentation:
l Create a custom IAM role l Assign a role to a service account
Note: Before you begin creating IAM custom role, ensure that you have created a dedicated service account in Google Cloud for the Cohesity cluster.
Considerations for AlloyDB for PostgreSQL Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect AlloyDB for PostgreSQL databases:
l Security Privileges Not Restored: Restoring database security privileges is not supported.
l Owner and Privilege Options: You can use the -no-owner and -no-privileges options during restore. The metadata captured during backup is displayed as the owner and ACL details in the restore activity logs.
l Missing Roles Do Not Block Restore: The restore operation does not fail if the owner or role from the source does not exist on the destination instance.
l Post-Restore Role Assignment: After restore, the database is assigned to the role configured in the Cohesity cluster for the destination instance.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

l Manual Ownership Updates: You must manually update database ownership after the restore, if required.
l Unsupported Characters in Database Names: The restore workflow does not support the following characters in database names: , @, \, [, ], !, #, %, ^, ., ,, &, *, (, ), <, >, ?, /, |, }, {, ~, :, ', ", ;, +, =, -
l Uppercase Usernames Not Supported: Uppercase usernames are not supported for users added after the AlloyDB PostgreSQL instance is created.
l Temporary Objects May Cause Backup Failures: Full or differential incremental backups may fail if temporary objects exist. Remove temporary objects manually and retry the backup.
l Version Downgrade Not Supported: Restoring a backup taken from a higher AlloyDB for PostgreSQL database version to a lower version is not supported.
l Cluster visibility: Only cluster with primary instances are displayed. Clusters without any instances are not displayed, even if the cluster exists.
l Cross-region charges: Cross-region backup and recovery operations will incur additional charges as per Google Cloud Platform (GCP) pricing policies and may result in higher overall costs due to data transfer and storage in multiple regions.
Backup AlloyDB for PostgreSQL Databases
After registering your Google Cloud source in the Cohesity cluster, it uses the provided service account credentials (JSON key or email and private key) to authenticate with Google Cloud.
Once authenticated, it automatically discovers all projects that the service account can access, as well as all supported workloads such as AlloyDB for PostgreSQL databases within those projects. The discovered workloads appear under Data Protection > Sources. When you open the registered Google Cloud source, each workload type is displayed on its own tab. Select the AlloyDB for PostgreSQL tab to view all the discovered databases.
The AlloyDB for PostgreSQL tab displays the entity hierarchy for the AlloyDB for PostgreSQL environment, allowing you to navigate from the project level down to individual databases.

Backup Scope by AlloyDB for PostgreSQL Hierarchy
Cohesity cluster allows you to back up AlloyDB for PostgreSQL databases at different levels of the hierarchy. You can choose to back up:
l Individual database: Back up a single database. l Multiple databases within a region: Back up selected databases from the same
region. l Region level: Back up all databases within a specific region. l Multiple databases across regions: Back up selected databases from different
regions. l Project level: Back up all databases in all regions within the specified Project ID.
AlloyDB for PostgreSQL Backup Process
When you run a protection job for AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, the Cohesity cluster performs a full backup of the databases specified in the Protection Group. The Cohesity cluster connects to the selected Cloud SQL instance using the database credentials you provided during

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

source registration and uses standard PostgreSQL backup utilities, such as pgdump, to export the complete database contents to the cluster.

Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports only full backups for AlloyDB for PostgreSQL databases. Incremental backups are not supported.
Protect AlloyDB for PostgreSQL
In the Cohesity cluster, Google Cloud AlloyDB for PostgreSQL databases are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy.
Prerequisites
Before you protect AlloyDB for PostgreSQL databases, ensure that you add the database credentials required to authenticate and connect to the AlloyDB cluster. These credentials allow the Cohesity cluster to establish a secure connection, perform the database dump, and complete backup and recovery operations.
Add Database Credentials
You must add credentials at least at the AlloyDB cluster level. You can also add credentials at any higher level in the hierarchy, such as the region. Credentials added at a higher level automatically apply to all objects beneath it. When multiple credentials exist in the hierarchy, the credentials closest to the AlloyDB cluster take precedence. For example:
l If region-1 has a set of credentials and cluster-1 under that region has its own, the Cohesity cluster uses the credentials on cluster-1 to authenticate to cluster-1.
l Another cluster, cluster-2, under the same region, the Cohesity cluster uses the region-level credentials for authentication because that is the closest level where credentials are defined.

Considerations for Cloud SQL for SQL Server Data Protection
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect Cloud SQL for SQL Server databases:
l Logical Backups Only: Snapshot-based backups are not supported. l Backup Coverage: Only user databases are supported. Backups of read-only
databases or databases running in single-user mode are not supported.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 10: Cloud Platforms

GCP

l Recovery Behavior: Databases can be recovered only as new databases. Crossregion and cross-account recoveries are not supported.
l Version Downgrade Not Supported: Restoring a backup taken from a higher Cloud SQL for SQL Server database version to a lower version is not supported.
l Cross-region charges: Cross-region backup and recovery operations will incur additional charges as per Google Cloud Platform (GCP) pricing policies and may result in higher overall costs due to data transfer and storage in multiple regions.

Cloud SQL for SQL Server Backup Process
When you run a protection job in the Cohesity cluster to back up Cloud SQL for SQL Server databases, the databases specified in the Protection Group are first exported from Cloud SQL for SQL Server to a staging bucket in Google Cloud Storage. The Cohesity cluster then copies the data from the staging bucket to the cluster. After the backup completes successfully, the contents of the staging bucket are deleted to free up storage.

Supported Backup Types
Cohesity supports both full backup and incremental backups for Cloud SQL for SQL Server databases.
Protect Cloud SQL for SQL Server
In the Cohesity cluster, Google Cloud Cloud SQL for SQL Server databases are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy.

Alerts

Description
Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Recover Cloud SQL for SQL Server Databases
You can restore Cloud SQL for SQL Server databases either to their original GCP source or to a different GCP source and region.
Cloud SQL for SQL Server Recovery Process
When you run a recovery job in the Cohesity cluster, one or more selected Cloud SQL for SQL databases backups are exported to a Google Cloud Storage staging bucket. The staging bucket temporarily stores the exported data before it is ingested into Cloud SQL for SQL deployment. After the export completes, Google Cloud automatically copies the data from the staging bucket to the Cloud SQL for SQL deployment. Once ingestion is successful, the contents of the staging bucket are then automatically deleted to free up storage and reduce costs.

l A staging bucket is available in Google Cloud Storage. Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

l If recovering to a new location: Ensure that you have added the database credentials for the Cloud SQL for SQL Server instance to which the data will be restored.

Description

l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Protection Groups.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve a similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
(Available only if the selected policy has at least one Quiet Time) When enabled, all the protection runs that are currently executing will cancel when the Quiet Time period starts. By default, this setting is disabled, meaning that after a protection run starts, it continues to execute even when a Quiet Time period starts. However, new protection runs will not start during a Quiet Time.

Field

Description

Primary Copy

Select Local from the drop-down to keep the primary copy data on the Cohesity cluster.
Select any external target for performing CloudArchive Direct wherein the primary copy of the data is stored on the external targets. For more information, see CloudArchive Direct.

DataLock

If applicable, add a DataLock for compliance and regulatory requirements, to ensure that your protected data, including local backups, archives, and replication, cannot be modified until the DataLock expiration.
Once applied, a DataLocked Snapshot will be deleted only after its retention period expires. A DataLock prevents all users, including those who have the Data Security role in Cohesity, from modifying or deleting any Snapshots that were generated by the Protection Groups that use this Policy. Only users with the Data Security role can add, modify, or remove a DataLock from a Policy.

Scheduled Backup

Defines when backups are captured, how long they are retained and the type of backup to capture.

Extended Retention

Add this to retain a subset of snapshots (backups) for longer than defined by the protection schedule.

Retry Options

Use this option to customize the retry settings for capturing Snapshots. By default, Cohesity attempts to capture Snapshots three times before the Protection Group fails. The default time between retries is five minutes. You can customize the number of retries and how long to wait between each attempt.

Periodic full backup

Use this option to choose when to run a periodic full backup.

Quiet Times

Quiet Times defines time periods when new protection runs are not started. For example, you might want to configure hourly backups that run during weekdays but not on Saturday or Sunday. Quiet Times only prevents new protection runs from starting during the specified time period.
The protection runs that started before the quiet time period will be dependent on the quiet time settings configured in the additional settings of the protection Group.
For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time period that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet time period.

Replication

To replicate snapshots to another cluster, click the Replication icon from the floating menu. The copied snapshots are stored in the storage domain of the remote cluster. .

Archival

To add an archive schedule, click archival icon from the floating menu.

Delete the Protection Group
Cohesity provides the following ways to delete the Protection Group associated with the AS3-compatible storage buckets:
l Delete Protection Group Only: Delete only the Protection Group. Any local snapshots and or archived snapshots stored on the external targets that were captured by this Protection Group are not deleted
l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots: Delete the Protection Group and all Snapshots, any local Snapshots captured by this Protection Group and stored on this cluster are deleted. l Delete Protection Group Only l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots
If the current Protection Group is replicating snapshots to a remote cluster or archiving snapshots to an external target, you should cancel these replication or archive tasks before deleting the Protection Group. For instructions, see Cancel Replication and Archive Copy Tasks of a Protection Group Run. If the Protection Group is replicating to a remote cluster, the inactive job created on the remote cluster is not deleted. In addition, the snapshots that were replicated (copied) to the remote cluster by this job are not deleted. You can log in to the remote cluster to delete the snapshots and the inactive job.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines
Cohesity unifies fragmented data protection solutions for virtualized environments. With Cohesity, organizations no longer need to deal with complex and expensive protection solutions that result in multiple infrastructure silos and copies of data.
Cohesity supports backing up Virtual Machines (VMs) from different hosts in a single Protection Group. Protection Groups can run repetitively on a schedule.
To learn more about the relationship between Protection Groups and Policies, see Manage Protection Policy. For instructions on how to use the Cohesity Dashboard to back up VMs, see Manage Protection Groups.
For example, you could create a Protection Group with a protection schedule that backs up all critical VMware VMs every hour as represented by the Critical Protection Group in the following figure and a second Protection Group that backs up important systems every night as represented by the Important Protection Group in the following figure. Note that the Critical Protection Group is a mix of VMs from the Engineering ESXi Host and the IT ESXi Host.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

About Encrypted VM Backup

During a Protection Group Run, Snapshots of the VMs are saved on the Cohesity cluster with a date and time stamp. If a VM is unavailable when the Protection Group runs, a Snapshot is not created for that VM in the Protection Group as shown by the 03/20/2015 01:55 AM protection run in the Important Protection Group. In this example, a Snapshot of VMDK3 is not created by the 03/20/2015 01:55 AM protection run because VM3 was unavailable when the Protection Group ran. If the VM becomes available at a later date, the next time the Protection Group runs a Snapshot of the VM is included in the Protection Group as shown by the 03/21/2015 01:55 AM Protection Group Run for the Important Protection Group.
For instructions on how to use the Cohesity Dashboard to back up VMs, see Add or Edit a Protection Group for Virtual Servers.
About Encrypted VM Backup
Cohesity supports backing up VMware VMs encrypted by a VMware storage policy. A single Protection Group can back up both encrypted and unencrypted VMs.
The VMware user account designated for data protection requires additional privileges to back up encrypted VMs. For more information, see Role Privileges for vCenter Server.
A Protection Group performs the following actions:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Plan and Prepare for VM Protection

1. Connects to the vCenter using an account with the proper privileges. 2. Takes a snapshot of encrypted VMs. 3. Decrypts and backs up data to the cluster. 4. Optionally, the backed-up data is encrypted. The recovered VM from the backup will be decrypted. You must re-enable encryption after recovery by applying an appropriate storage policy.
Plan and Prepare for VM Protection
This topic provides information on minimum permissions, prerequisites and considerations to protect VMware VMs and Hypervisors with the Cohesity cluster.
Minimum Permissions
Ensure you have the required minimum permissions to register VMware VMs and Hypervisors as a source with the Cohesity, and to perform backup and recovery. For more information, see Ensure Adequate Privileges for Cohesity on the Source.
Support Matrix
Before you register your VMware VMs and Hypervisors with the Cohesity cluster, ensure that Cohesity supports the VMware VMs and Hypervisor versions. For more information, see Supported Software.
Ports Used for Communication
Ensure all necessary ports are open in the firewall between the Cohesity cluster and VMware VMs and Hypervisors. For more information, see Manage Firewall Ports.
Prerequisites and Considerations
Standalone ESXi Hosts Review the following considerations:
l Throttling l SQL backup, clone or restore l File recovery to source l Instant volume mount l You must manually configure Storage vMotion.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Plan and Prepare for VM Protection

VMware Snapshots
Prerequisite
Cohesity and VMware recommend limiting the number of delta files in a snapshot chain. For more information, see Best practices for virtual machine snapshots in the VMware environment (1025279). You may want to consider disk consolidation.
Considerations
The Cohesity cluster creates snapshots of VMware VMs. The limitations that apply to VMware snapshots also apply to Cohesity cluster snapshots. These limitations are described in VMware Snapshot limitations.
Review the following snapshot considerations:
l During Protection Group runs, the Cohesity cluster can report The virtual machine requires manual consolidation alerts when attempts to consolidate data in VMs fails due to VMware issues such as locking issues and timeouts. During the next run, the Cohesity cluster will attempt to consolidate the data in each VM but if the cluster is unable to consolidate the data in a VM, the cluster will continue to report The virtual machine requires manual consolidation alerts and skip backing up those VMs with this issue. However, the rest of the VMs in the Protection Group will be backed up. For the Cohesity cluster to start backing up the VMs with this issue, you must perform a manual workaround as described in the Unable to delete the virtual machine snapshot due to locked files (2017072) Knowledge Base issue. Cohesity recommends attempting consolidation by right-clicking the VM and selecting Snapshot >Consolidate as explained in the note of step#2. If that does not fix the problem, try restarting the management agents on the ESXi hosts where the VMs are running as described in step#5 and right-click the VM and select Snapshot >Consolidate as explained in the note of step#2.
l Registering a VMware source or protecting VMware VMs on Wide Area Networks (WAN) is not supported. Cohesity recommends using a Cohesity cluster (Virtual or Cloud Edition) with LAN connectivity to the vCenter and ESXi Host to register and protect the VMs.
l Registering a vCenter source and using it for Data Protection on multiple Cohesity clusters is not recommended. Cohesity clusters running in parallel may deplete vCenter's resources (such as API sessions, API calls, network bandwidth, computing power, memory, IO resources, number of tasks, and much more) as resource usage is not coordinated across Cohesity clusters. If you want to protect portions of your vCenter, Cohesity suggests registering the corresponding Standalone ESXi host(s) to the Cohesity clusters rather than registering the entire vCenter.
l Registering VMware vCenter or ESXi hosts through intermediaries is not supported.
l Creating snapshots of fault-tolerant VMs is not supported by VMware vSphere or the Cohesity cluster. Cohesity clusters will not display fault-tolerant VMs among the list of protectable VMs discovered from the vCenter.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Plan and Prepare for VM Protection

l Creating snapshots of VMs with PCI vSphere DirectPath I/O devices is not supported by VMware vSphere or the Cohesity cluster.
l Creating snapshots of VMs with SR-IOV (Single Root I/O Virtualization) is not supported by the Cohesity cluster.
l When a VM with independent disks is protected, the independent disks are automatically skipped and the rest of the disks are backed up. After recovering or cloning these VMs from a Cohesity backup, you must manually attach the independent disks.
l Recovery of a VMware VM to a different vCenter does not attach tags of the original VM to the restored VM.

This means the same ESXi host was registered on vCenter in "lockdown" mode.

It is not supported for standalone ESXi sources. l Cohesity does not support application-consistent backups of VMware VMs that leverage Nutanix as the storage snapshot provider. l Cohesity does not support differential restore of VMware VMs backed by leveraging the storage snapshots. l If the protection run of VMware VMs is switched from VADP-based backup to storage snapshot-based backup, then the Cohesity cluster will initiate a full backup. l While performing storage snapshot-based backup, if a VMware VM snapshot is present on the ESXi host, then Cohesity will perform VADP backup. l Cohesity does not support leveraging storage snapshots for backing up VM templates.

Tip: You can also watch the Registering a VMware Source video to learn how to register a VMware vCenter Server or a Standalone ESXi host as a source.

Field Name
Latency Based Adaptive Throttling

Description
For VMware vCenter only. Toggle this setting on if you want the Cohesity cluster to adaptively throttle the running of tasks created by the Protection Groups protecting this source. This throttling helps to ensure that the datastores on the source (vCenter Server) are not adversely affected by the Protection Groups. You specify latency thresholds and if the observed latency on the datastore is greater than the specified threshold, the Cohesity cluster throttles the processing of the backup using that datastore as explained below.

Note:
l

Enabling throttling can increase how much time a Protection Group run takes to complete, resulting in SLA violations. You may want to increase the SLA for the Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Groups.

l Latency-based adaptive throttling is ineffective while leveraging storage array snapshots for VMware backups.

Specify the latency thresholds in milliseconds.
If you enable throttling, the following two fields appear:
l Latency Threshold for throttling the new tasks of Protection Group Runs--If the observed latency of a datastore is greater than the specified latency threshold, the Cohesity cluster throttles the processing of new backup tasks using that datastore. Throttling can occur in the middle of a protection run. For example, tasks creating the first snapshots of the protection run could complete without throttling but after the threshold is reached, the tasks creating the remaining Snapshots in the protection run are throttled.
l Latency Threshold for throttling the currently running tasks of Protection Group Runs--If the observed latency of a datastore is greater than the specified latency threshold, the Cohesity cluster throttles any currently running backup tasks using that datastore.
If throttling is enabled, the vCenter user specified for the source must have administrative datastore privileges.
When throttling is enabled and the vCenter user has the necessary administrative datastore privileges, the Cohesity cluster enables the collection of Storage IO Control (SIOC) statistics on the datastores if not already enabled. The Cohesity cluster uses the statistics from SIOC to calculate the observed latency of datastores. If throttling and the collection of SIOC statistics were initially enabled and then throttling is disabled, the Cohesity cluster does not change the SIOC collection statistic settings on the datastores.

Field Name Cap concurrent streams per Datastore
Cap concurrent VM Backups
Auto Cancel Backups if Datastore is running low on space

Description
Toggle this setting on if you want to limit the number of streams concurrently backed up per datastore. This helps to reduce any performance impact on the datastore. When registering a vCenter, you can configure the Number of Streams for all datastores in the vCenter only. After a vCenter is registered and the datastores in the vCenter are discovered, you can add overrides for individual datastores by clicking Add Datastore Override. Select a datastore, toggle on Cap and enter the number of Streams. If you toggle off Cap for a datastore, it is not subject to the vCenter's global concurrent streams cap.
Toggle this setting on if you want to limit the number of VMs of a vCenter to be backed up concurrently. In the Number of VM Backups field, you can set the number of VMs that can be backed up concurrently.
Turn this toggle ON if you want to set the minimum free space that should always be available in the datastore. Once set, Cohesity automatically prevents backups from starting if the datastore does not meet this requirement. Enter the minimum free space needed in the GiB or % fields. For example, if you enter 10 in the % field, 10% of the datastore space will always be available. The percentage option is more flexible because it auto-adjusts when the datastore shrinks or expands, even if a VM has multiple datastores. Which means, if two virtual disks of a VM reside in datastores of size 500 GB and 1 TB each, 10% of free space will apply to both the datastores.

Field Name

Description

Set Last Backup detail

For VMware vCenter only: Toggle this setting ON to set the last backup time and backup status for a VM in vCenter. These are published as custom attributes. By default, the option is turned OFF.
When a backup is performed on a vCenter with the feature enabled, the custom attributes "Last Cohesity Backup Attempt Time" and "Last Cohesity Backup Status" will be set or updated to reflect the backup time and status.
l Last Cohesity Backup Attempt - The exact timestamp when the last backup attempt succeeded.
l Last Cohesity Backup Status - Status of the last backup for each VM.

Note: When performing VM-based backups, if the backup is successful but has warnings caused by implicit fallbacks such as failure to utilize storage snapshots or issues with deleting the VM snapshot (which is a time-consuming operation), we will set the last backup status as 'Success' since the VM was successfully backed up. However, if there are errors or warnings due to explicit fallbacks (for example, transitioning from SAN to NBDSSL, or from app consistent to crash consistent), we will update the backup status to accurately reflect the error or warning.

Use VM BIOS UUID to track virtual machines

Toggle this setting on if you want the Cohesity cluster to track VMs using a unique BIOS UUID. You must enable the BIOS UUIDs toggle to support integration with Zerto--a continuous data protection (CDP) product. In addition, you must configure Zerto to preserve the BIOS UUIDs upon recovery. If both products are using BIOS UUIDS to uniquely identify VMs, VMs can be restored by either of the products and the link back to the original VM is not lost.
To protect a VM in the vCenter with this toggle on, all VMs must have a unique BIOS UUID. If the Cohesity cluster finds more than one VM with the same BIOS UUIDs, these VMs are not listed when selecting VMs to protect.

Important: This option must be set when you initially register a vCenter. After the vCenter has been registered, you cannot edit the hypervisor source and change this setting.

To configure Zerto to also use BIOS UUIDs, select Site Settings. Under Policies > Replication select For incoming replication, copy the BIOS UUID of the protected VM to the recovered VM.

Network for Data Transfer

(Applies only to VMware vCenter) Toggle this option on if you want to configure a secondary network for the backup and copy recovery of VMs on the ESXi host of the VMware vCenter, while also using NBDSSL as the transport mode.
By default, this option is turned off. If this option is turned off, the default network will be used for backup and recovery.
Configure a Secondary Network
To configure the secondary network, specify the subnet IP in the Subnet IP field and CIDR prefix in the CIDR prefix field.
When the ESXi host has multiple VMkernel adapters, then Cohesity cluster will use the IP address that belongs to the specified subnet for the backup and recovery of VMs on the ESXi host. To view the updated ESXi hostname to IP address mapping, from the Cohesity Dashboard, select Settings > Cluster > Networking and click the Host Mapping tab.

Note: When ESXi hosts are registered to VMware vCenter using IP addresses instead of hostnames, Host Mapping does not work.

Add Multiple Subnets To add multiple subnets, click the Add icon, and then specify the subnet IP and CIDR prefix. If you add more than one subnet, then the ESXi IP address selected for host mapping will be the one which matches the first subnet in the order they are provided. Example 1: Consider a VMware vCenter having two ESXi hosts and each ESXi has two VM kernel adapters. ESXi-1:
l VM kernel adapter 1: 111.255.190.57 l VM kernel adapter 2: 10.10.33.130 ESXi-2: l VM kernel adapter 1: 111.255.190.51 l VM kernel adapter 2: 10.10.33.120 Consider you have provided the subnet IP as 10.10.33.0 and CIDR as 24. During the backup and restore of VMs under both the ESXi hosts, Cohesity cluster will resolve the hostname of ESXi-1 and ESXi-2 to IP address 10.10.33.130 and 10.10.33.120 respectively since these IP addresses belong to the same subnet you have provided.

Configure Data Services IP for iSCSI Transport You can configure a segmented Data Services IP address for iSCSI transport at both the Prism Element and Prism Central levels to control how backup and recovery traffic flows between the Cohesity cluster and AHV sources. This enhancement provides greater flexibility in separating management and data transport networks for backup and recovery operations. This option is available after the AHV source is registered and can be configured from the Sources > Edit page. To Configure Data Services IP for iSCSI transport: Prerequisite Ensure that the Nutanix AHV sources (Prism Central and/or Prism Element) are already registered on the Cohesity cluster.
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Locate the registered AHV source (Prism Central or Prism Element). 3. Click the Actions ( ) menu for the source and select Edit. 4. On the Edit Source page, select either Use iSCSI Data Services IP (default) or Use segmented iSCSI
Data Services IP. 5. For a Prism Central source, select the Prism Elements that should use the segmented Data Services IP,
and leave others unselected to continue using the default IP. 6. For a Prism Element source, select the required option, Use iSCSI Data Services IP (default) or Use
segmented iSCSI Data Services IP. 7. Enter the required credentials if prompted. 8. Click Save.
During backup, recovery, and copy operations, the selected Data Services IP is used for iSCSI transport. For Prism Central, the transport selection applies at the Prism Element level. Backup and recovery operations record the transport IP used in the audit logs.

Download and Install the Cohesity Agent on Hyper-V Hosts
Ensure you install the Cohesity agent on any Hyper-V hosts that you want Cohesity to protect.
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click Download Cohesity Agent. Ensure the agent has been downloaded to the
appropriate hosts. 3. As an administrator with local system privileges, run the executable and complete the
installation wizard. For Hyper-V 2016 servers, install the agent without additional components. For incremental backups of individual VMs hosted by Hyper-V on Windows Server 2012 R2, install the File System CBT (Changed Block Tracker) component. 4. The agent starts automatically.
Guest Windows VM minimum recommended specifications: 2 GB RAM and the equivalent of a 1 GHz processor. Best practice: For Hyper-V 2016, configure all VMs' Automatic Stop Action to shut down or turn off, instead of save. This results in all powered-on VMs having minimal size .vmrs files. Because Cohesity does not back up .vmrs files that are greater than 10 MB (.vmrs file size, if set to save, scales to the amount of memory assigned to the VM). VMs in the saved state, by definition, generally have .vmrs files greater than 10 MB. This Cohesity Windows Agent registry value entry determines the maximum size of the .vmrs file supported per backup: agent_hyperv_max_vm_config_file_size_mb. Set it to zero to back up .vmrs files of all sizes.
Register a Hyper-V Source with the Cohesity cluster
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Select Register > Virtual Machines. 3. From the Select Hypervisor Source Type drop-down, select the hypervisor source
type and complete the fields. The available options are: l HyperV: SCVMM Server l HyperV: Standalone Host l HyperV: Failover Cluster
For detailed registration steps, see Register or Edit a Hypervisor Source. 1. Click Register.
After registration is completed, ensure the Cohesity cluster is joined to an Active Directory domain as described in Join Active Directory, which is required for Hyper-V VM backup and recovery. Now Cohesity can back up any Hyper-V hosts where the Cohesity agent is installed.

User Account Requirements for VM Protection
Specific user account configuration is required for the following operations:
l The user account that is used for auto-deploying agents in a Windows VMware environment must have administrator privileges on the VM where the agent is deployed. The account must have the "sysadmin" Server Role. If the Windows Firewall is used, add an inbound rule to accept the Cohesity Agent and TCP connections on local port 50051. Port 50051 may have limited requirements. It is needed for application integration, but not required for File-Level Recovery or Instant Volume Mount operations.
If the operation fails with an error indicating insufficient privileges, then check if the user account used for this operation allows remote command execution without a UAC prompt. Otherwise, use a persistent agent or other suitable recovery methods, if applicable.
Register a Storage Snapshot Provider
Cohesity can leverage the snapshots from the following storage snapshot providers:
l Cisco HyperFlex l Nimble Storage, HPE Alletra 5000, and/or HPE Alletra 6000 l NetApp ONTAP l Nutanix l Pure Storage Array l IBM FlashSystem
You can leverage snapshots only for VMware backups from the preceding storage snapshot providers. To leverage the storage snapshots, you must:
1. Register the snapshot providers with the Cohesity cluster. See the following sections on how to register the above snapshot providers.
2. Enable the Leverage Storage Snapshots for Data Protection field and select the storage snapshot provider from the drop-down when creating the Protection Group. For more information, see Add or Edit a Protection Group for Virtual Servers.
Considerations
l You can leverage only one storage snapshot provider for a Protection Group. l For IBM FlashSystem, Nimble Storage, HPE Alletra 5000, HPE Alletra 6000 and Pure
Storage, VMFS datastores are supported. l For NetApp, NFS 3 and NFS 4.1 datastores are supported. l Cohesity cannot leverage storage snapshots when VM has disks on volumes of
different storage systems.

For example, if you select this option for a Protection Group that backs up an ESXi host and that ESXi host is where cloned VMs are created, the new cloned VMs are also backed up the next time the Protection Group runs. You may want to edit the original Protection Group and explicitly exclude the new cloned VMs.
Note: In the Cohesity Dashboard, users with a restricted role (such as operator) cannot access the runs of a Protection Group for leaf objects (such as VMs) that were backed up because a higher level object (such as a datacenter) was auto-protected, even if that user has permissions to access those leaf objects. Cohesity supports assigning permissions to leaf level object such as VMs. Cohesity currently does not support assigning permissions to higher level objects such as a datacenter and since autoprotection is applied higher level objects, access is denied.

14. Defer Incomplete Objects in Concurrent Runs: (Applies only to VMware VMs) A Protection Group can protect both small (for example, 1 GB VM) and large VMs (for example, 1 TB VM). While a short VM usually completes its protection runs within a few minutes, a large VM might take longer and still be running when it's time for the next run. By default, when it's time to start the next run, the Cohesity cluster checks for any in-progress protection run in that Protection Group. If there are in-progress protection runs (typically a large VM), the Cohesity cluster cancels the next run for that Protection Group, causing the small VMs to also miss that run and the SLA. When the Defer Incomplete Objects in Concurrent Runs option is enabled, if there is an in-progress protection run, the Cohesity cluster postpones the subsequent run only for that VM. The postponed run resumes as soon as the current run is completed. The protection runs of the remaining VMs (typically small VMs) in that Protection Group are not affected and run on schedule.
For example, Protection Group PG1 runs every 8 hours to protect VMs A, B, and C. When the first protection run starts, A and B complete running in a few minutes. VM C, a large VM, needs 12 hours to complete running. If Defer Incomplete Objects in Concurrent Runs is disabled for PG1, when it's time for the second run, the Cohesity cluster cancels the second run in all three VMs because C is still in progress. However, the third run completes in all three VMs. Because C is a large VM, A and B miss every alternate run.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Add or Edit a Protection Group for Virtual Servers

If Defer Incomplete Objects in Concurrent Runs is enabled for PG1, when it's time for the second run, the Cohesity cluster starts the second run in A and B but postpones the run in C. C's second run resumes when its first run completes. As a result, A, B, and C do not miss any scheduled runs.
If PG1 also protects VM D, another large VM, which needs 20 hours to complete, when it's time for the second run, the Cohesity cluster postpones D's second run. When it's time for the third run, because D's first run is still in progress, the Cohesity cluster cancels its second run but postpones its third run. D's next run will resume automatically when its ongoing run completes.

When the Cohesity cluster cancels the backup task of an object (such as D) in the Protection Group (such as PG1), the Protection Group Details page displays the following message at the corresponding protection run:
"Failed to back up some of the objects in the protection run as they are already backed in another protection run. ".
At the corresponding task (D's second backup task), the following message is displayed:
"cancelled the backup task of this object as it is already being backup up by another protection run."
Enabling the Defer Incomplete Objects in Concurrent Runs option helps you meet the defined SLAs, and improves the efficiency of the scheduled runs, thereby enhancing the backup performance.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

snapshot by invoking VMware Tools/Nutanix Guest Tools (installed on the guest operating systems of the VM). The VMware Tools/Nutanix Guest Tools requests that applications on the guest OS quiesce their state so that application-consistent snapshots can be created. Quiescing of VMs before capturing snapshots ensures the integrity of the data saved in the snapshots.
If the Cohesity cluster fails to capture an app-consistent snapshot, you can use the Take a Crash Consistent backup if unable to perform an App Consistent backup option to capture a crash-consistent snapshot. The option is available only if the App-Consistent backups option is enabled.
For example, the Cohesity cluster may fail to perform an app-consistent backup for the following reasons: when VMware Tools/Nutanix Guest Tools is not installed on the VM, the VM (VMware) is powered off, or if the VM cannot be quiesced. If the Take a Crash Consistent backup if unable to perform an App Consistent backup is enabled in that Cohesity cluster, a crash-consistent snapshot is captured.
Note: App-consistent backups apply to VMs only. For physical servers, Windows is app-consistent by default and Linux is crash-consistent. For more information, see Creating Application-Consistent Snapshots.

Protection for NVRAM files
The NVRAM (non-volatile random-access memory) file of a VMware VM stores the boot drive setting and, in the case of multiple disks, the boot order. As VMware recommends, Cohesity automatically backs up the NVRAM file when backing up its VM.
Note: It is important to back up the NVRAM file if you created the VM with the Virtual Trusted Platform Module (vTPM).
Supported Workloads Cohesity supports the backup and recovery of NVRAM files when backing up VMware VMs.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Add or Edit a Protection Group for Virtual Servers

NVRAM backup and recovery is available for VMC, VCD, Storage Array Snapshot Arrays, Snapshot Integration, Archival, Replication, and Cloud Spins.
Troubleshooting with NVRAM Files
Errors
You might run into the following error scenarios when protecting VMware VMs:
l The backup of the VM(s) is successful, but the status of the protection run is set to "warning" and the VM fails to start.
l The VM(s) recovery is successful, but the VM fails to start. l If the NVRAM file is missing for a recovered VM (which can happen if the backup was
taken before upgrading the Cohesity cluster to 7.1), VMware will create a new NVRAM file with default settings. While this new file would suffice to start any VM, the VM might not start if the BIOS or UEFI settings were customized before recovery. For example, if you've modified the OS boot path, this setting will not be present in the newly created NVRAM file causing the VM to not start.
Solution
Follow these steps to start the VM by replacing its NVRAM file with the downloaded NVRAM file:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Recoveries. 2. Select Recover and then choose Virtual Machines from the menu. 3. Select the VM whose NVRAM file you want to download. 4. Perform one of the following:
1. If you've protected the NVRAM file, click the Actions Menu ( ) of that VM and select Download NVRAM File. The NVRAM file is downloaded to your local system.
2. If you have not protected the NVRAM file, download the NVRAM file from the original VM in the vCenter.
5. Ensure the name of the downloaded NVRAM file is the same as the NVRAM file in the recovered VM.
6. Replace the NVRAM file in the recovered VM with the NVRAM file downloaded in step 4.
7. Restart the VM.
Considerations
l If you are protecting a VM equipped with vTPM, enable the Manage KMS privilege in the vCenter for the user account registered with Cohesity.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Add or Edit a Protection Group for Virtual Servers

l If you are recovering a VM equipped with vTPM using a different KMS or replacing the current KMS with a new one, the vTPM VMs may not start after the recovery process, even if the new KMS has the same name.
l The supported maximum size of the NVRAM file is 10 MB. Contact your Cohesity account team if your NVRAM files are larger than 10 MB.
l Restoring the NVRAM file from the encrypted VMs is not supported, except for vTPM encryption.
Protection for vSphere DataSets files
The VM configuration files and vSphere DataSets files are stored together, and a reference to the DataSet (.dsd) is written into the virtual machine configuration file (.vmx). The datasets of the VM are stored within the DataSets file. The DataSets files are denoted with a .dsd extension and are stored alongside the VM configuration files. The maximum size of the DataSets file is 300 MB. Cohesity clusters now automatically back up the VM's DataSets file while protecting a VM and also allow you to recover the DataSets file. DataSets file functionality is available in vSphere 8.0 and requires the VM to be running virtual hardware version 20.
Supported Workloads
Cohesity supports the backup and recovery of DataSets files when backing up VMware VMs. vSphere DataSets file backup and recovery is available for VADP, Storage Array Snapshot Arrays, and HCI integration.
Troubleshooting with DataSets files
Errors
You might run into the following error scenarios when protecting VMware VMs:
l The backup task will raise a warning if the DataSets files are not backed up sccessfully.
l The restore task will raise a warning if the DataSets files are not restored successfully.
Considerations
l The maximum size of a DataSets file can be up to 300 MB. In most cases, the DataSets file size will be a few MBs. Contact your Cohesity account team if the files exceed 300 MB.
l Restoring the DataSets file from the encrypted VMs is not supported, except for vTPM encryption.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Nutanix AHV
Cohesity supports backup and restore of vTPM metadata. It also supports backup of directly attached Volume Groups for Nutanix AHV VMs. AHV Virtual Trusted Platform Module Directly Attached Volume Groups on Nutanix AHV
AHV Virtual Trusted Platform Module (vTPM)
You can now back up Virtual Trusted Platform Module (vTPM) metadata for AHV VMs. During backup, Cohesity records whether vTPM was enabled on the VM. vTPM configuration is backed up and restored only if it is enabled on the source VM at the time the backup is taken. This ensures that the original vTPM configuration is preserved. vTPM metadata is backed up and restored to ensure the security configuration of VMs. vTPM metadata does not include any cryptographic keys or other data stored within the vTPM.
Note: Ensure to manually back up the important cryptographic data stored in the vTPM. the cryptographic data stored in the vTPM module is important, it must be manually backed up by the user.
Directly Attached Volume Groups on Nutanix AHV
Nutanix AHV allows VMs to attach Volume Groups, which are collections of virtual disks exposed to the VM using the iSCSI protocol. Cohesity extends AHV VM protection to include these directly attached Volume Groups. During protection, set the Backup Directly Attached Volume Groups to Yes under Additional Settings to back up the VM along with its directly attached volume groups. On the Activity page, the volume groups that will be backed up are listed. If the option is disabled, the volume groups are displayed as skipped. If backup of directly attached volume groups is enabled but no volume groups are attached to the VM, this status is also reflected on the Activity page. It also displays the Nutanix UUID of the volume disk attached. When enabled, snapshots capture:
l The attached Volume Groups' configuration. l Disks belonging to the attached Volume Groups.
You can also configure disk inclusion and exclusion for volume groups. Disk selection is based on the disk address label. When creating a protection group, select Include or Exclude Disks option, and then specify the disks that you want to include in or exclude from the backup. On the Activity page, the volume groups and disks that are included or excluded from the backup are listed.

Creating Application-Consistent Snapshots
Cohesity supports application-consistent backup for VMware, Nutanix Acropolis, and HyperV. By enabling application-consistent backups for a Protection Group, the guest-operating systems of all the VMs in the Protection Group will be quiesced before snapshots of these VMs are created.
Application-Consistent Snapshots for VMware VMs
Toggle App-Consistent backups for a Protection Group if you want the guest operating systems of all the VMs in the job to be quiesced before snapshots of these VMs are created. If this option is selected, the Cohesity cluster makes a request to the VMware vSphere software to create a quiesced VM snapshot by invoking VMware Tools (installed on the guest operating systems of the VM). The VMware Tools requests that applications on the guest OS quiesce their state so application-consistent snapshots can be created. This quiescing of VMs prior to capturing snapshots ensures the integrity of the data saved in the snapshots.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Creating Application-Consistent Snapshots

App-consistent backups apply to VMs only. For physical servers, Windows is app-consistent by default and Linux is crash-consistent.
Snapshots created without quiescing are known as Crash-Consistent Snapshots.
When the App-Consistent backups toggle is on, all the guest Operating Systems of the protected Objects (VMs) in this Protection Group must have VMware Tools installed. The Cohesity Dashboard prevents you from saving the Protection Group if any selected VMs do not have VMware Tools installed.
If the App-Consistent backups toggle is on, the Take a Crash Consistent backup if unable to perform an App Consistent backup toggle is available. Toggle it on if you want the Cohesity cluster to capture a crash-consistent snapshot if the Cohesity cluster fails to capture an app-consistent snapshot. For example, the Cluster may be unable to perform an app-consistent backup when VMware Tools is not installed on the VM, the VM is powered off, or the VM cannot be quiesced. If the Take a Crash Consistent backup if unable to perform an App Consistent backup toggle is off and the Cohesity cluster is unable to perform an app-consistent backup of a VM, a snapshot is not captured.
If the App-Consistent backups option is selected for a Protection Group and the Job is protecting Linux VMs, the Cohesity cluster invokes the VMware vSphere software to create the Snapshot. For a Linux VM, the VMware vSphere software always reports that the VM was not quiesced because Linux does not provide a system quiescing mechanism like Windows VSS. Because of this VMware behavior, the Cohesity cluster does not check and report on the quiescing return status for Linux VMs. However, other status are checked and reported, for example if Snapshots of VMs are not created, the protection run fails.
If the App-Consistent backups option is selected for the Job, when the Cohesity cluster calls VMware vSphere software to quiesce Linux or Windows VMs, if quiesce custom prefreeze and post-thaw scripts can be found in the correct locations, these scripts are run as part of the quiescing and create Snapshot process. For more information, see the appropriate documentation for the Operating System type:
l Running custom quiescing scripts inside Windows virtual machine with ESX 3.5 Update 2 and later (1006671) Knowledge Base Article
l Configuring Custom Quiesce Scripts for Linux Virtual Machines
Application-Consistent Snapshots for AHV VMs
Toggle App-Consistent backups for a Protection Group if you want the guest operating systems of all the AHV VMs in the Protection Group to be quiesced before snapshots of these VMs are created. If this option is selected, the Cohesity cluster makes a request to the AHV software to create a quiesced VM snapshot by invoking the Nutanix Guest Tools (installed on the guest operating systems of the VM). When you invoke the Nutanix Guest Tools, the VSS and application-consistent snapshot applications are automatically enabled. With these applications enabled, the application-consistent snapshots for all the VMs that support VSS are taken using the Nutanix native in-guest VmQuiesced Snapshot Service (VSS) agent.
Snapshots created without quiescing are known as Crash-Consistent Snapshots.

l Hyper-V Integration Services installed. For more information, see Hyper-V Integration Services.
l Production Checkpoints enabled. For more information, see Enable Production Checkpoints.
If the Cohesity cluster fails to capture an app-consistent snapshot, you can use the Take a Crash Consistent backup if unable to perform an App Consistent backup toggle to capture a crash-consistent snapshot option. This option is available only if the AppConsistent backups toggle is ON. For example, the Cohesity cluster may be unable to perform an app-consistent backup for the following reasons: when Hyper-V Integration Services is not installed or running on the VM, or the VM cannot be quiesced. If the Take a Crash Consistent backup if unable to perform an App Consistent backup toggle is ON for that Cohesity cluster, a crash-consistent snapshot is captured.

Cancel Protection Run at Object Level

Cancel Protection Run at Object Level
You can now cancel the protection run of individual objects within a Protection Group created for VMware vCenter.
Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.

Protection Group States at Granular Level
A Protection Group run can be in the following states: l Protection Group is in progress; where the backup of the objects is in progress. l Protection Group is progress but the backup of a few objects is in failed status. l Protection Group is completed; where the backup of a few objects is failed and a few are success and is waiting in the retry interval time.
Note: Retry is the time you set for the Cohesity cluster to attempt backup before the Protection Group fails. Retry interval time is defined in the Protection Policy along with retry attempts.
l Retry attempts are over and the Protection Group is completed with Success or Failed status.
The protection run cancellation at the object level is applicable for the first three states mentioned above. You cannot cancel the protection run at the object level if the Protection Group run is complete and the retry attempts are over.
Cancel Protection Run at Object Level
To cancel the protection run of individual objects within a Protection Group, perform the following steps:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group.
The Protection page displays the protection runs of the Protection Group. 3. Select the in-progress protection run from which you want to cancel the protection
run of the individual objects. The Run details page displays the list of objects that are protected in the protection run. 4. Perform one of the following actions based on your requirement:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Migrate VMware VMs Using Cohesity

l To cancel the protection run of individual objects, click the actions menu ( ) next to the object and then click Cancel VM.
l To cancel the protection run of multiple objects, select the checkboxes next to the objects and click on the cross icon that appears on the column heading of the Run details page.
Considerations
Consider the following points when canceling the protection run of the objects when the protection run is in progress:
l If you are canceling the protection run of the objects that are being backed up, then the protection run of these objects will get canceled immediately.
l If you are canceling the protection run of the objects whose backups are failed, then the protection run of these objects will get canceled in the next retry attempt. The next retry attempt will happen once the current protection run is complete and retry interval is over.
l If you are canceling the protection run of the failed objects during the retry interval time (while the protection run is waiting for the next retry), then the protection run of these objects will get canceled immediately. For example, consider the following scenario: A Protection Group is created for backing up 10 objects. The retry time set is 5 minutes. During the protection run, l 5 objects (V1, V2, V3, V4, V5) are already backed up and status is success. l 3 objects (V6, V7, V8) are being backed up and the status is in progress. l 2 objects (V9, V10) are failed in backing up and status is failed. Now, if you cancel the protection run of V6, V7, or V8 objects then the protection run of these objects will get canceled immediately. If you cancel the protection run of V9 or V10 objects then the protection run of these objects will get canceled in the next retry attempt. The next retry attempt will happen 5 minutes after the current protection run is complete. If the protection run of V6, V7, and V8 is complete and you cancel the protection run of V9 and V10 during the retry interval time of 5 minutes, then the protection run of these objects would get canceled immediately and the next retry attempt will happen immediately for V9 and V10.
Migrate VMware VMs Using Cohesity
All the VMs that need to be migrated must be protected using one or more Protection Groups in Cohesity. When the initial backup run is started for the Protection Group, Cohesity

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Migrate VMware VMs Using Cohesity

first performs a full backup of the source VMs. Once the initial backup is completed, you can initiate the migration for the source VMware VMs. As a part of the migration, Cohesity creates a standby VM on the target vCenter for each source VM being migrated and restores the backed-up data to these standby VMs. Now, whenever there is an incremental backup, Cohesity migrates only the incremental backed-up data to standby VMs. When you decide to complete the migration, Cohesity will migrate the latest incremental backed-up data to standby VMs and then will stop syncing the data. You can power on the standby VMs once the migration is complete. This reduces the downtime of the VM migration as the cutover time (time between powering off the source VMs and powering on the standby VMs) is minimal.

Cohesity CDP for VMware
To protect your VMware VMs, you can optionally choose to leverage the Continuous Data Protection (CDP) option available on the Cohesity Data Cloud. Cohesity's CDP provides near-zero RPOs for your applications.
Every change to the VM (IOs) is captured and replicated to the Cohesity cluster. This provides a continuous window of protection allowing you to restore a VM to a selected pointin-time within the configured CDP window.
Cohesity uses the VMware API for I/O Filtering (VAIO) based solution for providing Continuous Data Protection. In this process, Cohesity deploys an I/O Filter in a vSphere environment. The scope of the filter installation is at a cluster level (also known as ClusterComputeResouce) within the vCenter. Once the filter installation is complete, an I/O Filter is attached to the VM marked for protection. This filter intercepts all the real-time IOs of the VM and sends the IOs to the Filter Daemon running on the ESXi host. The Filter

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Cohesity CDP for VMware

Daemon continuously replicates the IOs to the Cohesity cluster (IO Journal) based on the VM Storage Policy attached to the VM. In releases earlier than 7.0, the Cohesity cluster automatically deploys the VAIO filter on the ESXi host clusters. From release 7.0 onwards, Cohesity provides an additional option to download the VAIO from the Cohesity cluster and upload it to an HTTP server to deploy it manually on the ESXi host clusters using the vSphere IO filter installation APIs. For details, see Deploy the VAIO Filter Manually. You can either manually create or update an existing VM Storage Policy and then attach it to the VMs or Cohesity will automatically create and attach the VM Storage Policy to the VMs you want to perform continuous data protection. If you are manually attaching the VM Storage Policy, then ensure to:
l Attach a Storage Policy to the VMs before a CDP-enabled Protection Group is created for these VMs.
l While creating the VM Storage Policy, select the Enable host based rules checkbox in the Policy structure tab and create rules for Replication data service under Host based services with the following settings: l Provider: cohfilter l vCenterUUID: <vCenterUUID> l CohesityID: <ClusterId:IncarnationId> l CohesityClusterEndpoint: <endpoint>:20004 l HeartbeatInterval: 30
Note: You can view the default Storage Policy created by Cohesity on the VMware vCenter as a reference for the above settings.
During the backup process, all the IOs of a workload will be saved in a write-ahead-log (WAL), and is used to recover the applications at any point-in-time as long as all the previous IOs are available. If any IOs are missed during the CDP, then a VADP backup is triggered, and the CDP backup process is re-initialized. For better RTO, the hydrated snapshots of the VMs are also captured to the Cohesity cluster every 15 minutes.
Note: When using VMware CDP, disk exclusion settings do not prevent data capture on excluded disks. CDP operates at the I/O level and captures changes across all disks in the VM. CDP backups may fail when disk exclusion is used.

Core Components
This section lists the core components of the Cohesity CDP.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Cohesity CDP for VMware

l I/O Filter: An I/O Filter is run per VM on the ESXi host as part of the Virtual Machine Executable (VMX) process. It intercepts the IOs of a VM synchronously in real-time and replicates those IOs to the Cohesity cluster.
l I/O Filter Daemon: An I/O Filter Daemon, also implemented using VAIO, provides more resources to perform replication, caching, batching, and other operations. It runs in the ESXi host environment and communicates with individual VM's I/O Filters over a Unix socket. An I/O Filter Daemon is ideal for replicating collected IOs from VMs over the network asynchronously.
l Cohesity Data Cloud: The CDP service starts on all the Cohesity cluster nodes and receives the Filter Daemon requests.

For automatic upgrades or uninstallation of filters, a VMware cluster should have Distributed Resource Scheduler (DRS) enabled with shared storage.

Enable Cohesity CDP on VMs
To enable CDP on VMs, create a new protection policy and attach the Continuous Data Protection option to the policy. Within the CDP option specify the retain point in time configuration, and associate this policy with the VM's Protection Group.
After associating the protection policy with the Protection Group, the protection run will first initiate a full VADP-based backup and, in the process, attach the I/O Filter to the ESXi host. An incremental protection run follows the initial full backup, and the VM's continuous protection will begin from this point on. You can view all the continuously protected VMs from the same Dashboard page.
Steps
Perform these tasks to enable CDP for VMs:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Cohesity CDP for VMware

1. Create a Protection Policy with the Continuous Data Protection option.
2. Associate this policy with the VMs' Protection group that you plan to protect using CDP. See Add or Edit a Protection Group for Virtual Servers.
Create a Protection Policy
A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. Also, for Disaster Recovery, you can add CDP and replication for the Protection Group using the Protection Policy.
To create a Protection Policy with CDP & Replication:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Policies.
2. Click Create Policy located at the top right of the page.
The Create Protection Policy page appears.
3. In the Policy Name field, specify a protection policy name. The name can contain alphanumerics, underscores, hyphens, periods, and spaces. This field is required and can be changed later.
4. In the Incremental Backup field, specify when backups are captured, and how long they are retained.
5. Click More Options. 6. Click the Continuous Data Protection option from the floating menu. In the Retain
Point in Time for field, enter a number and select Minute, Hour, or Day from the drop-down. This value defines the period the Cohesity cluster will retain the captured CDP logs. You can use this option to restore the VM applications to a point-in-time as opposed to periodic snapshots available with regular protection runs.
When CDP is enabled for a protection policy, VM IOs are captured continuously and streamed in real time to the local cluster. As a result, data protected by CDP-enabled policies are available on the local cluster with near-zero RPO.
7. Click the Replication icon to replicate snapshots with CDP to another Cohesity cluster. The copied snapshots are stored in the storage domain of the remote cluster. (The storage domain, however, is specified in the Protection Group.) The replication schedule for copying Snapshots cannot be more often than the protection schedule for capturing Snapshots. For example if Snapshots are captured hourly, the Cohesity cluster cannot replicate them every 30 minutes but it can replicate them hourly or any value over one hour.
When Continuous Data Protection and Replication are enabled, VM IOs are captured real-time and replicated periodically (every 15 minutes by default) on the remote cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Cohesity CDP for VMware

a. Replicate to: Select either a Remote Cluster or AWS.
From the drop-down, select either a cluster source or an AWS S3 storage source to replicate snapshots. If you select an S3 storage object, you also need to select a region.
You can also register a new cluster to replicate to by selecting Register Remote Cluster.
From Cohesity release 7.0 onwards, you can enable CDP Synchronous Replication for a Protection Group. Once enabled, VM IOs of every VM in that Protection Group are streamed directly to the remote cluster (continuous streaming, not periodic).
As a result, Synch Replication makes data available for immediate (near-zero RPO) recovery. For details on enabling CDP Synchronous Replication, see Add or Edit a Protection Group for Virtual Servers section.
Note: Irrespective of whether you use an existing remote cluster or register a new one, you must enable the Encryption toggle in the remote cluster if you have enabled the CDP Synchronous Replication field in the Protection job to replicate the real-time IOs and logs to the remote cluster synchronously. For details on the CDP Synchronous Replication field, see Add or Edit a Protection Group for Virtual Servers. For detailed instructions on registering a remote cluster and enabling encryption, see Create a Connection to the Remote Cohesity Cluster.
b. Retain for xx days: Specify how long the snapshots are retained on the remote cluster.
To add additional replication schedules, repeat these steps. To replicate to multiple Cohesity clusters, create multiple replication schedules with different replication targets.
If you specify multiple replication schedules with the same replication target that replicate the same set of snapshots but with different retention periods, the snapshots are retained for the longest time period. For example if you define two replication schedules with the same replication target that retain the same set of snapshots but one schedule specifies a 90-day retention period and the other schedule specifies a 180 day retention period, the set of snapshots is retained for 180 days.
8. Click Save. The policy is immediately available to use in Protection Groups. If you want to configure additional policy settings, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Cohesity CDP for VMware

Note: If replication is enabled for CDP, then the blackout window option in the policy would not be honored.
Recovery
You can perform a point-in-time recovery of VMs, files and folders, Virtual Disks, and IVM of a CDP-based Protection Group s by selecting the points in the timeline bar on the recovery page. This timeline will also show when the VADP backups were taken. So, the user can optionally recover from the VADP snapshots as well. Deploy the VAIO Filter Manually
From release 7.0 onwards, you can deploy the VAIO filter manually on the ESXi host cluster. To deploy the VAIO filter, use the VMware vSphere IOFilterManager APIs that can be accessed through the vCenter MOB interface. The vibURL required to deploy the VAIO filter is generated by downloading the VAIO installer from the Cohesity cluster and directly hosting the VAIO installer on an HTTP server accessible from the vCenter server and the ESXi hosts where the VAIO filter needs to be installed. Prerequisites
l Ensure the VMware vCenter meets the CDP requirements. l Ensure the VMware vCenter meets the conditions and permissions required to install
the I/O filers in its ESXi host clusters. l Uninstall existing I/O Filters from the ESXi hosts and the ESXi host clusters.
Note: The VAIO filter can only be installed on the ESXi host cluster and not on the ESXi host.
Download the VAIO Filter from the Cohesity cluster To download the VAIO filter from the Cohesity cluster:

following:

l Provider: cohfilter l vCenterUUID: <vCenterUUID> l CohesityID: <ClusterId:IncarnationId> l CohesityClusterEndpoint: <endpoint>:20004 l HeartbeatInterval: 30
Note: You can view the default Storage Policy created by Cohesity on the VMware vCenter as a reference for the above settings.
l If there is no VM Storage Policy attached to the VMs, then when the Protection Group is run, Cohesity will automatically create and attach the VM Storage Policy required for CDP.
l A CDP-enabled Protection Group supports a maximum of 25 VMs per node and 40 VMs per ESXi host, in each Cohesity cluster. Attempts to create Protection Groups that exceed this limit fail with the following error messages:
The limit on the number of CDP-protected VMs from an ESXi host is being exceeded on the host.
The maximum number of VMware VMs supported on this cluster for CDP is <number of nodes in the Cohesity cluster times 25>
l If the Storage Policy attached to the VM does not have the correct CDP attributes configured, then a corresponding error message is displayed for that VM on the CDP status page (Protection> CDP > Protected Objects).

l CDP will stop if the FQDN of the Cohesity cluster is changed after the CDP protection runs are configured for a VMware VM. To reenable CDP, update the new FQDN in the CDP Storage policy and reapply the policy on all the VMs associated with that policy.
l If a Protection Group is deleted or paused, then you must either manually detach the VM Storage Policies that were manually attached or update the Storage Policies to remove the CDP attributes. Once you resume the Protection Group, you can reattach the VM Storage Policies with CDP attributes.
l If the time stamp on the Cohesity cluster and the workload VM are not in sync, then the CDP protection window displayed in the Cohesity cluster will be inaccurate.
l You can select point-in-time restore only for individual VMs and not for a Protection Group.
l The performance of your vCenter server might be impacted if many VMs are added to a CDP policy at once.
