Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Failover Protection Group for VMs

l Cohesity clusters monitor the I/O throughput of CDP-enabled objects continuously. The guardrails help you track the resource utilization, performance, and stability of the Cohesity cluster. When the I/O throughputs exceed the pre-defined thresholds, appropriate alert messages are displayed under the Message column of the Protection Run details page. l CDP disabled for a set duration. If the I/O throughput of an object sporadically increases above the threshold, causing a resource scarcity on the Cohesity cluster, CDP is disabled for a duration determined by Cohesity. Alert Message CDP was temporarily disabled at <hh:mm> because of High IO Throughput. It will be enabled automatically after <default period set by Cohesity>. CDP is automatically re-enabled once the time duration set by Cohesity expires. To modify the time duration set by Cohesity, contact your Cohesity account team. l CDP disabled temporarily: If the I/O throughput of a CDP-enabled object exceeds the threshold for a prolonged period, CDP is disabled until you enable it again. Alert Message CDP disabled at <hh:mm> PM because of continuous high I/O throughput. Please review the I/O throughput of an entity. Disabling CDP ensures the sustainability of the Cohesity cluster and prevents the objects that exceed the thresholds from affecting the other objects in the Cohesity cluster. When CDP is disabled with the preceding message, it is not enabled unless you manually enable it. You can review the I/O throughput of such entities and reenable CDP if you like. You may also contact your Cohesity account team for more details.
l CDP protection is not supported for the VMware VMs residing in the vVol datastores. l For CDP-enabled VMware VMs that use vSAN-based datastores, you must attach the
storage policy manually. For details, see CDP Offline Storage Attach for vSAN Datastores. l With ESXi 8.0.x versions, the automatic installation of the filter driver does not work as expected.
Failover Protection Group for VMs
Note: Failover of Protection Groups is only supported for VMware VMs.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Failover Protection Group for VMs

When a Protection Group with a replication schedule starts replicating snapshots from a primary Cohesity cluster to a remote Cohesity cluster, a Protection Group in Failover Ready state is created on the remote Cohesity cluster. If the original capturing Cohesity cluster and/or the original Source are down because there is a planned maintenance outage or a disaster destroys them, you can failover the Protection Group in Failover Ready state and deactivate the original task on the capturing Cohesity cluster. As part of the Failover, you are prompted to optionally recover the VMs from the replicated snapshots stored on the remote Cohesity cluster.
Note: When you create a Protection Group on a Cohesity cluster with a replication schedule after the first snapshot is replicated, a Failover Ready copy of the Protection Group is created on the remote Cohesity cluster that is receiving the snapshot. For more information on Failover Ready, see About Failover Ready. You can failover the Protection Group of VMs. You cannot failover the Protection Group of Views or SQL Servers. You can, however, clone replicated Views and restore SQL Servers. For more information, see Failover a Protection Group.
During Failover, the following actions occur:
1. Disaster at Source - On the primary Cohesity cluster, the backup job fails to capture the snapshots of the source.
2. Replication Fails - As the source is down or unreachable, the replication job fails to replicate the snapshots onto the remote Cohesity cluster. The Failover Ready for VMs on the remote Cohesity cluster is activated and causes the rejection of the incoming replicated snapshots created by the associated job on the primary Cohesity cluster.
3. Failover VMs - You are prompted to optionally recover the VMs from the replicated snapshots on the remote Cohesity cluster to a new source.
The state of a Protection Group may also become "Failover Ready" when an active Protection Group is deactivated. For more information, see About Failover Ready. For more information about what happens during a Failover, see Failover from Replicated Copies. For more information on disaster recovery of VMs using the Cohesity Cloud Edition, see Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to AWS Cloud. To Failover a Protection Group on the remote Cluster:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. Find the Protection Group in the Failover Ready state in the list, click on the actions
menu , and select Failover.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Failover Protection Group for VMs

3. Select a source to place the recovered VMs and click Failover Job and Continue to

Recovery. 4. Set Recover Options for VM Failover. 5. View VM Failover Confirmation. 6. Deactivate Original VM Protection Group. The Failover of the Protection Group in the
Cohesity Dashboard does not automatically deactivate the original task on the original cluster that captured the snapshots. To deactivate, you must follow the instructions in Deactivate Original VM Protection Group 7. Restore VM Protection Group to Running. The Failover of the Protection Group in the Cohesity Dashboard does not automatically restore the task to running on the new cluster. To restore the task to a running state, you must follow the instructions in Restore VM Protection Group to Running.

l Start Connected--For each recovered VM, connect to the original or new network when the VM reboots. If this option is not selected, the VMs are not connected to any network on reboot.
l Detach network--For each recovered VM, the virtual Network Interface Card (vNIC) is removed from the VM.
l Attach to a new network--For each recovered VM, attach the virtual Network Interface Card (vNIC) to a new network. The new network might be a standard port group or a distributed port group.
When recovering VMware VMs, the selected Network port group will be attached to all the network interfaces of the VMs being recovered.
When recovering Hyper-V VMs, the selected virtual switch will be attached to all the network interfaces of the VMs being recovered.

7. Select Leave recovered VMs powered off if you want the recovered VMs to remain powered off after they are created. If you recover VMs from a Storage Domain that has Cloud Tier enabled, Cohesity recommends leaving the VMs powered off.
8. Select Continue recovery even if errors occur when recovering VMs if you want the Recover task to continue even if errors occur when recovering the VMs. For example, if one of the VMs cannot be created, the Cluster will still attempt to create the other VMs. If this is unselected, then the Recover task is discontinued only if VM creation fails, so if VM creation succeeds, but VM storage migration fails, the task continues.

Failover Protection Group for VMs

Deactivate Original VM Protection Group
Only Protection Groups that are protecting VMs can be deactivated. Protection Groups that are protecting a view cannot be deactivated.
Note: If possible, deactivate the original Protection Group on the original capturing Cohesity cluster. If the original Cohesity cluster that captured the Snapshots is down or unreachable, you may be unable to deactivate the Protection Group.
The example below shows the deactivation of a Protection Group protecting VMs. Deactivating a Protection Group protecting SQL Servers is similar but not all details are the same. For example, the transaction logs are not described or pictured. During deactivation, the following actions occur:
1. Snapshots are no longer captured by the original Protection Group on the original capturing Cohesity cluster. However, the existing snapshots captured by the Protection Group remain in the storage domain. They are not deleted.
2. Snapshots created by the Protection Group are no longer replicated to the receiving (remote) Cohesity cluster. (If you have already initiated the failover procedure, the replication has already stopped.)
3. You can optionally choose that the VMs on the original source be powered off. The VMs and the VM files, however, are not deleted. (The Cohesity cluster may be unable to power off the VMs if the original source is down or unreachable.)

Viewing VM Snapshot Types
Cohesity records Snapshot consistency information (Application-Consistent, CrashConsistent, Not Powered On) for each VM that the Cluster backs up. You can view this information on the Run Details page. For information about creating App-Consistent backups, see Creating Application-Consistent Snapshots. To view a VM's Snapshot type:
1. On the Protection Group page, click the name of the Job that captured the Snapshot. 2. On the Job Details page, click the protection run that you want details for. 3. On the Run Details page, mouse over a VM to see its Snapshot type. A message may
also provide additional details about the Snapshot type.
When you create a Recover or Clone task, a Snapshot's type is viewable when selecting the Snapshot to Recover or Clone. To view a VM's consistency information, click Edit. If one type displays, this means all VMs in the snapshot are that type. If the Mixed type displays, this means the snapshot contains VMs of different types, such as crash-consistent and not powered on. You can display individual VMs to see each VM's type. Note the following about Application-Consistent Backups: Enabling or disabling the Application-Consistent option for an Incremental (CBT) Protection Group results in the creation of full snapshots (instead of incremental snapshots) during the next Protection Group run.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Truncate Logs in Microsoft Exchange Servers on VMs

Truncate Logs in Microsoft Exchange Servers on VMs
Cohesity supports the ability to truncate the Microsoft Exchange email server transaction logs after a successful backup of a Windows server that hosts the Exchange email server. After the Cohesity cluster successfully captures a snapshot during a Protection Group, the Cohesity cluster truncates the Exchange transaction logs on the server. Cohesity has qualified truncating logs for the following Microsoft Exchange servers running on virtual servers:
l Microsoft Exchange 2019 running on supported Windows servers (Standalone and DAG)
l Microsoft Exchange 2016 running on supported Windows servers (Standalone and DAG)
l Microsoft Exchange 2013 running on supported Windows servers (Standalone and DAG)
l Microsoft Exchange 2010 SP3 running on supported Windows servers (Standalone and DAG)
While selecting VMs to protect, you can toggle Exchange Log Truncation on for individual VMs where Exchange is registered with the Cohesity cluster.
Note: Cohesity supports log truncation of Microsoft Exchange servers on VMware VMs only.
If Exchange Log Truncation is on and the Windows server has an Exchange server but the log truncation fails, an error is reported. However, the backup can successfully complete. If App-Consistent Backups is on for the Protection Group and Exchange Log Truncation is on for some VMs in the job, the backup of these VMs is crash-consistent. However, these VMs contain VSS snapshots that were backed up while the Exchange server was quiesced (in an app-consistent state). You can restore this app-consistent VSS snapshot using the Microsoft VSS tools. Note that other applications in these VMs are not quiesced when VSS snapshots are backed up. These other applications were captured in the crash-consistent state in the VSS snapshot.
Note: l Exchange log truncation does not require an additional adapter, but Exchange must be registered on the VM you want to protect.
l App-Consistent Backups must be toggled on if you want to protect an Exchange VM.

Recover Virtual Machines
The VMs that are backed up onto the Cohesity cluster can be recovered as VMs, virtual disks, files and folders. You can also perform instant mount volume of the VMs.
Recover Files or Folders
Cohesity provides the ability to recover files and folders from a snapshot created earlier by a Protection Group. Files and folders can be recovered to their original location (limitations apply to physical servers and specific operating systems) or to a newly specified location, which can be within the original source or a different one. You can choose to retain the recovered files' and folders' original (at the time of the backup) permissions and attributes. You can also download files and folders from selected snapshots that were created by a Cohesity Protection Group. To learn more, see About File Recovery. For more information about the recovery options:
l Recover Files or Folders to the Original Location l Recover Files or Folders to a New Location

Windows VMs
l If the Storage Replica feature is enabled on a Windows server with GPT disks, then file recovery (using the Cohesity agent) or IVM recovery to the original location is not supported. Cohesity recommends the following alternatives:
l For file-level recovery, consider one of the following:
l Recover to an alternate location.
l Recover using VMware tools.
l Use the Download Files option.
l For IVM recovery, recover to an alternate location instead.
l After making system configuration changes to a Windows 8 or Windows 2012 System VM, such as renaming an existing drive letter or adding a new disk, these changes may not immediately take effect due to a Windows registry refresh issue. To force the drive letters to be updated on the VM, reboot the system in the VM. This issue affects how files are indexed by the Cohesity cluster and displayed while browsing the contents of the VM in the Cohesity Dashboard.
l Considerations when recovering to physical servers that run:
l Windows 2012 or later - None
If the OS does not support your recovery, you must recover to an alternate physical server running Windows 2012 Server or later, or use downloads.
l Windows behavior (giving each user its own set of mapped networked drives) prevents recovering to an SMB share that was mounted by a different user.
l Recovering files/folders with names longer than 200 characters may return an error. This limitation is due to Windows behavior when handling files/folders with long names.
l File-based recovery to Windows VMs does not support hardlinks and alternate data streams.
Linux VMs
l For Linux VMs, Cohesity supports file recovery from LVM volumes. One LVM volume can consume more than one loop back device, so Linux VMs may support fewer than 8 volumes when configured with the default number of loop devices.
l For Linux Logical Volume Manager (LVM), if all the disks for a volume group are not found by the Cohesity cluster, the Cohesity cluster will not process that volume group. As a result of that, no volumes of this volume group will be recognized or indexed by the Cohesity cluster.
l When recovering a Linux file, the Cohesity Linux Agent runs the following commands in sudo:

VMware Tools
If you use VMware Tools for recovery, ensure the destination VM meets the following conditions:
l The VM is powered on.
l The most recent version of VMware Tools is installed and running on the VM.
l open-vm-tools can be used on the supported Linux releases; open-vm-tools, if used, must be installed and running.
l The user account used to access the VM must be a local user with write permissions for that VM.
l Ensure you run VMware tools in sync with the vCenter and ESXi host versions. For compatibility of VMware Tools with guest operating systems, see the VMware article.
l The use of VMware tools for file-level recovery from a deduplicated Windows volume is not supported.
Considerations
If you recover files and folders of VMware VMs using VMware Tools, then consider the following:
l A VMware Tools service restart during a Recovery operation may disrupt Recovery. If the VMware Tools service restarts during a Recovery operation, the following error message is returned: The guest operations agent could not be contacted. After multiple retries to contact the guest operations agent, an error message stating that it started the copy but it could not get the status is returned. Go to the recovery location to verify whether the operation succeeded.
l The maximum recovery speed is 1-2 Mbps due to a known VMware limitation. For more details, see the VMware article.
l Ensure port 443 is open on the ESXi host that hosts the target VM. For more details, see Manage Firewall Ports.
l Cohesity recommends that you not use VMware Tools if the size of the recovered files or folders exceeds 10 GB or 10,000 files.
l For Windows VMs:
l ACLs cannot be restored even if you have enabled the Preserve File/Folder Attributes option. Only the VM data will be restored.
l Recovery of reparse points (such as shared folders, mount points, or junction points) cannot be restored.
l When using the VMware Tools option for FLR on Windows VMs, some ACLs cannot be recovered due to limitations in the VMware API.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Recover Virtual Machines

l If a Windows VM includes volumes created from a storage pool (Microsoft Storage spaces), FLR is not supported.
l For Linux VMs:
l The Preserve File/Folder Attributes option restores only basic user, group, world permissions, and timestamps. Advanced permissions and file attributes such as ACLs are not restored.
l Permissions for guest files and folders are retained only when the user running the restore operation has permission to change the group ownership on the restored files and folders. If the user does not have change group ownership permissions, the restore operation will fail. In this case, retry the operation without enabling the Preserve File/Folder Attributes option.
l VMware APIs do not support the creation of files in the root folder.
l VMware APIs cannot restore symbolic links.
l Restoring files to a folder is not supported if the user account doesn't have write permission to that folder (even if the user has sudo permissions). Cohesity recommends using a root user or a user account with write privileges to the target folder.
l If you restore files and folders using a guest user account that does not have permission to change file/folder ownership, the restored files are owned by the guest user account used to perform the restore. If you restore files and folders using a guest user account that has permission to change file/folder ownership, the restored files are owned by (or the ownership is retained by) the guest user account used to create the files and folders.
l When a parent folder is restored all of its sub folders are restored also; Empty folders can be restored only when the parent folder is restored.
l Restoring hard links is supported; hard links restored with their source files use the same index node (inode).
l Agent-based File-Level Recovery (FLR) can fail on Btrfs file systems running Ubuntu 22.x when recovering files to the same location due to a filesystem UUID conflict with the existing mounted filesystem. As a worksround, use toolbased FLR instead of agent-based FLR in this scenario.

Troubleshooting
l Error: When recovering files or folders, the virtual disks are part of the target VM. These virtual disks are attached as SCSI disks that can be any of the supported adapter types: LSI Logic Parallel, LSI Logic SAS or VMware Paravirtual. During this step, you may encounter the following error: "Disk adapter with required slots - <n> is not available. Try creating a new adapter". Here, <n> is the number of virtual disks that are being attached. This can occur if the VM's disk adapter does not have the required number of slots (one SCSI adapter can support 15 virtual disks).
Solution:Attempt the operation after creating a new SCSI adapter. Additionally, the number of virtual disks where files and folders are being recovered from is limited to 15 at a time. Remove some files (or folders) and retry the recovery.
l Error: If LVM is not configured, running a protection job fails with the "No LVM volume found in idbmantasdev" error.
Solution: For details on how to resolve this issue, see the Registering or running a Linux protection job fails when no LVM volumes are detected KB article.
Limitations
l You can download files and folders from selected snapshots that were created by a CohesityProtection Group. However, only items that were indexed when the snapshot was created can be downloaded. Recovering and searching for files and folders in snapshots created by other backup software is not supported.
l Indexing, file recovery and browsing files and folders on VMs are not supported for drives with disk-level encryption (such as BitLocker). On physical Servers, however, these workflows are supported.
l Encrypted folders that have been renamed or deleted cannot be recovered.
l Encrypted VMs are not indexed.
l Recovering files to a VM where vMotion is in process is not supported.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

l File recovery is not supported for ReFS volumes in these environments: physical, VMware, Hyper-V and AHV.
l Downloading files and folders from tape archive locations is not supported. l Recovering files and folders from VMs to physical servers and from physical servers to
VMs is not supported. l The downloadable zip file can contain regular files and folders only; symlinks are not
supported. When unzipping the downloaded files/folders, use a zip utility that supports the ZIP64 format. l If you perform point-in-time recovery of a file that is deleted within the CDP restore window, then the file-level recovery fails with the following error message:

The Cohesity cluster attempts to index all files and folders to a drive on both Windows and Linux systems. If the Cohesity cluster is unable to find mount point information about files or directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories in the lvol_N directory, where N is a unique number such as 1.
On Windows systems, if the Cohesity cluster finds the mount point information about files and directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories with a drive letter such as C:.
Linux LVM indexing supports the following LVM types only: Linear, Striped, Mirrored, Mirrored + Striped, Thin. On Linux systems, how files and directories are indexed and displayed is dependent on the conditions specified in the following table.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Recover Virtual Machines

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

Simple Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
UUID="ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc" /mnt ext4 auto 0
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point that was specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Linux Virtual Machine

LVM Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
/dev/mapper/VG1-root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
/dev/VG1/root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt. If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Linux Physical

LVM Volume

The Cohesity agent can only return mount data when the volume is mounted on the Linux physical Server. If the volume is mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the volume is not mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

l Download Files: If you are recovering a single file, this option downloads the file to your browser's download folder. For all other selections, this creates a recover task. When the task is completed, from the Recoveries page, click the task name and then click Download Files to download the generated zip file.
Character replacement explanation for : and \ in file and directory names in zip files
If the original file or directory name contains a `:' , it is replaced with `_COLON_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "a:b" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b"
l The original name is "a:b:c" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b_ COLON_c"
If the original file or directory name contains a `\', it is replaced with '_BACK_ SLASH_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "x\y" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_y"
l The original name is "x\y\z" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_ y_BACK_SLASH_z"
5. From the Recover To, select Original Server to recover the files or folders to the original server.
6. (Applies only if you are recovering files and folders of a VMware VM). Select one of the following Restore Method options and provide the required information:

The Cohesity cluster attempts to index all files and folders to a drive on both Windows and Linux systems. If the Cohesity cluster is unable to find mount point information about files or directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories in the lvol_N directory, where N is a unique number such as 1.
On Windows systems, if the Cohesity cluster finds the mount point information about files and directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories with a drive letter such as C:.
Linux LVM indexing supports the following LVM types only: Linear, Striped, Mirrored, Mirrored + Striped, Thin. On Linux systems, how files and directories are indexed and displayed is dependent on the conditions specified in the following table.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Recover Virtual Machines

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

Simple Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
UUID="ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc" /mnt ext4 auto 0
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point that was specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Linux Virtual Machine

LVM Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
/dev/mapper/VG1-root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
/dev/VG1/root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt. If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Linux Physical

LVM Volume

The Cohesity agent can only return mount data when the volume is mounted on the Linux physical Server. If the volume is mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the volume is not mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Character replacement explanation for : and \ in file and directory names in zip files
If the original file or directory name contains a `:' , it is replaced with `_COLON_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "a:b" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b" l The original name is "a:b:c" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b_
COLON_c"
If the original file or directory name contains a `\', it is replaced with '_BACK_ SLASH_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "x\y" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_y" l The original name is "x\y\z" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_
y_BACK_SLASH_z"

l You can choose this option if there are no hardware configuration changes involved in the original VM.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Recover Virtual Machines

In highly available VMs that migrate to another node in the Hyper-V cluster after a backup, recovery will fail because deleting VMs from a nonoriginal location is currently unsupported.
In the case of Hyper-V standalone clusters or clusters managed by SCVMM, restoring a VM will fail if a VM with the same UUID is present on multiple nodes. A VM can only be successfully restored if its original UUID is found on the original node.
If the VM exists on the host, it will be deleted first. If the VM is not present, the recovery process will proceed directly. Once it is confirmed that the VM is no longer on the host, it will be restored from the backup snapshot to its original location, using the same UUID. The recovery can be either instant or a copy recovery, depending on the options selected by the user.
VM recovery in SCVMM will fail if multiple VMs with the same original UUID are detected under SCVMM-managed hosts or clusters.
Note: This feature is only available if the cluster and agents are on the required version.
When you choose to overwrite an existing VM, the current VM will be deleted before the recovery process begins. If the recovery fails or is canceled, the original VM will be permanently lost. To recover the VM, you must initiate a new restore from a specific point in time, which is determined by the backup snapshot you select.
l AHV: From the Existing VM Handling options list, choose how you want to handle the original VM when recovering to the original location. This option is available in both Copy Recovery and Instant Recovery options:
l None: Recovers the VM as a new VM and retains the original VM. In the Rename field available in the Recovery Options, you can specify the name of the recovered VM by adding prefix and/or suffix strings to the name of the original VM. By default, the recovered VM is named as copy<original_VM_name>.
l Overwrite Existing VM:Recovers the VM by deleting the existing VM that has the same UUID. The recovered VM is created with the original UUID and retains the original identity and location. If you select Overwrite Existing VM, the system performs the following actions before initiating recovery:
l Removes the VM's volume group attachments
l Deletes the existing VM

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Recover Virtual Machines

The existing VM is deleted before the recovery process begins. Therefore, a recovery failure or cancellation can result in the loss of the original VM. When you select this option, a confirmation dialog box is displayed. Review the message, type YES, and click Confirm. The recovered VM is instantiated using the original UUID and is placed in the original location on the target cluster. l Keep Existing VM: Recovers the VM as a new VM while retaining the original VM. The system removes the existing VM's volume group attachments and creates a clone of the existing VM. The cloned VM is assigned a new UUID and it retains the name of the original VM, obsolete_<time_stamp><Orginal_VM_Name>, after which the volume group attachments are reattached to the cloned VM. The recovered VM is created with the original UUID and name of the recovered VM is changed based on the rename option, ensuring both the cloned VM and the recovered VM coexist in the environment.
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.

Create Empty Disks for Excluded Disks

(Applicable only to AHV and Hyper-V Protection Groups)
Enable this option if you want Cohesity to create blank disks for every disk you excluded from the backup. The metadata of the excluded disks will be used to create the blank disks. These blank disks are available post-recovery and only have the metadata of the original disk but no data. You can configure and run databases and applications on these disks, saving you from the effort of creating new disks. This feature is especially helpful if you have many VMs with excluded disks.

Leverage SAN Transport for Copy Recovery

Leverage SAN Transport SAN transport will work only with the Copy Recovery option. You can turn on the Leverage SAN Transport toggle when you want to perform the copy recovery of VMware objects to vCenter target environments. You can now perform copy recovery of vCloud Director (vCD) objects, such as VMs and vApps, to vCD target environments, You can also leverage the SAN transport mode while you perform the copy recovery of the vCD objects.
Once SAN Transport is enabled for copy recovery, the disk provisioning strategy selected during the Cohesity cluster setup will be reset to "Thick Provisioned Eager Zeroed" in adherence to the recommendation from VMware. For more details, see the KB article.
Cohesity supports SAN transport for Fibre Channel (FC) and iSCSI-based storage arrays and datastores that contain such storage arrays. Turn on this option to enable the SAN transport mode over FC or iSCSI for backing up VMware VMs to Cohesity cluster.
To use the SAN transport mode over FC, ensure the following pre-requirement:
l Fibre channel is installed and zoned appropriately between the Cohesity cluster and the primary storage (Pure Flash Array and HPE Nimble Storage Array).
To use the SAN transport mode over FC and iSCSI , ensure the following prerequirement:
l Volumes are mapped appropriately between the Cohesity cluster, ESXi hosts, and the primary storage.

Allow NB DSSL Transport Fallback You can turn on the Allow NBDSSL Transport Fallback toggle if you do not want to enforce strict SAN transport mode for backing up VMware to the Cohesity cluster. With the toggle enabled, backup doesn't fail if the SAN transport is not available. If you disable the toggle, the backup fails if SAN transport mode is unavailable. NBDSSL encrypts all data passed over the TCP connection.

Power State

Prerequisite
VMware licensing is required for all VMware products to facilitate processes such as backup or recovery with Cohesity. For more information on the VMware license, see the following VMware articles:
l VMware vSphere Storage APIs
l Storage vMotion Requirements and Limitations
Process Overview
The recover task completes the following steps:
1. A new physical instance (VMDK) is extracted from the Snapshot and stored temporarily in the View (datastore) on the Cohesity cluster.
2. The new VMDK is migrated from the View to the specified datastore in the vCenter using Cohesity's implementation of vSphere Storage vMotion.
3. The temporary View (datastore) is deleted automatically once the Storage vMotion migration is completed.
After a successful recovery, the disks are attached to the VM. Depending on your environment, if the virtual disks were mapped to volumes, additional steps may be required to bring them online. Note the following about recovering virtual disks:
l Support is currently limited to recovering VMware virtual disks. l If the Overwrite Original Disk option is selected, the original disk is removed from
the VM and deleted, and the backed-up Cohesity disk is attached. If the recovery fails during the overwrite, the original disk will not be available, but you can retry the recovery to restore the disks. l If a virtual disk gets deleted after it is backed up, the disk must be recovered as a new disk. l If one or more disks will be overwritten during recovery, the target VM will automatically be powered off prior to the recovery and can optionally be powered on automatically after the recovery. Cohesity recommends suspending activity on the VM prior to performing the disk recovery. l If a Windows VM includes volumes created from a storage pool (Microsoft Storage spaces), VMDK recovery is not supported.

Teardown of Failed VMDK Recovery Tasks
Cohesity supports the teardown of failed VMDK recovery tasks, allowing you to clean up residual resources left behind when these tasks do not complete successfully.

Note: Tearing down a successful recovery is not allowed.

To teardown a failed VMDK recovery task that has left behind certain resources: 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Recoveries. 2. Locate the VMDK Recovery task you wish to terminate.

To teardown a recovery task, Click the Actions menu ( Teardown.

) of that task and select

Note: The Teardown option is available only if there are objects to destroy.

3. When prompted to confirm the teardown, click Teardown. A confirmation dialog appears with a warning stating that the restored VMs with data on the Cohesity mounted NFS datastore will be removed.
4. Click Confirm. The teardown process is initiated, and the Cohesity cluster performs the following steps: 1. VMDKs hosted on Cohesity datastore are detached from the target VM. 2. The Cohesity datastore is unmounted from the ESXi host. 3. The underlying restore view is deleted. 4. The user interface for Cohesity will show the current status of the teardown task. 5. The teardown status of each VMDK is displayed under the "Instant Recovery" column. 6. "Destroyed" status indicates successful completion of the teardown process.

Instant Volume Mount
Instant volume mounting is supported for virtual and physical environments. This feature allows the selected backup volumes to be made available at the target location where you can then complete the desired operations. Instant Volume Mount is available for backed-up volumes, whether they are stored locally on the Cohesity cluster or archived to a registered external target. Use cases include granular recovery of Microsoft Exchange, SQL and SharePoint data.
You can mount the volume to its original location or to a new location. For more information, see:
l Instant Volume Mount to the Original Location l Instant Volume Mount to a New Location

Considerations
l When recovering a file or instantly mounting a volume from a Windows VM or Physical Server Backup Source that has Windows deduplication installed and enabled for one or more volumes, you must choose a target machine that also has Windows deduplication installed (it does not have to be enabled for any volume). (However, this rule does not apply to Nutanix AHV VMs. If AHV VMs are enabled with Windows deduplication, the only supported recovery option is full VM recovery.)
If the target does not have Windows deduplication installed:
l File level recovery will fail with the error message: "Windows Data Deduplication role is not installed on the target machine. Retry recovery after installing the Windows Data Deduplication role on the target machine."
l Instant volume mounting will fail with the error message: "Windows Data Deduplication role is not installed on the target machine. Retry recovery after installing the Windows Data Deduplication role on the target machine."
To determine if Windows deduplication is installed on the Source or target machine, follow the steps given below:
1. Open Server Manager. 2. Select Roles and Features > File and Storage Services > File and iSCSI
Services. 3. Select the Data Deduplication check box, if necessary.

l Review the following considerations when performing instant volume mount to HyperV VMs:
l Only Windows VMs are supported.
l Dynamic Disks (LDM and LVM) are not supported.
l The Bring Disks Online option requires the following:
l VM must be part of Active Directory, the VM and the Hyper-V host must be in the same AD.

l Instant volume mounting Hyper-V 2012 R2 VMs without a SCSI controller is not supported. This is because Hyper-V disallows dynamically adding a SCSI controller, which is required to add the virtual disks.
l On 2012 R2 VMs, if an instant volume mount disk is attached to a VM during a Protection Group run, that snapshot cannot be application-consistent. If this occurs, the event viewer may contain a VSS-catastrophic error or similar message.

Troubleshooting
This section provides troubleshooting information for issues that might occur during IVM recovery.
Authentication Failures
Error Message The IVM recovery fails due to an authentication failure and displays the following error: "The specified network password is not correct". Possible Root Cause The cluster joined the AD but the Windows host has not joined the AD. Solution
l Create a local user on the Cohesity cluster and use the local user to access the SMB share. To create a local user on the Cohesity cluster, contact Cohesity Support.
or
l Disable SMB Authentication on the Cohesity cluster. Perform the following steps to disable SMB Authentication: 1. Log in to the Cohesity cluster. 2. Select SmartFiles > Views and click the Global Settings tab. 3. Toggle off the SMB Authentication setting.

Download a VMX File of a Virtual Machine
Cohesity supports the ability to download the VMX file of a Virtual Machine from the latest Snapshot of a Protection Group. A VMX file is the primary configuration file for a VMware Virtual Machine. Advanced VMware administrators may want to download and view the settings in a VMX file. In addition, they may want to download, modify and then upload a VMX file back to the original datastore to implement workarounds or global changes.
Warning: Downloading a VMX file and uploading it directly back into your datastore without modifications can result in unusable and inaccessible VMs. This feature is for advanced VMware administrators who are experienced in directly editing VMX files and manually configuring VMs. Use at your own risk.
Before you download the VMX file of a Virtual Machine from the latest Snapshot of a Protection Group, you must create and run a Protection Group. To download a VMX file:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Recoveries. 2. Click Recover > Virtual Machines > VMs. 3. Search for the Virtual Machine with the associated VMX file that you want to
download. Enter characters of the VM name and a list of items displays. You can also optionally narrow the search results by specifying filter criteria, for example you can filter the search results by a specific Protection Group. You can optionally specify the wildcard character * in the search. 4. In the list, find the VM with the associated VMX file that you want to download, click
the Actions Menu ( ) and select Download VMX file for MyVM, where MyVM is the name of your VM.
If the Cohesity cluster locates the VMX file in the last Snapshot of the Protection Group, the VMX file is downloaded. (In some cases the VMX file may be unreachable when the Snapshot was originally created and therefore not saved and cannot be downloaded later. For example the Cohesity cluster cannot save a VMX file if the HTTPS port to the ESXi host was not open when the Snapshot was created.) In addition, if the last Run of the Protection Group failed to back up the specified VM, the VMX file for that VM cannot be downloaded. If you require downloading a VMX file from Snapshot besides the last Snapshot, contact Cohesity Support.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

Azure VMware Solution (AVS)

Warning: Downloading a VMX file and uploading it directly back into your datastore without modifications can result in unusable and inaccessible VMs. This feature is for advanced VMware administrators who are experienced in directly editing VMX files and manually configuring VMs. Use at your own risk.
Azure VMware Solution (AVS)
Cohesity makes it simple and affordable to back up, recover, and manage data in Azure VMware Solution (AVS). AVS combines VMware Software Defined Data Center (SDDC) with Microsoft Azure Cloud bare-metal infrastructure. See the following topics for details:
1. Plan and Prepare for AVS Protection 2. Register your AVS (SDDC) 3. Protect your AVS source 4. Recover VMs, files and folders
Plan and Prepare for AVS Protection
Before registering your AVS source, ensure it meets user privileges and firewall port requirements. User Privileges for VMware To protect your AVS solution software-defined data center (SDDC), you need a user account with the vCenter Server Privileges. Firewall Ports Ensure the firewall ports are open to allow communication between the Cohesity clusters and the AVS environment. Considerations File-level recovery from AVS VMs that reside on volumes with Windows Data Deduplication enabled is not supported.

Recover AVS Source
After you protect your AVS source, you can recover VMs and files from your backups to their original or new location. Recover AVS VMs to a New or Original Location Recover AVS Files or Folders to a New or Original Location
Recover AVS VMs to a New or Original Location
You can recover the AVS VMs to the original (same location as the source) or a new location. After selecting the restore point, you can modify the storage domain and network. While recovering, you can either auto-deploy a Cohesity Agent, use an existing agent, or use VMware tools.
Recover AVS Files or Folders to a New or Original Location
Cohesity provides the ability to recover AVS files and folders from a snapshot created earlier by a Protection Group. Files and folders can be recovered to their original location (limitations apply to physical servers and specific operating systems) or to a newly specified location, which can be within the original source or a different one. You can choose to retain the recovered files' and folders' original (at the time of the backup) permissions and attributes. You can also download files and folders from selected snapshots that a Cohesity Protection Group created. For more information on recovering AVS files or folders to a new or original location, see Recover Files or Folders.
VMware vCloud Director (vCD)
VMware vCloud Director (vCD) allows Cloud Service providers to manage multiple tenants with data centers in different geographic locations and data stores that require different performance levels. Cloud Service Providers can use vCD to create organizations that are virtual administration units. Each organization can streamline services to multiple tenants. Cohesity offers integration with vCD in two ways:
l Protect vCD resources from the Cohesity cluster l Protect vCD resources from the vCD web console
Considerations
l Not all vCD storage policy types are supported. During instant recovery, Cohesity uses a tag-based storage policy for the temporary Cohesity datastore. After the storage vMotion completes, the VM is reconfigured to the target storage policy. During copy recovery, you can select a target storage policy at recovery time.

Protect vCD resources from the Cohesity cluster
The Cohesity Data Cloud enables you to configure multi-tenant environments that can be securely isolated from each other. A single Cohesity cluster can service backups and workloads of multiple tenants with secure namespace isolation and per-tenant encryption. For more information, see Protect vCD Resources from the Cohesity Cluster.
Protect vCD resources from the vCD web console
By installing the Cohesity vCD plugin, you can integrate Cohesity protection services with the vCD web console. When vCD is combined with Cohesity Data Cloud, you can provide backup and recovery for your vCD tenants. Cohesity offers granular data protection by enabling you to protect the entire vCloud Director or just the organizations, VMs, and vApps within it. In addition to allowing cloud service providers or administrators to manage the organizations, Cohesity Data Cloud enables tenants to leverage data protection as self-service, lowering operating costs and strengthening tenant efficacy. Key Concepts for vCD Protection
vCD vCD allows Cloud Service providers to support multiple tenants with data centers across different geographic locations or data stores requiring different performance levels. vCD Web Console The vCD Web Console allows Service Providers to create organizations that are virtual administration units. Organization An organization is a collection of users, groups, and compute resources. System administrators create organizations while the organization administrations manage the users and groups in an organization. An organization is mapped to a vSphere data pool and can contain multiple data stores. vApp vApp is a deployment unit containing one or more VMs and their network configuration.

Cohesity supports backup and recovery of the metadata for VMware vCD objects such as vApps, VMs, and vApp templates. Metadata includes user-defined properties of the vCD objects whose values can be text, date, time, boolean, number, strings, badges, etc. You can recover metadata to the original location or a new location. The read-only metadata is not recovered while recovering vApps, VMs, and vApp templates. Cohesity also supports backup and recovery of metadata for Test & Dev clones.

Partial Refresh of the vCD Souce
You can perform a partial refresh of the vCD source using the API. A partial refresh is faster than a full source refresh. This enhancement allows you to selectively discover new VMs, vApps, Organizations, Org VDC, and vApp templates through the APIs into the vCD source, eliminating the need to wait for a full vCD refresh. You can refresh only the selected objects, such as specific VMs, vApps, Organizations, Org VDC, and vApp templates within the vCD source. To do a partial refresh of the vCD source using the API:
Endpoint
PUT /v2/data-protect/sources/{sourceId}/objects
Parameters

Parameter sourceId

Type integer

Required Yes

Description The Entity ID of the data protection source

Finding the sourceId
You can find the sourceId from the UI by navigating to the Sources page and clicking your desired vCD source. The URL will appear in the following format:
https://<Cluster IP>/protections/sources/details/{sourceId}/objects?environment=kVMware
The `{sourceId}` is the numeric ID you need for the API call. This value remains constant until the source is unregistered.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

"actionType": "Add", "vcdModifyParams": {

10. Start Time: Indicates when the Protection Group should run. The current time is displayed by default but you can change it. Enter the hour and minutes or use the up and down arrows on your keyboard. Verify the AM or PM setting.
The default time zone is the browser's time zone. You can change the time zone by selecting a different time zone.
11. SLA: The service-level agreement (SLA) defines the expected time to complete either a full backup or incremental backup. The backup completion time depends on the Windows volume size on AD, objects changed between incremental backups, network speed, and other Protection Groups running on the Cohesity cluster.
l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental protection run to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last protection run.
l Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup protection run to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).
12. Pause Future Runs: Enable this option to pause future protection runs for the Protection Group.
13. End Date: Optional. Toggle on and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.
14. QoS Policy: Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy.
Note: Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.
l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Protection Groups.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

l TestAndDev High: The Cohesity cluster writes the data to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. The I/Os with this QoS policy are given higher priority compared to other QoS policies. Use this policy for workloads that require lower I/O latency.
15. Defer Incomplete Objects in Concurrent Runs: (Applies only to VMware VMs) A Protection Group can protect both small (for example, 1 GB VM) and large VMs (for example, 1 TB VM). While a short VM usually completes its protection runs within a few minutes, a large VM might take longer and still be running when it's time for the next run. By default, when it's time to start the next run, the Cohesity cluster checks for any in-progress protection run in that Protection Group. If there are in-progress protection runs (typically a large VM), the Cohesity cluster cancels the next run for that Protection Group, causing the small VMs to also miss that run and the SLA. When the Defer Incomplete Objects in Concurrent Runs option is enabled, if there is an in-progress protection run, the Cohesity cluster postpones the subsequent run only for that VM. The postponed run resumes as soon as the current run is completed. The protection runs of the remaining VMs (typically small VMs) in that Protection Group are not affected and run on schedule.
For example, Protection Group PG1 runs every 8 hours to protect VMs A, B, and C. When the first protection run starts, A and B complete running in a few minutes. VM C, a large VM, needs 12 hours to complete running. If Defer Incomplete Objects in Concurrent Runs is disabled for PG1, when it's time for the second run, the Cohesity cluster cancels the second run in all three VMs because C is still in progress. However, the third run is completed in all three VMs. Because C is a large VM, A and B miss every alternate run.

If Defer Incomplete Objects in Concurrent Runs is enabled for PG1, when it's time for the second run, the Cohesity cluster starts the second run in A and B but postpones the run in C. C's second run resumes when its first run completes. As a result, A, B, and C do not miss any scheduled runs.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

If PG1 also protects VM D, another large VM, which needs 20 hours to complete, when it's time for the second run, the Cohesity cluster postpones D's second run. When it's time for the third run, because D's first run is still in progress, the Cohesity cluster cancels its second run but postpones its third run. D's next run will resume automatically when its ongoing run completes.

When the Cohesity cluster cancels the backup task of an object (such as D) in the Protection Group (such as PG1), the Protection Group Details page displays the following message at the corresponding protection run:
"Failed to back up some of the objects in the protection run as they are already backed in another protection run. ".
At the corresponding task (D's second backup task), the following message is displayed:
"cancelled the backup task of this object as it is already being backup up by another protection run."
Enabling the Defer Incomplete Objects in Concurrent Runs option helps you meet the defined SLAs, and improves the efficiency of the scheduled runs, thereby enhancing the backup performance.
Note: Defer Incomplete Objects in Concurrent Runs can be enabled for runs with replication or archiving enabled.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

16. Leverage SAN Transport for Data Protection: Cohesity supports SAN transport for Fibre Channel (FC) and iSCSI-based storage arrays and datastores that contain such storage arrays. Turn on this option to enable the SAN transport mode over FC or iSCSI for backing up VMware VMs to Cohesity cluster.
Note: Using the Leverage SAN Transport for Data Protection option with the Leverage Storage Snapshots for Data Protection option is not recommended.
To use the SAN transport mode over FC, ensure the following pre-requirements: l Fibre channel is installed and zoned appropriately between the Cohesity cluster and the primary storage (Pure Flash Array and HPE Nimble Storage Array). l Volumes are mapped appropriately between the Cohesity cluster, ESXi hosts, and the primary storage.
You can turn on the Allow NBDSSL Transport Fallback toggle if you do not want to enforce strict SAN transport mode for backing up VMware to the Cohesity cluster. With toggle enabled, the backup will not fail if the SAN transport is not available. If you disable this toggle, backup will fail if SAN transport mode is unavailable. NBDSSL encrypts all data passed over the TCP connection.
Note: Fallback to NBD is no longer supported if NBDSSL fails or is disabled.
Note: Ensure that the storage array connects to the primary environment (host) and the Cohesity node over the same protocol (FC on both ends or iSCSI on both ends). Cohesity does not support SAN transport for SAS (Serial Attached SCSI) based storage arrays.
17. Exclude Disks: (Applies only to VMware VM) By default, all the volumes on a selected server are protected. Toggle on to select disks to exclude for all VMs is this Protection Group. Provide the type of controller, bus number and unit number for each disk to exclude. Excluded disks are not backed up and are not recovered during VM recovery.
Note: If you exclude a disk that is part of a striped volume, the Cohesity cluster does not index the volume even if Indexing is toggled on for this Protection Group. You will not be able to search for or recover individual files in that volume.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

18. Exclude Physical RDM Volumes: (Applies only to VMware VM) VMware vSphere Storage APIs cannot be used to snapshot physical compatibility RDM disks. Enable this option to allow the backup of VMs by excluding physical compatibility RDM disks. If you disable this option, the backup of VMs with physical compatibility RDM disks will fail. Excluded disks are not backed up and are not recovered during VM recovery. Cohesity recommends you to use agent-based backups to protect data on the physical RDM disks.
Note: l VMware does not support taking the snapshot or backup of the VMs having RDM (physical and virtual) on Shared Bus.
l Backup of Virtual compatibility RDM disks is supported and does not depend on the Exclude Physical RDM Volumes toggle setting.
19. App Consistent Backup: Enable if you want the guest operating systems of all the VMs in the Protection Group to be quiesced before snapshots of these VMs are created. When this option is selected, the Cohesity cluster requests the VMware vSphere/AHV software to create a quiesced VM snapshot by invoking VMware Tools/Nutanix Guest Tools (installed on the guest operating systems of the VM). The VMware Tools/Nutanix Guest Tools requests that applications on the guest OS quiesce their state so that application-consistent snapshots can be created. Quiescing of VMs before capturing snapshots ensures the integrity of the data saved in the snapshots. If the Cohesity cluster fails to capture an app-consistent snapshot, you can use the Take a Crash Consistent backup if unable to perform an App Consistent backup option to capture a crash-consistent snapshot. The option is available only if the App-Consistent backups option is enabled. For example, the Cohesity cluster may fail to perform an app-consistent backup for the following reasons: when VMware Tools/Nutanix Guest Tools is not installed on the VM, the VM (VMware) is powered off, or if the VM cannot be quiesced. If the Take a Crash Consistent backup if unable to perform an App Consistent backup is enabled in that Cohesity cluster, a crash-consistent snapshot is captured.
Note: App-consistent backups apply to VMs only. For physical servers, Windows is app-consistent by default and Linux is crash-consistent. For more information, see Creating Application-Consistent Snapshots.
20. Indexing: Indexing is enabled by default and required for file recovery. The Cohesity cluster will scan all the files in the Protection Group and create an internal index that can be used later by a recover task to locate files by name. For information about customizing indexing, see Customize Indexing.

For more information, see Disaster Recovery of VMs Using AWS Cohesity Cloud Edition.
After enabling cloud migration, you can download the Cohesity Agent directly from the Cohesity Dashboard.
22. Cancel Runs at Quiet Time Start: Available only if the selected policy has at least one quiet time period. Toggle it on to specify that all currently executing protection runs should abort if a quiet time period specified for the Protection Group starts. By default this toggle is off, which means after a protection run starts, it continues to execute even when a quiet time period specified for this protection run starts. However, a new protection run will not start during a quiet time period.

l SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
For more information, see Alerts.
24. Priority: Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity supports concurrent backups, but if the number of Protection Groups exceeds the ability to process them, those with High priority are given the highest priority to execute, Medium the second-highest priority, and Low the lowest priority.

Note: The connection to the SMTP Server must be enabled to send email notification. You can enable the SMTP Server connection in the configuration settings page ( Cohesity UI > Settings > Summary > Configure > Enable SMTP Server).

Recover Organizations, vApps, and VMs to a New or Original Location

After selecting the restore point, you can modify the storage domain and network. While recovering, you can either auto-deploy a Cohesity Agent, use an existing agent, or use VMware tools.
You recover the VM files (such as the VMDK files) to their original datastores and create new instances of the VMs in the original location in the original Source.
Before you can recover VMs to their original location, snapshots of those volumes must exist on the Cohesity cluster. To create Snapshots, create and run a Protection Group.

Recovery Options Network

Description
By default, the VMs that are to be recovered do not have a virtual Network Interface Card (vNIC) attached.
Enable the Attach option to attach a virtual Network Interface Card (vNIC) to each VM that is to be recovered.
With the Attach option enabled, each VM will connect to its original network and the following option is displayed:
l Start Connected-- Enable this option to connect to the original network when the VMs reboots. If this option is disabled, the VMs are not connected to any network on reboot.
When recovering VMs to their original location, the original IP mode is restored to the respective NICs and the original IP address on each NIC is restored only if the original IP mode is set to "Static-Manual."
When recovering VMs to a new location, the original IP address and IP mode are not recovered to the NIC cards. By default, the IP mode is set to "none" and the IP address remains empty. Contact Cohesity support to recover the original IP addresses to a new location.
While recovering VMs to the original location, there is no explicit control to preserve the MAC address. If the Attach option is enabled and the VM is configured to have a manual MAC address assigned at the time of backup, the same address will be recovered. If the VM is configured to have an automatic MAC address at the time of backup, the same setting will be applied to the recovered VM. For information on preserving MAC address when recovering VMs to a new location, see Recover VMs to a New Location.

The Cohesity cluster attempts to index all files and folders to a drive on both Windows and Linux systems. If the Cohesity cluster is unable to find mount point information about files or directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories in the lvol_N directory, where N is a unique number such as 1.
On Windows systems, if the Cohesity cluster finds the mount point information about files and directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories with a drive letter such as C:.
Linux LVM indexing supports the following LVM types only: Linear, Striped, Mirrored, Mirrored + Striped, Thin. On Linux systems, how files and directories are indexed and displayed is dependent on the conditions specified in the following table.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

Simple Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
UUID="ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc" /mnt ext4 auto 0
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point that was specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Linux Virtual Machine

LVM Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
/dev/mapper/VG1-root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
/dev/VG1/root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt. If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Linux Physical

LVM Volume

The Cohesity agent can only return mount data when the volume is mounted on the Linux physical Server. If the volume is mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the volume is not mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Character replacement explanation for : and \ in file and directory names in zip files
If the original file or directory name contains a `:' , it is replaced with `_COLON_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "a:b" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b" l The original name is "a:b:c" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b_
COLON_c"
If the original file or directory name contains a `\', it is replaced with '_BACK_ SLASH_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "x\y" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_y" l The original name is "x\y\z" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_
y_BACK_SLASH_z" 7. Select one of the following Restore Method options and provide the required
information: l Auto Deploy Cohesity Agent: Select this option to automatically deploy the Cohesity Agent on the target VM. This allows you to use domain credentials to access the target VM. Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

should be either a domain administrator or a member of the local administrators group on the server.
l Use Existing Cohesity Agent: Select this option to use the existing Cohesity Agent deployed on the target VM.
Note: To recover files and folders of VMware VMs using Cohesity Agent, VMware tools must be installed and running on the target VM.
l Use VMware Tools: Select this option to use the VMware Tools for recovery. You have to enter the credentials required to access the target VM. If you are using domain credentials to access a target VM, then you should provide the username in the format <username@domain.com>. Ensure to install the VMware Tools on the target VM.
8. Optional. Edit the default settings of the following Recovery options:
l Overwrite Existing File/Folder: By default, this option is enabled to overwrite the existing files and folders. Disable this option to create the files and folders in the specified location. Any duplicate files are skipped.
Example for a Windows alternate location with Overwrite Existing File/Folder enabled and the target already exists:
Files to be recovered: "C:\foo\1.txt", "C:\foo\test\1.txt", "C:\bar", "C:\foo\bar". Specified alternate location: "C:\restore". At the end of the copy, the target folder looks like this:
l C:\restore\1.txt
l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_0\1.txt
l C:\restore\bar
l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_1\bar
If Overwrite Existing File/Folder is enabled, recovering a file to source when the file is in use may cause the open file to be overwritten. Whether overwriting occurs depends on the application using the file.
l Preserve File/Folder Attributes: By default, this option is enabled and the ACLs, permissions, and timestamps are preserved for all files and folders. If you disable this option, then ACLs and permissions are not preserved. If recovering both folders and files, then folders will receive the new timestamps, but files retain their original timestamps. If recovering only, files, then files will receive the new timestamps.
l Continue on Error: Enable this option if you want to continue the recovery even if one of the objects encounters an error. By default, this option is disabled and the recovery operation will fail if one of the objects encounters an error.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

l Cluster Interface: By default, the Auto Select option is enabled and the recovery task automatically selects the correct VLAN. If you disable this option, then select a configured interface group from the Interface Group drop-down.
l Task Name: Change the default name of the recovery task. l Save Success Files: Enable this option to download the success logs for a
recovery run. 9. Click Recover.
Protect vCD resources using the Cohesity vCD Plugin
Cohesity Plugin for VMware vCloud Director enables cloud providers to offer data protection as a service in multi-tenant environments. The vCD Plugin provides a seamless experience by facilitating backup and recovery operations in the same vCD console. It delivers selfservice securely through role-based access control. The vCD Plugin's integrated data protection service streamlines operations and provides a rich tenant experience.

Data Protection using the Cohesity vCD plugin involves the following steps:
1. Ensure that you meet the requirements. 2. Manage access to the tenants and providers. 3. Setup the Cohesity vCD Plugin
a. Register vCD as a source with the Cohesity cluster b. Enable Multi-tenancy on Cohesity cluster c. Create Organizations and Map to vCD Source d. Install the Cohesity vCD plugin e. Configure the Cluster and Map Tenants 4. Backup vCD Objects For details on how to protect, a single vCD object or multiple objects as a tenant, see Backup VMs, vApps, or vApp Templates. 5. Recover vCD Objects

l Restore VMs l Restore vApps l Restore Files or Folders Prerequisites for Cohesity vCD Plugin The prerequisites are as follows: l Signed and trusted certificate must be installed on the Cohesity cluster. l Cohesity cluster must be accessible through port 443.

For detailed information about the necessary privileges, see Create a Role with Necessary vCenter Server Privileges.
When specifying a Windows Active Directory username, use the following format: <domain>\<username> or <username>@domain. For all other cases, just enter: <username>.
l Password: Enter the password for the vCenter.
l Detect VM migration across vCenter to Preserve backup chain: Toggle this option on if you want your Cohesity cluster to detect the VMs that are migrated from the current VMware vCenter to vCD.

Partial Refresh of the vCD Souce
You can perform a partial refresh of the vCD source using the API. A partial refresh is faster than a full source refresh. This enhancement allows you to selectively discover new VMs, vApps, Organizations, Org VDC, and vApp templates through the APIs into the vCD source, eliminating the need to wait for a full vCD refresh. You can refresh only the selected objects, such as specific VMs, vApps, Organizations, Org VDC, and vApp templates within the vCD source. To do a partial refresh of the vCD source using the API:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

Endpoint
PUT /v2/data-protect/sources/{sourceId}/objects

Parameters

Parameter sourceId

Type integer

Required Yes

Description The Entity ID of the data protection source

Finding the sourceId
You can find the sourceId from the UI by navigating to the Sources page and clicking your desired vCD source. The URL will appear in the following format:
https://<Cluster IP>/protections/sources/details/{sourceId}/objects?environment=kVMware
The `{sourceId}` is the numeric ID you need for the API call. This value remains constant until the source is unregistered.

Headers

Header Content-Type Authorization

Type string string

Required Yes Yes

Description Must be `application/json` Bearer token for authentication

Request Body
The request body should include a JSON object with the following structure:
JSON {
"modificationRequests": [ {
"actionType": "Add", "vcdModifyParams": {
"urn": "string"

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

} } ] }

Field

Type

modificationRequests

array

modificationRequests[].actionType object

modificationRequests [].vcdModifyParams

string

modificationRequests [].vcdModifyParams.urn

string

Required Yes Yes Yes
Yes

Description Array of modification requests to process. Action to perform. Valid values: `Add`. vCD-specific parameters for the modification.
The URN (Uniform Resource Name) of the VCD object to be discovered

vCD URN Format
VCD URNs follow the format: `urn:vcloud:{type}:{uuid}` Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. The common VCD object types:
l `vapp` - Virtual Application l `vm` - Virtual Machine l `vapptemplate` - vApp Template l `org` - Organization l vdc` - Virtual Datacenter To Perform a Partial Refresh: 1. Authenticate: Obtain Access Token using Authentication API:
POST /irisservices/api/v1/public/accessTokens 2. Get Source ID of the vCD source as described above. 3. Discovery request API .
PUT /v2/data-protect/sources/{sourceId}/objects

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

Example Requests
1. Discover a new VM.
curl --location --request PUT 'https://10.136.5.86/v2/data-protect/sources/1/objects' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN_HERE' \ --data '{
"modificationRequests": [ { "actionType": "Add", "vcdModifyParams": { "urn": "urn:vcloud:vm:96228d49-a079-4b0e-a19f-c5e78acd65b1" } } ] }'
2. Discover a new VCD org.
JSON {
curl --location --request PUT 'https://10.136.5.86/v2/data-protect/sources/1/objects' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN_HERE' \ --data '{ "modificationRequests": [ { "actionType": "Add", "vcdModifyParams": { urn": "urn:vcloud:org:96228d48-a079-4b0e-a19f-f5e78acd65b1" } } ] }

JSON {
"results": [ {

Note: l You can include multiple objects in the modificationRequests array to process

l Hierarchical Dependencies: When you add a vApp, OrgVDC, or Organization, all descendant entities are automatically included.
l vCD Hierarchy: The system adheres to the vCD organizational hierarchy (Organization VDC vApp/vAppTemplate VM) when processing modifications.

Discover VMs

1. Log into the vCD Console as a tenant user. 2. Navigate to Data Protection > vApps or VMs. 3. Check the status of all the VMs in the Protection Status field. 4. If the status is Undiscovered for any VM, click Discover. This initiates a refresh
operation on the vCD source.
Note: After upgrading the vCD plugin, you must manually refresh the vCD source before you start protecting your vCD objects.
