Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

Protect Individual VMs, vApps, and vApp Templates
To protect a specific vCD object, you must first create a Protection Group following the process below. To protect individual VMs, vApps, and vApp Templates:
1. Log into the vCD Console as a tenant user. 2. Navigate to Data Protection > vApps or VMs. 3. Use the Org vDC and Object Type filter on the top to list to filter the objects based
on the selected vDC or choose from the listed VMs, vApps, and vApp Templates. Verify the status of the object in the Protection Status column. If any of the objects that you want to back up are in an Undiscovered state, then you must first discover that object. See Backup VMs, vApps, or vApp Templates. Once the status of the object changes to Unprotected, click on the ellipsis ( ) on the row for the unprotected object and select Protect VM (or vApp or vApp Template). If you choose AutoProtect Object (for a vApp or vApp Template), any VM that belongs to that object or any new VM created in that object will be protected automatically. 4. Click Create New Group in the Protect Object window. If you already have one, you can select an existing Protection Group instead. 5. Configure the Protection Group details and click Save.
Note: For more information on Leverage SAN Transport, see SAN Transport.
6. The Protection Status is updated as Protected.

SAN Transport
Leverage SAN Transport for Data Protection: Cohesity supports SAN transport for Fibre Channel (FC) and iSCSI-based storage arrays and datastores that contain such storage arrays. Turn on this option to enable the SAN transport mode over FC or iSCSI for backing up VMware VMs to the Cohesity cluster.
Note: Using the Leverage SAN Transport for Data Protection option with the Leverage Storage Snapshots for Data Protection option is not recommended.
To use the SAN transport mode over FC, ensure the following pre-requirement:
l Fibre channel is installed and zoned appropriately between the Cohesity cluster and the primary storage (Pure Flash Array and HPE Nimble Storage Array).
To use the SAN transport mode over FC, ensure the following pre-requirement:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

VMware vCloud Director (vCD)

l Volumes are mapped appropriately between the Cohesity cluster, ESXi hosts, and the primary storage. You can turn on the Allow NBDSSL Transport Fallback toggle if you do not want to enforce strict SAN transport mode for backing up VMware to the Cohesity cluster. With toggle enabled, backup will not fail if SAN transport is not available. If you disable this toggle, the backup will fail if the SAN transport mode is unavailable.
Note: l Fallback to NBD is no longer supported if NBDSSL fails or is disabled. l Ensure that the storage array connects to the primary environment (host) and the Cohesity node over the same protocol (FC on both ends or iSCSI on both ends). Cohesity does not support SAN transport for SAS (Serial Attached SCSI) based storage arrays.
l VMware SAN transport mode is not supported with Cohesity virtual nodes. To use SAN transport mode for backing up VMware VMs, zoning and granting datastores access to the Cohesity nodes has to be done manually. VMware SAN transport mode is not supported with Cohesity virtual nodes.

OpenStack
OpenStack is an open-source cloud computing platform that provides Infrastructure-as-aService (IaaS) for compute, storage, networking, and identity at scale. It is widely used by service providers, telecom operators, and large enterprises for private and managed clouds.
Protection of OpenStack VMs using Cohesity
OpenStack-native snapshot facilities (Nova, Cinder, Glance) are effective for short-term operational rollback, but they are not a complete enterprise data-protection solution. Cohesity protects OpenStack VMs through an integration with Storware: Storware acts as

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

OpenStack

the OpenStack-aware orchestrator and data mover, while Cohesity DataProtect provides the secure, scalable, policy-driven backup repository. In this solution, a Cohesity SmartFiles NFS 4.1 View is used as the Storware staging space and backup destination.
Note: OpenStack protection is delivered through a third-party integration with Storware. Storware-specific configuration is performed in Storware and documented in the Storware documentation; this guide focuses on the Cohesityside actions and references Storware where appropriate.
OpenStack-native snapshots lack the enterprise data-protection characteristics that customers require. The integration addresses the following gaps:

Capability

Enterprise Need

Gap with OpenStack-Native Snapshots

Cyber resilience

Immutable, isolated, encrypted backup copies

Native snapshots do not adequately protect against ransomware and malicious data destruction.

Retention management

Long-term retention with compliance support

Snapshots are short-term and often stored on the same underlying storage as production.

TCO

Deduplication and compression to optimize storage and cost

Native snapshots add storage overhead and fragmented management.

Disaster recovery

Geographically distributed protection Limited DR orchestration and cross-site recovery.

Long-term archival

Archival tiers and tape for compliance

No integrated support for archival workflows, tape export, or tiering.

Visibility and reporting

Centralized reporting, monitoring, chargeback

Native snapshots lack centralized governance and analytics.

Enterprise-wide protection

Unified protection across many workloads

Native snapshots are platform-specific, creating operational silos.

Storware uses a disaggregated architecture consisting of a Storware server (UI and API) and one or more Storware nodes that connect to the OpenStack source, move data, and run backup and restore operations. Storware does not provide its own storage; the nodes mount a Cohesity SmartFiles NFS 4.1 View and use it as the filesystem backup destination.
During backup, Storware nodes read VM data from OpenStack and write it to the Cohesity NFS View. During recovery, the nodes read the selected recovery point from the Cohesity View and restore the VM (or files) back to OpenStack. For NFS/filesystem backups,

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

OpenStack

Storware uses the same NFS share for both staging and backup, avoiding a separate staging copy.

l Plan and prepare for OpenStack VMs protection through an integration with Storware and Cohesity. For more information, see Plan and Prepare for OpenStack VMs Protection with Storware and Cohesity.
l Configure NFS 4.1 view in Cohesity. For more information, see Plan and Prepare for OpenStack VMs Protection .
l Backup OpenStack VMs with Storware and Cohesity. For more information, see Backup OpenStack VMs.
l Recover OpenStack with Storware and Cohesity. For more information, see Recover OpenStack VMs.

Plan and Prepare for OpenStack VMs Protection
This topic helps Cohesity users plan and prepare a joint Storware along with Cohesity DataProtect solution for OpenStack VM protection. It focuses on Cohesity-related preparation and links to Storware documentation for Storware-specific configuration.

l Network connectivity from the Cohesity cluster to the Storware nodes on NFS ports 111 and 2049.

Considerations
l Storware advises scheduling no more than 10 tasks per Storware node. l Keypairs the Storware user cannot access are not protected or recovered; restore
them manually under the same name. l A Storware node is required in each Availability Zone that needs protection. l Protection policies are independent chains, and a VM/instance can belong to only one
policy. l Storware retains one backup copy indefinitely as long as the source exists. l For NFS (filesystem) backups, a separate staging directory is not required; staging
and destination share the same NFS share.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

l If the primary backup location task fails, secondary targets are not attempted. l NFS recoveries are not instant because merge operations are required to hydrate
images. l Snapshots are garbage-collected once a day (configurable in Global Settings).
For the complete and current list of considerations, supported features, and limitations, see Storware OpenStack documentation.
Best Practices
l Back up the Storware internal database. Without it, backups can be lost if the Storware server node must be redeployed.
l When OpenStack uses an NFS storage backend, enable QCOW2 file support in the Cinder configuration so backup snapshots create QCOW2 files instead of RAW.
l Place backup storage on the same network or close to the Storware nodes for high throughput.
l Size the solution using the backup window, network bandwidth, storage type, and largest VM size; scale Storware nodes up or down as needed.
Configuration of NFS 4.1 View in Cohesity
1. Prepare the SmartFiles View 1. In Cohesity DataProtect, create a SmartFiles View for use as the Storware backup target. 2. Use Category: Backup Target; Type: General Backup; Read/Write Protocol: NFS 4.1; Performance Policy: Backup Target High. 3. Use a clear naming convention such as OpenStack-<region>-Storware or OpenStack-<tenant>-BackupTarget. 4. Record the NFS export path in the form <Cohesity_Cluster_Hostname_or_ VIP>:/<NFS_View_Name>.
For more information see, SmartFiles (File and Object Services). 2. Restrict NFS Access
1. Create either a global or view-level subnet allowed list for the SmartFiles View. 2. Allow only the Storware server/node subnets that require read/write access. 3. Avoid broad 0.0.0.0/0 access except for temporary lab validation. 3. Validate Network Requirements

Backup OpenStack VMs
Storware initiates and orchestrates OpenStack VM backups and writes backup data to the Cohesity SmartFiles NFS 4.1 View mounted on the Storware nodes.
Backup Architecture
l Storware initiates and orchestrates OpenStack VM backup activities.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

OpenStack

l Cohesity SmartFiles NFS 4.1 View is mounted on Storware nodes and used as the filesystem backup destination.
l For NFS/filesystem-based backups, the Storware can use the same NFS share for staging and backup storage, avoiding a separate staging directory.
Cohesity Backup Target Setup
Complete these Cohesity-specific steps before creating or running Storware backup policies:
1. Create the SmartFiles View as Backup Target > General Backup, with NFS 4.1 and Backup Target High performance policy.
2. Apply a subnet allowed list that allows the Storware node subnet(s) to access the view.
3. Share the NFS export path with the Storware administrator. 4. Confirm the Storware node OS user/group ownership requirement is met on the
mount point before backup execution.
Reference Mount Command
Use the following as the reference, after replacing the placeholders with values specific to your environment.
mount -t nfs -o rw,relatime,vers=4.1,rsize=1048576,wwsize=1048576,namlen=255,hard,proto=tcp,timeo=600,retrans=2,sec=sys <Cohesity_Cluster_Hostname_or_VIP>:/<NFS_View_Name> <View_Mount_Path>
For persistence across reboot, add the equivalent mount line to /etc/fstab after validating the mount manually.
Configure Backup in Storware
Perform the following in the Storware UI. Refer to the Storware documentation for detailed steps:
1. Upload the Storware license and run the configuration wizard; verify the Storware nodes are visible.
2. Choose OpenStack as the hypervisor and register the source with the Keystone API URL, region, endpoint type, and authentication domain settings.
3. Select Backup Destination type File System and enter the mount point where the Cohesity SmartFiles View is mounted.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 12: Virtual Machines

OpenStack

4. Create a backup policy: select projects/instances, configure retention and schedule (each schedule is an independent snapshot chain), and target the configured nodes.
5. Optionally test a small instance backup before broad rollout, and adjust the maximum tasks per node if needed.
Cohesity Validation Before Running Backups

Validation

Expected Result

NFS mount from Storware node

Mount succeeds and is read/write.

File creation test on mounted path Test file can be created and removed by the vprotect user/group.

Cohesity View access policy

Only intended Storware subnets are allowed.

Performance baseline

Initial small VM backup completes without NFS errors before broad policy rollout.

Capacity monitoring

SmartFiles capacity and growth are monitored during initial full backups.

Operational Guidance
l Start with a small VM backup to validate end-to-end connectivity, permissions, and backup target behavior.
l Scale concurrency carefully. Storware advises scheduling no more than 10 tasks per Storware node.
l If node count or load is too high, stagger full backups across multiple schedules and policies to reduce peak throughput demand.
l For NFS-based backups, reads from the source are limited by the write speed of the backup destination, because staging and destination share the same NFS share.
l Monitor backup target utilization, throughput, and errors from both Cohesity and Storware during the first production backup cycles.
Verification list for backup completion
l Initial test backup completed successfully.
l Backup data appears on the Cohesity SmartFiles View.
l Backup policy retention and cadence match the agreed protection plan.
l At least one restore validation is scheduled after the first successful backup.
l Storware internal database backup is included in the operational plan (backups can be lost if the Storware server node must be redeployed without its database).

Recover OpenStack VMs
Storware performs the OpenStack-aware recovery workflow and recreates the VM in OpenStack based on the selected recovery point and restore options. Cohesity provides the backup repository through the SmartFiles NFS View that contains the Storware backup data. Prerequisites
l Verify the Cohesity cluster and SmartFiles View are online and reachable from the Storware node.
l Confirm NFS mount access using the same mount point used during backup operations.
l Confirm the View still permits read/write access from the Storware node subnet.
l Validate sufficient capacity and performance headroom for recovery operations.
l For isolated or alternate-environment tests, confirm routing and DNS/IP reachability to the Cohesity cluster/VIP.
To recover OpenStack:
1. Confirm the Cohesity SmartFiles View used as the backup destination is accessible from the Storware node.
2. In Storware, select the VM recovery point and recovery mode (recovery to virtualization provider, VM instance mount, or file-level recovery) per the Storware documentation.
3. During recovery, monitor Cohesity-side NFS availability, throughput, and any View access errors.
4. After Storware reports completion, validate from OpenStack that the VM was recreated and is reachable according to the restore objective.
5. Document the recovered VM name, target project, target flavor, target network, recovery point used, and any deviations from the original VM configuration.
Recovery Options in the Storeware UI:

Chapter 13: Databases

Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora

Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora
You can use a Protection Group to back up Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) database instances and Amazon Aurora. Supported database engines include PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle Database, and SQL Server. Cohesity protects the data using RDS snapshots (no data is stored on the cluster).
Prerequisite
For replicating encrypted RDS snapshots from one location to another:
l The KMS key Aliases used to encrypt the RDS snapshots in the source location must be available in the target location.
l The IAM user/role used to register the target source must have access to the KMS key at the target location.
Considerations
l The backup and recovery of Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora at instance level (snapshot-based protection) is supported on physical clusters, virtual edition clusters, and Cohesity Cloud Editions.
l The backup and recovery of Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora at database level (ingest-based protection) is supported only on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS.
l Cohesity uses the Amazon RDS API to take snapshots according to the scheduled protection policy.
l Cohesity supports automated and manual RDS snapshots. l You can restore the backups to the original location or a new location. l Cohesity does not support recovery to different accounts with different regions but
recovery to different accounts with the same region, the same account with the same region, and the same account with different regions are supported. l Point in time recovery is supported only if you enable automated backups on the RDS instance. You can select a time and restore the database instance to the time selected. Automated backups occur once daily at the time selected. You can restore to any point in time within your backup retention period. l Amazon Aurora Serverless backups are not supported. l Recovery of an RDS instance encrypted with the default CMK (Customer Managed Key) to a different account is not supported as AWS does not support sharing a snapshot that is encrypted using the default KMS key of the AWS account. l You cannot recover an Amazon RDS database to the same or alternate location if the name of the database you are restoring and at the target location are the same. Before you begin
When you create a Protection Group, you can select an existing source, policy, or storage domain. You can also create them while creating the Protection Group. However, you might find it easier to create them prior to creating the Protection Group, as described in the following topics.
l Register or Edit a Hypervisor Source l Create or Edit a Standard Policy l Create or Edit Storage Domains
To create a Protection Group for Amazon RDS:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection and do one of the following: l To create a Protection Group--Click Protect on the top-right of the page and then select the type of Protection Group.
l To edit a Protection Group--Click the action icon ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit.
If creating a Protection Group for Amazon RDS, select Databases > Amazon RDS. If creating a Protection Group for Amazon Aurora, select Databases > Amazon Aurora. 2. Name: Enter a name for the Protection Group. The name can contain alphanumeric characters, underscores, dashes, and periods. 3. Source: Select the database you want to protect. You can also register a new source with the Cohesity cluster so you can protect it. 1. Select the source objects to back up or exclude. By default, all objects in the source
are excluded as indicated by the unselected check box. Expand the source objects and select the objects you want to include in the Protection Group. A selected check
box ( ) indicates the object is selected to be backed up. 2. Use the filtering options to tailor the list of servers. You can also filter the objects
based on the tags by clicking the Tags icon and selecting the required tag from the Tags drop-down list. 3. Click the arrow adjacent to the Object (Expand All) to expand the entire Object hierarchy. Click the arrow again (Collapse All) to collapse the entire Object hierarchy. 4. The graphical representations in the table are described below.
When creating a new Protection Group, a shield next to the Object name indicates the Object is already been protected by another Protection Group.
Click the icon to see details about the object.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora

If the object name is in red, it is inaccessible, invalid, or orphaned. If the object is in one of the specified states when the Protection Group runs, no snapshot is created. If the object becomes accessible, a snapshot is created the next time the Protection Group runs.
5. Click Save Selection.
6. Policy: Select an existing protection policy or create a new one by selecting New Policy.
Note: For Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora snapshot protection, the actual snapshot remains on AWS and metada about the snapshot is stored in the cohesity cluster. The data lock policy applies to the metadata stored within Cohesity. Changes made from the AWS end for the snapshots cannot be controlled by Cohesity
The selected Storage Domain will contain the new View where the script results are stored.
7. Start Time: Indicates when the Protection Group should run. The current time is displayed by default but you can change it. Enter the hour and minutes or use the up and down arrows on your keyboard. Verify the AM or PM setting.
The default time zone is the browser's time zone. You can change the time zone by selecting a different time zone.
8. End Date: Optional. Toggle on and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.
9. Cancel Runs at Quiet Time Start: Available only if the selected policy has at least one quiet time period. Toggle it on to specify that all currently executing protection runs should abort if a quiet time period specified for the Protection Group starts. By default this toggle is off, which means after a protection run starts, it continues to execute even when a quiet time period specified for this protection run starts. However, a new protection run will not start during a quiet time period.
10. Alerts: Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Create an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Create a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora

For more information, see Alerts. 11. Priority: Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity supports
concurrent backups, but if the number of Protection Groups exceeds the ability to process them, those with High priority are given the highest priority to execute, Medium the second-highest priority, and Low the lowest priority. 12. Email Recipients: You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the Protection Group.
Note: The connection to the SMTP Server must be enabled to send email notification. You can enable the SMTP Server connection in the configuration settings page ( Cohesity UI > Settings > Summary > Configure > Enable SMTP Server).
13. SLA: The service-level agreement (SLA) defines the expected time to complete either a full backup or incremental backup. The backup completion time depends on the Windows volume size on AD, objects changed between incremental backups, network speed, and other Protection Groups running on the Cohesity cluster. l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental protection run to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last protection run. l Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup protection run to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).
14. Description: Optional. Click the plus sign and enter a description for the Protection Group.
15. Click Protect. The Protection page is displayed and includes the new Protection Group.
Recover Amazon RDS or Amazon Aurora
Cohesity provides the ability to recover the Amazon RDS database or Amazon Aurora to its original location or an alternate location. For more information, see:
l Recover Amazon RDS or Amazon Aurora to the Original location l Recover Amazon RDS or Amazon Aurora to an Alternate Location
Recover Amazon RDS or Amazon Aurora to the Original location
To recover the Amazon RDS or Amazon Aurora to the original location:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora

1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Recoveries.
2. Click Recover at the top right of the page and then select Databases > Amazon RDS.
The Amazon RDS page appears.
3. Search for the database you want to recover by entering the characters of the database name or by specifying the wildcard character *.
A list of VMs displays.
You can optionally filter the search results by Source, Protection Group, Storage Domain, or Date.
4. From the list of search results, select the database you want to recover.
By default, the latest snapshot is selected for recovery.
5. To recover from a different snapshot, mouse over the snapshot from the selected list, and then click the edit icon.
The Edit recovery point for <VM_name> page appears.
By default, the option to select the snapshot is displayed in Timeline mode. You can also choose to view the option in List mode by clicking the List tab in the top-right corner of the page.
l To select a snapshot from the Timeline mode:
a. From the Choose a date drop-down, select a date for the recovery point.
b. The snapshots available on the selected date are displayed in blue dots on the timeline bar.
c. Select the snapshot to be recovered by clicking the corresponding blue dot on the timeline bar.
If multiple snapshots are available, then you can choose any point in timeline (Point-in-Time snapshot) between the two snapshots either by adjusting the timeline bar or by selecting the time from the timer field. If you have selected an invalid time, then the nearest valid snapshot will be selected for recovery.
d. Click Select Recovery Point and then go to step 6.
l To select a snapshot from the List mode:
a. Select the List tab from the top-right corner of the Edit recovery point for <VM_name> page.
b. By default, the page displays the snapshots available in the last one month.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora

c. You can also select a snapshot from a different date range by selecting the date range from the Date drop-down list. The page displays the available snapshots in the specified range.
d. Select the snapshot to be recovered.
e. Click Select Recovery Point and then go to step 6.
6. Click Next: Recover Options.
7. From the Recover To options, select Original Location to recover the Amazon RDS to the original location.
8. Provide the following Network Settings information:
1. VPC: Select an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) to store the recovered RDS.
2. Subnet: From the drop-down list, select a subnet in the Amazon VPC to store the recovered Amazon RDS.
3. Availability Zone: From the drop-down list, select an availability zone in AWS to recover the RDS.
9. Configure the following Additional Settings:
The Database Engine field auto-populates the database engine name used for this instance.
1. Database Instance Identifier: Specify the unique key that identifies the database instance that will be recovered.
2. DB Port: Specify the TCP/IP port that the DB instance will use for application connections. The connection string of any application connecting to the DB instance must specify the port number of the DB instance. Both the security group applied to the instance and your company's firewalls must allow connections to this port.
3. DB Option Group: Select an option group that contains the option you want to attach to the DB instance that will be recovered. If there are not any option groups compatible with the selected engine, a default group will be created at launch.
4. DB Parameter Group: Select the database parameter group to associate with the DB instance.
5. Multi A-Z Deployment: Enable this option if you want the DB instance to be recovered to have a standby instance deployed in another availability zone. This option is disabled by default.
6. IAM DB Authentication: Enable this option if you want to manage your database user credentials through AWS IAM users and roles. This option is disabled by default.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Amazon RDS and Amazon Aurora

7. Public Accessibility: Enable this option if you want the DB instance to also have a public IP address in addition to the private IP address. This option is disabled by default.
8. Copy Tags To Snapshots: Enable this option for copying tags to snapshots. This option is disabled by default.
9. Auto Minor Version Upgrade: Enable this option if you want the DB instance to automatically upgrade when a new minor database engine version is available. This option is disabled by default.
10. Optional. Change the default name of the recovery task in the Task Name field. 11. Click Start Recovery.
The recovery process is initiated. You can monitor the recovery task from the Recoveries page.

Cassandra
28 July 2026
The Cohesity Cassandra DataProtect solution natively integrates with Apache Cassandra and Datastax Enterprise to provide consistent backup and recovery for clustered Cassandra deployments. See the following topics for details:
Based on the policy settings, the Cohesity NoSQL and Hadoop Service initiates a backup of the Cassandra Database. The initial protection run/first backup is a full-backup and everything after that is an incremental backup only. The service automatically determines the number of backup channels, based on the compute resources on Cohesity and the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

topology of the Cassandra cluster. The necessary Cohesity Views are automatically generated where the backups are going to be written. Communication between Cohesity and the Cassandra Databases is managed by the NoSQL and Hadoop Service as described in the section below.
Core components
The following lists the core components of the Cohesity Cassandra solution:
l Physical or virtual Cassandra instance. l Cohesity Data Cloud. l Cohesity Compute Nodes. l Cohesity NoSQL and Hadoop Service running on Cohesity Compute Nodes. l Optional. Archive or tiering target at your data center or cloud provider of choice.
As illustrated in the figure below, you can integrate Cohesity with an existing Cassandra infrastructure by installing the Cohesity NoSQL and Hadoop Service on Compute Nodes. Once the service is installed and running, you can create protection policies, and Protection Groups for the Cassandra database. Once the database is protected, it can be archived, sent to tape, and or replicated to another instance running in the cloud or on-premises as shown in the image below.

Cassandra Features
Following are the key Cassandra-specific features of the solution:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

l Incremental-forever backups - after the first full backup, all subsequent backups are incremental only forever
l Granular backup and recovery - backup and recover tables or keyspaces l Schema & data backed up and restored l Multi-DC aware - option to back up data from a local data center l Optimized restore - much faster recovery if Cassandra cluster topology is unchanged l Backup & Recover DSE Solr indexes l Handle topology changes seamlessly (node addition, removal, IP changes, etc.) l Support Kerberos and LDAP authenticated clusters l Support SSL-enabled clusters l Change schema on restore

SSL Enabled Cassandra Clusters
Steps Required to Support SSL Enabled Cassandra Clusters
The cassandra.yaml file is the main configuration file for Cassandra. Check the following SSL options in the cassandra yaml file:
l client_encryption_options (Client-to-node encryption) l enabled: By default, the enabled option is set to False. If the enabled option is set to True, then you must Setting up truststore:. l require_client_auth: By default, the require_client_auth is set to False. If the require_client_auth is set to True, then you must Setting up keystore and import them in all Cassandra nodes, and restart Cassandra services for the changes to take effect
l server_encryption_options (Node-to-node encryption) l internode_encryption: If this option is set to all, dc or rack, then you must copy Cassandra certificates into NoSQL and Hadoop Services TrustStore using imanis_cli.sh -c ssl.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

l require_client_auth: By default, the require_client_auth is set to False. If set to true, then you must copy NoSQL and Hadoop Services SSL certificates into every Cassandra nodes TrustStore and restart Cassandra node for the changes to take effect.
l Additionally, if encryption is enabled for JMX communication, the truststore and keystore parameters are specified in cassandra-env.sh using the following JVM options: l javax.net.ssl.keyStore l javax.net.ssl.keyStorePassword l javax.net.ssl.trustStore l javax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword Use the values from these options to create SSL certificates and import them into the NoSQL and Hadoop Service truststore, following the same process as client_ encryption_options or server_encryption_options.

Setting the Number of Open Files Limit for Cassandra
The default setting for the number of open files in Cassandra primary is 1024. Please set the number of open files to 100,000 by running the following command on the Cassandra primary. ulimit -n 100000
Note: Without this step you may face an error on the Primary cluster while executing Cassandra restore.
Enabling JMX
Enable remote JMX connection on all the Cassandra nodes before you add Cassandra as a source. Cassandra DataProtect Solution connects to the primary using the remote JMX connection so a local JMX cannot be used in this case.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

Note: You need to use the same JMX credentials on all Cassandra nodes that belong to the same source/cluster.
To enable JMX:
1. Enable the Remote JMX connection: For Cassandra 2.0.14 (2.0 branch) and Cassandra 2.1.4 (2.1 branch) onwards.
2. Access the cassandra-env.sh from the Cassandra configuration directory on all the Cassandra nodes and set ["$LOCAL_JMX" = "yes"] entry to "no".
3. For the default DSE installation, the preceding file is available in /etc/dse/cassandra. 4. For a successful data source discovery in DSE 6.7.x, the following parameter must be
set in /etc/dse/cassandra/cassandra-env.sh. "JVM_OPTS"="JVM_OPTS -Djava.rmi.server.hostname=<ip>" 5. Restart Cassandra services.
Note: If JMX communication is SSL-encrypted, see Steps Required to Support SSL Enabled Cassandra Clusters for information on importing the corresponding SSL certificates.
Considerations
l For users who have their Cassandra cluster set up with public address = rpc_ address/broadcast_rpc_address and private address = listen_address, for DSE below 6.x (5.x and below), a bulk restore will not work if the private IPs for the Cassandra nodes are not accessible by the Cohesity cluster (SCP restore will work as expected).
l Users must refresh a data source when configuration settings of the data source are modified. For example, if changes are made to cassandra.yaml, cassandra-env.sh, or dse.yaml file of a data source, then the data source must be re-discovered and reverified.
l Backup is not supported for the following system keyspaces: l system l system_auth l system_distributed l system_schema l system_traces l dse_leases

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

l dse_perf l dse_security l dse_system l solr_admin l dse_insights_local l dse_insights l dse_system_local l system_virtual_schema l system_views l system_backups
Note: The system_auth and system_schema keyspaces are not protected as part of the regular auto-protection job. Although these keyspaces may appear as protected in the Protected Objects and All Objects tabs on the Sources page when auto-protect is enabled, protection of system keyspaces is not supported as part of regular protection jobs. To back up these keyspaces, create a separate protection job by enabling the Backup System Keyspaces option on the New Protection page.
l Restore of system keyspaces such as OpsCenter is only supported for the same cluster from which it was backed up.
l Backup and recovery of system keyspaces and of keyspaces using SimpleStrategy are not supported in hybrid Cassandra environments, because these keyspaces require access to all data centers for consistent backup and restore operations.
l Backup and recovery of tables containing semicolon (';') in the column name is not supported.
l Data recovery from Cassandra 2.x to 3.x is not supported if the backed-up tables contain dropped columns.
l For Cassandra 2.x or DSE 4.x, backup recovery is not supported for tables where all columns are part of the Primary Key.
l Appending suffix is not supported while restoring graph objects. This is because individual graph keyspaces cannot be renamed. This issue occurs during the jobtag recovery process when the global suffix is applied to all keyspaces thus wrongly renaming the '_system' keyspace for a graph. For example, we need to back up two types of keyspaces for a graph. If the name of the graph is `exampleGraph', then we should back up `exampleGraph' and `exampleGraph_system'. However, during jobtag

Protect Cassandra Objects Cassandra Objects are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group enables you to select the objects that you want to back up. It uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured, retained, archived, and replicated. A Protection Policy is a reusable list of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. Also, for disaster recovery, you can add replication for the Protection Group using the Protection Policy. For detailed instructions on how to create a Protection Policy, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy. To protect a Cassandra object:
1. Data Protection > Protection. 2. Click Protect on the top-right of the page and then select Databases > Cassandra.

4. Data Centers: Select the required Data Center from the drop-down menu. 5. Log Backup Selection: Toggle on the Log Backup setting to schedule a backup of
the log archives of the Cassandra source.
Note: l Once Log Backup is enabled you cannot select any objects. l You can only create one Log Backup Protection Group for a Cassandra source.
6. Select the required objects to protect.
Note: This option is available only if the Log Backup Selection toggle setting is off.

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy.
Note: Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.
l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Protection Groups.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve a similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

l SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created. For more information, see Alerts.

Enable or Disable Auto Protect
The Auto Protect option enables you to automatically protect the objects that are added to the Cassandra source. You can auto protect either the entire cluster or a Keyspace.

Note: When auto-protect is enabled on the entire Cassandra source, the system_ auth and system_schema keyspaces may appear as protected in the Protected Objects and All Objects tabs on the Sources page. However, protection of system keyspaces is not supported as part of regular protection jobs. To protect system keyspaces, create a separate protection job by enabling the Backup System Keyspaces option on the New Protection page.

When the Auto Protect option is enabled:
l All the objects that are added to the Cassandra source in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run.
l All the objects that are removed from the Cassandra source in the future are automatically removed from the Protection Group and are not protected from the next protection run. The existing backups are preserved until the snapshot expires.
When the Auto Protect option is disabled, you need to manually:
l Add newly added objects in the Cassandra source to the Protection Group. l Remove existing objects that are removed from the Cassandra source. The existing
backups are preserved until the snapshot expires.
To enable or disable Auto Protect:
1. Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for
Cassandra. For more information, see Protect Cassandra Objects.
3. Click next to the Protection Group and select Edit. 4. On the Edit Protection page, in the Object area, click Edit.

Enable/Disable Megafile support
Megafile feature improves Cassandra backup/restore task performance by copying mega files (greater 32 GB in size) by splitting them into subfiles and copying the subfiles in parallel. It requires a modified version of SCP binary on the primary nodes to achieve this. By enabling this feature, you allow the NoSQL and Hadoop Service to copy this binary to primary cluster nodes on demand and execute them as needed.
Note: The directory to copy the binary should be accessible by the user to allow the backup/restore functionality to work. You may also need to explicitly allow this executable in puppet/chef tools (if required).
Run imanis_cli tool from any Cohesity node where the NoSQL and Hadoop Service is running. $ imanis_cli.sh -c megafile --help INFO : Checking reachability of pod imanis-nodemanager-0 --------------------------------------------------------------------imanis_cli.sh -c megafile --connector <cname> [--workdir <dirpath>] --enable true|false --connector value can be cassandra-backup or cassandra-restore --workdir value will be the directory path on primary cluster where talena-scp will be copied NOTE: --workdir is not needed in case of '--enable false' --workdir is optional in case of cassandra-restore ---------------------------------------------------------------------
Enable Megafile support Run the following commands to enable megafile support: $ imanis_cli.sh -c megafile --connector cassandra-backup --workdir /data/binaries/talenascp --enable true INFO : Checking reachability of pod imanis-nodemanager-0 NOTE: Megafile feature improves the performance of Cassandra backup/restore tasks by

Recover Cassandra
28 July 2026 You can recover the protected Cassandra Objects using Cohesity. You can recover to the same location or an alternate location.
Considerations
l Recovering at the protection group level is supported for Cassandra. l Recovering with a suffix at the protection group level applies the suffix to the leaf-
level objects in the selected protection group. l Recovering multiple protection groups in a single recovery task is not supported.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

l Recovering items in the same protection group but from different recovery points is not supported in the same recovery task. You need to create different recovery tasks for different recovery points.
l Recovering objects from more than one protection group in a single recovery task is not supported.
Recover Cassandra Objects
To recover Cassandra objects you can search through the backups using the protection group, keyspaces or table name for the objects you plan to recover, and then start the recovery. To recover Cassandra objects:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Recoveries. 2. Click Recover on the top-right of the page and then select Databases >
Cassandra. The Databases | Cassandra page appears. 3. Enter characters of the object name or Protection Group name or source name, or Use
Wildcard * in Search for Recovery. A list of protected items appears. You can optionally filter the search results by Source, Protection Group, or Storage Domain. 4. By default, the latest snapshot is selected for recovery. Perform the following steps to recover from a different snapshot:
1. From the selected list, hover the mouse pointer over the highlighted snapshot, and then click . The Edit recovery point page appears.
2. From the built-in calendar, select a date range. 3. Select the snapshot point for recovery. 4. Click Select Recovery Point. Perform the following steps to recover to a point in time: 1. From the selected list, hover the mouse pointer over the highlighted snapshot,
and then click . The Edit recovery point page appears. 2. Select Timeline view. 3. From the Choose a date drop-down, select a date. The snapshots available on the selected date are displayed in blue dots on the timeline bar. 4. For snapshot recovery, select the snapshot to be recovered by clicking the corresponding blue dot. You can also select any point from the green solid line

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

on the slider if you want to restore to a specific point in time. 5. Click Select Recovery Point. 5. Click Next: Recover Options. The recovery details are displayed. 6. Under Recover As select Replace Original, Modify Original, or New Object.
l Replace Original - Select the Data Center to replace the object(s) back to the source from where it was backed up.
l Modify Original - Choose this option and select the Data Centers to perform the object(s) restore on live Cassandra tables. This option allows you to skip truncate and retain the current Cassandra data while recovering objects.
Warning: The live Cassandra table restore operation may result in undesirable outcomes, ensure that you review and understand the recommendations and limitations before performing live table restore. For more information, see Considerations for Live Cassandra Table Restore.
l New Object: a. Target - Specify the target for the recovered object. b. Overwrite existing objects with the same name - Toggle this setting on if you want to overwrite existing objects with the same name. A warning is displayed, type YES to proceed.
7. Log Restore Directory: Specify the path of the directory on the Cassandra cluster to which you want to recover the commit logs. You must specify the same path for all Cassandra nodes.
Note: l The SSH user must have read and write permissions to the archive directory. l The user running the Cassandra process must have read permissions to the archive directory.
8. Staging Directory List: Specify the staging directory path to which you want to recover the files. You can specify one or more directories separated by comma.
Note: Applicable only when restoring DSE 6.x.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

You must create a script or command so that the Cassandra services can be either stopped or started with the appropriate credentials and permissions. l If the command is not provided: l For DSE, Cohesity uses nodetool stopdaemon API using remote JMX connection to Cassandra nodes to stop the Cassandra services. Cohesity runs the service dse start command as the SSH user to start the Cassandra services. l For Apache, Cohesity uses nodetool stopdaemon API using remote JMX connection to Cassandra nodes to stop the Cassandra services. Cohesity runs the <Config_Dir>/../bin/cassandra -R command as the SSH user to start the Cassandra services. b. Restart Immediately: Select this option to restart the Cassandra cluster immediately after recovery is complete. c. Restart On: Select this option if you want to schedule the restart of the Cassandra cluster on a specific date and time after recovery is complete. i. Description

Maximum number of recovery streams that will be created to exchange data with the cluster.
Maximum network bandwidth that each recovery stream can use for exchanging data with the cluster.
Recovery task name.

11. Click Start Recovery to start the recovery operation.
Considerations for Live Cassandra Table Restore
Review and understand the following recommendations and limitations before performing live table restore:
l Live Cassandra table restore can only be performed if you restore the objects on the same Cassandra cluster.
l Ensure you run Imanis Apps on all data centers where the Cassandra cluster will be deployed.
l During live Cassandra table restore operation, renaming or changing object properties is prohibited.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

l Point-in-time recovery (PITR) recovery is not supported. l Sequentially perform the restore operations. Only start live table restore on other
data centers once the expected restoration of one data center is successfully finished. l Live-table restore only applies to objects with a "NetworkTopologyStrategy" as the
replication strategy. l Live Cassandra table restore is only possible if the objects being restored exist in the
target Cassandra database. l Live table restore can only be performed if the schema of the objects to be restored is
the same as that of the backed-up objects. l To ensure efficient data restoration, Cohesity recommends taking backup snapshots
of different data centers, including the data center from which regular restores will be performed and the data centers from which live-table restores will be performed. These snapshots should be taken almost simultaneously and should contain similar objects. l If different snapshots have different objects, then live-table restore is only possible for those common objects present in all the snapshots. l Cohesity recommends replicating snapshots using a replication policy between clusters for both restore types (regular and live-table). l Live Cassandra table restore only applies if table properties (compaction & compression) match their backup properties. l Avoid using any mutation operation (insert/update/delete) on any objects (backed up by the same snapshot) after starting a regular restore on one data center and before completing the live-table restore on any other data center. l When performing a live-table restore, it is crucial to carefully choose the source cluster or data center from where the data will be restored. This will help ensure a successful restoration process.
Cassandra Instant Recovery
28 July 2026
Cassandra Instant Recovery is designed to significantly reduce the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for Apache Cassandra and DataStax Enterprise (DSE) clusters protected with Cohesity. By retaining native Cassandra snapshots on the original source nodes and coordinating recovery using those snapshots, Cohesity enables a near-immediate recovery experience.
Actual RTO can vary based on factors such as such as source cluster size, snapshot integrity, cluster health, network conditions, and whether any portion of the recovery must fall back to Cohesity-stored backups. For more information, see Continue on Error.
How Instant Recovery Works
During backup, Cohesity invokes the native Cassandra snapshot APIs and retains those snapshots on the original Cassandra source nodes instead of deleting them at the end of the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

backup cycle. As a result, two synchronized copies of each snapshot are maintained:
l One copy on the Cohesity cluster (primary backup copy).
l One copy on the original Cassandra source nodes (native source snapshot).
Because the native source snapshots remain available, Instant Recovery can directly reuse them without fully rehydrating data from the Cohesity cluster. Data rehydration refers to the traditional process of copying all backed-up data back from the Cohesity cluster to the source systems. By avoiding this step, Instant Recovery achieves substantially faster restore times.
Prerequisites
Before performing Cassandra Instant Recovery, ensure that all the following prerequisites are met:
l Configure Protection Policy with Native Source Snapshot Retention Instant Recovery requires keeping native snapshots on the Cassandra source cluster. This must be explicitly defined in the protection policy. To configure, see Configure Protection Policy with Native Source Snapshot Retention.
l Enable Preserve Native Snapshot in Protection Group Instant Recovery requires that snapshots be retained on the Cassandra source cluster. This setting must be explicitly enabled in the protection group. To configure, see Enable Preserve Native Snapshot in the Protection Group.
Considerations
l Verification of Source Snapshots
Cohesity verifies that valid native Cassandra snapshots exist on the source nodes before starting Instant Recovery. If required snapshots are missing or compromised, Instant Recovery cannot be completed solely from source snapshots. In such scenarios, the recovery behavior depends on how the backup job is configured:
l If the backup job is run without enabling Continue on Error, the job fails and notifies the user of the failure details, including affected nodes and snapshot files that are missing or compromised.
l If the backup job is run with Continue on Error enabled, the recovery can proceed by falling back to Cohesity-stored backup copies. This fallback may result in increased recovery time compared to recovery from native Cassandra snapshots.
l Source and Target Cassandra Clusters Must Match
Instant Recovery requires restoring data back to the same Cassandra cluster from which the backup was originally taken. Recovery to a different cluster is not supported.
l No Topology Changes Allowed

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

The Cassandra cluster's topology such as number of nodes, their IP addresses, token ranges, and data distribution must remain unchanged. In addition, the replication factor for each keyspace must match exactly between the source (at the time of backup) and the target environment during recovery. Cohesity validates both the cluster topology and keyspace replication factors at recovery time and prevents Instant Recovery if any mismatch is detected.
Limitations
Cassandra Instant Recovery does not support Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) or commitlog-based recovery.

Continue on Error
In a standard recovery, the Continue on Error option allows the recovery process to proceed even if some objects fail to recover. Instead of stopping the entire job, the system completes recovery for all valid objects and reports the failures separately. Instant Recovery relies on native snapshots present on Cassandra source nodes. In some cases, one or more snapshot files may be compromised, for example due to a checksum mismatch. If Continue on Error is NOT enabled:
l The Instant Recovery fails completely when compromised snapshot files are detected. l The system reports:
l Which snapshot files are compromised l Why the Instant Recovery failed
This ensures transparency and allows you to decide the next step. When to Use Continue on Error for Instant Recovery Use Continue on Error when:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

l You want to maximize recovery speed, even if some snapshot files are unusable. l You are willing to recover healthy data instantly and allow the system to fall back to
backup copies for problematic files.
How it Works with Instant Recovery When Continue on Error is enabled during Instant Recovery:
l All intact native snapshot files are recovered instantly from the Cassandra source nodes.
l Any compromised snapshot files are automatically recovered from the primary backup copy stored in the Cohesity cluster.
l The recovery completes successfully without stopping the entire job.
Note: In this scenario, not all files can be recovered using Instant Recovery. For example, if there are 1,000 files and 2 of them have issues, the remaining 998 files are recovered using Instant Recovery. The 2 problematic files will be restored from the Cohesity backup copy. Because a portion of the data must be recovered from a backup copy rather than the snapshot, we cannot commit to a specific RTO. However, the overall recovery process will still be significantly faster.

Cassandra Point-in-time Recovery (PITR)
Point in Time Recovery (PITR) enables you to have aggressive Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) for Cassandra source. PITR provides more granular recovery to scenarios of accidental data error or corruption. For PITR, commit logs on the Cassandra cluster are backed up which helps you to select a recovery point on a time scale.
Prerequisites
l On the Cassandra cluster: l You must enable commit log backup for successful point-in-time recovery. l You must ensure that the location to which the commit logs are restored must have sufficient disk space for new logs. l Cassandra service must be restarted on all nodes after enabling Commit Log Archival for backup to copy the commit logs. l You must run one full backup after enabling point in time on the Cassandra cluster. l The SSH user must have read and write access to the backup location.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

l The backup location must be the same for all nodes on the Cassandra cluster where PITR is enabled.
l For PITR, the Cassandra cluster must be registered on one Cohesity cluster only. Configure Commit Log Archival For PITR, the archival of commit logs must be enabled on the Cassandra cluster. You need to configure the commit log archival on the Cassandra cluster in the commitlog_ archiving.properties configuration file. The commit log is put to the archive location at node startup and when a commit log is written onto disk, or at a specific point-in-time. The command archive_command expects only a single command with arguments. The parameters must be entered verbatim. STDOUT and STDIN or multiple commands cannot be executed. To execute multiple commands you need to create a script with multiple commands and then call the script from the configuration file.
Enable Commit Log Archival
You must specify the parameters in the archive_command to enable commit log archival. The following is a sample command: archive_command=/bin/ln %path /backup/%name where
l %path is the fully qualified path of the segment to archive. l /backup is the location where you want to archive the commit log. l %name is the name of the commit log.
Note: l The SSH user must have read and write access to the /backup location.
l The backup location must be the same for all nodes on the Cassandra cluster where PITR is enabled.
Disable Commit Log Archival
To disable commit log archival, you must reset the archive_command as archive_command= (must be set to empty).
Points to Note
l The modification on the commitlog_archiving.properties configuration file must be done on all the Cassandra nodes.
l The Cassandra process must be restarted after editing the configuration file. l Commit logs are archived frequently because all writes to Cassandra are part of
commit logs and this may consume more disk space. The disk on which the archive

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

location is mounted must have adequate disk space. l For improved performance, it is recommended to have the Cassandra directory and
commit log directory on separate disks.
Configure Log Replay
Note: By default, Cohesity configures the log replay. Optionally, if you do not want Cohesity to make any changes on the Cassandra cluster you can manually configure log replay by following the procedure given below. Before you start with the procedure, contact Cohesity Support to update a setting on the Cohesity cluster thus allowing you to manually configure the log replay.
You need to configure the restore_command, restore_directories, and restore_point_ in_time commands on the Cassandra cluster. The command restore_command expects only a single command with arguments. The parameters must be entered verbatim. STDOUT and STDIN or multiple commands cannot be executed. To execute multiple commands you need to create a script with multiple commands and then call the script from the configuration file.
Enable Restore of Archived Commit Log
You must specify the parameters in the restore_command to enable the restoration of the archived commit log. The following is a sample command: restore_command=/bin/cp -f %from %to where
l %from is the fully qualified path of the archived commit log segment from the restore_directories.
l %to is the name of the live commit log directory.
You must also specify the parameters in the restore_directories command. The following is a sample command: restore_directories=/restore_directory You must also specify the parameters in the restore_point_in_time command to restore to a point-in-time. Cassandra replays all the logs in the restore directory till the specified time. The command accepts the time in the following format represented in GMT: YYYY::MM::DD HH:MM:SS The following is a sample command: restore_point_in_time=2013:12:11 17:00:00

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

Disable Restore of Archived Commit Log
To disable the restore of commit log archival, the restore_command, restore_ directories, and restore_point_in_time commands must be set to empty. Register To configure Cassandra for data protection on Cohesity, you need to register it as a source. For more information, see Register a Cassandra Source. Backup A point-in-time backup is achieved by backing up the data and the commit logs of the Cassandra cluster. Data can be backed up at a lesser frequency than the logs. In Cassandra, commit logs are generated for the entire node and cannot be filtered based on keyspaces or tables. Therefore, the commit log backup and data backups cannot be tied together based on keyspace or table. You need to create two Protection Groups, one for data backup (keyspace and table) and the other for commit log backup. For more information, see Backup Cassandra. Perform the following steps to create a Cassandra commit log backup:
l Configure the commit log archival in the Cassandra cluster. For more information, see Configure Commit Log Archival.
Note: The SSH user must have read and write permissions to the archive directory.
l Specify the archive log location while registering the Cassandra cluster as a source. For more information, see Register a Cassandra Source.
l Create a protection policy that has the commit log backup details. You can also use an existing policy that has the commit log backup details. For more information, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.
l Create a Protection Group to backup the commit log. For more information, see Backup Cassandra.
Note: Cohesity removes the backed-up commit logs from the /backup location.
Recover Point-in-time recovery is achieved by copying both the data and commit logs on the Cassandra primary. Data restore is a copy of the ss tables from Cohesity. Commit log restore included both copying and replaying the logs. For more information, see Recover Cassandra.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Cassandra

Considerations
l Commit logs can be replayed only to the original Cassandra cluster and with the same schema.
l Archival of Log Backups is not supported. l For PITR, object renaming is not supported. l DDL changes are not restored during log replay. l You cannot back up specific keyspace or table commit logs for point-in-time recovery.
The commit log backup is for the entire Cassandra cluster. l You must have performed at least one protection run after the first commit log backup
for successful point-in-time recovery. l For recovery from a remote cluster (archival or replication), you must specify the

A PITR recovery attempt for such objects within this time range will also fail. l To remove commit log-based PITR from a Cassandra source, you must first delete the local log Protection Group, and backup snapshots associated with the source. The replicated log Protection Groups can still exist and do not need to be deleted. l For PITR:
l Do not register Cassandra on multiple Cohesity clusters. l Do not register the same Cassandra cluster with different names or IPs on a

retention for Cassandra Log (PITR) Backups on a replicated Cohesity cluster higher than the retention on the Primary Cohesity cluster to avoid data loss.

Cassandra Hot Standby allows you to recover the latest snapshots from a full or incremental backup. You can recover the incremental changes of the protected Cassandra objects using Cohesity Platform. The first recovery is a full recovery and all subsequent recoveries are incremental.

Considerations
l The Cassandra version on the source cluster and the target cluster must be the same. l Two consecutive protection runs of the Cassandra objects must be less than the gc_
grace_seconds of a table. l Table truncation is not supported. l Multiple schema alteration queries executed on the single column on the source
Cassandra cluster between two backups is not restored to the target Cassandra cluster during a single invocation of incremental data recovery and results in an error. For example, if the following schema alteration commands are used on a table:
l ALTER TABLE newyork.transit_map DROP events [where events column is dropped]
l ALTER TABLE newyork.transit_map ADD events text [where events column of type text is added again to the schema]
The preceding commands are performed on the Cassandra cluster and then the incremental data recovery workflow is executed which moves data objects to the destination Cassandra cluster. This results in an error with the incremental data recovery workflow as schema alteration queries executed on the source Cassandra cluster will not be propagated to the destination Cassandra cluster during a single invocation of data recovery workflow.

Protect Couchbase Deployments Using Connector Agent
Couchbase deployments are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group enables you to specify the objects such as buckets, scopes, and collections that you want to back up.
The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured.
A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection GroupFor more information, see Manage Protection Policy.
To protect Couchbase deployments:
1. Do one of the following:
l Select Data Protection > Protection. Click Protect on the top-right of the page and then select Universal Data Adapter.

l Select Data Protection > Sources. Click the actions menu ( Couchbase source and then select Protect.

2. From the Source drop-down list, select the registered Couchbase source or click Register Source to register a Couchbase source. For more information, see Register Couchbase as a Source.

3. In the Objects section, select the object(s) that you plan to protect.

Note: You can select the objects using checkboxes or auto-protect. If you select the checkbox, all the collections inside the selected object will be backed up. If you select auto-protect, all the collections inside the selected object and any newly added collections will also be backed up. For recovering buckets, the auto-protect has to be enabled at the bucket level and for scopes, the auto-protect has to be enabled at either scope or bucket level. The manual selection of scopes and buckets using the checkbox will only allow recovery at the scope level.

4. In the Protection Group section, enter a name for the Protection Group in the Name field.

MongoDB
28 July 2026
The Cohesity MongoDB DataProtect solution natively integrates with MongoDB to provide consistent backup and recovery for MongoDB deployments.
Based on the policy settings, the Cohesity NoSQL and Hadoop Service initiates a backup of the MongoDB Database. The first backup is a full backup and everything after that is an incremental backup only. Occasionally, a full backup will be required if the oplog rollsover between two incremental backups. This can be avoided by increasing the frequency of backups or by increasing the size of the oplogs. The service also automatically determines the number of backup channels, based on the compute resources on Cohesity and the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

MongoDB

topology of the MongoDB cluster. The necessary Cohesity Views are automatically generated where the backups are going to be written. Communication between Cohesity and the MongoDB Databases is managed by the Cohesity NoSQL and Hadoop Service as described in the section below. See the following topics for details:
Core components
The following lists the core components of the Cohesity MongoDB solution:
l Physical or virtual MongoDB instance. l Cohesity Data Cloud. l Cohesity Compute Nodes. l Cohesity NoSQL and Hadoop Service running on Cohesity Compute Nodes. l Optional. Archive or tiering target at your data center or cloud provider of choice.
As illustrated in the figure below, you can integrate Cohesity with an existing MongoDB infrastructure by installing the Cohesity NoSQL and Hadoop Service on Compute Nodes. Once the service is installed and running, you can create protection policies, Protection Groups, and replication schedules for the MongoDB database. Once the data is protected, it can be archived, sent to tape, and or replicated to another instance running in the cloud or on-premises as shown in the image below.

MongoDB Features
Following are the key MongoDB-specific features of the solution:

MongoDB

l Support replica sets and sharded clusters l Granular backup and recovery - backup and recover individual collections l Index definitions are backed up and restored l Option to back up from secondary MongoDB nodes l Handle topology changes seamlessly (node addition, removal, IP changes, etc.) l Support Kerberos, LDAP, and SCRAM authenticated clusters l Support SSL-enabled clusters. l Support Continuous Data Protection (CDP).

To disable MongoDB CDP:

1. Run the following command: $ imanis_cli.sh -c mongocdp disable
2. Check the pod status from Cohesity node with command "kubectl.sh get pods -A" and verify that no mongocdp pods are running.

Ensuring all Nodes in MongoDB Cluster are Reachable
Make sure that all nodes in the MongoDB cluster are reachable through hostname and IP address from all containers running the NoSQL and Hadoop Services. Generally this is not a problem if the MongoDB servers are registered in DNS. If this is not the case, then refer To Manage the NoSQL and Hadoop Services.
Sizing the Primary Oplog of MongoDB Primary
Ensure that the oplog of MongoDB primary is sized to hold at least 30 minutes of data even when there is heavy load. This means, MongoDB primary would need a larger oplog if it has a larger maximum ingestion rate.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

MongoDB

Syncing Time Between MongoDB Cluster and Cohesity Cluster
Ensure that the time on MongoDB cluster and Cohesity cluster is in sync. This is a mandatory requirement as NoSQL and Hadoop Services access MongoDB Oplogs for incremental backups.
Ensuring Unique Value of _id in a Collection
This prerequisite is to verify that all collections have a unique value for _id. The field name _id is reserved for use as a primary key for a document and its value must be unique in the collection.
Warning: If a collection has more than one document with the same _id, it can cause data corruption as we cannot identify the documents uniquely. Even with data corruptions backup/restore will succeed without any errors.
Refer to the following MongoDB documentation for more information: l Field Names l Unique Indexes

Minimum Permissions This section describes the minimum set of permissions needed for the MongoDB DataProtect Solution to communicate with the source. MongoDB User & Roles The user specified in the MongoDB source registration page must have clusterAdmin and readWriteAnyDatabase roles. For example: db.createUser( { user: "username", pwd: "password", roles : [ { role: "clusterAdmin", db: "admin" }, { role: "readWriteAnyDatabase", db: "admin" } ] } ) The user must exist in all replicas. For a sharded environment, the user must exist in all replicas across all shards.
For more information on the preceding roles, refer to the MongoDB documentation on BuiltIn Roles.
Note: This Is applicable for LDAP authentication as well.
Best Practices l Ensure that the oplog of MongoDB primary is sized to hold at least 30 minutes of data even when there is heavy load. If you notice that a full backup is occurring frequently, consider increasing the size of the oplogs. l MongoDB Data Protection solution uses replica set oplog to capture incremental data. Standalone MongoDB clusters do not have an Oplog so they must be converted to replica sets using the process outlined in Convert a Standalone to a Replica Set.
Considerations l Re-creating a collection between two successive backups (drop a collection and recreate a collection with the same name) is not supported. The Protection Group must be re-created in that case.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

MongoDB

l MongoDB supports a special type of collection called 'Capped Collections'. A full backup is performed for capped collections in every run.
l Backup and recovery of MongoDB Views are not supported.
l Distributed transactions (introduced in MongoDB 4.2) are not supported.
l If a shard is added to a MongoDB cluster, the shard should not be removed before the next backup run. Removing the shard results in data loss and the user should recreate the workflow.
l If the shard key of a collection is modified using the refineCollectionShardKey command, the latest shard Key may not be recovered in PITR. PITR will recover the shardKey which was assigned to the collection at the time of the last incremental backup.
l If a collection is resharded, PITR is not supported after reshardCollection till the next backup. The next backup will automatically take a full backup of the resharded collection.
l The available PITR timeline starts from the oldest incremental or full backup run which is within the CDP retention period set in the policy.
l If you upgrade the NoSQL and Hadoop Service from a version older than 5.2, PITR will only be available after the next policy-based incremental run. To use PITR, the protection group policy should be modified to include CDP. For more information, see Using MongoDB CDP.
l Backup and recovery of collections with non-unique values in the _id field is not supported.
l Standalone MongoDB clusters are not supported because they do not have an Oplog. Standalone clusters must be converted to replica sets using the process outlined in the reference link - Convert a Standalone to a Replica Set.
l Meta operations like collection addition or deletion are captured in the backup run immediately following the operation. For this reason, the list of collections on a MongoDB database selected for point-in-time recovery is captured in the latest backup run before the selected time (called base backup). The point-in-time recovery recovers only those collections that are available in the base backup. If any such collection is deleted before the selected point in time, it is still recovered.
l Cohesity recommends taking a periodic full backup at least once per week or whenever more than 150 million documents are inserted, updated, or deleted in any of the collections being protected by the Protection Group. Additionally, in order to reclaim space, the interval between two full backups must be less than the retention period set in the policy.
l The support for MongoDB time series collections has the following considerations.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

MongoDB

l Sharded time series collections are not supported. l Secondary indexes on time series collections are not supported. l The backup process might not work during MongoDB upgrades. l The Pause Future Run function does not work for MongoDB protection groups if a run is in progress. l Cohesity does not support registering a MongoDB cluster using a mix of IPv4 and IPv6 addresses. l For IPv6, Kerberos authentication is not supported.
