Backup MongoDB
28 July 2026 Cohesity provides a simple sequence of tasks that constitute the procedure for backing up your MongoDB source. Once MongoDB is registered as a source on Cohesity, you can start configuring your backups.
Note: In case of the full backup, the Sharded Cluster Balancer is automatically disabled. Disabling the balancer for the duration of the backup procedure is a recommended practice. For more information, refer to the MongoDB documentation on Disabling Balancer During Backups. If the balancer is active when the full backup starts, then Cohesity disables the balancer. After the full backup is complete, Cohesity automatically reactivates the balancer if it was originally running when the full backup started. However, in a rare scenario, if MongoDB fails or if a running backup workflow is killed, the balancer does not get reactivated. In this case, it is recommended that users manually enable the balancer on the MongoDB cluster. Refer to the MongoDB documentation on Manage Sharded Cluster Balancer.
Continuous Data Protection (CDP) The Cohesity Continuous Data Protection (CDP) provides near-zero RPOs for MongoDB environments. The CDP captures and protects the application data every time there is a change in data so that it can be restored to a point in time as opposed to periodic snapshots available with regular backups. For MongoDB CDP, Cohesity uses a specialized CDP Service which runs on the Cohesity cluster. The CDP Service captures changes from MongoDB oplog in real time and continuously backs up the changes to the Cohesity cluster. These changes are saved on the Cohesity cluster in a write-ahead-log (WAL) which can be used to recover collections to any point-in-time as long as all the previous changes are available.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

MongoDB

Cohesity manages rare instances of oplog rollover by doing a full backup instead of an incremental one.
Using MongoDB CDP

Note: Ensure that the Prerequisites are met before using MongoDB CDP.

To enable CDP, create a new protection policy and attach the Continuous Data Protection option to the policy. Within the CDP option specify the retain point in time configuration, and associate this policy with the MongoDB source's Protection Group.
After associating the protection policy with the Protection Group, the protection run will first initiate a full backup. The initial full backup is followed by an incremental protection run and the continuous protection of the source will begin from this point on. You can view all the continuously protected sources from the Cohesity UI.
To create a new protection policy with the Continuous Data Protection option, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.
Protect MongoDB Objects
MongoDB Objects are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group enables you to select the objects that you want to back up. It uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured, retained, archived, and replicated .
A Protection Policy is a reusable list of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule and backup snapshot retention. Also, for Disaster Recovery, you can add replication for the Protection Group using the Protection Policy. For detailed instructions on how to create a Protection Policy, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.

Minimum Permissions To use the Cohesity Connector for MongoDB backup, the Cohesity agent and MongoDB connector executables must be installed and run on each MongoDB host node. Both the Cohesity agent and the MongoDB connector come as Installer RPM packages and need to be installed as root. Based on the options selected during installation, the service can run in one of the following modes:
1. Default: Run as a user with User ID 0 (root privileges). 2. Run as a service user (non-root) with sudo privileges. 3. Run as a service user (non-root) configured with specific capabilities using setcap
(use this if sudo/root access is not permitted).
Note: The sudo package is a required dependency for the Cohesity Linux Agent and must remain installed on the host even when the agent is configured to run as a non-root user without sudo privileges. For the full list of dependencies, see Install Cohesity Linux Agent.
Relevant command line options must be set while installing the RPMs. For more details, refer to Install Cohesity Linux Agent RPM Package. Considerations Review and understand the following recommendations before protecting your MongoDB cluster:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

MongoDB via Ops Manager

l MongoDB recommends that if any node in the cluster goes down, the backup process fails, requiring a full backup to be triggered again.
l MongoDB strongly recommends scheduling periodic full backups at least once per week to prevent data inconsistency scenarios.
l MongoDB backup protection jobs might fail during high-ingestion periods with significant application writes.
l The Cohesity solution does not support the use of Organization-level API keys. This is because the solution is designed to protect the entire OpsManager instance rather than individual organizations. You must generate and use a Global API Key for successful registration and integration.
l MongoDB recomments not running a resync on any node while a backup is active, as this will cause the snapshot and backup workflow to fail.
l Do not perform a primary stepdown during an active backup, as it may result in snapshot failure.
l The amount of data backed up in an incremental backup may not exactly match the data ingested in the source during that period. This amount depends on multiple factors such as source side compaction, the distribution of the changes, etc.
l Standalone MongoDB deployments are not supported and are filtered out by Cohesity.
l Multiple concurrent operations within the same project are not allowed. For example, if a project has two clusters, A and B, and a recovery operation is in progress on cluster A, then any backup or recovery operations for cluster B must wait until cluster A's recovery is complete.
l Non-ASCII or special characters in dbPath are not supported.
l The in-memory storage engine is not supported.
l MongoDB deployment configuration options must be the same for both the source (backup) and destination (recovery) clusters.
l Before recovery, make sure that the destination hosts have adequate storage available.
l If a protection group is edited to add a new collection or a new cluster gets protected as part of autoprotect, the immediate log backup for those collections is not enforced. Log backups for them would run at the next policy-defined time, and the restore timeline would be available from the first incremental backup that happens after at least one log backup is taken following a recovery.
l Once an Ops Manager source is created, the hostname and port cannot be edited. However, the authentication details can still be edited.

Install Cohesity Linux Agent RPM Package
1. Download the Cohesity Linux agent package (el-cohesity-agent) from the Cohesity Download portal and copy it to all MongoDB nodes.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

MongoDB via Ops Manager

2. Choose the execution mode. The Cohesity Linux agent supports the following execution modes: l Option 1: Run as a user with User ID 0 (root user). l Option 2: Run as a service user (non-root) with sudo privileges. l Option 3: Run as a service user (non-root) configured with specific capabilities using setcap.
Note: l In all execution modes, the RPM installation must be done as the root user. l The sudo package is a required dependency for the Cohesity Linux Agent and must remain installed on the host even when the agent is configured to run as a non-root user without sudo privileges.
Option 1: For running the Linux agent as the root user, install using the following command: For example: [root@hostname.example.com ~]$ rpm -ivh el-cohesity-agent-xx1.x86_64.rpm
Option 2: For running the Linux agent as a non-root service user with sudo access, install using the following command: For example: [root@hostname.example.com ~]$ export COHESITYUSER=<service-user> ; ; rpm -ivh el-cohesity-agent-xx-1.x86_64.rpm
Note: l Ensure the service user is an existing user on the host. l In addition, it is necessary to create and preserve the following settings in the /etc/sudoers file for the service user:
<username> ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL Defaults:<username> !requiretty
Option 3: For running the Linux agent as a non-root service user without sudo access, install using the following commands:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

MongoDB via Ops Manager

For example: [root@hostname.example.com ~]$ export COHESITYUSER=<service-user> ; export COHESITY_AGENT_SKIP_ALL_NO_SUDO=1 ; rpm -ivh el-cohesityagent-xx-1.x86_64.rpm
Note: l Ensure the service user is an existing user on the host.
l Setting capabilities using setcap is a one-time activity and is performed only during RPM installation or upgrade scenarios. Once capabilities are set using setcap, during regular execution of agent and connector, sudo access is not required.

[root@hostname.example.com ~]$ rpm -ivh cohesity-mongodb-connector-XXX1.x86_64.rpm
Prerequisites
The following configurations are necessary prerequisites for the protection and recovery of MongoDB deployments via Ops Manager:
l Enable third-party backup management for the relevant projects in the Ops Manager. l Enable the Ops Manager Backup daemon on the admin page. l Install and configure the MongoDB Ops Manager agent on each server in the
deployment to be protected. Also, make sure that the agent has read/write access to any of the configured directories. Make sure to configure the Oplog export path for MongoDB to store the Oplog Data. l Synchronize system clocks to ensure consistent timestamps across machines using Network Time Protocol. l Activate monitoring and backup services on the MongoDB deployment to be protected. Make sure the Monitoring, Backup, and automation are enabled on the Ops Manager agent for each host of the MongoDB Deployment to be protected. l Create a Global API key with Global Backup Admin, Global User Admin, and Global Owner permissions if not already present. Manage Agents - View Agent and Connector Installation Status for MongoDB Nodes
To protect your MongoDB clusters using Cohesity through Ops Manager, every MongoDB node must have both the Cohesity Agent and the Cohesity Connector installed. These components work together to enable application-consistent backups and ensure your data is fully protected. The Manage Agents flow can be used to verify whether all the necessary components are installed across all nodes. Missing even one Agent or Connector on a node results in the following:
l Backups cannot run successfully l Some parts of the cluster remain unprotected l Troubleshooting becomes time-consuming
This feature provides complete visibility into the installation status of both the Cohesity Agent and Connector across all MongoDB hosts in Ops Manager. With this feature, you can quickly:
l See which MongoDB hosts have both components installed l Identify MongoDB hosts missing the Agent or Connector l Check the version of the installed Cohesity Agent l View health status for each node l Filter large environments to find exactly what you need
This helps ensure that your MongoDB clusters are always fully prepared for successful backup operations. To view the Cohesity Agent and Connector installation status:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Select the MongoDB source you want to review.
3. Click on the actions menu ( ) and select Manage Agents. The Manage Agents dialog appears and displays all discovered hosts and their installation status. You can view the following information: 1. Hostname - Displays the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of the MongoDB host.

Enable or Disable Auto Protect
The Auto Protect option enables you to automatically protect the objects that are added to the MongoDB source. You can auto-protect either the entire ops manager instance, the entire organization or an ops manager project. When the Auto Protect option is enabled:
l All the objects that are added to the MongoDB Ops Manager entity in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run.
Note: The Cohesity agent must be installed on all hosts in the newly added clusters.
l All the objects that are removed from the MongoDB source in the future are automatically removed from the Protection Group and are not protected from the next protection run. The existing backups are preserved until the snapshot expires.
When the Auto Protect option is disabled, you need to manually: l Add newly added objects, in the MongoDB source, to the Protection Group. l Remove existing objects, that are removed from the MongoDB source, from the Protection Group. The existing backups are preserved until the snapshot expires.

Source-Side Deduplication for MongoDB
The source-side deduplication feature for MongoDB is designed to optimize backup efficiency by eliminating redundant data at the MongoDB source before transferring it to the Cohesity cluster. This optimization significantly reduces network bandwidth consumption, shortens backup windows, and optimizes storage consumption on the target, making it especially beneficial for large MongoDB deployments. When source-side deduplication is enabled, only unique data blocks that have not been previously protected are transmitted to the Cohesity cluster. This capability integrates with Cohesity's built-in deduplication to further enhance storage efficiency by processing only new data blocks.
Advantages of Source-Side Deduplication
l Reduced Network Traffic: Minimizes data transferred between MongoDB hosts and the Cohesity cluster, helping conserve network bandwidth.
l Faster Backups: Shortens backup windows, particularly for large MongoDB databases that require periodic full backups.
l Optimized Storage Consumption: Reduces upfront storage usage on the Cohesity cluster by sending only unique data blocks.
l Improved Scalability: Offloads deduplication processing from the Cohesity cluster, enabling the system to support a higher number of concurrent backup workloads.
Enable Source-Side Deduplication for MongoDB
To enable source-side deduplication for MongoDB, contact Cohesity Support.
Note: Source-side deduplication is effective only when deduplication is enabled on the Storage Domain associated with the Protection Group. If deduplication is disabled on the Storage Domain, source-side deduplication does not take effect.

Recovery options

Field

Description

Staging Directory Path

Specify the full directory path where oplog files will be temporarily stored during point-in-time recovery. This path must exist and be writable by the Cohesity service user on every host in the destination MongoDB deployment. Ensure sufficient disk space is available. The staging directory must have enough free space to store the oplog data generated since the earliest snapshot backup within the selected point-in-time recovery (PITR) window. You can estimate the required space by multiplying the average data change rate by the duration of the PITR window. Note that the change rate may vary throughout the day due to spikes in data ingestion. For example, if the change rate is 1 MB/s and the PITR window spans 6,000 seconds, you will need at least 6 GB of free space. Cohesity recommends allocating additional space as a buffer to prevent potential issues. (This option is available only if a specific point in time is selected for recovery).

Task Name Specify a name for the recovery task. A default name is pre-populated, which can be changed.

Cancel a Recovery Run When you cancel a recovery run, MongoDB cancels the job by terminating the recovery processes. To cancel a recovery run:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Recoveries. 2. Click the action icon ( ) next to the recovery run and click Cancel Run. 3. In the Cancel Recovery dialog box, select any one of the following:
l Continue Recovery if you want to continue to recovery run. l Cancel Recovery if you want to cancel the recovery run.

Pinecone
Cohesity Pinecone protection enables secure, policy-driven backup and recovery for Pinecone vector database indexes, which are commonly used in AI and machine learning workloads such as Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), semantic search, and recommendation systems.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Pinecone

Cohesity integrates directly with Pinecone's native Backups API to protect serverless indexes without moving customer data out of the Pinecone cloud. Only backup metadata is stored on the Cohesity cluster, ensuring zero data movement and avoiding data egress costs.
Pinecone protection is implemented through a dedicated Universal Data Adapter v2 (UDAv2) adapter that communicates securely with Pinecone over HTTPS and integrates with existing Cohesity services and workflows. The result is a unified approach to protecting AI vector data alongside other enterprise workloads.

Pinecone Protection Core Components
The following are the core components for protecting Pinecone indexes: l Pinecone cloud - external service where vector index data is stored, and native backup snapshots are created. l Cohesity cluster - backup metadata such as snapshot identifiers and index details are stored.
Pinecone Features
Following are the key characteristics of Pinecone protection: l Backup Manager Style: Cohesity does not move data but orchestrates the Pinecone's native backup mechanism of using Backups API for serverless indexes. l Zero Data Movement: Backups remain stored in Pinecone's infrastructure. l Metadata Management: Cohesity tracks backup metadata and manages lifecycle/retention policies.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Pinecone

l Index Type Detection: Automatically detects serverless indexes and uses the appropriate backup and recovery method.
Plan and Prepare for Pinecone Protection
To protect Pinecone with the Cohesity cluster, you must register your Pinecone account/organization as a source in the Cohesity cluster. Prerequisites for Pinecone Protection Following are the prerequisites for Pinecone Protection:
l Ensure that the service accounts have enterprise-level Pinecone subscription. l Ensure outbound connectivity is supported for *.pinecone.io via HTTPS. Considerations l Unsupported Functionalities - The following functionalities are not supported for
Pinecone: l Replication and archival of Pinecone snapshots l Auto-protection and Tag-based Auto-protection
l Full back up support - Only full backup is supported; incremental backup is not available for Pinecone.
l New Location Recovery - Recovering the Pinecone indexes to a new location are not supported.
Register and Manage Pinecone Source
To protect your Pinecone objects, you need to register Pinecone as a source on the Cohesity cluster. Pinecone organizations are registered using OAuth2 service account credentials.
Note: The service account must have owner-level permissions to discover all the projects and indexes.
To register Pinecone as a source: 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click Register on the top-right of the page and then select Databases > Pinecone. 3. On the Register Pinecone page, perform the following: 1. In the Client ID field, enter the Pinecone OAuth client identifier used by Cohesity to authenticate API requests.

Note: The storage space reclaimed by deleting the Protection Group takes some time to reflect.
To delete the Protection Group: 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for Pinecone. 3. Click ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Delete. 4. In the Delete Protection Group? dialog, perform the following: 1. Select Delete Snapshots to delete the snapshots along with the Protection Group. 2. Type YES to confirm. 3. Click Delete Group.
Note: Deleting all Snapshots will delete all the storage snapshots associated with the protection group. Any Cloudspin artifacts generated by the Protection Group must be deleted from the respective cloud portals. Snapshots under DataLock cannot be deleted.

Agent Minimum Permissions for Microsoft SQL Server Protection
You can use either the host LOCAL SYSTEM account or an account that meets the requirements to install the Cohesity agent. It is recommended to run the Cohesity Agent service with an Active Directory domain user account that is a member of the local administrator of the SQL Server host. The AD domain user account must be a member of the SQL sysadmin server role. The user account must have log-on rights to the SQL Server host in the local security policy of the SQL Server host. If you do not use the LOCAL SYSTEM account, ensure the following for the chosen account:
l The account must be a member of the local Windows Administrators group. For example, qa01\tme-backup is an Active Directory user account in the data center. If the backup admin plans to use this account, qa01\tme-backup must be part of the local Windows Administrators group on the SQL server.
l The account must have Log on as a service in the User Rights Assignment on the MS SQL server to install the Cohesity agent.
l The account must have the sysadmin role in the MS SQL Server instance.
Ports Used for Communication
l On physical servers or VMs with an ephemeral or installed agent, open the ports 445, 11113, 11117, and 50051. For more information, see Manage Firewall Ports.
l If the Windows Firewall is used: l Inbound rules: l Add a rule to accept SQL Server traffic and TCP connections on local port 1433. l Set Remote Port to All Ports. l Outbound rules (for MS SQL Server 2016 running on Windows 2016): Update the "Block network access for R local user accounts in SQL server instance MSSQLSERVER" rule by going to General tab > Action window > select "Allow the connection".

Credentials and Privileges for Microsoft SQL Server Protection
There are three accounts you must consider when installing the Cohesity Agent:
l Installation Account: The account you use to log in to the host and run the installer.
l Service Account: The account under which the Cohesity Agent service runs on the SQL Server host. (Selected at the time of installation.)
l SQL Server login account: The SQL Server account by which the Cohesity Agent has access to the databases. (Configured after installation.)
Installation Account
When installing the Cohesity Agent on a Microsoft Windows host, you must log onto the SQL Server host with an account that has local administrator privileges. This is because the Windows agent installer installs the Cohesity Agent service. Microsoft requires the installation account to have administrator privileges on the host.
Choose the Service Account
The installer gives you the option between two types of service accounts:
l The LocalSystem account. l A user account. Assigning privileges to the service account will differ depending on
which type of account you choose. Cohesity recommends using either the LocalSystem account or an Active Directory Domain User account. See the chart below for a comparison of service account types.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

Comparison of Service Account Types

SERVICE ACCOUNT LocalSystem (Default)
User Account

TYPE

DEFINITION

RECOMMENDATION

LocalSystem Account (Built-in Host Account)

The LocalSystem account is a predefined local account on the host computer.

Recommended: The Local System account is a predefined local account used by the service control manager. It has extensive privileges on the local computer, and acts as the computer on the network. Its token includes the NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM and BUILTIN\Administrators SIDs; these accounts have access to most system objects.

Domain User Account (Active Directory)

A user whose username and password are stored in Active Directory.

Recommended: A domain user account enables the service to take full advantage of the service security features of Windows and Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services. The service has whatever local and network access is granted to the account, or to any groups of which the account is a member.

Local User Account (Host account)

In Windows, a local user is one whose username and encrypted password are stored locally, only on the computer itself.

Not recommended: When you log in as a local user, the computer checks its own list of users and its own password file to see if you are allowed to log in to the computer. The computer itself then applies all the permissions and restrictions that are assigned to you for that computer.

Note: If you are unsure which account to use, choose the LocalSystem account. This account already has most of the required permissions. The agent service account can be changed later if needed.

SQL System

Definition
A Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) enabled SQL database has its data files encrypted, known as encrypting data at rest. TDE performs real-time I/O encryption and decryption of the data and log files. For details, see Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) in the Microsoft documentation. NOTE: Cohesity does not manage the keys associated with the TDE database.
A Filestream enabled SQL Database is a database that contains a table that stores its data outside the database on the host file system. SQL Filestream leverages the OS file system's ability to handle large objects like images, PDFs, Binary, Bmp, Docs, and other unstructured data. For details, see Filestream (SQL Server) in the Microsoft documentation.
SQL Server maintains a set of four system-level databases (master, model, msdb, tempdb), which are essential for the operation of a server instance. System databases must be backed up after every significant update. The system databases that you must always back up include msdb, master, and model. System databases are not supported for log backups. For details, see Backup & restore: system databases (SQL Server) in the Microsoft documentation.

Database Recover and Clone Actions
In the Databases tab click a protected database to display available recover and clone actions. To recover or clone the latest snapshot, click the arrow next to the Protect button at the top right corner and select an action. By default, the latest snapshot is selected. You can optionally choose to restore from a
different snapshot by clicking Edit ( ). You can also provide a specific time to restore to if transaction logs are available. Click a date on the calendar to select a snapshot from that date. The default point selected will be the latest log transaction or the latest full or incremental, whichever is the latest. The slider also displays available points in time and displays snapshots as circles. Manually select a point on the slider if you want to restore to a specific point in time. Selecting an invalid time from the slider automatically changes to the closest available snapshot. If your manual selection is within 10 minutes of a snapshot, your selection automatically snaps to it. You can also select a specific point in time by entering it in the time fields. After selecting the desired recover point, click Recover. You can choose to clone the selected recover point by clicking the arrow adjacent to recover and selecting Clone. In this workflow, deleted snapshots may be displayed as valid recover points for a brief period until they are removed from the search index by a background process.

AG FCC as a Source
Always On Availability Group (AG) First-Class Citizen (FCC) allows you to manage AG databases for backups using a single entity rather than multiple AG replicas. Points to Remember Before Enabling AG FCC
l Once you switch to AG FCC, you must perform full backups for all the AG databases, since this is a new entity.
l Volume-based backup and VMware VSS-based backup are not supported by AG FCC sources.
l AG FCC is a cluster-level feature. On multi-tenant Cohesity clusters, AG FCC cannot be enabled for a single tenant; it must be enabled for all tenants.
l You can continue to protect the AG databases using the older method if there are concerns about modifying all AG SQL protection groups on the cluster.
l Log backups will not run until the initial full backup of the AG FCI is completed. Ensure to monitor the potential log growth during this period.
l AGs discovered on the registered standalone physical hosts or failover clusters are registered as sources internally.
l If AG FCC is enabled, after registration, databases belonging to an AG will appear only under the AG listed in the Sources page and not under the registered SQL host (AG replica). SQL host lists only the local databases.
l When AG sources are being protected in a protection group, other physical sources cannot be protected in the same protection group.
l Once you upgrade to AG FCC, protection runs for the existing AG databases displays the following warning: "In order to enable advanced SQL Available Group functionality, please remove AG databases from Protection Groups, then refresh the physical hosts that are members

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

of an AG. To disable this warning, gflagmagneto_sql_display_warning_to_enable_ aag_fcc_on_prem_feature can be updated to false." l AG FCC is enabled by default on new Cohesity clusters running version 7.3 or later. However, when an existing cluster with AG volume-based protection is upgraded to version 7.3 or later, AG FCC is not enabled automatically. Existing volume-based backups continue to run, and you can create new protection groups because AG FCC remains disabled.
To enable AG FCC:
1. Remove all AG databases from the protection groups.
Note: If you are unable to remove the AG databases due to legacy AAG blocking the migration, delete the AG/FCI protection groups. You can exclude snapshots.
2. Refresh the SQL sources that host AG databases. This identifies the sources as AG entities instead of individual SQL servers. You do not need to unregister these sources.
3. Create new backup jobs and start the backup.

Set Up Microsoft SQL Server FCI
This topic describes how to set up an MS SQL Failover Cluster Instance (FCI) to be protected by a Cohesity cluster. To set up a standalone MS SQL Server or MS SQL AG, follow the steps described in Set Up Standalone Microsoft SQL Server or Microsoft SQL Server AGs.
MS SQL FCI - Overview
An MS SQL FCI is an MS SQL instance installed on a Windows server that is part of a Windows Server Failover Cluster (WSFC or simply Windows Cluster for short). The SQL instance physically exists on (and is accessible from) only one node of the WSFC at any given time. If the FCI's current node goes down, the FCI moves to another node in the WSFC. The FCI is addressed by a Virtual IP (VIP) which points to the physical IP of the node on which it currently resides.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

Set Up MS SQL FCI Overview
MS SQL FCI setup has the following steps:
1. Ensure Prerequisites Are Met 2. Download and Install the Agent on Each Node 3. Register an MS SQL FCI as a Source 4. Register an MS SQL FCI as MS SQL
Ensure Prerequisites Are Met
Ensure the prerequisites listed in Prerequisites for Microsoft SQL Server Protection are met.
Download and Install the Agent on Each Node
Before registering an MS SQL Server FCI, you must download and install the Cohesity agent on each node within the MS SQL FCI.
1. Select Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click Download Cohesity Agent. Ensure the agent has been downloaded to the
appropriate server. 3. As an administrator with local system privileges on that server, run the executable
and complete the installation using the following steps: 4. Volume CBT (Changed Block Tracker): Install this component to leverage
Cohesity's built-in CBT technology. Without this component, only full backups can be performed. Installing this component requires a one-time reboot to load the Cohesity CBT driver. Until a reboot, only full backups can be performed. File System CBT (Changed Block Tracker): Install this component to perform MS SQL file-based protection.
Note: Installing the Volume CBT or File System CBT is not necessary for MS SQL VDI-based protection.
5. Service Account Credentials: You can use either the LOCAL SYSTEM account or an account that meets the requirements to install the Cohesity agent. If you do not use the LOCAL SYSTEM account, ensure the following: l The account must be a member of the local Windows Administrators group. For example, qa01\tme-backup is an Active Directory user account in the data center. If the backup admin plans to use this account, qa01\tme-backup must be part of the local Windows Administrators group on the SQL server. l The account must have Log on as a service in the User Rights Assignment on the MS SQL server to install the Cohesity agent.
6. Wait for the installation to finish.

You can register and back up a Windows Server that participates in an MS SQL FCI. You can separately register the FCI clusters and their standalone nodes. This allows you to backup local drives for physical server backups.
Prerequisites
l Ensure that all the SQL agents are upgraded.

Best Practices for Microsoft SQL Server
Cohesity recommends the following best practices when protecting MS SQL:
l Cohesity recommends triggering a full backup whenever a database file (.mdf, .ndf, .ldf) is added or removed from the database.
l Multiple Cohesity clusters concurrently backing up an MS SQL VM is not recommended because the jobs will interfere with the other's log chain.
l For MS SQL point in time restores, the Full Recovery Model is recommended as a best practice. For more information, see Choosing the Recovery Model for a Database.
l Set MS SQL Server to autostart.
l To accurately report the size of transaction log data read/written during log backups, the Windows local or domain Administrator account that is registered with Cohesity for backup must be added as a user to the 'model' system database. Use the following query: -- Configures accurate reporting of the size of transaction log data read/written during log backup USE [model] GO CREATE USER [HOSTNAME\Administrator] FOR LOGIN [HOSTNAME\Administrator]
GO Where HOSTNAME is the hostname of the SQL server. This assumes that the Administrator account used to register MS SQL is already

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

registered in the SQL server instance's Security Logins and has the "sysadmin" role per documentation. If privileges are not correct, the logical bytes read stat ("Size" column on the Job's details page) for MS SQL log backups will be the same as the physical bytes read stat ("Read" column on the Job's details page). If privileges are correct, then the size reported will be the sum of the sizes of all the .ldf files for the database.
Considerations for Microsoft SQL Server
General
l Windows Physical and Microsoft SQL Server refresh for a host can fail with the following error when the agent process reaches a high memory watermark.
"kAgentError: Excessive memory usage (spike) on the Agent."
This watermark is based on the peak memory usage of the agent. As a result, the refresh can continue to fail even after the current memory usage of the agent decreases.
As a workaround, restart the agent.
l For file-based Protection Group, object-level granularity is not supported for Rolebased access control (RBAC), such as setting access to objects through Active Directory and roles.
l If using native or third-party backup software to back up an application (such as MS SQL), note that the following behavior breaks the differential chain for the application on that server:
l Performing an app-consistent backup on a VMware SQL VM.
l Backing up a physical server using a (non-SQL) volume-based physical server Protection Group. You are allowed to run a file-based physical server Protection Group with a SQL Protection Group or 3rd party SQL protection tools. This is a Microsoft limitation. For more information, see Various Causes of Log Chains Breaking Issue in SQL Server.
l The SQL Server VDI log backup and restore operations require Sysadmin privileges which is a Microsoft requirement. For more details, see Microsoft Documentation on SQL Server VDI backup.
l On-prem SharePoint databases can be backed up and recovered through Microsoft SQL Server. To recover granular items, you must use third-party software, Ontrack Power Controls, to mine the database.
Protection
l Ensure that all AG databases you want to protect are selected from the respective replica.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

l For file-based backups, Cohesity operations rely on default MS SQL file extensions (.mdf, .ndf, .ldf).
l SQL Database and logs residing on SMB/NFS can be protected using the MS SQL Native method.
l SQL Database and logs residing on Clustered Shared Volumes (CSV) can be protected using the MS SQL Native and MS SQL VDI methods.
l CBT information does not persist after a reboot for the file-based backup method.
l As per Microsoft requirements, VDI backups executed on secondary replicas are copyonly full backups. Copy-only backups on secondary replicas do not impact the log chain. For more information, see Offload supported backups to secondary replicas of an availability group.
l Overwriting Filestream database is not supported; this may prevent the completion of recovery.
l Generally, volume-based backups over Resilient File System (ReFS) are not supported. But if the volume is presented through the Windows Cluster Shared Volume (CSV) layer, the ReFS file system detection fails causing the volume-based backups to succeed.
l You can run log backups in parallel with existing log backup runs. This helps reduce storage buildup on the primary SQL Server when multiple large backups are in progress. This feature is supported only for file-based, VDI-based, and Filestream (backed up using VDI-based method) backups.
Note: When you run a log backup for a database backup job, any preceding backup job for the same database may skip the log backup if the new backup job is completed before the previous backup job for the database is started.
The resource manager reserves additional slots specifically for Run Now based log backups to start immediately. The databases in queue are skipped, and the log backup is initiated.
Recovery
l Performing a point-in-time restore of an Always On Availability Group replica requires full backups from that replica. Log backups are merged across all replicas; full backups are not. During restore, the user sees multiple results for the same database from different replicas. Each replica shows a set of Snapshots for full backups done on that particular replica. For point in

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

time restore to a specific replica, the user must select a full backup Snapshot from that replica only. If a full backup does not exist, point in time restore is not possible.
Restore the database to the desired MS SQL Server instance on a replica that has a full backup.
l Using the "Restore to Original SQL Server instance" option is not supported if any of the following occurs:
l The Windows host name changed and you attempt to restore a snapshot that was taken before the host name change.
l Granular DB restore performed from a higher SQL Server version to a lower version. This is a Microsoft limitation.
You can, toggle off "Restore to Original SQL Server Instance" and perform a database restore.
For more information, see Rename computer hosting instance - SQL Server.
Restoring a snapshot taken after the name change or upgrade is supported.
l Restoring MS SQL Server from backups of dynamic disks to the same machine is not supported.
l Use File-based or VDI-based backup methods to protect TDE databases. Follow the Microsoft TDE best practices for key and cert management.
l If multiple restore tasks are run on the same target host, the restore tasks will be serialized.
l For system database recovery:
l Recovering the system database to an alternate instance is not supported.
l When recovering to the original database, the original database is deleted before the recovery. Therefore, a recovery failure will also lead to the loss of the original database.
l If you are recovering the system databases individually, then the recovery of the system database must be in the following order:
1. Master
2. MSDB
3. Model
l You cannot recover a system database along with a user database.
l If you are recovering more than one system databases in a recovery task, then the recovery point for the selected system databases must be the same.
l For recovering a database to an Amazon RDS Custom SQL Server, the recovery destination path must be under the D:\rdsdbdata folder.
l Download and File-Level recovery of SQL files from FortKnox is not supported.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

Clone
l Cloning an MS SQL database and renaming the database via SSMS can leave the cloned database in the "Recovery Pending" state during a clone teardown task. This is because the Cohesity cluster database clone operation assumes the cloned database name and files are associated with the original clone operation. To prevent a disconnect between the Cohesity cluster and SQL Server operation, it is recommended to clone a new database with the intended database name rather than rename a cloned database.
Migration
l Cohesity does not support the migration of MS SQL FILESTREAM databases. l Once a migration task is configured and created, the target SQL Server or database
paths cannot be modified for the existing migration task. l Cohesity does not detect changes/deletions to the target database with a running
migration task. Changes made external to the migration task before finalizing can cause the migration task to fail. l Cohesity does not support the migration of MS SQL databases that are replicated to an alternate Cohesity cluster.

Known Issues that lead to backup failure

Very High transaction rate on databases may occur resulting in backup failure. Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

Cohesity also supports VM-based Backup and SQL Native Backup.
Volume-based Backup
A Cohesity MS SQL volume-based backup captures all MS SQL databases running on a VMware or Physical Server, whose files reside on one or more volumes, as well as all other files that are stored on the corresponding OS volume. This approach contrasts with a filebased MS SQL backup, which includes only the selected databases. The Cohesity cluster captures full database server backups and can optionally back up database transaction logs, so you can roll forward to any point in time. For information on performing MS SQL volume-based backup, see Backup Microsoft SQL Server (Volume-based). All configurations are for illustrative purposes only. Cohesity recommends following MS SQL best practices. An example of MS SQL running on a Windows server that contains the following:
l Multiple volumes, C, D and F in the figure below l Volume D is running multiple MS SQL databases l Volume F contains database logs

The MS SQL volume-based backup task consists of the following actions:
1. During an MS SQL protection run, a VSS snapshot of MS SQL is captured using Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS). The VSS snapshot resides on the local drive as a special VSS volume. This capturing of the VSS snapshot is a full database server backup. This is the same for MS SQL running on VMware and physical servers.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

2. The snapshot is captured and saved on the Cohesity cluster with a date and time stamp. You can optionally choose for the Cohesity cluster to utilize Change Block Tracking (CBT) when backing up the snapshot. VMware VMs leverage VMware CBT to back up the snapshot. Physical servers leverage Cohesity CBT to back up the snapshot.

3. If specified in the policy, the database transaction logs are backed up to the Cohesity cluster using MS SQL Server Virtual Device Interface (VDI). The logs allow you to roll back to a specific point in time. MS SQL Server automatically truncates the SQL logs after a successful SQL log backup and marks the Virtual Log Files (VLFs) for reuse.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

File-based Backup
A Cohesity cluster MS SQL file-based backup protects only the MS SQL databases you choose. It captures only the database files for those selected databases. This approach contrasts with a volume-based backup, which captures any and all the files contained on the volume. The Cohesity cluster captures full database server backups and can optionally back up database transaction logs, so you can roll forward to any point in time. The advantage of a file-based backup is that a smaller amount of data is captured, which allows the Protection Group to run more quickly.
Note: To enable file-based backup, you must install the File System CBT component during Cohesity agent installation.
For information on performing MS SQL file-based backup, see Backup Microsoft SQL Server (File-based). All configurations are for illustrative purposes only. Cohesity recommends following MS SQL best practices. An example of MS SQL running on a Windows server that contains the following:
l Multiple volumes, C, D, E and F in the figure below l Volume D is running two MS SQL databases l Volume E is running three MS SQL databases l Volume F contains database logs

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

The MS SQL file-based backup task consists of the following actions:
1. During SQL database protection run, a VSS snapshot of the specified MS SQL databases is captured using Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS). The VSS snapshot resides on the local drive as a special VSS volume. This VSS snapshot is a full database server backup.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

2. The snapshot is captured and saved on the Cohesity cluster with a date and time stamp. You can optionally choose for the Cohesity cluster to utilize Change Block Tracking (CBT) when backing up the snapshot. VMware VMs leverage VMware CBT to back up the snapshot. Physical servers leverage Cohesity CBT to back up the snapshot.

3. Backups of database transaction logs use MS SQL Server Virtual Device Interface (VDI) and are stored on the Cohesity cluster. The logs allow you to roll back to a specific point in time. MS SQL Server automatically truncates the SQL logs after a successful SQL log backup and marks the Virtual Log Files (VLFs) for reuse.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

VDI-based Backup
A Cohesity cluster MS SQL VDI-based backup captures the native MS SQL server backups. It captures VDI-based backups of a specific database on a SQL Server instance running on a VMware or physical server.
The Virtual Device Interface (VDI) is a Microsoft interface that allows the Cohesity agent to execute SQL Server Native backup and restore commands. This backup type produces a standard SQL Server Native backup of type (.BAK), transaction logs, (.TRN), and differentials, (.DIFF). These backup files are stored on a Cohesity View and take advantage of View compression, deduplication, encryption, replication, and archiving features.
For information on performing MS SQL VDI-based backup, see, see Backup Microsoft SQL Server (VDI-based).
All configurations are for illustrative purposes only. Cohesity recommends following MS SQL best practices.

l Multiple volumes, C, D and F in the figure below l Volume D is running multiple MS SQL databases l Volume F contains database logs

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

The MS SQL VDI-based backup task consists of the following actions:
1. During an MS SQL protection run, a "BACKUP DATABASE" command for the specified MS SQL databases is initiated using MS SQL Server Virtual Device Interface (VDI). The generated backup file is saved on the Cohesity cluster with a date and time stamp.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

2. If the policy is configured to take incremental database backups, it translates to differential backups in case of VDI-based backup.
3. If transaction log backups are specified in the policy, the database transaction logs are backed up to the Cohesity cluster using MS SQL Server Virtual Device Interface (VDI). The logs allow you to roll back to a specific point in time. MS SQL Server automatically truncates the SQL logs after a successful SQL log backup and marks the Virtual Log Files (VLFs) for reuse.

About Log and Full DB Backup Retention Periods
The retention periods of log files and full database server backups are independent of each other. Consider the following examples to help determine the best retention periods for your database server backups. These retention guidelines also apply to full database server and log replication schedules. Retention periods of log files and full database backups must adhere to Microsoft rules for restoring databases.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

1. A point-in-time restore using SQL log backups is dependent on a full backup because a full database server backup must also be available to apply the logs.
When the Cohesity cluster restores to a specific point in time, it must first restore a full database server backup and then apply the appropriate set of logs. If a full database server backup is not available because the retention period of the full database server backup is too short, the Cohesity cluster cannot restore to a point in time within the specified log retention period. For example if the log retention period is three weeks and the full database server backup captures snapshots weekly with a retention period of two weeks, the Cohesity cluster will not be able to restore to any point in time from three weeks ago. In addition, the logs from three weeks ago cannot be utilized and are using disk space.

2. If the log retention period is shorter than the full database server backup retention period, the Cohesity cluster cannot restore to a point in time where the logs are not saved. For example, if the log retention period is two weeks and the full database server backup captures snapshots weekly with a retention period of three weeks, the Cohesity cluster will not be able to restore to any point in time between two and three weeks ago. The Cohesity cluster can, however, restore to the snapshot from three weeks ago.

3. Cohesity recommends specifying a log retention period with extra time to allow for failed full database server backups as demonstrated by the following example. A full database server backup is scheduled weekly with a three-week retention period for both full database server and logs. If the full database server backup failed two weeks ago, the Cohesity cluster can still restore to the point in time from the log indicated by

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases the green arrow.

Microsoft SQL Server

The Cohesity cluster restores full database server backup from three weeks ago and applies the appropriate logs to restore the state to a point.

You can restore to a specific transaction in the log.

Note: A full database backup is not a transaction log backup. Ensure that your SQL Server protection policy has transaction log backup for full and bulk-logged recovery model requirements.

Consider the following when using the Auto Protect option on the backup job
l If new databases are added to the host, the existing filters are applied to the newly added databases. For example, if the exclude filter matches the newly added databases then these databases will be excluded in the backup job.
l If any system databases are excluded by the filters in an SQL server, it will exclude all the system databases belonging to that SQL server.
l When defining filters to exclude AG databases, ensure that the filters are configured on all the AG hosts. For example, to exclude an AG database and if the AG database has 4 hosts, then ensure that the filters are defined on all the four AG hosts.
l Auto protect functionality is supported only for physical SQL jobs (file-based, Native, and volume-based)
l To selectively exclude a SQL database from the protection job, you must upgrade all the cluster nodes to version 6.5.1 and later.
If MS SQL belongs to an AG network, selecting that server displays options for protecting the AG.
l Select all servers that belong to this AG network.
Note: If backing up VMs within an AG, protecting the AG databases requires that all servers within the AG are registered with the Cohesity cluster and are selected for protection. Otherwise AG databases are skipped and only local databases will be backed up. New servers added to AG are not automatically protected.
When using this option when there are multiple AGs, only interlinked AG nodes are automatically selected. For example:
l If there are AGs that use only Node1 and Node2 and other AGs that use Node3 and Node4, if you select Node2 as a source, only Node1 is added automatically.
l If AG1 uses Node1 and Node2, AG2 uses Node2 and Node4, AG3 uses Node3 and Node5. If you select Node2, then these nodes are selected: Node1, Node2 and Node4. Node3 and Node5 are not selected.
When adding nodes to an AG that is protected by Cohesity, ensure you register the node with Cohesity and add it to the Protection Group. Otherwise the AG databases will not be protected.
When removing nodes from an AG that is protected by Cohesity, you can remove it from the Protection Group or keep it in the job; the AG databases remain protected in either case. If the removed node remains in the Protection

This policy tries to achieve similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
l TestAndDev High: The Cohesity cluster writes the data to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. The I/Os with this QoS policy are given higher priority compared to other QoS policies. Use this policy for workloads that require lower I/O latency.

Deduplication in SQL Server File-based Backup
Cohesity supports an efficient Source-Side Deduplication mechanism (to detect changed blocks) for SQL Server File-based backups, that tracks the block-level changes and maintains CPU efficiency even when CBT (Change Block Tracking) is unavailable. When a host reboot occurs during backup, the CBT map is cleared, and the CBT data is lost. This forces you to run a full backup instead of an incremental backup which can be very time-consuming for large SQL Server databases. With this deduplication mechanism enabled for protection groups, if the CBT data is lost due to a Windows host server restart, the changed blocks are identified and transferred from the source. This reduces backup time and ensures efficient CPU utilization. After the next full backup, CBT is re-established and used for subsequent backups.
Note: Source-side deduplication functionality increases the CPU usage during backup operation (when CBT is lost).
The functionality is only supported for new protection groups. The backup of existing protection groups that already use source-side deduplication will complete with a warning which includes the instructions to use the efficient version of source-side deduplication. You can set the deduplication for a protection group using the Source Side Deduplication option in the Additional Settings of a protection.

Microsoft SQL Server VDI-based Recovery Recommendations
The Virtual Device Interface (VDI) is a Microsoft interface that allows the Cohesity agent to execute SQL Server Native backup and restore commands. This backup type produces a standard SQL Server Native backup of type (.BAK), transaction logs, (.TRN), and differentials, (.DIFF). These backup files are stored on a Cohesity View and take advantage of View compression, deduplication, encryption, replication, and archiving features.
The aim of the SQL DBA is to have a combination of backups so that the database can be restored to any point in time. A good combination of backups consists of having a full backup, differential (in Cohesity, incremental) backups, and log backups. For example, all SQL database restores must begin with a full database backup, secondly, a differential can then be applied to the full, and finally, log backups can be applied in sequence to complete the database restore.
When the backups are applied during the database restore process, you are sequentially adding the captured changes to the database: FULL+DIFF+Log1+Log2+Log3 = Restored Database.
All Microsoft VDI backups, their differentials, and their logs are dependent on a full backup to perform a database restore. Microsoft requires that in order to restore a SQL database, you must start with a full backup, then its transaction logs can be applied. This means your backup retention policy must keep a full backup along with its log backups in order to successfully restore a database.
Simply put, a SQL VDI-based database restore requires a full backup to seed the database, then differential and/or log backups are applied to the specified point in time.
We recommend retaining two sets of full backups with their differential and log backups.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

Note: A good backup plan always includes a combination of full, differential, and log backups.
Recover Microsoft SQL Server Volume-based Backups from Archive
Follow one of the workflows described in the following sections to restore a volume-based MS SQL backups from the archive. Using standard MS SQL restore workflows are not supported when restoring from the archive. This is because the backup is volume-based which cannot extract the MDF, NDF, and LDF files from the archive workflow. The volumes that contain the database files must be retrieved from the archive.
Note: When restoring from the archive for file-based MS SQL backups, you can use standard MS SQL restore from archive workflows. For file-based backup, the MDF, NDF, and LDF files can be directly extracted from the archive. For VDI-based backup, the .bak files can be directly extracted from the archive.
For file-based backup, the MDF, NDF, and LDF files can be directly extracted from the archive. You can manually recover database files from a volume-based backup and then use them to manually create a new database in SQL Server.
Note: This method is supported only for full and incremental backups and not log backups.
Files from volume-based backup can be recovered using the following workflows.
Restore to Original Cohesity Cluster (from where MS SQL was Archived)

Recover Microsoft SQL Server Database as Flat Files Cohesity allows you to recover the SQL database backup files to the specified location on the target host, rather than as a database. This provides flexibility for self-service recovery where direct access to the backup files is required. The backup files are recovered to a subdirectory in the specified destination path, with the following file name format: <OriginalHostName>_<OriginalInstanceName>_ <OriginalDatabaseName> For example, the backup files are recovered to C:\RestoreDir\SQLHost01_ MSSQLSERVER_AdventureWorks\ where,
l C:\RestoreDir\ is the destination path, l SQLHost01 is the host, l MSSQLSERVER is the instance, l AdventureWorks is the database.
Note: This is applicable only for the SQL Servers backed up using file-based and VDI-based backup and not applicable to volume-based backup.

SQL Maintenance Mode
You can enable maintenance mode for SQL Server instances and databases. Enabling maintenance mode skips any scheduled activities or manually initiated protection runs. To place a SQL Server instance or database in maintenance mode:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click on the action menu ( ) of the source and select Maintenance. 3. You can initiate the maintenance mode immediately or later.
To initiate the maintenance mode immediately:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

1. Select Start Now. The Start Maintenance Now dialog displays the list of Protection Groups available in the source.
2. Review the list of Protection Groups and enter Yes to confirm. 3. Optionally, you can enter a note. 4. Click Confirm. To schedule the maintenance mode: 1. Select Schedule. 2. On the Schedule Maintenance dialog, enter the start date and time and the
end date and time. 3. Optionally, you can enter a note. 4. Click Save. The SQL Server instance or database will be set in maintenance mode accordingly. AG in Maintenance Mode When maintenance mode is enabled for a SQL instance hosting the AG database, the replica hosting the instance is not considered for the AG backup plan. This behavior is common to both legacy (non-first-class citizen) and first-class citizen features. For legacy AG backup, only the replica for which maintenance mode is enabled will be skipped. You must enable maintenance mode on all the replicas to skip the entire backup.

Migrate Microsoft SQL Server
The following topics provide guidance to help you migrate MS SQL databases:
About Migrating Microsoft SQL Server Databases
You can use MS SQL database migration for the following use cases:
l Back up and migrate a database from a single pane of glass. Leverage database backup to achieve database migration. No more shipping logs across multiple sites or multiple data centers. Upgrade the MS SQL Server version while minimizing application downtime and maintaining the ability to restore to any point in time.
l Staging a database on the target server for faster recovery with Cohesity's database migration. Stage a database on the target SQL server and perform only incremental updates at the file level to improve RPO.
Database migration for file-based MS SQL backups consists of the following actions, which must be initiated manually:
1. Perform the initial copy of database files to the target MS SQL server. 2. Sync forward to the latest incremental/full snapshot available on the cluster. You can
trigger multiple syncs.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

For each sync, Cohesity performs incremental file updates to database files on the target MS SQL server. Syncs ensure files are up to date. The files are not attached to the database until you complete the finalized workflow. This ensures that the database is up to date when finalization occurs. 3. Finalize the migration. Finalizing is available only if the target database is synced to the latest snapshot. This brings the database online. After the database is online and the finalize step succeeds, the recovery task is completed successfully. You cannot perform syncs after this point because the migration workflow is complete.
Migrate Microsoft SQL Server Databases
Before you migrate an MS SQL database, ensure that a file-based snapshot exists on the cluster.
Migrate MS SQL Database
This section lists the steps to migrate an MS SQL database.
1. Select Dashboard and from the drop-down, select MS SQL. 2. Select Migrate from the database's actions menu.
You can also start a restore task by navigating to Data Protection > Recoveries> Recover > Migrate Database (MS SQL only). 3. Search for an MS SQL server or database. Enter characters of the name and a list of items displays. You can optionally specify the wildcard character *. For more information, see Use Wildcard * in Search for Recovery. You can also optionally narrow the search results by specifying filter criteria, for example, you can filter the search results by a specific Protection Group. Click the Add Filters icon, specify the filter and click Add. 4. Select a database and set the migration options for the MS SQL database you want to migrate.
1. Task Name: Optionally change the default name for the task. 2. Objects Being Recovered: This displays the database to be migrated. 3. Sync Options: Specify the sync options for the database to be migrated.
Note: Transaction log backup is not synced. Only the incremental and full backup is synced.
l Auto Sync Databases: This option automatically keeps the database in sync with the latest available snapshot until you finalize the database and bring it online.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Microsoft SQL Server

l Manually Sync Databases: Once the initial database migration is completed, you can sync the migrated database files with newer snapshots available until you finalize the database and bring it online.
4. Recover Point: This displays the selected recover point for the migration. 5. Settings: Specify the SQL Host and SQL Instance to migrate the database
to. Provide the full path location to restore all database files. You can optionally restore data files and log files to different locations. Click Add Alternative Log File Locations and Custom Rules to provide locations for data and log files and any custom rules. For data files, you can provide a full path or pattern for the original files and a location to restore to. When providing a location, use the standard path format. For example, use C:\path for Windows instead of the extended path format \\?\c:\path. This is only used for the destination path in a custom rule and not the source. Accept the file patterns and examples:
l Wildcard character used for file matching such as * l *.ndf - All ndf files. Useful if you want every ndf file to go to the same folder l m:\*.ndf - Every ndf file on drive m: l c:\*1.ndf - Every ndf file on drive c: with a suffix of 1.ndf
l Regex pattern l .*\.ndf - All files with the ndf extension l ^.*foo1.*\.ndf$ - All files with the word foo1 and the extension ndf
l Full path to a source database file Database files that have non-default file extensions or that do not match a specified filename or pattern are restored to the data file restore location. Click Add Another Custom Rule to add multiple custom rules.
Note: Ensure to follow the standard regular expression rules. Specify a dot '.' before asterisk '*' to match all characters, for example, L:.*.ndf.
5. By default, an MS SQL restore WITH RECOVERY is performed. You can optionally toggle this off to perform a restore WITH NO RECOVERY.
6. Click Start Migration. The initial file copy task starts. This is the first step in the migration process.

Cancel Migration
You can cancel an in-progress migration task. Canceling the migration prevents syncing or finalizing the database and may leave it in an unusable state. Delete the database files manually and then start another migration task as needed.
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Recoveries. 2. Find the migration task in the list and click the task name to display its detail page. 3. Click the Cancel button located at the top right of the page. 4. Respond to the confirmation prompt.

Cohesity's software-defined platform provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective backup, recovery, and data management solution for growing Oracle database environments. Cohesity integrates with Oracle Recovery Manager (RMAN) to deliver an integrated and centralized approach to manage Oracle backup jobs. It provides a single location to register and schedule all RMAN scripts across the Oracle environment. See the following topics for details:
Our platform provides several integrations for protecting the Oracle Databases:
l Cohesity Oracle Adapter: Cohesity Oracle Adapter integrates with Oracle Recovery Manager (RMAN) to provide application-consistent backup and recovery for Oracle databases. The adapter provides a unified user interface allowing users to manage and provision all the Oracle database protection services, supporting Oracle single instance, RAC or Oracle Multitenant databases. For details, see Cohesity Oracle Adapter.
l Cohesity Remote Adapter: Cohesity Oracle Remote Adapter is a built-in component of Cohesity that offers flexible management of scripts running on remote hosts. Cohesity Oracle Adapter
The Cohesity Oracle Adapter natively integrates with Oracle Recovery Manager (RMAN) to provide application-consistent backup and recovery for Oracle single-instance deployments, Oracle Exadata Databases Real Application Clusters (RAC), and Veritas Active-Passive.
Based on the policy settings, the Cohesity Oracle Adapter executes an RMAN backup command to initiate a backup of the Oracle Database. The adapter also automatically determines the optimal number of backup channels, based on the compute resources on the Oracle Database server and the number of nodes in the Cohesity cluster. The necessary Cohesity Views are automatically generated (that is, an NFS mount point on the client and an NFS View on Cohesity), where the backups are going to be written. Communication between Cohesity and the Oracle Databases is managed by the Cohesity Oracle Adapter as described in the section below.
Core components
The following lists the core components of the Cohesity Oracle adapter.

l Physical or virtual Oracle instance. l Cohesity Data Cloud. l Cohesity Oracle Adapter. l Archive or tiering target at your data center or cloud provider of choice.

Once the agent is installed, you can create protection policies, jobs, and replication schedules for the Oracle database. Once the database is protected, it can be archived, sent to tape, and or replicated to another Cohesity cluster running in the cloud or on-premises as shown in the below image.

Cohesity Oracle Adapter Benefits
The following table highlights the benefits of using an Oracle Adapter for your Oracle database backup solution:

DB Backup and Storage Challenges

Solutions

Backup agent degrades database performance

The Cohesity Oracle Adapter is a lightweight agent on the target host and does not degrade the application performance.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

DB Backup and Storage Challenges

Solutions

Lack of point-in-time (PIT) Support for recovery and cloning

The Cohesity Oracle Adapter offers an intuitive user interface for PIT Recovery and Clone workflows.

Expensive usage of primary storage

The Cohesity Oracle Adapter supports auto-tiering and global dedupe or compression thereby offering flexibility and cost efficiencies.

Slow data restores

The Cohesity Oracle Adapter offers faster restores as every database backup is fully hydrated using Cohesity snapshots and Oracle incremental merge capabilities.
The traditional backup workflow requires repeated time consuming full backup schedules and Cohesity does not require this because customers only need to do one full backup, then the rest is 'incremental forever'.

Protection against compromised data

Cohesity performs an incremental merge after each incremental backup and validates the backup image to achieve a 'fully hydrated' image copy of the backup. The backup image is stored internally on the Cohesity cluster as an immutable snapshot. The merge will fail if the incremental backup is corrupted.

Higher Total cost of ownership

The distributed web-scale platform is designed for secondary data. Performance and capacity can be scaled linearly simply by adding nodes that eliminates the need for forklift upgrades. You can use the Cohesity Oracle adapter like a pay-as-you-go architecture.

Complex dataprotection environments

The Cohesity Oracle Adapter simplifies the data protection by replacing multiple data protection silos (target storage, media servers, master servers, and cloud gateways) with a single hyperconverged solution for backup, recovery, replication, cloud tiering, archiving, and target storage.

Inability to leverage public cloud for longterm retention

The Cohesity Oracle adapter provides native cloud integration with: l Amazon Web Services (AWS) l Microsoft Azure l Oracle Cloud l Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
It supports long-term retention and tiering of cold data. If the snapshots are sent to the cloud, they can be downloaded on another Cohesity cluster and restores can be performed from this cluster.

RMAN scripts maintenance overhead

No need to maintain any RMAN scripts.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

DB Backup and Storage Challenges

Solutions

No single dashboard to manage Oracle Database data protection

The Cohesity Oracle adapter offers a single dashboard to manage Oracle Database data protection.

Lack of Oracle pointin-time (PIT) restore from cloud archived snapshots

Cohesity supports the PIT restore and clones from cloud archived snapshots.

Mount Point Management

The Cohesity Oracle self-healing manager periodically checks the availability of all the mount points created by the Cohesity Oracle adapter. If a mount point is not available within a specific duration, the self-healing manager performs these actions:
l Treats the mount point as a non-responsive mount point. l Unmount this mount point. l Clean the RMAN sessions associated with the non-responsive mount point.

Managing Standby Databases

Cohesity supports taking backup from standby databases and restore or clone from those backups to protect Oracle data from failures, disasters, human error, and data corruption while providing high availability for mission-critical applications
l Physical StandBy Support We support physical standby databases for all Oracle Configurations.
l Logical StandBy Support We support Oracle Logical Standby with single instance config (non-CDB, non TDE) for Linux only.
Exceptions for Logical StandBy All restrictions for Logical Standby from Oracle will apply to Cohesity. For example, If a logical standby database is not a block-for-block copy of the primary database, you cannot use a logical standby database to back up the primary database. Supported Cohesity Versions We will support this for 6.5.1x, 6.6.x, and future versions only.

Prerequisites for Oracle Database
Make sure the following prerequisites are met before using Oracle Adapter:
l DBIDs: All the Oracle Databases that are protected using the Cohesity cluster should have a unique DBID on the Oracle source where the databases reside.
l SCAN VIP (Applies only to Linux and AIX): To register Oracle RAC, the user must use SCAN-NAME or SCAN-VIP, Otherwise, registration, backup, and recovery of the Oracle databases will fail.
l Installation Agent Type: You must use the same agent installation type (Script or RPM) on all the Oracle RAC nodes.
l Authentication: For database-level authentication, the tns-listener service name must be the same as the database name.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

l Archive Log Mode: Archive Log mode must be enabled for the database opened in Read-Write mode, otherwise the backup task will fail.
l Version: The recovery source and target database must be the same version of the Oracle Database. For example, snapshots of the 11g Oracle Database cannot be recovered to the 12c Oracle Database.
l Full Backup: Cohesity recommends taking a full database backup after any activity that changes the control file (such as adding or removing a data file, restoring to the original location with overwrite, or changing the log file location).
l Oracle Single Instance Deployment: l For Oracle single instance database, the database must be entered into the /etc/oratab file for Linux and AIX and /var/opt/oracle/oratab file for Solaris. Otherwise, Cohesity will not be able to discover this database.
l For Oracle single instance database running on Windows OS, OracleService${ORACLE_SID} service must be running.
l VCS Deployment (Applies only to Linux and AIX): For Veritas Cluster Server (VCS) deployments, the Oracle database environment should be configured in the /etc/oratab on all the VCS nodes.
l Register Oracle RAC: To register an Oracle RAC or a RAC node as a physical server, "host" command must be executed on each of the nodes of that RAC.
The "noac" flag for NFS mounts must be set for Oracle RAC versions 11gR2 and 12cR1. If not set, Oracle RAC backup fails.
l Oracle RAC Database (Applies only to Linux and AIX) l Cohesity Linux Agent must be installed on all the Oracle servers that are part of an Oracle RAC.
l The GRID_HOME must be mentioned in /etc/oratab or /etc/oraInst.loc file .
l DB Authentication If you choose DB authentication, then all the DBs on the system should have the same username and password. Special characters is not supported in the DB authentication password.
l SBT Library (Applies only to Windows): On the Windows Oracle Server, install the SBT library in the same directory where the Windows Agent is installed. By default, the agent is installed in the c:\Program Files\Cohesity\oracle directory. Contact Cohesity Support to obtain the SBT library installer.
l For Oracle alternate restore to the ASM disk group, check the following prerequisite before starting restores on the Cohesity cluster:
l ASM Compatibility ( COMPATIBLE.RDBMS )
The disk group attributes that determine compatibility are COMPATIBLE.ASM, COMPATIBLE.RDBMS. and COMPATIBLE.ADVM. The COMPATIBLE.ASM and COMPATIBLE.RDBMS attribute settings determine the minimum Oracle

The value for the COMPATIBLE.RDBMS disk group attribute determines the minimum COMPATIBLE database initialization parameter setting for any database instance that is allowed to use the disk group.
