Credentials and Privileges for Oracle Database
Once you register your physical servers with Cohesity as Oracle servers, Cohesity will discover your Oracle Database automatically. For Cohesity to successfully discover your Oracle Databases, the user running the Cohesity agent must have the appropriate credentials and privileges.
The Cohesity Linux Agent can be installed as a ROOT user or with a separate OS user (also known as the `OS Service Account user'). The AIX Java Agent and Solaris can be installed only as a ROOT user.
When connecting to the Oracle databases, Cohesity can use either the Oracle OS Authentication or Oracle DB Authentication method. These two types of Oracle authentication are possible for both cases where the Agent is run with the ROOT user or a separate OS Service Account user. Most Oracle Adapter operations can be done using either OS or DB authentication. Some specific operations would require either OS or DB authentication. For more information, see Oracle Authentication Method Option table.
Running Agent with ROOT
You can install Linux Agent or the AIX Java Agent, or Solaris Java Agent to run with the ROOT user:
1. The agent runs every command using the ROOT user, except for Oracle commands and utilities like RMAN or SQLPLUS. To run Oracle commands and utilities, the agent will `su' to the user who is the owner of the Oracle binary in the current Oracle Home. If an Oracle operation is run against a source database that has DB Authentication configured (where the user has previously configured DB credential for this Oracle source database in the Cohesity Oracle Adapter), DB Authentication will be used to run Oracle commands and utilities. Otherwise, OS Authentication via the Oracle binary owner will be used.
2. To use Oracle RAC Multinode Multichannel Backup, you must configure the corresponding source RAC database with DB credentials to allow the Agent to use the required DB Authentication method to run this feature.
3. When you install the Cohesity agent to run with the ROOT user, there is no need to configure additional SUDOERS privileges.
Running Agent with OS Service Account User
The Linux Agent can be installed to run with a specific OS Service Account user that meets the following requirements:
1. The following environmental variables should be set to match the Oracle user when the Cohesity agent is running as non-root and not oracle:
l LD_LIBRARY_PATH
l ORACLE_HOME

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

2. This Service Account user must be granted additional Sudoers privileges to allow the Agent to run operations like NFS mounting Cohesity views. For the complete list of the required Sudoer commands, see Sudoers Permissions for Service Account User .
3. This Service Account user must be part of the OS group that enables this user to either to have the Oracle SYSDBA or SYSBACKUP privileges. For example, on a typical Linux operating system, the OS group `DBA' (dba) often enables the corresponding Oracle SYSDBA privilege. Another customer-defined OS Group, example: 'BACKUPDBA' (backupdba), can enable the corresponding SYSBACKUP privilege. This gives the Service Account user the ability to use the OS Authentication method to connect to Oracle databases with the intended privilege level.
4. If the Agent is running on an Oracle host that is part of a RAC cluster that uses ASM, or a non-RAC Oracle host that uses ASM that is available to that Oracle instance, the Service Account user should also be part of the OSDBA group of your ASM environment. This gives the Service Account user the ability to use the OS Authentication method to indirectly connect to the ASM instance to do things like reading ASM files during backup or restoring files into ASM during database recovery.
5. To use Oracle RAC Multinode Multichannel Backup, you must configure the corresponding source database with DB credentials to allow the Agent to use the required DB Authentication method to run this feature.

Oracle Precheck Utility
When you perform an Oracle adapter workflow such as a backup, alternate restore, or clone operation, the precheck utility automatically checks permissions, disk space, ArchiveLog mode, and so on, based on the parameters you provided. The Precheck utility supports both C++ and AIX Java agents for Oracle.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

If there are discrepancies with the parameters or the environment (server) where the workflow will run, the precheck utility displays the cause of the discrepancies on the Cohesity Dashboard. You can then resolve the discrepancies and try the workflow again. Oracle adapter precheck is a utility that performs environmental checks and reporting for the Oracle Adapter. This precheck ensures that all key criteria are met for running any Oracle Adapter workflow.
Note: This feature is supported only for Oracle databases with Linux agent.
How Precheck Utility Works
Before running the Oracle workflows like backup, alternate restore, or clone, the precheck utility performs sanity checks (permission, disk space, ArchiveLog mode, and so on) based on the parameters you provided. If there is any discrepancy in the parameters you provide or with the environment (server) where the workflow is going to get executed, then the precheck operation fails, resulting in the bailout of Oracle workflow. The precheck utility then displays the cause for the discrepancy on the Cohesity Dashboard to notify the user about the restrictions and prerequisites for the environment and the Oracle adapter workflow.
Performing Prechecks
The precheck utility performs sanity checks for the following Oracle Adapter workflows: l Discovery l Backup l Alternate restore l Clone
Common Checks
l Checks if the Oracle binaries, SQL Plus, RMAN, oraadm, and srvctl have required access permissions for the Oracle agent for work.
l Checks if the Oracle shared libraries (.so) libsql.so has required access permission for the Oracle agent to work.
l Checks if ORACLE_HOME has required RD/WR permission for the agent to run the backup, restore, and clone workflows.
Discovery
The utility performs the following checks while discovering the DBs on the Oracle Host:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

l Checks the password in the case of DB based authentication in Oracle Registration. l Checks if the Cohesityagent user is part of the DBA group. l Oracle Home and Oracle Base binaries and libraries are accessible by Agent user and
DBA group. l Checks the access for ORACLE_HOME/rman ORACLE_BASE l Checks if the ORATAB file is present on the system (generally/etc/oratab). l For RAC, the precheck utility checks if there is +ASM entry the /etc/oratab. l Checks if the /etc/oratab entries are valid.
Backup
The utility performs the following checks before running the backup workflow:
l If Archivelog is enabled: If Archivelog is not enabled, you cannot schedule a backup job.
l If Block Change Tracking (BCT) is enabled: If BCT is not enabled, a warning message is displayed on the Cohesity Dashboard and the backup process will experience high latency.
l SYSDBA privilege: Check if the Cohesityagent user (user running Cohesity agent) is part of the DBA group.
l Adequate permission checks on ORACLE_HOME, and Oracle binaries and libs. l MultiNode-MultiChannel check: In the case of MNMC backup, the precheck utility tries
to connect to all the nodes selected for a backup. l Checks if DB is in READ-WRITE mode for backup.
Alternate Restore
The precheck utility performs the following checks before running the alternate restore workflow:
l Checks if the Cohesityagent user is part of the DBA group. l Adequate permission checks on ORACLE_HOME, ORACLE_BASE, and Oracle binaries
and libs. l Oracle DBSID: Checks the database whether the same SID exists. If the SID exists,
the restore will fail. l Checks for the datafile space for Alternate Restore. l Checks for permission and existence of BCT file (if BCT file location is given from
Cohesity Dashboard). l Checks for permission and existence of DIAG_DEST (if DIAG_DEST is provided from
Cohesity Dashboard).

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

l Checks for permission and existence of AUDIT_LOG_DEST (if AUDIT_LOG_DEST is provided from Cohesity Dashboard).
l Checks if the spfile<NEW_DB_SID> or init<NEW_DB_SID>.ora exists in the new ORACLE_HOME when performing the Restore to alternate DB. This check is to safeguard against the existence of DB with the same name in Shutdown state or a deleted DB which is not cleared properly.
l Oracle version: Restore will fail if the source and destination database versions are not the same.
l Oracle DBNAME: Checks whether the database with the same name exists. If the name exists, restore will fail.
l Existence and permission of the path given at the time of alternate restore. l Disk space availability while performing the alternate restore. l Existence of Oracle Home, Oracle Base, and the required permissions for these
directories. l Checks if the total memory is more than the SGA target. l Checks if the Cohesity agent is installed with a different user than the Owning user of
Oracle binaries (SQL Plus, RMAN, NID).
l Check the database instance name in /etc/oratab. If it exists, the alternate restore will fail.
Clone
The utility performs the following checks before running the clone workflow:
l Checks if the Cohesityagent user is part of the DBA group. l Adequate permission checks on ORACLE_HOME, ORACLE_BASE, and Oracle binaries
and libs. l Checks if the Cohesity view is mounted with the correct option (nolock or lock). l Checks if the spfile<NEW_DB_SID> or init<NEW_DB_SID>.ora exists in the new
ORACLE_HOME when performing the Restore to alternate DB. This check is to safeguard against the existence of a DB with the same name in a Shutdown state or a deleted DB which is not cleared properly. l Oracle compatibility versions: The compatibility is performed by checking the version of SQL Plus in the given ORACLE_HOME_DIR. l Checks if the total memory is more than the SGA target l Oracle DBNAME: Checks whether the Database with the same name exists. l Checks if the Cohesity agent is installed with a different user than the Owning user of Oracle binaries (SQL Plus, RMAN, NID).

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

Best Practices for Oracle Database
Cohesity recommends you follow these best practices when you plan to deploy the Cohesity Oracle adapter:
l If you use choose to DB authentication, then all the DBs on the system should have the same username and password.
l Optional: Create a database user for Cohesity Oracle backup and restore workflow. l Both the Oracle and Cohesity user agents should have permission to write to the
adump and diag directories, the control file, and the database restores locations. l Archivelog mode needs to be enabled to do a backup of an Oracle database opened in
Read-Write mode. l Block Change Tracking (BCT) should be enabled to improve the incremental backup
performance of the Oracle adapter.
The following best practices apply only for Oracle adapter for Linux and AIX:
l Assign sudoers to the user running the Cohesity agent.
l Make the Cohesity agent user part of the Oracle dba group.
l In the case of a RAC or if you are using an Oracle ASM environment, then the Cohesity agent user should be part of the OSDBA group for ASM (also known as ASMDBA group).
Note: In Oracle Adapter workflows, Oracle databases running on Linux and Windows must be protected in separate protection groups. Do not include Linuxand Windows-based Oracle databases in the same protection group.
Considerations for Oracle Database
Review the following considerations:
l If the original database is unavailable (disaster recovery scenario) and no pfile/spfile is present, you should start an instance with the same db_name as the original database in NOMOUNT mode before proceeding with an overwrite recovery of the original database from Cohesity.
l Cohesity does not support the backup of Oracle databases on a physical standby (with open_mode set to 'READ ONLY WITH APPLY') in a Data Guard deployed on Windows.
l Cohesity supports restoring a database from Data Guard Standby to standalone oracle database.
l Our incremental forever backup workflow uses Oracle imagecopy. You have to consider that, if the backup is done with SECTION SIZE breaking up the imagecopy, restore of the imagecopy cannot be done in SECTION SIZE as Oracle RMAN restore

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

does not support that. This results in longer restore time as one RMAN channel will have to restore a complete datafile, instead of the possibility of breaking down this datafile into different 'sections' using SECTION SIZE and have multiple RMAN channels to restore the same datafile in parallel. l Cohesity does not currently support the backup of the Oracle RAC database and Oracle VCS on the Windows server. l Parallel log backup is allowed only for policy-driven backup and not using the 'run now' option. l If you are using the Oracle 21c version and the Oracle Home location is marked as read-only then the alternate restore and clone jobs on the Cohesity cluster may fail. l Backup of the read-only database is only supported on the Standby role. l A replication task of a log backup run of an Oracle Protection Group shows a high amount of "logical data transferred" as it replicates the last successful full/incremental backup data. l Currently, a single instance is only supported with clones regardless of whether the source is Oracle single instance or Oracle RAC. l Cohesity recommends performing a full backup before a log backup for the Oracle databases.
Windows
l For alternate recovery with Oracle on Windows adapter, You must use the "oradim" tool to create the target database service. You should run this service before the recovery, or the recoveries will fail.
l Before the 6.8.1_u2 release, for Oracle on Windows, if a full backup snapshot is deleted, then all subsequent incremental snapshots are not recoverable until the next full backup is available. From Cohesity release 6.8.1_u2 onwards, you can recover an incremental snapshot without the previous full backup on the Cohesity cluster.
AIX
l After cloning the Oracle database running on the AIX server, you must update /etc/filesystem manually to make the mount point used for clone persistent across reboot.
l Instant recovery is not supported for Oracle on AIX.

If you are running the executable file using the following command options, then the agent will be installed on behalf of the specified user and group.

Oracle Database

l -S is the Oracle OS user. l -G is the group where oracle_user is a member. l -c prevents the user from being created if it already exists. In case the

Register Oracle Cluster
Before You Start
Verify the following before registering the RAC source:
1. The system will first scan /etc/oraInst.loc on each node of RAC to get the ORA inventory file path to get the GRID HOME location. If the GRID HOME location is present in the inventory file path, we do not need to parse the /etc/oratab file to look for GRID_HOME.
2. If GRID HOME is not found in the/etc/oraInst.loc file, Cohesity will proceed to look for GRID HOME from /etc/oratab file. Entries in the ORATAB file that starts with the `+' character will be considered as ORATAB entries referring to the GRID HOME. One of such example would be the ASM instance, which would have an entry that starts with `+ASM1:' in the ORATAB file. If multiple such entries are found, Cohesity will use the first entry to retrieve the GRID HOME. The following example indicates the ASM instance and its correspond GRID HOME: +ASM3:/u01/app/12.1.0/grid_1:N.
3. The registration should be done using SCAN IP or NAME (Short Name) so that the Cohesity agent will detect it as RAC.
4. The Cohesity agent must be running on all the nodes in the RAC cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

5. Choose your Oracle Authentication method: OS Authentication (default) or DB Authentication. For more information, see Credentials and Privileges for Oracle Database.
To register the Oracle cluster, follow the steps listed below:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. For an Oracle cluster (RAC - Real Applications Clusters or AP - Active-Passive), Click
Register > Databases > Oracle Source. 3. In the Select Source Type drop-down, select Oracle Cluster. 4. Enter SCAN/VIP Address, for an Oracle cluster, specify the SCAN IP or NAME
(Short Name or FQDN) of the Oracle cluster. 5. Enter Connect Endpoint (optional), specify a reachable endpoint for your Oracle
cluster, this endpoint should be reachable the first time when Cohesity discovers the Oracle cluster. This optional endpoint can be provided if the Scan endpoints are not reachable from the Cohesity cluster. 6. Authentication Type, specify the Authentication Type to register the Oracle source. When connecting to the Oracle databases, Cohesity can use either the Oracle OS Authentication or Oracle DB Authentication method. If you use DB authentication, provide the database username and password. 7. Cohesity Network Interface, Select one of the following options to assign the interface group for the Oracle source.
l Auto Select: If you select this option, the system automatically selects the interface group to use for the VLAN.
l Interface Group: If you select this option, you must select the interface group to use for the source.
Note: If You select a different interface group from what was selected during the Physical source registration, the system will use this VLAN for all the objects in the protection job.
8. Click Register.
If the registration is successful, the registered Oracle cluster appears in the list on the Sources page.

Backup Oracle Database The Cohesity Oracle adapter performs backup and recovery procedures and protect your Oracle databases against data loss or corruption and reconstructs the data if a data loss occurs.

The Recovery Manager (RMAN) is an Oracle utility that can back up, restore, and recover database files. Cohesity Oracle adapter integrates with Oracle RMAN to deliver an integrated and centralized approach to manage Oracle backup jobs and recovery jobs using a single dashboard.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

Cohesity uses the Incremental Merge capability of the Oracle database to create an image copy of a database and periodically update the image copy by merging incremental changes into a new backup copy. The resulting image copy can be used for restore and recovery, duplicating databases, and switching a database to the image copy as shown below.

Cohesity Oracle Adapter Performance
Cohesity Oracle adapter supports multi-threading using multiple RAC nodes and multiple channels for improving backup performance and uses RMAN channels creation Logic given below: RMAN channels=MIN(2* # of Cohesity nodes, 2* # of target server CPU
Note: From Cohesity version 6.4, the backup channels on a single instance and RAC database nodes can be increased from default to 64. (However, the limit from Oracle is 255 channels).

Delete Archive Log

Toggle on and specify the days after which the archived logs on the source database should be deleted. If you specify the value as "0" days, source archived logs will be deleted immediately after each successful Cohesity backup.
If you choose this option, Cohesity issues RMAN DELETE ARCHIVELOG command to delete archived logs after each successful Cohesity backup. Logs are deleted if they are backed up at least once by RMAN and they are older than the days specified in this option. In addition, if you have archived logs not backed up previously by Cohesity and the time satisfies the log delete eligibility, then these logs will be deleted.
However, If you do not enable this option, Cohesity will not delete the archived logs after each Cohesity backup.
If you are using the "Oracle RMAN archived log delete policy" to manage archived logs deletion on this database, depending on the policy, it may prevent Cohesity from deleting the archived logs as Oracle manages the policy.
If you have upgraded Cohesity Data Cloud (both the Cohesity cluster and Cohesity agent) from a previous version, then the archived logs for the existing Protection Group will not be deleted.
Starting with release 6.4.1, the archived logs are not deleted by default.

Recover Oracle Database
The Cohesity Oracle adapter performs recovery procedures to restore a physical backup of a data file or control file and make it available to the Oracle database server using the Recovery Manager (RMAN). Cohesity integrates with the Oracle Recovery Manager (RMAN) to restore data files from backup sets or image copies on disk, either to their current location or to a new location. RMAN automatically restores the archived logs that are needed for recovery and deletes them after the recovery is finished as shown in the illustration below.

The Cohesity Oracle adapter uses the Incremental Merge capability of the Oracle database to perform a backup of database files. The Incremental Merge process involves IMAGE COPY backups that are typically indistinct copies needing redo to be applied to make them consistent. The process makes use of a single RMAN script for backup and restore. The

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

merge process creates a single backup dump that you can use for instantaneous recovery of the backed-up data.

Considerations for Oracle Restore

l Cross-platform Oracle database restore is not supported. (for example, Linux vs Other : AIX, SLES, HP UNIX, etc.)
l Restore across versions is not supported (for example, restoring 11G database to 12c and vice versa)
l Restore from the incremental snapshot is not supported when there is no preceding full backup (as it might have expired) for Oracle on Windows backups.
Recover Oracle Database
Enterprise customers may choose to use the Oracle container Database (CDB) model to leverage the benefits in consolidation and data management. This configuration is also known as Oracle's multitenant (MT) architecture.
A CDB includes zero, one, or many customer-created pluggable databases (PDBs). A PDB is a portable collection of schemas, schema objects, and non-schema objects that appear to an Oracle Net client as a non-CDB.
Cohesity now supports fully automated data protection and management for Oracle CDBs and PDBs Cohesity provides flexible data protection capabilities at both the CDB and PDB level.
To recover a recent or previous backup of an MT and non-MT Oracle Database, perform the steps listed below.

Roll Forward

You can use the Roll Forward recovery option to restore the Oracle databases to the state it was in just before the failure occurred.
We will auto-select the latest backup available and apply the provided archive logs to rollforward the database.
The following inputs will be needed:
l Archive log location: Path at which archive logs are present on the source Oracle host. In the case of a clustered Oracle host, this location can be an ASM path or a path that is present (shared) in all the cluster nodes.
l Restore point-in-time: Optional field to specify the date-time to which the database must be rolled forward. This date-time must be in the future of the latest Cohesity backup. If nothing is specified, then the database will be restored at the latest time possible.
If the Roll Forward option is disabled the database will be restored to the selected point-in-time.

Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.

Instant Recovery - CDB/Oracle Database (Standalone and RAC)
Note: l The Instant Recovery workflow is applicable only for CDB and Oracle Databases.
l Instant recovery will be slower as compared to running a DB on primary till the migration is completed.
Instant Recovery provides near-instant RTO for databases. This is particularly helpful in disaster recovery situations and in cases where complete database failure or downtime can have a significant business impact on the users. With the Oracle Instant Restore functionality, you can quickly bring up the Oracle databases similar to the Clone operations. Once the database is successfully brought

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

up, you can choose to migrate the DATAFILES and LOGFILES from the Cohesity storage to the target Oracle host while the newly restored Oracle database is active and open for read-write operation. The migration operation in the Instant Restore is seamless, and there is no downtime of the Oracle database. Hence using this functionality, you can achieve a near-instant RTO for the Oracle databases.
Note: The Instant Recovery functionality is supported from Oracle 12c and later.
Provide the following information to Instant Recovery: Select one of the following options to proceed with the instant recovery of the source database: Instant Migration If you select this option, the database will be brought up, but the DATAFILES and LOGFILES are present in the Cohesity storage. This is similar to the Clone procedure of the Cohesity recovery workflow for Oracle.

l Channels: Specify the number of channels to perform the restore job. The system will run these channels in parallel to improve the restore performance.

Recover Oracle TDE Database
Introduction
Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) enables you to encrypt sensitive data that you store in tables and tablespaces. After the data is encrypted, this data is transparently decrypted for authorized users or applications when they access this data. TDE helps protect data stored on media (also called data at rest) in the event that the storage media or data file is stolen. You can encrypt sensitive data at the column level or the tablespace level. At the column level, you can encrypt data using selected table columns. TDE tablespace encryption enables you to encrypt all of the data that is stored in a tablespace.
Supported Oracle TDE Wallet types
Cohesity does not impose restriction on wallet types used by the source database for the backup workflow. Your source database can use hardware or software keystore, as well as Oracle Key Vault to centralize your wallet keys management. For restore and clone workflow, Cohesity requires you to set up the appropriate duplicated keystore on your target hosts before using Cohesity restore or clone workflow. In these workflows, only software keystores are supported and keystores must be put into the auto log-in mode before issuing the Cohesity restore or clone workflow.
Recover TDE Database
When you recover a Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) database backup, Oracle performs media recovery on files restored from Cohesity. To perform media recovery on encrypted blocks, Oracle requires access to the respective TDE keystore. TDE keystore considerations

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

l Oracle mandates each database has its own keystore. l A cloned Oracle database must have its TDE keystore with keys that were used during
the previous restore operation. l Cohesity does not store, manage, or solicit any TDE keystore passwords from users. l Cohesity requires users to manage the TDE keystore for your source and restore
target databases.
This design allows you to control and manage the operation and placement of your TDE keystores to ensure it meets your organization's security requirements. To use Cohesity to restore from a backup taken from a TDE database, you must set up a duplicate keystore on the restore target host with a chosen keystore configuration mechanism that is supported by Oracle. To duplicate a keystore from your source database, you can use one of the following methods as recommended by Oracle:
l Backup and close your source keystore and physically copy the keystore to a new location.
l Use the ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT CREATE KEYSTORE command to first create an empty keystore, then use the ADMINISTER KEY MANAGEMENT MERGE KEYSTORE command to populate your new keystore with the keys from the source keystore.
Oracle supports keystore configuration in the following ways:
l For Oracle versions 18c and later, you can use DB parameters WALLET_ROOT and TDE_ CONFIGURATION to direct your database on how to locate your keystore for your database.
l Use the ENCRYPTION_WALLET_LOCATION parameter in sqlnet.ora to configure your keystore location. The file path of this sqlnet parameter can be made dependent on a shell variable that can uniquely identify your database. For example, the value of the shell variable can be your DB UNIQUE NAME.
l Place your keystore in one of the following default locations:
$ORACLE_BASE/admin/<db_unique_name>/wallet
$ORACLE_HOME/admin/<db_unique_name>/wallet
Note: Cohesity requires the restore target keystore to be in auto log-in mode. You can create an auto log-in keystore from your duplicated password-protected keystore. For more information, see Creating an Auto-Login or a Local Auto-Login Software Keystore.
If your Oracle database version is 18c or above, and you would like to use the DB parameters WALLET_ROOT and TDE_CONFIGURATION to configure your restore target

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

database keystore, you can use the Cohesity Version 6.5.1 and later to add the configuration of these DB parameters as part of the restore workflow.
If you choose to configure your restore target database auto log in keystore using sqlnet.ora and you are using a shell variable as part of the file path of the wallet, you have to provide the variable name and its values to be used to the Cohesity Restore workflow. For more information, see Recover Oracle Database.
Source database key rotations considerations
l Cohesity does not store, manage, or solicit any TDE keystore passwords from users. Ensure that you manage the TDE keystore for your source and restore target databases. Refresh your duplicated keystore on the restore target host from time to time if master keys are changed in your source database.
l You can change your source database master keys because a new master key is created, or the keys are rotated.
l A successful Cohesity clone operation from a chosen point-in-time is only possible for a TDE database if your duplicate clone target host keystore has the correct set of master keys from that point-in-time. You do not need the exact set of keys for that point-in-time. It is sufficient if you have those keys as well as more keys than you need in your duplicated keystores. Therefore, the easiest way is to always refresh your duplicate keystore from the latest version of your source keystore.
l Oracle does not provide commands or APIs to delete old master keys from the keystore. Keys can only be added or re-used by key rotation.

Recover Archive Logs for Oracle Database
You can also choose to recover the archive logs for a specific range of the target database. You can restore Archive logs using the LSN (Log Sequence Number), time range, and SCN (System Change Number).
To recover archive logs of an MT and non-MT Oracle Database, perform the steps listed below.
1. Select Data Protection > Recoveries > Recover > Databases > Oracle.
2. Select Archive Logs as the Recover Type.
3. Search for the Oracle instance that needs to be restored or use a wildcard name to search for a specific database instance.
4. Click the change icon (ICON) and select one of the following options:
1. Log Sequence Number: Use this option to restore the Archive logs by the Log Sequence Number (LSN). Specify the LSN range to restore the archive logs.
2. Time: Use this option to restore the Archive logs by time frame. Specify a time range between which you need the archive logs.
3. System Change Number: Use this option to restore Archive logs by System Change Number (SCN). Specify the LSN range to restore the archive logs.
5. Click Next: Recovery Options and specify the recovery options.
1. Restore Archive Logs to: Specify the path to an existing empty directory. The restored Archive logs will reside in this path.
2. Oracle Home: The ORACLE_HOME value for the host where Archive logs are restored. This is required when recovering the archive logs to an alternate Oracle host.
3. Base Directory: The directory for the restored database. This is required when recovering the archive logs to an alternate Oracle host.

Pfile Parameters

The Pfile parameters option allows you to see the target database parameters before the clone job is initiated. The Pfile inherits some source database parameters to the target database and allows you to edit the target database parameters based on your requirement by specifying the additional parameters as a key=value pair. For example, if SGA_TARGET is specified as a part of the pfile parameters, the clone operation will use the value specified in the pfile during the cloning of the source database.

SGA (System Global Area)

The SGA is an area of memory (RAM) allocated to an Oracle Instance when it starts up. Ideally, SGA's value varies from 1024M to 102400M.

Change DBID

If this option is disabled, the cloned database UUID will be the same as the source database and it will not be displayed on the Source page. Later, If the cloned databases are required to be discovered by Cohesity, then follow the steps below:
1. Start the database in MOUNT mode. 2. Run the following query to get the DBID:
"select DBID from GV$database". 3. Change the database DBID using the NID command. 4. Run the following query "select DBID from GV$database" and confirm that the DBID
is different from the one we obtained in step 2. 5. Once confirmed, start the database in OPEN mode. 6. Add the database entry in the oratab file. 7. Do a source refresh. 8. The database should be listed there now. If none of the other databases on the Oracle host have DBID the same as that of the cloned database then, skip steps 1 to 5.

Delete a Protection Group
Perform the following steps to delete a Protection Group:
Note: If the protection group is deleted with snapshots, then no restores can be done from that job unless the snapshots are archived.
1. Select Data Protection > Protection. 2. Find the Job in the list and in the Actions column select Delete.
Alternatively, drill-down on a Job name in the Job column of the list. In the Job Details page, click the (Delete Job) icon. 3. Choose one of the following:
l Delete Job Only: Select this option to delete only the Protection Group. Any local snapshots and or archived snapshots stored on the external targets that were captured by this Job are not deleted.
l Delete Job and Snapshots: If you select the option to delete the Job and all Snapshots, any local Snapshots captured by this Job and stored on this Cluster are deleted. In addition, any archived Snapshots stored on external targets that were captured by this Job are also deleted. (To selectively delete the Snapshots for specific protection runs without deleting the Job, see Deleting Snapshots or Objects.)

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

If the current job is replicating snapshots to a remote cluster or archiving snapshots to an external target, you should probably cancel these replication or archive tasks before deleting the job. For instructions, see Cancel Replication and Archive Copy Tasks of a Protection Group Run. If the Job is replicating to a remote cluster, the inactive job created on the remote cluster is not deleted. In addition, the snapshots that were replicated (copied) to the remote cluster by this job are not deleted. You can log in to the remote cluster to delete the snapshots and the inactive job.

Creating Remote Adapter Job
1. You will create an RMAN data Protection Group leveraging a pre-existing RMAN script. Start by navigating to the Protection Group landing page through the Protection menu option and then click Remote Adapter. Then choose Remote Adapter as the job type. This will start the Protection Group setup workflow with each step of the workflow identified at the top of the screen. For the complete set of instructions on how to create a remote adapter Protection Group, see Add or Edit a Remote Adapter Protection Group.
2. From the New Remote Adapter Protection Group page, either select New Policy to create a new policy or select an existing "Protection Policy". With the existing policy, you can ignore the default "Protection Schedule and Options" as this schedule does not apply for Oracle backups. For more information, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.
3. In the next Specify Script Settings page, specify the Oracle database host information, SSH keys, and script locations. Ensure the SSH key is verified to allow remote login and execution of scripts. This can be verified by running a test script that echoes an output. For more details, see Creating a NFS Export on the Cohesity Storage.
4. Specify a descriptive job name, an appropriate Cohesity storage domain, and a Cohesity View. For more details, see Create or Edit Views.
A summary of the settings appears. Review the summary to ensure that all the settings are correct.
Remote Adapter Considerations for Oracle Database
l Limited Support: Remote Adapter is not supported for Windows. l Register Recovery Scripts: There is no single location to register recovery scripts
when using the remote adapter. l Tracking: You cannot track and report all the recovery tasks and alerts from Cohesity
UI when using the remote adapter. l Data Read Column: The Data Read column in the Protection Group Run details page
shows the total size of the Oracle Databases protected by the job. This is because of an RMAN limitation.

Oracle Database

RMAN NFS Target for Oracle Database
Cohesity provides an efficient integration option with Oracle's Recovery Manager (RMAN) using the NFS mount points. You can present Cohesity as an NFS target for native RMAN backups using the NFS mounts.
To store your RMAN backups on the Cohesity cluster, you need to create a Cohesity View. The View allows you to set the appropriate options for deduplication, compression, and QoS Policies and lets you use NFS mounts to assign channels to every node in a Cohesity cluster.

Each node in a Cohesity cluster has a Virtual IP (VIP). You can use these VIPs in your RMAN scripts when you allocate channels to every node in a Cohesity cluster. By assigning separate channels to every node, you are assigning parallel resources of each node to share the workload and thus making your backups faster.
You can use multiple backup RMAN channels in the backup operation and map several channels to the same VIP to increase the parallel processing. A combination of multiple channels and multiple mount points (defined using VIPs) will yield faster backup performance.

Tip: For best performance, create a mount point for each node in your Cohesity cluster using that node's unique VIP.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

Allocating too many or too few channels can degrade the backup performance. Cohesity recommends that you determine the optimal combination of channels and mount points based on the backup operation on the Oracle side to give you the best performance. The number of channels should be in multiples based on your cluster node count.
For example, if your Cohesity cluster has 3 nodes, then use channels in multiples of 3 (3, 6, 9, 12).
Create NFS Export on Cohesity Storage for Oracle Database
In order to create an NFS export from the Cohesity Data Cloud, follow the steps listed below:
1. Create a storage domain to define the policy settings on the exported shares. For more information, see Create or Edit Storage Domains.
2. Set the data management policies within the storage domain, such as enabling data reduction functionality, the type of data deduplication, and whether inline or post process.
3. Create a View and enter the View Name. The View name is also used to create the exported share name. In the Advanced Settings, select a specific protocol such as NFS. In this example, NFS is the protocol choice for Linux and Unix. For more details, Create a View.
4. Associate this view with the Storage Domain you created. This View inherits the policies associated with the Storage Domain.
5. Allowlist the IP subnet of the Oracle database server. Add the IP address or IP subnet of the Oracle database servers that are allowed to access exported NFS share in the Cohesity View. For more information, see Add Subnets to Allowlists.
Backup and restore for NFS are completely driven at the user or customer end. If you choose Cohesity Data Cloud as NFS target, it just acts as storage.
RMAN NFS Best Practices for Oracle Database
For Oracle RMAN backup configured with NFS Export, the capacity savings are extremely dependent on how RMAN is used. Oracle datafiles contain data blocks, which have block headers at the start of the block. These contain numbers, which are unique for each datafile, making deduplication impossible at the database block size. Also, the end of each block contains a tail check section that features a number generated using data such as the SCN. Even if the block is divided into two, the second half would offer a limited opportunity for deduplication while the first half would offer none. To maximize deduplication efficiency when using RMAN, understand these settings and best practices:
l FILESPERSET=1
This setting suppresses Oracle multiplexing of more than one data file into a backup set. When you suppress Oracle multiplexing, Oracle creates the backup set identically each time the backup runs and maximizes the dedupe rate.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

BACKUP FILESPERSET=1 %BACKUP_TYPE% FORMAT 'bk_u%%u_s%%s_p%%p_t%%t' DATABASE;
l Compression/Encryption
Both compression and encryption must be disabled in RMAN to see effective deduplication. However, compression should be enabled when backing up transaction logs and control files because they don't see good deduplication rates.
RMAN> CONFIGURE BACKUP OPTIMIZATION OFF; RMAN> CONFIGURE ENCRYPTION FOR DATABASE OFF;

l QoS settings for NFS view
NFS view should be created with TestAndDev High QoS settings. This will provide higher priority when Cohesity runs other tasks such as VM backup jobs.
The following table lists the QoS policies in the increasing order of QoS and helps in I/O tuning.

QoS Policy

Description

Backup Target Low

Use this policy for non-latency sensitive workloads such as backups, which keep many I/Os outstanding. Data is written to HDD and has higher latency compared to other QoS policies writing to a SSD.

Backup Target High

The same as Backup Target Low, except that the priority for processing workloads with this policy is higher than workloads with Backup Target Low when there is contention.

Backup Target SSD

Use this policy for workloads such as backups, which keep many I/Os outstanding. However, in this case, Cohesity sends both sequential and random I/Os to SSD. The latency is lower than other Backup Target policies.

Backup Target CommVault

Use this policy to intelligently detect and exclude application-specific markers to achieve better deduplication when CommVault backup application is writing to a Cohesity View. Data is written to SSD and has the same priority and latency as TestAndDev High.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

QoS Policy TestAndDev Low
TestAndDev High

Description
Use this policy for workloads that require lower I/O latency or do not keep many I/Os outstanding, as the I/Os are given higher priority compared to other QoS policies. Data is written to SSD and has lower latency compared to Backup Target SSD.
The same as TestAndDev Low, except that the I/Os with this QoS policy are given higher priority compared to I/Os with TestAndDev Low when there is contention.

l Load balancing RMAN jobs
To get the best performance with Oracle RMAN, the load from backup and restore jobs should be distributed between all the Cohesity nodes in the cluster. To load balance work between the nodes, create multiple mount points with different VIP of the Cohesity Data Cloud on the Oracle Server as RMAN target.
For example, assume a view named nfs_view created (using Step 4) by selecting the suitable QoS at Cohesity Domain. The same view is used to create multiple mount points with different VIP of the Cohesity Data Cloud.
This is an example how the mount is performed:
create directory structure

mkdir -p /orcl2 mkdir -p /orcl3 mkdir -p /orcl4

mkdir -p /orcl1

The following Linux NFS settings are the recommended options for the Cohesity as they provide the best performance:

noatime,vers=3,proto=tcp,rsize=1048576,wsize=1048576,hard,intr,nolock
Example: Mount VIPs using the options above:
sudo mount -t nfs -o noatime,vers=3,proto=tcp,rsize=1048576,wsize=1048576,hard,intr,nolock 192.10.2.10:/nfs_view /orcl1 sudo mount -t nfs -o noatime,vers=3,proto=tcp,rsize=1048576,wsize=1048576,hard,intr,nolock 192.10.2.11:/nfs_view /orcl2 sudo mount -t nfs -o noatime,vers=3,proto=tcp,rsize=1048576,wsize=1048576,hard,intr,nolock 192.10.2.12:/nfs_view /orcl3

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

sudo mount -t nfs -o noatime,vers=3,proto=tcp,rsize=1048576,wsize=1048576,hard,intr,nolock 192.10.2.13:/nfs_view /orcl4

RMAN Full backup script looks similar to this example:
CONFIGURE DEFAULT DEVICE TYPE TO DISK; CONFIGURE DEVICE TYPE DISK PARALLELISM 4 BACKUP TYPE TO BACKUPSET;
run { allocate channel t1 type disk FORMAT '/orcl1/%d_%T_%U'; allocate channel t2 type disk FORMAT '/orcl2/%d_%T_%U'; allocate channel t3 type disk FORMAT '/orcl3/%d_%T_%U'; allocate channel t4 type disk FORMAT '/orcl4/%d_%T_%U';
sql 'alter system archive log current'; backup spfile tag 'spfile'; CONFIGURE CONTROLFILE AUTOBACKUP OFF; backup current controlfile tag 'controlfile_1'; backup incremental level 1 for recover of copy with tag 'Full_1' database plus archivelog delete input; RECOVER COPY OF DATABASE WITH TAG 'Full_1'; }
l Archive Logs and Control Files By default, RMAN interleaves archive (transaction) logs and control files with database content. This defeats deduplication because it changes the alignment of the data. When used with deduplication, these additional files should be written to separate streams.
l The Cohesity cluster will work with Oracle compression and encryption functionality. If encryption and compression are turned on, make sure to disable data deduplication on the Cohesity View.
l When the native deduplication built-in to the Cohesity Data Cloud is not used, the alternate storage and time-saving option is native Oracle compression with the multichannel target. For storage, RMAN compression shows around 50% reduction and also shows a good backup time reduction. However, these are dependent highly on Oracle RMAN performance and tuning. This may cause extra load to the Oracle DB server.
For more information, see Cohesity and Oracle RMAN Guide.

Cohesity Oracle SBT Plug-in
The Cohesity Oracle SBT Plug-in allows you to use Cohesity as target storage for backing up Oracle databases. Cohesity Oracle SBT Plug-in protects the Oracle databases using the Oracle Recovery Manager (RMAN) script. Cohesity natively integrates with Oracle Recovery Manager (RMAN) to provide application-consistent backup and recovery for Oracle databases including single instance or Real Application Clusters (RAC). Check the Databases section in the Supported Software topic for a complete list of supported Oracle versions for Cohesity SBT Plug-in and the supported Cohesity cluster versions.
Backup and Restore using Cohesity Oracle SBT Plug-In
Note: l Cohesity recommends you schedule periodic full backups for the Oracle database
protection using Oracle SBT Plug-In.
l For Oracle 19c, the Oracle SBT plug-in supports backing up of containerized databases (CDB/PDB).
To back up a database:
1. Create views as the target where the databases need to be backed up. 2. Add the Oracle host(s) to the allowlist of the view or global allowlist. 3. Allocate SBT channels in the RMAN scripts to include the Cohesity-specific
parameters. For example:
'ALLOCATE CHANNEL c1 DEVICE TYPE SBT_TAPE PARMS 'SBT_ LIBRARY=/opt/cohesity_sbt/lib/libsbt_linux_x86_64.so, SBT_PARMS=(data_ view=/SbtView1/db1,vips=192.0.2.1)'
4. Schedule the backup with Cohesity Remote Adapter or external scheduler by running the script from the previous step.
To restore a database:
1. Select the view or snapshot where the backup data exists for a specific Database for restore.
2. Expose the snapshot to a view if necessary and optionally mount to a target source if the customer wants to see the backup pieces on the view.
3. Write RMAN restore scripts to include the Cohesity-specific parameters same as the

4. Run the script manually to perform the restore.

Source-Side Deduplication for Oracle Database
The source-side deduplication feature is built into the Cohesity SBT plugin. As long as you use the SBT plugin, the source-side deduplication will be enabled automatically by default.
The Cohesity source-side deduplication provides storage-efficient deduplication that enhances your Oracle environment with faster backups and reduced network traffic between Oracle servers and the Cohesity.
This functionality is enabled by default on the Cohesity cluster. It shifts the deduplication processes to the Oracle server and reduces CPU consumption on the Cohesity allowing further scaling to support more workloads. Additionally, the source-side deduplication

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

plugin Cohesity integrates with the Platform's built-in deduplication and minimizes data traffic by moving only the new data blocks.
Advantages of the Source-Side Deduplication Plugin
l Faster backups l Reduce network traffic between Oracle servers and Cohesity l Enables more frequent backups resulting in higher RPOs l Offloading deduplication reduces the CPU consumption and enables the Cohesity to
run more backup workload sessions.
The following diagram illustrates how source-side deduplication reduces CPU consumption by offloading the deduplication to the source client.

For a complete set of instructions on how to enable source-side deduplication for Oracle when using the Remote Adapter RMAN script, see Install Cohesity Oracle SBT Plug-in (For Linux).
Cohesity Oracle SBT Plug-In for ZDLRA
The Cohesity SBT plug-in for ZDLRA will be used in the customer data center to facilitate ZDLRA copy jobs to the Cohesity. These copy jobs are queued and executed by ZDLRA according to the configured copy job policies.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

Cohesity acts as a tape device for the ZDLRA appliance and provides cost-efficiency by offloading backups to Cohesity for long-term storage. Backups are stored on Cohesity cluster and snapshotted into immutable views to guarantee data protection. Cohesity does its cataloging of backups by collecting metadata of backups and stores this metadata in the Catalog View.
Once the backup is on the Cohesity cluster, protection jobs can be configured to replicate backups to other Cohesity clusters, or archived to Cloud storage. Cohesity provides flexible restore options through ZDLRA or directly from Cohesity without ZDLRA. Refer to the Restore section for more details.
Roles
There are 3 roles in a ZDLRA environment with a Cohesity cluster. Cohesity administrator, ZDLRA administrator, and Oracle DBA.
l Cohesity Administrator: Cohesity administrator manages the views and protection jobs for ZDLRA to copy the backup data to and restore from the Cohesity cluster.
l ZDLRA Administrator: ZDLRA administrator configures ZDLRA copy jobs to copy the backup data to the Cohesity views created by the Cohesity administrator.
l Oracle DBA: Oracle DBA performs the restore from ZDLRA or directly from Cohesity with the view information provided by the Cohesity administrator.
Cohesity Views for ZDLRA
A view provides a storage location in a storage domain on the Cohesity cluster. These views can only be accessed by machines specified in the allowlisted subnets. A view that is created and used specifically as a storage location for the ZDLRA copy job is only accessible via the Cohesity SBT driver that is installed on the ZDLRA.
Two distinct types of views are required for ZDLRA backups.
Data View

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

a. A Data View is used to store the backup data that is copied to the Cohesity cluster through ZDLRA.
b. Multiple Data Views can be configured for one ZDLRA. Each Data View can be used for more than one database.
c. The Cohesity administrator will provide the ZDLRA administrator the information about the view that is required to configure the ZDLRA copy job attributes.
d. The data view name needs to be configured as the value of the parameter data_view in the ZDLRA copy job Attribute Set.
Catalog View
a. A Catalog View is used for storing the metadata of the backup data that is copied to the Cohesity Data Views through ZDLRA.
b. This metadata is used by the Cohesity SBT code when ZDLRA issues a restore or crosscheck operation to the Cohesity SBT.
c. The Cohesity administrator will provide the ZDLRA administrator with information about the Catalog View. The ZDLRA administrator will need to know this information to correctly install the Cohesity ZDLRA Package on ZDLRA.
d. The Catalog View name needs to be configured as the value of the parameter a part of catalog_view in the ZDLRA copy job Attribute Set and in the configuration file /opt/cohesity_sbt/config/sbt_config.cfg on ZDLRA hosts.
Data Flow
When the copy job runs on the ZDLRA, via the SBT library, it will write data to two separate locations on the Cohesity. Each backup piece received from ZDLRA will be written to the Data View and its corresponding metadata will be written to the Catalog View with a filename that is the same name as the backup piece filename.
Note: The file names on both views are the same; however, the contents of the files are different. Do not configure the Data View and Catalog View as the same view, or else your copy job execution will fail.
Prerequisites
This section lists the prerequisites for ZDLRA and Oracle host.
ZDLRA Requirements
The following files are required on the ZDLRA:
1. SBT Library File: The SBT library file is a single .so file extracted from the ZDLRA Package.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

2. Configuration File: The configuration file is a text file created by the ZDLRA administrator on ZDLRA hosts to set the catalog view for ZDLRA copy jobs.
3. ZDLRA Utility File: The ZDLRA utility file is an executable that can be run on ZDLRA to list the total number of files and the total size of the data copied to Cohesity for each DB in a particular time range. This file is an optional tool. The ZDLRA backup and restore are not affected without this tool.
Oracle Host Requirements
The following files are required on the Oracle host when restoring directly from Cohesity:
1. RMAN Script: Oracle DBA needs to write a restore script based on the sample RMAN script provided by the Cohesity administrator.
2. SBT Library File: The SBT library file is a single .so file extracted from the ZDLRA Package.
Installation and Configuration
This section lists the configuration steps for both the Cohesity cluster and the ZDLRA appliance.
l Configuring Cohesity Cluster l Configuring ZDLRA
Configuring Cohesity Cluster
The steps listed in this section are performed by the Cohesity Administrator.
1. Verify the Cohesity Cluster Version. The cluster must be running with the locked view and apiKey features. Cluster versions 6.5.1 or above support these features. If your cluster runs on a special version, contact Cohesity support to confirm if it supports ZDLRA. If your cluster is running on another version, contact Cohesity Support to confirm if it supports ZDLRA.
2. Configure View Indexing. 3. Create a Cohesity Protection Policy.
Create Cohesity Protection Policies to be used for the view protection jobs for both the catalog view and all the data views. The retention period of the data views should be equal or greater than the retention period of the corresponding SBT copy job. For more information, see Protect Oracle Database.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

Note: The schedule of the Cohesity protection policy for data views will be ignored because the protection jobs are triggered by ZDLRA instead of Cohesity. Cohesity will expire the data based on the retention of the Cohesity protection policy, it won't affect the data and metadata on the ZDLRA end. If the SBT retention on the ZDLRA side is less than the one on the Cohesity side, the catalog entries in the Cohesity catalog view will be deleted when ZDLRA expires the data but the data in the Cohesity snapshots of the data view will NOT be deleted.
4. Install the ZDLRA Package on a Linux host which will be used to manage the Cohesity views and jobs for ZDLRA/SBT backups. a. Download the ZDLRA package cohesity_zdlra.tar.gz from the Cohesity Downloads Site to the management Linux host. b. Run the following command to extract the file:
tar xvf cohesity_zdlra.tar.gz
c. Run the following command to install the installer in the extracted directory cohesity_zdlra: sudo ./cohesity_zdlra_sbt_linux_x86_64_installer for default installation which will install the package to /opt/cohesity_sbt or ./cohesity_zdlra_sbt_linux_x86_64_installer -- -d <install_dir> for customized installation.
d. Refer to the "Cohesity Installer Details" section in the Appendix for more information about what the package installs.
5. Create a Cohesity Data Security user. Log in to Cohesity UI as an admin. Create a user with a Data Security role. The user will be used to manage the views for the ZDLRA copy and restore jobs. For more information, see Manage Roles. Optionally, you can generate an API key by running the following CLI command in the Cohesity CLI:
<install_dir>/bin/view_cli generate --host <cluster_name_or_ip> -username <user_with_admin_role> --password <password> --apikeyusername <data_security_username> --apikeyname <choose_your_own_keyname>
For more information on arguments description, see ZDLRA CLI Commands. 6. Create Cohesity Views and Protection Jobs.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

There are two ways to create the Cohesity views and view protection jobs for ZDLRA copy jobs. One is to run the script from the Cohesity admin's Linux host. The other is to create them from Cohesity UI.
a. Create Cohesity Views and Protection Jobs with Script The ZDLRA package installer contains a convenient script that will create the Cohesity View and Protection Job at the same time. The script is called cohesity_create_view_for_zdlra.sh. It is located in /opt/cohesity_ sbt/bin for default installation or <install_dir>/bin for customized installation. The parameters that can be used with this script are explained in detail in the Appendix section of this document. The -u and -p options are not needed if the API key (generated in step 5) is supplied. Each ZDLRA can have one Catalog View and one or more Data Views. i. As a user with the Data Security Role, create a Catalog View by running the following command:
./cohesity_create_view_for_zdlra.sh -V <zdlra_catalog_view_ name> -I <cluster_ip> -P <policy_name> -W <allowlist/subnet_ mask> -s <storage_domain> [-u <user_with_data_security_role> -p <password_for_user> -J <job_name>]
ii. As a user with the Data Security Role, create a Data View by running the following command:
./cohesity_create_view_for_zdlra.sh -V <zdlra_data_view_name> -I <cluster_ip> -P <policy_name> -W <allowlist/subnet_mask> s <storage_domain> -C <zdlra_catalog_view_name> [-u <user_ with_data_security_role> -p <password_for_user> -J <job_ name>]
Note: A data view can only be created after the catalog view is created and must set the catalog view name with the -C option.
The views created using the script are locked views that cannot be deleted or updated from Cohesity UI. The allowlist should be a valid IPv4 address and the subnet_mask should be an integer between 0 and 32. If the value of subnet_mask is 32, it is for the single IP, in this case, the "/32" can be omitted. If multiple IPs need to be allowlisted, separate them with ",". For example,

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

./cohesity_create_view_for_zdlra.sh -V zdlra_catalog -I cluster01 -P zdlra_365 -W 169.22.61.10,169.22.61.12/24 -s DefaultStorageDomain
b. Create Cohesity Views and Protection Jobs from Cohesity UI.
This section lists steps the to create the views and jobs for ZDLRA from Cohesity UI. Please note the views created from Cohesity UI are not locked views so that they can be updated from Cohesity UI.
i. Create the catalog view as a regular view
I. From the Cohesity UI, navigate to File Services > Views, then click the + button in the upper-right corner and click New View from the dropdown list.
II. Provide the view attributes and click the Create button.
ii. Create a view protection job for the catalog view
I. From the Cohesity UI, navigate to Data Protection > Protection, then click the + button in the upper-right corner and click the View menu from the dropdown list.
II. Select the catalog view name and click the Save Selection button.
III. Provide the job attributes and click the Protect button.
iii. Create the data view from the ZDLRA view template
I. From the Cohesity UI, navigate to File Services > Views, then click the + button in the upper-right corner and click the New View from Template menu from the dropdown list.
II. Select ZDLRA from the dropdown list.
III. Provide the view attributes and click the Create button.
iv. Create a view protection job for the data view
I. From the Cohesity UI, navigate to Data Protection > Protection, then click the + button in the upper-right corner and click the View menu from the dropdown list.
II. Select the data view name and click the Save Selection button.
III. In addition to the job name and policy, configure the catalog view by clicking the Additional Settings dropdown and select SBT as the client type of Externally Triggered Settings and set the catalog name to the Catalog View option.
IV. Click the Protect button to create the job.

a. Data View name and VIPs Data View name and VIPs are used in the configuration of the environment variables for the ZDLRA copy job Attribute Set on the ZDLRA.

Configuring ZDLRA
The steps listed in this section are performed by the ZDLRA Administrator.
1. Install the Cohesity ZDLRA Plug-in. Optionally, obtain the file libst_linux_x86_64.so from the Cohesity administrator and place it in a directory on saved on the Oracle databse server. For example:
/opt/cohesity_sbt/lib.
2. Create the configuration file. Manually create a configuration file called /opt/cohesity_sbt/config/sbt_ config.cfg and add the following entry to this file for each Cohesity cluster:
Cohesity_cluster : { catalog_view: "<catalog_view_name>" catalog_vips: "<cluster_VIPs>" }
l The catalog_vips could be one or more IP addresses or hostnames of the Cohesity cluster VIPs. If more than one VIPs are specified, separate them with :. For example:
catalog_vips:"10.2.100.178:10.2.100.180:10.2.100.182"
l By default, the SBT log will be written to the sbtio.log of ZDLRA, you may add the optional parameter log_dir to the configuration file to redirect the logs to any directory of your choice. For example:
log_dir: "/opt/cohesit_sbt/logs"
l By default, the SBT log_level is 1 which will generate normal information such as the file names, speed, parameters, etc. This value can be set to 0 in the configuration file to allow only error messages to be generated. For example:
log_level: 0 #log_level: 0 for error, 1 for info, 2 for debug

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

The log_level can also be configured in the copy job attribute by adding log_ level=n in the ENV of PARMS. In this case, the log_level only applies to the specific copy job.
A sample sbt_config.cfg file is given below:
[oracle@rack110dbadm01 ~]$ cat /opt/cohesity_sbt/config/sbt_ config.cfg log_level: 1

cohesity_cluster: { catalog_view: "catalog" catalog_vips: "10.14.25.96:10.14.25.97:10.14.25.98"
}

cohesity_cluster: { catalog_view: "catalog" catalog_vips: "10.14.53.50:10.14.53.103:10.14.53.111"
}

cohesity_cluster: { catalog_view: "catalog_400d" catalog_vips: "10.2.200.64"
}

This file should only be created on the ZDLRA, not on the Oracle hosts. 3. Create the ZDLRA SBT library using DBMS_RA.CREATE_SBT_LIBRARY.
For example:

DBMS_RA.CREATE_SBT_LIBRARY(

LIB_NAM

=> 'COHESITY_SBT',

DRIVE

=> 24,

RESTORE_DRIVES

=> 8,

PARMS

=> 'SBT_LIBRARY=/opt/cohesity_sbt/lib/libsbt_linux_x86_64.so'

);

4. Create the ZDLRA copy job Attribute Set. Coordinate with your Cohesity administrator on the data views and catalog views to be used for copy jobs.
For example:

'ENV=(data_view=<data_view_name>,vips=<cluster_vips>,catalog_ view=<catalog_view_name>,is_zdlra_copy_job=true,<log_level=<log_ level>>)'
);

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

The VIPs could be one or more IP addresses of the Cohesity cluster VIPs. If more than one VIPs are specified, separate them with ":".

Note: All the VIPs configured in the ZDLRA copy job attributes must exist in the corresponding cluster entry in the configuration file /opt/cohesity_ sbt/config/sbt_config.cfg on the ZDLRA hosts.

By default, the log_level is 1, which will generate normal information such as the file names, speed, parameters, etc. This value can be set to 0 to allow only errors to be generated or set to 2 for debug logs.
Example 1: Single VIP

DBMS_RA.CREATE_SBT_ATTRIBUTE_SET (

35,vips=10.2.32.123,catalog_view=zdlra_400d,is_zdlra_copy_job=true)'

);

Example 2: Multiple VIPs

=> `COHESITY_SBT',

=> `ZDLRA_TEST',

=> 16,

=> 'ENV=(data_view=zdlra_

100,vips=10.2.32.123:10.2.32.125:10.2.32.127:10.2.32.129,catalog_

view=zdlra_400d,is_zdlra_copy_job=true)'

Example 3: Multiple VIPs and disable regular logs

DBMS_RA.CREATE_SBT_ATTRIBUTE_SET (

=> 'COHESITY_SBT',

ATTRIBUTE_SET_NAME

=> 'ZDLRA_TEST',

STREAMS

=> 16,

PARAMS

=> 'ENV=(data_view=zdlra_

100,vips=10.2.32.123:10.2.32.125:10.2.32.127:10.2.32.129,catalog_

view=zdlra_400d,is_zdlra_copy_job=true,log_level=0)'

5. Create a ZDLRA copy job template for each copy job. For example:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

DBMS_RA.QUEUE_SBT_BACKUP_TAST(`DB123_FULL');

Restore

This section lists the steps for restoring data from ZDLRA and direct restore without ZDLRA, using the Cohesity cluster.
l Restore through ZDLRA from the Local Cohesity Cluster l Restore through ZDLRA from Replicated Cohesity Cluster l Direct Restore without ZDLRA l Direct Restore from the Remote Cluster without ZDLRA l Restore from the Remote Cluster through ZDLRA l Direct Restore from Archival without ZDLRA l Restore from Archival through ZDLRA

Restore through ZDLRA from the Local Cohesity Cluster

Connect to the ZDLRA catalog to run the restore. ZDLRA will automatically read the backup data from the Cohesity cluster if they were copied to Cohesity and the local copy has been deleted.

Restore through ZDLRA from Replicated Cohesity Cluster

Cohesity administrator updates the whitelists of both replicated data view and catalog view to the IP addresses of the ZDLRA nodes.
ZDLRA administrator adds the replicated Cohesity cluster VIPs and replicated catalog view name in the configuration file /opt/cohesity_sbt/config/sbt_config.cfg on the ZDLRA hosts.
Connect to the ZDLRA catalog to run the restore. ZDLRA will automatically read the backup data from the replicated Cohesity cluster if they were copied to Cohesity and the local copy has been deleted.
Note: The files already expired on the local Cohesity cluster can not be restored by this way. To restore the files older than the retention of the policy on the local cluster, please follow the direct restore from Cohesity instructions.

Direct Restore without ZDLRA

The steps listed in this section are performed by the Oracle DBA and Cohesity Administrator.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

1. Oracle DBA requests the cohesity_zdlra.tar.gz tar file from the Cohesity administrator and extract the Cohesity SBT plug-in libsbt_linux_x86_64.so file.
The libsbt_linux_x86_64.so file is then placed in the directory of their choice. For example:
/opt/cohesity_sbt/lib.
2. Oracle DBA provides the following information to the Cohesity administrator:
i. The path of the Cohesity SBT plugin. For example:
/opt/cohesity_sbt/lib/libsbt_linux_x86_64.so.
ii. The DB name to be restored.
iii. The time range of the files to be used for restore. The time is determined by the time point when the files were copied to the Cohesity cluster.
iv. The IP address of the database server to which the files need to be restored. If the database server has more than one IP address, provide the IP address used to connect the Cohesity cluster. If you are not sure which one is used for connecting to the Cohesity cluster, all the IP addresses can be provided.
3. The Cohesity administrator generates an RMAN re-catalog script by running the cohesity_prepare_restore.sh script and with the information provided by the Oracle DBA.
The following example generates the re-catalog script for database testdb for backup pieces within the time range 2020/04/14-23:53:01 to 2020/07/16-19:48:43.
./cohesity_prepare_restore.sh -I 10.2.148.135 -S /opt/cohesity_ sbt/lib/libsbt_linux_x86_64.so -D testdb -W 0.0.0.0/0 -s 2020/04/1423:53:01 -e 2020/07/16-19:48:43 -J jobname
4. The Cohesity administrator provides the sample script generated by the cohesity_ prepare_restore.sh to the Oracle DBA.
The sample script can be found from /tmp/cohesity_sbt_<timestamp>/cohesity_ catalog_sbt.<dbname>.rman.
5. Oracle DBA performs the re-catalog and restores the database based on the sample script provided by the Cohesity administrator by following steps below:
i. Oracle DBA opens the RMAN script to read the comments, which contains the list of available backup pieces, each with an associated time stamp and file size, that matches your input to the script.
ii. Identify the control file name that needs to be restored and write an RMAN script to restore the control file according to the SBT parameters in the sample script.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

iii. Use RMAN to directly restore from individual backup pieces, or run the sample script in RMAN to re-catalog all the backup pieces if the target Oracle database is already mounted or open.
iv. Write an RMAN script to restore the database according to the SBT parameters in the sample script.
6. After the restore/recovery is finished, the Cohesity administrator cleans the cloned views and temp files with the script cohesity_end_restore.sh. For example:
./cohesity_end_restore.sh -I 10.2.148.135 -d /tmp/cohesity_sbt_ 20200611_100424
Direct Restore from the Remote Cluster without ZDLRA
To restore the files replicated to the remote cluster, follow the same procedure of Restore through ZDLRA from the Local Cohesity Cluster from the local cluster but set the cluster IP to the remote cluster.
Restore from the Remote Cluster through ZDLRA
To restore the files replicated to the remote cluster, follow the following steps.
1. The Cohesity administrator runs the script cohesity_prepare_restore.sh as described in the section Direct restore without ZDLRA and adds the option -Z. For example:
./cohesity_prepare_restore.sh -Z -I 10.2.148.135 -S /opt/cohesity_ sbt/lib/libsbt_linux_x86_64.so -D testdb -W 0.0.0.0/0 -s 2020/04/1423:53:01 -e 2020/07/16-19:48:43 -J jobname
2. ZDLRA administrator adds the remote cluster vip and the catalog view created in the previous step to the /opt/cohesity_sbt/config/sbt_config.cfg files on all the ZDLRA nodes.
3. Oracle DBA runs the restore on the target Oracle host against ZDLRA. 4. After the restore, the Cohesity administrator runs the script cohesity_end_
restore.sh to clean up the cloned views and the ZDLRA administrator deletes the catalog view entries from the files /opt/cohesity_sbt/config/sbt_config.cfg on all the ZDLRA nodes.
Direct Restore from Archival without ZDLRA
To restore the files archived to the cloud, follow the same procedure of Direct restore without ZDLRA from the local cluster and add the -A <archival_target> option to the cohesity_prepare_restore.sh command.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

Restore from Archival through ZDLRA
To restore the files archived to the cloud through ZDLRA, follow the same procedure of Direct Restore from Archival without ZDLRA from the local cluster and add the -Z option to the cohesity_prepare_restore.sh command.
ZDLRA and SBT restore visibility
The ZDLRA and SBT restore visibility feature allows you to check the reading activities against externally triggered views through the Cohesity SBT plugin. Typically the reading happens when restoring Oracle databases from the data view snapshots or clones of them. To enable the ZDLRA and SBT restore visibility feature, you have to configure the File Service Audit Logs on the cluster and upgrade both the SBT plugin and the ZDLRA package to the latest version.
Enable or Disable File Services Audit Logs
By default, the File Services Audit setting is disabled. You should enable the File Services Audit option for Cohesity to start logging the Cohesity SBT read events. You can disable or enable it back from the Settings tab of the Audit Logs page. When you disable the option, the old logs are retained until the retention period ends. To enable or disable File Services Audit, complete the following:
1. Navigate to System > Audit Logs > Log Settings. 2. In the Log Settings tab, turn on/off the File Services Audit toggle to enable or
disable. After enabling the File Services Audit, the Log Retention Period audit information option appears. Use this option to set the audit logs retention period.
Set Log Retention Period for File Services Audit Logs
You can set the retention period for file services audit logs on the Cohesity cluster.
Note: The default retention period is 90 days. You can increase or decrease the renewal period. Once the retention period expires, the audit logs are deleted automatically.
To set a retention period for File Services Audit Logs, complete the following: 1. Navigate to System > Audit Logs > Log Settings. 2. In the File Services Audit section of the Log Settings tab, click the icon for the Log Retention Period option, type the desired number, and select the retention period (Days, Weeks, Months, or Years).

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

The Log Retention Period is displayed in days as Cohesity converts weeks, months, or years into days. 3. Click Save.
Add IP Allowlist for File Services Audit Logs
The host that installed the ZDLRA package has to be included in the IP allowlist of the File Service Audit Logs to print the SBT read report. By default, every client that is part of the Global Allowlist set at the cluster level can access the File Services audit logs. You can change access permission by the Override Allowlist option to allow or deny access to a subnet. To override the global IP allowlist set at the cluster level and add a subnet to the allowlist for file service audit:
1. Navigate to System > Audit Logs > Log Settings. 2. In the IP Allowlist section of the Log Settings page, turn on the Override Global
IP Allowlist toggle. 3. Click Add. 4. In the Add Allowlist dialog, complete the following:
a. Type the Subnet IP address in CIDR format. Example: Subnet in CIDR format (IPv4 - 10.0.0.0/24 or IPv6 FE80:CD00::211E:729C/60).
b. The NFS Permissions, SMB Permissions, or S3 Permissions can be any value. (Read/Write, Read Only, or Disabled).
c. Optionally, type a description. d. Click Add. 5. The added allowlist IP subnet details appear in the File Services Audit section of the page.
Print the SBT Read Report

Enabling SSL/TLS for ZDLRA

Cohesity SBT supports SSL/TLS by transferring the encrypted data through secure gRPC. l Enable SSL/TLS for ZDLRA Copy Job l Enable SSL/TLS for Restore from Cohesity

Enable SSL/TLS for ZDLRA Copy Job
