2. Copy the generated certificate file to the Oracle hosts and add the -c <full path of the certificate file> when running the script cohesity_prepare_restore.sh.
For Example,
$ ./cohesity_prepare_restore.sh -I konacluster -S /opt/cohesity_ sbt/lib/libsbt_linux_x86_64.so -D OL7312C -W 10.0.0.0/1 -c /opt/cohesity_sbt/config/oracle1.cert /tmp/cohesity_sbt_20210811_150508/cohesity_catalog_sbt.OL7312C.rman is the sample RMAN script to catalog your requested backup for the database OL7312C
Non-ZDLRA Backup and Restore
Backup Oracle Database without ZDLRA
The following steps can be used to back up Oracle databases to immutable views on a Cohesity cluster.
1. Oracle DBA provides the IP addresses of the Oracle servers which are used to connect to the Cohesity cluster to the Cohesity administrator.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

2. The Cohesity administrator creates the data view and catalog view for the database to be backed up and adds the IP addresses to both the data view and catalog view for the database and provides the vips, data view name and catalog view name to the Oracle DBA.
3. Oracle DBA puts the SBT library to any directory and writes RMAN scripts with vips, data_view and catalog_view in the parameters of the RMAN channels in the following format.
SBT_PARMS=(vips=<vips of the cluster>, data_view=<data view name>, catalog_view=<catalog view name>)
or
ENV=(vips=<vips of the cluster>, data_view=<data view name>, catalog_ view=<catalog view name>)
For example
run { ALLOCATE CHANNEL c1 DEVICE TYPE sbt PARMS 'SBT_LIBRARY=/opt/cohesity_ sbt/lib/libsbt_linux_x86_64.so, SBT_PARMS=(data_ view=data,vips=10.14.53.50,catalog_view=catalog)'; ALLOCATE CHANNEL c2 DEVICE TYPE sbt PARMS 'SBT_LIBRARY=/opt/cohesity_ sbt/lib/libsbt_linux_x86_64.so, SBT_PARMS=(data_ view=data,vips=10.14.53.103,catalog_view=catalog)'; backup database; }
Note: If restoring the database to a host other than the one used for backup, the Cohesity administrator needs to whitelist the IPs of the destination host to both the catalog and data views.
For example:
./view_cli update -host test_cluster -whitelist 10.14.56.80,10.14.58.241 -view catalog
./view_cli update -host test_cluster -whitelist 10.14.56.80,10.14.58.241 -view data
Restore Oracle Database from Non-ZDLRA Backups
There are two scenarios to restore an Oracle database from the Non-ZDLRA backups. One is that the RMAN catalog is available. The other is that the RMAN catalog is not available.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

Restore Database with RMAN Catalog from Local Cluster to Alternate Host
If restoring the database to a host other than the one used for backup, the Cohesity administrator needs to add the IPs of the destination hosts to the catalog view whitelist either with the command view_cli or through Cohesity REST API. After the restore target hosts are whitelisted for the catalog view, add the parameter sbt_ allow_copy_catalog_whitelist=true to the SBT channel of the RMAN restore script. For example:
run { ALLOCATE CHANNEL c1 DEVICE TYPE sbt PARMS 'SBT_LIBRARY=/opt/cohesity_ sbt/lib/libsbt_linux_x86_64.so, SBT_PARMS=(data_view=data,catalog_vieww=catalog,vips=vmdp,sbt_allow_copy_catalog_whitelist=true)'; restore database; }
The format of the view_cli command is `view_cli update -host <cluster_name> -view <view_name> -whitelist <new_whitelists>`. For example:
./view_cli update -host test_cluster -whitelist 10.14.56.80,10.14.58.241 view catalog
The view_cli update command will overwrite the existing whitelist of the views. To keep the existing whitelist, first run the view_cli listwhitelist command to get the existing whitelist and then append the new IPs to the existing one for the update. For example:
./view_cli listWhitelist -host test_cluster -view catalog 10.0.0.1/32./view_ cli update -host test_cluster -whitelist 10.0.0.1/32,10.14.56.80,10.14.58.241 -view catalog
Restore Database Without RMAN Catalog or from Replicated Cluster or Archival
If the RMAN catalog is not available, a re-catalog is needed for the restore. The procedure is the same as the one of direct restore from Cohesity for the ZDLRA backups.
SBT Alerts on Backup and Restore Failures
Starting with Cohesity cluster version 7.3 and SBT release 20250626_0548b3bd, the cluster generates alerts for failed SBT backup and restore operations if:
l The catalog view is used, and
l The SBT requests can reach the Backup Manager service through the I/O Operation service when the error occurs.
If the SBT plug-in successfully connects to the Backup Manager service at the start of a backup or restore but later loses the connection due to a network or I/O Operation error, the Backup Manager will raise a timeout alert after the configured threshold (30 minutes by default).

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

Note: The timeout alert may not be generated if the Backup Manager service is restarted during the timeout period.

Replicate Oracle Database
Oracle application administrators can use Cohesity replication for cost-effective disaster recovery (DR). Cohesity provides a policy-based data replication solution from the core to the cloud or to the edge, from one cluster to another cluster. As part of replication, Cohesity always performs source-side compression and deduplication first, and sends only the changed data over the network.

Replicate Oracle Database
For more information about database replication, see Creating a Connection to the Remote Cluster.
Considerations
1. Overwrite restore is not supported for replication sites. 2. Failover is not supported for the Cohesity Oracle adapter. You have to perform a force
re-register of the same sources on the replication cluster and start the backup process all over again. 3. In case of a failover, after the re-registration, a full backup is required before you can perform an incremental or a log backup.
CloudArchive and CloudRetrieve for Oracle Database
Cohesity offers cost-effective, reliable data storage and protection solutions for rapidly growing environments that deploy Oracle Databases. The data in these environments can grow to terabytes and even petabytes in size.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Oracle Database

Cohesity provides a policy-based method to archive to public clouds (AWS, Azure, GCP, and Oracle Cloud), to any S3-compatible storage, to tape, and/or to any NFS mount point. Oracle application administrators can use Cohesity CloudArchive to address long-term data retention requirements and can choose to restore an entire database. The archived data is efficiently transferred and stored by sending only deduplicated, compressed incremental backups, thereby reducing network and storage utilization. Once the data is archived, Oracle application administrators can make use of Cohesity CloudRetrieve features as a cost-effective alternative for disaster recovery and georedundancy. If the cluster from which the data is archived becomes unavailable, you can retrieve your data onto a different cluster.
CloudRetrieve for Oracle Database
The CloudRetrieve approach involves the following steps:
1. Register the cloud container (where you archived the Oracle Database) with a new Cohesity cluster.
2. Provide the search parameters, such as cluster name, Protection Group name, and date range.
3. Cohesity retrieves the data that you specify onto the new Cohesity cluster, based on your search of the metadata.
For more information, see CloudRetrieve Searches.
Note: CloudArchive and CloudRetrieve are agnostic of Cohesity Oracle Adapter and Remote Adapter versions.

Oracle Database Troubleshooting
This topic provides the troubleshooting information for the Cohesity Oracle Adapter.

Oracle agent troubleshooting checklist

1. Verify the agent user (cohesityagent by default) is part of the dba and/or the oinstall groups. Use the command ID to check:

id cohesityagent uid=1002(cohesityagent) gid=1001(dba) groups=1001(dba)

2. Verify the /etc/sudoers file has the agent configured. For example:

cohesityagent

ALL=(ALL)

NOPASSWD:ALL

Defaults:cohesityagent !requiretty

Note: Use spaces and not tabs as tabs may lead to syntax errors.
3. Verify the home of the agent user is configured with the drwxr-xr-x minimum permission. For example: ls -ld /home/cohesityagent drwxr-xr-x 6 cohesityagent cohesityagent 198 Jan 17 08:58 /home/cohesityagent To change the permissions, execute the following command: chmod 755 /home/cohesityagent
4. Verify .bashrc in the home of the agent user has umask 0002. 5. Verify the agent is running:
/etc/init.d/cohesity-agent status 6. Verify with the DBA that the database to be backed up is in /etc/oratab and has the
correct ORACLE_HOME path.
Note: Ensure the third field contains Y or N.

CohesityOra:/oracle/app/oracle/product/12.2.0/dbhome_1:Y

^database^ ^ORACLE_HOME path

^

7. If database access will use OS authentication, the Cohesity agent user must have sysdba privileges on the database. If database authentication will be used, the database user also requires sysdba privileges. Verify using sqlplus commands:

SQL> column sysdba format a10 SQL> select username,sysdba from v$pwfile_users; USERNAME SYSDBA

8. Verify the Linux physical server has been registered as a source. a. Navigate to Protection > Sources. b. Click Register Source located at the top right of the page. c. Click Physical Server. d. Enter the Oracle server Host Address. e. Click Register Server.

Oracle Remote Adapter Job error "Execution of script failed with exit code: 255, error msg: Received disconnect from X.X.X.X port 22: Too many authentication failures for oracle Authenticatio n failed"

This can occur if Public Key (Password less) authenticati on between Cohesity Nodes and the Oracle server is not working.

l Access the Cohesity bash shell, as described in How to access the bash shell on a Cohesity node and run the below command to confirm password less authentication is working to the Oracle server:
ssh oracle@<oracle_host>
l If the above step prompts for password, it means that the Public Key (Password less) authentication between Cohesity Nodes and the Oracle server is not working. Perform the following to resolve the issue:
o Attempt to re-copy the RSA key from the Cohesity Job edit page to the oracle server authorized_keys file for the corresponding user.
o Check the permissions on the authorized_keys file is owned by the correct user and file permission allows the same user to read.
o Refer to the Cohesity Documentation and search for the section Add or Edit a Remote Adapter Protection Group.

Oracle Database

Issue

Cause

Workaround

Oracle protection job fails with " [kAgentError]: ORA-00312: online log 2 thread 1: ORA-19809: limit exceeded for recovery files"

This failure results from a serverside issue.

Refer to the Oracle documentation on the ORA error codes. ORA-000312: session marked for kill Cause: The session specified in an ALTER SYSTEM KILL SESSION command cannot be killed immediately (because it is rolling back or blocked on a network operation), but it has been marked for kill. This means it will be killed as soon as possible after its current uninterruptible operation is done. Action: No action is required for the session to be killed, but further executions of the ALTER SYSTEM KILL SESSION command on this session may cause the session to be killed sooner. ORA-19809: limit exceeded for recovery files Cause: The limit for recovery files specified by the db_recovery_file_dest_size was exceeded. Action: The error is accompanied by 19804. See message 19804 for further details ORA-19804: cannot reclaim string bytes disk space from string limit Cause: Oracle cannot reclaim disk space of specified bytes from the DB_RECOVERY_ FILE_DEST_SIZE limit. Action: There are five possible solutions: 1) Take frequent backup of recovery area using RMAN. 2) Consider changing RMAN retention policy. 3) Consider changing RMAN archivelog deletion policy. 4) Add disk space and increase DB_RECOVERY_FILE_DEST_SIZE. 5) Delete files from recovery area using RMAN.

CockroachDB
Cohesity natively integrates with CockroachDB to provide backup and recovery for clustered CockroachDB deployments. Using Cohesity Connector Agent, you can backup and restore the CockroachDB database. The Cohesity Connector Agent provides a simple workflow to back up and restore your CockroachDB deployment.
Cohesity provides a CockroachDB connector for backup and restore of enterprise CockroachDB deployments. The CockroachDB connector leverages the backup and restore capabilities provided by CockroachDB.
The CockroachDB connector enables you to back up and restore the following:
l Backup: l Full backup of the following with or without revision history: l Cluster l Database l Table l Incremental backup of the following with or without revision history: l Cluster l Database l Table

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

CockroachDB

l Restore: Full restore of the following: l Cluster l Database l Table
l Point In Time Restore (PITR) of the following: l Cluster l Database l Table
Core Components
The following are the core components for protecting CockroachDB databases: l CockroachDB cluster l Cohesity CockroachDB connector (DB Agent) l Cohesity Connector Agent (Physical Agent) l Cohesity S3 View
As illustrated, you can integrate Cohesity with your CockroachDB deployments using the Cohesity CockroachDB connector and Cohesity Connector Agent.

Plan and Prepare for CockroachDB Protection
Before you register your CockroachDB deployment as a source with Cohesity, and protect CockroachDB databases, ensure the following prerequisites:
l Identify the node(s) in your CockroachDB cluster with adequate resources to execute the CockroachDB connector.
l Ensure that the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of the Cohesity cluster is resolvable from all the nodes in the CockroachDB cluster.

Install the CockroachDB Connector
Before you install the CockroachDB Connector, ensure that you have sudo privileges. To install the CockroachDB connector:
1. Log on to the CockroachDB node where you have copied the CockroachDB connector RPM-based installer, cohesity-cockroachdb-connector-<version>.x86_64.rpm.
2. Run the following command to install the CockroachDB connector: sudo rpm -ivh /home/cockroach/cohesity-cockroachdb-connector<version>.x86_64.rpm --prefix <connector_install_directory>
Where <connector_install_directory> is the CockroachDB node's directory where you want to install the CockroachDB connector. If you do not define the installation directory, then by default, the connector is installed in the /opt/cohesity/cockroachdb/scripts directory.

Additional Settings End Time QoS Policy

Description
Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Maximum number of backup streams that will be created to exchange data with the cluster. By default, maximum scaling is capped at 16.

l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.

Epic Database Protection using Cohesity Physical Agents

Epic Database Protection using Cohesity Physical Agents
Epic database administrators face the challenges of prolonged backup durations, rapid data growth, escalating storage costs, and the need for enhanced flexibility and storage management tools within Epic. In addition to these challenges, today's database protection must encompass more than obtaining a clean copy; it must also include factors such as security, storage efficiency, minimizing impact on production systems, automation, and scalability. Cohesity protection for Epic provides a solution to these challenges. It simplifies database backups and restores through secure, streamlined workflows. You can protect and manage your workloads and execute available protection and recovery workflows with a few steps. The Cohesity Physical Agents provide flexible deployment options to make Epic backup and restores simple and secure. The backup and recovery of the Epic Caché database involves snapshotting the LUNs on the storage array. This method is agnostic of the OS on which Epic is hosted. Also, this method doesn't need the mount host but still requires a Proxy server to host the Epic freeze- thaw script.
Plan and Prepare for Epic Database Protection
This topic provides information on minimum permissions, prerequisites, and considerations to protect physical servers with a Cohesity cluster.
Support Matrix
Before you register your physical servers with the Cohesity cluster, ensure that Cohesity supports the physical server versions. For more information, see Supported Software.
Minimum Agent Requirements
For details on hardware and software agent requirements, see Minimum Agent Requirements.
How Cohesity Works with Epic Databases
Using the Mount host method for backing up the Epic database involves utilizing the Cohesity Linux or AIX agents on an independent mount host. The mount host has the Epic LUNs mounted to it from a previous Snap of the primary storage. Cohesity's Linux or AIX agent integrates with the mount point host to provide a file-based backup and recovery solution for Epic deployments.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Epic Database Protection using Cohesity Physical Agents

The following steps illustrate the steps that the script handles, and it can be modified to meet your requirements.
1. Script (executed by Cohesity Pre-Script option) a. Freeze Caché in production. b. Take a SAN/LUN Snapshot on primary storage. c. Unfreeze Caché. d. Present the snapshot from primary storage to the proxy host. e. Mount the File System on the proxy host.
2. Initiate a Cohesity file-based backup of the filesystem 3. Script (continues from Cohesity Pre-Script option)
a. Unmount the file system from the proxy host. b. Delete snapshot in primary storage.
Deployment Steps
Install the Cohesity Physical Agents for Linux or AIX on the mount point host you plan to use.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Epic Database Protection using Cohesity Physical Agents

Once you complete the installation of the Physical Agents on each host, you are ready to register them as a source. You must complete the following steps to configure the Epic environment for protection:
1. Register Epic Database Source 2. Mount Host Server Script Setup for Epic Database
Register Epic Database Source
Downloading and installing the Physical Agents for Linux or AIX on the mount point server allows you to register it as a source with the Cohesity cluster. The Cohesity cluster can then use a file-based Protection Group for backups. Before you install the Physical Agents, ensure the following prerequisites are met. For details, see Port Requirements and Firewall Settings. Note: Install the Cohesity Linux or AIX Physical Agents on each host that is potentially a restore target. Install the Linux or AIX Agent on Selected Hosts Cohesity recommends the RPM installer for Linux installations. For details on installing the Cohesity Physical Agents for Linux or AIX, refer to the Linux or AIX sections in Download and Install Agent for Physical Servers.
Note: The Cohesity cluster can be tuned using cluster and agent gflag values to achieve its performance. Your Cohesity team needs to determine recommended flag values based on the size of your cluster. Contact the Cohesity Account team for cluster configuration.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Epic Database Protection using Cohesity Physical Agents

Mount Host Server Script Setup for Epic Database
The mount host is used as the target location where the script mounts the newly snapped LUNs. These LUNs are then backed up by Cohesity, and it is also the location for the existing script. All Epic customers generally have the Epic freeze and thaw script that snapshots the Epic database and mounts it on a mount host. This script can also live on a script server (the most common method) or be part of Cohesity agent pre- and post-script (uncommon, but wholly supported). The examples in the following sections will show you how to incorporate your existing script into the Cohesity agent pre- and post-script options in the protection group. Your existing script must perform these major tasks:
1. Freeze the Epic database. 2. Execute a snap of the storage LUNs. 3. Unfreeze the Epic database. 4. Mount the newly snapped LUNs on the mount host.
Use the mount host method:
l If granular file folder recovery is required. l If zero impact to the production server is required.
Existing Script Location and Modification

Required System Authorities
To perform backup or restore operations on a DB2 instance, the protection user account of the DB2 instance must have one of the following levels of authority:
l SYSADM l SYSCTRL l SYSMAINT
When restoring to a new database server, either SYSADM or SYSCTRL authority is required. System authorities (SYSADM, SYSCTRL, and SYSMAINT) are determined by group membership and are defined in the database manager configuration file for a given instance:
l SYSADM Authority l Assigned to the group specified by the sysadm_group configuration parameter. l Users with SYSADM authority can also perform the functions of users with SYSCTRL and SYSMAINT authorities.
l SYSCTRL Authority l Assigned to the group specified by the sysctrl_group configuration parameter. l Users with SYSCTRL authority can also perform the functions of users with SYSMAINT authority.
l SYSMAINT Authority l Assigned to the group specified by the sysmaint_group configuration parameter.

Backup IBM DB2 Database
Cohesity Platform provides a simple workflow to back up your IBM DB2 databases. After registering the IBM DB2 as a source on the Cohesity Platform, you can start configuring your backups. Backup Process Cohesity Platform provides a DB2 Connector for backup and restore of IBM DB2 deployments. The IBM DB2 Connector leverages the native backup capabilities provided by IBM DB2. After registering the IBM DB2 source on the Cohesity Platform, you can create a Protection Group and specify the objects such as databases you want to backup. Log Backup Methods Cohesity provides the following two log backup methods:
l Dump and sweep - In this backup method: l IBM DB2 archives log files to local archive locations configured in the LOGARCHMETH1 option in the database configuration.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

IBM DB2

l The Cohesity IBM DB2 connector copies log files from the local archive location to Cohesity storage during scheduled log backup execution.
l Log files that are copied to Cohesity storage and older than "X" hours are pruned from the local archive location as a part of the scheduled log backup workflow. Where "X" is the prune hours value configured in the Protection Group.
l Log Archival to Cohesity View using Vendor Library - In this backup method, l The IBM DB2 Vendor library approach is used for log archival. l In the DB2 database configuration, the LOGARCHMETH2 option is configured to use the Cohesity DB2 vendor library to archive log files directly to Cohesity storage instead of the local archive location on DB2 nodes. l Logs from the Cohesity storage are pruned or deleted based on the retention period configured in the Protection Policy.
Considerations for Using the Log Backup Methods
Review and understand the following before you use the vendor library-based approach for direct log archival to Cohesity storage:
l The LOGARCHMETH2 option in the database configuration is used to archive logs directly to the Cohesity view.
l During the first full backup for a database, Cohesity IBM DB2 Connector performs the following: l Configures LOGARCHMETH2 and LOGARCHOPT2 to utilize the Cohesity DB2 log archival library and Cohesity storage configurations. l Deactivates the database, performs an offline backup on the database, and then activates the database to change the LOGATHMETH option. This results in database downtime, as required by IBM DB2. For more information, see https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/db2/11.5?topic=parameters-logarchmeth2secondary-log-archive-method. l The first full database backup will take extra time because of additional offline backup.
Note: If you want to use only LOGARCHMETH2 for log archival, make sure to manually turn off LOGARCHMETH1-based archival (if configured). The Cohesity IBM DB2 connector will not turn off LOGARCHMETH1-based archival.
Review and understand the following before you use LOGARCHMETH1 and LOGARCHMETH2 both on a database:
l In IBM DB2 nodes, you can configure LOGARCHMETH1 and LOGARCHMETH2 options in the database configuration to backup logs. If there is an archival failure in one of the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

IBM DB2

archive methods, IBM DB2 will continue to retry the log archival for failed files until the log files are successfully archived using both the methods. l Using both archival methods on a DB2 database will impact Cohesity log backup or archival performance.
Important: l Log Archival to Cohesity View using the vendor library backup method cannot be enabled on a registered source.
l The backup jobs added before the release of version 7.1.1 will continue to utilize dump and sweep-based log backups.
l To use the Log Archival to Cohesity View using the vendor library backup method, you must register a new source and enable the backup method during registration.
Offline Backup Best Practices
If you want to periodically perform an online and offline backup on the same database, then the following is the best practice workflow:
1. Create a Protection Group for online backup, for example, DB1_online_backup. 2. Create a different Protection Group for offline backup, for example, DB1_offline_
backup. 3. Always keep the Protection Group, DB1_offline_backup, in the Paused state. 4. Run the Protection Group, DB1_offline_backup, as per the defined schedule in the
protection policy. 5. When you want to perform an offline backup, pause the Protection Group for online
backup, DB1_online_backup, and wait for the current protection run to finish before triggering the offline backup. 6. Perform the offline backup using the RunNow option, and bring the database online. 7. Unpause the Protection Group for online backup, DB1_online_backup.

Description
Enable Pause Future Run only if you do not want to schedule future runs of the Protection Group.
Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Maximum number of backup streams that will be created to exchange data with the cluster. By default, maximum scaling is capped at 16.

A Protection Policy can be attached to multiple Protection Groups, and any changes in the policy settings impact all the Protection Groups that are associated with the Protection Policy. You can create and attach a new Protection Policy with the required policy settings to your Protection Group. The new policy is applied to the Protection Group from the next scheduled protection run.
To attach a new Protection Policy to the Protection Group:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Protection.
2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for IBM DB2.

3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit.

4. On the Edit Protection page, click on the Objects section.
5. In the Policy drop-down list, select the new Protection Policy for the Protection Group.
6. Click Save.

Pause Future Protection Runs

You can pause future protection runs of the Protection Group from executing. However, if the Protection Group is currently executing a protection run, the current run continues to execute and only future runs of the Protection Group are paused.
To pause future protection run:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for IBM
DB2.

3. Click the actions menu ( Runs.

) next to the Protection Group and select Pause Future

Resume Paused Protection Runs

You can resume a paused protection run. When you resume a protection run, if the backup snapshots are expired, then a full backup is triggered. To resume a paused protection run:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had paused.

3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Resume.

c. Click Select Recovery Point and then go to step 5.

a. Select the List tab from the top-right corner of the Edit recovery point for <database_name> page.

b. You can also select a recovery point from a different date range by selecting the date range from the Date drop-down list. The page displays the available recovery points in the specified range.

MySQL EE
Cohesity natively integrates with MySQL to provide backup and recovery for MySQL deployments. Using Cohesity Connector Agent, you can backup and restore the MySQL database. The Cohesity Connector Agent provides a simple workflow to back up and restore your MySQL deployment. The MySQL Connector enables you to back up and restore the following:
l Full and incremental backup of a MySQL database. l Physical level restore (No option to restore on a per-database level).
Core Components
The following are the core components for protecting MySQL databases:
l MySQL Linux machine l MySQL Connector l Cohesity Connector Agent l Cohesity View
As illustrated, you can integrate Cohesity with your MySQL deployments using the MySQL Connector and Cohesity Connector Agent.

Before you register your MySQL deployment as a source with Cohesity and protect MySQL instances, ensure the following prerequisites:

Backup MySQL Database
Cohesity provides a simple workflow to back up your MySQL databases. After registering MySQL as a source on Cohesity, you can start configuring your backups. Backup Process Cohesity provides a MySQL EE connector for backup and restores of enterprise MySQL deployments. The MySQL EE connector leverages the backup capabilities provided by MySQL. After registering the MySQL source on Cohesity, you can create a Protection Group and specify the MySQL instances that you want to back up. In the Protection Group, you need to define the script parameters that enable you to provide additional parameters required by the backup statements provided by MySQL.
Note: Cohesity recommends that you configure periodic full backups.
Backup Parameters In the Protection Group, you can define the following parameters for your MySQL backup configuration: (parameters are to be passed comma(,) separated)

Backup Parameters

Description

number-ofbuffers

Optional.
Specify the number of buffers to use during multithreaded operations.
you can use a high number of buffers for CPU-intensive processing such as backup, particularly when using compression, and use a low number of buffers for disk-intensive processing such as restoring a backup. This value should be at least as high as the number of read threads or write threads, depending on the type of operation.
For more information, see MySQL Enterprise Backup 8.0 User's Guide :: 20.10 Performance / Scalability / Capacity Options.

read-thread

Optional. Specify the number of threads to use for reading data from the disk. For more information, see MySQL Enterprise Backup 8.0 User's Guide :: 20.10 Performance / Scalability / Capacity Options.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

MySQL EE

Backup Parameters processthreads
writethreads
limitmemory

Description
Optional. Specify the number of threads to use for processing data. This includes compression and uncompression, encryption and decryption, apply-log operations, and packing and extracting backup images. For more information, see MySQL Enterprise Backup 8.0 User's Guide :: 20.10 Performance / Scalability / Capacity Options.
Optional. Specify the number of threads to use for writing data to disk. For more information, see MySQL Enterprise Backup 8.0 User's Guide :: 20.10 Performance / Scalability / Capacity Options.
Optional. Specify maximum memory in megabytes that can be used by mysqlbackup.
Note: Do not include any suffixes such as MB or KB in the option value.
For more information, see MySQL Enterprise Backup 8.0 User's Guide :: 20.10 Performance / Scalability / Capacity Options.

Example
number-of-buffers=10, read-threads=5, process-threads=5, write-threads=5, limit-memory=500

Additional Settings

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

MySQL EE

Additional Settings

Description

Pause Future Run

Enable Pause Future Run only if you do not want to schedule future runs of the Protection Group.

End Time

Optional.
Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A Protection Group run that starts before this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Alerts

Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Create an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Create a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Description

Description

l High-priority protection groups l Medium-priority protection groups l Low-priority protection groups.
The service-level agreement (SLA) defines how long the administrator expects a Protection Group run to take.

Considerations
Review and understand the following before you protect your Percona MySQL database.
l Only RHEL is supported. l Database instance auto-discovery and object search are not supported. l You cannot protect multiple hosts using a single Protection Group. l Multiple object restore is not supported. l MySQL Connector upgrade is not supported. To use the latest version of the MySQL
Connector, uninstall the existing MySQL Connector and install the latest version. l Only instance-level backup and restore are supported. Granular-level use cases such
as database-level backup and restore are not supported. l Log backups and PITR recovery are supported. l Recovery is performed only at the instance level; hence, you cannot rename the
database after recovery. l Only backup and restore of a single Percona MySQL database on the source machine
is supported. If the source machine has multiple database instances, you cannot backup and restore the database. l Recovery from a replication copy of the database is not supported.

Backup Percona MySQL Database
Cohesity provides a simple workflow to back up your Percona MySQL deployment. After registering the Percona MySQL as a source on Cohesity, you can start configuring your backups.
Backup Process
Cohesity provides a MySQL connector to protect Percona MySQL deployments. The MySQL Connector uses the XtraBackup FIFO data sink method from Percona to stream data efficiently during backup. When a protection job runs, multiple parallel threads write database data into a set of FIFO (First-In-First-Out) pipes on the source system. These FIFO pipes act as streaming interfaces. The Cohesity cluster then reads the data from the pipes and transfers it directly to the Cohesity cluster for protection.
Backup Scope
l Backups are supported at the instance level. l If the instance contains multiple databases, all databases are included in a single
backup workflow. l Selective database-level backups are not supported.
Backup Types Supported
Cohesity supports the following types of backups:
l Full Backup Captures a complete copy of the entire MySQL instance, including all databases, tables, indexes, tablespaces, and logs.
l Incremental Backup

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

Percona MySQL on Linux

Captures only the changes made since the last successful full or incremental backup on the Cohesity cluster. XtraBackup performs incremental backups based on the last redo log position of the previous backup. l Log Backup Captures the binary logs (binlogs), which contain all database changes (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) with associated timestamps. Log backups enable point-in-time recovery by replaying changes after a full or incremental backup.
Backup Parameters
In the Protection Group, you can define the following parameters for your Percona MySQL backup configuration: (parameters are to be passed space (" ") separated)
Note: The backup parameters are not applicable for log backups.

Backup Parameters

Mandatory?

--fifo-streams

No

--parallel-threads No

Description Number of FIFO streams used for backup. Default: 6. Number of parallel threads writing to the FIFO streams. Default: 18.

Example
--fifo-streams=8 --parallel-threads=24

Additional Settings QoS Policy
Alerts
Priority

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Create an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Create a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.
Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity supports concurrent backups. However, if the number of protection groups exceeds the ability to process protection groups, this will be the priority of implementation of the protection groups:
l High-priority protection groups l Medium-priority protection groups l Low-priority protection groups.

Recover Percona MySQL Database
You can restore the protected Percona MySQL data to the same Percona MySQL deployment or to a different Percona MySQL deployment. Recovery Process Cohesity Platform supports instance-level recovery for Percona MySQL using the MySQL connector. If multiple databases were included in the backup, all databases are restored together within the same recovery workflow. Recovery Options Cohesity provides the following restore options:
l Full or Incremental Image Restore Restores the database instance using a full backup or a combination of full and incremental backups. Recovery is performed to the state captured in the selected backup image(s).
l Point-in-Time Restore (PITR) Restores the database instance to an exact point in time defined by the user. PITR combines full backups, incremental backups, and binary logs (binlogs) to replay changes up to the requested timestamp, providing granular recovery.

Considerations
Review and understand the following before you protect your SAP HANA database:
l SAP HANA 1.0 is not supported. l Source-side deduplication is not supported for SAP HANA on PowerPC platform. l You cannot protect multiple hosts using a single Protection Group. l You cannot restore multiple objects, search and recover an object. l Scheduling log backups in the Cohesity cluster is not supported, as SAP HANA
automatically performs log backups. l Cohesity supports backup and restore of SAP HANA(x86) databases running on dual-
stack (IPv4 and IPv6) mode or single-stack (only IPv6) mode. l Cohesity supports the recovery of SAP HANA 2.0 backups across both Intel x86-64
and Power PC platforms, allowing you to restore your critical SAP HANA data regardless of the underlying hardware architecture. l Restoring backups from a higher version of SAP HANA to a lower version is not supported. l Cohesity supports SAP HANA scale-out deployments that use independent disks for each node. l Only Pacemaker-based cluster stacks provided by RHEL and SLES are supported for SAP HANA HA cluster data protection.
Note: The Pacemaker version 0.9.167 is supported.
l It is mandatory to connect to the Cohesity cluster securely using secure gRPC when writing or reading data. From 7.2.2 version onwards, it is mandatory to connect to the Cohesity cluster securely using secure gRPC when writing or reading data.
l For a secure connection between the Cohesity cluster and the SAP HANA database, you need to generate an SAP HANA certificate for authentication. For a secure connection between the Cohesity cluster and the SAP HANA database, Cohesity cluster certificate is required for authentication. The certificate is autogenerated only after you run the first database UDA protection job. Post running the job, certificate is auto-created. The SAP HANA log backup may fail until the first protection job is running.
Note: The certificate is not created during source registration.
l Cohesity supports native SAP HANA backup encryption. When encryption is enabled, backup data is encrypted and transferred to the Cohesity cluster for backups created

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP HANA

using the Cohesity SAP HANA Connector Agent. l Supported encryption methods include: l SAP HANA Backup Encryption l System PKI SSFS (for internal communication encryption) l Data and Log Volume Encryption
Supported secure stores: l SSFS (Secure Store and File System) l LSS (Local Secure Store)
Create the Secure User Store (hdbuserstore) Key
Create the SAP HANA hdbuserstore key to connect to SYSTEMDB. For detailed instructions, see Secure User Store (hdbuserstore). Use the following command to create the hdbuserstore key:
hdbuserstore SET <KEY> <host:port> <USERNAME> <PASSWORD>
Note: Ensure that the user account of the secure user store has the following administrator privileges: - BACKUP ADMIN - DATABASE ADMIN - DATABASE START - CATALOG READ - MONITORING
Sample:
hdbuserstore SET SYS_KEY test-FI:30013 SYSTEM testpassword
After you have created the hdbuserstore key, verify if the key has the required SAP HANA connection information, such as hostname or login credentials. Verify the key using the following command:
tecadm@test-FI:/usr/sap/TEC/home> hdbsql -AU SYS_KEY "select DATABASE_NAME,ACTIVE_STATUS from m_databases" | DATABASE | ACT | | -------- | --- | | SYSTEMDB | YES | | TEC | YES | | SRC | YES | | DST | YES | 4 rows selected (overall time 28.150 msec; server time 659 usec) tecadm@test-FI:/usr/sap/TEC/home>

Backup SAP HANA Database
Cohesity provides a simple workflow to back up your SAP HANA databases. After registering the SAP HANA as a source on Cohesity, you can start configuring your backups. Backup Process Cohesity provides a SAP HANA database agent for the backup and restore of enterprise SAP HANA deployments. The SAP HANA database agent leverages the backup capabilities provided by SAP HANA. After registering the SAP HANA source on Cohesity, you can create a Protection Group and specify the objects such as databases and tables that you want to backup. In the Protection Group, you need to define the parameters that enable you to provide additional parameters required by the backup statements provided by SAP HANA.

Log Backups SAP HANA automatically triggers log backups, you can view these log backups on the Cohesity cluster and perform the following:

backup replication. For more information, see Enable Log Backups Replication. 2. While registering or updating the SAP HANA source to the Cohesity cluster, set the -
et-log-backup source registration parameter to true. For more information, see Register SAP HANA as a Source. 3. Create a new Protection Group and select a Protection Policy with log backups job in the Protection Group for SAP HANA backups. For more information, see Protect SAP HANA Deployments.
Note: l To replicate jobs, select the replication option, while creating the Protection Group. l In the source, after setting the source parameter -et-log-backup to true, the log backups will not be displayed on the Cohesity UI or be replicated for older Protection Groups. You must create a new Protection Group with the updated source.
4. Create a Full Backup for the first time. Replication to the secondary Cohesity cluster will be enabled after the first successful full backup, and log backups will be displayed on the Cohesity UI.
Note: Catalog backups are not displayed on the Cohesity UI.

provided by SAP HANA. For more information, see Backup Parameters.

A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see About Policies and Protection Groups.

Additional Settings QoS Policy
Concurrency

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
The maximum number of restore streams that is created to exchange data with the cluster. By default, maximum scaling is set to empty.
Note: The same value is set to the parallel_data_backup_backint_channels parameter in the global.ini file for the protected database. Also, the same value is set for the max_restore_streams parameter in the SAP HANA parameter file of the database selected for protection.

Alerts

Optional.
Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created. For more information, see Alerts.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Cancel a Recovery Run
When you cancel a recovery run, the recovery process is terminated. If the recovery run is canceled during an ongoing restore operation, the SAP HANA database may enter an offline or inconsistent state. To bring the SAP HANA database back online, you must initiate a new recovery run. To cancel a recovery run:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Recoveries.
2. Click the action icon ( ) next to the recovery run and click Cancel Run. 3. In the Cancel Recovery dialog box, select any one of the following:
l Continue Recovery. if you want to continue to recovery run l Cancel Recovery. if you want to cancel the recovery run.

SAP HANA Certificate Authentication
The SAP HANA Certification provides the necessary authentication and also verifies whether the SAP HANA database, which performs backups to the Cohesity cluster, is a trusted entity. This certification provides the capability to set verification which allows only trusted sources to write to the Cohesity cluster through the SpanFS.
Create an SAP HANA Authentication Certificate
This section lists the steps for creating an SAP HANA authentication certificate.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP HANA

1. Start the Cohesity CLI locally and log in to the Cohesity cluster using the ssh command with the support user account and specify the IP address. For more information, see Using the Cohesity CLI and List of Cohesity CLI Commands. ssh support@198.51.100.12
2. If prompted, enter the password. [support@198.51.100.12's password:
The cohesity_shell prompt is displayed. 3. Log in to the CLI:
cohesity shell# iris_cli

admin@198.51.100.12> help

Deploy an SAP HANA Certificate in a Multi-node Setup
This section lists the steps to deploy an SAP HANA authentication certificate in a multi-node SAP HANA setup.
1. Generate and deploy the SAP HANA authentication certificate to any one of the nodes in a multi-node SAP HANA system using the instructions provided in the previous section.
2. Use SCP to securely transfer the certificate to a target location on all the remaining (N-1) nodes.
scp <certificate_config_path> ip_address:<certificate_config_path>
Example
scp /usr/sap/ORC/home/install/cert.cfg 10.2.146.72: /usr/sap/ORC/home/install/cert.cfg
3. Change the cluster_port parameter value to 11117 and update the certificate_ config_path parameter value to the correct path of the certificate in the respective paramfile of each of the N nodes.

Considerations
Review and understand the following before you protect your SAP Sybase IQ database:
l You can back up only one database per Protection Group. l Currently only online backup of databases is supported. l The same database should not be part of multiple Protection Groups. l Log backups are not supported. l SAP Sybase IQ does not support Point in time recovery (PITR) from backups taken
using a third-party dynamic link library (DLL). l In the case of multiplex database restore, data is restored to only one node
(coordinator). You need to set the multiplex roles and start the multiplex database manually. l Cohesity supports backup and restore of SAP Sybase IQ databases running on dualstack (IPv4 and IPv6) mode or single-stack (only IPv6) mode.
Prerequisites
l For backups, the database server must be up and running. l For Kerberos authentication, the keytab file must be available on all nodes at the
given location and accessible by the user used to run the Cohesity Linux Agent. l SSL certificates must be used for connecting to the database servers. The SSL
certificates must be available in the same path on all servers and accessible by the user used to run the Cohesity Linux Agent.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP Sybase IQ

l To securely connect to the Cohesity cluster while reading or writing data, you can use secure gRPC.
Note: l From 7.2.2 version onwards, it is mandatory to connect to the Cohesity cluster securely using secure gRPC when writing or reading data. l Using non-secure gRPC for data transfer between Cohesity and database hosts will result in unsecured communication. l Enabling secure gRPC will increase data transfer time between Cohesity and database hosts compared to non-secure communication.
To use secure gRPC, perform the following: 1. Copy /home/cohesity/<clustername>.cfg from the Cohesity node to all your SAP Sybase IQ nodes at the same location. For example, /opt/certs/<clustername>.cfg.
Note: Ensure that the root or non-root user used to install the Cohesity Linux agent and your SAP Sybase IQ Connector has read access to the generated certificate config file.
3. While registering the your SAP Sybase IQ source, provide the following as a part of Source Registration Options: --certificate-config-path=opt/certs/<clustername>.cfg

Download and Install the SAP Sybase IQ Connector Installer
Cohesity Platform provides an SAP Sybase IQ connector for the backup and restore of SAP Sybase IQ deployments. Sybase IQ supports backup and restore operations with third-party products using a dynamic link library loaded at run time(.dll or .so).
Download the SAP Sybase IQ Connector
Cohesity Platform provides a SAP Sybase IQ Connector to backup and restore SAP Sybase IQ databases. The SAP Sybase IQ Connector is available as a datasource agent on the Cohesity Download portal. Log on to the Cohesity Download portal, download the respective datasource agent for SAP Sybase IQ Connector, and copy the datasource agent to the SAP Sybase IQ host.
Install the SAP Sybase IQ Connector
Before you install the SAP Sybase IQ Connector, ensure that you have sudo privileges. To install the SAP Sybase IQ connector:
1. Log on to the SAP Sybase IQ node where you have copied the SAP Sybase IQ connector RPM-based installer, cohesity-sybaseiq-connector-<version>.x86_ 64.rpm.
2. Run the following command to install the SAP Sybase IQ connector:
sudo sh -c 'export SYBASEIQ_ENV_PATH=/path/to/SAP Sybase IQ/IQ-16_0/IQ16_0.sh ; yum localinstall /home/cohesity/cohesity-sybaseiq-connector<version>.x86_64.rpm'
Where /path/to/SAP Sybase IQ/ is the directory where the SAP Sybase IQ connector is installed.
Note: If you do not explicitly specify the details, the hostname is applied as the value for control nodes and source name. Also, a unique hash value is applied for the source UUID.
Upgrade the SAP Sybase IQ Connector
To upgrade the SAP Sybase IQ Connector, run the following command with appropriate parameters on SAP Sybase IQ node's CLI:
$ sudo sh -c 'export SYBASEIQ_ENV_PATH=/opt/sybase/iq16/IQ-16_1/IQ-16_1.sh ; yum update cohesity-sybaseiq-connector-<version>-1.x86_64.rpm'
Uninstall the SAP Sybase IQ Connector
To uninstall the SAP Sybase IQ Connector, run the following command with appropriate parameters on SAP Sybase IQ node's CLI: Using yum:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP Sybase IQ

sudo yum remove cohesity-sybaseiq-connector-<version>.x86_64
Using rpm: sudo rpm -e cohesity-sybaseiq-connector-<version>.x86_64.rpm

Protect SAP Sybase IQ Deployments
In Cohesity, SAP Sybase IQ deployments are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group enables you to:
l Specify the objects such as databases and tables that you want to backup. l Based on your requirement, define the parameters for the backup statements
provided by SAP Sybase IQ. For more information, see Backup Parameters.
The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see About Policies and Protection Groups. To protect SAP Sybase IQ deployments:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, do one of the following: l Select Data Protection > Protection. Click Protect on the top-right of the page and then select Universal Data Adapter.

l Select Data Protection > Sources. Click the actions menu ( Sybase IQ and then select Protect.

4. In the Protection Group section, do one of the following: l Select New Group to create a new Protection Group. Additional Settings

Additional Settings Pause Future Run End Time QoS Policy
Concurrency

Description
Enable Pause Future Run only if you do not want to schedule future runs of the Protection Group.
Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Maximum number of backup streams that will be created to exchange data with the cluster. By default, maximum scaling is capped at 16.

Priority
SLA
Description

Description
Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created. For more information, see Alerts.

a. High-priority protection runs b. Medium-priority protection runs c. Low-priority protection runs
The service-level agreement (SLA) defines how long the administrator expects a Protection Group run to take.
l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental backup Protection Group run takes to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last run.
l Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup Protection Group run takes to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).
Optional. Enter a brief description about the Protection Group.

Attach New Protection Policy to the Protection Group
A Protection Policy can be attached to multiple Protection Groups, and any changes in the policy settings impact all the Protection Groups that are associated with the Protection Policy. You can create and attach a new Protection Policy with the required policy settings to your Protection Group. The new policy is applied to the Protection Group from the next scheduled protection run.
To attach a new Protection Policy to the Protection Group:

You can pause future protection runs of the Protection Group from executing. However, if the Protection Group is currently executing a protection run, the current run continues to execute and only future runs of the Protection Group are paused.

SAP MaxDB on Linux
Cohesity natively integrates with SAP MaxDB to provide backup and recovery for clustered SAP MaxDB deployments. Using Cohesity Connector Agent, you can backup and restore the SAP MaxDB database. Cohesity provides a Cohesity BACKINT plug-in for the backup and restore of enterprise SAP MaxDB deployments. The Cohesity BACKINT plug-in leverages the backup and restore capabilities provided by SAP MaxDB. The Cohesity BACKINT plug-in enables you to back up and restore both TenantDB and SystemDB. It provides:
l Backup: l Full backup l Incremental backup l Scheduled Log backup
l Restore: l Restore the database to the point in time. l Restore the database to a specific data backup.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

SAP MaxDB on Linux

l Alternate restore of SAP MaxDB database: l Alternate restore to a new database or active database on the same SAP MaxDB system. l Alternate restore to a new or active database on a different SAP MaxDB system.

l A database user with database admin user privileges. l Download and install the Cohesity Linux Agent on the SAP MaxDB Linux machine. l Download and install the SAP MaxDB Connector agent. l Create a XUSER key. l Create a backup template. Considerations
Review and understand the following before you protect your SAP MaxDB database:
l SAP MaxDB with liveCache technology is not supported. l NFS datapath is not supported. l Only PIPE backups are supported. File backups are not supported, and hence only
scheduled log backups are supported, and automatic log backups are not supported. l In a protection run, you cannot back up multiple objects. l Only the single-node MAXDB database system is supported. l Canceling restore operations is not supported. l For alternate restore, the target SAP MaxDB database must be created before starting
the restore operation. l For alternate restore to a different SAP MaxDB host, the path specified in
IndepDataPath must be the same. l Cohesity replication is supported.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP MaxDB on Linux

l After a successful database restore, Cohesity recommends to trigger a full backup to ensure that incremental and log backups do not fail. For more information, see Data backup missing (backup history lost).
l If the database system administration (SUPERDBA) password is different in both the source and the target SAP MaxDB hosts, then when you perform an alternate restore of a specific data backup to the target SAP MaxDB host, the recovery run completes with the following errors:
-24907,ERR_DBAWRONG: Wrong database system administrator -24988,ERR_SQL: SQL error -4008,Unknown user name/password combination
To avoid the issue in the future, you must change the database system administrator password on the target SAP MaxDB host before the system copy to be consistent with the source SAP MaxDB host's password. Once the system copy completes, you can change the password.
l Ensure that the SAP MaxDB database versions in both the source and target systems are compatible.
l Cohesity supports backup and restore of SAP MaxDB databases running on dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) mode or single-stack (only IPv6) mode.
l It is mandatory to connect to the Cohesity cluster securely using secure gRPC when writing or reading data.

SAP MaxDB on Linux

Register and Manage the SAP MaxDB on Linux Source
To protect your SAP MaxDB databases, you need to register your SAP MaxDB deployment as a source on Cohesity. After registering your SAP MaxDB deployment as a source, you can:
l Update the username and password of the database user. l Refresh the source details. l Unregister the SAP MaxDB source from Cohesity. Register SAP MaxDB as a Source Before you register SAP MaxDB as a source, ensure that you: l Review the requirements and limitations. l Perform the prerequisite tasks. For more information, see Plan and Prepare for SAP MaxDB on Linux Protection. To register SAP MaxDB as a source: 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click Register on the top-right of the page and then select Universal Data
Adapter. 3. In the Register Universal Data Adapter page, perform the following:
a. From the Source Type drop-down menu, select SAP MaxDB. b. From the Host OS Type drop-down menu, select Linux. c. In the Hostname/IP Addresses field, enter the hostname or IP address of
the node(s) you have identified to run the Cohesity SAP MaxDB connector. For more information, see Plan and Prepare for SAP MaxDB on Linux Protection.
Note: Cohesity supports the backup and restore of SAP MaxDB databases running on dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) mode or single-stack (only IPv6) mode.
d. In the Datasource Agent Installation Path field, enter the directory path on the SAP MaxDB node, where you have installed the Cohesity SAP MaxDB connector. For more information, see Install the SAP MaxDB Connector.
e. Ignore the In the APP Authentication section. It is not applicable for SAP MaxDB source registration.
f. Enable Custom Options, perform the following:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP MaxDB on Linux

i. Ignore the Mounts View option. It is not applicable for SAP MaxDB source registration.
ii. Ignore the Source Registration Options field. g. Click Register. Update the SAP MaxDB Source Configuration After registering your SAP MaxDB as a source on Cohesity, you can: l Update the username and password of the database user. l Modify the Source Registration Options based on your requirements. l Update the Datasource Agent Installation Path only if you have uninstalled and reinstalled the Cohesity SAP MaxDB connector in a different directory on the SAP MaxDB node. To update the SAP MaxDB source configuration: 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources.
2. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the SAP MaxDB source and select Edit. 3. On the Update Universal Data Adapter page, update the required configurations. 4. Click Update. Refresh the SAP MaxDB Source Configuration You can refresh the SAP MaxDB Source and re-verify the source with the available source registration parameters. To refresh the SAP MaxDB Source Configuration: 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources.
2. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the SAP MaxDB Source and select Refresh. Unregister the SAP MaxDB Source If you plan to stop taking the backup of your SAP MaxDB databases, you can unregister the SAP MaxDB source from the Cohesity. To unregister the SAP MaxDB source:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources.
2. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the SAP MaxDB source and select Unregister.
Backup SAP MaxDB on Linux Database
Cohesity provides a simple workflow to back up your SAP MaxDB databases. After registering the SAP MaxDB as a source on Cohesity, you can start configuring your backups.

SAP MaxDB on Linux

Backup Process Cohesity provides a SAP MaxDB connector for backup and restore of enterprise SAP MaxDB deployments. The SAP MaxDB connector leverages the backup capabilities provided by SAP MaxDB. After registering the SAP MaxDB source on Cohesity, you can create a Protection Group and specify the objects such as databases and tables that you want to backup. In the Protection Group, you need to define the parameters that enable you to provide additional parameters required by the backup statements provided by SAP MaxDB.
Note: Cohesity recommends that you configure periodic full backups.
Backup Parameters In the Protection Group, you can define the following parameters for your SAP MaxDB backup configuration:

Backup Parameters --xuser-key=<key>
--backup-template
--use-securegrpc=<true/false>

Mandatory? Optional Mandatory
Optional

Description
By default, SAP MaxDB uses the XUSER key provided during the SAP MaxDB connector installation. You can override the XUSER key using the parameter based on your requirements. For example: --xuser-key=XUSER_KEY
Specify the backup template that you have created for the backup. Ensure that you create specific backup templates for COMPLETE DATA, INCREMENTAL DATA, AND LOG DATA. For detailed instructions to create a backup template, see backup_ template_create on SAP documentation. For example: --backup-template=BACKData
Set the parameter to true, if you want to use secure gRPC communication during backup. For example: --use-secure-grpc=true
Note: It is mandatory to connect to the Cohesity cluster securely using secure gRPC when writing or reading data.

--sap-certificatepath=<cert_file_ path>

Mandatory? Optional

Description
Specify the path of the self-signed certificate if you want to use it for secure gRPC communication during backups. For example: --sap-certificate-path=/tmp/certs/sap_ cert1837348343.cfg Use the following command to generate the certificate: ~/<release-version>/crux/bin/client_tls_cert_ generator_exec -cert_name <clustername> -output_ file /home/cohesity/<clustername>.cfg

Protect SAP MaxDB on Linux Deployments
SAP MaxDB deployments are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group enables you to:
l Specify the objects such as databases and tables that you want to backup. l Based on your requirement, define the parameters for the backup statements
provided by SAP MaxDB. For more information, see Backup Parameters.
The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see About Policies and Protection Groups. To protect SAP MaxDB deployments:
1. Do one of the following: l Select Data Protection > Protection. Click Protect on the top-right of the page and then select Universal Data Adapter.

l Select Data Protection > Sources. Click the actions menu ( SAP MaxDB source and then select Protect.

) next to the

2. From the Source drop-down list, select the registered SAP MaxDB source or click Register Source to register a SAP MaxDB source. For more information, see Register SAP MaxDB as a Source.

3. In the Objects section, add the object that you plan to protect. The object should be a database name. To back up a database, enter the name of the database. For example, H00. Then, click Save Selection.

4. In the Protection Group section, do one of the following:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP MaxDB on Linux

l Select New Group to create a new Protection Group. In the Protection Name field, enter a name from the Protection Group.
l Select Existing Group to use the settings of an existing Protection Group. From the Group list, select an existing Protection Group and click Protect.
5. From the Policy drop-down list, select an existing Protection Policy or create a new Protection Policy.
6. In the Settings section, do the following:
1. Select the appropriate Storage Domain. For more information, see Manage Storage Domains.
2. In the Start Time field, define when the protection run should start. This option is only available if the selected policy is set to Backup Daily. Enter the hour and minutes, or use the up and down arrows on your keyboard.
Verify the AM or PM setting. The default time zone is the browser's time zone. You can change the time zone of the protection run by selecting a different time zone.
3. In the Backup Script Arguments section, enter the Backup Parameters in the Full Backup, Incremental Backup, and Log Backup fields based on your requirements.
For example:

Additional Settings QoS Policy
Concurrency Alerts
Priority

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Not applicable for SAP MaxDB data protection.
Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created. For more information, see Alerts.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.
Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity supports concurrent backups. However, if the number of protection runs exceeds the ability to process runs, this will be the priority of implementation of the protection runs:
a. High-priority protection runs b. Medium-priority protection runs c. Low-priority protection runs

Additional Settings SLA
Description

Description
The service-level agreement (SLA) defines how long the administrator expects a Protection Group run to take.
l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental backup Protection Group run takes to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last run.
l Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup Protection Group run takes to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).
Optional. Enter a brief description about the Protection Group.

Manage the SAP MaxDB on Linux Backup Configuration
A backup configuration includes a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. You can modify the existing Protection Group and the Protection Policy based on your requirements.
Attach New Protection Policy to the Protection Group
A Protection Policy can be attached to multiple Protection Groups, and any changes in the policy settings impact all the Protection Groups that are associated with the Protection Policy. You can create and attach a new Protection Policy with the required policy settings to your Protection Group. The new policy is applied to the Protection Group from the next scheduled protection run. To attach a new Protection Policy to the Protection Group:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for SAP
MaxDB.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit.
4. On the Edit Protection page, click in the Objects section. 5. In the Policy drop-down list, select the new Protection Policy for the Protection
Group. 6. Click Save.
Pause Future Protection Runs
You can pause future protection runs of the Protection Group from executing. However, if the Protection Group is currently executing a protection run, the current run continues to execute and only future runs of the Protection Group are paused.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

To pause future protection run:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for SAP
MaxDB.
