) next to the Protection Group and select Pause Future

Resume Paused Protection Runs

You can resume a paused protection run. When you resume a protection run, if the backup snapshots are expired, then a full backup is triggered. To resume a paused protection run:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had paused.

3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Resume.

Cancel Protection Run

To cancel a recovery run: 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection.

2. Click the action icon ( ) next to the protection run and click Cancel Run.

Delete the Protection Group

You can delete a Protection Group if you:
l Do not want to retain the backups and the local and archived snapshots that are generated by the Protection Group.
l Want to reclaim the storage space utilized by the Protection Group.
Cohesity provides the following ways to delete a Protection Group:
l Delete Protection Group Only: Allows you to delete the Protection Group. All the backups generated by the Protection Group are preserved till the snapshots expire.
l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots: Allows you to delete the Protection Group and all the local and archived Snapshots generated by the Protection Group.

Note: After deleting the Protection Group, the reclaimed storage space details are not displayed immediately. It will take some time to reflect on the Cohesity.

To delete the Protection Group:

MaxDB.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Delete. 4. In the Delete Protection Group? dialog box, select any one of the following
options: l Delete Protection Group Only l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots

Recover SAP MaxDB on Linux Database
You can restore the SAP MaxDB object(s) such as databases in SAP MaxDB. You can restore to the same SAP MaxDB cluster or a different SAP MaxDB cluster.
The SAP MaxDB connector leverages the restore statements provided by SAP MaxDB. You can create a Recovery configuration and specify the objects such as databases backed up using the Protection Group.
In the Recovery configuration, you need to specify the object you plan to restore and define the parameters required by the restore statements provided by SAP MaxDB.

In the Object field, enter the name of the database or table that you had backed up using the selected Protection Group. By default, the latest snapshot is selected for recovery. l For point-in-time snapshots, in the Edit recovery point for <Protection_ Group_Name> dialog, click the Timeline tab, choose the Date and select the point-in-time from the timeline slider and click Select Recovery Point.

6. Click Next: Recover Options.

Alternate Restore to SAP MaxDB Host with Different SIDs
You can perform an alternate restore to SAP MaxDB hosts with different SIDs.
Prerequisites
Ensure that you configure the source and target SAP MaxDB host's Cohesity BACKINT parameter files (/opt/cohesity/maxdb_java_plugin/profile/init<SID>.utl) with the same Cohesity cluster and Cohesity View details. To perform an alternate restore to SAP MaxDB host with different SIDs:
1. Using the Command-Line Interface (CLI) or SAP MaxDB Studio, take backups on the source SAP MaxDB host.
2. Copy the recover catalog files from the source SAP MaxDB host to a temporary directory (/tmp/logs) on the target SAP MaxDB host. You can locate the recover catalog files using the param_directget command. For example:
>dbmcli - u <username>,<password> -d <DBname> param_directget RunDirectoryPath

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP MaxDB on Linux

3. On the target SAP MaxDB host, update the temporary directory path in the ORIGINAL_ RUNDIRECTORY parameter in the /opt/cohesity/maxdb_java_ plugin/profile/bsi.env file.
For example:

bash-4.2$ cat /opt/cohesity/maxdb_java_plugin/profile/bsi.env BACKINT /opt/cohesity/maxdb_java_plugin/bin/backint.sh INPUT /opt/cohesity/maxdb_java_plugin/workflow/input OUTPUT /opt/cohesity/maxdb_java_plugin/workflow/output ERROROUTPUT /opt/cohesity/maxdb_java_plugin/workflow/error PARAMETERFILE /opt/cohesity/maxdb_java_plugin/profile/initSID.utl TIMEOUT_SUCCESS 600 TIMEOUT_FAILURE 300 CHECK_AVAILABILITY YES ORIGINAL_RUNDIRECTORY /tmp/logs

4. Restore to the target SAP MaxDB host using the restore commands. Sample for full database backup:

>db_activate recover BACKData DATA Externalbackupid "MAXDB 1630306452_ v48g /tmp/maxdb/pipe_data" OK Returncode 0 ... ...

Sample for incremental backup:

>recover_start BACKPages PAGES EBID "MAXDB 1630306540_bzx6 /tmp/maxdb/pipe_pages" [18/979] OK Returncode 0 ... ...

Sample for log backups:

>recover_start BACKLog LOG EBID "MAXDB 1632394917_0af3 /tmp/maxdb_log_

pipe" UNTIL 20210923 163300

OK

Returncode

-8020

...

>recover_replace BACKLog ExternalBackupID "MAXDB 1632395036_yxg0 /tmp/maxdb_log_pipe"

OK Returncode

-8020

Note: Execute the following command, if the database is not online: >recover_ignore OK Returncode 0

SAP MaxDB on Windows
Cohesity DataPlatform natively integrates with SAP MaxDB to provide backup and recovery for clustered SAP MaxDB deployments. Using Cohesity Connector Agent, you can backup and restore the SAP MaxDB database. The Cohesity Connector Agent provides a simple workflow to back up and restore your SAP MaxDB deployment. Cohesity DataPlatform provides an SAP MaxDB Connector for backup and restore of enterprise SAP MaxDB deployments. The SAP MaxDB Connector leverages the backup and restore capabilities provided by SAP MaxDB. The SAP MaxDB Connector enables you to back up the various databases. It provides:
l Backup: l Full backup l Incremental backup l Scheduled Log backup
l Restore: l Restore the database to a specific data backup l Restore the database to the point in time l Alternate restore of SAP MaxDB database l Alternate restore to a new database or active database on the same SAP MaxDB system. l Alternate restore to a new or active database on a different SAP MaxDB system.

Plan and Prepare for SAP MaxDB on Windows Protection
Before you register your SAP MaxDB deployment as a source with Cohesity and protect SAP MaxDB databases, ensure the following prerequisites:
l Ensure that the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of the Cohesity cluster is resolvable from the SAP MaxDB Windows machine.
l Synchronize the SAP MaxDB Windows machine time with a Network Time Protocol (NTP) server.
l A database user with database admin user privileges.
l Download and install the Cohesity Windows Agent on the SAP MaxDB Windows machine.

Considerations Review and understand the following before you protect your SAP MaxDB database:
l SAP MaxDB with liveCache technology is not supported. l Spaces in the installation path are not supported.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP MaxDB on Windows

l Only PIPE backups are supported. File backups are not supported, and hence only scheduled log backups are supported, and automatic log backups are not supported.
l Only backup and restore to the same Operating System is supported. l Only the single-node SAP MaxDB database system is supported. l Cohesity replication is supported. l For alternate restore, the target SAP MaxDB database must be created before starting
the restore operation. l If the database system administration (SUPERDBA) password is different in both the
source and the target SAP MaxDB hosts, then when you perform an alternate restore of a specific data backup to the target SAP MaxDB host, the recovery run completes with the following errors:
-24907,ERR_DBAWRONG: Wrong database system administrator -24988,ERR_SQL: SQL error -4008,Unknown user name/password combination
To avoid the issue in the future, you must change the database system administrator password on the target SAP MaxDB host before the system copy to be consistent with the source SAP MaxDB host's password. Once the system copy is completed, you can change the password. l Ensure that the SAP MaxDB database versions in both the source and target systems are compatible. l It is mandatory to connect to the Cohesity cluster securely using secure gRPC when writing or reading data.

Backup SAP MaxDB on Windows Database
Cohesity provides a simple workflow to back up your SAP MaxDB databases. After registering the SAP MaxDB as a source on Cohesity, you can start configuring your backups. Backup Process Cohesity provides an SAP MaxDB Connector for the backup and restore of enterprise SAP MaxDB deployments. The SAP MaxDB Connector leverages the backup capabilities provided by SAP MaxDB. After registering the SAP MaxDB source on Cohesity, you can create a Protection Group and specify the objects such as databases and tables that you want to backup. In the Protection Group, you need to define the parameters that enable you to provide additional parameters required by the backup statements provided by SAP MaxDB.
Note: Cohesity recommends that you configure periodic full backups.
Backup Parameters In the Protection Group, you can define the following parameters for your SAP MaxDB backup configuration:

Backup Parameters --xuser-key=<key>
--backup-template

Mandatory? Optional
Mandatory

Description
By default, SAP MaxDB uses the xuser key provided during the SAP MaxDB connector installation. You can override the xuser key using the parameter based on your requirements. For example: --xuser-key=XUSER_KEY
Specify the backup template that you have created for the backup. Ensure that you create specific backup templates for COMPLETE DATA, INCREMENTAL DATA, AND LOG DATA. For detailed instructions to create a backup template, see backup_ template_create on SAP documentation. By default, SAP MaxDB uses the `BACKData' template for full backup, `BACKPages' template name for incremental backup, `BACKLog' template name for log backups. For example: --backup-template=BACKData

l Specify the objects such as databases and tables that you want to backup. l Based on your requirement, define the parameters for the backup statements
provided by SAP MaxDB. For more information, see Backup Parameters.
The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see About Policies and Protection Groups. To protect SAP MaxDB deployments:

Additional Settings

Additional Settings Pause Future Run End Time QoS Policy
Concurrency Alerts

Description
Enable Pause Future Run only if you do not want to schedule future runs of the Protection Group.
Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
The maximum number of streams that are created to exchange data with the cluster. By default, maximum scaling is set to empty.
Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created. For more information, see Alerts.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Description

a. High-priority protection runs b. Medium-priority protection runs c. Low-priority protection runs

Purge SAP MaxDB on Windows Backups Cohesity cluster provides an in-built purge functionality that you can use to automatically remove the expired data and log backups from the Cohesity cluster. The purge operation works based on the retention period that you have configured on the Protection policy associated with the data backup. For information on how to set the retention period for a data backup, see About Policies and Protection Groups.
Note: The retention period you have configured for log backups is not honored because only the last successful full backup is considered based on the retention period. Any backups older than the full backup are deleted.
For example, In the protection policy, if you have configured to take backup every day, the retention period is 14 days. Assuming that the current date is November 26th, in that case, the last successful full backup on or before November 12th is retained, and any backups older than the full backup are deleted.

Note: Ensure that the new database exists on the target SAP MaxDB host.

Cohesity Platform natively integrates with SAP Sybase ASE to provide backup and recovery for SAP Sybase ASE deployments. Using Cohesity Connector Agent, you can backup and restore the SAP Sybase ASE databases. Cohesity Platform provides a SAP Sybase ASE connector that enables you to perform a full backup, differential backup, log backup, restore and point in time restore at the database level. The SAP Sybase ASE connector leverages the third-party dynamic link library (DLL) based capabilities provided by SAP Sybase ASE for backup and restore functionality.

Considerations
Review and understand the following requirements before you protect your single node SAP Sybase ASE deployment.
l Backup or restore for SAP Sybase ASE HA cluster deployments are not supported. l Ensure that the database is not in use (active connections) during recovery. l Once Cohesity protects the Sybase ASE database, it is not recommended to use the
SAP backup and/or restore tools outside of Cohesity, including native dump or load tools provided by SAP Sybase ASE. l The same database should not be part of multiple Protection Groups. l If the hole is introduced in the backup timeline, then point-in-time recovery (PITR) is possible only after the subsequent successful full or incremental backup is completed. l Cohesity supports backup and restore of SAP Sybase ASE databases running on dualstack (IPv4 and IPv6) mode or single-stack (only IPv6) mode.

Additional Settings

Additional Settings Pause Future Run End Time
QoS Policy

Description
Enable Pause Future Run only if you do not want to schedule future runs of the Protection Group.
Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Description

In the Cohesity Platform, a backup configuration includes a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. You can modify the existing Protection Group and the Protection Policy based on your requirements.
Attach New Protection Policy to the Protection Group
A Protection Policy can be attached to multiple Protection Groups, and any changes in the policy settings impact all the Protection Groups that are associated with the Protection Policy. You can create and attach a new Protection Policy with the required policy settings to your Protection Group. The new policy is applied to the Protection Group from the next scheduled protection run. To attach a new Protection Policy to the Protection Group:

6. Click Save.

Recover SAP Sybase ASE on Linux Database
You can restore to the same SAP Sybase ASE deployment or to a different SAP Sybase ASE deployment. The Cohesity SAP Sybase ASE connector leverages the restore tool provided by SAP Sybase ASE. You can create a Recovery configuration and specify the object such as a database to recover.

Recover SAP Sybase ASE on Linux Databases
To restore SAP Sybase ASE databases:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Recoveries. 2. Click Recover at the top right of the page and then select Universal Data Adapter. 3. Search for the Protection Group that contains the snapshots to recover from by

Plan and Prepare for SAP Sybase ASE on Windows Protection
Before you register your SAP Sybase ASE deployment as a source with Cohesity Platform, ensure the following prerequisites:
l The user account of the SAP Sybase ASE instance must have database admin privileges or operator privileges.
l Download and install the Cohesity Windows Agent on the SAP Sybase ASE host. l Download and install the Cohesity SAP Sybase ASE Connector on the SAP Sybase ASE
host using the same user that was used for installing Cohesity Windows Agent. l Review and understand the limitations.
Supported Versions
For more information on supported SAP Sybase ASE versions, see SAP Sybase ASE versions.
Port Requirements
You must open certain ports in the firewall to allow the Cohesity cluster to transmit and receive data. Ensure that you open the following port in the firewall to allow data transfer between the SAP Sybase ASE host and the Cohesity cluster:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP Sybase ASE on Microsoft Windows

Port 50051 11113

Source SAP Sybase ASE SAP Sybase ASE

Target Cohesity cluster Cohesity cluster

Direction Bidirectional Unidirectional

Network Protocol TCP/IP TCP/IP

Considerations
Review and understand the following requirements before you protect your single-node SAP Sybase ASE deployment.
l Backup or restore for SAP Sybase ASE HA cluster deployments are not supported. l Ensure that the database is not in use (active connections) during recovery. l Once Cohesity protects the Sybase ASE database, it is not recommended to use the
SAP backup and/or restore tools outside of Cohesity, including native dump or load tools provided by SAP Sybase ASE. l The same database should not be part of multiple Protection Groups. l Kerberos authentication is currently not supported. l Backup or restore not supported if the SAP Sybase ASE server is listening on IPV6. l If the hole is introduced in the backup timeline, then point-in-time recovery (PITR) is possible only after the subsequent successful full or incremental backup is completed. l Cohesity supports backup and restore of SAP Sybase ASE databases running on dualstack (IPv4 and IPv6) mode, single-stack (only IPv6) mode, and single-stack (only IPv4) mode.
Prerequisites
l The user account used to install the Cohesity Windows Agent and Cohesity ASE connector must have administrator privileges
l Local System Account must not be used for installing and running Cohesity Windows agent and connector.
l Enable incremental backups on the SAP Sybase ASE host using the following database command:
use <dbname> master ..sp_dboption <dbname>, "allow incremental dumps", false

Note: After enabling incremental backups, you have to first initiate a full backup through the Cohesity Dashboard.

l Only IPv4 is supported and hence ensure that the SAP Sybase ASE server listens on IPv4 address.
l In a multitenant environment that has a hybrid extender-based configuration, if the data source does not use a secure gRPC client, then ensure that you execute the following commands on each hybrid extender before registering the SAP Sybase ASE source on the Cohesity cluster:
$bifrost.sh stop $bifrost.sh start --magneto_grpc_timeout_msecs=300000 --tcp_proxy_ connector_ports=445:445,2049:2049,80:80,443:443,11117:11117,11113:11113 $sudo firewall-cmd --add-port=11113/tcp --zone=public --permanent && sudo firewall-cmd --reload

The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured.
A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see About Policies and Protection Groups.

Additional Settings QoS Policy
Concurrency Alerts
Priority

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Maximum number of backup streams that will be created to exchange data with the Cohesity cluster. By default, maximum scaling is 16. Available concurrency is distributed across multiple databases to be backed up or restored.
Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created. For more information, see Alerts.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.
Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity Platform supports concurrent backups. However, if the number of protection runs exceeds the ability to process runs, this will be the priority of implementation of the protection runs:
a. High-priority protection runs b. Medium-priority protection runs c. Low-priority protection runs

Before you restore the master database, ensure that you perform the following on the SAP ASE host:
1. Start the Adaptive Server in single-user mode, for detailed instructions, see How to Start Adaptive Server in Single-User Mode in SAP documentation.
2. Restart the SAP ASE server.
To restore the master database, follow the steps in the SAP Sybase ASE Databases restore procedure, and ensure that you disable the Create Database option in the Restore Settings section.
Cancel a Recovery Run
When you cancel a recovery run, the SAP Sybase ASE connector cancels the job by terminating the recovery processes. To cancel a recovery run:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Recoveries. 2. Click the action icon (...) next to the recovery run and click Cancel Run. 3. In the Cancel Recovery dialog box, select any one of the following:
l Continue Recovery if you want to continue the recovery task. l Cancel Recovery if you want to cancel the recovery task.

Known Issues and Workaround The following table lists the known issues and workarounds:

Known Issue

Workaround

After the Cohesity Windows Agent is restarted, in certain cases a few stale DBs may continue to run during a recovery job run.

Manually drop the database, recreate and retry the restore.

PITR restore fails with the following error: error " [13]:Cannot find data backup run for PITR 1623883236"

If the point in time selected for restore is before the first full backup, then you may see this error. Please select a point later than the end of the first full backup.

In case of SAP Sybase ASE version mismatch , database fails to come online after a successful restore.

Try to online the database manually, online database <dbname>

SAP on Oracle for Linux
Cohesity natively integrates with SAP on Oracle to provide backup and recovery for SAP on Oracle deployments. Cohesity provides an Oracle Connector that enables you to do the following:
l Backs up data files, control files, and online redo log files of the database. l Backs up offline redo log files. l Restores data files, control files, and online and offline redo log files. l Recovers database files and restores profiles and log files. l Manages the database instance, space, and segments (that is, tables and indexes). l Performs database administration tasks such as statistics update, check database
system, adapt next extents, clean up logs and DBA tables. l Functions as a help tool to monitor the database during a backup. l Functions as an internal help tool started by BRBACKUP, BRARCHIVE, and
BRRESTORE.

Considerations
Review and understand the following before you protect your Oracle database:
l SAP on Oracle installations performed using the oracle user are not supported because they require a BRTools configuration as specified in SAP Note 1598594. However, Cohesity only supports the BRTools configuration outlined in SAP Note 113747.
l Automatic database creation is not supported. You need to create a database before running either backup or restore.
l Alternate restore to a new database on a different SAP on Oracle system with a different SID option is not supported.
l SAP on Oracle Connector agent does not support auto-discovery and entity hierarchy; hence you cannot browse or search and select objects for backup.
l Offline backup of the database is not supported. l Indexing is not supported. l You cannot protect multiple hosts using a single Protection Group.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP on Oracle for Linux

l You cannot backup multiple databases in a single Protection Group. l You cannot restore multiple objects, search, and recover an object. l The RPM-based installer is not currently supported. l SAP Oracle ASM deployment is not supported. l Ensure that the SAP on Oracle DB instance uses an SPFILE to start up as
recommended by SAP. For more information, see https://me.sap.com/notes/1598594. l It is mandatory to connect to the Cohesity cluster securely using secure gRPC when writing or reading data. Download and install the Cohesity Linux Agent The Cohesity Linux Agent is available as script-based and RPM-based installers, based on your requirements download the installer and install it accordingly on the SAP on Oracle database. For detailed instructions, see Download and Install the Linux Agent.
Note: Ensure you meet the following prerequisites below before you install the Cohesity Linux agent.
Download and Install the SAP on Oracle Connector Cohesity provides a SAP on Oracle Connector to backup and restore SAP on Oracle databases. The SAP on Oracle Connector is available as a datasource agent on the Cohesity Download portal. Log on to the Cohesity Download portal, download the respective datasource agent for SAP on Oracle Connector, and copy the datasource agent to the SAP on Oracle host.
Install the SAP on Oracle Connector
On the SAP on Oracle host where you have copied the SAP on Oracle Connector (scp cohesity_secure_connector_service_6.6.0b_ent_sap_oracle_java_installer), perform the following to install the SAP on Oracle Connector: Before You Install
l Before you install the SAP on Oracle Connector, ensure the following prerequisites: Ensure the variables $SAPDATA_HOME and $ORACLE_HOME are set for the user performing the installation.
Note: Cohesity recommends using the "root" user account to install the SAP on Oracle Connector.
Example:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP on Oracle for Linux

$ export ORACLE_HOME=</oracle/SID/121> $ export SAPDATA_HOME=</oracle/SID>
l During the SAP on Oracle Connector installation, you need permission to write to /usr/sap/<SID>/ directory as it is the default installation location. If you do not have write access, please specify the custom installation directory using "-I" or "--installdir" while running the installer. Example:
./cohesity_secure_connector_service_sap_oracle_java_installer -- -install -s SID -w uda -S ora<sid> -I /home/ora<sid>/uda_install/
l The BRTOOLS are pre-installed on the SAP on Oracle System. The Cohesity SAP on Oracle connector integrates with BRTOOLS for backup and restore. SAP recommends BRTOOLS version 7.40 Patch 46 or greater. For more information, see https://launchpad.support.sap.com/#/notes/3060252.
l Ensure that the BRTOOLS' ownership and permissions follow the SAP note: https://me.sap.com/notes/113747. For example:
-rwsrwxr-- 1 orasid sapsys 10022600 Aug 23 2012 brarchive -rwsrwxr-- 1 orasid sapsys 10251536 Aug 23 2012 brbackup -rwsrwxr-- 1 orasid sapsys 12179560 Aug 23 2012 brconnect -rwxr-xr-x 1 sidadm sapsys 10708840 Aug 23 2012 brrecover -rwxr-xr-x 1 sidadm sapsys 4140576 Aug 23 2012 brrestore -rwxr-xr-x 1 sidadm sapsys 12778384 Aug 23 2012 brspace -rwxr-xr-x 1 sidadm sapsys 4711664 Aug 23 2012 brtools
l Use "bash" shell to install the SAP on Oracle Connector and to run backups and restore workflows of SAP on Oracle databases.
l Ensure that the NTP time is in sync between the client and the Cohesity cluster. Perform the following on the client: l Verify if NTP is enabled and synchronized in the client using the following command:
timedatectl
l If the NTP time is not synchronized, use the following command to synchronize the NTP time
timedatectl set-ntp true
To install the SAP on Oracle Connector:
1. Log on to the SAP on Oracle host as a root user where you have copied the SAP on Oracle script-based installer, cohesity_secure_connector_service_6.6.0b_ent_

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP on Oracle for Linux

sap_oracle_java_installer.
Note: During the SAP on Oracle connector installation, by default, the script installer extracts the files to the /tmp directory. If you plan to extract the files to a different directory, you can define the directory path in the TMPDIR environment variable as follows: export TMPDIR=<directory_path>.
2. Run the following command to install the SAP on Oracle Connector (cohesity_ secure_connector_service_6.6.0b_ent_sap_oracle_java_installer):
./cohesity_secure_connector_service_6.6.0b_ent_sap_oracle_java_ installer -- --install -I <install_directory> -s <SID> -w uda
Where: 1. -i <install_directory> - The directory on the SAP on Oracle host on which you want to install the SAP on Oracle Connector. By default, the SAP on Oracle Connector is installed in the /usr/sap/<SID>/cohesity directory. You can use -i <install_directory> if you want to change the default installation location from /usr/sap/SID/cohesity/. 2. -w <workflow> - The type of workflow you intend to install the SAP on Oracle Connector. For UDA workflow, specify uda. 3. -s <SID> - SAP System Identification (SID) is a unique three-character code that is available for every R/3 installation (SAP system) that consists of a database server and several application servers. If you have different permissions (for the owner user and group) in the abovementioned files, it is necessary to run backup and restore operations with the sudo user. Cohesity recommends adding the following in the sudoers file: 1. Add the following in the sudoers file:
ora<sid> ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:SETENV: /bin/chown, /bin/java, /bin/chmod
2. Edit following line in ${INSTALL_DIR}/backint.sh to:
JAVA="sudo -E java"
Refer to SAP recommendations for the default owner and permissions of init<DBSID>.ora, init<DBSID>.sap, $SAPDATA_HOME: https://launchpad.support.sap.com/#/notes/113747. You can also run the following command to know more details about the options used in the above command.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP on Oracle for Linux

$ ./cohesity_secure_connector_service_6.6.0b_ent_sap_oracle_java_ installer -- --help

3. After installation, if the user does not have access to $SAPEXE (/usr/sap/<SID>/SYS/exe/run), create a soft link to backint.sh in $SAPEXE directory using the following command.
Example:

ln -sf '/home/ora<sid>/uda_install/backint.sh' '${SAPEXE}/backint' chown -h "ora<sid>":"sapsys" "${SAPEXE_DIR}/backint"

4. Optional. Create a softlink to uda_scripts manually, if the installer (cohesity_ secure_connector_service_6.6.0b_ent_sap_oracle_java_installer) fails to create the soft link using the following command:

chmod -R 755 /opt/cohesity ln -sf /home/ora<sid>/uda_install/uda_ scripts /opt/cohesity/agent/uda_scripts

Register and Manage the SAP on Oracle for Linux Source
To protect your SAP on Oracle databases, you need to register your SAP on Oracle deployment as a source on Cohesity. After registering your SAP on Oracle deployment as a source, you can:
l Update the username and password of the database user. l Refresh the source details. l Unregister the SAP on Oracle source from Cohesity.
Register SAP on Oracle as a Source
Before you register SAP on Oracle as a source, ensure that you:
l Review the requirements and limitations. l Perform the prerequisite tasks.
For more information, see Plan and Prepare for SAP on Oracle for Linux Protection. To register SAP on Oracle as a source:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click the Register on the top-right of the page and then select Universal Data
Adapter. 3. In the Register Universal Data Adapter page, perform the following:
1. From the Source Type drop-down menu, select SAP Oracle. 2. From the Host OS Type drop-down menu, select Linux. 3. In the Hostname / IP Addresses field, enter the hostname or IP address of
the SAP on the Oracle host you have identified to run the secure connector service for SAP Oracle. For more information, see Plan and Prepare for SAP on Oracle for Linux Protection. 4. In the Datasource Agent Installation Path, enter the directory path on the SAP on Oracle host, where you have installed the secure connector service for SAP Oracle. For more information, see Download and Install the SAP on Oracle Connector. 5. In the APP Authentication section, provide the SAP on Oracle database's Username and Password.
Note: The Password field is optional.
6. Enable Custom Options, and perform the following: 1. Ignore the Mounts View option. It is not applicable for SAP on Oracle source registration.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP on Oracle for Linux

2. Ignore the Source Registration Options. It is not applicable to SAP on Oracle registration.
7. Click Register. Update the SAP on Oracle Source Configuration After registering your SAP on Oracle as a source on Cohesity, you can:
l Update the username and password of the database user. l Update the Script Directory Path only if you have uninstalled and reinstalled the
secure connector service for SAP Oracle in a different directory on the SAP on Oracle host. To update the SAP on Oracle source configuration: 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources.
2. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the SAP on Oracle source and select Edit. 3. On the Update Universal Data Adapter page, update the required configurations. 4. Click Update. Refresh the SAP on Oracle Source Configuration You can refresh the SAP on Oracle Source and re-verify the source with the available source registration parameters. To refresh the SAP on Oracle Source Configuration: 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources.
2. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the SAP on Oracle Source and select Refresh. Unregister the SAP on Oracle Source If you plan to stop taking the backup of your SAP on Oracle databases, you can unregister the SAP on Oracle source from the Cohesity Cluster. To unregister the SAP on Oracle source:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources.
2. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the SAP on Oracle source and select Unregister.
Backup SAP on Oracle for Linux Database
Cohesity provides a simple workflow to back up your SAP on Oracle databases. After registering the SAP on Oracle as a source on Cohesity, you can start configuring your backups.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP on Oracle for Linux

Backup Process Cohesity provides a SAP on Oracle Connector for backup and restore of enterprise SAP on Oracle deployments. The SAP on Oracle Connector leverages the backup capabilities provided by SAP. After registering the SAP on Oracle source on Cohesity, you can create a Protection Group and specify the objects such as databases and tables that you want to backup. In the Protection Group, you need to define the parameters that enable you to provide additional parameters required by the backup statements provided by SAP on Oracle.
Note: Cohesity recommends that you configure periodic full backups.
Backup Parameters In the Protection Group, you can define the following parameters for your SAP on Oracle backup configuration:

Backup Parameters
--use-securegrpc=<true/false>

Mandatory? Optional

Description
Set the parameter to true, if you want to use secure gRPC communication during backup. For example: --use-secure-grpc=true

Protect SAP on Oracle for Linux Deployments
SAP on Oracle deployments is protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group enables you to specify the objects such as databases and tables that you want to back up.
The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured.
A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see About Policies and Protection Groups.
To protect SAP on Oracle deployments:
1. Do one of the following:
1. Select Data Protection > Protection. Click Protect on the top-right of the page and then select Universal Data Adapter.

2. Select Data Protection > Source. Click the actions menu ( SAP on Oracle source and then select Protect.

) next to the

2. From the Source drop-down list, select the registered SAP on Oracle source or click Register Source to register an SAP on Oracle source. For more information, see Register SAP on Oracle as a Source.

3. In the Objects section, add the object that you plan to protect. The object can be a database or a table. To back up a database, enter the name of the database.

4. In the Protection Group section, do one of the following:

1. Select a New Group to create a new Protection Group. In the Protection Name field, enter a name from the Protection Group.

2. Select Existing Group to use the settings of an existing Protection Group. From the Group list, select an existing Protection Group and click Protect.

5. In the Settings section, do the following:

1. Select the appropriate Storage Domain. For more information, see Manage Storage Domains.

2. In the Start Time field, define when the protection run should start. This option is only available if the selected policy is set to Backup Daily. Enter the hour and minutes, or use the up and down arrows on your keyboard.

Verify the AM or PM setting. The default time zone is the browser's time zone. You can change the time zone of the protection run by selecting a different time zone.

Additional Settings QoS Policy
Concurrency

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
The maximum number of restore streams that are created to exchange data with the cluster. By default, maximum scaling is set to 16.
Note: Cohesity recommends that concurrency should be set to the number of nodes on the Cohesity cluster.

Alerts

Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Create an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Create a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created. For more information, see Alerts.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Description

Description
Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity supports concurrent backups. However, if the number of protection groups exceeds the ability to process protection groups, this will be the priority of implementation of the protection groups:
l High-priority protection groups l Medium-priority protection groups l Low-priority protection groups.
The service-level agreement (SLA) defines how long the administrator expects a Protection Group run to take.
l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental backup Protection Group run takes to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last run.
l Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup Protection Group run takes to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).

A Protection Policy can be attached to multiple Protection Groups, and any changes in the policy settings impact all the Protection Groups associated with the Protection Policy. Prerequisites Ensure that:
l The Oracle Database state should be nomount state when performing alternate or cross restores.
l The Protection Group associated with the object that you plan to restore is paused or in not running state.
l If you perform an alternate restore, ensure the SAP on Oracle versions on the source and the target host are the same.

SAP on Oracle for Microsoft Windows

SAP on Oracle for Microsoft Windows
Cohesity natively integrates with SAP on Oracle to provide backup and recovery for SAP on Oracle deployments running on the Microsoft Windows platform. Using Cohesity Connector Agent, you can backup and restore the SAP on Oracle databases. The Cohesity Connector Agent provides a simple workflow to back up and restore your SAP on Oracle deployment. Cohesity provides an SAP on Oracle connector that enables you to perform a full backup, incremental (differential) backup, log backup, restore and point in time restore at the database level.
Core Components
The following are the core components for protecting SAP on Oracle databases:
l Oracle Database l Cohesity SAP on Oracle Connector l Cohesity Connector Agent l Cohesity View
As illustrated, you can integrate Cohesity with your SAP on Oracle deployments using the SAP on Oracle connector and Cohesity Connector Agent.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP on Oracle for Microsoft Windows

Plan and Prepare for SAP on Oracle for Windows Protection
Before you register your SAP on Oracle deployment as a source with Cohesity, ensure the following prerequisites:
l The user account of the SAP on Oracle instance must have database admin privileges. l Download and install the Cohesity Windows Agent on the SAP on Oracle host. l Download and install the Cohesity SAP on the Oracle Connector on the SAP on Oracle
host using the same user account that you used to install the Cohesity Windows Agent.
Supported Versions
For more information on supported SAP on Oracle versions, see Supported Software versions.
Considerations
Review and understand the following before you protect your Oracle database:
l Automatic database creation is not supported. You need to create a database before running either backup or restore.
l In a protection run, you cannot back up multiple objects. l In a recovery run, you cannot restore multiple objects. l Cross-platform (Windows to Linux or vice versa) backup and restore are not
supported. l SAP on Oracle Connector agent does not support auto-discovery and entity hierarchy;
hence you cannot browse or search and select objects for backup. l Indexing is not supported. l Offline backup of the database is not supported. l You cannot protect multiple hosts using a single Protection Group. l You cannot backup multiple databases in a single Protection Group. l You cannot restore multiple objects, search and recover an object. l You cannot cancel a running restore operation. l SAP Oracle ASM deployment is not supported. l Ensure that the SAP on Oracle DB instance uses an SPFILE to start up as
recommended by SAP. For more information, see https://me.sap.com/notes/1598594. l It is mandatory to connect to the Cohesity cluster securely using secure gRPC when writing or reading data.

Chapter 13: Databases

SAP on Oracle for Microsoft Windows

Troubleshooting Backup Error
Issue: Log backup fails with the following error:
BR0013W No offline redolog files found for processing
Problem: The issue occurs when the Oracle database is opened after recovery with ALTER DATABASE OPEN RESETLOGS, and the "log sequence number" is reset to 1. However, since the BRARCHIVE log arch<SID>.log in the directory $ORACLE_HOME/saparch still contains entries for successful archive log backups with higher numbers. BRARCHIVE does not recognize the new logs as the logs to be saved. Workaround: To mitigate this issue, refer to the following SAP recommendation:
l https://me.sap.com/notes/490976 (refer to step 4. Database was reset with RESET LOGS)
l https://me.sap.com/notes/10170

The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. Description

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Define the concurrency or number of channels to use for exchanging data with the cluster. For SAP on Oracle data protection on Windows, the concurrency depends on the SAP on Oracle license.
l For Standard editions, only a single channel is supported. l For Enterprise editions, more than one channel is supported.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

PostgreSQL

Cohesity Platform provides a PostgreSQL connector that enables you to perform a full backup, differential backup, log backup, restore and point in time restore at the cluster level.
Core Components
The following are the core components for protecting PostgreSQL databases: l PostgreSQL Installation l Cohesity PostgreSQL connector l Cohesity Connector Agent
As illustrated, you can integrate the Cohesity Platform with your PostgreSQL deployments using the Cohesity PostgreSQL connector and Connector Agent.

Plan and Prepare for PostgreSQL Protection

Prerequisites
Ensure that:
l You use a root user or non-root user to install the Cohesity Linux agent and Cohesity PostgreSQL Connector. If you choose to use a non-root user, you must add the sudo privileges for the non-root user using the syntax given below:
<user_name> ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:SETENV: /path/to/command1, /path/to/command2, /path/to/command3
The following is the sudo commands for PostgreSQL Connector:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

cohesityagent ALL=NOPASSWD:SETENV: /bin/chmod, /bin/chown, /bin/mkdir, /bin/rm, /bin/psql, /usr/bin/ps, /usr/sbin/runuser, /bin/java, /usr/bin/netstat, /bin/test
Note: l If the cohesityagent user entry is already present in /etc/sudoers, append the list of commands to the existing entry. l The actual paths for each command might vary in each system. For more information, see Download and Install the Linux Agent.
l Java version 1.8 or higher is installed on all PostgreSQL nodes and available in the path for the Cohesity agent, the root user, and the postgres user.
l Java binary is available in the $PATH environment variable. l The default postgres database is present on the PostgreSQL instance. l To securely connect to the Cohesity cluster while reading or writing data, you can use
secure gRPC.
Note: l It is mandatory to connect to the Cohesity cluster securely using secure gRPC when writing or reading data. l Using non-secure gRPC for data transfer between Cohesity and database hosts will result in unsecured communication. l Enabling secure gRPC will increase data transfer time between Cohesity and database hosts compared to non-secure communication.
To use secure gRPC, perform the following: 1. Generate the certificate config file on the Cohesity node using the following command: ~/<release-version>/crux/bin/client_tls_cert_generator_exec -cert_ name <clustername> -output_file /home/cohesity/<clustername>.cfg
2. Copy /home/cohesity/<clustername>.cfg from the Cohesity node to all PostgreSQL nodes at the same location. For example, /opt/certs/<clustername>.cfg.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

Note: Ensure that the root or non-root user used to install the Cohesity Linux agent and PostgreSQL Connector has read access to the generated certificate config file.
3. While registering the PostgreSQL source, provide the path of the certificate config file in the Cohesity SSL Settings field.
l If you are restoring to the same or different cluster, ensure that the port you want to use for the restored instance is not in use.
l In case of Cohesity Cloud Edition deployment with any PostgreSQL setup, ensure that the Cohesity cluster name resolves to the IP addresses of all nodes through DNS.
Considerations
Review and understand the following limitations and known issues before you protect your PostgreSQL deployment:
l Only physical backup is supported. l Backup or restore is performed at the cluster level. Object-level backup or restore is
not supported. l Restore across different PostgreSQL versions is not supported. l For optimum performance in log backups, it is recommended to set the WAL size to
1GB. l If the hole is introduced in the backup timeline, then point-in-time recovery (PITR) is
possible only after the subsequent successful full or incremental backup is completed. l Cohesity supports backup and restore of PostgreSQL databases running on dual-stack
(IPv4 and IPv6) mode or single-stack (only IPv6) mode. l Cohesity supports granular-level database permissions which allows the non-
superuser to register the PostgreSQL source and perform the backups. See Configure Privileges for Non-Admin Users. l FIPS mode is not currently supported for PostgreSQL backups.
Considerations for HA Cluster Deployments
Review the following additional considerations when protecting HA cluster:
l Register the source by specifying all Patroni member node names or IP addresses in the hostname field during source registration.
l Backups run only on the current Patroni leader node. Standby and replica nodes are not backed up.
l Immediately trigger a full backup after a failover, switchover, or any event that changes the Patroni leader node.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

l Restores are attempted only on the first Patroni member node defined in the source registration's hostname field. To change the restore target, update the source registration and reorder the node list.
l SSL keys must not be stored in the PostgreSQL data directory for Patroni deployments. Because Cohesity backs up only the active leader node, SSL keys stored in the data directory may not be available across all nodes after restore. Store SSL certificates in an external directory and specify the custom SSL certificate path during source registration.
l Restores are not Patroni-aware and always result in a standalone PostgreSQL instance. Additional manual steps are required to rebuild the Patroni cluster after restore. For more information, see Recover a Patroni-Managed PostgreSQL Cluster.
l Backups from a Patroni-managed (replicated) source can only be restored to a new location.
l Point-in-time recovery (PITR) from archived backups is not supported for Patroni deployments.
l Instant restore is not supported for Patroni-managed PostgreSQL deployments. l In the case of the HA cluster, the backup is executed from the active node only. l In case of a failover in the HA cluster, the next backup run will be a full backup.
Consideration for Transparent Data Encryption (TDE)
l Cohesity does not encrypt or decrypt PostgreSQL data or WAL files; encryption is handled by PostgreSQL.
l If you enable TDE, ensure that a master encryption key is created using the Cohesity REST API before registering the PostgreSQL source. The Cohesity user invoking the API must have appropriate Users and Groups to create and manage encryption keys.
Note: If your organization rotates the PostgreSQL master wrapping key (for example, every 30 or 90 days), ensure that the key required to decrypt the backup is available on the restore target. Cohesity recovers encrypted data files as-is. The recovery job can complete successfully, but PostgreSQL will not start if the required master wrapping key is missing or inaccessible.
l Cohesity does not create, manage, back up, or recover encryption keys (including the master wrapping key).
l After a recovery, PostgreSQL can start only if the required master wrapping key is available on the restore target. If the key is missing or inaccessible, the restore job may complete successfully, but PostgreSQL will not start.
l You cannot restore a non-TDE snapshot to a PostgreSQL instance that is already running with TDE enabled on that port. The recovery will fail.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

Note: Cohesity backs up and restores EDB PostgreSQL TDE data as-is, and PostgreSQL can start after restore only if the required unwrap configuration and master wrapping key are available on the restore target.
Download and Install the Cohesity Linux Agent The Cohesity Linux Agent is available as RPM-based installers, based on your requirements download the installer and install it accordingly on the PostgreSQL hosts to be protected. For detailed instructions, see Download and Install the Linux Agent. Download and install the PostgreSQL Connector Cohesity Platform provides a PostgreSQL Connector for backup and restore of enterprise PostgreSQL deployments.
Download the PostgreSQL Connector
Cohesity Platform provides a PostgreSQL Connector to backup and restore PostgreSQL deployments. The PostgreSQL Connector is available as a datasource agent on the Cohesity Download portal. Log on to the Cohesity Download portal, download the respective datasource agent for PostgreSQL Connector, and copy the datasource agent to the PostgreSQL database host.
Install the PostgreSQL Connector
On the PostgreSQL database host where you have copied the PostgreSQL Connector, perform the following to install the PostgreSQL Connector. To install the Cohesity PostgreSQL connector:
1. Log on to the PostgreSQL Linux machine using the user with sudo privileges. 2. Navigate to the directory where you have copied the RPM-based installer. 3. Install the Cohesity PostgreSQL connector using the following command:
Using yum: # sudo yum -y install cohesity-postgres-connector-<version>.rpm
Using rpm -ivh: # sudo rpm -ivh cohesity-postgres-connector-<version>.rpm
Uninstall the PostgreSQL Connector
To uninstall the Cohesity PostgreSQL connector, run the following command on PostgreSQL host: Using yum: # sudo yum -y remove cohesity-postgres-connector-<version>

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

Using rpm:
# sudo rpm -e cohesity-postgres-connector-<version>.rpm
Upgrade the PostgreSQL Connector
To upgrade the Cohesity PostgreSQL connector, run the following command on PostgreSQL host:
sudo rpm -U cohesity-postgres-connector-<version>.rpm
Migration script for New User Experience
Cohesity provides a new improved user experience that streamlines the process of registration, protection, and recovery of PostgreSQL database. To migrate the existing PostgreSQL database to the new workflow, Cohesity provides a migration script. However, the source and protection jobs for the existing PostgreSQL will continue to function as they are. After the migration script is runned successfully, Cohesity displays the PostgreSQL instances listed separately under the DataProtection > Sources > PostgreSQL section. Ensure that:
l Migration script file should have execute permission on the PostgreSQL server. l PostgreSQL server can reach the Cohesity cluster on the required network ports listed
in this document. l Cohesity admin or equivalent user should perform the task.
To migrate the PostgreSQL database to new workflow:
1. Log on to the PostgreSQL Linux machine. 2. Navigate to /opt/cohesity/postgreSQL/scripts. 3. Run the following script files using chmod +x command:
a. migrate_scource.sh - to migrate the source configurations. b. migrate_protection.sh - to migrate the protection jobs.
For example: chmod +x migrate_source.sh To view the help options, run the command as chmod +x migrate_source.sh --help

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

Note: l Original backup jobs are paused and not deleted. l No roll back script provided. If the migration script fails, check the logs to resolve the issue and re-run the migration script. The log file for Source is located: registration_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log
The log file for Protection Groups is located: create_protection_ groups_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).log l Verify the new source in the UI: Navigate to Data Protection > Sources.
Configure Privileges for Non-Admin Users
Previously, the PostgreSQL connectors required admin or superuser privileges for backups due to PostgreSQL's design for physical backups using CHECKPOINT. See, CHECKPOINT in PostgreSQL for more details. Cohesity now supports granular-level database permission. From PostgreSQL version 15 onwards, non-admin users can perform backup operation by applying the required configurations and grants. This can be configured manually and script based. Ensure that:
l The instance must be running PostgreSQL version 15 or later. l The PostgreSQL instance is up-and-running on the specified port. l The user executing the script must have PostgreSQL superuser credentials. To configure the privileges using script: 1. Navigate to Datasource Agent Installation path. 2. Run the configure-pg-backup.sh script file with the following parameters on the
PostgreSQL host machine where the database is installed: <installation_dir>/configure-pg-backup.sh --host <host> --port <port> -db <database> \
--superuser <user> --superuser-pass <password> \
--db-user <backup_user> [--restart true|false] [--pgctl /path/to/pg_ ctl]
For example: ../configure-pg-backup.sh --host 10.14.20.60 --port 6004 \
--superuser 'postgres' --superuser-pass xxxxxx \

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

--db-user user1 --restart true --pgctl /usr/pgsql-15/bin/pg_ctl
Refer to the table below for script parameters 3. You need to restart PostgreSQL database to reflect the changes. Run the following
command: pg_ctl restart -D <datadirectory>

Script parameters --host --port --db --superuser --superuser-pass --db-user --restart --pgctl -h, --help

Parameter descriptions Database host Database port Database to connect PostgreSQL superuser (required) Superuser password (required) Database user to whom privileges to be granted (required) Restart PostgreSQL after applying settings (true or false) Explicit path to pg_ctl binary (if not in PATH) Display help and exit

Default values 127.0.0.1 5432 postgre N/A N/A N/A false N/A N/A

To configure the privileges manually:
1. Log on to the PostgreSQL database as a super user and execute the following command to grant the required roles to the backup users:
GRANT pg_read_all_settings, pg_checkpoint TO <dbuser>;
2. Grant the execute permissions on the SQL functions using the following command:
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_switch_wal() TO <dbuser>; GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_backup_start(text, boolean) TO <dbuser>; GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_backup_stop(boolean) TO <dbuser>;
3. Edit and update the archive parameter in postgresql.cong file with the following parameters:
archive_mode = on wal_level = replica

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

archive_command = '<installation_dir>/stream-log.sh %p %f <installation_dir>/archive_config_<system_id>'
4. Restart PostgreSQL database using the following command. The restart is required to reflect the changes to archive_mode and wal_level:
pg_ctl restart -D <data_directory>

Backup PostgreSQL Database
Cohesity Platform provides a simple workflow to back up your PostgreSQL deployment. After registering the PostgreSQL as a source on Cohesity DataPlatform, you can start configuring your backups. Backup Process Cohesity Platform provides a PostgreSQL connector for backup and restore of PostgreSQL deployments. Cohesity PostgreSQL connector uses the JDBC interface to connect the PostgreSQL Server. After registering the PostgreSQL source on the Cohesity Platform, you can create a Protection Group with the required parameters and start protecting PostgreSQL deployment.

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

Backup Behavior for HA Cluster Deployments
l For Patroni-managed PostgreSQL deployments, backups are always executed on the current leader node. Standby and replica nodes are not backed up directly.
l After a failover or switchover event that changes the Patroni leader, you must immediately trigger a full backup. The next scheduled backup after a leader change will automatically be a full backup.
l Ensure that the Cohesity Linux Agent and PostgreSQL Connector are installed and running on all Patroni member nodes to support automatic leader detection during backup.
Protect PostgreSQL Deployments
In Cohesity Platform, PostgreSQL deployments are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. The Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured.
A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. You can select a standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy.

Important: If you have upgraded your PostgreSQL server version after registering the source, it's important to update the directory path to the PostgreSQL binaries that you set using the --pg-bin parameter during registration. Make sure to update the path to the new PostgreSQL binaries path, such as "/usr/pgsql-14/bin" if pgsql-14 is the upgraded version. Also, you need to create a new Protection Group to protect the upgraded PostgreSQL instance.

To protect PostgreSQL deployments:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, do one of the following: l Select Data Protection > Protection. Click Protect on the top-right of the page and then select Databases > PostgreSQL.

l Select Data Protection > Sources. Click the actions menu ( PostgreSQL source and then select Protect.

) next to the

2. From the Source drop-down list, select the registered PostgreSQL source or click Register Source to register a PostgreSQL source. For more information, see Register PostgreSQL as a Source.

3. Click Add Objects and Add Objects dialog is displayed. Select the required instance. Cohesity displays all the database in the selected instance. Select the instance and click Continue.

PostgreSQL

Note: Cohesity supports instance level and NOT database level protection.

Protection Policy. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy. Note: If you re initialize an EnterpriseDB PostgreSQL instance to enable Transparent Data Encryption (TDE), the encrypted instance is treated as a new instance. Existing protection groups created for the unencrypted instance cannot be reused. You must create a new protection group to protect the encrypted instance.
6. Click More Options and perform the following: 1. Select the appropriate Storage Domain. For more information, see Manage Storage Domains. 2. Concurrency Alerts

Description
Optional. Click and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Maximum number of backup streams that will be created to exchange data with the cluster. By default, maximum scaling is set to 16.
Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Creates an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the protection group.

Manage the PostgreSQL Backup Configuration
In the Cohesity Platform, a backup configuration includes a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. You can modify the existing Protection Group and the Protection Policy based on your requirements.
Add Object(s) to the Protection Group
You can add new databases or tables to the existing Protection Group for backup. The newly added object is backed up from the next protection run, and it will be a full backup for the newly added object. To add object(s) to the Protection Group:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for
PostgreSQL.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit.
4. On the Edit Protection page, click in the Objects section. 5. In the Objects section, Click the plus icon (+) to enter multiple objects that you plan
to back up. click Save Selection. 6. Click Save.
Attach New Protection Policy to the Protection Group
A Protection Policy can be attached to multiple Protection Groups, and any changes in the policy settings impact all the Protection Groups that are associated with the Protection Policy. You can create and attach a new Protection Policy with the required policy settings to your Protection Group. The new policy is applied to the Protection Group from the next scheduled protection run.

Recover PostgreSQL Database
You can restore the protected PostgreSQL data to the same PostgreSQL deployment or to a different PostgreSQL deployment.
Instant Restore Instant restore allows you to start a PostgreSQL instance instantly after the restore. Instant restore mounts the Cohesity View as a PostgreSQL data directory and immediately starts a PostgreSQL instance pointing to the same data directory. For EDB PostgreSQL with TDE enabled, Cohesity restores encrypted files as-is. To start PostgreSQL after the restore, ensure that the master wrapping key is available on the restore target. If the master wrapping key is not available, the restore can complete but PostgreSQL will not start.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

The pulse logs show the instance restore's status and whether the PostgreSQL instance is ready to use. The following is a sample of the pulse log:
Instant restore is done, it's ready for use. Please cancel the restore job when done using the instantly restored data
Note: l For external tablespaces, soflinks are created from the mounted Cohesity View
(pointing to the tablespace data) to the expected tablespace location on the local filesystem.
l The instant restore run is shown in the Running state, until you explicitly cancel it from the Cohesity UI.
l To shut down the PostgreSQL instance that started using instant restore, you must cancel the instant restore run from Cohesity UI. Once you cancel the instant restore run, the PostgreSQL instance is stopped, and the Cohesity View is unmounted from the cluster.
l Instant restore does not support point-in-time recovery (PITR).

PostgreSQL. 3. Search for the Protection Group that contains the snapshots to recover from by
entering characters of the Protection Group name, or by specifying the wildcard character *. 4. From the list of search results, select the Protection Group that contains the snapshots to recover. 5. Click Next: Recover Options. 6. In the Recover To section, to restore to the Original Location and type YES to perform instant restore to the same PostgreSQL node.

Regular Restore
Regular restore allows you to restore PostgreSQL instance using latest backups and applying write-ahead-logging (WAL) files during recovery. This recovery method allows you to specify mapping of the PostgreSQL tablespaces to an alternate directory.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

Note: l For versions prior to 7.1.2_u4, redirected restore is not supported for external tablespaces. All tablespaces are restored to the same location as the source. Ensure that the same location as the source is available on the cluster where you are restoring the PostgreSQL data. If the same locations are unavailable on the target cluster, you can create softlinks pointing to the actual storage location.
For example:
ln -s <actual-storage-location> <tablespace-location-same-assource>
For EDB PostgreSQL with TDE enabled, Cohesity recovers encrypted files as-is. To start PostgreSQL after the recovery, ensure that the master wrapping key is available on the restore target. If the master wrapping key is not available, the recovery can complete but PostgreSQL will not start.
Recover using Regular Restore to the Original Location
Perform a regular restore of the PostgreSQL instance to its original location by selecting the protection group, confirming restoration, and configuring recovery options. To restore PostgreSQL:

Roll Forward Database
The Roll Forward Database feature allows to recover PostgreSQL instance using the most recent snapshot backup along with write-ahead-logging (WAL) files that are backed up to

Cohesity but not part of a log backup. This feature is supported only when recovering to the latest snapshot backup and applying all WAL files that are available after it. To enable this option during recovery, select Regular Restore to a New Location option.
Note: Default is No RollForward where recovery is performed without applying the WAL files.
Cohesity supports two roll forward recovery modes: 1. Automatic RollForward: Cohesity automatically applies these logs during recovery. Select this method for quick recovery. 2. Manual RollForward: Cohesity only copies WAL files to the specified path. Specify the path where the WAL files need to be copied with read-write permissions.
