Cancel a Recovery Run
When you cancel a recovery run, the PostgreSQL connector cancels the job by terminating the recovery processes. To cancel a recovery run:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Recoveries.
2. Click the action menu ( ) next to the recovery run and click Cancel Run. 3. In the Cancel Recovery dialog, select any one of the following:
1. Click Continue Recovery if you want to continue a recovery run. 2. Click Cancel Recovery if you want to cancel the recovery run.
Recover HA Cluster Deployment
This topic describes the recovery workflows for PostgreSQL high availability (HA) cluster deployments. The procedures and examples use Patroni as a sample configuration; however, they can be used as a reference for any PostgreSQL HA deployment. Adjust the commands and configuration paths as needed for your specific HA framework. Depending on your recovery requirements, you can:
l Perform a full disaster recovery to rebuild the entire cluster. l Restore an individual node as a standalone PostgreSQL instance. l Convert a standalone instance back into an HA-managed cluster. Recover a Patroni-Managed PostgreSQL Cluster (Disaster Recovery) When recovering a Patroni-managed PostgreSQL cluster, Cohesity restores data to a single node (the first node defined in the source registration). After the restore, you must manually rebuild the remaining standby and replica nodes to re-form the Patroni cluster.
Note: While this section uses Patroni as a reference, the recovery procedures described here are applicable to any PostgreSQL HA cluster deployment. Adjust the commands and configuration paths as needed for your specific setup.
The overall disaster recovery workflow consists of three phases:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

l Pre-Restore l Restore l Post-Restore
Pre-Restore
Before restoring the Patroni cluster, perform the following steps: 1. Stop Patroni on all nodes: systemctl stop patroni 2. Remove the old cluster state from the Distributed Configuration Store (DCS): patronictl -c /etc/patroni.yml remove <cluster-name>
Note: Replace <cluster-name> with the name of your Patroni cluster. The Patroni configuration file path may vary based on your installation.
3. Identify the restore target node. Cohesity restores to the first node defined in the source registration's hostname field. To restore to a different node, update the source registration and move the preferred node to the first position in the hostname list before initiating the restore.
Restore (Single Identified Node)
Recover the PostgreSQL data using a Regular Restore to the original location. Follow the standard restore procedure described in the Recover using Regular Restore to the Original Location topic.
Note: Only PITR (point-in-time recovery) restores are supported for Patronimanaged PostgreSQL deployments.
Post-Restore (Recover Standby and Replica Nodes)
After the restore completes successfully on the identified node, perform the following steps to rebuild the Patroni cluster:
1. Stop the PostgreSQL instance that was started by Cohesity during recovery: pg_ctl stop -D <data-directory> -m fast Example: pg_ctl stop -D /var/lib/pgsql/16/data -m fast
2. Start Patroni on the restored node only:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

systemctl start patroni 3. Verify that the restored node has assumed the Leader role:
patronictl -c /etc/patroni.yml list Expected output shows the restored node as Leader in running state. 4. Rebuild each standby or replica node:
Note: Perform on all nodes that were NOT restored.
1. Stop Patroni (confirm it is stopped): systemctl stop patroni
2. Remove the old PostgreSQL data directory contents: rm -rf <data-directory>/*
Important: This command permanently deletes all data in the specified directory. Verify the correct path before executing.
3. Start Patroni to trigger automatic replica rebuild: systemctl start patroni
Note: Wait at least 10 seconds before starting Patroni on the next standby node. It is recommended to verify the node has joined the cluster using 'patronictl list' before proceeding to the next node.
5. Verify the complete cluster is operational: patronictl -c /etc/patroni.yml list The output should show all member nodes with their respective roles (Leader, Replica) and a running state.
Restore a Patroni Node as Standalone PostgreSQL You can restore a backup from a Patroni-managed source to a standalone PostgreSQL instance. This is useful when you need to recover data without rebuilding the full Patroni cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

Pre-Restore
1. Remove the target node from the Patroni source registration: Update the PostgreSQL Source Configuration to remove the node you plan to restore as standalone.
2. Register the node as a standalone PostgreSQL source: Follow the standard source registration procedure in Register PostgreSQL as a Source.
3. Stop Patroni on the target node only: systemctl stop patroni
Restore
Restore to the alternate host by selecting the standalone source registered in the prerestore step. Follow the standard procedure in the Recover using Regular Restore to a New Location topic.
Note: Only PITR (point-in-time recovery) restores are supported for Patronimanaged PostgreSQL deployments.
Convert a Standalone PostgreSQL Instance Back to Patroni After restoring a Patroni node as a standalone PostgreSQL instance, you can convert it back to a Patroni-managed cluster using the following procedure:
1. Stop Patroni on all cluster nodes: systemctl stop patroni
2. Remove the old cluster state from the DCS: patronictl -c /etc/patroni.yml remove <cluster-name>
3. Stop the restored standalone PostgreSQL database: pg_ctl stop -D <data-directory> -m fast
4. Start Patroni on the restored node only: systemctl start patroni
5. Verify the restored node is the Leader: patronictl -c /etc/patroni.yml list
6. Rebuild each standby/replica node: Perform the following on all nodes that were NOT restored:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 13: Databases

PostgreSQL

1. Stop Patroni: systemctl stop patroni
2. Remove old data directory contents: rm -rf <data-directory>/*
3. Start Patroni: systemctl start patroni
Note: Wait at least 10 seconds before starting Patroni on the next node.
7. Verify the complete cluster: patronictl -c /etc/patroni.yml list
8. Update the source registration: 1. Remove the standalone PostgreSQL source that was registered during the prerestore steps. 2. Add the restored node back as a hostname under the original Patroni source registration. See Update the PostgreSQL Source Configuration.

SMB DFS Referral The Cohesity SMB client now follows the Distributed File System (DFS) referral. The Distributed File System has a collection of shares on different machines that serve a file system namespace. If one machine does not have a particular file requested by the client, it is referred to check the other machine. Users can now backup the entire DFS namespace by simply registering the share with the hostname directly as a Generic NAS SMB mount point.
Note: Before the 6.8 version, registering each share as a Generic NAS source and backing it up in a Protection Group was suggested by Cohesity support as a workaround in some cases. After the upgrade, the Cohesity cluster may end up backing up the same data multiple times causing data bloat and an increase in the run time.
If you are using this method, then you should contact Cohesity Support to transition to the SMB DFS Referral method.

Automatic Denylisting in NAS Sources
When connecting to a NAS source's IP address, network issues such as timeouts can result in backup failures. Cohesity now supports implementation of automatic denylisting of problematic IP addresses associated with a NAS source. This feature aims to prevent NAS protection jobs from failing due to specific IPs or interfaces becoming unreachable or having limited bandwidth, ensuring smoother backup operations.

Protect NAS
NAS Protection Group captures snapshots and these snapshots are required for the following tasks:
l Recover volumes l Replicate snapshots l Archive snapshots l Files and folders recovery (CloudArchive Direct)

16. Pre & Post Scripts: Toggle Enable to run scripts on a Unix server before and/or after a Protection Group runs. If configured, scripts are run every time an object (or entity) is backed by a protection run. For example if there are five mount/shares that are backed up as part of the NAS Protection Group and the Pre Script is configured, then five instances of the Pre Script is executed in parallel. You can distinguish between the scripts that are run on the different objects (entities) using the COHESITY_BACKUP_ENTITY environment variable. The Cohesity cluster populates this environment variable with the name of the backed object (or entity).
Note: The specified Unix server does not need to be attached to the NAS target, it just needs to be a Linux VM or machine that can either invoke APIs on or ssh in to a NAS target.
Configure the settings for running the Pre and Post scripts.

Hostname or IP Address (Unix only): Specify either the hostname or the IP address of the remote Unix server where the script will run. (Only Unix is currently supported.)
Cluster SSH Public Key: Click Copy Key to Clipboard to copy the entire string including the ssh-rsa string preceding the key, the public key and the username@cluster_name string after the key. Open the authorized_keys file (typically located in the ~/.ssh directory) and paste the entire string to the end of the file.
Username: Specify the username on the remote Unix machine that will execute the script. The username must match the username specified in the authorized_keys file.
You can configure a Pre-Script, a Post-Script or both scripts.
Pre-Script
l Script Full Path: Specify the full path and name of the script to run. A script matching the specified name must be available in the specified directory. The script can be in any format, such as a shell script or executable. The script must be configured with the permissions to allow execution (+x).
Important: Cohesity does not validate the content of the script and is not responsible for the content of the script or any actions done by the script. You must verify the script actions before a script or executable is run.
l Script Params: Optional field for passing one or more parameters to the script. All specified parameter values are passed as a single string to the script.
l Timeout: Optional field for specifying how long a script is allowed to execute before the Cohesity cluster stops the execution of the script. By default, the timeout is 15 minutes. If no value is specified, there is no timeout and the script is not stopped. This can cause a protection run to hang if the script never completes. The timeout is applied from the moment the script starts. For example, if the timeout is set to 15 minutes but the script takes 20 minutes to complete, it will be stopped after 15 minutes. Therefore, users should set the timeout based on the expected runtime of the script to avoid premature termination.
l Continue Backup if script fails: This toggle applies only to Pre-Scripts and is enabled by default. When this toggle is enabled, the Protection Group backs up the objects even if the Pre-Script fails. If this toggle is disabled and the PreScript fails, the backup is canceled but the Post-Script still runs.
Post-Script

Important: Cohesity does not validate the content of the script and is not responsible for the content of the script or any actions done by the script. You must verify the script actions before a script or executable is run.

More about failures, cancellations and logging:
l If the backup is successful but the Pre-Script or Post-Script fails, a warning is issued with the script error. A script failure occurs for any of the following conditions:
l script is not found in the expected location
l script cannot be executed
l script returns a failure return code of non-zero
A script is successful when the return code is 0.
l If a Post-Script is configured, the script always executes even if the backup fails.
l If a protection run is canceled, all subsequent phases are canceled. l For example, if a protection run is canceled while the Pre-Script is running, the Pre-Script is canceled, then the backup task is canceled and then the Post-Script is canceled. l For example, if a protection run is canceled while the backup task is running, the backup task is canceled and then the Post-Script is canceled.

17. Skip Files on Errors: Toggled on by default. The Protection Group continues to run even if it encounters errors on files, such as permissions errors. If files are skipped, the protection run details page indicates a warning status and provides additional information. If toggled off, the Protection Group stops when it encounters an error.
18. Encryption: Toggle on this option to enable in-flight encryption of data traffic between the Cohesity cluster and external NAS source while backing up NFS AND SMB Volumes. This option is disabled by default.
Note: Encrypting in-flight data will have a minor impact on the performance. To use the encryption functionality for NFS volumes, you must join the Cohesity cluster to the active directory as the Kerberos server or add the Kerberos provider in the Cohesity cluster Access Management section.
19. File DataLock: Toggle on this option to preserve the access time of the files and folders of the selected volumes. The access time provides the lock period of the files and folders that are applied when these files and folders are recovered to the Cohesity View. For more information on File DataLock, see NAS File DataLock. Select one of the following DataLock modes: l Compliance: In this mode, files and folders cannot be deleted or modified during the retention period. After the lock expires, no user can modify the files folder. However, a root user can delete the files and folders. Only a user with Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Compliance mode.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Create a Protection Group for NAS Volumes

l Enterprise: In this mode, files and folders cannot be modified by any user before or after the lock retention period expiration. However, a root user can delete the files and folders before or after the lock retention period. An admin user or a user with a Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Enterprise mode. This mode is useful for giving storage administrators additional control over the file.
You can further configure the File DataLock settings to:
l Set the lock period for the new files and folders created on the recovered Cohesity View
Provide the following information to set the lock period for the new files and folders that will be created on the recovered Cohesity View. These settings are not applicable to the existing NAS source files and folders recovered on the Cohesity View.
l Default Lock Period: Provide the time period during which the files should remain locked. When the time period ends, files can be deleted but not changed. By default, the files are locked forever.
l Autolock Files: By enabling this option, the files are automatically locked if they are not modified in the time period you specify. By default, this option is disabled.
l Manually Lock Using: Select when the files are to be locked:
l Read-Only: Select this option to lock files when the file permission is set to read only, for example; by setting the Windows file properties attribute or using the Linux chmod command. By default, the files are locked when the file permission is set to read only.
l FutureATime: Select this option to lock files when the last access time (atime) is set, for example, by using Windows PowerShell commands or the Linux touch command.
Optionally you can set a Minimum Retention and/or a Maximum Retention period to ensure that a file's last access time cannot be set outside this period. A request to do so results in a permission denied error if the manual locking mode is FutureATime. Otherwise, the request will be silently rejected and the file will be locked for the minimum retention duration.
l Override the locking period of the existing files and folders recovered on the Cohesity View:
The following option can be applied to all the existing files and folders that will be recovered on the Cohesity View.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Create a Protection Group for NAS Volumes

l Override (Lock all files until a specific date ): Enable this option and select a date to override the locking period of the existing files and folders. When you recover the files to the Cohesity View, Cohesity applies the farthest lock period between the override lock period you specify and the source file's lock period. For example; l The lock period of the source file is 09/09/2023 and the override lock period you specified is 09/08/2022. When you recover the file to the Cohesity View, then the lock period of the source file is applied to the recovered file, which is 09/09/2023. l The lock period of the source file is 09/09/2022 and the override lock period you specified is 09/08/2024. When you recover the file to the Cohesity View, then the override lock period you specified is applied to the recovered file, which is 09/08/2024. In Compliance mode, a user with Data Security privileges can extend the override date into the future, but no user can shorten the date. In Enterprise mode, a user with admin or Data Security privileges can extend or shorten the override date.
Note: l You cannot enable or disable File DataLock once the Protection Group is created.
l If you have disabled File DataLock while creating a Protection Group, then when you edit this Protection Group, the File DataLock option will not be displayed.
l You can delete Protection Groups and Snapshots having File DataLock enabled.
File DataLock also preserves the ATimes of the hardlinks and symlinks.

21. Exclusions and Inclusions: Everything is included by default. Toggle on Exclusions and Inclusions if you want to exclude or include locations. By creating exclusion and inclusion rules, you can limit the Protection Group to a specific set of files and directories and therefore minimize the disk space used to store the data.
Note: To add an exclusion or inclusion, you must prefix a forward slash (`/') or suffix an asterisk (`*') to the path or to a particular file within the protected object. For example, `/test' or `*.txt'.
Add Inclusion: Click to include a particular path or a particular file within the protected object. For example, consider four directories - test, test1, test2, and test3 under the protected object with path /ifs/TestShare1/Folder1. The table below lists the input types for an inclusion list of folders and their respective outcome:

Input /

Outcome
Everything inside the protection path is backed up, if exclusions are not defined.

Input /test
/test/

Outcome
When the inclusion path is not suffixed by '/', Protection Group will include all folders starting from the protection path. In this example, /test will behave as /test* and Protection Group will include 'test', 'test1', 'test2', and 'test3' from protection path for backup.
When inclusion path is suffixed by '/' , it will only include specific folder. In this example, /test/ behaves as /test/* and Protection Group will only include 'test' from protection path for backup.

Note: Do not provide the folder name along with the backup path while including files and folders for a Protection Group. The backup path is considered by default. For example, /ifs/TestShare1/Folder1/test does not include any folder.
If exclusions are defined, they will take precedence over inclusions.

22. Indexing: Toggle on this option to index the data of the Protection Group. Indexing improves files and folders search. Cohesity performs incremental indexing where only the data that has changed since the previous snapshot is scanned and indexed. You can add custom indexing rules.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Create a Protection Group for NAS Volumes

By default, a rule to include the root directory (/) is defined and therefore by default the entire file system is indexed. When a directory is indexed, all of the child subdirectories are also indexed. (Indexing is recursive.)
By creating exclusion and inclusion rules, you can limit indexing to a specific set of files and directories and therefore minimizing the disk space used to store the index. For example, you could add two additional rules to the first default rule:
l include /
l exclude /var
l include /var/log
In this example, all files in the / root directory are indexed except the files found in the /var directory. However, the files in the /var/log are indexed because there is an explicit include rule.
23. Quiet Time: This option is available only if the selected policy has at least one quiet time period. Toggle the Stop in-progress runs when quiet time starts option to pause or abort the runs during quiet time. If this option is toggled off, after a protection run starts, execution continues even when the quiet time period specified for this Protection Group starts. However, a new protection run will not start during a quiet time period.
l Pause Runs - Select this option to pause the currently executing protection runs and resume the runs when quiet time ends.
l Abort Runs - Select this option to abort the currently executing protection runs when the quiet time period specified for the Protection Group starts.
Note: If the quiet time window for multiple protection runs is scheduled at the same time, then when the protection run is resumed, prioritization of the protection run does not work
24. Alerts: Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:
l Success: Create an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Create a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
For more information, see Alerts.

25. Priority: Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity supports concurrent backups, but if the number of Protection Groups exceeds the ability to process them, those with High priority are given the highest priority to execute, Medium the second-highest priority, and Low the lowest priority.
26. Email Recipients: You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the Protection Group.
Note: The connection to the SMTP Server must be enabled to send email notification. You can enable the SMTP Server connection in the configuration settings page ( Cohesity UI > Settings > Summary > Configure > Enable SMTP Server).
27. SLA: The service-level agreement (SLA) defines the expected time to complete either a full backup or incremental backup. The backup completion time depends on the Windows volume size on AD, objects changed between incremental backups, network speed, and other Protection Groups running on the Cohesity cluster. l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental protection run to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last protection run. l Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup protection run to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).

Add NAS to the Protection Group
You can add new NAS volumes to the existing Protection Group for backup. The newly added NAS volumes are backed up from the next protection run and it will be a full backup. Perform the following steps to add NAS volumes to the Protection Group:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you created for NAS. 3. Click the Actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit.
4. On the Edit Protection page, in the Object field, click the edit icon. 5. Select the NAS volume you want to add to the Protection Group. 6. Click Save Selection > Save. The newly added NAS volumes are backed in the next scheduled protection run.
Remove NAS from the Protection Group
From the Edit Protection page, you can remove NAS volumes from the Protection Group that you do not want to back up in the next protection run. Perform the following steps to remove NAS volumes from the Protection Group:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you created for NAS. 3. Click the Actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit.
4. On the Edit Protection page, in the Object field, click the edit icon. 5. Unselect the NAS volume you want to remove from the Protection Group. 6. Click Save Selection > Save.
Enable or Disable Auto Protect
The Auto Protect option enables you to automatically protect the new NAS volumes that are added to the selected parent NAS server. However, you cannot enable auto-protect at the server-level containing both Read-Write volumes and Data-Protect volumes. Perform the following steps to enable auto protect:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you created for NAS. 3. Click the Actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit.
4. On the Edit Protection page, in the Object field, click the edit icon.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Delete the Protection Group
You can delete a Protection Group if you:

l Want to reclaim the storage space utilized by the Protection Group.
Cohesity provides the following ways to delete a Protection Group:
l Delete Protection Group Only: Delete only the Protection Group. Any local snapshots and or archived snapshots stored on the external targets that were captured by this Protection Group are not deleted.
l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots: Delete the Protection Group and all snapshots, any local snapshots captured by this Protection Group and stored on this cluster are deleted. In addition, any archived snapshots stored on external targets that were captured by this Protection Group are also deleted.

options: l Delete Protection Group Only l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots
If the current Protection Group is replicating snapshots to a remote cluster or archiving snapshots to an external target, you should cancel these replication or archive tasks before deleting the Protection Group. For instructions, see Cancel Replication and Archive Copy Tasks of a Protection Run. If the Protection Group is replicating to a remote cluster, the failover job created on the remote cluster is not deleted. In addition, the snapshots that were replicated (copied) to the remote cluster by this job are not deleted. You can log in to the remote cluster to delete the snapshots and the failover job.

NAS File DataLock
Many organizations now rely on WORM (Write Once Read Many) data storage such as Nutanix Files, NetApp Snaplock, and Isilon Smartlock volumes to retain their files and folders in unmodified form for compliance and regulatory purposes and to protect the files from accidental deletion or modification.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

NAS File DataLock

When you backup these WORM-capable volumes to the Cohesity cluster, it is essential to have the ability to easily lock the files and folders of the volumes while protecting themselves from accidental or malicious attempts to delete or modify these files. The backup should also provide a strong guarantee for data non-mutability and non-erasability for a certain period of time.
This capability is achieved using Cohesity's File DataLock feature.
FileDataLock is a Cohesity feature that preserves the WORM attributes of any files and folders created in the Cohesity View. You can apply the File DataLock feature for NAS backup (NFS exports and SMB shares) while creating a NAS Protection Group.
With File DataLock enabled in a NAS Protection Group, Cohesity preserves the future AccessTime (ATime) of the files and folders. The AccessTime provides the lock period for files and folders. You can also override this lock period in the File DataLock settings of the NAS Protection Group. This lock period is applied to these files and folders when they are recovered to the Cohesity View. This prevents the users or administrator from modifying or deleting these locked files until the locking period expires.
You can also set lock periods for the new files and folders created on recovered Cohesity View in the File DataLock settings of the NAS Protection Group.
When you recover File DataLock enabled storage volumes to the Cohesity View, the View details page will display a lock icon for the files and folders having File DataLock.
File DataLock is supported for all types of NAS sources including NetApp 7-mode and is agnostic of the NAS protocol.
For information on how to enable File DataLock, see Protect NAS.
File DataLock Modes
You can use the File DataLock feature in one of the two modes:
l Compliance mode: The WORM files are protected at the disk level. This mode implements strict regulatory requirements for data retention and complies with SEC Rule 17a-4. In this mode, files and folders cannot be deleted or modified during the retention period. After the lock expires, no user can modify the files and folders. However, a root user can delete the files and folders. Only a user with a Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Compliance mode.
l Enterprise mode: The WORM files are protected at the file level. This mode does not implement strict regulatory requirements for data retention. In this mode, files and folders cannot be modified by any user before or after the lock retention period expiration. However, a root user can delete the files and folders during or after the lock retention period. An admin user or a user with the Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Enterprise mode

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

NetApp ONTAP

Note: An admin user or a user with the Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings and switch from the Enterprise mode to Compliance mode. But switching from Compliance mode to Enterprise mode is not supported.
Things to remember for File DataLock
l You cannot enable or disable File DataLock once the View is created. l If you have disabled File DataLock while creating a Protection Group, then when you
edit this Protection Group, the File DataLock option will not be displayed. l You can delete Protection Groups and snapshots having File DataLock enabled.
File DataLock also preserves the ATimes of the hardlinks and symlinks.
l Recovery l Recovering a File DataLock enabled backed-up volume as a Cohesity View will preserve ATimes and the locking period for the file. l Recovering a File DataLock enabled volume to the original location with `Overwrite existing files/folder' as the recovery option will encounter an error if the files and folders are read-only. However, the ATime and other attributes of other files and folders of the source volumes are preserved. l Recovering a File DataLock enabled volume to an alternate NAS recovery will preserve ATimes and other attributes of files and folders of the source volumes. l Cloning a recovered View having File DataLock enabled will not inherit the File DataLock properties.
l Replication When you replicate to a remote Cohesity cluster, the File DataLock settings are also replicated.
l Archival File DataLock settings are preserved when you recover volume from an archived snapshot whose Protection Group has File Datalock enabled, to a Cohesity View.
l Cloud Archive Direct File DataLock settings are preserved when you recover from a Cloud ArchiveDirect snapshot whose Protection Group has File Datalock enabled, to a Cohesity View.
NetApp ONTAP
NetApp ONTAP is a hardware and software-based data storage and retrieval system. It responds to network requests from clients and fulfills them by writing data to or retrieving data from its disk array.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

NetApp ONTAP

You can backup and recovery NetApp ONTAP volumes using the following two backup approaches:
l Cohesity File-Runner based backup approach: Cohesity uses the Cohesity's built-in CFT method to protect data. In this method, Cohesity uses its internal FileRunner to discover the delta between two snapshot copies.
l NetApp SnapDiff-based backup approach: Cohesity leverages NetApp's SnapMirror cloud functionality to move the data to the Cohesity cluster and NetApp's SnapDiff functionality to get the changed file list.
Note: l In this document, NetApp SnapDiff means Cohesity's implementation of SnapDiff using NetApp SnapDiff v3 APIs.
Supplemental terms regarding the Cohesity implementation of the SnapDiff API. Please review before use.
NetApp ONTAP File-Runner Based Backup
In the Cohesity File-Runner based backup approach for NetApp ONTAP, Cohesity uses the Cohesity's built-in CFT method to protect data. In this method, Cohesity uses its internal File-Runner to discover the delta between two snapshot copies.
Plan and Prepare for File-Runner Based NetApp ONTAP Backup
This topic provides information on the supported NetApp ONTAP versions and volumes, minimum permissions, and the prerequisites to register and protect NetApp ONTAP with Cohesity cluster. For more information, see Register NetApp ONTAP. Before you register your NetApp ONTAP with Cohesity cluster and protect the volumes and data, ensure the following prerequisites:
l The Storage Virtual Machines (SVMs) that you plan to protect must have: l an active logical interface attached to the SVM. l the NFS and CIFS services configured on the SVM.
l The Cohesity cluster requires access to the snapshot directory on ONTAP. This access is enabled by default. However, it is recommended to verify that it is enabled in your environment. 1. To check the access status of the snapshot directory, run the following command:
volume show -vserver -volume -fields snapdir-access
Example output, where volume name is vol1:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

NetApp ONTAP

clus1::> volume show -vserver vs0 -volume vol1 -fields snapdiraccess

vserver vs0

volume vol1

snapdir-access true

2. If the snapshot directory access is False, enable it using the following command:
volume modify -vserver <SVM_name> -volume <vol_name> -snapdiraccess true
Example output, where volume name is vol1:
clus1::> volume modify -vserver vs0 -volume vol1 -snapdir-access true
Volume modify successful on volume vol1 of Vserver vs0. For more information about performing these changes through the ONTAP System Manager console, see the NetApp documentation. l The Allow Superuser Access check box is selected in export policy to register SVM with the Cohesity cluster. l Read or write or full control permissions are added under Share Access Control for the registered SMB user, for the volume share being backed up using the SMB protocol. l The required firewall ports are open to enable communication between Cohesity cluster and NetApp ONTAP. l If volume export policies are not in use, but export policies are applied at the Qtree level, Cohesity IP addresses must be manually added to the Qtree-level export policies to ensure proper access. l Review and understand the considerations and best practices.

Minimum Permissions
Ensure you have the required minimum permissions to register NetApp ONTAP as a source with the Cohesity cluster, and to perform backup and recovery.
Minimum Permissions for Registering NetApp ONTAP
The user account used for registering NetApp ONTAP SVM or NetApp ONTAP Cluster must have the required permissions to communicate with the Cohesity cluster. The following user-role types are used for File-Runner-based NetApp ONTAP Backup:
l ONTAPI (Legacy) l HTTP
You can assign a role to the NetApp user which specifies permission for the user. The role type can be either REST or Zephyr Application Programming Interface (ZAPI) permissions role. You can configure both these roles from the NetApp UI.
l REST role: Using the REST permission role, you can specify permissions using the NetApp REST APIs. You can use the REST role to specify permissions for both ZAPI and REST APIs.
l ZAPI ONTAPI role (Legacy): Using the ZAPI permission role, you can specify permissions using the NetApp CLI commands or ZAPI calls. It is a legacy role and is used for ZAPI API permissions only.

Minimum Permissions for SMB/CIFS Shares Backup and Recovery
To backup NetApp ONTAP SMB/CIFS shares to the Cohesity cluster, the user must have local or domain user credentials that allow at least read access to the SMB share. To recover the SMB/CIFS shares from the Cohesity cluster, the local or domain user must have full access control on the target where data is being restored. You can assign the following privileges to the user:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

NetApp ONTAP

l SeBackupPrivilege to the SMB user to be able to back up the SMB data without modifying the ACL on the SMB shares.
l SeRestorePrivilege to restore files and directories, override any ACLs, and set a valid user or group SID as the file owner.
l SeChangeNotifyPrivilege to bypass traverse checking. Users with this privilege are not required to have traverse (x) permissions to traverse folders, symlinks, or junctions.
Minimum Permissions for NFS Export Backup and Recovery
To backup NFS export, the user must have the read and superuser access permissions on the NFS volume that needs to be backed up and on the parent root volume. Before starting the backup, Cohesity verifies if the user has these permissions, if not, the Cohesity cluster adds a new rule index for the Cohesity node subnet in the export policy attached to the backup volume. You must add the permissions manually for the Cohesity node subnet for the parent root volume. To restore NFS export, the user needs the read/write and superuser access permissions on the NFS volume that needs to be restored. Before starting the restore, you must add a new rule index for the Cohesity node subnet in the export policy attached to the source volume and parent root volume to give permissions to the Cohesity node subnet/IPs.
Permissions for NTFS Trees on UNIX Security Style Volumes
When you protect NetApp volumes that use a UNIX security style and contain NTFS trees by using File Runner-based backups, the SMB service must have Read access to the CIFS c$ share on the SVM. This access is required because the File Runner workflow accesses the SVM root context during entity discovery. For restore scenarios that involve full volume recreation or operations that require Write access at the SVM root level, the SMB account must have Full Control permissions on the c$ share.
Credentials for NetApp ONTAP Backup with Multiple SVMs
To register NetApp ONTAP with multiple storage virtual machine (SVM), create a custom role with the required permissions and a local user at the SVM level. Assign the custom role to the local user. Use the respective local user account to register multiple SVMs.
Ports Used for Communication
For information on port numbers required, see Manage Firewall Ports.
Best Practices
Cohesity protects NetApp ONTAP volumes by communicating with a NetApp ONTAP cluster or Storage Virtual Machine (SVM). As a security best practice, you must enable SSL before registering the cluster or SVM as a source on the Cohesity cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

NetApp ONTAP

To enable SSL, run the following ONTAP CLI commands on your NetApp ONTAP cluster:
1. To verify the settings, run the following command:
netapp_cluster::> security ssl show -vserver <cluster/vservername>
2. To enable SSL, run the following command:
netapp_cluster::> security ssl modify -vserver <cluster/vservername> server-enabled true
3. After enabling SSL, run the following command to verify the settings:
netapp_cluster::> security ssl show -vserver <cluster/vservername>.
Considerations
Review and understand the following considerations before you protect your NetApp ONTAP data:
l The NAS storage FQDN must be resolvable. Even if registered by IP, SMB restore workflows depend on the FQDN for repeated SMB share connections. Ensure that the DNS or cluster host mapping resolves the storage FQDN.
l Instant Volume Mount for NetApp ONTAP stub file is not supported. l You cannot restore the NetApp Data-Protect volume to the original location or to an
alternate Data-Protect volume because the Data-Protect volume is a read-only volume. l To backup NetApp DP volumes with SMB share, the volume needs to be in the junction path on the NetApp. l Cohesity skips the backup of the following security style Qtrees:
l Mixed-mode security style Qtrees l UNIX security style Qtree when root volume security style is NTFS. l Volume recovery: The restored volume (target volume) should have the same security style as that of the volume being protected. When volumes with Qtrees are recovered and the Qtrees have a different export policy than the parent volume, update the export policy on the recovered Qtrees to match the original Qtrees. l If volume export policies are not in use, but export policies are applied at the Qtree level, Cohesity IP addresses must be manually added to the Qtree-level export policies to ensure proper access. l Recovering files/folders with Qtrees: The security style of the location (target) to which the files or folders are restored should have the same security style as the restored files and folders.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

NetApp ONTAP

l Cohesity supports the backup of the symbolic link reparse point, IO_REPARSE_ TAG_SYMLINK in an SMB share.
l Cohesity recommends a first full and incremental forever backup approach to back up your NAS sources.
l When browsing files or folders for recovery, Cohesity does not display files or folders with an absolute path length exceeding approximately 3,500 characters. To recover these files or folders, select the parent directory.
The following are the considerations for NetApp NFSv4.1 volumes: l Encryption is not supported. l Kerberos is not supported. l If the NFS backup preference selected in the Cohesity UI is NFSv4.1, and if the NetApp Vserver has NFSv4.1 disabled, all the volumes belonging to this Vserver will use the NFSv3 protocol for backup. l Recovering an NFS 4.1 volume to NFSv3 is not supported. l Recovering an NFS 4.1 volume to the Cohesity View is not supported.

Backup NetApp ONTAP Using File-Runner

After registering your NetApp ONTAP server as a source on the Cohesity cluster, you can create a Protection Group to backup NetApp ONTAP. You can backup one or more NetApp ONTAP NFS or SMB shares in a Protection Group while preserving ACLs on SMB.

Select NetApp ONTAP Volumes for Backup

Cohesity supports the backup of both NetApp ONTAP read-write (RW) and data protection (DP) volumes. NetApp ONTAP DP volumes are read-only volumes which are used as destination volumes for NetApp ONTAP's replication applications such as SnapMirror and SnapVault. These applications replicate data from NetApp ONTAP primary source volumes to NetApp secondary destination DP volumes. The volume can be of NFS export only, SMB share only, or of both NFS and SMB (mixed) type. Based on the volume and protocol you select for backup, you must provide additional information when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Protect NetApp ONTAP Using File-Runner Based Backup.

Note: The file-runner is supported on the NetApp Storage Virtual Machine (SVM) and Storage Virtual Machine for Disaster Recovery (SVM-DR).

The following table lists the additional information required to perform backup based on the volume type and protocol you choose while creating a Protection Group:

Considerations
l You cannot select both RW and DP volumes in the same Protection Group. For example, in a Protection Group, if you select a RW volume, then you cannot select another volume with the DP mode.
l If you are selecting the objects to be backed up at a NetApp ONTAP cluster-level or server-level having both RW volumes and DP volumes, then RW volumes will take precedence over data protection volumes. That is, only RW volumes of the NetApp ONTAP server will be selected for the backup.

Chapter 14: NAS

NetApp ONTAP

l You cannot enable auto-protect at the server-level containing both RW volumes and data protection volumes.
l The snapshot prefix setting is applicable to both DP and RW volumes. However, Cohesity will only implement these settings on DP volumes.
l To backup NetApp DP volumes with NFS/SMB share, the volume needs to be in the junction path on the NetApp.
Snapshot Prefix for DP Volumes
Cohesity cannot create snapshots of the NetApp data protection volume because it is a read-only volume. Therefore, for backing up NetApp data protection volume, Cohesity DataPlatform leverages the existing snapshots present in the DP volume that are replicated from the NetApp ONTAP source volume to the DP volume. When creating a Protection Group, you can select one of the following options and provide the required information to leverage the existing snapshots present in the DP volume:
l None: By selecting this option, Cohesity will take the full backup from the oldest snapshot available on the DP volume and incremental backup from the latest snapshots available on the DP volume.
l Snapshot Prefix: By selecting this option, Cohesity will take the full and incremental backup from the snapshots that have the prefix name you specify.
l Incremental snapshot label
The prefix of the snapshot name present in the DP volume from which the Cohesity cluster can take incremental backup. If there are multiple snapshots that match the specified name, then theCohesity cluster will take the backup from the latest snapshot. The create time of this latest snapshot should be later than the create time of the snapshot that was last used in the most recent backup.
If the snapshot label specified in the Protection Group is not present in the DP volume, then the following error message appears when you run the Protection Group:
No snapshot with label: <label_name> found in the volume: <DP_ volume_name> on vserver <NAS_server_name>. Cohesity discovers snapshots for DataProtect volumes and use existing snapshots for taking backups. Please verify the labels for the snapshot provided.
l Full snapshot label: The prefix of the snapshot name present in the DP volume from which theCohesity cluster can take the first full backup. If there are multiple snapshots that match the specified name, then the Cohesity cluster will take the backup from the latest snapshot. For example, if you specify the prefix name of snapshot label as weekly and in the DP volume there are three snapshots with labels, weekly1, weekly2, and weekly3 (latest snapshot), then

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

NetApp ONTAP

the Cohesity cluster will take the first full backup from the latest snapshot, which is weekly3.
Considerations
l When creating the SnapMirror policy to replicate the source volume to the DP volume, ensure to provide the snapshot retention period depending on the size of the volume you backup.
l Since Cohesity does not create and manage the snapshots present in the DP volume, you must ensure that the snapshot label of the DP volume you specified does not get deleted within the backup duration you configured in the protection policy.
l When assigning or creating backup policies to a Protection Group for DP volumes, it is recommended to create the schedule of backup policy in-sync or less aggressive than the SnapMirror or SnapVault schedule. This ensures the presence of the snapshot in the DP volume, prior to the incremental backup triggered by Cohesity backup policy schedule.
l When creating snapshots for DP volume backup, ensure not to use the same prefixes that are automatically generated by NetApp SnapMirror.
User Access Credentials to Back Up SMB Shares
To back up SMB shares of any volume type, you must provide the local or Active Directory user credentials that allow at least read access to the NetApp ONTAP SMB share. You can provide these credentials while registering the NetApp ONTAP server with the Cohesity cluster or later when creating the Protection Group. For more information, see, Register and Manage NetApp ONTAP Source.
Backup Preferences For Mixed Mode Volumes
If the volume you plan to backup is exposed to both NFS export and SMB share, then you must choose how you want the Cohesity cluster to backup that volume while creating the Protection Group. Cohesity will backup the ACLs according to the selected backup preference.
If you select NFS as the preference mode, then the SMB access control lists (ACLs) would be lost and only the NFS POSIX ACLs will be backed up.
If you select SMB as the preference mode, then the NFS POSIX ACLs would be lost and only the SMB ACLs will be backed up.
Backup Preferences for NFS Volumes
If you select NFS as the preference mode and the selected volume has:
l NFSv3 enabled, then the SMB ACLs will be lost and only the NFS POSIX ACLs will be backed up.
l NFSv3 and NFSv4.1 enabled, then you can choose to use NFSv4.1 to back up the volume. If you choose NFSv4.1, then the SMB ACLs will be lost, and the NFSv4.1 ACLs

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

NetApp ONTAP

will be backed up. However, if you do not toggle the "Use NFSv4.1 protocol for NFS volumes" option on the Cohesity Dashboard, then only the NFS POSIX ACLs will be backed up. l NFSv4.1 enabled (NFSv3 disabled), the backup will be performed using NFSv4.1 automatically and the Use NFSv4.1 protocol for NFS volumes toggle option will not be available on the Cohesity Dashboard.
Note: NetApp NFSv4.1 volumes are supported from the Cohesity 6.6.0d version onwards. To enable this feature, contact Cohesity Support.

Protect NetApp ONTAP Using File-Runner Based Backup
In Cohesity, NetApp ONTAP volumes are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, archived, or replicated. A Protection Policy is a reusable set of settings that define how and when objects are protected and replicated. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy. This topic provides information on how to protect NetApp ONTAP volumes using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy:
l Protect Data Protection Volumes with Only SMB Share or NFS Export l Protect Data Protection Volumes with Both NFS and SMB Share (Mixed Mode) l Protect Read-Write volumes with Only SMB Share or NFS Export l Protect Read-Write Volumes with Both NFS and SMB Share (Mixed Mode) l Protect Snapshots of VMware VMs stored in NetApp NFS volumes
Note: Cohesity recommends a first full and incremental forever backup approach to back up your NAS sources.

Description
Toggle on this option to preserve the AccessTime of the files and folders of the selected volumes. The AccessTime provides the lock period of the files and folders that are applied when these files and folders are recovered to the Cohesity View.

Select one of the following DataLock modes:
l Compliance: In this mode, files or folders cannot be deleted or modified during the retention period. After the lock expires, no user can modify the files or folders. However, a root user can delete the files and folders. Only a user with Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Compliance mode.
l Enterprise: In this mode, files or folders cannot be modified by any user before or after the lock retention period expiration. However, a root user can delete the files or folders before or after the lock retention period. An admin user or a user with a Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Enterprise mode. This mode is useful for giving storage administrators additional control over the file.
You can further configure the File DataLock settings to:
l Set the lock period for the new files and folders created on the recovered Cohesity View

l Default Lock Period: Provide the time period during which the files should remain locked. When the time period ends, files can be deleted but not changed. By default, the files are locked forever.
l Autolock Files: By enabling this option, the files are automatically locked if they are not modified in the time period you specify. By default, this option is disabled.
l Manually Lock Using: Select when the files are to be locked:
l Read-Only: Select this option to lock files when the file permission is set to read only, for example; by setting the Windows file properties attribute or using the Linux chmod command. By default, the files are locked when the file permission is set to read only.
l FutureATime: Select this option to lock files when the last access time (atime) is set, for example, by using Windows PowerShell commands or the Linux touch command.

File DataLock Modes

NAS File DataLock
Many organizations now rely on WORM (Write Once Read Many) data storage such as Nutanix Files, NetApp Snaplock, and Isilon Smartlock volumes to retain their files and folders in unmodified form for compliance and regulatory purposes and to protect the files from accidental deletion or modification.
When you backup these WORM-capable volumes to the Cohesity cluster, it is essential to have the ability to easily lock the files and folders of the volumes while protecting themselves from accidental or malicious attempts to delete or modify these files. The backup should also provide a strong guarantee for data non-mutability and non-erasability for a certain period of time.
This capability is achieved using Cohesity's File DataLock feature.
FileDataLock is a Cohesity feature that preserves the WORM attributes of any files and folders created in the Cohesity View. You can apply the File DataLock feature for NAS backup (NFS exports and SMB shares) while creating a NAS Protection Group.
With File DataLock enabled in a NAS Protection Group, Cohesity preserves the future AccessTime (ATime) of the files and folders. The AccessTime provides the lock period for files and folders. You can also override this lock period in the File DataLock settings of the NAS Protection Group. This lock period is applied to these files and folders when they are recovered to the Cohesity View. This prevents the users or administrator from modifying or deleting these locked files until the locking period expires.
You can also set lock periods for the new files and folders created on recovered Cohesity View in the File DataLock settings of the NAS Protection Group.
When you recover File DataLock enabled storage volumes to the Cohesity View, the View details page will display a lock icon for the files and folders having File DataLock.
File DataLock is supported for all types of NAS sources including NetApp 7-mode and is agnostic of the NAS protocol.
For information on how to enable File DataLock, see Protect NAS.
File DataLock Modes
You can use the File DataLock feature in one of the two modes:
l Compliance mode: The WORM files are protected at the disk level. This mode implements strict regulatory requirements for data retention and complies with SEC Rule 17a-4. In this mode, files and folders cannot be deleted or modified during the retention period. After the lock expires, no user can modify the files and folders. However, a root user can delete the files and folders. Only a user with a Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Compliance mode.
l Enterprise mode: The WORM files are protected at the file level. This mode does not implement strict regulatory requirements for data retention. In this mode, files and folders cannot be modified by any user before or after the lock retention period

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Things to remember for File DataLock

expiration. However, a root user can delete the files and folders during or after the lock retention period. An admin user or a user with the Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Enterprise mode
Note: An admin user or a user with the Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings and switch from the Enterprise mode to Compliance mode. But switching from Compliance mode to Enterprise mode is not supported.

Things to remember for File DataLock
l You cannot enable or disable File DataLock once the View is created.
l If you have disabled File DataLock while creating a Protection Group, then when you edit this Protection Group, the File DataLock option will not be displayed.
l You can delete Protection Groups and snapshots having File DataLock enabled.
File DataLock also preserves the ATimes of the hardlinks and symlinks.
l Recovery l Recovering a File DataLock enabled backed-up volume as a Cohesity View will preserve ATimes and the locking period for the file. l Recovering a File DataLock enabled volume to the original location with `Overwrite existing files/folder' as the recovery option will encounter an error if the files and folders are read-only. However, the ATime and other attributes of other files and folders of the source volumes are preserved. l Recovering a File DataLock enabled volume to an alternate NAS recovery will preserve ATimes and other attributes of files and folders of the source volumes. l Cloning a recovered View having File DataLock enabled will not inherit the File DataLock properties.
l Replication
When you replicate to a remote Cohesity cluster, the File DataLock settings are also replicated.
l Archival
File DataLock settings are preserved when you recover volume from an archived snapshot whose Protection Group has File Datalock enabled, to a Cohesity View.
l Cloud Archive Direct
File DataLock settings are preserved when you recover from a Cloud ArchiveDirect snapshot whose Protection Group has File Datalock enabled, to a Cohesity View.

Add Inclusion

Exclusions and Inclusions for NAS Protection Group
In a NAS Protection Group, all the files and folders are included by default for data protection. While creating a Protection Group, you can toggle on Exclusions and Inclusions from the Advanced Settings options if you want to exclude or include locations. By creating the exclusion and inclusion rules, you can limit the Protection Group to a specific set of files and directories. As a result, you can minimize the disk space used to store the data.
Note: l To add an exclusion or inclusion rule, you must prefix a forward slash (`/') or suffix an asterisk (`*') to the path or to a particular file within the protected object. For example, `/test' or `*.txt'.
l In exclusion or inclusion rules, file names and folder names are casesensitive, which means `test.txt' and `Test.txt' are considered separate files. Use the correct capitalization of file or folder names to ensure that the rules recognize your file or folder.

Add Inclusion
From the Additional Settings options on the Protection Group page, toggle on Exclusions and Inclusions. Click Add Inclusion to include a particular path or a particular file within the protected object.
For example, consider four directories - test, test1, test2, and test3 under the protected object with path /ifs/TestShare1/Folder1. The table below lists the input types for an inclusion list of folders and their respective outcome:

Input /
/test

Outcome
Everything inside the protection path is backed up if exclusions are not defined.
When the inclusion path is not suffixed by '/', Protection Group will include all folders starting from the protection path. In this example, /test will behave as /test* and Protection Group will include 'test', 'test1', 'test2', and 'test3' from the protection path for backup.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Add Exclusion

Input /test/

Outcome
When the inclusion path is suffixed by '/', it will only include the specific folder. In this example, /test/ behaves as /test/* and Protection Group will only include 'test' from the protection path for backup.

l Do not provide the folder name along with the backup path while including files and folders for a Protection Group. The backup path is considered by default. For example, /ifs/TestShare1/Folder1/test does not include any folder.
l If exclusions are defined, they will take precedence over inclusions.

Add Exclusion
From the Additional Settings options on the Protection Group page, toggle on Exclusions and Inclusions. Click Add Exclusion to exclude a particular path or a particular file within the protected object. You can also specify regular expressions for excluding files in the format regex:<regex pattern>.
For example, consider there are three directories - Test, Test1, and Folder1 and a file, TestFile.tmp under the protected object with path /ifs/TestShare1.
l The Test1 folder has TestFile1.tmp, TestFile2.tmp files.
l The Folder1 folder has TestFile3.tmp, TestFile4.tmp files, and SubFolder1 which further has a Test folder with File.txt, File1.txt files in it.

Adaptive Backup for NetApp
Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
You can now apply a threshold on the CPU capacity utilization for the NetApp source. The Cohesity cluster will adaptively adjust the number of backup IO requests sent to the NetApp source such that the CPU capacity utilized does not exceed the set threshold. For example, if the threshold value specified is 40% and the primary workload utilizes 30% of the CPU capacity, then the Cohesity cluster will send backup IO requests so as not to exceed 40% CPU on NetApp by consuming only 10% CPU for backup. If the primary load on the NetApp now increases to 35%, then Cohesity cluster will adapt to drop its IO request to consume only 5% of CPU capacity instead of 10% of the CPU capacity. To summarize, Cohesity backup is adaptive, source aware, and sensitive to the load condition on the NetApp primary device.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Considerations

Note: Since the Cohesity cluster adaptively increases or decreases the percentage of the CPU capacity utilized for the backup operations, setting up a low CPU utilization threshold value might affect the backup duration.
Manage the NetApp ONTAP Backup Configuration
In Cohesity, a backup configuration includes a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. You can modify the existing Protection Group and the Protection Policy based on your requirement.
Note: You cannot update the registered NetApp ONTAP Server and the assigned Storage Domain in the Protection Group settings. You cannot enable or disable the NetApp SnapDiff option on an existing Protection Group.
Add NetApp ONTAP volumes to the Protection Group
You can add new NetApp ONTAP volumes to the existing Protection Group for backup. The newly added volumes are backed up from the next protection run and it will be a full backup. To add NetApp ONTAP volumes to the Protection Group:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for NetApp
ONTAP. For NetApp Snapdiff backup, select the NetApp SnapDiff-enabled Protection Group that you had created for NetApp ONTAP. 3. Click the action icon next to the Protection Group and select Edit. 4. Enable Auto Protect

ONTAP. 3. Click the action icon next to the Protection Group and select Edit. 4. On the Edit Protection page, in the Object field, click Edit Objects. 5. Click the shield icon to enable Auto Protect. 6. Click Save Selection > Save.
When this option is enabled on the parent NetApp ONTAP server, all the NetApp ONTAP volumes that are added to the parent NetApp ONTAP server in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run. For example, you create a Protection Group that backs up a NetApp ONTAP SVM. The Protection Group runs for two weeks and then a new volume is added to the NetApp ONTAP SVM. The next time the Protection Group runs, if the object hierarchy has been refreshed on the Cohesity cluster, the new volume is also backed up even though the new volume has not been explicitly selected to be included in the Protection Group. The object hierarchy is automatically refreshed every four hours. To manually refresh the object hierarchy, select Data Protection > Sources, find the source in the list, and click . NetApp ONTAP SnapDiff-based Backup
In the SnapDiff-based backup approach, Cohesity leverages NetApp's SnapMirror cloud functionality to move the data to the Cohesity cluster and NetApp's SnapDiff functionality to get the changed file list. This section provides information on how Cohesity performs the backup and recovery of NetApp ONTAP data protection (DP) and Read-Write (RW) volumes using the SnapDiff-based backup approach.
Note: In this document, NetApp SnapDiff means Cohesity's implementation of SnapDiff using NetApp SnapDiff v3 APIs.
Supplemental terms regarding the Cohesity implementation of the SnapDiff API. Please review before use.
Plan and Prepare for NetApp ONTAP SnapDiff-based Backup
This topic provides information on the supported NetApp ONTAP versions and volumes, minimum permissions, and the prerequisites to register and protect NetApp ONTAP with Cohesity cluster using SnapDiff-based backup approach. For more information, see Register NetApp ONTAP. Before you register your NetApp ONTAP with the Cohesity cluster and protect the DP volumes and read-write volumes using the NetApp SnapDiff-based backup approach, ensure the following prerequisites:
Prerequisites for NetApp
l Obtain the SnapMirror Cloud license or ONTAP One license for enabling NetApp SnapDiff-based backup.
l Ensure the Cohesity cluster has the FQDN setup configured and all VIPs resolved to the FQDN of the NetApp cluster.
l Enable NetApp Snapdiff V3 on your NetApp Vservers/SVMs by running the following commands:
::> set adv
::*> vserver snapdiff-rpc-server on -vserver <svm_name>
l NFS must be enabled on the data LIFs to run SnapDiff APIs for File Level Recovery and to allow RPC initialization.
l To ensure protection using the SnapDiff approach, all NetApp ONTAP volumes must have the 'snapdif-access' capability enabled.

Considerations
The following are the important considerations to be noted before you protect your NetApp ONTAP data using NetApp SnapDiff-based backup:
l The NAS storage FQDN must be resolvable. Even if registered by IP, SMB restore workflows depend on the FQDN for repeated SMB share connections. Ensure that the DNS or cluster host mapping resolves the storage FQDN.
l To use NetApp SnapDiff-based backup, ensure your Cohesity cluster has the FQDN setup configured and all VIPs resolve to the cluster name.
l Cohesity does not support NetApp SnapDiff-based backup if the NetApp source is registered as NetApp ONTAP SVM.
l You cannot protect the same NetApp volume in two Protection Groups (Protection Groups created within a Cohesity cluster or different Cohesity clusters) with NetApp SnapDiff-based backup. However, you can protect the same NetApp volume in two Protection Groups if one Protection Group is with SnapDiff enabled and the other Protection Group is without SnapDiff enabled.
l The backup of a NetApp volume will fail if there is already a SnapMirror cloud relationship created between the NetApp volume and another Cohesity S3 View.
l SnapDiff-based backups are immutable. That is, you cannot delete the SnapDiffbased backed-up data.
l When assigning or creating backup policies to a Protection Group for NetApp volumes, it is recommended to create the schedule of backup policy in-sync or less aggressive than the SnapMirror or SnapVault schedule. This ensures the presence of the snapshot in the volume, prior to the incremental backup triggered by the Cohesity backup policy schedule.
l CloudArchive Direct is not supported.
l CloudArchive with Periodic full is not supported. However, CloudArchive with incremental forever format to an S3-compatible target, NAS, and Tape is supported.
l You cannot delete the latest snapshot available on both local and remote clusters.
l You cannot delete the snapshot when indexing is in progress.
l NetApp requires an S3 Access key for accessing a Cohesity S3 view. For generating Cohesity S3 access keys, you must use one of the following accounts to create an S3 View:
l A local Cohesity user.
l An Active Directory user that was explicitly added to the Cohesity cluster and assigned a role. This user does not rely on an AD group for access to the Cohesity cluster.
S3 access keys will not be generated for a Helios user or for an AD user that has Cohesity cluster access through an Active Directory group only.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Considerations

l Pausing an ongoing SnapDiff-based protection run and resuming the protection run at a later time is not supported.
l Failover and failback are not supported. l If the latest snapshot in the NetApp ONTAP volume is already backed up and there is
no new snapshot in the NetApp volume, then the backup will fail. l You should not manually perform 'snapmirror update'. Ie, you should not update the
Cohesity S3 View. The following error message will be displayed when you perform SnapDiff-based backup after updating Cohesity S3 View:
Unable to establish a SnapDiff session.
l Cohesity recommends a first full and incremental forever backup approach to back up your NAS sources.
The following are the considerations for Storage Volume Recovery:
l The recovery target must be a DP volume. l Recover to the Original Location recovery workflow is not supported. l You must select a new DP volume, which is not in a SnapMirror relationship. When a
volume that was backed up via SnapDiff is recovered to an alternate NetApp DP volume, then the target DP volume will become an RW volume. Therefore, you cannot use the same volume as the target volume for the next volume recovery task. l Recovering data to the following is not supported as NetApp SnapDiff stores the data in a proprietary format: l Recovering to a non-NetApp NAS. l Recovering to a new Cohesity View.
The following are the considerations for Directory-level Recovery:
l Directory-level recovery is supported through file and folder recovery. l Due to SnapMirror limitations, you can recover up to eight individual files or one folder
at a time.
The following are the considerations for File-level Recovery:
l The recovery target must be a Read-Write volume. l To perform file recovery, indexing must be enabled on the Protection Group. l You can select up to eight files for recovery at a time. If you select more than eight
files for recovery, then the recovery task will fail. l Downloading zip files is not supported. l Recovery of hardlinks and symbolic links is not supported. l Mtime is not preserved for SMB.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Considerations

l File and folder recovery from an archive (incremental forever archival format) is not supported.
l When browsing files or folders for recovery, Cohesity does not display files or folders with an absolute path length exceeding approximately 3,500 characters. To recover these files or folders, select the parent directory.
Best Practices for SnapDiff-based Backup
1. NFS protocol must be enabled on the SVM from which volumes are backed up using SnapDiff.
2. The SnapDiff API will run over data LIFs (logical interface) since they cannot be run over management LIF. Therefore, NFS must be enabled on the data LIFs used by the SVM to allow RPC initialization.
3. An inter-cluster LIF must be configured on the NetApp ONTAP cluster. NetApp ONTAP verifies connectivity prior to saving this configuration information.
Register and Manage NetApp ONTAP Source To protect your NetApp ONTAP data, you need to register your NetApp ONTAP as a source on the Cohesity cluster. After registration, you can manage the source on the Cohesity cluster in the following ways:
l Update the NetApp ONTAP source configuration l Refresh the source details l Unregister the NetApp ONTAP source from the Cohesity cluster.
Register NetApp ONTAP as a Source
Before you register NetApp ONTAP as a source on the Cohesity cluster, ensure that you: 1. Review the requirements, considerations, and best practices. 2. Perform the prerequisite tasks.
For more information, see Plan and Prepare for File-Runner Based NetApp ONTAP Backup.
Note: Before you register NetApp ONTAP as a source on the Cohesity cluster, ensure that you have reviewed and completed the instructions provided in the Plan and Prepare for File-Runner Based NetApp ONTAP Backup

l Deny IPs: Select this option and specify the IP addresses of the NetApp ONTAP source through which the communication to the Cohesity cluster must not happen. You can provide the IP addresses in a comma-separated list or in a CIDR format.

Storage Array Snapshots

Enable this option to manage the snapshots of VMware VMs stored in NetApp NFS volumes from the Cohesity cluster.
l Cap number of snapshot per volume: Enter the maximum number of snapshots that can be stored on each NetApp storage volume.
l Cap storage consumed by snapshot per volume: Enter the percentage of the NetApp volume's storage you want the snapshots to consume.

Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.

Backup NetApp ONTAP Using SnapDiff

After registering your NetApp ONTAP server as a source on the Cohesity cluster, you can create a Protection Group to back up your NetApp ONTAP DP and RW volumes. You can back up one or more NetApp ONTAP NFS or SMB shares in a Protection Group while preserving the ACLs and Extended attributes on SMB.
To perform SnapDiff-based backup, you must enable the NetApp SnapDiff option available while creating a Protection Group. For leveraging the existing snapshots present in a NetApp ONTAP volume using SnapDiff-based backup, you must create a Cohesity S3 View.
When a Protection Group with the NetApp SnapDiff option enabled is run, Cohesity will request NetApp to transfer the data. For the full backup, NetApp starts ingesting the list of files in the volume to Cohesity in parallel to the data transfer. For incremental backup, ingesting the list of files and data transfer occurs sequentially.
For ingesting the list of files, Cohesity creates a SnapDiff session and ingest files sequentially. For data transfer, Cohesity uses NetApp's SnapMirror cloud functionally which writes to the Cohesity S3 View.
Once the SnapDiff session is initialized, for NetApp ONTAP DP volume, a snapshot with the label, snapmirror.<cluster_ID>.<Year-Month-Date-time> is created on the NetApp ONTAP volume. Cohesity takes the full backup from this snapshot leveraging NetApp to write the data from this snapshot to the Cohesity S3 View. For taking a full backup of a DP

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Considerations

volume, you must initialize the DP volume with the RW volume before creating a Protection Group. When you create a Protection Group for the NetApp ONTAP volumes with the NetApp SnapDiff option enabled, you must select an existing or create a new Cohesity S3 View. When creating an S3 view, ensure to select :
l Object Services as the Category value l Object ID as the Object Key Pattern value. l S3 as the Read/Write Protocol value
For information see, Create Views Using a Custom Template. For information on:
l The prerequisites for registering and protecting NetApp, see Plan and Prepare for NetApp ONTAP SnapDiff-based Backup.
l Registering NetApp ONTAP with Cohesity cluster, see Register and Manage NetApp ONTAP Source.
Protect NetApp ONTAP Using SnapDiff-based Backup
In Cohesity, NetApp ONTAP volumes are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, archived, or replicated. A Protection Policy is a reusable set of settings that define how and when objects are protected and replicated. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy.
Note: Cohesity recommends a first full and incremental forever backup approach to back up your NAS sources.
To protect NetApp ONTAP volumes with SnapDiff-based backup approach:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Protection. 2. Click Protect on the top-right of the page and then select NAS. 3. Click Add Objects and from the Registered Source drop-down list, select the
NetApp source that contains the volumes you want to back up. You can also register a NAS new source with the Cohesity cluster so you can protect it. To register a new NAS source, click Register Source from the drop-down. For more information, see Register and Manage NetApp ONTAP Source. 4. From the list of volumes, select the NetApp ONTAP volumes for which you want to perform the SnapDiff-based backup. 5. Click Continue.
