Policy Settings for NetApp ONTAP
The following table lists the applicable policy settings for NetApp ONTAP:

Field

Description

Primary Copy Select Local from the drop-down to keep the primary copy data on the Cohesity cluster.

DataLock

If applicable, add a DataLock for compliance and regulatory requirements, to ensure that your protected data, including local backups, archives, and replication, cannot be modified until the DataLock expiration.
Once applied, a DataLocked Snapshot will be deleted only after its retention period expires. A DataLock prevents all users, including those who have the Data Security role in Cohesity, from modifying or deleting any Snapshots that were generated by theProtection Groups that use this Policy. Only users with the Data Security role can add, modify, or remove a DataLock from a Policy.

Backup

Defines when backups are captured, how long they are retained and the type of backup to capture.

Periodic full backup

Use this option to choose when to run a periodic full backup.

Quiet Times

Quiet Times defines time periods when new protection runs are not started. For example, you might want to configure hourly backups that run during weekdays but not on Saturdays or Sundays. Quiet Times only prevent new protection runs from starting during the specified time period.
The protection runs that started before the quiet time period will be dependent on the quiet time settings configured in the additional settings of the protection Group.
For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time period that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet time period.

Retry Options

Use this option to customize the retry settings for capturing Snapshots. By default, Cohesity attempts to capture Snapshots three times before the Protection Group fails. The default time between retries is five minutes. You can customize the number of retries and how long to wait between each attempt.

Troubleshoot NetApp Protection
l If backing up a NetApp volume fails with the following error: An entity being protected was not found in the global entity hierarchy, this could have been caused because the volume was moved to a different aggregate.
Workaround - Edit the Protection Group that protects the volume that was moved and select the moved volume for protection.
l Registering and backing up a NetApp volume as an NFS NAS mount point results in a larger backup size because all files inside the .snapshot directory are backed up.
Workaround - Do one of the following:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Nutanix Files

l Register a path to a snapshot on that NetApp volume l Register it as a NetApp source instead of a NAS mount point l In the Protection Group's settings configure the filter to skip the .snapshot
directory l Disable the configuration on that NetApp volume to show the .snapshot
directory l For an incremental backup, if there is no snapshot created in the DP volume after the
last snapshot that is used for the full or incremental backup, then the protection run fails with the following error message:
No new snapshot found to take backup. Last snapshot used for backup: <snaphot_name> with create time: <create_time> for volume: <volume_ name> on vserver: <server_name>
l If the snapshot label specified in the protection group does not match with the snapshot label in the DP volume, then the protection run fails with the following error message:
No snapshot with label: home found in the volume: <volume_name> on vserver: <server_name>. Cohesity discovers snapshots for DataProtect volumes and uses existing snapshots for taking backups. Please verify the labels for the snapshot provided.
l If the backup fails for a protection group that has Snapshot Array Management enabled with the following error message, ensure the Storage Array backing the DataStore in which the VM resides is registered with the Cohesity Cluster:
VM cannot be backed up due to error: [kUnknownStorageDevice]: Storage array of the datastore is not registered.
l If you do not enable the Snapshot Prefix option while creating the Protection Group, then the backup of NetApp DP volume may fail with the following error.
[kInvalidRequest]: Error: No new snapshot found in the volume: <volume_ name> on vserver: <vserver_name>. Cohesity discovers snapshots and uses existing snapshots for taking backups. Please verify the labels for the snapshot provided
Workaround - If the Snapshot Prefix option is not enabled, then ensure that an appropriate older snapshots are available in the NetApp source.
Nutanix Files
Nutanix Files is a hardware and software-based solution for file storage and retrieval. You can configure Cohesity to back up and restore data on Nutanix Files arrays. You can back up and restore Nutanix Files mount targets using the Cohesity File-Runner backup method or the vendor-native Change File Tracking (CFT) method. Cohesity File-

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Nutanix Files

Runner facilitates the backing up of Nutanix Files mount targets by leveraging snapshots. The tool specifically identifies differences between two snapshot copies, allowing for incremental backups and minimizing redundancy.
In the CFT method, Cohesity leverages the Nutanix Files CFT API to identify the delta between two snapshot copies.
See: Plan and Prepare for Nutanix Files Protection

System (DFS) referral. The Distributed File System has a collection of shares on different machines that serve as a file system namespace. If one machine does not have a particular file requested by the client, it is referred to check the other machine. l You can protect DFS shares using the NFS V4.1 and V3 protocols.

Protect Nutanix Files
In Cohesity, Nutanix Files mount targets are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, archived, or replicated.
A Protection Policy is a reusable set of settings that define how and when objects are protected and replicated. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy.
This topic provides information on how to protect Nutanix Files mount targets using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy.
Protect Read-Write mount targets with SMB Share or NFS Export
You can protect Nutanix Files RW mount targets using either SMB or NFS protocols.

NAS File DataLock
Many organizations now rely on WORM (Write Once Read Many) data storage such as Nutanix Files, NetApp Snaplock, and Isilon Smartlock volumes to retain their files and folders in unmodified form for compliance and regulatory purposes and to protect the files from accidental deletion or modification.
When you backup these WORM-capable volumes to the Cohesity cluster, it is essential to have the ability to easily lock the files and folders of the volumes while protecting themselves from accidental or malicious attempts to delete or modify these files. The backup should also provide a strong guarantee for data non-mutability and non-erasability for a certain period of time.
This capability is achieved using Cohesity's File DataLock feature.
FileDataLock is a Cohesity feature that preserves the WORM attributes of any files and folders created in the Cohesity View. You can apply the File DataLock feature for NAS backup (NFS exports and SMB shares) while creating a NAS Protection Group.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Nutanix Files

With File DataLock enabled in a NAS Protection Group, Cohesity preserves the future AccessTime (ATime) of the files and folders. The AccessTime provides the lock period for files and folders. You can also override this lock period in the File DataLock settings of the NAS Protection Group. This lock period is applied to these files and folders when they are recovered to the Cohesity View. This prevents the users or administrator from modifying or deleting these locked files until the locking period expires. You can also set lock periods for the new files and folders created on recovered Cohesity View in the File DataLock settings of the NAS Protection Group. When you recover File DataLock enabled storage volumes to the Cohesity View, the View details page will display a lock icon for the files and folders having File DataLock. File DataLock is supported for all types of NAS sources including NetApp 7-mode and is agnostic of the NAS protocol. For information on how to enable File DataLock, see Protect NAS.
File DataLock Modes
You can use the File DataLock feature in one of the two modes:
l Compliance mode: The WORM files are protected at the disk level. This mode implements strict regulatory requirements for data retention and complies with SEC Rule 17a-4. In this mode, files and folders cannot be deleted or modified during the retention period. After the lock expires, no user can modify the files and folders. However, a root user can delete the files and folders. Only a user with a Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Compliance mode.
l Enterprise mode: The WORM files are protected at the file level. This mode does not implement strict regulatory requirements for data retention. In this mode, files and folders cannot be modified by any user before or after the lock retention period expiration. However, a root user can delete the files and folders during or after the lock retention period. An admin user or a user with the Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Enterprise mode
Note: An admin user or a user with the Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings and switch from the Enterprise mode to Compliance mode. But switching from Compliance mode to Enterprise mode is not supported.
Things to remember for File DataLock
l You cannot enable or disable File DataLock once the View is created. l If you have disabled File DataLock while creating a Protection Group, then when you
edit this Protection Group, the File DataLock option will not be displayed. l You can delete Protection Groups and snapshots having File DataLock enabled.
File DataLock also preserves the ATimes of the hardlinks and symlinks.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Nutanix Files

l Recovery l Recovering a File DataLock enabled backed-up volume as a Cohesity View will preserve ATimes and the locking period for the file. l Recovering a File DataLock enabled volume to the original location with `Overwrite existing files/folder' as the recovery option will encounter an error if the files and folders are read-only. However, the ATime and other attributes of other files and folders of the source volumes are preserved. l Recovering a File DataLock enabled volume to an alternate NAS recovery will preserve ATimes and other attributes of files and folders of the source volumes. l Cloning a recovered View having File DataLock enabled will not inherit the File DataLock properties.
l Replication When you replicate to a remote Cohesity cluster, the File DataLock settings are also replicated.
l Archival File DataLock settings are preserved when you recover volume from an archived snapshot whose Protection Group has File Datalock enabled, to a Cohesity View.
l Cloud Archive Direct File DataLock settings are preserved when you recover from a Cloud ArchiveDirect snapshot whose Protection Group has File Datalock enabled, to a Cohesity View.
Exclusions and Inclusions for NAS Protection Group
In a NAS Protection Group, all the files and folders are included by default for data protection. While creating a Protection Group, you can toggle on Exclusions and Inclusions from the Advanced Settings options if you want to exclude or include locations. By creating the exclusion and inclusion rules, you can limit the Protection Group to a specific set of files and directories. As a result, you can minimize the disk space used to store the data.
Note: l To add an exclusion or inclusion rule, you must prefix a forward slash (`/') or suffix an asterisk (`*') to the path or to a particular file within the protected object. For example, `/test' or `*.txt'.
l In exclusion or inclusion rules, file names and folder names are casesensitive, which means `test.txt' and `Test.txt' are considered separate files. Use the correct capitalization of file or folder names to ensure that the rules recognize your file or folder.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Nutanix Files

Add Inclusion
From the Additional Settings options on the Protection Group page, toggle on Exclusions and Inclusions. Click Add Inclusion to include a particular path or a particular file within the protected object.
For example, consider four directories - test, test1, test2, and test3 under the protected object with path /ifs/TestShare1/Folder1. The table below lists the input types for an inclusion list of folders and their respective outcome:

Input / /test
/test/

Outcome
Everything inside the protection path is backed up if exclusions are not defined.
When the inclusion path is not suffixed by '/', Protection Group will include all folders starting from the protection path. In this example, /test will behave as /test* and Protection Group will include 'test', 'test1', 'test2', and 'test3' from the protection path for backup.
When the inclusion path is suffixed by '/', it will only include the specific folder. In this example, /test/ behaves as /test/* and Protection Group will only include 'test' from the protection path for backup.

l Do not provide the folder name along with the backup path while including files and folders for a Protection Group. The backup path is considered by default. For example, /ifs/TestShare1/Folder1/test does not include any folder.
l If exclusions are defined, they will take precedence over inclusions.
Add Exclusion
From the Additional Settings options on the Protection Group page, toggle on Exclusions and Inclusions. Click Add Exclusion to exclude a particular path or a particular file within the protected object. You can also specify regular expressions for excluding files in the format regex:<regex pattern>.
For example, consider there are three directories - Test, Test1, and Folder1 and a file, TestFile.tmp under the protected object with path /ifs/TestShare1.
l The Test1 folder has TestFile1.tmp, TestFile2.tmp files.
l The Folder1 folder has TestFile3.tmp, TestFile4.tmp files, and SubFolder1 which further has a Test folder with File.txt, File1.txt files in it.

Manage the Nutanix Files Backup Configuration
In Cohesity, a backup configuration includes a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. You can modify the existing Protection Group and the Protection Policy based on your requirement.
Note: You cannot update the registered Nutanix Files cluster and the assigned Storage Domain in the Protection Group settings.
Add Nutanix Files mount targets to the Protection Group
You can add new Nutanix Files mount targets to the existing Protection Group for backup. The newly added mount targets are backed up from the next protection run and it will be a full backup. To add Nutanix Files mount targets to the Protection Group:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for Nutanix
Files. 3. Click the action icon next to the Protection Group and select Edit. 4. On the Edit Protection page, in the Object field, click the Edit icon. 5. Select the Nutanix Files mount targets you want to add to the Protection Group. 6. Click Save Selection > Save.

The next time the Protection Group runs, if the object hierarchy has been refreshed on the Cohesity cluster, the new mount target is also backed up even though the new mount target has not been explicitly selected to be included in the Protection Group. Dell EMC Isilon
Isilon is a network-attached storage platform offered by Dell EMC and provides a clusterbased storage array based on industry-standard hardware. Using the policy-based data protection solution from Cohesity, you can protect the data stored on Isilon. This section provides information on how to back up and recover Isilon data using Cohesity.

Considerations
l The NAS storage FQDN must be resolvable. Even if registered by IP, SMB restore workflows depend on the FQDN for repeated SMB share connections. Ensure that the DNS or cluster host mapping resolves the storage FQDN.
l The Cohesity Dashboard estimates the total size of protected and unprotected Isilon shares by multiplying the number of shares by about 3.5 GiB. Cohesity cannot determine the actual size because each share is a subdirectory of the root /ifs directory.
l For Isilon OneFS 9.2.x or earlier versions, the maximum filename length or full path length limits to 255 bytes.
l Root permissions are required to set the ACLs. To set the permissions, you can perform the following:
l for the share that belongs to System Access Zone, add "Backup files from /ifs" and "Restore files to /ifs" privileges for the role to which the user or group belongs.
l for non-System Access Zone, set the share permissions for the user as "Run as root".
l Cohesity recommends a first full and incremental forever backup approach to back up your NAS sources.
l When browsing files or folders for recovery, Cohesity does not display files or folders with an absolute path length exceeding approximately 3,500 characters. To recover these files or folders, select the parent directory.
l If the SMB credentials on the source change during an active backup, Isilon SMB backup jobs automatically pause and display a pause note: "Auto-paused due to credential/logon failure."
The jobs resume after you update the SMB credentials on the Cohesity cluster. This behavior prevents loss of overall backup progress. Any missed files are backed up in the next incremental run.

Isilon SmartConnect

Isilon SmartConnect is a feature that offers load balancing and failover capabilities for connections to an Isilon cluster. It effectively manages requests from multiple connections, manages DNS requests, and oversees multiple IP addresses.
SmartConnect is a licensed software module of the EMC Isilon OneFS, designed to enhance performance and availability by enabling intelligent client connection load balancing and failover support. If the Isilon cluster has SmartConnect enabled, it can be used for backup operations.
To utilize SmartConnect, you need to configure it after registering the Isilon source. You must register the Isilon Adapter Source using the SmartConnect IP (SIP), which provides multiple addresses for the Cohesity cluster to access
SmartConnect can be configured under Cluster Management > Network Configuration, where you can view or edit the subnet settings. Cohesity supports using the SmartConnect Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) to discover and connect to the Isilon cluster.

Backup Isilon
After registering your Isilon cluster as a source on the Cohesity cluster, you can create a Protection Group to protect the Isilon volumes. The volume can be of NFS export only, SMB share only, or of both NFS and SMB (mixed) type. To back up SMB shares of any volume type, you must provide the local or Active Directory user credentials that allow at least read access to the Isilon SMB share. You can provide these credentials while registering the Isilon cluster with the Cohesity cluster or later when creating the Protection Group. For more information, see, Register and Manage Isilon Source. You can backup one or more Isilon NFS mount points, SMB shares, or mixed volumes in a Protection Group while preserving ACLs and Extended attributes on SMB.
Protect Isilon
In Cohesity, Isilon volumes are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, archived, or replicated. A Protection Policy is a reusable set of settings that define how and when objects are protected and replicated. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy. You can protect Isilon volumes with only SMB share, NFS export, or the volumes that are exposed to both NFS export and SMB share (mixed volumes). For Isilon mixed volumes, Cohesity will back up both NFS POSIX ACLs and SMB access control lists (ACLs).
Note: Cohesity recommends a first full and incremental forever backup approach to back up your NAS sources.
To protect Isilon volumes:

l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group.

Additional Settings Skip Files on Errors
Use Isilon Change Lists

Description
Toggled on by default. The Protection Group continues to run even if it encounters errors on files, such as permissions errors. If files are skipped, the protection run details page indicates a warning status and provides additional information. If toggled off, the Protection Group stops when it encounters an error.
Toggle on this option to use the vendor-native Change File Tracking (CFT) method for file discovery during an incremental backup. In this method, Cohesity leverages the Isilon CFT API to identify the delta between two snapshot copies. It reduces the time taken to discover the files and folders to backup. If this option is toggled off, Cohesity uses the Cohesity's built-in CFT method. In this method, Cohesity uses its internal File-Runner to discover the delta between two snapshot copies. By default, this option is disabled.

Note: Due to the limitations set by Isilon, only one change list can be run at a time. If the Protection Group contains multiple shares to back up, Isilon creates delta for each share serially.

Encryption

Toggle on this option to enable in-flight encryption of data that are backed up to the Cohesity cluster. This option is disabled by default. To use the encryption functionality for NFS volumes, you must join the Cohesity cluster to the active directory as the Kerberos server or add the Kerberos provider in the Cohesity cluster Access Management section. This option is disabled by default.
Note: Encrypting in-flight data will have a minor impact on the performance.

Additional Settings

Description

File DataLock

Toggle on this option to preserve the AccessTime of the files and folders of the selected volumes. The AccessTime provides the lock period of the files and folders that are applied when these files and folders are recovered to the Cohesity View.
For more information on File DataLock, see NAS File DataLock.
Select one of the following DataLock modes:
l Compliance: In this mode, files or folders cannot be deleted or modified during the retention period. After the lock expires, no user can modify the files or folders. However, a root user can delete the files and folders. Only a user with the Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Compliance mode.
l Enterprise: In this mode, files or folders cannot be modified by any user before or after the lock retention period expiration. However, a root user can delete the files or folders before or after the lock retention period. An admin user or a user with the Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Enterprise mode. This mode is useful for giving storage administrators additional control over the file.
You can further configure the File DataLock settings to:
l Set the lock period for the new files and folders created on the recovered Cohesity View
Provide the following information to set the lock period for the new files and folders that will be created on the recovered Cohesity View. These settings are not applicable for the existing NAS source files and folders recovered on the Cohesity View.
l Default Lock Period: Provide the time period during which the files should remain locked. When the time period ends, files can be deleted but not changed. By default, the files are locked forever.
l Autolock Files: By enabling this option, the files are automatically locked if they are not modified in the time period you specify. By default, this option is disabled.
l Manally Lock Using: Select when the files are to be locked:
l Read-Only: Select this option to lock files when the file permission is set to read only, for example; by setting the Windows file properties attribute or using the Linux chmod command. By default, the files are locked when the file permission is set to read only.
l FutureATime: Select this option to lock files when the last access time (atime) is set, for example, by using Windows PowerShell commands or the Linux touch command.
Optionally you can set a Minimum Retention and/or a Maximum Retention period to ensure that a file's last access time cannot be set outside this period.

Description
A request to do so results in a permission denied error if manual locking mode is FutureATime. Otherwise, the request will be silently rejected and the file will be locked for the minimum retention duration.
l Override the locking period of the existing files and folders recovered on the Cohesity View: The following option can be applied to all the existing files and folders that will be recovered on the Cohesity View. l Override (Lock all files until a specific date ): Enable this option and select a date to override the locking period of the existing files and folders. When you recover the files to the Cohesity View, Cohesity applies the farthest lock period between the override lock period you specify and the source file's lock period. For example; l The lock period of the source file is 09/09/2023 and the override lock period you specified is 09/08/2022. When you recover the file to the Cohesity View, then the override lock period you specified is applied to the recovered file, which is 09/08/2024. In Compliance mode, a user with the Data Security privileges can extend the override date into the future, but no user can shorten the date. In Enterprise mode, a user with admin or the Data Security privileges can extend or shorten the override date.

This option is available only if the selected policy has at least one quiet time period. Toggle the Stop inprogress runs when quiet time starts option to pause or abort the runs during quiet time. If this option is toggled off, after a protection run starts, execution continues even when the quiet time period specified for this Protection Group starts. However, a new protection run will not start during a quiet time period.
l Pause Runs - Select this option to pause the currently executing protection runs and resume the runs when quiet time ends.
l Abort Runs - Select this option to abort the currently executing protection runs when the quiet time period specified for the Protection Group starts.
Note: If the quiet time window for multiple protection runs is scheduled at the same time, then when the protection run is resumed, prioritization of the protection run does not work.

l Failure: Create a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l Success: Create an informational alert when the Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.

Quiet Times

Quiet Times defines time periods when new protection runs are not started. For example, you might want to configure hourly backups that run during weekdays but not on Saturday or Sunday. Quiet Times only prevents new protection runs from starting during the specified time period.
The protection runs that started before the quiet time period will be dependent on the quiet time settings configured in the additional settings of the protection Group.
For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time period that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet time period.

NAS File DataLock
Many organizations now rely on WORM (Write Once Read Many) data storage such as Nutanix Files, NetApp Snaplock, and Isilon Smartlock volumes to retain their files and folders in unmodified form for compliance and regulatory purposes and to protect the files from accidental deletion or modification.
When you backup these WORM-capable volumes to the Cohesity cluster, it is essential to have the ability to easily lock the files and folders of the volumes while protecting themselves from accidental or malicious attempts to delete or modify these files. The backup should also provide a strong guarantee for data non-mutability and non-erasability for a certain period of time.
This capability is achieved using Cohesity's File DataLock feature.
FileDataLock is a Cohesity feature that preserves the WORM attributes of any files and folders created in the Cohesity View. You can apply the File DataLock feature for NAS backup (NFS exports and SMB shares) while creating a NAS Protection Group.
With File DataLock enabled in a NAS Protection Group, Cohesity preserves the future AccessTime (ATime) of the files and folders. The AccessTime provides the lock period for files and folders. You can also override this lock period in the File DataLock settings of the NAS Protection Group. This lock period is applied to these files and folders when they are recovered to the Cohesity View. This prevents the users or administrator from modifying or deleting these locked files until the locking period expires.
You can also set lock periods for the new files and folders created on recovered Cohesity View in the File DataLock settings of the NAS Protection Group.
When you recover File DataLock enabled storage volumes to the Cohesity View, the View details page will display a lock icon for the files and folders having File DataLock.
File DataLock is supported for all types of NAS sources including NetApp 7-mode and is agnostic of the NAS protocol.
For information on how to enable File DataLock, see Protect NAS.
File DataLock Modes
You can use the File DataLock feature in one of the two modes:
l Compliance mode: The WORM files are protected at the disk level. This mode implements strict regulatory requirements for data retention and complies with SEC Rule 17a-4. In this mode, files and folders cannot be deleted or modified during the retention period. After the lock expires, no user can modify the files and folders. However, a root user can delete the files and folders. Only a user with a Data Security

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Dell EMC Isilon

role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Compliance mode. l Enterprise mode: The WORM files are protected at the file level. This mode does not
implement strict regulatory requirements for data retention. In this mode, files and folders cannot be modified by any user before or after the lock retention period expiration. However, a root user can delete the files and folders during or after the lock retention period. An admin user or a user with the Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings in the Enterprise mode
Note: An admin user or a user with the Data Security role can edit the File DataLock settings and switch from the Enterprise mode to Compliance mode. But switching from Compliance mode to Enterprise mode is not supported.
Things to remember for File DataLock
l You cannot enable or disable File DataLock once the View is created. l If you have disabled File DataLock while creating a Protection Group, then when you
edit this Protection Group, the File DataLock option will not be displayed. l You can delete Protection Groups and snapshots having File DataLock enabled.
File DataLock also preserves the ATimes of the hardlinks and symlinks.
l Recovery l Recovering a File DataLock enabled backed-up volume as a Cohesity View will preserve ATimes and the locking period for the file. l Recovering a File DataLock enabled volume to the original location with `Overwrite existing files/folder' as the recovery option will encounter an error if the files and folders are read-only. However, the ATime and other attributes of other files and folders of the source volumes are preserved. l Recovering a File DataLock enabled volume to an alternate NAS recovery will preserve ATimes and other attributes of files and folders of the source volumes. l Cloning a recovered View having File DataLock enabled will not inherit the File DataLock properties.
l Replication When you replicate to a remote Cohesity cluster, the File DataLock settings are also replicated.
l Archival File DataLock settings are preserved when you recover volume from an archived snapshot whose Protection Group has File Datalock enabled, to a Cohesity View.
l Cloud Archive Direct File DataLock settings are preserved when you recover from a Cloud ArchiveDirect snapshot whose Protection Group has File Datalock enabled, to a Cohesity View.

Exclusions and Inclusions for NAS Protection Group
In a NAS Protection Group, all the files and folders are included by default for data protection. While creating a Protection Group, you can toggle on Exclusions and Inclusions from the Advanced Settings options if you want to exclude or include locations. By creating the exclusion and inclusion rules, you can limit the Protection Group to a specific set of files and directories. As a result, you can minimize the disk space used to store the data.
Note: l To add an exclusion or inclusion rule, you must prefix a forward slash (`/') or suffix an asterisk (`*') to the path or to a particular file within the protected object. For example, `/test' or `*.txt'.
l In exclusion or inclusion rules, file names and folder names are casesensitive, which means `test.txt' and `Test.txt' are considered separate files. Use the correct capitalization of file or folder names to ensure that the rules recognize your file or folder.

Add Inclusion
From the Additional Settings options on the Protection Group page, toggle on Exclusions and Inclusions. Click Add Inclusion to include a particular path or a particular file within the protected object.
For example, consider four directories - test, test1, test2, and test3 under the protected object with path /ifs/TestShare1/Folder1. The table below lists the input types for an inclusion list of folders and their respective outcome:

Input /
/test

Outcome
Everything inside the protection path is backed up if exclusions are not defined.
When the inclusion path is not suffixed by '/', Protection Group will include all folders starting from the protection path. In this example, /test will behave as /test* and Protection Group will include 'test', 'test1', 'test2', and 'test3' from the protection path for backup.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Dell EMC Isilon

Input /test/

Outcome
When the inclusion path is suffixed by '/', it will only include the specific folder. In this example, /test/ behaves as /test/* and Protection Group will only include 'test' from the protection path for backup.

l Do not provide the folder name along with the backup path while including files and folders for a Protection Group. The backup path is considered by default. For example, /ifs/TestShare1/Folder1/test does not include any folder.
l If exclusions are defined, they will take precedence over inclusions.
Add Exclusion
From the Additional Settings options on the Protection Group page, toggle on Exclusions and Inclusions. Click Add Exclusion to exclude a particular path or a particular file within the protected object. You can also specify regular expressions for excluding files in the format regex:<regex pattern>.
For example, consider there are three directories - Test, Test1, and Folder1 and a file, TestFile.tmp under the protected object with path /ifs/TestShare1.
l The Test1 folder has TestFile1.tmp, TestFile2.tmp files.
l The Folder1 folder has TestFile3.tmp, TestFile4.tmp files, and SubFolder1 which further has a Test folder with File.txt, File1.txt files in it.

Description

/Test/

Click Save Selection > Save.

The next time the Protection Group runs, if the object hierarchy has been refreshed on the Cohesity cluster, the new volume is also backed up even though the new volume has not been explicitly selected to be included in the Protection Group. Recover Storage Volume
Cohesity's recover storage volume capability allows you to select and restore specific NAS shares from any previous backup. Before you can recover storage volumes, ensure that snapshots of those volumes exist in the Protection Groups on your Cohesity cluster. For more information, see Recover NAS Storage Volumes.

Cohesity's recover files or folders capability allows you to search and recover specific files and whole folders from any previous NAS backup. Before you try to recover files or folders, ensure that snapshots of these files and folders appear on the Cohesity cluster in a Protection Group. For backed-up SMB volumes, the user account must have full control on the target as Cohesity uses that user to perform recovery. Cohesity now allows the recovery of up to eight files or one folder from SnapDiff-based backups. For more information, see Recover NAS Files or Folders.
Hardlink
A hardlink set consists of file references (hardlinks) with the same inode, pointing to the data's location on the filesystem.

Character replacement explanation for : and \ in file and directory names in zip files
If the original file or directory name contains a `:' , it is replaced with `_COLON_' in the archive. Example:

Recover hardlinks
A hardlink set consists of file references (hardlinks) with the same inode, pointing to the data's location on the filesystem.
You can restore the hardlinks to their original location or restore multiple directories containing common hardlinks.
Recover hardlinks to the original location
When recovering, you can enable or disable the "Overwrite" option. If the option is disabled, only the missing hardlinks from any hardlink set will be recreated after the restore. In this case, a new inode pointing to the backed-up version of the data will be created for the missing hardlink file, and all the other hardlinks to be restored will point to this inode. However, if the option is enabled, all hardlinks from any hardlink set are recreated after restoration, pointing to a new inode that points to the backed-up data version.
For example, let's say there is a hardlink set containing files from A to F, all of which are backed up. If we delete the hardlinks A, B, and C, and then restore to the original path with the "Overwrite" option disabled, a new inode will be created. This inode will point to a new backed-up version of the data, and hardlinks A, B, and C will be recreated and point to this new inode. The hardlinks D, E, and F will remain unchanged and have the original inode.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Replicate NAS Data

With the Overwrite option enabled, all files (A to F) will be recreated as new hardlinks, pointing to a new inode that contains the backed-up data version.
Recover multiple directories containing common hardlinks
If multiple folders are being restored, and they contain common hard links, each folder is restored independently. This means that a new inode is created for each hardlink set within a folder, pointing to a new backed-up version of the data. Any missing hardlinks are recreated, pointing to the new inodes of their respective folders.
Consider a scenario where directories A, B, and C have multiple hardlinks: A1 and A2 in A, B1 and B2 in B, and C1 and C2 in C, all pointing to the same file (with inode 100). With these hardlinks missing, if we restore only the directories A, B, and C instead of the entire volume, all these hard links will be recreated. The newly created A1 and A2 will point to a new inode (101), while B1 and B2 will point to a new inode (102), and C1 and C2 will point to a new inode (103). Each of these inodes will then reference separate backed-up versions of the data.
Replicate NAS Data
You can replicate Isilon data backup to the Cohesity cluster to another Cohesity cluster for disaster recovery use cases. For more details about replication, see Replication and Remote Access Setup.
Cohesity provides a policy-based replication solution for Isilon data. In the Protection Policy, you can specify the remote Cohesity cluster, define conditions for replication, specify the retention period of the data on the remote Cohesity cluster, and other parameters.
To replicate Isilon data to another Cohesity cluster:
1. Configure replication to another Cohesity cluster. For more details, see Replication and Remote Access Setup.
2. Edit the existing Protection Policy that you had created for backup or create a new Protection Policy for backup. Configure the replication settings as per your requirement. For more information, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.
3. Run the Protection Group that you have created for Isilon based on your requirement or the replication settings will take effect in the next scheduled Protection Group run.
Archive NAS Data
Cohesity provides the option to store a copy of your data backed up onto the Cohesity cluster to a designated external target, such as tape or cloud storage for long-term retention purposes. The process of storing a copy of the data backed up on the Cohesity cluster to an external target is called Archival. For more information, see About Cloud Archival.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 14: NAS

Archive NAS Data

Cohesity provides a policy-based archival solution for NAS data. In the Protection Policy, you can define the archive schedule, select the external target, and specify the retention period of the data on the external target.
To archive NAS data:
1. Register an external target. For more details, see Register an External Target.
2. Edit the existing Protection Policy that you had created for backup or if you are creating a new Protection Policy for backup. Configure the Archival settings as per your requirement. For more information, see Step 14 in Create or Edit a Standard Policy.
3. Run the Protection Group that you have created for the respective NAS source based on your requirement or the Archival settings will take effect in the next scheduled Protection Group run.

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365
Microsoft 365 is a subscription service that bundles the traditional office productivity applications and delivers them as SaaS applications. Microsoft 365 includes Exchange Online, OneDrive for Business, SharePoint Online, Teams, and other applications. Cohesity provides enterprise-grade backup and recovery solutions for Microsoft 365. Cohesity's software-defined platform provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective data protection solution for the following Microsoft 365 applications:
l Exchange Online
Note: Starting October 2026, Cohesity will discontinue support for Public Folder protection, following Microsoft's retirement of APIs for managing Public Folders.

Enhance Backup of Large Microsoft 365 Data
When it comes to ingesting Microsoft 365 data, the size can vary from hundreds of terabytes (TBs) to a few petabytes (PBs) in some cases. One of the issues that may arise while performing the initial full backup of such large data is throttling from the Microsoft 365 APIs.
Cohesity recommends using only one application ID for Microsoft 365 backups. However, when you back up a large amount of data, using only one application ID may result in a prolonged ETA for the first full backup. Contact your Cohesity account team to determine

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Prerequisites

the appropriate number of application IDs to optimize the performance while ensuring that the Microsoft Tenant Level Throttling limits are not exceeded, which may cause service failures for Microsoft 365. After completing the first full backup, using multiple application IDs is not usually required. However, in certain situations, a single application ID may be inadequate. For guidance on the appropriate number of application IDs for incremental backups following the initial full backup, Contact your Cohesity account team. Cohesity also supports Microsoft paid APIs to perform the first full backups faster. These APIs come with higher limits, ensuring the backups are performed faster at a higher API rate. The paid APIs are configured to be used in addition to the existing backup capacity allocated by Microsoft, rather than as a substitute, to help minimize additional costs.
Update Microsoft Organization Setting for Mailbox Size Reporting
By default, Microsoft reports, using Graph API, display information as de-identified names for users, groups, and sites. However, for Mailbox size reporting to work in Cohesity, you need to have identifiable information in the Email activity reports. To do that, you need to disable de-identified names for users, groups, and sites in Microsoft 365 reports. Update the following organization setting in your Microsoft 365 admin center:
1. Log in to your Microsoft 365 admin center as a Microsoft 365 tenant administrator. 2. Go to Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports. 3. In Reports, ensure the information is identifiable by deselecting Display concealed
user, group, and site names in all reports. 4. Click Save.

Set Up a Windows Connector for Microsoft 365
A Windows Connector is a Microsoft Windows VM that is required by the Cohesity cluster for downloading your backed-up mailboxes or email(s) in PST format.
You need to register a Windows Connector as a physical server source on Cohesity and connect it with your Microsoft 365 source. The following is the supported specification for the Windows Connector:

Specification Operating System vCPU RAM Disk

Microsoft Windows 10, 2016, 2019, or 2022. 2 8 GB (minimum) 20 GB

Prerequisites Ensure that:
l Cohesity Windows Agent is installed on Windows Connector.
Note: You do not have to install the Volume CBT or File CBT kernel drivers.
l Cohesity recommends that the Windows Connector is dedicated to Microsoft 365 data protection and is not part of any other workflows provided by Cohesity.
l The Windows Connector VM has internet connectivity. l The Windows Connector VM is in English locale. Non-English locale is not supported. l If your Cohesity cluster is joined to the Active Directory (AD) domain, ensure that the
Windows Connector is also part of the AD domain. l You exclude the following directory paths from Windows Security:
l C:\Program Files\Cohesity l C:\ProgramData\Cohesity l C:\Windows\Temp l You open specific ports in the firewall to allow data transfer between the Windows Connector and the Cohesity cluster.

Points to note:

Microsoft 365 Certificate-Based Authentication
Cohesity supports Certificate-Based Authentication (CBA) to protect Microsoft 365 applications. This feature allows you to authenticate with an X.509 certificate and provides phishing resistant authentication. For more information on CBA, see Microsoft Entra Certificate-Based Authentication. To register a new Microsoft 365 domain using CBA, see one of the following as required:
l Express Registration for Microsoft 365 Sources Using Certificate-Based Authentication l Manual Registration for Microsoft 365 Sources Using Certificate-Based Authentication
If you have already registered a Microsoft 365 source using app-secret-based authentication, you can switch it to CBA. To do this, you need to migrate the Azure applications used for Microsoft 365 registration to CBA. You can use either of the following workflows:
l Manual migration workflow l Express migration workflow

Considerations
Before you proceed with migration, review the following considerations:
l An error may occur during Microsoft 365 source registration or migration if the certificate selected on the source registration page is not uploaded to the respective Azure application in the Azure portal.
l Certificates generated by Cohesity are valid for one year. By default, Cohesity attempts to renew certificates 60 days before their expiration date. If the renewal attempt fails, alerts and warnings are displayed 45 days before the certificates expire.
l The certificate display name can be up to 32 characters long, and the maximum permitted validity is 397 days.
l When importing custom certificates, the certificates must be uploaded to the application before clicking Register in the UI, which will otherwise cause the registration to fail.

Certificate Generated Locally vs Certificate Generated in Cohesity Certificate Store

Certificate Generated Locally

Certificate Generated in Cohesity Certificate Store

If you choose to generate a certificate locally and use it for registration, follow this workflow:
l Generate the certificate locally. The certificate display name can be up to 32 characters long, and the maximum permitted validity is 397 days. For more information on guidelines to generate certificates, see Certificates.
l Map the certificate to the respective Azure application in the Azure portal.
l Assign one additional permission to the Azure application, Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy.
l Import the certificate into the Cohesity Certificate Store. l Use this certificate during registration.
The certificate type is displayed as Imported.

Note:
l

Certificates generated locally are not renewed automatically; you must renew the certificate manually before it expires.

l When importing the custom certificates, the certificates must be uploaded to the Azure application before clicking Register in the UI, which will otherwise cause the registration to fail.

If you choose to generate a certificate in the Cohesity Certificate Store and use it for registration, follow this workflow:
l Generate the certificate directly in the Cohesity Certificate Store.
l You download the certificate.
l Map the certificate to the respective Azure application in the Azure portal.
l Assign one additional permission to the Azure application, Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy.
l You use this certificate during registration.
The certificate type is displayed as Generated.
Note: Certificates generated by Cohesity are valid for one year. By default, Cohesity attempts to renew certificates 60 days before their expiration date. If the renewal attempt fails, alerts and warnings are displayed 45 days before the certificates expire.

Registration Workflows and Authentication Methods
When registering your Microsoft 365 domain with Cloud Protection Service, you must decide which registration workflow and authentication method to use.

Workflow/Authentication Method Registration workflows
Authentication methods

Description
You can use one of the following workflows: l Manual Registration: In this workflow, you create the required number of Azure applications in your Azure portal, assign the recommended permissions to the applications, and then provide the application details such as App ID and Client Secret in the Cloud Protection Service UI while registering the source. l Express Registration: In this workflow, Cloud Protection Service automatically creates the Azure application in your Azure portal and assigns the required permissions. The same application is then used for registration.
You can use one of the following authentication methods for the Azure application: l Client Secret Authentication: The Azure application authenticates using an App ID and a Client Secret. l Certificate-Based Authentication (CBA): The Azure application authenticates using an X.509 certificate instead of a Client Secret, providing phishing-resistant authentication.

The following combinations of workflow and authentication method are available for registration:
l Express Registration for Microsoft 365 Sources Using Client Secret l Manual Registration for Microsoft 365 Sources Using Client Secret l Express Registration for Microsoft 365 Sources Using Certificate-Based Authentication l Manual Registration for Microsoft 365 Sources Using Certificate-Based Authentication

EWS to Graph API Migration for User and Shared Mailboxes
The user and shared primary mailboxes can be transitioned to use Microsoft Graph APIs instead of Exchange Web Services (EWS) APIs for backup and recovery.
Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Considerations
Before you enable EWS to Graph API Migration for user and shared mailboxes, you must review the following considerations.
l Microsoft is deprecating EWS in April 2027. To continue using EWS until then, you must configure your tenant by October 1, 2026. For more information, see Microsoft's EWS deprecation announcement.
l When the EWS-to-Graph API migration feature is enabled on your Cohesity cluster, Cohesity checks whether all Azure applications registered with the source have the required Graph API permissions.
l After transitioning from EWS APIs to Microsoft Graph APIs, the following mailbox folders will no longer be backed up because Microsoft Graph APIs do not support them. l Primary Mailbox folders l Archive Mailbox folders
l Cohesity now supports Exchange Online mailbox backup and recovery using Microsoft Graph APIs, replacing Exchange Web Services (EWS) APIs. This transition ensures seamless and uninterrupted mailbox protection while providing greater flexibility and compatibility. Existing backups remain fully usable, with no need for data re-ingestion. The EWS to Graph transition supports only user and shared primary mailboxes in this release. Teams mailboxes, Groups mailboxes and user/shared mailboxes that protect the in-place archive continue to use EWS.
l Data that was previously backed up from these folders using EWS remains available for recovery from existing snapshots taken before the Graph transition. New snapshots taken after the transition will not include these folders.
Prerequisites
Before starting, ensure all Azure applications registered with your Microsoft 365 source have the required Graph API permissions. For the full list of permissions, see Register Custom App in Microsoft Entra ID. The following new permissions must be added:
l MailboxItem.ImportExport.All l MailboxFolder.ReadWrite.All

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Register Microsoft 365 Sources

l MailboxItem.Read.All l Mail.Read l Tasks.Read.All l Calendars.Read l Contacts.Read
Add Graph API permissions to an existing Microsoft 365 source
1. Navigate to Sources and click Register > Microsoft 365. 2. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Microsoft 365 source and then click Edit. 3. If Graph API permissions are missing from any Azure application, the following
warning banner appears in the Azure application ID section: "This source is not yet ready to migrate APIs for Mailbox from EWS to Graph due to missing permissions." 4. Do one of the following as required:
1. To add permissions automatically (recommended): Click Update App Permissions. This initiates the Express workflow using a device code flow to add all required Graph permissions to each application ID.
2. To add permissions manually: In the Azure portal, navigate to App Registrations and add the required Graph API permissions to each registered App ID. For the complete list of permissions, see the Permission Descriptions topic in Register Custom App in Microsoft Entra ID. You can also click the Learn More link in the banner to view the permissions page.
5. Click Register to save the updated source configuration. 6. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Microsoft 365 source and select Refresh.

Exchange Online Mailboxes
Microsoft Exchange Online is a SaaS application that is bundled in your Microsoft 365 subscription service. It is a hosted messaging solution that delivers the capabilities of Microsoft Exchange Server as a cloud-based service. It gives users access to email, calendar, contacts, and tasks from PCs, the web, and mobile devices. Using the policy-

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Exchange Online Mailboxes

based data protection solution from Cohesity, you can protect Exchange Online data on Microsoft 365.

Cohesity now supports Exchange Online mailbox backup and recovery using Microsoft Graph APIs, replacing Exchange Web Services (EWS) APIs. This transition ensures seamless and uninterrupted mailbox protection while providing greater flexibility and compatibility. Existing backups remain fully usable, with no need for data re-ingestion. The EWS to Graph transition supports only user and shared primary mailboxes in this release. Teams mailboxes, Groups mailboxes and user/shared mailboxes that protect the in-place archive continue to use EWS. If your Cohesity cluster has the EWS-to-Graph migration feature enabled, Express Registration is the recommended method to register a new source.
Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Plan and Prepare for Mailbox Protection
Before you register your Microsoft 365 domain with Cohesity to protect Microsoft 365 data, ensure:
l You have completed all the Prerequisites. l You have reviewed and understood the Considerationsand Best Practices.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Exchange Online Mailboxes

Important: By September 2026, Cohesity will migrate from Exchange Web Services (EWS) APIs to Microsoft Graph APIs to protect Microsoft 365 Applications. This is as per the Retirement of Exchange Web Services in Exchange Online announcement from Microsoft. For more information, see Deprecation of Exchange Web Services in Exchange Online.
As part of the migration to Microsoft Graph APIs, Cohesity now supports Exchange Online mailbox backup and recovery using Microsoft Graph APIs as an Early Access feature, replacing Exchange Web Services (EWS) APIs. This transition ensures seamless and uninterrupted mailbox protection while providing greater flexibility and compatibility. Existing backups remain fully usable, with no need for data re-ingestion. The EWS to Graph transition supports only user and shared primary mailboxes in this release. Teams mailboxes, Groups mailboxes and user/shared mailboxes that protect the in-place archive continue to use EWS.
Considerations
Review and understand the following considerations before you protect your Microsoft 365 Exchange Online data:
l Recovery can be performed at the mailbox, folder, or item level. Currently, recovery at the Protection Group level is not supported.
l Recovery of items in the same mailbox from different recovery points is not supported in the same recovery task. You need to create different recovery tasks for different recovery points.
l If the email already exists at the destination during the recovery workflow, the email will be updated
l The backup or recovery of Mailboxes, OneDrives, SharePoint Online Sites, and MS Teams are executed in parallel as long as there are enough resources on the Cohesity cluster. However, the backup or recovery operations are serialized for the Mailboxes and OneDrives that belong to the same user, and the operations execute in first-infirst-out order.
For example, if the backup of a user's mailbox is in progress, then the backup of the user's OneDrive starts only after the backup of the mailbox completes.
l Converted-shared mailboxes are not backed up by default. To enable backup of converted-shared mailboxes, contact Cohesity Support.
l The Retirement of RBAC Application Impersonation in Exchange Online has no known impact on the Microsoft 365 Exchange Online Mailboxes, Teams, and Groups protection workflow on the Cohesity cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Exchange Online Mailboxes

l By default, the Conversation History/Team Chat folder is excluded during the Exchange Online backup.
l Following the Microsoft changes for EWS APIs, Cohesity no longer backs up mailbox items of the type IPM.Teams.SkypeMessage. For more details, see the KB Article.
l Exchange Online Mailboxes protection is supported only for users present on Azure AD and not for users on the on-premises Active Directory.
l Exchange Online Mailboxes protection is: Supported for: l Users present in Azure AD l Hybrid setup with users present on Azure AD Not supported for: l Users on on-premises Active Directory l Users natively on on-premises Active Directory that are synchronized to Azure AD
l Microsoft 365 items with only special characters will not be listed in granular search. The item name must contain at least one alphanumeric character to be listed in the search result.
l Cohesity supports protecting 100k Microsoft 365 objects. This includes the following: l Objects on individual applications, for example, 100k Mailboxes. l Objects on combined applications, for example, 50k Mailboxes, 30k Teams, and 20k Groups.
Validation messages are displayed when backing up more than 7500 objects and recovering more than 5000 objects.
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
l Backup and recovery of Recoverable Items: l Deletions, Purges, Discovery Holds, and SubstrateHolds folders are currently supported for backup and restore.
l Audits, Calendar Logging, and Versions folders are not supported. l Backup and download of the following is not supported:
l Self-message (messages sent to self) l Saved or pinned messages property in the conversation

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Exchange Online Mailboxes

l Meeting recordings metadata from private chats l Emojis and Stickers l Restoration at the protection group level is not supported for Microsoft 365.
l Recovery for items in the same mailbox from different recovery points is not supported in the same recovery task. You need to create different recovery tasks for different recovery points.
l If the size of the mailbox is large, then exporting the mailbox to PST format takes a longer duration.
l The exported PST of the mailbox or the email is valid for 72 hours. Ensure that you download the PST file within 72 hours of the recovery task completion.
l PST recovery of emails with more than 2000 recipients is not supported.
l The Cohesity cluster and connector must be a member of the same or any trusted AD for PST recovery.
l Backup and recovery of files with sensitivity labels is supported. For files with sensitivity labels, l Only a user with access via the label can open the file after downloading, provided the label is not permanently deleted in SharePoint. l When recovering to original location, if the file is already present in the destination, the recovery fails. If the file is not present in the destination, a new file will be created. l The files downloaded from SharePoint are encrypted. You can download the same file from the backup storage.
l Backup and download of Teams Chat are supported; however, restore is not supported currently.
l Backup and recovery of Exchange Online mailboxes using security groups is supported. You must review the following considerations before protecting mailboxes using a security group:
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
l Each protection group can contain only one security group. Mixing multiple security groups within the same protection group is not supported.
l The member count for a security group includes only users present in the Entity Hierarchy, regardless of whether they have a valid mailbox or OneDrive license. If a user's license is removed, they remain in the count until the next source refresh filters them out. Members without a valid license will fail individually

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Exchange Online Mailboxes

during backup, but the protection job proceeds for the remaining members.
l Security group membership is fetched from Microsoft Entra ID. Newly added members are included in the next scheduled refresh; members removed from the group or deleted from Entra ID are automatically excluded after the next refresh. If security group optimization is enabled, members are not fetched during the entity hierarchy refresh and are instead fetched during the backup run.
l Security group protection is supported only for the members of the security group, not the owners of the group.
l Both mail-enabled and mail-disabled security groups are supported.
l Members of nested security groups are automatically included in protection. The member count displayed reflects the unique (deduplicated) count across all levels of nesting.
l If the selected security group has no members, the protection job fails. Jobs resume normally once members are added to the group and the next entity hierarchy refresh completes.
l Remove the protection group manually if the security group is deleted from Entra ID.
l If a user is a member of two security groups that are each assigned to a separate protection group, that user's mailbox or OneDrive is backed up by both protection jobs.
l The security group itself is manually selected for protection; individual members within the group are treated as auto-protected.
l Recovery of mailboxes or OneDrives protected via a security group follows the same workflow as recovery of individually protected objects. There is no change to recovery workflows.
l Backup and recovery of external users from a security group is supported.
Best Practices
To protect your Microsoft 365 data, Cohesity recommends the following best practices:
l Set Retry Options to 1, as the Microsoft 365 connector already has the retry mechanism handling failed requests. There is no need to increase the value for this setting in the Cohesity Protection Policy.
l Use Auto-Protect to avoid adding new users to the Protection Group manually. l Avoid adding the same users in multiple Protection Groups.
EWS to Graph API Migration for User and Shared Mailboxes
The user and shared primary mailboxes can be transitioned to use Microsoft Graph APIs instead of Exchange Web Services (EWS) APIs for backup and recovery.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Exchange Online Mailboxes

Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Considerations
Before you enable EWS to Graph API Migration for user and shared mailboxes, you must review the following considerations.
l Microsoft is deprecating EWS in April 2027. To continue using EWS until then, you must configure your tenant by October 1, 2026. For more information, see Microsoft's EWS deprecation announcement.
l When the EWS-to-Graph API migration feature is enabled on your Cohesity cluster, Cohesity checks whether all Azure applications registered with the source have the required Graph API permissions.
l After transitioning from EWS APIs to Microsoft Graph APIs, the following mailbox folders will no longer be backed up because Microsoft Graph APIs do not support them. l Primary Mailbox folders l Archive Mailbox folders
l Cohesity now supports Exchange Online mailbox backup and recovery using Microsoft Graph APIs, replacing Exchange Web Services (EWS) APIs. This transition ensures seamless and uninterrupted mailbox protection while providing greater flexibility and compatibility. Existing backups remain fully usable, with no need for data re-ingestion. The EWS to Graph transition supports only user and shared primary mailboxes in this release. Teams mailboxes, Groups mailboxes and user/shared mailboxes that protect the in-place archive continue to use EWS.
l Data that was previously backed up from these folders using EWS remains available for recovery from existing snapshots taken before the Graph transition. New snapshots taken after the transition will not include these folders.
Prerequisites
Before starting, ensure all Azure applications registered with your Microsoft 365 source have the required Graph API permissions. For the full list of permissions, see Register Custom App in Microsoft Entra ID. The following new permissions must be added:
l MailboxItem.ImportExport.All l MailboxFolder.ReadWrite.All l MailboxItem.Read.All l Mail.Read l Tasks.Read.All

Exchange Online Mailboxes

l Calendars.Read l Contacts.Read
Add Graph API permissions to an existing Microsoft 365 source
1. Navigate to Sources and click Register > Microsoft 365. 2. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Microsoft 365 source and then click Edit. 3. If Graph API permissions are missing from any Azure application, the following
warning banner appears in the Azure application ID section: "This source is not yet ready to migrate APIs for Mailbox from EWS to Graph due to missing permissions." 4. Do one of the following as required:
1. To add permissions automatically (recommended): Click Update App Permissions. This initiates the Express workflow using a device code flow to add all required Graph permissions to each application ID.
2. To add permissions manually: In the Azure portal, navigate to App Registrations and add the required Graph API permissions to each registered App ID. For the complete list of permissions, see the Permission Descriptions topic in Register Custom App in Microsoft Entra ID. You can also click the Learn More link in the banner to view the permissions page.
5. Click Register to save the updated source configuration. 6. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Microsoft 365 source and select Refresh.
Verify that the warning banner is no longer displayed on the source. The source is ready for the Graph API migration. The next incremental backup for each mailbox will run a transition backup (using both EWS and Graph APIs). Subsequent backups will use Graph APIs only.
Backup Exchange Online Mailboxes
Exchange Online mailboxes are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group enables you to select and group the objects that you want to back up. It uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured and replicated. A Protection Policy is a group of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. Also, for Disaster Recovery, you can add replication for the Protection Group using the Protection Policy. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more information, see Manage Protection Policy. Before you proceed with recovery, you must review the considerations. For more information, see Plan and Prepare for Mailbox Protection. Policy Settings for Exchange Online
The following table lists the applicable policy settings for Exchange Online:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Exchange Online Mailboxes

Field DataLock

Description
Add a DataLock for compliance and regulatory requirement. This ensures that your protected data, including local backups, archives, and replication, cannot be modified until the DataLock expiration. Once applied, a DataLocked Snapshot will be deleted only after its retention period expires. A DataLock prevents all users from modifying or deleting any Snapshots that were generated by the protection runs that use this Policy. The users include those who have the Data Security role in Cohesity as well.
Note: Only users with the Data Security role can add, modify, or remove a DataLock from a Policy.

Scheduled Backup

Defines when backups are captured, how long they are retained, and the type of backup to capture.

Extended Retention

Add this to retain a subset of snapshots (backups) for longer duration than defined by the protection schedule.

Retry Options

Use this option to customize the retry settings for capturing Snapshots. By default, Cohesity attempts to capture Snapshots three times before the protection run fails. The default time between retries is thirty minutes. You can customize the number of retries and how long to wait between each attempt.

Note: Set Retry Options to 1, as the Microsoft 365 connector already has the retry mechanism handling the failed requests. There is no need to increase the value for this setting in the Protection Policy.

Quiet Times Replication

Quiet Times define time periods when new protection runs are not started. For example, you might want to configure hourly backups that run during weekdays but not on Saturdays or Sundays. Quiet Times only prevent new protection runs from starting during the specified time period. The protection runs that started before the quiet time period are not affected and will continue to run.
For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time period that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet time period.
Replicate snapshots to another Cohesity cluster.

Enable or Disable Auto Protect
The Auto Protect option enables you to automatically protect the new mailboxes that are added to Microsoft 365. When the Auto Protect option is enabled:
l All the mailboxes that are added to Microsoft 365 in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run.
l All the mailboxes that are removed from Microsoft 365 in the future are automatically removed from the Protection Group and are not protected from the next protection run. The existing backup for the user is preserved until the snapshot expires.
When the Auto Protect option is disabled, you need to manually:
l Add newly onboarded users on Microsoft 365 to the Protection Group. l Remove existing users that are offboarded on Microsoft 365 from the Protection
Group. The existing backups of the users are preserved until the snapshot expires.

Exchange Online Public Folders
Cohesity enables data protection of Microsoft Exchange Online. Cohesity provides a policybased data protection solution for protecting Microsoft Exchange Online Public Folders on Microsoft 365.
Note: Starting October 2026, Cohesity will discontinue support for Public Folder protection, following Microsoft's retirement of APIs for managing Public Folders.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Exchange Online Public Folders

Plan and Prepare for Public Folders Protection
Before you register your Microsoft 365 domain with Cohesity to protect Microsoft 365 data, ensure:
l You have completed all the Prerequisites. l You have reviewed and understood the Considerations and Best Practices. l An Exchange Online license with a mailbox provisioned. l A default Public folder mailbox configured (preferably Primary).
Considerations
Review and understand the following considerations before you protect your Exchange Online public folder data:
l For public folder backups, if you move a subfolder from one root folder to another root folder, a full backup of the subfolder will be performed in the next run.
l Exclusion list is not supported for Public Folders Protection Group. l Suppose a newly added folder at any location in the folder hierarchy does not have
the required permissions mentioned in required Public Folder Root Permissions for Microsoft 365 User Account. The folder, including its subfolders, is not discoverable and hence will not be backed up by Cohesity. l Microsoft does not support OAuth for Public Folders and backups will fail if you have enabled OAuth for Exchange Online backup.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Exchange Online Public Folders

l Restoring the public folder or content of the public folder from the backup to an alternate location in a different Microsoft 365 domain is not supported.
l Public Folders are not supported in Government Community Cloud (GCC) High. l Microsoft 365 items with only special characters will not be listed in granular search.
The item name must contain at least one alphanumeric character to be listed in the search result. l Backup and recovery of files with sensitivity labels is supported. For files with sensitivity labels,
l Only a user with access via the label can open the file after downloading, provided the label is not permanently deleted in SharePoint.
l When recovering to original location, if the file is already present in the destination, the recovery fails. If the file is not present in the destination, a new file will be created.
l The files downloaded from SharePoint as encrypted. You can download the same file from the backup storage.
Best Practices
To protect your Microsoft 365 data, Cohesity recommends the following best practices:
l Set Retry Options to 1, as the Microsoft 365 connector already has the retry mechanism handling failed requests. There is no need to increase the value for this setting in the Cohesity Protection Policy.
l Use Auto-Protect to avoid adding new users to the Protection Group manually. l Avoid adding the same users in multiple Protection Groups.
Register and Manage Microsoft 365 Exchange Online Public Folders
To start protecting Microsoft 365 applications, you need to register the Microsoft 365 domain as a source in Cohesity. Cohesity uses the Microsoft Graph API for object discovery, backup, and recovery in Microsoft 365. Cohesity uses an Azure application created and registered on the Azure portal with the necessary permissions to use the Graph API. You can either let Cohesity create the Azure application or you can manually enter Azure application details while registering your Microsoft 365 domain as a source in Cohesity.
Express Registration for Microsoft 365 Sources
Before you register Office 365 as a source on Cohesity, ensure that you:
l Review the requirements, considerations, and best practices. l Perform the prerequisite tasks.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Exchange Online Public Folders

1. Navigate to Sources and select Register > Microsoft 365. 2. Choose Public Folders as the Microsoft 365 Applications to discover. 3. In the Account Credentials section, enter the Microsoft 365 Username and

4. Adding multiple Microsoft 365 service accounts using the Additional Service Accounts section requires OAuth disabled, as Microsoft has enabled OAuth by default, ignore adding multiple Microsoft 365 service accounts.

Policy Settings for Exchange Online
The following table lists the applicable policy settings for Exchange Online:

Field DataLock

Description
Add a DataLock for compliance and regulatory requirement. This ensures that your protected data, including local backups, archives, and replication, cannot be modified until the DataLock expiration. Once applied, a DataLocked Snapshot will be deleted only after its retention period expires. A DataLock prevents all users from modifying or deleting any Snapshots that were generated by the protection runs that use this Policy. The users include those who have the Data Security role in Cohesity as well.
Note: Only users with the Data Security role can add, modify, or remove a DataLock from a Policy.
