Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Exchange Online Public Folders

Field

Description

Scheduled Backup

Defines when backups are captured, how long they are retained, and the type of backup to capture.

Extended Retention

Add this to retain a subset of snapshots (backups) for longer duration than defined by the protection schedule.

Retry Options

Use this option to customize the retry settings for capturing Snapshots. By default, Cohesity attempts to capture Snapshots three times before the protection run fails. The default time between retries is thirty minutes. You can customize the number of retries and how long to wait between each attempt.

Note: Set Retry Options to 1, as the Microsoft 365 connector already has the retry mechanism handling the failed requests. There is no need to increase the value for this setting in the Protection Policy.

Quiet Times Replication

Quiet Times define time periods when new protection runs are not started. For example, you might want to configure hourly backups that run during weekdays but not on Saturdays or Sundays. Quiet Times only prevent new protection runs from starting during the specified time period. The protection runs that started before the quiet time period are not affected and will continue to run.
For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time period that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet time period.
Replicate snapshots to another Cohesity cluster.

Enable or Disable Auto Protect
The Auto Protect option enables you to automatically protect the new public folder(s) that are added to Microsoft 365. When the Auto Protect option is enabled:
l All the public folders that are added to Microsoft 365 in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run.
l All the public folders that are removed from Microsoft 365 in the future are automatically removed from the Protection Group and are not protected from the next protection run. The existing backups for the public folder are preserved until the snapshot expires.
When the Auto Protect option is disabled, you need to manually:
l Add newly onboarded public folder on Microsoft 365 to the Protection Group. l Remove existing public folders that are offboarded on Microsoft 365 from the
Protection Group. The existing backups of the public folders are preserved until the snapshot expires.

OneDrive for Business
OneDrive for Business is a SaaS application that is bundled in your Microsoft 365 subscription service. It is an intelligent files app for Microsoft 365 connecting you to all your files so you can share and work together from anywhere while protecting your work. It enables you to easily store, access, and discover your individual and shared work files in Microsoft 365. Using the policy-based data protection solution from Cohesity, you can protect OneDrive for Business data on Microsoft 365.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

OneDrive for Business

Plan and Prepare for OneDrive Protection
Before you register your Microsoft 365 domain with Cohesity to protect Microsoft 365 data, ensure:
l You have completed all the Prerequisites. l You have reviewed and understood the Considerations and Best Practices.
Considerations
l SharePoint does not support file or folder names that contain unsupported special characters. Backup, restore, or download of such items is not supported. See, Restrictions and limitations in OneDrive and SharePoint.
l Backup and recovery of OneNote files in OneDrive is supported. Consider the following:
l Certificate-based authentication must be enabled. For more information, see Microsoft 365 Certificate-Based Authentication.
l The first OneNote backup after enabling this feature may take longer than usual incremental backups, as it will include all OneNote files that were previously skipped.
l Backup and recovery of the Recycle Bin in OneDrive is not supported.
l Backup of the mailbox and the OneDrive for an individual user happens sequentially. However, backup of mailboxes and OneDrive belonging to different users may happen in parallel.
l The backup or recovery of Mailboxes, OneDrives, SharePoint Online Sites, and MS Teams are executed in parallel as long as there are enough resources on the Cohesity cluster. However, the backup or recovery operations are serialized for the Mailboxes and OneDrives that belong to the same user, and the operations execute in the firstin-first-out order.
For example, if the backup of a user's mailbox is in progress, then the backup of the user's OneDrive starts only after the backup of the mailbox completes.
l The user list containing users with protected mailboxes shows as protected when creating a Protection Group for OneDrive and vice-versa.
l OneDrive protection is supported only for users present on Azure AD or Hybrid setup with users present on Azure AD and not for users on the on-premises Active Directory.
l File/folder permissions with no role will not be recovered since Microsoft does not allow adding such permissions via Graph APIs. For example, no role will be assigned when a Restricted View permission is added to a user from Advanced Setting.
l OneDrive does not support item permissions from applications and devices.
l Microsoft 365 items with only special characters will not be listed in granular search. The item name must contain at least one alphanumeric character to be listed in the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

OneDrive for Business

search result. l Permissions are recovered only at file level and not folder level. l If more than 50 thousand files are present, the permissions are recovered only for 50
thousand files (there is no option to identify these files in advance). l Sharing links permissions are not recovered. l Cohesity supports protecting 100k Microsoft 365 objects.
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
This includes the following: l Objects on individual applications, for example, 100k Teams. l Objects on combined applications, for example, 50k Teams, 30k Mailboxes, and 20k Groups.
Validation messages are displayed when backing up more than 7500 objects and recovering more than 5000 objects. l Backup and recovery of Preservation Hold Library (PHL) is supported. Consider the following points:
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Note: PHL is a hidden, system-managed library that OneDrive and SharePoint automatically create when a retention policy, retention label, or legal/eDiscovery hold is applied. It stores preserved copies of files that are edited or deleted while under retention.
l Shared permissions are not restored: Recovering PHL data recovers the file content only. Any sharing permissions it had must be reapplied manually after recovery.
l No granular recovery: PHL data can only be recovered as part of a full OneDrive recovery; individual PHL files or folders cannot be recovered.
l PHL data is not searchable: PHL data is not indexed by standard Microsoft Search and cannot be browsed or searched directly.
l Recovery time and space impact: Recovering PHL data may increase

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

OneDrive for Business

recovery time substantially. Recovery will fail if sufficient space is not available at the target location.
l Backup and recovery of files with sensitivity labels is supported. For files with sensitivity labels:
l Only a user with access via the label can open the file after downloading, provided the label is not permanently deleted in SharePoint.
l When recovering to original location, if the file is already present in the destination, the recovery fails. If the file is not present in the destination, a new file will be created.
l The files downloaded from SharePoint as encrypted. You can download the same file from the backup storage.
l The following metadata fields are restored when SharePoint data is restored:
l Created By (author)
l Modified By (editor)
l Created Date
l Modified Date
During cross-domain restore operations, the Created By (author) and Modified By (editor) fields are not restored because the corresponding users from the source domain will be unavailable in the target domain. The Created By metadata is not restored if the user referenced in the Created By field is deleted. The Modified By and Created By metadata are not restored if the user referenced in the Modified By field is deleted.
l Backup and recovery of Exchange Online mailboxes using security groups is supported. You must review the following considerations before protecting mailboxes using a security group:
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
l Each protection group can contain only one security group. Mixing multiple security groups within the same protection group is not supported.
l The member count for a security group includes only users present in the Entity Hierarchy, regardless of whether they have a valid mailbox or OneDrive license. If a user's license is removed, they remain in the count until the next source refresh filters them out. Members without a valid license will fail individually during backup, but the protection job proceeds for the remaining members.
l Security group membership is fetched from Microsoft Entra ID. Newly added members are included in the next scheduled refresh; members removed from

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

OneDrive for Business

the group or deleted from Entra ID are automatically excluded after the next refresh. If security group optimization is enabled, members are not fetched during the entity hierarchy refresh and are instead fetched during the backup run.
l Security group protection is supported only for the members of the security group, not the owners of the group.
l Both mail-enabled and mail-disabled security groups are supported.
l Members of nested security groups are automatically included in protection. The member count displayed reflects the unique (deduplicated) count across all levels of nesting.
l If the selected security group has no members, the protection job fails. Jobs resume normally once members are added to the group and the next entity hierarchy refresh completes.
l Remove the protection group manually if the security group is deleted from Entra ID.
l If a user is a member of two security groups that are each assigned to a separate protection group, that user's mailbox or OneDrive is backed up by both protection jobs.
l The security group itself is manually selected for protection; individual members within the group are treated as auto-protected.
l Recovery of mailboxes or OneDrives protected via a security group follows the same workflow as recovery of individually protected objects. There is no change to recovery workflows.
l Backup and recovery of external users from a security group is supported.

l Use Auto Protect to avoid adding new users to the Protection Group manually. l Avoid adding the same users in multiple Protection Groups.

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. QoS policies are designed for workloads such as backups, which keep a lot of IOs outstanding. We recommend one of the following:
l Backup Target HDD (Default): This policy assumes higher latency is OK and the workload will get high throughput if it issues a lot of writes in parallel. The data lands on hard disks if it is sequential and on SSDs if it is random writes.
l Backup Target SSD: With this policy, both sequential and random IOs land on SSDs, but the IOs are not treated as high-priority IOs and we assume the workload keeps lots of IOs outstanding.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
Select the paths that you plan to exclude from the backup.

Create or Use an Existing Protection Policy
A Protection Policy is a reusable set of settings. It enables you to define how and when OneDrive data is protected and replicated. A standard policy provides various settings that you can configure for a Protection Group. Create a Protection Policy with the settings listed in the Policy Settings for OneDrive. For detailed instructions on how to create a Protection Policy, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.
Policy Settings for OneDrive
The following table lists the applicable policy settings for OneDrive:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

OneDrive for Business

Field DataLock

Description
Add a DataLock for compliance and regulatory requirement. This ensures that your protected data, including local backups, archives, and replication, cannot be modified until the DataLock expiration. Once applied, a DataLocked Snapshot will be deleted only after its retention period expires. A DataLock prevents all users from modifying or deleting any Snapshots that were generated by the protection runs that use this Policy. The users include those who have the Data Security role in Cohesity as well.
Note: Only users with the Data Security role can add, modify, or remove a DataLock from a Policy.

Scheduled Backup

Defines when backups are captured, how long they are retained, and the type of backup to capture.

Extended Retention

Add this to retain a subset of snapshots (backups) for longer duration than defined by the protection schedule.

Retry Options

Use this option to customize the retry settings for capturing Snapshots. By default, Cohesity attempts to capture Snapshots three times before the protection run fails. The default time between retries is thirty minutes. You can customize the number of retries and how long to wait between each attempt.

Note: Set Retry Options to 1, as the Microsoft 365 connector already has the retry mechanism handling the failed requests. There is no need to increase the value for this setting in the Protection Policy.

Quiet Times Replication

Quiet Times define time periods when new protection runs are not started. For example, you might want to configure hourly backups that run during weekdays but not on Saturdays or Sundays. Quiet Times only prevent new protection runs from starting during the specified time period. The protection runs that started before the quiet time period are not affected and will continue to run.
For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time period that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet time period.
Replicate snapshots to another Cohesity cluster.

Enable or Disable Auto Protect
The Auto Protect option enables you to automatically protect the new OneDrives that are added to Microsoft 365. When the Auto Protect option is enabled:
l All the OneDrives that are added to Microsoft 365 in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run.
l All the OneDrives that are removed from Microsoft 365 in the future are automatically removed from the Protection Group and are not protected from the next protection run. The existing backup for the user is preserved until the snapshot expires.
When the Auto Protect option is disabled, you need to manually:
l Add newly onboarded users on Microsoft 365 to the Protection Group. l Remove existing users that are offboarded on Microsoft 365 from the Protection
Group. The existing backups of the users are preserved until the snapshot expires.
To enable or disable Auto Protect:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for
OneDrive.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit.
4. On the Microsoft 365 - OneDrive page, click in the Users section. 5. From the User list, click the shield icon to enable or disable Auto Protect. 6. Click Protect.

SharePoint Online
SharePoint Online is a SaaS application bundled with the Microsoft 365 service. It provides an extensive range of collaborative and creative capabilities enabling organizations to share, manage, and access information from almost any device. Using the policy-based data protection solution from Cohesity, you can back up and recover the SharePoint Online site templates. Thus enabling you to backup and recover the SharePoint Online sites or subsites and their contents such as document libraries, lists, view, and so on.

Site Tagging
SharePoint Online sites are containers that are used to store and organize information in SharePoint. Sites can be standalone or can be associated with Groups and Teams referred to as Groups sites and Teams sites respectively. The Site Tagging option categorizes the sites and tags them to their respective containers.
Note: Any Site that is tagged as a Group or Team will not be visible in the Sites section and these sites will be protected through the corresponding Group or Team protection.

l Unsupported items for site pages recovery to an alternate location When recovering site pages to a new or alternate location, the following items are not recovered:
l Page analytics
l Page favorite status
l Pin to Top status
l Comments
l Likes
l Save for Later actions
l Site page granular recovery behavior These considerations apply to both full site recovery and granular recovery, and to both original and alternate location recoveries.
l Granular recovery to an alternate location always recovers only the content. Referenced images and files are not recovered. Links and IDs referenced in the site page are not changed; as a result, links and web parts may not work.
l Granular recovery recovers only the latest version of the site pages when recovering to the original location or alternate location.
l Granular recovery of individual site pages is supported only to an existing site pages document library. Recovery to a different document library is not supported.
l Unsupported site pages features Recovered site pages may have layout and functionality inconsistencies for the following:
l Flexible Sections
l Picture as Section Background
l Page Title Formatting
l Empty Sections
l Site pages library prerequisite If the site pages library is deleted, it must be manually created before initiating

Best Practices
To protect your SharePoint Online data, Cohesity recommends the following best practices:
l In the Protection Policy, set Retry Options to 2 or 3, with a small interval between the retry attempts.
l Use Auto Protect to automatically include the newly added sites on SharePoint Online to the Protection Group.
l Avoid adding the same sites in multiple Protection Groups.
Backup SharePoint Online
SharePoint Online is protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group enables you to select the objects that you want to back up. It uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured and replicated.
A Protection Policy is a reusable list of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. Also, for Disaster Recovery, you can add replication for the Protection Group using the Protection Policy. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more details, see Manage Protection Policy.

Policy Settings for SharePoint Online
The following table lists the applicable policy settings for SharePoint Online:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

SharePoint Online

Field DataLock

Description
Add a DataLock for compliance and regulatory requirement. This ensures that your protected data, including local backups, archives, and replication, cannot be modified until the DataLock expiration. Once applied, a DataLocked Snapshot will be deleted only after its retention period expires. A DataLock prevents all users from modifying or deleting any Snapshots that were generated by the protection runs that use this Policy. The users include those who have the Data Security role in Cohesity as well.
Note: Only users with the Data Security role can add, modify, or remove a DataLock from a Policy.

Scheduled Backup

Defines when backups are captured, how long they are retained, and the type of backup to capture.

Extended Retention

Add this to retain a subset of snapshots (backups) for longer duration than defined by the protection schedule.

Retry Options

Use this option to customize the retry settings for capturing Snapshots. By default, Cohesity attempts to capture Snapshots three times before the protection run fails. The default time between retries is thirty minutes. You can customize the number of retries and how long to wait between each attempt.

Note: Set Retry Options to 1, as the Microsoft 365 connector already has the retry mechanism handling the failed requests. There is no need to increase the value for this setting in the Protection Policy.

Quiet Times Replication

Quiet Times define time periods when new protection runs are not started. For example, you might want to configure hourly backups that run during weekdays but not on Saturdays or Sundays. Quiet Times only prevent new protection runs from starting during the specified time period. The protection runs that started before the quiet time period are not affected and will continue to run.
For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time period that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet time period.
Replicate snapshots to another Cohesity cluster.

Enable or Disable Auto Protect
The Auto Protect option enables you to automatically protect the new sites that are added to Microsoft 365. When the Auto Protect option is enabled:
l All the sites that are added to SharePoint Online in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run.
l All the sites that are removed from SharePoint Online in the future are automatically removed from the Protection Group and are not protected from the next protection run. The existing backup for the site is preserved until the snapshot expires.
When the Auto Protect option is disabled, you need to manually: l Add newly onboarded sites on SharePoint Online to the Protection Group. l Remove existing sites that are offboarded on SharePoint Online from the Protection Group. The existing backups of the sites are preserved until the snapshot expires.

Considerations
l Restoring to an alternate Microsoft 365 domain is not supported. l Backup and recovery of OneNote files in Groups is supported. Consider the following:
l Certificate-based authentication must be enabled. For more information, see Microsoft 365 Certificate-Based Authentication.

incremental backups, as it will include all OneNote files that were previously skipped. l Using a Group recovery job, you can restore only one Group. l Recovering system document libraries (libraries that are present in the Group site by default - Site Assets, Style Library, Documents, and Form Templates) is not supported. l The files downloaded from SharePoint are encrypted. You can download the same file from the backup storage.

Backup Microsoft 365 Groups
Microsoft 365 Groups data is protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group enables you to select the objects that you want to back up. It uses the schedules and settings defined in the Protection Policy to determine when and how backups are captured and replicated. A Protection Policy is a reusable list of settings that define the type of backup, backup schedule, and backup snapshot retention. Also, for Disaster Recovery, you can add replication for the Protection Group using the Protection Policy. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. For more details, see Manage Protection Policy.

Description
Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy.
Note: Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.
l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Protection Groups.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve a similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.
By default, indexing is enabled.

l Failure: Creates a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Creates a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created. For more information, see Alerts.

Policy Settings for Microsoft 365 Groups
The following table lists the applicable policy settings for Microsoft 365 Groups:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Groups

Field DataLock

Description
Add a DataLock for compliance and regulatory requirement. This ensures that your protected data, including local backups, archives, and replication, cannot be modified until the DataLock expiration. Once applied, a DataLocked Snapshot will be deleted only after its retention period expires. A DataLock prevents all users from modifying or deleting any Snapshots that were generated by the protection runs that use this Policy. The users include those who have the Data Security role in Cohesity as well.
Note: Only users with the Data Security role can add, modify, or remove a DataLock from a Policy.

Scheduled Backup

Defines when backups are captured, how long they are retained, and the type of backup to capture.

Extended Retention

Add this to retain a subset of snapshots (backups) for longer duration than defined by the protection schedule.

Retry Options

Use this option to customize the retry settings for capturing Snapshots. By default, Cohesity attempts to capture Snapshots three times before the protection run fails. The default time between retries is thirty minutes. You can customize the number of retries and how long to wait between each attempt.

Note: Set Retry Options to 1, as the Microsoft 365 connector already has the retry mechanism handling the failed requests. There is no need to increase the value for this setting in the Protection Policy.

Quiet Times Replication

Quiet Times define time periods when new protection runs are not started. For example, you might want to configure hourly backups that run during weekdays but not on Saturdays or Sundays. Quiet Times only prevent new protection runs from starting during the specified time period. The protection runs that started before the quiet time period are not affected and will continue to run.
For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time period that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet time period.
Replicate snapshots to another Cohesity cluster.

Enable or Disable Auto Protect
The Auto Protect option enables you to automatically protect the new sites that are added to Microsoft 365. When the Auto Protect option is enabled:
l All the groups that are added to Microsoft 365 in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run.
l All the Groups that are removed from Microsoft 365 in the future are automatically removed from the Protection Group and are not protected from the next protection run. The existing backups for the user are preserved until the snapshot expires.
When the Auto Protect option is disabled, you need to manually:
l Add newly onboarded groups on Microsoft 365 to the Protection Group. l Remove existing groups that are offboarded on Microsoft 365 from the Protection
Group. The existing backups of the users are preserved until the snapshot expires.
To enable or disable Auto Protect:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for
OneDrive.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit.
4. On the Microsoft 365 - Groups page, click .
5. From the Groups list, click the icon in the domain level to enable or disable Auto Protect and click Save Selection.
6. Click Protect.

l Supported recovery scenarios l Full recovery of shared channels is supported. l Granular recovery, that is recovery of items within shared channels, is supported.
l Supported recovery destinations l Recovery to the original location is supported. l Recovery to an alternative location (different Teams and channels) in the same tenant is supported. l Recovery to an alternative location (different Teams and channels) in another tenant is supported, that is, cross-tenant recovery is supported.
l Backup and recovery of the following items in shared channels is not supported: l Sensitivity labels
l Recovery of member teams associated with shared channels is not supported. l Once enabled, shared channels are automatically included in the next Teams
backup, no job changes are required. l Shared channels are indexed and searchable, with support to download or
restore content and messages to original or alternate locations. l Backup and recovery is supported even when a shared channel has no owner. l Backup and recovery of Microsoft Teams tabs is supported. You must review the following considerations before you proceed with the backup and recovery of Teams tabs.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Teams

Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
l Supported tab types l Backup and recovery is supported only for configurable channel tabs and group chat tabs. l Personal tabs added only for one user are not supported.
l Recovery limitations l Only the last backed-up version of a tab is restored.
l Restore scope l Tabs are restored only as part of their associated Teams channel or group chat. l Granular restore of individual tabs or tab components is not supported. l Tabs cannot be restored independently outside their Team or channel.
l Permissions and access l Restoring tabs does not modify user permissions on the associated content. l Restoring PDF and OneNote tabs in newly created tenants requires Certificate-Based Authentication (CBA). l In existing tenants, the registered applications must have SharePoint Administrator permissions.
Best Practices
To protect your Microsoft 365 Teams data, Cohesity recommends the following best practices:
l In the Protection Policy, set Retry Options to 2 or 3, with a small interval between the retry attempts.
l Use Auto Protect to automatically include the newly added sites on Microsoft 365 Teams to the Protection Group.
l Avoid adding the same sites in multiple Protection Groups.

Description

QoS Policy

Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy. Note: Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.

l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group. l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Protection Group.
Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Protection Groups. l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both
SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve a similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. But it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

SLA

The service-level agreement (SLA) defines how long the administrator expects a Protection Group run to take.

l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental backup Protection Group run takes to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last run.
l Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup Protection Group run takes to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).

Note: Users with similar SLAs can be grouped together and a custom policy and Protection Group can be created to achieve different SLAs.

Policy Settings for Microsoft 365 Teams
The following table lists the applicable policy settings for Microsoft 365 Teams:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Teams

Field DataLock

Description
Add a DataLock for compliance and regulatory requirements. This ensures that your protected data, including local backups, archives, and replication, cannot be modified until the DataLock expiration. Once applied, a DataLocked Snapshot will be deleted only after its retention period expires. A DataLock prevents all users from modifying or deleting any Snapshots that were generated by the protection runs that use this Policy. The users include those who have the Data Security role in Cohesity as well.
Note: Only users with the Data Security role can add, modify, or remove a DataLock from a Policy.

Scheduled Backup

Defines when backups are captured, how long they are retained, and the type of backup to capture.

Extended Retention

Add this to retain a subset of snapshots (backups) for longer duration than defined by the protection schedule.

Retry Options

Use this option to customize the retry settings for capturing Snapshots. By default, Cohesity attempts to capture Snapshots three times before the protection run fails. The default time between retries is thirty minutes. You can customize the number of retries and how long to wait between each attempt.

Note: Set Retry Options to 1, as the Microsoft 365 connector already has the retry mechanism handling the failed requests. There is no need to increase the value for this setting in the Protection Policy.

Quiet Times

Quiet Times define time periods when new protection runs are not started. For example, you might want to configure hourly backups that run during weekdays but not on Saturdays or Sundays. Quiet Times only prevent new protection runs from starting during the specified time period. The protection runs that started before the quiet time period are not affected and will continue to run.
For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time period that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet time period.

Enable or Disable Auto Protect
The Auto Protect option enables you to automatically protect the new sites that are added to Microsoft 365. When the Auto Protect option is enabled:
l All the Teams that are added to Microsoft 365 in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run.
l All the Teams that are removed from Microsoft 365 in the future are automatically removed from the Protection Group and are not protected from the next protection run. The existing backups for the user are preserved until the snapshot expires.
When the Auto Protect option is disabled, you need to manually:
l Add newly onboarded Teams on Microsoft 365 to the Protection Group. l Remove existing Teams that are offboarded on Microsoft 365 from the Protection
Group. The existing backups of the users are preserved until the snapshot expires.
To enable or disable Auto Protect:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for
OneDrive.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit.

5. From the Groups list, click the icon in the domain level to enable or disable Auto Protect and click Save Selection.
6. Click Protect.

You can also initiate registering a new tenant by clicking the Registered Source option. From Target Teams, select the required team where you want to recover the selected channel/item. From Target Channel, select the required channel, or create a new one. To create a new channel, click Create New, click Shared Channel, enter a name for the new channel, enter the name of the owner, and then click Create.
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
8. Under Recovery Options, do the following:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 15: Microsoft 365

Teams

l By default, the Restore Original Owner Members option is enabled. Disable this option if you do not want to recover the original owners and channel members to the newly created team.
l The Restore Original Owner Members option is not applicable if you are recovering the Team's data to a different Microsoft 365 domain.
l From the Additional Team Owner drop-down list, select the target team owner that needs to be added to the original team owners.
l Enable the Continue on Error option if you want to continue the recovery even if one of the objects encounters an error. By default, this option is disabled, and the recovery operation fails if one of the objects encounters an error.
l In the Task Name field, enter the name of the recovery task if you want to change the default recovery task name.
9. Click Recover to start the recovery operation.

replication, specify the retention period of the data on the remote Cohesity cluster, and other parameters.

3. Run the Protection Group that you have created for Microsoft Exchange Online or OneDrive based on your requirement or the replication settings will take effect in the next scheduled Protection Group run.

Prerequisites and Considerations
Physical Server Protection
Prerequisites
l The Cohesity Agent running on the hosts should be Cohesity version 6.2 onwards. l If physical servers are behind NAT, add the NAT server's IP address to the Cohesity
cluster's subnets specified in the allowlist.
Physical Server - Generic Considerations
l Making a disk offline and then online triggers a full backup for Simple, Striped and Spanned volumes. Mirrored volumes are not affected.
l Recovering a file or instantly mounting volumes from an AD-joined Cohesity cluster to a server that does not belong to that AD domain is not supported.
l Instant volume mounting does not currently support using drive letters on the target physical Server. Volumes are under C:\CohesityMounts\... for Windows and /opt/cohesity/agent/mount_paths/vol_mounts/..... for Linux systems.
l You cannot add different types of physical servers (Windows, Linux) in a single Protection Group as the supported features of Cohesity Data Cloud are different for different physical servers.
l Cohesity supports recovery only from physical server to physical server. Recovering physical server to VM and vice-versa is not supported.
l Cohesity supports recovering files and folders from Linux to Linux, AIX to AIX, and Solaris to Solaris only. Recovering files and folders from one operating system to another is not supported. For example, recovering files and folders from Linux to AIX or Solaris is not supported.
l After creating a directive file-based Protection Group for a physical server, you can simultaneously trigger more than one protection run of the Protection Group to backup only a specific set of files and folders in each run. However, you cannot simultaneously trigger multiple protection runs to back up the same file or folder.
l When browsing files or folders for recovery, Cohesity does not display files or folders with an absolute path length exceeding approximately 3,500 characters. To recover these files or folders, select the parent directory.
l Due to variations across operating systems and file systems, sparse files may not be detected accurately. In such scenarios, they'll be backed up as regular files, with

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 16: Physical Servers

Plan and Prepare for Physical Server Protection

relevant updates in pulse logs.
l When sparse files are detected and processed during backups and recoveries, the amount of data processed during backups and recoveries will reflect the non-zero content. This is likely to differ from previous backups or recoveries where sparse files were processed as normal files.
Windows - Considerations
l When performing a recovery for a Windows physical server, if deduplication functionality is enabled for the backed-up data (files, folders, volumes, or mount volumes), the target machine should have deduplication functionality enabled by default, or the recovery jobs would fail.
l Recovery of deduplicated volume from archival is not supported for Windows physical servers.
l For file and folder recoveries to Windows machines, if the machine is apart of an AD Domain then the Cohesity Cluster must be joined to the same AD domain. The only alternative is to disable SMB Security in Cohesity Views Global Settings and allow Guest login on the Windows machine.
l Windows file-based backup does not support the following:
l Backup and recovery of encrypted files (EFS) and alternate data streams (ADS).
l Backup of symbolic links within a symbolic link pointing to the NAS target.
l A subsequent Full (No CBT) backup would also occur after a machine restart unless it is an intentional restart of a Windows physical server with the Capture Incremental After Server Restart option toggled on.
l You cannot add different types of physical servers (Windows, Linux) in a single Protection Group as the supported features of Cohesity Data Cloud are different for different physical servers.
l Source-side deduplication is not supported in Windows 2008 R2 servers.
l By default, VSS writers are not used for Windows file-based protection. This can be controlled using the crash-consistent backup settings. For more information, see Protecting a Physical Server (File-based).
l To avoid antivirus scans on the Cohesity folder saved on the C: drive, place it under the exclusion of the antivirus software.
l For Windows block-based backups, there are additional consideration, see Windows Block-Based iSCSI FC Volume Backups.
Linux
Prerequisites
l To use the Linux PowerPC, Linux on z/Architecture or Linux on ARM (aarch64) agent, the following prerequisites are required:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 16: Physical Servers

Plan and Prepare for Physical Server Protection

l Java Runtime Environment (JRE) 8+ (JRE 8, 11, 17) l Minimum free space of 102400KB is required in /var and /usr directories l Minimum memory of 2GB is recommended
Considerations
l For block-based backups, the Cohesity Linux agent uses LVM snapshots to back up volumes. LVM does not support any consistency across volumes, so snapshots of different volumes, even in the same backup run, will have slightly different point in time snapshot timestamps.
l Linux block-based backup does not support CBT (Changed Block Tracking). Therefore, every incremental backup is a full backup.
l For block-based backup of the Linux server, Cohesity does not support thin-pool configurations, which allows snapshots to be created outside the volume group.
l For block-based backup of the Linux server, Cohesity supports snapshot creation only inside the same volume group. If there is no space within the same volume group, block-based backup of the Linux server will fail.
l For SLES 11 SP4, the Linux agent is supported for the root user only. l Linux PowerPC supports only file-based backups. l Linux PowerPC supports only RPM-based installation. l Linux on PowerPC, z/Architecture, and ARM (aarch64) supports only file-based
backups. l Linux on PowerPC, z/Architecture, and ARM (aarch64) supports only RPM-based
installation.
AIX
Prerequisites
l To use the AIX agent (Java based), Java Runtime Environment (JRE) 8 needs to be installed on the source system.
l AIX agent (Java based) being installed should be a higher version than the existing version of GoAgent.
l Install 64-bit version 8 of IBM-supported AIX compatible Java. l 1.5 GB of free RAM (at run time) to account for JRE overhead. l Sudo package must be installed. l Latest version of Bash must be installed. For more information, see AIX Toolbox for
Linux Applications. l Java Agent must be installed as the Root user.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 16: Physical Servers

Plan and Prepare for Physical Server Protection

Considerations
l Only file-based Protection Groups are supported. l The mount point used for Oracle DB cloning is not persistent across reboots. To
resolve this issue, manually update the /etc/filesystem file using any editor and update the mount path information. l IVM (Instant Volume Mount) is not supported. l The AIX physical server does not support the following:
l Source-side deduplication l AIX clustering l AIX version earlier than 6.1 l Power HA l JFS2-based snapshots l Veritas Cluster Server l BMR l Workload partitions (WPARs).
Red Hat High Availability (Pacemaker) Cluster
Considerations
l Pacemaker version 2.1 or higher with PCS is supported. l Only resources of class ocf, provider heartbeat, type IpAddr2, and Filesystem are
supported. l The Cohesity agent must be installed on all nodes belonging to the cluster. If any
additional node is added to the cluster at a later stage, the agent should be installed on it as well. l It is expected that Filesystem resources are active on the same node where the IpAddr2 resource is running. Cohesity itself assumes no coupling between IpAddr2 and Filesystem resources. l Backup and recovery are supported only if the agent is installed as the root user. l If failover happens during the backup run, there may be a few files missed in the run. Explicit failover detection and handling can be enabled by contacting Cohesity Support.
Veritas Cluster Server (VCS)
Prerequisites
l One node in the VCS cluster must be active and the other nodes must be passive. l Each node in the VCS cluster must have its own service group and each service
requires access to all the shared volumes.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 16: Physical Servers

Plan and Prepare for Physical Server Protection

l The same version of the Cohesity Linux Agent must be installed on all the nodes in the VCS cluster.
l The following commands must exist on all the nodes in the VCS cluster: l whereis hares l whereis hagrp l whereis hasys l whereis haclus l whereis lltconfig
If the command output returns the path of the command, the command is present on the node.
Considerations
l Only file-based backup and recovery of the VCS cluster running on a physical server is supported.
l Only active-passive VCS cluster configuration is supported (active-active configuration is not supported).
l If you are upgrading Cohesity Linux Agents of the VCS cluster from the Cohesity cluster using the VIP, then only the Agent on the node to which the VIP is pointing will be upgraded. Other nodes can be upgraded by one of the following methods: l Add individual nodes to the Cohesity cluster as a physical server and upgrade the Cohesity Linux Agent. l Do failover of VIP to other nodes and then upgrade the Cohesity Linux Agent. l Install fresh Agents on other nodes.
l To protect a VCS cluster shared disk, use VIPs to register the VCS cluster. To protect local disks, register the VCS nodes with their Private IPs.
l If a failover happens during backup, then the backup of some files might be skipped. These skipped files will be backed up in the next Protection Group run.
l If the failover takes more than 10 minutes, then the Protection Group run might fail. l If a failover happens during the restore, the maximum delay permitted is 10 minutes.
If the failover is more than 10 minutes, the restore will fail. l If you mount a volume to a VIP using the Instant Volume Mount capability, and
perform a failover followed by a teardown, then the teardown might fail, and the node's VIP will be orphaned.
Solaris
Prerequisites
l Java Agent must be deployed on the server. l Physical source should be installed with Java version 8.

Considerations
l Block-based, BMR, Source side dedupe and volume recovery are not supported for Solaris.
l Solaris Zones in Solaris x86_64 are not supported. HP-UX
Considerations
l Cohesity supports only file-based backup and restores on HP-UX servers. l Cohesity does not support block-based, BMR, and source side dedupe backups on HP-
UX servers.
Register or Edit a Physical Server
Before registering a physical server with the Cohesity cluster, you must download and install the Cohesity agent on each server you plan to register.
Overview
1. Download the Cohesity agent to the physical server. 2. Install the agent on the physical server.
Instructions for silent installation on Windows servers are available here: Silently Install the Cohesity Agent on Windows Physical Servers. 3. Register the physical server with the Cohesity cluster.
Download and Install the Agent
Installing the agent on a physical server allows it to be registered as a source with the Cohesity cluster.
1. Select Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click Download Cohesity Agent. 3. Follow the installation instructions for the corresponding agent operating system:
Windows Agent 1. Ensure the agent has been downloaded to the server you want to protect. 2. As an administrator with local system privileges on that server, run the executable with Run as administrator and complete the installation wizard. Install the Volume CBT (Changed Block Tracker) component to perform incremental backups. Installing this component requires a reboot. Without a

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 16: Physical Servers

Register or Edit a Physical Server

reboot, only full backups can be performed. Not installing this component means only full backups can be performed.
Note: The Cohesity Volume CBT driver creates the Cohesity_Bitmap.cty file at the root of each volume. There are multiple ways to backup Windows physical server but the Cohesity_Bitmap.cty file will be available on the system only if the Volume CBT driver is installed. This file is used to maintain the CBT data for incremental block-based backups across Windows server reboots. Do not move or delete the ".cty" file.
The File System CBT (Changed Block Tracker) component is required for MS SQL file-based protection. 3. The agent starts automatically.
Note: This installation does not require a restart. You can wait until a normal maintenance window (such as a Patch Tuesday) to restart. However, until you do, some Protection Groups that depend on Volume CBT will run in full backup mode.

Action

How to

Download the Agent installer

From the Download Agents window, based on your Linux distribution, select RPM, Debian, or SUSE RPM and download it to the server you want to protect.

Navigate to the downloaded directory

As the root user with local system privileges on that server, change the directory to the location of the installer package.

Install the Custom certificates

LINUX If you are using a Cohesity certificate then run the following commands to install the user certificate followed by agent installation:
export ENFORCE_USE_CUSTOM_CERTS=true && export AGENT_CERT_ FILE=<path-to-agent-certificate-in-Cohesity-format>

Install the Agent

Run the following command depending on the installer package: l RPM: rpm -i el-cohesity-agent-7.4.1-1.x86_64.rpm or yum localinstall ./el-cohesityagent-7.4.1-1.x86_64.rpm l Debian: dpkg -i cohesity-agent_7.4.1-1_amd64.deb l SUSE RPM: rpm -i cohesity-agent-7.4.1-1.x86_64.rpm

Install the agent as root user

Run the executable file with the following command syntax:
/<path_to_installer_file> -- --install -c 0 -S root -G root
Followings are the command options in details: 1. -S this is the user to run the agent, specify root. 2. -G this is the group permission the Agent will use for files and directories installed by the agent, specify root. 3. -c this boolean switch controls if the OS user and group should be created. 0 means do not create the OS user and group, 1 means the agent installation will create the specified OS user and group. (When choose to run with the root user, specify `-c 0' as `root' already exists)

Action
Install the agent as nonroot user

How to
To start the service as a non-root user, create a new user or use an existing user with sudo permission and run the following command:
l RPM: export COHESITYUSER=<username> ; rpm -i el-cohesityagent-7.4.1-1.x86_64
l Debian: COHESITYUSER=<username> dpkg -i cohesity-agent_7.4.1-1_ amd64
l SUSE RPM: export COHESITYUSER=<username> rpm -i cohesityagent-7.4.1-1.x86_64 Where, <username> is the user name with sudo permission.

Note: By default, the installation uses the root user permission for all the files, and the service is started as root. Therefore, it is required to add non-root users to the sudoers list by making the following changes in the /etc/sudoers file:
<user_name> ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL
Defaults:<user_name> !requiretty

An example of the sudoers file is as given below:

dgoble ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL
Defaults:dgoble !requiretty cohbackup ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL Defaults:cohbackup !requiretty

<user_name> ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:/path/to/command1, /path/to/command2, /path/to/command3
Remove NOPASSWD from the command above if you do not want to authenticate every sudo commands with password.

Network Bandwidth and CPU Throttling for Physical Server
You can throttle the network bandwidth and CPU on the Windows and Linux physical servers registered with the Cohesity cluster. Network throttling optimizes the data transfer rate from the server to the Cohesity cluster when a Protection Group is run. CPU throttling optimizes the CPU capacity utilized when a Protection Group with source-side deduplication is run on the server.

Enable Network Bandwidth and CPU Throttling

enable network bandwidth and CPU throttling.

To schedule network bandwidth throttling for specific days and time durations: 1. Click Add. 2. From the On field, select the days during which you want to optimize the network bandwidth. 3. In the Start Time and End Time duration fields, specify the time duration for throttling. 4. In the Throttle to field, specify the maximum data transfer rate from the server to the Cohesity cluster. 5. To configure multiple schedules for throttling, click + and repeat steps b to d. Example: If you want to limit the data transfer rate to 100 MB/S on Mondays and Wednesdays from 12.00 to 16.00, then from the On field, select M and W, set the Start Time as 12.00, End Time as 16.00, and in the Throttle to field, enter 100 as the throttling rate.
Note: For the days and duration for which you have not scheduled the network bandwidth throttling, Cohesity will take the throttling value specified at the server level.
4. Enable the Throttle CPU option and in the Throttle to field, specify the maximum CPU capacity (in percentage) of the server that Cohesity cluster backup runs with source-side deduplication enabled can utilize.

Add or Edit a Protection Group for Physical Servers
In Cohesity Data Cloud, Protection Groups use Protection Policies. Protection Policies reflect the backup and archival frequency, and retention requirements for each Protection Run. A Protection Group defines operational requirements, such as which source objects to protect, the Protection Policy to use, and operational considerations like indexing, exclusions and inclusions, and more. A Protection Group that protects physical servers captures snapshots which are required for the following tasks:
l Recover files l Instant volume mount l Replicate snapshots l Archive snapshots

Compare Block-Based and File-Based Backup Methods
Cohesity offers two distinct approaches for physical server backups: Block-based and Filebased. While both methods serve the purpose of safeguarding critical data, understanding their differences is essential for choosing the most suitable backup strategy for your organization's needs.

Cohesity Facet

Cohesity Block-based Physical Server Backups

Cohesity File-based Physical Server Backups

Granularity

Operates at the disk block level, capturing modified or new data blocks.

Operates at the file level, preserving entire files for backup and recovery.

Speed and Performance

Enables faster backup and recovery times by tracking changes at the block level and transferring only modified data blocks.

Offers straightforward backup and recovery operations, relying on the identification and preservation of entire files.

Optimized Storage Efficiency

Significantly reduces storage requirements by capturing only the changed data blocks.

File-based backups rely on deduplication within the storage domain for optimization. It provides file-level accessibility, allowing selective recovery.

Simplicity and Familiarity

Requires familiarity with block-level operations.

Follows traditional file-level backup approaches that administrators are accustomed to.

Flexibility and Accessibility

Focuses on individual data blocks, enabling more granular and incremental backups.

Ensures the accessibility of individual files and directories, simplifying selective recovery.

Metadata and Indexing

Relies on metadata which is available once indexing occurs after the backup is complete.

Includes comprehensive metadata and indexing capabilities for quick search and file location.

Dependencies

Block-based backups depend on the volume CBT driver on Windows and LVM snapshots in Linux.

No dependency in the case of file-based backups.

Supported Configurations

Block-based backups are supported with specific file systems (NTFS for Windows, small group for Linux x64).

File-based backups are less restrictive and can work with a wider range of filesystems and operating systems (AIX etc)

Supported Recoveries

Block-based allows for IVM recovery,

File-based only allows for File-level recovery.

Source Backup

Block-based backup allows only one backup against one Source

File-based backup allows multiple backups to be configured against one Source.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 16: Physical Servers

Add or Edit a Protection Group for Physical Servers

In summary, Cohesity provides two distinct methodologies for physical server backups: Block-based and File-based. While Block-based backups excel in speed, efficiency, and granularity at the disk block level, File-based backups offer simplicity, flexibility, and filelevel accessibility. Choosing the appropriate backup method depends on your organization's specific requirements, data protection goals, and recovery objectives. The decision between Cohesity's Block-based and File-based Physical Server backups should be based on factors such as backup speed, storage efficiency, data granularity, ease of recovery, and the desired level of accessibility. By understanding the differences between the two backup approaches, organizations can effectively leverage the backup functionality to enhance their data protection strategies to optimize their overall businesses.

Options All Volumes

Descriptions
Use this option to protect all the local volumes on the specific host. If you select this option, the system dynamically enumerates all the local volumes present during the backup protection group run and protects them.

Note: In Windows, local volumes are the volumes listed in the "Disk Management" utility of the Windows host.

If you choose to use the Add Exclusions functionality when using this option, you can either specify:
l Individual files or folders within a volume by specifying the fully qualified path names
l Individual files or folders across all the volumes using the wildcards l Entire volumes by defining the volume path
If the exclusion path is not present at the time of a backup run, the system ignores this entry and proceeds to the next.
This option overrides any exclusion path specified as global exclude.
Example
If you specify /mnt/banapps/ as a global exclude path but the local mount points are /mnt/banapps/ar_techsis_views and /mnt/banapps/common, then all the files and folders inside these local mount points will be included.
If you want the Protection Group to exclude all the local mount points inside /mnt/banapps/, then you can either add these local mount points as explicit exclude paths or choose a normal backup and then give "/" as the include path, and /mnt/banapps/ as the exclude path.
Add Exclusions
You can use this option to add exclusion entries for Individual files and folders and Protect all local volumes. For more information, see Add Exclusions.

Directive File

The directive file defines the locations of the files and folders that you can back up in a protection group. Specify the file path of the directive file (meta-file) on the source while adding it to a protection group. For more information, see Directive File Backup.

Note: Applies only to Windows, AIX, and Linux servers file-based backup

l If /temp is provided as global exclude for a protection group and /temp/data as include path for a source, then /temp/data will be skipped by the Cohesity cluster.

Start On-demand Multiple Protection Runs for Physical Server

Start On-demand Multiple Protection Runs for Physical Server
After creating a directive file-based Protection Group for a physical server, Cohesity supports to simultaneously trigger more than one protection run of the Protection Group to backup only a specific set of files and folders in each run. This functionality can be achieved using the Cohesity REST API, /public/protectionJobs/run/{id}. To trigger a protection run, add the metadata file path parameter in the JSON body of the API and provide the directive file path having the file or folder you plan to backup as the value. Example to trigger a protection run from using the REST API:
URI
https://<cluster_name>/irisservices/api/v1/public/protectionJobs/run/<protectionGroupID>
Method
POST
JSON body
{ "copyRunTargets": [ ], "runNowParameters": [ { "physicalParams": { "metadataFilePath": "/home/cohesity/dirfile2" }, "sourceId": 5 } ], "runType": "kFull"
}
Where /home/cohesity/dirfile2 is the directive file path that contains a list of files and folders folder that will be backed up using this API. Similarly, you can simultaneously trigger multiple protection runs of a Protection Group.
Limitation
You cannot simultaneously trigger multiple protection runs to back up the same file or folder.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 16: Physical Servers

Source-Side Deduplication and Cache Optimization for Physical Server

For example, you cannot start a protection run with the directive file path as /home/cohesity/dirfile2 if there is already another active protection run of the same Protection Group, which is using the same directive file path.
Source-Side Deduplication and Cache Optimization for Physical Server
Source-side deduplication is a Cohesity feature designed to optimize backup efficiency by eliminating redundant data at the source (physical server) before transferring it to the Cohesity cluster. This process reduces network usage and speeds up backup operations, ensuring efficient data protection for your physical servers. With source-side deduplication enabled for a physical server during Protection Group creation, unique data blocks that have not been previously transferred are sent to the Cohesity cluster. This significantly minimizes network bandwidth utilization and reduces data transfer times. Additionally, source-side deduplication integrates seamlessly with Cohesity's built-in deduplication, further optimizing storage by processing only new data blocks. Advantages of Source-Side Deduplication
l Reduced Network Traffic: This feature minimizes the amount of data transferred between physical servers and the Cohesity cluster, conserving network bandwidth.
l Faster Backups: Speeds up backup processes, particularly over slower networks such as WANs, enabling quicker recovery point objectives (RPOs).
l Efficient Resource Utilization: Offloads deduplication processing from the Cohesity cluster, allowing the system to handle a higher volume of backup workload sessions.
l Lower Storage Costs: Reduces overall storage consumption by transmitting only new or changed data blocks.
Cache Optimization
Cache Optimization is a specialized feature that enhances the performance of backups for large files (over 64 GiB) by further refining source-side deduplication functionality. When enabled, only the changed blocks of target files are backed up during subsequent incremental backup runs, rather than the entire file. This ensures efficient storage utilization and reduced backup times.
Requirements
To use Cache Optimization, ensure that both the Cohesity agent and the Cohesity cluster are running version 7.0 or later. Advantages of Cache Optimization

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 16: Physical Servers

Protect Windows Failover Cluster

l Reduced Network Traffic: Optimizes data transfers between physical servers and the Cohesity cluster.
l Lower CPU Usage: Reduces CPU load on the source server compared to standard source-side deduplication.
l Improved Performance: Provides enhanced backup efficiency, particularly for large files, by transferring only changed blocks.
Protect Windows Failover Cluster
With the Failover Clustering feature, users using the Cohesity clusters experience minimum disruptions in service. If one or more nodes of the cluster fail, the backup nodes begin to provide service by a process known as failover. Currently, Cohesity does not have out-of-box support for backing up Clustered disk resources managed by Windows Failover Cluster (WFC). However, it is still possible to protect Cluster data leveraging existing Physical Protection Jobs using one of the following methods: Protecting Shared and Local Drives using Block-based Physical Backup Protecting Shared and local Drives using a File-based Backup (Volume backup)
Protecting Shared and Local Drives using Block-based Physical Backup
To create a block-based protection group for WFC, follow the steps listed below:
1. Install Cohesity Agent on each node of the Windows Failover Cluster and register each Node of WFC as a separate Physical Server. For more information, see Register or Edit a Physical Server.
2. Create a Protection Group (physical server block-based). For more information, see Add or Edit a Protection Group for Physical Servers.
3. Enable Automatically protect all volumes on this Server option on every node when creating a protection group. If you enable this option, disk changes are automatically detected when a resource failover occurs and required volumes are backed up without requiring any changes to the Protection jobs created.
Note: If there is no failover, all the backups are incremental (Leveraging CBT) for the Shared disks. If there is a failover/failback on a shared disk over to the other node, the next backup will be a full backup.

Instant Volume Mount for Physical Server
Instant volume mounting is supported for virtual and physical environments. This feature allows the selected backup volumes to be made available at the target location where you can then complete the desired operations. Instant Volume Mount is available for backed-up volumes, whether they are stored locally on the Cohesity cluster or archived to a registered external target.Use cases include granular recovery of Microsoft Exchange, SQL and SharePoint data.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 16: Physical Servers

mounted depends on free loop device availability. By default, the number of available loop devices is 8, but this number can be customized. If the number of configured loop devices is the default of 8, up to eight volumes can be mounted. In this example, if an attempt to mount more than 8 volumes occurs, the mounting of all the volumes after the 8th volume fails and errors are reported. l Tearing down a cloned database or instant volume mount deletes the mounted volumes. Register the mount-target physical server on that cluster and ensure network and agent prerequisites are met.
Before you can instantly mount a volume, a Snapshot of the Object you want to recover must exist.
Troubleshooting
This section provides troubleshooting information for issues that might occur during IVM recovery.
Authentication Failures
Issue The IVM recovery fails due to an authentication failure and displays the following error: "The specified network password is not correct". Possible Root Cause The cluster joined the AD but the Windows host has not joined the AD. Troubleshooting steps
l Create a local user on the Cohesity cluster and use the local user to access the SMB share. To create a local user on the Cohesity cluster, contact Cohesity Support.
or
l Disable SMB Authentication on the Cohesity Data Cloud. Perform the following steps to disable SMB Authentication: 1. Log in to the Cohesity Data Cloud. 2. Select File Services > Views and click the Global Settings tab. 3. Toggle off the SMB Authentication setting.

Physical Server Recovery

Recover Physical Server Files or Folders
Cohesity provides the ability to recover files and folders from a Snapshot created earlier by a Protection Group. Files and folders can be recovered to their original location (limitations apply to physical Servers and specific operating systems) or to a newly specified location, which can be within the original Source or a different one. You can choose to retain the recovered files' and folders' original (at the time of the backup) permissions and attributes. You can also download files and folders from selected Snapshots that were created by a CohesityProtection Group. However, only items that were indexed when the Snapshot was created can be downloaded. Recovering and searching for files and folders in Snapshots created by other backup software is not supported. For information on managing these Protection Groups, Add or Edit a Protection Group for Physical Servers.
To learn more, see About File Recovery.
For more information about the recovery options:
l Recover Files or Folders to the Original Location
l Recover Physical Server Files or Folders to a New Location
l The Cohesity cluster attempts to index all files and folders to a drive on both Windows and Linux systems. If the Cohesity cluster is unable to find mount point information about files or directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories in the lvol_N directory, where N is a unique number such as 1.
On Windows systems, if the Cohesity cluster finds the mount point information about files and directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories with a drive letter such as C:.
Linux LVM indexing supports the following LVM types only: Linear, Striped, Mirrored, Mirrored + Striped, Thin. On Linux systems, how files and directories are indexed and displayed is dependent on the conditions specified in the following table.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Physical Server Recovery

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine
Linux Virtual Machine
Linux Physical

Simple Volume
LVM Volume
LVM Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
UUID="ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc" /mnt ext4 auto 0
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point that was specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt. If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.
The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
/dev/mapper/VG1-root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
/dev/VG1/root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt. If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.
The Cohesity agent can only return mount data when the volume is mounted on the Linux physical Server. If the volume is mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point such as /mnt/example/test.txt. If the volume is not mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

The Cohesity cluster attempts to index all files and folders to a drive on both Windows and Linux systems. If the Cohesity cluster is unable to find mount point information about files or directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories in the lvol_N directory, where N is a unique number such as 1.
On Windows systems, if the Cohesity cluster finds the mount point information about files and directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories with a drive letter such as C:.
Linux LVM indexing supports the following LVM types only: Linear, Striped, Mirrored, Mirrored + Striped, Thin. On Linux systems, how files and directories are indexed and displayed is dependent on the conditions specified in the following table.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 16: Physical Servers

Physical Server Recovery

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

Simple Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
UUID="ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc" /mnt ext4 auto 0
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point that was specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Linux Virtual Machine

LVM Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
/dev/mapper/VG1-root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
/dev/VG1/root /mnt ext4 defaults 1 1
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt. If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Linux Physical

LVM Volume

The Cohesity agent can only return mount data when the volume is mounted on the Linux physical Server. If the volume is mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the volume is not mounted, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 16: Physical Servers
