l Download Files: If you are recovering a single file, this option downloads the file to your browser's download folder. For all other selections, this creates a recover task. When the task is completed, from the Recoveries page, click the task name and then click Download Files to download the generated zip file.
Character replacement explanation for : and \ in file and directory names in zip files
If the original file or directory name contains a `:' , it is replaced with `_COLON_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "a:b" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b"
l The original name is "a:b:c" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b_ COLON_c"
If the original file or directory name contains a `\', it is replaced with '_BACK_ SLASH_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "x\y" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_y"
l The original name is "x\y\z" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_ y_BACK_SLASH_z"
5. From the Recover To, select Original Server to recover the files or folders to a Original server.
6. To recover to a different location in the original server, disable the Recover to Original Path option, and then provide the location to which the files or folders are to be recovered in the Recover To field. By default, the files and folders will be recovered to the original location.
7. Optional. Edit the default settings of the following Recovery options:
l Authorized User - Select the user account that will be used to authenticate the SMB mount during file and folder recovery to a Windows machine. Option include:
l Automatic - Choose this option to let Cohesity automatically select the appropriate user for SMB mount authentication. Use this setting when the Cohesity cluster and the Windows host have a trust relationship at the Active Directory domain or forest level.
l Local User - Select this option to authenticate the SMB mount using a local user account on the Windows machine. Use a local user who has the required permissions to authenticate SMB mounts created by the Cohesity cluster. Such a user should have been granted 'Allow SMB

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 16: Physical Servers

Physical Server Recovery

Access Tokens' as a privilege. For more details, see User Settings.
l Specific AD Identity - Select this option when the agent is not joined to Active Directory but the Cohesity cluster is joined to AD. Specify the Active Directory domain and provide the AD user credentials that should be used to authenticate the SMB mount.
l Overwrite Existing File/Folder: By default, this option is disabled to create the files and folders in the specified location. Enable this option to overwrite the existing files and folders. Any duplicate files are skipped.
Example for a Windows alternate location with Overwrite Existing File/Folder enabled and the target already exists:
Files to be recovered: "C:\foo\1.txt", "C:\foo\test\1.txt", "C:\bar", "C:\foo\bar". Specified alternate location: "C:\restore". At the end of the copy, the target folder looks like this:
l C:\restore\1.txt
l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_0\1.txt
l C:\restore\bar
l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_1\bar
If Overwrite Existing File/Folder is enabled, this will overwrite the existing files and folders. Whether overwriting occurs depends on the application using the file.
l Preserve File/Folder Attributes: By default, this option is enabled and the ACLs, permissions, and timestamps are preserved for all files and folders. If you disable this option, then ACLs and permissions are not preserved. If recovering both folders and files, then folders will receive the new timestamps, but files retain their original timestamps. If recovering only, files, then files will receive the new timestamps.
l Continue on Error: Enable this option if you want to continue the recovery even if one of the objects encounters an error. By default, this option is disabled and the recovery operation will fail if one of the objects encounters an error.
l Cluster Interface: By default, the Auto Select option is enabled and the recovery task automatically selects the correct VLAN. If you disable this option, then select a configured interface group from the Interface Group drop-down.
l Task Name: Change the default name of the recovery task.
l Save Success Files: Enable this option to download the success logs for a recovery run.

Active Directory
This chapter includes the following topics: l Active Directory Key Concepts l Active Directory Protection Requirements l Active Directory Best Practices l Active Directory Non-Cohesity-Specific Information l Set Up Active Directory for Data Protection l Protect Active Directory l Recover Active Directory Objects l Recover Active Directory Domain Controller l Active Directory Data Protection FAQs

Active Directory Key Concepts
The following topics introduce you to key concepts about Active Directory protection and object recovery.
About Active Directory Data Protection
A Cohesity Active Directory (AD) backup captures an app-consistent VSS snapshot of all volumes on the Active Directory domain controller (DC). For instructions on how to use the Cohesity UI to back up AD, review Protect Active Directory.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 17: MS Applications

Active Directory

Cohesity's AD backup implementation is intended to protect sufficient AD data to enable granular object recovery and object attribute compare and recovery.
If the objective is to recover an entire AD DC virtual server, protect the VM as described in Add or Edit a Protection Group for Virtual Servers. For AD DC bare metal server recovery, protect the process described in Add or Edit a Protection Group for Physical Servers. Appconsistent VM/bare metal snapshots and crash-consistent snapshots are available.
All configurations are for illustrative purposes only. Cohesity recommends following Active Directory best practices.
The following diagram displays an example Microsoft application environment that contains Active Directory.

The AD backup task consists of the following actions:
1. When a Protection Group starts, the Cohesity cluster requests an AD snapshot be taken.

2. A Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) snapshot of AD is captured using VSS. The snapshot is a full VSS backup and uses Cohesity change block tracking (volume CBT).
3. The snapshot data is copied to the Cohesity cluster. 4. The VSS snapshot is deleted.
About Active Directory Object Recovery
A Cohesity Active Directory (AD) recovery mounts the volume that contains NTDS.dit. For instructions on how to use the Cohesity UI to recover AD, review Recover Active Directory Objects.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 17: MS Applications

Active Directory

You can use Cohesity for these Active Directory recovery types: l Granular object recovery For example, Users, Computers and Groups l Granular object attribute compare and recovery For example, description, email address, group membership, custom attributes l Group Policy Object (GPO)
The AD recover task consists of the following actions: 1. When an AD recovery starts, the Cohesity cluster creates an instant volume mount (IVM) on the cluster that contains the requested snapshot of AD data (NTDS.dit).

2. The Cohesity agent mounts the IVM and accesses it through SMB. If the Cohesity cluster has joined an AD domain, then the cluster must join that AD domain (Join an AD Domain) to access the SMB volume.
3. The agent accesses the snapshot on a custom LDAP port, such as 53389, and the three subsequent ports. LiveAD is accessed to execute LDAP queries based on user input to compare objects, accept object or attribute and update LiveAD.
4. Optionally unmount the IVM. You can tear down the IVM when you finish using it.
Group Policy Object Recovery
You can recover the GPO if you have accidentally deleted it or if the GPO was updated and you do not want the updates. GPO recovery involves recovering the following two components of the GPO and also the GPO links:
l Group Policy Container - It represents the attributes relevant to the GPO content. Each GPO contains two containers Machine and User and the respective containers contain specific information related to the machine and user nodes of the GPO. For

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 17: MS Applications

Active Directory

more information, see Group-Policy-Container class.
l Group Policy Template - Contains the content of the GPO. It resides in a share known as SYSVOL. The share is replicated to every DC in the domain and the share contains separate directories named with GPO GUID for each GPO.
l GPO links - A GPO can be linked to different AD objects such as Domain, Site, and OrganizationalUnit. The links are maintained as the attribute (gPLink) of the corresponding AD objects.
Cohesity enables you to recover the following using the Cohesity UI:
l the Group Policy Container in AD. l the SYSVOL folder for the GPO l GPO links for all the objects that are linked to the GPO in cases where the GPO was
deleted.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 17: MS Applications

Active Directory

Active Directory Protection Requirements
Supported Versions
For more information on the supported versions, see Microsoft Applications.
Prerequisites
l Verify anti-virus exclusions are added for Cohesity Windows agent binaries under C:\Program Files\Cohesity and the log folder, C:\ProgramData\Cohesity.
l For the protection and granular recovery, the minimum required Cohesity version and agent is 6.4.
l Group Policy Object (GPO) on PowerShell execution. On all AD DCs where the Cohesity agent is running, Windows PowerShell script execution must be enabled.
Protection
l On all DCs where the agent is installed, open Cohesity port 50051 (For more information, see Manage Firewall Ports.)
Recovery
l On the recovery target DC, open the custom LDAP ports specified in the recover task. See Recover Active Directory Objects for more information.
l The AD Adapter has the same port requirements as filesystem backup. For recovery, it is the same as filesystem via an SMB (445), plus the addition of any 4 free consecutive ports of your choice.
l If the Cohesity cluster has joined an AD domain, then the cluster must join the target recovery AD domain to access the SMB volume. If the cluster has joined a forest (root/parent domain) and Trusted Domain Discovery is enabled from the cluster, the cluster does not need to join the child domains to perform recovery.
The SMB volume is accessed using the Cohesity cluster computer object credentials registered in the AD. Ensure that there is a DNS server entry for the cluster computer object FQDN and that clocks are synchronized between AD and the Cohesity cluster (Kerberos allows no more than 5 minute skew).
l To perform object recovery to a Windows 2019 AD DC, you must join the Cohesity cluster to the Windows 2019 domain due to SMB security requirements.
l The recovering administrator user must have View privileges (the minimum permissions) on the production AD object. Otherwise, object recovery is prevented and the object is displayed as `missing' and its properties are not shown.
l When recovering a deleted object from an earlier forest/domain functional backup (such as Windows 2000 functional level) to a later AD DC (such as Windows 2012 R2),

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 17: MS Applications

Active Directory

you may see differences in attributes (such as ntSecurityDescriptor) on the recovered object due to AD schema upgrades and prebuilt group memberships. l Get-SystemAttributesInternal attributes (such as objectGuid, objectSid, usnChanged) are considered system properties, which are not compared and cannot be recovered due to AD restrictions. They are, however, displayed when browsing a snapshot. The Cohesity REST API has the ability to include system properties in attribute comparison. l Manually teardown and rerun the domain recovery search and attempt object recovery if the connection to the mounted AD snapshot is lost. This happens if your Windows machine reboots in the middle of a granular restore or if the single-node cluster gets upgraded/rebooted.
Multitenancy
l The Cohesity cluster is part of both domains. l A DNS server is set with conditional forwarding that forwards requests to the right
Domain DCs. l AD replicas are in the same DC as the Cohesity cluster.
Supported Workflows
The AD adapter supports the following workflows:
l Backup of Domain Controllers. l Granular Recovery of AD objects. l Granular Recovery of GPOs (Group Policy Objects). l Granular Recovery of AD object attributes.
Minimum Permissions
l Agent installation - Install the agent on all AD DCs with FSMO roles that you want to protect. Use an AD Domain Admin account to install the Cohesity agent with the Volume CBT driver. The service can run as the LocalSystem account.
l Recovery - The AD account that performs recovery must be one of the following: l Domain Admin or Enterprise Admin l Domain user with delegated permissions to the OU where objects will be recovered, and reanimate permission on the AD Recycle Bin, if enabled (Delegation of Active Directory Recycle Bin).

Limitation
l Mounting a snapshot that was captured as a lower version domain/forest functional level/AD schema than the target DC FFL/Schema version, requires setting this gflag to true: magneto_active_directory_mount_ntds_allow_upgrade. Otherwise, the mount may fail after a 1 hour timeout. Obtain the AD schema version from:
Get-ADObject (Get-ADRootDSE).schemaNamingContext -Property objectVersion
l If a Cluster or Windows machine is not part of Active Directory, workflows involving mounting Cohesity View on the Windows machine over SMB, including IVM restore, file folder restore from block-based backup, CBMR backup, and other Hyper-V workflows, will fail on the Cohesity cluster from Cohesity version 6.8 onwards.
Active Directory Best Practices
Cohesity recommends the following best practices when protecting Active Directory:
l Protect all domain controllers that have FSMO roles. For example, in the case of role failover this practice helps to ensure a backup (snapshot) is present even if a backup DC becomes primary at some point.
Active Directory Non-Cohesity-Specific Information
This section discusses Active Directory requirements, limitations and behavior that are not specific to Cohesity.
Target AD Server Reboot During Recovery
If a target AD server is rebooted or a single-node Cohesity cluster is upgraded/rebooted during a recovery, the recovery will fail. The Cohesity admin must perform a tear down operation of the recovery task and then re-attempt object recovery.
Objects Recovered with New SIDs when AD Recycle Bin is not Enabled
Any recovered user, group and computer objects will have a new security descriptor (SID) if the Recycle Bin is not enabled on the AD forest, or if you recover after the tombstone lifetime has expired. This is due to an AD limitation that prevents APIs setting object SIDs. The SID is permanent within a domain during an object's lifetime. This is a general limitation for all backup vendors and Microsoft API users. If these SIDs were inherent to any groups or ACLs, they would need to be adjusted manually. Cohesity always attempts to recover a missing object from the Recycle Bin and creates a new object (thus, a different SID) only when it is not found in the Recycle Bin. An object comparison reveals the SID difference.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 17: MS Applications

Active Directory

NTDS VSS Limitation
Microsoft NTDS VSS writer does not support Ntds.dit files on a mount point (such as C:\mount).
ntSecurityDescriptor ACL Attribute Recovery
The ntSecurityDescriptor security ACL attribute of an object within an OU may be delegated and inherited. In this case, the ACL cannot be recovered for the object because AD prevents it, showing the attribute as different. Recover the ntSecurityDescriptor of the OU.
Object Recovery by a Non-Domain Admin/Enterprise Admin
If a non-domain administrator/enterprise administrator account (such as HelpDesk) is delegated to perform object recovery and the Recycle Bin feature is enabled on the AD forest, the account must have Reanimate Tombstone object permissions to look up and recover objects from the AD Recycle Bin. For more information, see MSDN.
Delegated Permissions for a Non-Admin for Recovery
When giving delegated permissions to a non-admin user, choosing everything under "Delegate the following common tasks" gives delegate permissions for create/delete/manage user accounts, groups and inetOrgPerson accounts. You should specify permissions for other object types (such as computers and organizational units) separately. For object recovery to succeed, you must grant permissions to read and write all attributes in addition to create and delete object permissions.

Advanced Settings
l Start Time: Indicates when the Protection Group should run. The current time is displayed by default but you can change it. Enter the hour and minutes or use the up and down arrows on your keyboard. Verify the AM or PM setting.
The default time zone is the browser's time zone. You can change the time zone by selecting a different time zone.
l End Date: Optional. Toggle on and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.
l QoS Policy: Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy.
Note: Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.
l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Protection Groups.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
l TestAndDev High: The Cohesity cluster writes the data to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. The I/Os with this QoS policy are given higher priority compared to other QoS policies. Use this policy for workloads that require lower I/O latency.
l Pre & Post Scripts: Edit this option to run scripts on the protected server before and/or after a Protection Group runs. If configured, the scripts are run every time an object is backed up by a Protection Group run.
For configuration details, see Configure Pre & Post Scripts.
l Cancel Runs at Quiet Time Start: Available only if the selected policy has at least one quiet time period. Toggle it on to specify that all currently executing protection runs should abort if a quiet time period specified for the Protection Group starts. By default this toggle is off, which means after a protection run starts, it continues to execute even when a quiet time period specified for this protection run starts. However, a new protection run will not start during a quiet time period.
l Alerts: Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:

l Success: Create an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Create a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
For more information, see Alerts. l Priority: Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity supports
concurrent backups, but if the number of Protection Groups exceeds the ability to process them, those with High priority are given the highest priority to execute, Medium the second-highest priority, and Low the lowest priority. l Email Recipients: You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the Protection Group.
Note: The connection to the SMTP Server must be enabled to send email notification. You can enable the SMTP Server connection in the configuration settings page ( Cohesity UI > Settings > Summary > Configure > Enable SMTP Server).
l SLA: The service-level agreement (SLA) defines the expected time to complete either a full backup or incremental backup. The backup completion time depends on the Windows volume size on AD, objects changed between incremental backups, network speed, and other Protection Groups running on the Cohesity cluster. l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental protection run to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last protection run. l Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup protection run to complete. This port and the 3 consecutive port numbers after it must be currently unused and opened for inbound traffic in the Windows Firewall. Windows Server 2008 and newer versions of Windows Server have increased the dynamic client port range for outgoing connections. The new default start port is 49152, and the default end port is 65535. Note: These LDAP ports do not need to be opened for hosts outside the AD DC. Only the Cohesity agent must use these ports.

Recover Active Directory Domain Controller
Cohesity provides the ability to recover the Active Directory (AD) Domain Controllers that are backed up on the Cohesity cluster. The procedural steps below align with Microsoft best practices. Prerequisites and Considerations For recovering AD:
l Snapshots of the AD domain controller must be available on the Cohesity cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Active Directory

l You must have the local administrator username and password. l Windows Firewall should permit TCP Port 50051 inbound traffic from the Cluster for
the instant mount l Permission should be given to the instant volume mount to access the temporary SMB
mount used during the recovery. l The steps listed here are specific to the recovery of the AD Domain Controller.
Recover AD Domain Controller
Perform the following steps to recover AD Domain Controller:
1. On the Domain Controller, configure the Domain Controller host to boot in Directory Services Repair Mode (DSRM): 1. Press WIN+R on the keyboard. 2. Type msconfig and click OK. 3. Select the Boot tab. 4. Under Boot Options, select the Safe Boot check box.
Note: Once the Safe Boot is enabled, the AD services are disabled. DNS and all other AD services are not available.
5. Select Active Directory repair and click OK. 6. Restart the Domain Controller host. 2. Log in to the Domain Controller host as the local administrator. 3. In the Cohesity UI, select the snapshot for restore, then download the folders containing the AD data (NTDS and SYSVOL). For more information, see Instant Volume Mount. 4. On the Domain Controller host: 1. Rename the old NTDS and SYSVOL folders. 2. Copy over the same folders (NTDS and SYSVOL) from the Instant Volume
Mount to the Domain Controller host. 5. From the Cohesity UI, tear down the Instant Volume Mount. For more information,
see Teardown a Mounted Volume. 6. On the Domain Controller, configure the Domain Controller host to boot in normal
mode: 1. Press WIN+R on the keyboard. 2. Type msconfig and click OK. 3. Select the Boot tab.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 17: MS Applications

Active Directory

4. Under Boot Options, clear the Safe boot check box. 5. Restart the Domain Controller host. 7. Log in to the Domain Controller host as the domain administrator.
Active Directory Data Protection FAQs
This topic answers frequently asked questions about protecting and recovering Active Directory (AD) objects. Sources Where do I need to install the Cohesity agent? Install the agent on all DCs with FSMO roles that you want Cohesity to protect. How do I upgrade the agent? You can upgrade agents to the latest version from the Cohesity cluster. Permissions What permissions are required?
l Agent installation - Install the agent on all AD DCs with FSMO roles that you want to protect. Use an AD Domain Admin account to install the Cohesity agent with the Volume CBT driver. The service can run as the LocalSystem account.
l Recovery - The AD account that performs recovery must be one of the following: l Domain Admin or Enterprise Admin l Domain user with delegated permissions to the OU where objects will be recovered and reanimate permission on the AD Recycle Bin, if enabled (Delegation of Active Directory Recycle Bin).
Protection If I protect the DCs, will the servers they run on be protected? AD protection is intended to protect sufficient AD data to enable granular object and attribute recovery. The implementation does not protect the entire VM or physical server. To accomplish that, define separate VM/physical server protection. If I protect a forest DC, are all DCs in the forest protected? No. Protecting forest a DC does not protect all DCs in the forest. You must protect individual DCs. Recovery Do I need to open firewall ports when recovering?

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 17: MS Applications

MS Exchange Server

Yes. Recovery requires opening firewall ports to mount a snapshot on AD. For example, port 33389 and the 3 subsequent ports must be opened. A snapshot is missing a user that was added to production AD. What is wrong? If a new user was added to production AD after the snapshot was captured, the user will not be present in the snapshot on the cluster. How do I recover an entire OU? First recover the OU container and then recover all objects inside it. Can I recover multi-value attributes? Yes. Merge/overwrite options are provided for multi-value attributes such as url, telephone, etc. Can I recover a deleted OrganizationalUnit object? Yes. If the OrganizationalUnit (OU) is accidentally deleted, you can recover the OU from the snapshot. When you recover an OU object, all the attributes of the OU object including the gPLink attribute are recovered. Can I recover GPO links for Domain, Site or OrganizationalUnit? Yes. You can recover GPO links by initiating the recovery at an attribute level for an object. For example, recovery of attribute gPLink for OrganizationalUnit. Can I recover Active Directory Domain Controller? Yes. For more information, see Recover Active Directory Domain Controller. Can I recover all AD objects? Yes. You can recover all AD objects including GPOs except system attributes. Can I recover system attributes? No. You cannot recover system attributes. For example, system IDs or object IDs. Cohesity cannot restore system attributes if the object is deleted or not available in the AD recycle bin. Can I recover attributes from the AD recycle bin if the AD recycle bin is enabled? If the AD recycle bin is enabled, Cohesity will attempt to restore from the AD recycle bin and attempt to preserve everything of that object from the AD recycle bin restore. If the AD recycle bin is not enabled or the object is past TTL, the system attributes of that object are not restored.

Description Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy.

Note: Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.

l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Protection Groups.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve a similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
For best performance, Cohesity recommends the Backup Target SSD policy. If necessary, you can change the policy at any time later. but it doesn't change or take effect on the currently running task.

Indexing

This option is enabled by default and is required for file recovery. By enabling this option, Cohesity cluster will scan all the files in the Protection Group and create an internal index that can be used later by a recover task to locate files by name.

Exchange Log Truncation

This option is enabled by default and truncates the Exchange server transaction logs. If this option is disabled, then "copy only" backup is taken and transaction logs are not truncated.

Cancel Runs at Quiet Time Start

Available only if the selected policy has at least one quiet time period. Toggle it on to specify that all currently executing job runs should abort if a quiet time period specified for the Protection Group starts. By default this toggle is off, which means after a job run starts, it continues to execute even when a quiet time period specified for this job starts. However, a new job run will not start during a quiet time period.

Recover MS Exchange Server
This topic describes how to recover the Exchange Server objects (Exchange Databases) that you have successfully backed up on the Cohesity cluster. Cohesity supports two types of recovery options for Exchange Server objects.
View-Based Recovery
Cohesity mounts the view over SMB on the target server. The mounted views contain the database files and transaction logs. You can use Ontrack to perform recovery of mailbox databases including granular recoveries such as individual mailboxes, emails, files, and folders.
Note: Microsoft Exchange (on-premises) requires Ontrack® software and a license for the granular recovery of mailbox databases such as individual mailbox, emails, files and folders. Cohesity recommends you to install Ontrack® on a separate Windows machine (than Exchange server) with an AD account that has appropriate mailbox permissions. The Windows machine must be registered as a physical source on Cohesity. On recovery, Cohesity will expose an SMB share with Exchange database files that can be opened using Ontrack®. You can also use Exchange tools such as ESEUTIL.EXE to perform manual inspection and recovery.
The Exchange database files will be recovered to the following SMB path of the Cohesity View:
\\<cluster_Ip>\<storage _domain>.<view_name>.fs\exchange
For example:
\\10.10.10.10\DefaultStorageDomain.ExchView_1585178933.fs\exchange
Database recovery
MS Exchange database recovery allows you to restore Exchange Server databases to a healthy state during a failure or data loss event. These databases store email messages, calendar items, contacts, and other vital information, making their recovery crucial for business continuity. When recovering an MS Exchange database, you can either overwrite the original database or restore to an alternate database.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 17: MS Applications

MS Exchange Server

Important: If you want to Overwrite the Original Database, you must enable the This database can be overwritten by a restore parameter from the Exchange Admin Center. To enable the parameter:
1. Log in to the Exchange Admin Center. 2. Select Servers from the left-nav and then navigate to databases.
This will list all the databases on the Exchange Server. 3. Select the database you want to overwrite and then click the Edit icon at the
top-right corner to open the database properties window. 4. In the database properties window, navigate to the Maintenance Tab and
select the This database can be overwritten by a restore check-box. 5. Click Save.

User name of the mailbox c. E-mail address of the mailbox d. IP address or hostname of Exchange Server. 5. You can optionally specify the wildcard character *. You can also optionally narrow the search results by specifying filter criteria, for example, you can filter the search results by a specific Protection Group, source or date.
Note: If you choose multiple databases, recovery to the original location is the only option available.
6. Select the object(s) you want to recover.

MS Exchange Server

RDBs allow you to recover data from a backup or copy of a database without disrupting user access to current data. b. Mount Database: Enable this option to restart the Information Store service and mount the new Database.

Unregister MS Exchange Server
You can unregister an Exchange Server from the Cohesity cluster. Before you unregister it, you must delete the Protection Groups associated with the Exchange Server.
1. Delete a Protection Group 2. Unregister Exchange Server 3. Uninstall the Cohesity Agent
Delete a Protection Group
Perform the following steps to delete a Protection Group: If the Protection Group is deleted, then overwrite restores cannot be performed on the job.
1. Select Data Protection > Protection. 2. Find the Job in the list and in the Actions column select Delete.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 17: MS Applications

MS Exchange Server

Alternatively, drill-down on a Job name in the Job column of the list. In the Job
Details page, click the (Delete Job) icon.
3. Choose one of the following: l Delete Protection Group Only: Select this option to delete only the Protection Group. Any local snapshots and or archived snapshots stored on the external targets that were captured by this Job are not deleted. l Delete Protection Group and Snapshots: If you select the option to delete the Job and all Snapshots, any local Snapshots captured by this Job and stored on this Cluster are deleted. In addition, any archived Snapshots stored on external targets that were captured by this Job are also deleted. (To selectively delete the Snapshots for specific protection runs without deleting the Job, see Deleting Snapshots or Objects.)
If the current job is replicating snapshots to a remote cluster or archiving snapshots to an external target, you should probably cancel these replication or archive tasks before deleting the job. For instructions, see Cancel Replication and Archive Copy Tasks of a Protection Group Run. If the Job is replicating to a remote cluster, the inactive job created on the remote cluster is not deleted. In addition, the snapshots that were replicated (copied) to the remote cluster by this job are not deleted. You can log in to the remote cluster to delete the snapshots and the inactive job.

Truncate Logs in Microsoft Exchange Servers on Physical Windows Servers
Microsoft Exchange Email Server truncates transaction logs dynamically after a successful backup of a physical Windows Server that hosts the Exchange Email Server. Cohesity has qualified truncating logs for the following Microsoft Exchange Servers hosted on physical Servers:
l Microsoft Exchange 2019 running on supported Windows Servers (Standalone and DAG)
l Microsoft Exchange 2016 running on supported Windows Servers (Standalone and DAG)
l Microsoft Exchange 2013 running on supported Windows Servers (Standalone and DAG)
l Microsoft Exchange 2010 SP3 running on supported Windows Servers (Standalone and DAG)
When a protection run protecting physical servers occurs, an app-consistent backup is always triggered so if the physical server is a Windows server with Microsoft Exchange, the Exchange logs are dynamically truncated by Microsoft Exchange. To disable log truncation for Microsoft Exchange with VMware VADP backups, see Enable or Disable Log Truncation. If the Windows Server has an Exchange server but the log truncation fails, an error is reported. However, the backup can successfully complete.
Note: The physical Server adapter includes Exchange Log Truncation functionality. You can also backup the Exchange Server using the Exchange Server adapter.
For more information on how to leverage Cohesity for Exchange Server backups using the physical adapter, see the How to protect and truncate logs for Exchange VMs (Standalone or DAG) on Hyper-V KB article. Cohesity provides support for backup and recovery of Microsoft Exchange Servers (Standalone and DAG) running on a physical server or VM. For more information, see Protect MS Exchange Server.

Category Source Registration Recovery

Issue

Workaround

IP address-based DAG Exchange registration may fail due to Cohesity Cluster not able to resolve FQDN of the DAG nodes.

Add the Exchange node DNS server to Cohesity cluster DNS server or to Cohesity host mapping.

Repeatedly mounting SMB share of the Exchange database recovery with the same view name and tearing down may cause issues in accessing the view in Windows Explorer.

Provide a unique view name for each database recovery.

Incremental backup schedule after a Windows reboot or DAG node switchover pulls the entire Exchange database EDB file.

None.
File- based change block tracking (CBT) information is not preserved across Windows reboots. Log backup is not affected by this and only new log files are pulled for a DAG database copy.

Deletion of snapshots from protection runs in the middle or expiration of the log backup may subsequent snapshots until incremental/full to be not recoverable .

None. Delete only the oldest snapshots of backup runs.

Plan and Prepare for IBM Storage FlashSystem
This topic provides information on minimum permissions, prerequisites and considerations to protect IBM Storage FlashSystem with Cohesity cluster. Minimum Permissions Ensure that the IBM Storage FlashSystem user account you use to register, manage, and protect the FlashSystem resources has an Administrator role. For security reasons, Cohesity recommends not to use the IBM superuser account or any account configured within the SecurityAdmin group. Support Matrix Before you register your IBM Storage FlashSystem with the Cohesity cluster, ensure that Cohesity supports the IBM Storage FlashSystem versions. For more information, see Supported Software.

Prerequisite
l IBM Storage FlashSystem API and data traffic ports should be accessible from all the Cohesity nodes. For more information, see Ports Used for Communication.
l It is important to note that the Cohesity cluster's node(s) should not be added manually as a host or host cluster on the IBM Storage FlashSystem as this will be done automatically when registering the array as a source on the Cohesity cluster.
Considerations
l Due to the IBM Storage FlashSystem volume name character limit, Cohesity does not support backing up volumes with names greater than 45 characters.
l IBM Storage FlashSystem supports block-based backups of volumes and volume groups.
l With IBM Storage FlashSystem, you have the flexibility to create volumes while utilizing various capacity-saving methods such as thin-provisioning, compression, deduplication, or a combination of these methods. However, it's important to note that if there is a predefined provisioning policy set for the storage pool, the volumelevel settings will not be applicable. In case of a restore, the system will restore the capacity-saving options based on the target storage pool's properties and the existence of any predefined provisioning policies.
l IBM Storage FlashSystem supports Safeguarded Snapshot creation for basic volumes, but it is not supported for mirrored volumes.
Register or Edit an IBM Storage FlashSystem
You can register IBM Storage FlashSystem on the Cohesity cluster to protect the IBM Flash volumes.
Before you Begin
Meet Prerequisites
Ensure that the requirements for the IBM FlashSystem, such as software version, user account role privileges, and firewall ports, are met.
Check iSCSI connectivity
By registering an IBM FlashSystem as a storage array, you can ensure that its Logical Unit Number (LUN) becomes eligible for protection on the Cohesity cluster. The LUN of both the Internet Small Computer Systems Interfaces (iSCSI) or Fiber Channels (FC) is needed to access the storage device.

Plan and Prepare for Pure FlashArray
This topic provides information on minimum permissions, prerequisites and considerations to protect Pure FlashArray with Cohesity cluster.
Minimum Permissions
Ensure you have the required minimum permissions to register Pure FlashArray as a source with the Cohesity. For more information, see Ensure Adequate Privileges for Cohesity on the Source.
Support Matrix
Before you register your Pure FlashArray with the Cohesity cluster, ensure that Cohesity supports the Pure FlashArray versions. For more information, see Supported Software.
Ports Used for Communication
Ensure all necessary ports are open in the firewall between the Cohesity cluster and Pure FlashArray. For more information, see Manage Firewall Ports.
Prerequisite
The Pure Flash array needs to have a Network Interface Card (NIC) and iSCSI discovery IP configured on the array.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 18: SAN Volume

Pure Storage

Considerations
l For storage-backed snapshots to work, the SAN transport must be configured over iSCSI.
l iSCSI needs to be configured on the Pure FlashArray for volume backup.
l Recovering a Pure Storage volume with the same name as a volume that is pending eradication is not supported.
Workaround - Recover the volume with a different name or log in to the Pure FlashArray and eradicate the deleted volume.
l If a Pure FlashArray reaches its maximum number of volumes or snapshots, Pure Storage backup jobs and recovery tasks for that array will fail. A Pure Storage volume also has a maximum number of allowed snapshots. If it reaches this limit, backing up the volume fails.
Workaround - Delete and eradicate some volumes or snapshots and then trigger the backup or recovery.
l Due to a Pure Storage volume name character limit, Cohesity does not support backing up volumes with names greater than 45 characters.
l Cohesity does not currently support backing up Pure FlashArrays with ChallengeHandshake Authentication Protocol (CHAP) authentication enabled.
l If a Cohesity cluster has been destroyed and then recreated, its Cohesity host entry from the original Pure FlashArray registration is retained on the array. This causes IQN collision when registering the same Pure FlashArray with the recreated Cluster. IQN collision causes Cohesity backups of the array to fail.
Workaround - Follow the below steps:
l Run the following command on any Node in the Cluster to obtain the Cluster's IQN: allssh cat /etc/iscsi/initiatorname.iscsi
l On the Pure FlashArray, remove the host entry that matches the obtained IQN. l Unregister and re-register the Pure FlashArray with the Cohesity cluster.
l If a Cluster upgrade is running during a Pure Storage backup job, the job may fail. The job will succeed on the next retry attempt.
l Cohesity does not currently support Pure Storage PODS or Active Cluster but you can register the individual arrays within the Active Cluster separately as standalone arrays.
l There is a limitation on the number of hosts that can be accommodated in the Pure FlashArray. When this limit is reached, it may lead to iSCSI communication failures during the backup processes.
Error Message:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 18: SAN Volume

Pure Storage

Encountered HTTP error kBadRequest with GET request for /host/cohesity1732787028580538/volume [Host does not exist.]
Workaround Follow the below steps:
l Create a free slot for a new host entry in the Pure FlashArray. l Choose one of the following options:
l Restart the Backup Manager service using the following CLI commands:
iris_cli cluster stop service-names=magneto
iris_cli cluster start service-names=magneto
l Alternatively, you can wait for an hour for the host creation process to complete.
l The following lists the considerations for a Pure Protection Group during the backup and recovery process: l Cohesity does not support the protection of empty Pure Protection Groups. l The name of the Pure Protection Group and Pure volumes created during recovery will be based on the specified suffix and prefix. l If the newly created PPG or a volume has the same name as that of the PPGs or volumes belonging to an existing PPG, then the recovery jobs will fail. l Volume Group will not be created. It should pre-exist. The recovery volumes will be created in the same volume group in which the original volume was present. If the volume group is not present at the time of recovery then the recovery job will fail.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 19: Hadoop

The Cohesity Hadoop DataProtect solution natively integrates with Cloudera distributions to provide consistent backup and recovery for Hadoop deployments. The Cohesity solution supports Hive, HBase, and HDFS data sources.

Based on the policy settings, the Cohesity NoSQL and Hadoop Service initiates a backup of the HDFS, Hive, or Hbase. The first backup is a full backup and everything after that is an incremental backup only. The service scales horizontally based on the available compute and memory resources on Cohesity. Multiple backup and recovery streams run in parallel to reduce the backup and recovery window. The necessary Cohesity Views are automatically generated where the backups are going to be written. Communication between Cohesity and Hadoop is managed by the NoSQL and Hadoop Service as described in the section below. See the following topics for details:

Core components

Hadoop Features

Plan and Prepare for Hadoop Protection

Register a Hadoop Source

Backup Hadoop

Recover Hadoop

Core components
The following lists the core components of the Cohesity Hadoop solution:
l Physical or virtual Hadoop clusters. l Cohesity Data Cloud. l Cohesity Compute Nodes. l Cohesity NoSQL and Hadoop Service running on Cohesity Compute Nodes. l Optional. Archive or tiering target at your data center or cloud provider of choice.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 19: Hadoop

Hadoop Features

As illustrated in the below figure, you can integrate Cohesity with an existing Hadoop infrastructure by installing the Cohesity NoSQL and Hadoop Service on Compute Nodes. Once the service is installed and running, you can create protection policies, Protection Groups, and replication schedules for the Hadoop file system and databases. Once the data is protected, it can be archived, sent to tape, and or replicated to another instance running in the cloud or on-premises as shown in the below image.

Hadoop Features
Following are the key Hadoop-specific features of the solution: l Support Cloudera distributions of Hadoop. l Support Hive, Hbase, and HDFS. l Incremental-forever backups - after the first full backup, all subsequent backups are incremental only forever. l Granular backup and recovery - backup and recover individual tables, databases, or files. l Automatically handle topology changes seamlessly (node addition, removal, IP changes, etc.) l Support Kerberos enabled clusters. l Support SSL-enabled clusters.

Kerberos-Enabled Hadoop
The following section describes the steps you need to perform for adding a Kerberized Hadoop data repository. Adding Kerberized Hadoop data repository: This section describes the steps that must be performed on the primary source cluster prior to successfully add new Kerberized HDFS, HBase, or Hive data repositories. These steps are also needed when you are adding a new data repository with a new set of Kerberos principals.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 19: Hadoop

Plan and Prepare for Hadoop Protection

Note: At the end of these steps, service restart is required on both Primary and NoSQL Hadoop clusters. Protection runs will be killed. Please plan this activity when no protection runs are in progress.
1. Add the new realm to NoSQL and Hadoop Services as mentioned in the section Work with Kerberos Security enabled primaries for data protection.
2. Make changes to the Primary cluster's HDFS, Hive and HBase configuration. Let us assume that you plan to use the following as backup/recovery user principals on your primary Hadoop cluster:
imanis_hdfs@PRIMARY.REALM - Kerberos principal used for HDFS workflows
imanis_hbase@PRIMARY.REALM - Kerberos principal used for HBase workflows
imanis_hive@PRIMARY.REALM - Kerberos principal used for Hive workflows
These Kerberos principals map to corresponding Unix users. For example, imanis_ hdfs@PRIMARY.REALM maps to Unix user imanis_hdfs on your primary cluster nodes. Similarly, imanis_hbase@PRIMARY.REALM maps to imanis_hbase and imanis_ hive@PRIMARY.REALM maps to imanis_hive Unix user. All these three users should be added to a group, for example, imanis_supergroup in all cluster Nodes of your primary hadoop cluster. The steps for performing the changes on the primary cluster differ from vendor to vendor. The below example is applicable for Cloudera 6.0. For other vendors and versions please refer to the vendor-specific documentation.
l Grant superuser privileges in the primary Hadoop cluster to the Kerberos principals used for backup/recovery. a. In Cloudera Manager Admin Console, click HDFS service > Configuration tab. b. Search for the dfs.permissions.superusergroup property and add imanis_ supergroup to this property. c. Save the changes and restart HDFS service.
l Set hbase.superuser to imanis_hbase a. In Cloudera Manager Web UI, click HBase > Configuration tab. b. Search for hbase.superuser and set it to imanis_hbase. c. Deploy the changed configuration and restart HBase service.
l On the primary Hadoop cluster, add hbase.superuser property to the hbasesite.xml if not already present.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 19: Hadoop

Plan and Prepare for Hadoop Protection

<property> <name>hbase.superuser</name> <value>imanis_hbase</value> </property>
l On the primary Hadoop cluster, add dfs.webhdfs.enabled property in the hdfssite.xml file:
<property> <name>dfs.webhdfs.enabled</name> <value>true</value> </property>
SSL-Enabled Hadoop
The following section describes the tasks you need to perform before adding SSL-enabled Hadoop as a source data repository in the Cohesity cluster. Before adding SSL-enabled Hadoop, do the following:
1. Consult your Hadoop system admin to get the SSL certificates of all nodes in your production Hadoop system.
2. Import SSL certificates from your primary cluster into Cohesity by following the steps documented in Manage SSL enabled NoSQL primary clusters .
3. After importing the SSL certificates(step #2), run the following command from any one node of the Cohesity cluster to verify if your Hadoop primary is accessible from the NoSQL and Hadoop Service node.

Log in to one of the Cohesity cluster nodes and run the following:

$ kubectl.sh get pods --all-namespaces

athena-104 3

imanis-nodemanager-0 41h

| grep

imanis-nodemanager-0

1/1

Running

Log in to imanis container using the following command:

$ kubectl.sh exec -it imanis-nodemanager-0 -n athena-104 /bin/bash

Check if you can reach the primary namenode host from Imanis container using the following command:

$ ping <primary_namenode_hostname> hdfs dfs -ls swebhdfs://<primary_namenode_hostname>:50470/

4. Go ahead and add this SSL-enabled Hadoop as a data repository in Cohesity.

Kerberos + SSL-Enabled Hadoop

The following section describes the tasks you need to perform before adding Kerberos + SSL-enabled Hadoop as a source data repository in Cohesity.
Before adding Kerberos + SSL-enabled Hadoop, do the following:

$ kubectl.sh get pods --all-namespaces | grep imanis-nodemanager-0

athena-104 3

imanis-nodemanager-0 41h

1/1

Running

Considerations
Hadoop HDFS
l Unicode characters in hdfs file and directory names are not supported. l Special characters % ; + (percent semicolon plus) in hdfs file and directory names are
not supported. l Access Control Lists (ACLs) are not supported.
Hive
l Backup and Recovery across versions/vendors is not supported. For example, performing a data backup from CDH 5.8.2 and then recovering it to CDH 5.12.2 might cause data loss.
l Special characters, except underscore( _ ), are not supported for database and table names.
l Access Control Lists (ACLs) is not supported. l For Cloudera Data Platform 7.x, backup and Recovery of hive databases: sys and
information_schema is not supported.
HBase
l Backup and Recovery across versions/vendors is not supported. For example, performing a data backup from CDH 5.8.2 and then recovering it to CDH 5.12.2 might cause data loss.
l Access Control Lists (ACLs) is not supported.
Firewall Ports
For more information on the required firewall ports that are to be open to enable communication between Cohesity and Hadoop DataProtect Solution, see Open-Source Software Platform.
Minimum Permissions
This section describes the minimum set of permissions needed for the Hadoop DataProtect Solution to communicate with the source. For kerberized setup: User principal provided in UI must have super user privileges of production hadoop cluster and must have full access to the production HDFS/HIVE/Hbase system. For non-kerberized setups: NoSQL and Hadoop Service user (hdfs) must have full access to the production HDFS/HIVE/Hbase setups.

Enable or Disable Auto Protect
The Auto Protect option enables you to automatically protect the objects that are added to the Hive/ HBase source. You can auto protect either the entire cluster or a Keyspace. When the Auto Protect option is enabled:
l All the objects that are added to the Hive/ HBase source in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run.
l All the objects that are removed from the Hive/ HBase source in the future are automatically removed from the Protection Group and are not protected from the next protection run. The existing backups are preserved until the snapshot expires.
When the Auto Protect option is disabled, you need to manually:
l Add newly added objects, in the Hive/ HBase source, to the Protection Group. l Remove existing objects, that are removed from the Hive/ HBase source, from the
Protection Group. The existing backups are preserved until the snapshot expires.
To enable or disable Auto Protect:

HBase. For more information, see Protect Hive Objects and Protect HBase Objects.

1. Navigate to Data Protection > Recoveries. 2. Click Recover on the top-right of the page and then select Hadoop> Hive. The New
Recovery dialog is displayed. 3. Search for the Hive protection groups or objects such as hive databases, tables, or
views. that need to be recovered.
Note: Wildcards are supported in the search.
4. Accept the latest Recovery Point or click and select a different recovery point. l Snapshots: Select a different recovery point. You can change the time zone before or after selecting a new restore time.
5. Click Next: Recover Options. The recovery details are displayed. 6. Under Recover As select Replace Original or New Object.
l Replace Original - Replace the object(s) back to the source from where it was backed up.

l New Object - Specify the target for the recovered object. Use the toggle to Overwrite existing objects with the same name. A warning is displayed, enter YES to proceed.

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter
Note: Cohesity Remote Adapter functionality is not supported if SmartFiles is not licensed on your Cohesity cluster.
Remote Adapter Protection Groups provide the ability to run scripts or executables on a remote AIX or Linux machine using protection schedules defined by a Cohesity Policy. Typically Remote Adapter Protection Groups invoke scripts that back up using third party tools such as Oracle's RMAN. During the configuration of the Remote Adapter Job, a new View is created to store the results of the backup. After a script run, the Job captures a Snapshot of the View with the backup results. If the Policy associated with the Remote Adapter Job has a replication schedule and an archive schedule, the View Snapshot is copied to a remote Cluster and to an archive External Target. For example, a Remote Adapter Job could invoke a script that backs up Oracle databases using Oracle's Recovery Manager (RMAN). The results of the backup are stored in a new View created during the configuration of the Remote Adapter Job. Cohesity provides an example Bash shell script that invokes an Oracle's RMAN to back up a database.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter The Job captures a Snapshot of the View with the backup results.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter
If the Policy associated with the Remote Adapter Job has a replication schedule, the Snapshot is copied to a remote Cluster ("EngReserve", below).

Replication occurs if the following conditions are met:
l The Policy associated with the Remote Adapter Protection Group has a replication schedule. In this example, the Policy defines a Weekly replication schedule.
l The Policy associated with the Remote Adapter Protection Group specifies a remote Cluster as the replication Target and there is a Storage Domain pairing between the capturing Cluster and this remote Cluster. In the example above, the Policy specifies the EngReserve Cluster as a Replication Target and there is Storage Domain pairing between DevStorageDomain on the EngMain Cluster and EngBackupStorageDomain on the EngRerserve Cluster.
If the Policy associated with the Remote Adapter Job has an archive schedule, the Snapshot is copied to an archive External Target.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Recommendations for Dedupe-focused Backups with RMAN

Archival occurs if the following conditions are met:
l The Policy associated with the Remote Adapter Protection Group has an archive schedule. In this example, the Policy defines a Monthly archive schedule.
l The Policy associated with the Remote Adapter Protection Group specifies an External Target as the archive Target. In this example, the Policy specifies the EngArchive External Target as an archive Target.
For more information about creating and configuring a Remote Adapter Protection Group, see Add or Edit a Remote Adapter Protection Group.

Example of a full RMAN backup script In the example below, four Oracle channels are created and each channel is directed to a separate Cohesity node leveraging the Cohesity dedupe:
DATABASE = "Name of DB" ORACLE_HOME=/u01/OracleHomes/db/product/dbhome_1 COHESITY_DIR_PATH =/mnt/oracle01 COHESITY_DIR_PATH2=/mnt/oracle02 COHESITY_ DIR_PATH3=/mnt/oracle03 COHESITY_DIR_PATH4=/mnt/oracle04
set ORACLE_SID=${DATABASE} $ORACLE_HOME/bin/rman target=/ << EOF RUN { allocate channel C1 type disk FORMAT '$COHESITY_DIR_PATH/%U' MAXOPENFILES 1; allocate channel C2 type disk FORMAT '$COHESITY_DIR_PATH2/%U' MAXOPENFILES 1; allocate channel C3 type disk FORMAT '$COHESITY_DIR_PATH3/%U' MAXOPENFILES 1; allocate channel C4 type disk FORMAT '$COHESITY_DIR_PATH4/%U' MAXOPENFILES 1;
BACKUP FULL DATABASE PLUS ARCHIVELOG FILESPERSET 1 TAG 'dedupe_focused'; RELEASE CHANNEL C1; RELEASE CHANNEL C2; RELEASE CHANNEL C3; RELEASE CHANNEL C4; }
EOF
Add or Edit a Remote Adapter Protection Group
Remote Adapter Protection Groups provide the ability to run scripts or executables on a remote AIX or Linux machine using protection schedules defined by a Cohesity Policy. Typically Remote Adapter Protection Groups invoke scripts that back up using third party tools such as Oracle's RMAN. During the configuration of the Remote Adapter Job, a new View is created to store the results of the backup. After a script run, the Job captures a Snapshot of the View with the backup results. If the Policy associated with the Remote Adapter Job has a replication schedule and an archive schedule, the View Snapshot is copied to a remote Cluster and to an archive External Target. The Protection Group captures snapshots of views and snapshots of views are required for the following tasks:
l creating a new view from a view snapshot l replicating snapshots

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

Add or Edit a Remote Adapter Protection Group

l archiving snapshots
The Cohesity cluster supports backing up the following entities stored in the view:
l ordinary files l directories l symbolic links l hard links
These entities can be captured in a view snapshot and restored to a new view. The backup and recovery of the following special files is supported: pipes, block devices, sockets and character devices.
Limitation:
If Remote Adapter jobs are running on a Cohesity cluster and the cluster is upgraded, the nodes are restarted and any scripts still running on the remote system are killed and restarted. This may happen repeatedly. When you create a Remote Adapter Protection Group, you will create a View or use an existing View to store the result of the scripts. You must then mount the View on your system and configure your script to write the results to a directory in the mounted View. At the end of the Remote Adapter protection run, the Cohesity cluster captures a Snapshot of the View. When you create a Remote Adapter Protection Group, you can select an existing Policy, Storage Domain and View. You can also create them while creating the Protection Group. However, you might find it easier to create them prior to creating the Protection Group, as described in the following topics.
l Create or Edit a Standard Policy l Create or Edit Storage Domains l Create Views Using a Predefined Template
To create a Remote Adapter Protection Group:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection and do one of the following: l To create a Protection Group--Click Protect on the top-right of the page and then select the type of Protection Group.
l To edit a Protection Group--Click the action icon ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Edit.
Here the Protection Group type is Remote Adapter. 2. Name: Enter a name for the Protection Group. The name can contain alphanumeric
characters, underscores, dashes, and periods. 3. Linux Hostname or IP: Specify the Hostname or the IP Address of the Linux system
where the scripts are located and will be run.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

Add or Edit a Remote Adapter Protection Group

4. Username: Specify the username on the Linux system that will be running the scripts.
5. Cluster SSH Public Key: Set up permissions on the Linux system to allow the Cohesity cluster to run the scripts remotely on the system. a. Click Copy Key to Clipboard to copy the SSH public key into the clipboard. b. Log in to the Linux system with the username specified earlier. c. In the home directory of the user, determine if there is a .ssh directory that contains a file called authorized_keys:
ls -lr ~/.ssh
d. Add the SSH key to the authorized_keys file located in the ~/.ssh directory of the specified User: l If the directory and file do not exist, create the .ssh directory in the home directory.
[oracle@localhost ~]$ cd ~ [oracle@localhost ~]$ mkdir .ssh
l Change directories into the .ssh directory, create the authorized_keys file and paste the SSH key into a new line of the file.
[oracle@localhost ~]$ touch ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
l If the .ssh directory exists but the file does not, change directories into the .ssh directory, create the authorized_keys file and paste the SSH key into a new line of the file.
l If the authorized_keys file exists in the .ssh directory, edit the authorized_keys file and paste the SSH key into a new line of the file.
e. Set the .ssh directory and authorized_keys file permissions:
chmod 700 .ssh
chmod 640 .ssh/authorized_keys
6. Policy: Select an existing protection policy or create a new one by selecting New Policy.
7. Script (with Full Path): Enter the full path to the script, for example /home/joe/scripts/myscript.sh.
8. Parameters: If the script requires parameters, enter them in this field. Storage Domain: Select an existing storage domain or create a new one by selecting New Storage Domain.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

Add or Edit a Remote Adapter Protection Group

Note: Once you create a Protection Group, you cannot change the Storage Domain you selected for that job.
The selected Storage Domain will contain the new View where the script results are stored.
9. NFS View: Select an existing View create a new one by selecting Add View. For more information, see Create Views Using a Predefined Template. The View will contain the script results.
10. NFS Mount Path: Click Copy NFS Path to Clipboard for use later when you mount the View on the Linux system.
11. Start Time: Indicates when the Protection Group should run. The current time is displayed by default but you can change it. Enter the hour and minutes or use the up and down arrows on your keyboard. Verify the AM or PM setting.
The default time zone is the browser's time zone. You can change the time zone by selecting a different time zone.
12. End Date: Optional. Toggle on and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.
13. QoS Policy: Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy.
Note: Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.
l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Protection Groups.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
l TestAndDev High: The Cohesity cluster writes the data to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. The I/Os with this QoS policy are given higher priority compared to other QoS policies. Use this policy for workloads that require lower I/O latency.
14. Alerts: Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

About SAP HANA Database Backups

l Success: Create an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Create a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
For more information, see Alerts. 15. Priority: Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity supports
concurrent backups, but if the number of Protection Groups exceeds the ability to process them, those with High priority are given the highest priority to execute, Medium the second-highest priority, and Low the lowest priority. 16. Email Recipients: You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the Protection Group.
Note: The connection to the SMTP Server must be enabled to send email notification. You can enable the SMTP Server connection in the configuration settings page ( Cohesity UI > Settings > Summary > Configure > Enable SMTP Server).
17. SLA: The service-level agreement (SLA) defines the expected time to complete either a full backup or incremental backup. The backup completion time depends on the Windows volume size on AD, objects changed between incremental backups, network speed, and other Protection Groups running on the Cohesity cluster. l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental protection run to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last protection run. l Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup protection run to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).
18. Description: Optional. Click the plus sign and enter a description for the Protection Group.
19. Click Protect. The Protection page is displayed and includes the new Protection Group.

Create a Cohesity View with IP Allowlist for SAP HANA node
Create a Cohesity view to provide a storage location in a storage domain on the Cohesity cluster for the SAP HANA database nodes. For more information on views, see Cohesity Views. To provide effective authorization and prevent rogue access to the Cohesity cluster, the SAP HANA node IP address must be added in the Cohesity view configuration. For detailed instructions to create a view, see Create Views Using a Predefined Template.
Adding Custom Allowlist for the Cohesity View
While creating a Cohesity View, you have an option to add an allowlist for the View. Ensure that you add the SAP HANA node IP address in the Allowlist for the Cohesity View. To add subnets to the allowlist of the Cohesity view:
1. In the Create View page, under the Advanced section, expand Security. 2. In the Allowlist section, perform the following:
1. Select Override Global Allowlist and click Add Allowlist. 2. In the Subnet IP and Subnet Mask fields respectively, enter the Subnet IP
address and Subnet Mask to specify a range of systems that should have permissions to access and mount the Cohesity View. 3. In the NFS Permissions, SMB Permissions, and S3 Permissions dropdown lists, select the NFS, SMB, and S3 permissions respectively. 4. In the NFS Root Squash and NFS All Squash drop-down lists, specify whether to turn on NFS Root or NFS All squash respectively. 5. In the Description field, enter a brief description. 6. Click Add. 7. Repeat these steps to add additional subnets to the allowlist of the Cohesity view.
Note: l To use the IP allowlist feature the Cohesity cluster should be upgraded to 6.3 release or later.
l If the Override Global Allowlist toggle is off, this View can only be accessed and mounted by systems specified by the Global Cohesity cluster Allowlist.
l In case of a multinode HANA setup, specify all nodes individually in the global IP allowlist.

timedatectl set-ntp true

Update the Cohesity Parameter File
As part of the Cohesity BACKINT plugin installation, Cohesity provides a parameter file (cohesity_param_file) that enables SAP HANA to use the Cohesity BACKINT plugin for a backup job. The parameter file is available in the <backint_install_directory>. Edit the parameter file and enter the values for the following parameters:

Parameter cluster_ips

Description List of IP addresses of the Cohesity Cluster.
Note: Ensure that you provide only the virtual IP addresses.

cluster_port

The port number of the Cohesity cluster nodes that the plugin uses to establish communication between SAP HANA and the Cohesity cluster. The default port number is 11113 (gRPC).

Note: You can also use the 11111 (SunRPC) port to establish communication between SAP HANA and the Cohesity cluster. Ensure that you open the 11111 (SunRPC) port on the Cohesity cluster.

view_name

The name of the Cohesity view used to store the backup data.
Note: Ensure that the Cohesity view name does not contain the path of the Cohesity view or Cluster Name or IP address.

io_thread_ count

The number of IO threads for reading or writing data on the Cohesity view.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

About SAP HANA Database Backups

max_ outstanding_io

The number of pending IO threads. The range is 1-128 and the recommended value is 32.

max_io_size_ bytes

Maximum size of each IO in bytes. The range is 1048576-4194304 bytes and the recommended value is 4194304 bytes.

max_cached_io

The maximum number of IO cached/prefetched. The range is 1-128 and the recommended value is 64.

rpc_timeout_ msecs

Timeout in milliseconds for RPC requests.

inquire_ period_days

The number of days for which the inquire information is returned. The default value is 180 days.

Note: Once you create a Protection Group, you cannot change the Storage Domain you selected for that job.
The selected Storage Domain will contain the new View where the script results are stored.
10. NFS View: Select an existing View create a new one by selecting Add View. For more information, see Create Views Using a Predefined Template. The View will contain the script results.
11. NFS Mount Path: Click Copy NFS Path to Clipboard for use later when you mount the View on the Linux system.
12. Start Time: Indicates when the Protection Group should run. The current time is displayed by default but you can change it. Enter the hour and minutes or use the up and down arrows on your keyboard. Verify the AM or PM setting.
The default time zone is the browser's time zone. You can change the time zone by selecting a different time zone.
13. End Date: Optional. Toggle on and select the date when the Protection Group stops capturing snapshots. A protection run that starts prior to this date runs until completion even if it completes after this date.
14. QoS Policy: Select an appropriate quality of service (QoS) policy.
Note: Cohesity recommends specifying Backup HDD, which is the default.
l Backup HDD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an HDD drive for this Protection Group.
l Backup SSD: The Cohesity cluster writes the data directly to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. Only specify this policy if you need fast ingest speed for a small number of Protection Groups.
l Backup Auto: (Applicable only for Cohesity C6000 series) The Cohesity cluster writes the data to both SSDs and HDDs. The distribution of data will be based on the current usage of SSD and HDD. This policy tries to achieve similar backup performance as the Backup SSD policy and reduces the SSD wear-out compared to the Backup SSD policy.
l TestAndDev High: The Cohesity cluster writes the data to an SSD drive for this Protection Group. The I/Os with this QoS policy are given higher priority compared to other QoS policies. Use this policy for workloads that require lower I/O latency.
15. Alerts: Optional. Select one or more of the following settings if you want alerts to be created for the following triggers:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

About SAP HANA Database Backups

l Success: Create an informational alert when a Protection Group completes successfully. Emails are not sent when informational alerts are created.
l Failure: Create a critical alert if the Protection Group fails to complete. Emails are sent when critical alerts are created.
l SLA Violation: Create a warning alert if the Protection Group takes longer than the time period specified in the SLA field. Emails are sent when warning alerts are created.
For more information, see Alerts.
16. Priority: Select a priority for the Protection Group execution. Cohesity supports concurrent backups, but if the number of Protection Groups exceeds the ability to process them, those with High priority are given the highest priority to execute, Medium the second-highest priority, and Low the lowest priority.
17. Email Recipients: You can add email addresses to a Protection Group to notify the email recipients when alerts are triggered for the Protection Group.
Note: The connection to the SMTP Server must be enabled to send email notification. You can enable the SMTP Server connection in the configuration settings page ( Cohesity UI > Settings > Summary > Configure > Enable SMTP Server).
18. SLA: The service-level agreement (SLA) defines the expected time to complete either a full backup or incremental backup. The backup completion time depends on the Windows volume size on AD, objects changed between incremental backups, network speed, and other Protection Groups running on the Cohesity cluster.
l Incremental: Enter the number of minutes you expect an incremental protection run to complete. An incremental backup captures only the differences (changed blocks) since the last protection run.
l Full: Enter the number of minutes you expect a full backup protection run to complete. A full backup captures the entire object (all blocks).
19. Click Protect.
The Protection page is displayed and includes the new Protection Group.
To Create a Purge Job for SAP HANA Database
The purge Remote Adapter job removes the expired backups (decided by the retention period) from the Cohesity view. The full backup is independent, and the incremental, log, and differential backups depend on the full backup. Hence, we retain the last successful full backup on or before the retention period.
For example, suppose the purge Remote Adapter job is triggered on November 26th, and the retention period is configured as 14 days. In that case, the last successful full backup on

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

About SAP HANA Database Backups

or before November 12th is retained, and any backups older than the last successful full backups are deleted.
Note: DataLock is not supported when using the Remote Adapter workflow.
1. Run the following command on the SAP HANA node's bash CLI as an SAP HANA admin user. ID is DEV and secure connector service installation location is /usr/sap/DEV/home/install. /usr/sap/DEV/home/install/purge_job.sh
2. The steps for creating a purge job is similar to creating a backup job for the SAP HANA database. Follow the same steps listed in the Create a Remote Adapter Job for SAP HANA Database section.
However, you must note the following: l For Script (with Full Path): Enter the full path to the script. /usr/sap/DEV/home/install/purge_job.sh l For Parameters:, enter the following parameters.
Note: You can define the values for the purge_job.sh script parameters either using the long or short options. Ensure that:
l If you are using the long options, you need to define the value for the parameter using the "=" character. For example, --tenantdatabase-names=BHE.
l If you are using the short options, you need to define the value for the parameter using a single whitespace. For example, -t BHE.
