SAP HANA Certificate Authentication
The SAP HANA Certification provides the necessary authentication and also verifies whether the SAP HANA database, which performs backups to the Cohesity cluster, is a trusted entity. This certification provides the capability to set verification which allows only trusted sources to write to the Cohesity cluster through the SpanFS.
Create an SAP HANA Authentication Certificate
This section lists the steps for creating an SAP HANA authentication certificate.
1. Start the Cohesity CLI locally and log in to the Cohesity cluster using the ssh command with the support user account and specify the IP address. For more information, see Using the Cohesity CLI and List of Cohesity CLI Commands.
ssh support@198.51.100.12
2. If prompted, enter the password.
[support@198.51.100.12's password:
The cohesity_shell prompt is displayed. 3. Log in to the CLI:
cohesity shell# iris_cli

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

About SAP HANA Database Backups

The admin prompt is displayed. 4. Optionally, run the help command for a list of CLI commands.
admin@198.51.100.12> help
5. Run the cluster gen-src-cert command to generate a new SAP HANA certificate.
admin@198.51.100.12 cluster gen-src-cert cert-name="newdemocert" certvalidity=100 host-name="10.2.146.175" host-target="/tmp" Success: Certificate "newdemocert" generation and deployment successful.

Parameter Name cert-name cert-validity host-name
host-target

Description
Name of the certificate file. Its naming format is ${cert-name}_<random_number>.cfg. The validity of the source certificate generated. The time is displayed in days. The IP address/host name of the target system where you want to move the certificate. This is a mandatory parameter because the certificate generation process needs details of the host machine to generate public and private keys. The file directory path on the Cohesity cluster where the certificate is generated.

Note: After the SAP HANA certificate is generated on the Cohesity cluster, manually copy the certificate to your SAP HANA machine.
6. Update the following parameters in the parameter file.

Parameter Name Description

cluster_port

Port number on Cohesity cluster nodes to which the BACKINT executable connects. Use the port 11117 for secure connection (certificate config path should be a valid path). Use the port 11111 for an insecure connection (certificate config path should be an empty string). Contact Cohesity Support to enable these ports.

7. Run the list-source-certificates command to check all the global certificates deployed from the cluster.
Deploy an SAP HANA Certificate in a Multi-node Setup
This section lists the steps to deploy an SAP HANA authentication certificate in a multi-node SAP HANA setup.
1. Generate and deploy the SAP HANA authentication certificate to any one of the nodes in a multi-node SAP HANA system using the instructions provided in the previous section.
2. Use SCP to securely transfer the certificate to a target location on all the remaining (N-1) nodes.
scp <certificate_config_path> ip_address:<certificate_config_path>
Example
scp /usr/sap/ORC/home/install/cert.cfg 10.2.146.72: /usr/sap/ORC/home/install/cert.cfg
3. Change the cluster_port parameter value to 11117 and update the certificate_ config_path parameter value to the correct path of the certificate in the respective paramfile of each of the N nodes.

Source-Side Deduplication for SAP HANA
The Cohesity source-side deduplication provides storage efficient deduplication that enhances your SAP HANA environment with faster backups and reduced network traffic between SAP HANA and Cohesity cluster.
Enabling this functionality shifts the deduplication processes to the SAP HANA node and reduces the CPU consumption on the Cohesity cluster thus allowing further scaling to support more workloads. Additionally, source-side deduplication plugin integrates with Cohesity's built-in deduplication and minimizes data traffic by moving only the new data blocks.
Advantages of the source-side deduplication plugin:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

About SAP HANA Database Backups

l Faster backups. l Reduces network traffic between SAP HANA nodes and Cohesity cluster. l Enables more frequent backups resulting in higher RPOs. l Offloading deduplication reduces the CPU consumption and enables the Cohesity
cluster to run more backup workload sessions. You can enable source-side deduplication during a backup or recovery process. To enable source-side deduplication during backup: Edit the cohesity_param_file located at <backint_install_directory>. Set the enable_dedup_write parameter to true.
Note: By default, source-side deduplication is disabled during the backup process.

Replicate View and Restore SAP HANA Database
You can replicate the SAP HANA database data captured on a Cohesity cluster to a remote Cluster by performing the following tasks:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

About SAP HANA Database Backups

Note: To restore from archival or replication, one needs to disable auto log backups.
1. From the Cohesity cluster (source) where the SAP HANA data is captured, create a connection to the receiving (target) cluster where the view will be replicated. For information about registering a connection to the target cluster, see Create a Connection to the Remote Cohesity Cluster.
2. From the target cluster, create a connection back to the source cluster. 3. From the source cluster, create a Remote Adapter Protection Group with replication
enabled in the policy. For information about creating Remote Adapter job with replication enabled, see Add or Edit a Remote Adapter Protection Group. Restore SAP HANA DB from the Replicated View To restore the replicated data back to a SAP HANA Database, perform the following steps: 1. On the target cluster, create a clone of the replicated View. For information about cloning a View, see Clone a View. 2. Log in to the HANA database where you want to restore the replicated data. In the parameter file, replace the existing cluster IP address (source cluster IP address) with the target cluster IP address 3. Perform the restore operation. For more information about SAP HANA restore, see Alternate Restore of SAP HANA Database.

Retrieve Archived Data to an Alternate Cohesity cluster
CloudRetrieve provides the ability to download data that was archived from a Cohesity cluster to an alternate Cohesity cluster. For more information see, About CloudRetrieve.
To retrieve the SAP HANA data from the external target to another Cohesity cluster, perform the following steps:
1. Register the external target that contains the data you want to download to the alternate Cohesity cluster.
2. Submit a search for Protection Groups that contain the data you want to download from the cloud external target. The search may take a few hours to complete. If the job to be downloaded is from a particular Cohesity cluster, specify the job name and cluster name to narrow the results.
2. If the external target's encryption key file is managed manually, upload the key file to the alternate Cohesity cluster before triggering the search. See Create a CloudRetrieve Search Task for more details.
3. Download a snapshot from any of the Protection Groups in the search results. You can also build a local index of Protection Groups that ran during a specified date range. Downloading can take a few hours to complete. See Create a CloudRetrieve Download Task for more details.
4. Recover or clone any downloaded objects using the Cohesity recovery or clone workflows. See CloudRetrieve Downloaded Protection Groups for more details.
Restore HANA DB from the Archived View
You can restore the retrieved data from the remote Cohesity cluster to the SAP HANA database by performing the following steps:
To restore the replicated data back to a SAP HANA Database, perform the following steps:
1. On the remote Cohesity cluster, create a clone of the retrieved View. For information about cloning a View, see Clone a View.
2. Login to the SAP HANA database where you want to restore the retrieved data. In the parameter file, replace the existing Cohesity cluster IP address (primary clusterCohesity cluster IP address) with the remote Cohesity cluster IP address.
3. Perform the restore operation. For more information about SAP HANA restore, see Alternate Restore of SAP HANA Database.
SAP HANA Database FAQ
1. Which SAP HANA versions are supported by Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin on 6.2 DataProtect? SAP HANA Platform Edition 2.0.
2. Is Cohesity SAP HANA Certified? Yes, Cohesity is certified on SAP HANA Platform Edition 2.0.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

About SAP HANA Database Backups

3. Which SAP HANA Environments are supported by the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin on 6.2 DataProtect onwards? Single Tenancy and Multitenancy environments are supported.
4. Which OS version is supported with the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin on 6.2 DataProtect onwards? All versions that are supported by SAP HANA Platform Edition (Intel platforms).
5. What is Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin? It is an SAP HANA agent installed on the SAP HANA appliance.
6. Does the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin leverages BACKINT? Yes, the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin leverages SAP HANA BACKINT to protect the SAP HANA appliance.
7. Does the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin install requires a reboot of the SAP HANA nodes? No, the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin (Cohesity SAP HANA agent) does not require a reboot of the SAP HANA nodes or restart of the SAP HANA instances.
8. Does the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin support client-side dedupe? Yes, it is supported from the 6.4.1x release onwards.
9. Is the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin leverages NFS? Yes. The Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin for IBM PowerPC systems leverages NFS. But, the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin for Intel x86 based systems does not leverage the NFS protocol. It uses remote snapFS.
10. If I have a Multi-node SAP HANA system, do I need to install the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin in all the nodes? Yes, this would allow the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin to take advantage of the high availability functionality when any of the SAP HANA nodes are down to service the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin.
11. Does the SAP HANA Studio require a restart if the global.ini was modified via the CLI? Yes. If you have modified global.ini for the Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin for Intel x86 based systems then the SAP HANA Studio requires a restart to apply the changes.
12. Does SAP HANA have any dependencies with Cohesity Linux or Oracle adapters?
No, Cohesity SAP HANA BACKINT plugin is independent of the Linux file/block or Oracle adapters. SAP HANA BACKINT plugin does not need the Cohesity Linux agent service to be installed for SAP HANA protection. However, both the SAP HANA BACKINT plugin and the Linux agent can coexist together for their respective functionalities.
13. Do we need to create a folder, or use the SAP HANA View created for the Remote adaptor job?

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

SAP on Oracle

No. Do not manually create any folders inside the View dedicated to the Remote adaptor job, as the Purge script will fail if any folders or files are created manually within the SAP HANA View.
SAP on Oracle
Cohesity provides a simple, fast, and cost-effective backup, recovery, and data management solution for Oracle databases running on the large-scale SAP ERP on Linux operating systems. SAP uses backup BR*TOOLS to back up Oracle databases. Cohesity provides the following methods to backup Oracle database leveraging the BR*TOOLS:
l Backup using BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle - Cohesity provides an SAP-certified BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle that leverages BR*TOOLs for protecting Oracle databases.
l Backup using custom Oracle SBT (Secure Backup to Tapes) and BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle - Cohesity provides a custom SBT extension that you can use along with BACKINT Secure Connector Service to backup Oracle databases.
Using the backup methods you can back up and restore the following for Oracle databases running in an SAP system:
l Oracle database files such as data files (*.dbf) and control files (*.ctl) l Archived redo logs l Parameter files such as PFILE or SPFILE l SAP BR*TOOLS files l SAP files
Core Components
The following are the core components for protecting Oracle databases running on an SAP system:
l Oracle Database l SAP BR*TOOLS l Cohesity BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle l Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-Managed)
As illustrated, you can integrate the Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-Managed) with new or existing Oracle database deployments in SAP by installing the Cohesity BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle.

Create a Cohesity View with IP Allowlist for the SAP Node

Create a CohesityView to provide a storage location in a storage domain on the Cohesity cluster for the SAP on Oracle nodes. For more information on views, see Cohesity Views.
To provide effective authorization and prevent rogue access to the Cohesity cluster, the SAP node IP address must be added to the allowlist in the Cohesity view configuration.

Adding Custom Allowlist for the Cohesity View

While creating a Cohesity View, you have an option to add an allowlist for the View. Ensure that you add the SAP HANA node IP address to the allowlist for the Cohesity View.
To add subnets to the allowlist of the Cohesity view:

1. In the Create View page, under the More Options, expand Security. 2. In the IP Allowlist section, perform the following:
1. Select Override Global Allowlist and click Add Allowlist. 2. In the Subnet IP and Subnet Mask fields respectively, enter the Subnet IP
address and Subnet Mask to specify a range of systems that should have permissions to access and mount the Cohesity View. 3. In the NFS Permissions, SMB Permissions, and S3 Permissions dropdown lists, select the NFS, SMB, and S3 permissions respectively. 4. In the NFS Root Squash and NFS All Squash drop-down lists, specify whether to turn on NFS Root or NFS All squash respectively. 5. In the Description field, enter a brief description. 6. Click Add. 7. Repeat these steps to add additional subnets to the allowlist of the Cohesity view.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

SAP on Oracle

Note: l To use the IP allowlist feature, you need to upgrade the Cohesity cluster to 6.3 release or later. l If the Override Global Allowlist toggle is off, this View can only be accessed and mounted by systems specified by the Global Cohesity cluster Allowlist.
l In case of a multinode HANA setup, specify all nodes individually in the global IP allowlist.

The BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle is available as a script installer for x8664 systems. To download the installer:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources, and click Download Cohesity Agent. 2. In the Download Agents window, click SAP on Oracle and then select Script
installer or RPM based on your requirement. The installer of BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle is downloaded to your local machine. 3. Copy the installer to the node or nodes of the SAP deployment.
Install the BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle
Cohesity BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle is an SAP-certified service that enables you to establish communication between the Cohesity cluster and the SAP on Oracle nodes. The BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle can be installed using a root user account or using a user account with sudo user privileges. Cohesity supports IPv6 for SAP Oracle in x86_64 architectures with gRPC data transfer. If you are installing the BACKINT Secure Connector Service using a sudo user account, for example, oracle. Ensure that you add the following entries in the sudoers file of the oracle user account:
Defaults:oracle !requiretty oracle ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL
Prerequisites
l Before installing the BACKINT Secure Connector service for Oracle you must set the ORACLE_HOME and SAPDATA_HOME exports on the SAP Oracle host. Syntax:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

SAP on Oracle

l export ORACLE_HOME=<oracle database>
Example:
export ORACLE_HOME=/oracle/SAL/121
l export SAPDATA_HOME=<oracle database>
Example:
export SAPDATA_HOME=/oracle/SAL
l Run the following command on the SAP Oracle node to synchronize time between the SAP Oracle server and the Cohesity NTP server:
timedatectl set-ntp true
Install the BACKINT Secure Connector Service using the Script Installer
On the SAP node, perform the following to install the BACKINT Secure Connector Service using the script installer, cohesity_secure_connector_service_sap_oracle_installer_ sap_oracle_java_installer. To install the BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle:
1. Log on to the SAP node's bash CLI. 2. Navigate to the directory where you have downloaded the script installer. 3. Make the Secure Connector Service installer (cohesity_secure_connector_
service_sap_oracle_installer_sap_oracle_java_installer) executable using the following command:
[oracle@sapnet ~]$ chmod +x cohesity_secure_connector_service_sap_ oracle_installer_sap_oracle_java_installer
4. Install the Secure Connector Service for Oracle using the following command:
cohesity_secure_connector_service_sap_oracle_installer_sap_oracle_java_ installer -- --install -s <SID> -a <comma_separated_cohesity server_ip_ addresses> -v <view_name> -S ora<SID>
Where: l -s <SID> - SAP System Identification (SID) is a unique three-character code that is available for every R/3 installation (SAP system) that consists of a database server and several application servers. l -a <comma_separated_cohesity server_ip_addresses> - The commaseparated list of virtual IP addresses of the servers in the Cohesity Cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

SAP on Oracle

Note: You can also specify the hostname instead of the IP addresses to perform the mount. For successful mount operation, you must specify the proper mapping between the IP addresses and the hostname in the /etc/hosts file.

Update the Cohesity Parameter File
As part of the BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle installation, Cohesity provides a parameter file (initSID.utl) that enables the SAP on Oracle node to use the BACKINT Secure Connector Service for a backup job. The parameter file is available at: <SAPDATA_ HOME>/sapprof/initSID.utl. The following is a sample initSID.utl file:
##----------------------------------------------------------------------------## List of IPs' of Cohesity cluster. Only VIPs can be used and not physical IPs. ##----------------------------------------------------------------------------cluster_ips : "${IP_ADDRESS}"
##----------------------------------------------------------------------------## If service_type is 'REMOTESNAPFS' then port number on Cohesity cluster nodes ## to which BACKINT executable connects. ## Port 11117 for secure connection (certificate config path should be a valid ## path) otherwise port 11111 for insecure connection (certificate config path ## should be an empty string). ## If service_type is 'NFS' then this field is not applicable. ##----------------------------------------------------------------------------cluster_port : 11113
##----------------------------------------------------------------------------## Name of the view on which backup data resides (Note: View Name should not ## contain the View Path or Cluster Name/IP). ##----------------------------------------------------------------------------view_name : "${VIEW_NAME}"
##----------------------------------------------------------------------------## Mount path for nfs approach. ##--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Backup Using BACKINT Secure Connector Service
SAP provides BR*TOOLS to back up Oracle databases. The Cohesity BACKINT Secure Connector Service leverages BR*TOOLs for protecting Oracle databases. When the BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle is installed and configured on the SAP system, it manages the communication between the SAP system and the Cohesity cluster. The SAP BR*TOOLS includes a BRBACKUP tool that enables you to back up data files, control files, and online redo log files of the database. When you back up the files on the SAP system using the BRBACKUP tool, it calls the Cohesity BACKINT Secure Connector Service to transfer the backup files to the Cohesity cluster. For more information on SAP BR*TOOLS, refer to SAP on Oracle Documentation.
Considerations
Review and understand the following considerations before you protect your SAP on Oracle databases using Cohesity BACKINT Secure Connector Service:
l Incremental backups of the Oracle databases are not supported. For incremental backups, use the custom Oracle SBT along with the BACKINT Secure Connector Service. For more information, see Backup Using Oracle SBT and BACKINT Secure Connector Service.
l Source-side deduplication is not supported if you use only BACKINT Secure Connector to backup SAP on Oracle databases.
Backup Using a Remote Adaptor Protection Group
As part of the BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle installation, Cohesity provides a backup script for the backup of SAP on the Oracle database. The backup script leverages the SAP BR*TOOLS capabilities provided by SAP. You can create a Remote Adaptor Protection Group and define the script parameters that enable you to back up the SAP on the Oracle database.
Backup Script Parameters
In the Remote Adaptor Protection Group, you can define the following script argument for your SAP on Oracle backup configuration:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

SAP on Oracle

Backup Script Parameters -m, --mode
-t, --type

Descriptions
The mode of backup. You can specify the following: l full for full backup. l incr for incremental backup l arch to archive offline redo log files
The type of backup. You can specify offline or online backups based on your requirements.
Note: In case of offline backup, the database is shut down before performing the backup.

-D, --device

The device type for performing the backup. The following are the device types, you can specify: l util_file: To backup all the files using the BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle. l rman_util: To backup the data files using the custom SBT extension and other files using the BACKINT Secure Connector Service for Oracle.

-l, --log-file [file]

The filename of the log file where you want to log the backup script logs. By default the logs are stored as follows:
/tmp/cohesity_backup_script_logs/cohesity_oracle_backup_script_<time_ in_seconds>_<pid>.log

-c, --channels

Specify the number of channels configured for backups using RMAN.
By default, the number of channels configured in the rman_channels parameter in the init<SID>.sap file is used.

-r, -retention-days

The retention period in days. The backups older than the specified retention period are deleted from both the catalog and the Cohesity View.

-d, --debug

Allows you to enable shell script debugging with set -x. By default, shell script debugging is disabled.

Create a Remote Adapter Protection Group for SAP on Oracle
To create a Remote Adapter Protection Group:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

SAP on Oracle

1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection and do one of the following:
a. To create a Protection Group--Click the plus icon on the top-right of the page and then select the type of Protection Group.
b. To edit a Protection Group--Click the action icon next to the Protection Group and select Edit.
2. Here the Job Type is Remote Adapter. Name: Enter a name for the Protection Group. The name can contain alphanumeric characters, underscores, dashes and periods. This field is required.
3. Linux Hostname or IP: Specify the Hostname or the IP Address of the Linux system where the scripts are located and will be run.
4. Username: Specify the username on the Linux system that will be running the scripts.
5. Cluster SSH Public Key: Set up permissions on the Linux system to allow the Cohesity cluster to run the scripts remotely on the system.
a. Click Copy Key to Clipboard to copy the SSH public key into the clipboard.
b. Log in to the Linux system with the username specified earlier.
c. In the home directory of the user, determine if there is a .ssh directory that contains a file called authorized_keys:
ls -lr ~/.ssh
d. Add the SSH key to the authorized_keys file located in the ~/.ssh directory of the specified User:
1. If the directory and file do not exist, create the .ssh directory in the home directory, change directories into the .ssh directory, create the authorized_keys file and paste the SSH key into a new line of the file.
2. If the .ssh directory exists but the file does not, change directories into the .ssh directory, create the authorized_keys file and paste the SSH key into a new line of the file.
3. If the authorized_keys file exists in the .ssh directory, edit the authorized_keys file and paste the SSH key into a new line of the file.
e. Set the .ssh directory and authorized_keys file permissions:
chmod 700 .ssh chmod 640 .ssh/authorized_keys
6. Policy: Select an existing protection policy or create a new one by selecting New Policy.
7. Script (with Full Path): Enter the full path to the script, for example:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

SAP on Oracle

rhel-sap-oracle-003:devadm> /usr/sap/SAL/cohesity/scripts/backup_ job.sh
8. Parameters: Enter the parameters for the backup script based on your requirements. For more information, see Backup Script Parameters. For example:

Use Cases

Sample Script Arguments

Create a full online backup using the BACKINT Secure Connector Service.

-m full -t online -D util_file

Create a full online backup using the BACKINT Secure Connector Service with 30 days retention period.

-m full -t online -D util_file -r 30

Archive offline redo log files using BACKINT Secure Connector Service.

-m arch -D util_file -r 30

Backup Using Oracle SBT and BACKINT Secure Connector Service Oracle database provides a custom third-party backup extension called SBT (Secure Backup to Tapes) for Oracle database backups. Cohesity provides a custom SBT extension that provides full backup and restore capabilities for Oracle databases. SAP BR*TOOL supports extensions to back up the Oracle databases using the custom SBT extension libraries. You can use the custom SBT extension along with the BACKINT Secure Connector Service to perform:
1. Incremental Oracle database backups. 2. Multistream the multi-node backups using Oracle RMAN channels, thus enabling you
to split the data between multiple nodes for optimal performance. 3. Source side deduplication.
Note: Backing up SAP on Oracle databases using custom Oracle SBT and BACKINT Secure Connector Service is supported only on SAP on Oracle databases running on Linux (x86-64) system.
Backup Process
The Oracle database is backed up using the custom SBT extension in the following phases: 1. The BRBACKUP or BRARCHIVE commands call RMAN and start the Oracle server process. The Oracle server process reads the Oracle database files to be backed up

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

SAP on Oracle

from the Oracle database and transfers it to the external backup library. The external backup library acts as a backup client, and it passes the data to the backup server. The server backs up the data to the Cohesity cluster. 2. The BRBACKUP uses the BACKINT Secure Connector Service to transfer the control file, the initialization profile, and the log files to the backup client. The backup client then transfers the data to the backup server, and the backup server backs up the data to the Cohesity cluster.
Note: The control file contains the information related to the files' backup from the first phase.
For more information, see the values rman_disk or rman_stage for the backup_dev_type parameter.

4. Username: Specify the username on the Linux system that will be running the scripts.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 20: About the Remote Adapter

SAP on Oracle

5. Cluster SSH Public Key: Set up permissions on the Linux system to allow the Cohesity cluster to run the scripts remotely on the system. a. Click Copy Key to Clipboard to copy the SSH public key into the clipboard. b. Log in to the Linux system with the username specified earlier. c. In the home directory of the user, determine if there is a .ssh directory that contains a file called authorized_keys:
ls -lr ~/.ssh
d. Add the SSH key to the authorized_keys file located in the ~/.ssh directory of the specified User: 1. If the directory and file do not exist, create the .ssh directory in the home directory, change directories into the .ssh directory, create the authorized_keys file and paste the SSH key into a new line of the file. 2. If the .ssh directory exists but the file does not, change directories into the .ssh directory, create the authorized_keys file and paste the SSH key into a new line of the file. 3. If the authorized_keys file exists in the .ssh directory, edit the authorized_keys file and paste the SSH key into a new line of the file.
e. Set the .ssh directory and authorized_keys file permissions:
chmod 700 .ssh chmod 640 .ssh/authorized_keys
6. Policy: Select an existing protection policy or create a new one by selecting New Policy.
7. Script (with Full Path): Enter the full path to the script, for example:
rhel-sap-oracle-003:devadm> /usr/sap/SAL/cohesity/scripts/backup_ job.sh
8. Parameters: Enter the parameters for the backup script based on your requirements. For more information, see Backup Script Parameters. For example:

Archive Offline Redo Log Files
The SAP BR*TOOLS includes a BRARCHIVE tool that enables you to archive offline redo log files. When you archive the offline redo log files on the SAP system using the BRARCHIVE tool, it calls the Cohesity BACKINT Secure Connector Service to transfer the archived files to the Cohesity cluster. For more information on SAP BR*TOOL, refer to SAP on Oracle Documentation.

Restore SAP on Oracle Databases
The SAP BR*TOOLS includes a BRRESTORE tool that enables you to restore an entire database backup or parts of it when the backup was performed using the BRBACKUP tool. For more information on SAP BR*TOOL, refer to SAP on Oracle Documentation.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes
Kubernetes is an open-source software platform that automates the deployment, management, and scaling of containerized applications. Using Cohesity Data Cloud, you can backup (file-based) and recover the Kubernetes cluster resources, PersistentVolumesClaims (PVCs), and metadata of the Kubernetes namespaces. Cohesity uses the Cohesity's Data Mover pod that will be deployed in the Kubernetes cluster for backing up the PVCs of the Kubernetes namespaces. Cohesity uses the third-party software, Velero, to back up the cluster and namespace scoped Kubernetes resources.
Plan and Prepare for Protecting Kubernetes Clusters
Before you register your Kubernetes cluster with the Cohesity cluster and protect the namespaces of the Kubernetes container, ensure that:
l Cohesity cluster supports the Kubernetes cluster version you plan to protect. For more information, see Supported Versions.
l The firewall ports required for the communication between the Cohesity cluster and Kubernetes cluster are open. For more information, see Network Firewall Considerations.
l You have the minimum permission required to register and manage your Kubernetes cluster. For more information, see Minimum Permission.
l You meet the prerequisites to register and manage your Kubernetes cluster. For more information, see Prerequisites.
l You have read the considerations for the backup and recovery of the Kubernetes cluster. For more information, see Considerations.
Supported Versions
Cohesity cluster supports data protection and recovery of the Kubernetes clusters. For supported versions of the Kubernetes clusters, see Supported Versions.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Minimum Permission
To register the Kubernetes cluster with the Cohesity cluster, you must provide the Bearer token ID of the Kubernetes service account. Ensure that the service account has the clusteradmin role on the Kubernetes cluster.
Note: This Bearer token ID will be used for all communications with the Kubernetes API server.

Prerequisites
Ensure that you meet the following prerequisites to register and manage your Kubernetes cluster:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Plan and Prepare for Protecting Kubernetes Clusters

l Valid Certificate with Subject Alternative Name (SAN) field --On the Cohesity cluster, install a valid certificate with the SAN field. The SAN field is used to specify additional host names (such as sites, IP addresses, and common names) to be protected by a single SSL certificate, such as a Multi-Domain or Extend Validation Multi-Domain Certificate. For more information, see Update SSL Certificates Using Cohesity CA or Customer CA certificate for Agent to Cluster Communication.
l Create a Cohesity service account on Kubernetes to register Kubernetes on Cohesity cluster--For registering a Kubernetes cluster with the Cohesity cluster, you can either use a default service account with the cluster-admin role or a dedicated service account with the cluster-admin role account. Cohesity recommends you to create a dedicated account in the default namespace. For example, to create a 'cohesity' service account on Kubernetes, use the following command:
kubectl create serviceaccount cohesity -n default
Assign the cluster-admin role to the 'cohesity' service account using the following command:
kubectl create clusterrolebinding cohesity-admin --clusterrole=clusteradmin --serviceaccount=default:cohesity
The above example can be run from any client or workstation from which kubectl is typically run for a given Kubernetes cluster that is registered and protected by the Cohesity cluster.
Note: Custom roles can be used as an Early Access feature after contacting Cohesity support.
l If you use a Kubernetes cluster 1.24 or later, run the following command to generate the Bearer Token ID or secret token for your service account.
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata:
name: cohesity-token annotations:
kubernetes.io/service-account.name: cohesity type: kubernetes.io/service-account-token EOF
Sample Ouput
secret/cohesity-token created

Considerations
l Cohesity uses the third-party software Velero to facilitate the backup and restore of namespace data.
If your Kubernetes clusters are of versions earlier than 1.16, use Velero 1.4. If your Kubernetes clusters are of versions 1.16 or later, use Velero 1.16.2. For more information, see Upgrade Velero and Datamover.
l If Kubernetes is not accessed through the internet, you must provide the path to the registry from which Velero should be pulled.
l Cohesity cluster only supports the backup of the user-created application namespaces of the Kubernetes cluster and does not support the backup of default or infrastructure namespaces such as kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, and so on.
l Cohesity supports restoring namespaces backed up from one Kubernetes cluster to a different Kubernetes cluster if the storage class of the Kubernetes clusters is the same.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Register and Manage Kubernetes Cluster

l Cohesity does not support Tanzu Kubernetes Grid Integrated Edition (TKGI). l Cohesity does not support data protection of Kubernetes clusters in private networks
behind NAT gateways (Dynamic/Static NAT, Port Address Translation PAT). l For new protection jobs, S3 embedded credentials are used by default. l For existing protection jobs, incremental backups continue using the Cohesity S3
account ID. S3 embedded credentials are used only after a full backup is performed. l For recovery, the credential type depends on the snapshot selected:
l If the snapshot was created using the Cohesity S3 account, recovery uses the same.
l If the snapshot was created using S3 embedded credentials, recovery uses embedded credentials.
l For replication, the target cluster must support S3 embedded credentials (version 7.3 or later). Otherwise, the replication job will fail.
Note: Do not delete the Cohesity user if any protection job is still using the old approach (Cohesity S3 account ID). Deleting the user will cause incremental backups to fail, and existing snapshots will become unrecoverable.
l When restoring to an alternate cluster, Cohesity (through Velero) does not automatically restore Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs). This is an intentional design choice meant to avoid potential conflicts or compatibility issues that could occur if the target cluster already has CRDs with different versions or schemas.
l In Kubernetes and OpenShift environments, restore operations might fail partially with the PartiallyFailed status due to resource restore order dependencies. This might happen in namespaces with complex inter-resource dependencies. The following error appears: "[KubernetesError]: Restore job failed with reason PartiallyFailed." Workaround: If the restore operation fails partially due to resource restore order dependencies, retry the restore operation. The initial restore attempt might have already recovered prerequisite resources, and therefore the dependency that caused the failure might be satisfied during the subsequent restore attempt.

8. (Optional) Service Type: Enable this field to route external traffic to your Kubernetes cluster node via dedicated VLANs.
From the drop-down, select one of the following service types:

l NodePort service type allows you to route external traffic through a fixed port (which you can set within the range of 30000-32767) on every Kubernetes node. In a NodePort setup, external traffic has direct access to the Kubernetes node.
l Load Balancer service type allows you to route external traffic via an external Load Balancer functionality. Load Balancers monitor the availability of your Kubernetes pods and route incoming service requests to the relevant pods. In a Load Balancer setup, external traffic has access to the Kubernetes node through the Load Balancer only. Configure User-defined PriorityClass, Labels, and Annotations for Cohesity Deployed Resources
You can provide the priority class names for pods deployed by it. You also have the option to select labels and annotations that will be applied to the pods and services deployed by Cohesity.
The Kubernetes source must include a PriorityClass resource with the specified name. The PriorityClass is assigned to each pod in its configuration. Labels track pods, while annotations on pods and services manage external network access rules.
You can specify the priority class for pods and also apply user-defined labels and annotations to the pods and services deployed by Cohesity at the Kubernetes source for data protection.
To provide Priority Class, Labels, and Annotations:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources.
2. Click Register and then select Kubernetes Cluster.
The Register Kubernetes Source page appears.
3. Click the actions menu ( ) next to the Kubernetes cluster source and select Edit.
4. Select the Optional field.
5. (Optional) Priority Class Name: In the Priority Class Name field, enter the name of the PriorityClass object available at the source. Pods deployed by Cohesity will specify this priority class name in their specifications. If a priority class for the pods is

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Register and Manage Kubernetes Cluster

specified during the registration or modification of the source, the priority class will first be validated to ensure it exists at the source. If it does not exist, the registration or editing process will fail.
During registration, the Velero and Datamover pods use the priority class to ensure they receive the appropriate priority assignment.
The Velero and Datamover pods will be updated with the new value during modification. Consequently, the pods will restart automatically.
If a priority class was specified during registration and you later deleted it from the Kubernetes source, the existing pods will remain unchanged. Upon the next refresh, it will be detected that the priority class no longer exists in the source, and an error message will be displayed on the sources page.

Note: Before adding the priority class name, make sure that the priority class is already existing in the Kubernetes source.
6. (Optional) Resource Labels Key and Resource Labels Value: Enter the Resource Labels key-value pairs. (Optional): Resource Annotations Key and Resource Annotations Value: Enter the Resource Annotations key-value pairs.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Register and Manage Kubernetes Cluster

If labels or annotation maps are provided during source registration, Velero and Datamover pods and services will be labeled and annotated accordingly.
When source modifications occur, such as changes to labels or annotation maps, both the Velero and Datamover pods are updated with the new labels and annotations. This update triggers a restart of the pods, which can disrupt ongoing backup and recovery processes. Any subsequent attempts within the same run will be successful. While the Datamover services will be updated with new labels and annotations, they will not be restarted.
If a label or annotation with a specific key is deleted, the associated pods and services will be updated to reflect an empty string as the value for those keys. Additionally, if the Velero deployment or the data mover DaemonSet and services are deleted, and a manual refresh of the source is initiated, any labels and annotations with empty string values will be removed.
When you perform a search, you can filter the labels or annotations you provide and list the resources accordingly.
This is supported for both Load Balancer and NodePort service types.

Upgrade When the Cohesity Namespace is Present

Example - kubectl delete ns cohesity-21234567891234
3. Run the following command on any node of that Kubernetes cluster (or from a node in another Kubernetes cluster that has access to the Kubernetes command-line tool) to delete the Velero CRD: - kubectl delete crds -l component=velero

Backup Kubernetes Cluster Resources, PVCs, and Namespaces
Cohesity supports the backup of PVCs, Kubernetes cluster resources and metadata of the Kubernetes namespaces. Cohesity uses the Data Mover pod that will be deployed in the Kubernetes cluster for backing up the PVCs of the Kubernetes namespaces. Cohesity supports the backup of PVCs with the volumeMode set to Filesystem. The supported file systems include ext3, ext4, xfs, vxfs, ReiserFS, autofs, cvfs, zfs, fuse.mfs, nfs, nfs3, cifs, gpfs, and mmfs. Cohesity also supports the backup of PVCs with CSI drivers using CSI volume snapshotting capability.
Note: The backup of PVCs with CSI drivers using CSI volume is an Early Access feature. Contact Cohesity Support support for enabling this feature.
After registering the Kubernetes cluster as a source on the Cohesity cluster, you can start configuring your backups. Cohesity recommends the first full and an incremental forever approach for the backup. However, you can do periodic full backups, based on your requirements. The temporary pods created during backups by Cohesity will have their priority class set to the specified value for the source. Additionally, the labels and annotations will be applied to the temporary pods.
Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.

Protect Kubernetes Namespaces
In the Cohesity cluster, Kubernetes namespaces are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, archived, or replicated.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Backup Kubernetes Cluster Resources, PVCs, and Namespaces

A Protection Policy is a reusable set of settings that define how and when objects are protected and replicated. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group.
To protect the namespaces of the Kubernetes containers:
1. In the Cohesity cluster UI, perform one of the following:
l Select Data Protection > Protection. Click Protect displayed on the topright of the page and then select Kubernetes Cluster.
l Select Data Protection > Sources. Click the Actions menu ( ) next to the Kubernetes source and then select Protect.
2. From the Registered Source drop-down list, select the registered Kubernetes source or click Register Source to register an Kubernetes source. For more information, see Register Kubernetes Cluster as a Source.
3. From the Objects list, select the namespaces that you plan to backup and click Save Selection.

Note: You can use the advanced filters that are available to search and find the namespaces you plan to protect. Also, you can click the shield icon to enable Auto Protect at the Kubernetes cluster level or based on the namespace label(s). For more information, see Enable or Disable Auto Protect.

Create or Use an Existing Protection Policy
A Protection Policy is a reusable set of settings. It enables you to define how and when Kubernetes namespaces are protected, replicated, and archived. A standard policy provides various settings that you can configure for a Protection Group. Create a Protection Policy with the settings listed in the Policy Settings for Kubernetes. For detailed instructions on how to create a Protection Policy, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.
Policy Settings for Kubernetes
The following table lists the applicable policy settings for Kubernetes:

Field

Description

DataLock

If applicable, add a DataLock for compliance and regulatory requirements, to ensure that your protected data, including local backups, archives, and replication, cannot be modified until the DataLock expiration.
Once applied, a DataLocked Snapshot will be deleted only after its retention period expires. A DataLock prevents all users, including those who have the Data Security role in Cohesity Data Cloud, from modifying or deleting any Snapshots that were generated by the Protection Groups that use this Policy. Only users with the Data Security role can add, modify, or remove a DataLock from a Policy.

Backup

Defines when backups are captured, how long they are retained and the type of backup to capture.

Periodic Full Backup

Use this option to choose when to run a periodic full backup.

Extended Retention

Add this to retain a subset of snapshots (backups) for longer than defined by the protection schedule.

Quiet Times

Quiet times define time periods when new protection runs are not started. For example, you might want to configure hourly backups that run during weekdays but not on Saturdays or Sundays. Quiet times only prevent new protection runs from starting during the specified time period. The protection runs that started before the quiet times are not affected and will continue to run.
For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet times.

Retry Options

Use this option to customize the retry settings for capturing Snapshots. By default, the Cohesity cluster attempts to capture Snapshots three times before the Protection Group fails. The default time between retries is five minutes. You can customize the number of retries and how long to wait between each attempt.

Quiesce Kubernetes Workloads during Backups
Quiescing involves pausing an application to achieve a consistent state in preparation for a backup.
Cohesity supports quiescing stateful Kubernetes workloads before capturing Persistent Volume Claims (PVCs) volume snapshots during backup in a namespace. After the snapshots are taken, the Kubernetes workloads are automatically unquiesced. This ensures consistent and reliable snapshots for stateful applications running in Kubernetes.
When running a protection job for a namespace, there are pre-snapshot and post-snapshot hooks. Before taking a snapshot of any PVC attached to a Kubernetes pod within an application, the application should be in a consistent state. After taking the snapshot, a post-snapshot hook is executed called "unquiescing," which allows applications to resume their operations.
You can define actions to be executed before and after taking a snapshot. Hooks allow specific scripts to run within a group of pods identified by key-value pairs known as label selectors (each pod will have its labels). You can select pods constituting an application (which needs to be quiesced) by specifying labels. Velero will execute the designated script within the pod's container and provide the exit status of the script.
Each script has a timeout feature, with a default of 60 seconds. You can extend this duration if necessary. The scripts are executed at the container level, running on each container within a pod. You can specify a container name to execute a script on specific containers within the same pod.
To quiesce Kubernetes workloads during backups:
1. Register Kubernetes source.
2. Edit the Protection Group that contains Kubernetes source.
3. In the Add Objects section, click the Edit icon.
4. In the list of protected objects, click the Edit icon next to the Kubernetes namespace for which you want to create or modify quiescing rules.
5. Switch to the Scripts tab and select Quiesce Rules to view the different quiesce modes.
6. Choose a Quiesce Mode to add different rules.. The following quiesce modes are available:
l Apply following rules together
l Apply following rules independently
l Apply following rules sequentially

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Backup Kubernetes Cluster Resources, PVCs, and Namespaces

Application quiescing involves defining one or more rules (for example, Rule 1, Rule 2, and Rule 3) to pause or quiesce an application , allowing snapshots to be taken. Once the snapshots have been captured, the application resumes and the backup process continues. The execution of these rules is managed by the quiescing mode, which offers two options: parallel mode, in which rules are executed simultaneously, and sequential mode, where rules are executed one after another.
l Together mode: This mode operates using a single volume group, allowing all processes to run independently and in parallel. Quiescing occurs simultaneously, with all rules executed before a snapshot is taken. After applying the rules, snapshots are created, followed by unquiescing, and then the backup is performed. This approach results in faster backup speeds compared to sequential mode.
l Independent mode: This mode operates with multiple volume groups, allowing for parallel and independent processes. Quiescing happens simultaneously; for example, while volume group 1 is quiescing for Rules 1 and 2, volume group 2 may have already completed the quiescing and begun the snapshot process. As a result, this mode provides the fastest backup speed.
l Sequential mode: This mode operates with a single volume group, where all processes are interdependent and executed in a specific sequence. Quiescing occurs in stages, following defined rules. For example, Rule 1 is executed first,

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Backup Kubernetes Cluster Resources, PVCs, and Namespaces

then Rule 2, followed by Rule 3, and so on. After applying these rules, snapshots are created, the system is unquiesced, and the backup process is performed. This sequential approach applies to both the quiescing and unquiescing processes. Consequently, the backup speed in this mode is the slowest compared to the other two options.
In sequential mode, rules are executed one after another. If Rule 2 encounters an issue, you can either continue or stop all backups at the namespace level. This means that any error will cause the backup to fail for all rules. This mechanism manages backup processes in case of failures related to quiescing rules.
7. Click Add Rule to add a rule. You can add multiple rules by clicking Add Rule.
8. Add the Key value under the Pod Selector Labels for the rules to run on.

9. Select the Pre Snapshot Scripts.
10. Enter the container name, the command that needs to be run, and the timeout value in seconds. You can add multiple scripts by clicking Add Scripts for a particular rule selected under Pre Snapshots Scripts. Enter the command sh -c pre_script.sh in the command prompt.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Backup Kubernetes Cluster Resources, PVCs, and Namespaces

11. Select the Post Snapshot Scripts.
12. Enter the container name, the command that needs to be run, and the timeout value in seconds. You can add multiple scripts by clicking Add Scripts for a particular rule selected under Post Snapshots Scripts.
Enter the command sh -c post_script.sh in the command prompt.

13. You can choose between "True" or "False" to indicate whether the backup should continue or fail when the script fails by selecting Continue Backup when Script fails. If the script fails, the protection job will still back up the PVC. However, if the script fails, the protection job will also fail.

The pre-snapshot hook is triggered prior to taking snapshots of the PVCs. After the backup of the PVCs is completed, the post-snapshot hook is triggered to finalize the process. The Backup Task Activity for quiescing-ins, as shown in the pulse logs, will provide details about the execution of both the pre and post-snapshot hooks.

Recovering Namespaces to the Same Location
When you are recovering the namespaces to the same or original location, then only the resources, PVCs, or the metadata of the Kubernetes namespaces that are missing or deleted from the original location are restored from the namespace snapshot you selected for recovery. Cohesity does not overwrite or restore the resources, PVCs, or the metadata of the Kubernetes namespace that already exists in the original location. For example, a Kubernetes namespace you want to restore to the same location contains a deployment resource and a service account. When Cohesity initiates the restore to the original location and if the service account is missing from the original location, then Cohesity will restore only the service account. The restore of the deployment resource is skipped. To restore the namespaces of a Kubernetes cluster to the same location:

Granular Recovery of Files and Folders
Cohesity supports Kubernetes clusters for granular recovery of files and folders within Persistent Volume Claims (PVCs). It allows for the selective recovery of files and folders from backed-up data volumes instead of restoring the entire volume in case of data corruption. This capability enables users to recover specific files or related files and folders efficiently.
While you register a Kubernetes source on the Cohesity cluster and create a Protection Group, you can perform the backup of namespaces. This allows you to search and browse the backed-up PVC folders and files you want to recover by providing their names. Each file and folder is indexed within volumes of type PersistentVolumeClaims in Kubernetes namespaces from snapshots taken during Kubernetes backups. Once indexed, the files and folders are available for searching and browsing.
You have the option to either download the files or initiate the recovery of files and folders. You can specify the download path if you choose to download the files. If you choose the restore option, you can select one or more files and folders from a single object. The recovered files and folders can be restored to their original location (such as the source, namespace, PVC, and file path) or an alternate location wherein the target source must be registered.
You can specify the recovery path and choose to preserve the original permissions and attributes of the recovered files and folders at the time of the backup. Additionally, you can overwrite files and folders or download them from selected snapshots created by a Cohesity Protection Group.
Note: l For archived items, only downloading is supported.
l If restoring to a different location, you must turn on the PVC inclusion/exclusion feature and enable the corresponding magneto flag. This is necessary to list the PVCs available for selection during recovery.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Recover Kubernetes

Considerations
l Granular recovery from archival is not supported. Only download is supported.
l If recovering to an alternate location, ensure that the file system of the target supports the recovery of files.
l Granular recovery is only supported for volumes of type PersistentVolumeClaims. l Recovery of files and folders to an alternate location is restricted to already registered
Kubernetes sources. l Granular recovery does not support file and folder recovery involving multiple
namespaces. l Granular file recovery from the archive to the original sources is not supported. Only
file downloads are allowed. l Attempt to resubmit a failed Kubernetes restore job may fail with the following error
message: "Error while calling FileStat for /cohesity-data/cohesity-data/pv-5tb: [kNotFound]: Bridge error: Directory not present." The issue occurs due to a known UI bug, which adds an extra "cohesity-data" to the file path with each resubmission. A fix for this issue is expected in a future release.
For more information about the recovery options:
l Recover Files or Folders to the Original Location l Recover Files or Folders to a New Location within the original source

Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization
Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization is a feature of Red Hat OpenShift that allows you to manage and run VMs and container workloads together. It is based on the open-source project KubeVirt and uses a Kernel-based VM (KVM) within Kubernetes.
OpenShift API for Data Protection (OADP)
Cohesity now supports the OpenShift API for Data Protection (OADP) operator, a Red Hat solution that simplifies the registration and maintenance of Velero and Plugin versions. OADP is based on the open-source tool Velero, which allows for effective metadata backup.

Minimum Permissions
To register the Red Hat OpenShift cluster with the Cohesity cluster, you must provide the Bearer token ID of the service account. Ensure that the service account has the clusteradmin role on the Red Hat OpenShift cluster.
Prerequisites
Ensure that you meet the following prerequisites to register and manage your Red Hat OpenShift cluster:
l Valid Certificate with Subject Alternative Name (SAN) field --On the Cohesity cluster, install a valid certificate with the SAN field. The SAN field is used to specify additional host names (such as sites, IP addresses, and common names) to be protected by a single SSL certificate, such as a Multi-Domain or Extend Validation Multi-Domain Certificate. For more information, see Update SSL Certificates Using Cohesity CA or Customer CA certificate for Agent to Cluster Communication.
l Create a Cohesity service account--For registering a Red Hat OpenShift cluster with the Cohesity cluster, you can either use a default service account with the cluster-admin role or a dedicated service account with the cluster-admin role account. Cohesity recommends you to create a dedicated account in the default namespace.
For example, to create a 'cohesity' service account, use the following command:
kubectl create serviceaccount cohesity -n default
Assign the cluster-admin role to the 'cohesity' service account using the following command:
kubectl create clusterrolebinding cohesity-admin --clusterrole=clusteradmin --serviceaccount=default:cohesity
The above example can be run from any client or workstation from which kubectl is typically run for a given Red Hat OpenShift cluster that is registered and protected by the Cohesity cluster.
l For current version of Red Hat OpenShift, run the following command to generate the Bearer Token ID or secret token for your service account.
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF apiVersion: v1 kind: Secret metadata:
name: cohesity-token annotations:
kubernetes.io/service-account.name: cohesity

To upload the Cohesity DataProtect Plugin image: 1. Download the DataProtect Plugin image - Obtain the DataProtect Plugin tarball that closely matches your Cohesity cluster version from the Cohesity Download page. 2. 3. Verify the loaded image - Run the following command to check the loaded image and note the Image ID:
docker images
4. Tag and push the image to your registry - Tag the image using your private image registry location using the following commands:
docker tag <image-id> <image-registry>/cohesity-dataprotectplugin:<tag>
docker push <image-registry>/cohesity-dataprotect-plugin:<tag>
To prepare the source Cohesity cluster: Before upgrading the DataProtect Plugin, ensure that the Red Hat OpenShift source is in a clean state.
1. Stop all running Red Hat OpenShift protection jobs and verify that no protection runs are currently active.
2. Delete the Cohesity namespace from the Red Hat OpenShift cluster using the following command:
oc delete ns <cohesity-namespace>

l Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization is supported only in on-premise environments.
l While protecting VMs with Block mode, ensure that you are using the latest version of Datamover.
l Cohesity does not support the restoration of VMs with partially selected PVCs. As a result, the VMs will not get provisioned. Also, configuration change is required to remove the excluded disk configurations.
l PVCs not attached to any pods are protected if a CSI snapshot is available for the Volume.
l You must toggle ON the CSI snapshot for crash-consistent backups. If a CSI snapshot is not enabled on the Protection Group or fails during its creation, the backup may still proceed for the VM. However, this backup may be inconsistent.
l Cohesity does not support granular recovery of files and folders within VMs.
l Cohesity does not support quiescing VMs during backups.
l If SELinux is enabled on the VM, correct permissions should be set on qemu-agent to allow it to run guest-fsfreeze commands.
l Cohesity does not support recovery from backups if the storage class is deleted after the backup is made from the source and that same storage class is not present on the alternate cluster.
l If the Machine type is not supported on the alternate cluster then recovery is successful but the VM quits unexpectedly. Ensure that the required Machine type is available on the alternate location cluster.
l In scenarios where the Red Hat OpenShift cluster lacks external IP support, a configuration change may be needed to support backups and recoveries. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
l During the backup process, metadata for all resources in the namespace is backed up, but only the volumes of the selected VMs are included in the backup.
l During the recovery process, if all VMs in a namespace are being recovered, the entire metadata for that namespace is also recovered along with the VMs and their

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization

associated volumes.
l If VMs are selectively recovered, only the metadata of the resources connected to those selected or backed up VMs, along with their volumes, will be restored.
l If the version of the Red Hat OpenShift cluster is lower than 4.17, the deployment of the OpenShift API for Data Protection (OADP) operator is not supported.
l During the deployment of the operator, the subscription channel is set to stable-1.4, which automatically manages any minor updates to the operator. If you have deployed another OADP operator with a different stable channel, then the Cohesity operator deployment is not supported.
l If the Velero CRDs are already present, you cannot deploy the OADP operator by default. You must delete the CRDs and click refresh on the OpenShift source in the Cohesity UI to deploy the operator.
l After restoring a VM with a hotplug disk, the disk appears in the VM configuration but is not visible within the VM. As a workaround, either restart the VM or remove the older hotplug pod that is currently running to detect the hotplug disk within the VM.
l Backups fail if the namespace contains a VM that is in a paused state. As a workaround, stop the paused VM and reinitiate the backup. As a workaround, for assured data consistency during backups, VMs should be powered down before initiating the backup.
l Backing up a VM that uses LVM or has a file system spanning multiple disks may result in data corruption. The issue occurs when the snapshots of the underlying volumes or PVCs are not captured at the same point in time, resulting in inconsistencies
l For IPv6 support, the Cohesity cluster must be configured with a preferred IPv6 address.
l Instant recovery feature is supported starting from OpenShift 4.18.
l VM recovery using the override option is not supported.
l When creating target data volumes for VM migration, the volume mode (Filesystem or Block) is not explicitly specified.
l A Velero backup may fail if the PVC associated with a VM is deleted before the backup is triggered. As a result, the Velero fails to backup deleted PVC and marks the metadata backup as failed:
"Backup job failed by Velero."
l After upgrading the Cohesity cluster from version 7.2.2_u2 to 7.3.1, if an incremental backup is run using an existing Protection Group to generate a new snapshot, instant recovery of a VM from that snapshot may fail with the following error:
"Failed to clone the namespace backup view."

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization

Instant Recovery is supported starting from version 7.3.1. For existing Protection Groups, a forced full backup is required. Run a full backup of the affected Protection Group to ensure that subsequent backups create separate views.
l If a VM's Network Attachment Definitions (NADs) are located in a different namespace than the VM being backed up, those NADs are not included in the backup for that VM.
l NFS-mounted file systems (and other file systems that do not support extended attributes) such as security.selinux are not supported as target locations for file-level recovery, and restores may fail.
l On OpenShift 4.19 for Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization, File-Level Recovery (FLR) may fail with "Hotplug volumes did not reach Ready state within 300 seconds" when a block-mode PVC is already hotplugged, causing subsequent hotplug operations to fail unless you manually delete the existing hotplug pod.
l For KubeVirt
Below are the considerations for KubeVirt. For more information, see limitations:
o Migration of hot-plug disks is not supported.
o Migration of shareable disks is not supported, as data consistency cannot be guaranteed with multiple writers.
o Live migration is not supported when using virtiofs because it does not currently provide live migration capabilities.
o Original disks may support the SCSI protocol, but the destination PVC storage class might not support it.
o KubeVirt currently supports live migration only between separate nodes.
Note: After upgrading to version 7.3.1, ensure you run a full backup of all VMs in the existing protection jobs.

Backup Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization
Cohesity supports the backup of PVCs, VMs, Red Hat OpenShift cluster resources and metadata of the Kubernetes namespaces. Cohesity uses the Data Mover pod that will be deployed in the Red Hat OpenShift cluster for backing up the PVCs of the Kubernetes namespaces. Cohesity supports the backup of PVCs with the volumeMode set to Filesystem or Block. Cohesity uses the VM Snapshot API that enables taking a single snapshot of all volumes associated with a VM in one backup operation. PVCs that are not associated with the VM but exist within the same namespace will continue to use individual volume snapshots for backup purposes. The supported file systems include ext3, ext4, xfs, vxfs, ReiserFS, autofs, cvfs, zfs, fuse, mfs, nfs, nfs3, cifs, gpfs, and mmfs. Cohesity also supports the backup of PVCs with CSI drivers using CSI volume snapshotting capability.
Note: Cohesity recommends that the entire namespace containing VMs should be protected, without any exclusions. Additionally, it is recommended to use CSI snapshots.
After registering the Red Hat OpenShift cluster as a source on the Cohesity cluster, you can start configuring your backups.
Protect Red Hat OpenShift Cluster
In the Cohesity cluster, Kubernetes namespaces are protected using a Protection Group and a Protection Policy. A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, archived, or replicated. A Protection Policy is a reusable set of settings that define how and when objects are protected and replicated. You can select which standard or custom policy to use when creating a Protection Group. To protect the namespaces of the Kubernetes containers:
1. In the Cohesity cluster UI, perform one of the following: l Select Data Protection > Protection. Click Protect displayed on the topright of the page and then select Kubernetes Cluster. l Select Data Protection > Sources. Click the Actions menu ( ) next to the Red Hat OpenShift source and then select Protect.
2. From the Registered Source drop-down list, select the registered Red Hat OpenShift source or click Register Source to register a Red Hat OpenShift source. For more information, see Register Red Hat OpenShift Cluster as a Source.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization

3. From the Objects list, select the namespaces that you plan to backup and click Save Selection.
Note: You can use the advanced filters that are available to search and find the namespaces you plan to protect. Also, you can click the shield icon to enable Auto Protect at the Red Hat OpenShift cluster level or based on the namespace label(s). For more information, see Enable or Disable Auto Protect.
4. In the Protection Group section, perform one of the following:
l Select New Group to create a new Protection Group. In the Name field, enter a name from the Protection Group and go to step 5.
l Select Existing Group to use the settings of an existing Protection Group. From the Group list, select an existing Protection Group and click Protect.
5. From the Policy drop-down list, select an existing Protection Policy or create a new Protection Policy. For more information, see Create or Use an Existing Protection Policy .
6. Select the appropriate Storage Domain. For more information, see Manage Storage Domains.
7. In the Start Time field, select the time and time zone to start the protection run. This option is available only if the selected policy is set to Backup Daily. The current time is displayed by default but you can change it. Enter the hour and minutes or use the up and down arrows on your keyboard. Verify the AM or PM setting. The default time zone is the browser's time zone. You can change the time zone of the protection run by selecting a different time zone.
8. Cohesity supports protecting PVCs with the snapshot and restore feature of Container Storage Interface (CSI) drivers on CSI volumes. This option is disabled by default in your Cohesity protection job. To enable this feature, turn ON the Leverage CSI snapshot toggle. Once enabled, Cohesity clusters will begin utilizing snapshots captured by CSI drivers to protect the PVCs. These snapshots are crash-consistent, meaning that the PVC is in the same state as it was during the crash. If you are protecting entire namespaces, this setting must be enabled manually. When protecting individual VMs, the setting is applied automatically.
9. If you need to change any of the advanced settings on the Protection Group page, click the down arrow icon next to Advance Settings and click Edit on the right. For more information, see Advanced Settings.
10. Click Protect.
Your new Protection Group is now active and running.

Create or Use an Existing Protection Policy
A Protection Policy is a reusable set of settings. It enables you to define how and when Kubernetes namespaces are protected, replicated, and archived. A standard policy provides various settings that you can configure for a Protection Group. Create a Protection Policy with the settings listed in the Policy Settings for Kubernetes. For detailed instructions on how to create a Protection Policy, see Create or Edit a Standard Policy.
Policy Settings for Red Hat OpenShift
The following table lists the applicable policy settings for Red Hat OpenShift:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization

Field

Description

DataLock

If applicable, add a DataLock for compliance and regulatory requirements, to ensure that your protected data, including local backups, archives, and replication, cannot be modified until the DataLock expiration.
Once applied, a DataLocked Snapshot will be deleted only after its retention period expires. A DataLock prevents all users, including those who have the Data Security role in Cohesity Data Cloud, from modifying or deleting any Snapshots that were generated by the Protection Groups that use this Policy. Only users with the Data Security role can add, modify, or remove a DataLock from a Policy.

Backup

Defines when backups are captured, how long they are retained and the type of backup to capture.

Periodic Full Backup

Use this option to choose when to run a periodic full backup.

Extended Retention

Add this to retain a subset of snapshots (backups) for longer than defined by the protection schedule.

Quiet Times

Quiet times define time periods when new protection runs are not started. For example, you might want to configure hourly backups that run during weekdays but not on Saturdays or Sundays. Quiet times only prevent new protection runs from starting during the specified time period. The protection runs that started before the quiet times are not affected and will continue to run.
For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet times.

Retry Options

Use this option to customize the retry settings for capturing Snapshots. By default, the Cohesity cluster attempts to capture Snapshots three times before the Protection Group fails. The default time between retries is five minutes. You can customize the number of retries and how long to wait between each attempt.

Replication

To replicate snapshots to another, click the Replication icon from the floating menu. The copied snapshots are stored in the storage domain of the remote cluster.

Archival

To add an archive schedule, click the Archival icon from the floating menu.

Enable or Disable Auto Protect
You can enable the Auto Protect option at the:
l Red Hat OpenShift cluster level: Automatically protect the new namespaces that are added to the Kubernetes container.
l Label level of the namespaces: Automatically protect the new namespaces that are tagged with the same label you selected while enabling the auto protect.
When the Auto Protect option is enabled:
l All the namespaces that are added to the Red Hat OpenShift cluster or tagged with the same label in the future are automatically added to the Protection Group and are protected from the next protection run.
l All the namespaces that are removed from the Red Hat OpenShift cluster or untagged from the specified label in the future are automatically removed from the Protection Group and are not protected from the next protection run. The existing backup for the namespace is preserved until the snapshot expires.
When the Auto Protect option is disabled, you need to manually:
l Add newly added namespaces to the Protection Group. l From the Protection Group, remove existing namespaces that are deleted on Red Hat
OpenShift. The existing backups of the namespaces are preserved until the snapshot expires.

Pause Future Protection Runs
You can pause future protection runs for the Protection Group. However, if the Protection Group is currently executing a protection run, the current run continues to execute and only future runs of the Protection Group are paused. To pause future protection run:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had created for Red Hat
OpenShift. 3. Click the Actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Pause Future
Runs.
Resume Paused Protection Runs
You can resume a paused protection run. When you resume a protection run, if the backup snapshots are expired then a full backup is triggered. To resume a paused protection run:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the Protection Group that you had paused. 3. Click the Actions menu ( ) next to the Protection Group and select Resume.

You can delete a Protection Group if you:

l Want to reclaim the storage space utilized by the Protection Group.

l Delete Protection Group Only: Allows you to delete the Protection Group. All the backups generated by the Protection Group are preserved till the snapshots expire.
