Source-Side Deduplication and Cache Optimization for VMs and PVCs
Note: This is a Controlled Availability feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization

Source-side deduplication is a Cohesity feature designed to optimize backup efficiency by eliminating redundant data at the source (VMs and PVCs) before transferring it to the Cohesity cluster. This process reduces network usage and speeds up backup operations, ensuring efficient data protection for your VMs and PVCs.
With source-side deduplication enabled for a VM or PVC during Protection Group creation, unique data blocks that have not been previously transferred are sent to the Cohesity cluster. This significantly minimizes network bandwidth utilization and reduces data transfer times.
Additionally, source-side deduplication integrates seamlessly with Cohesity's built-in deduplication, further optimizing storage by processing only new data blocks.
Advantages of Source-Side Deduplication
l Reduced Network Traffic: This feature minimizes the amount of data transferred between VMs or PVCs and the Cohesity cluster, conserving network bandwidth.
l Faster Backups: Speeds up backup processes, particularly over slower networks such as WANs, enabling quicker recovery point objectives (RPOs).
l Efficient Resource Utilization: Offloads deduplication processing from the Cohesity cluster, allowing the system to handle a higher volume of backup workload sessions.
l Lower Storage Costs: Reduces overall storage consumption by transmitting only new or changed data blocks.
Considerations
After enabling source-side deduplication, if you back up a VM that uses a sparse filesystemtype PVC, recovering the PVC converts it to a thick provisioned format. This results in increased storage consumption on the Red Hat OpenShift cluster. For large recovery operations, the increased space usage may lead to insufficient storage capacity on the Red Hat OpenShift side.

Recovering Namespaces to the Same Location
When you are recovering the namespaces to the same or original location, then only the VMs, resources, PVCs, or the metadata of the Kubernetes namespaces that are missing or deleted from the original location are restored from the namespace snapshot you selected for recovery. Cohesity does not overwrite or restore the VMs, resources, PVCs, or the metadata of the Kubernetes namespace that already exists in the original location.
For example, a Kubernetes namespace you want to restore to the same location contains a deployment resource and a service account. When Cohesity initiates the restore to the

original location and if the service account is missing from the original location, then Cohesity will restore only the service account. The restore of the deployment resource is skipped. Indexing and Recovery
Note the following about indexing and recovering files: The Cohesity cluster attempts to index all files and folders to a drive on both Windows and Linux systems. If the Cohesity cluster is unable to find mount point information about files or directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories in the lvol_N directory, where N is a unique number such as 1. On Windows systems, if the Cohesity cluster finds the mount point information about files and directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories with a drive letter such as C:. Linux LVM indexing supports the following LVM types only: Linear, Striped, Mirrored, Mirrored + Striped, Thin. On Linux systems, how files and directories are indexed and displayed is dependent on the conditions specified in the following table.

Server Type

Volume Type

Linux Virtual Machine

Simple Volume

The Cohesity cluster detects mount points for entries in the /etc/fstab file with the following formats:
UUID=ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc /mnt ext4 auto 0
UUID="ccd1d599-e68e-4b88-ba9b-6f75b63f1bdc" /mnt ext4 auto 0
If the Cohesity cluster can detect a mount point, it indexes and displays files and directories in the volume with the mount point that was specified in the /etc/fstab file. For these example entries, files and directories are indexed with the /mnt mount path, such as /mnt/example/test.txt.
If the Cohesity cluster cannot detect a mount point, the Cohesity cluster indexes the files and directories into a lvol_N directory. For example, the /mnt/example/test.txt file is indexed as /lvol_1/example/test.txt.

l Cohesity supports recovering files/folders from NTFS (Windows VMs) to Windows VMs, and from Linux VMs to Linux VMs only.
l When recovering a file or instantly mounting a volume from a Windows VM or Physical Server Backup Source that has Windows deduplication installed and enabled for one or more volumes, you must choose a target machine that also has Windows deduplication installed (it does not have to be enabled for any volume). (However, this rule does not apply to Nutanix AHV VMs. If AHV VMs are enabled with Windows deduplication, the only supported recovery option is full VM recovery.)
If the target does not have Windows deduplication installed:
l File level recovery will fail with the error message: "Windows Data Deduplication role is not installed on the target machine. Retry recovery after installing the Windows Data Deduplication role on the target machine."
l Instant volume mounting will fail with the error message: "Windows Data Deduplication role is not installed on the target machine. Retry recovery after installing the Windows Data Deduplication role on the target machine."
To determine if Windows deduplication is installed on the Source or target machine, follow the steps given below:

Prerequisites
QEMU Guest Agent Installation
The QEMU Guest Agent must be installed and running inside the RHOV virtual machine. The guest agent is required to execute commands inside the VM for file-level recovery operations.
Linux VMs
1. Install the guest agent:
sudo apt-get install -y qemu-guest-agent
2. Enable and start the service:
sudo systemctl enable qemu-guest-agent sudo systemctl start qemu-guest-agent

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization

Windows VMs Install the VirtIO drivers and QEMU Guest Agent and run the qemu-ga-x86_64.msi installer. The service starts automatically after installation.
Verify Guest Agent Connectivity
1. Verify that the QEMU Guest Agent is connected from outside the VM: oc get vmi <vm-name> -n <namespace> -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}' | python3 -m json.tool
2. Confirm that the following condition is present: "type": "AgentConnected" "status": "True"
Enable guest-exec Command
The guest-exec and guest-exec-status RPC commands must be enabled in the QEMU Guest Agent configuration. Linux VMs
1. Edit the configuration file: sudo vi /etc/sysconfig/qemu-ga
2. Update RPC settings: l If using BLOCK_RPCS, remove: guest-exec, guest-exec-status l If using AL, add LOW_RPCS: guest-exec, guest-exec-status
3. Restart qemu-guest-agent. Windows VMs
1. Update the QEMU Guest Agent service configuration to ensure guest-exec is not blocked.
1. Restart-Service QEMU-GA.
Verify guest-exec Enablement
l Run the following command oc exec -it <virt-launcher-pod> -n <namespace> -c compute -- \ virsh qemu-agent-command <namespace>_<vm-name> \ '{"execute":"guest-exec"}'
l A successful response returns:

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization

{"return":{"pid":<pid>}} ``` [1](https://cohesity-
SELinux Configuration (Linux Only)
Configure SELinux to allow QEMU Guest Agent operations:
sudo semanage permissive -a virt_qemu_ga_t
Considerations
l Dependency on QEMU Guest Agent l File-level recovery requires the QEMU Guest Agent to be installed and connected. l Recovery operations depend on successful communication with the agent.
l guest-exec Command Requirement l File-level recovery depends on the guest-exec and guest-exec-status commands being enabled. l These commands are disabled by default and must be explicitly configured.
l SELinux Restrictions l SELinux in enforcing mode can restrict operations required for file-level recovery, such as mounting backup disk partitions.
l Platform-Specific Behavior l SELinux configuration applies only to Linux VMs. l Windows VMs do not require SELinux-related configuration.
l Agent Connectivity Requirement l The QEMU Guest Agent must report a connected state (AgentConnected = True) for recovery operations to proceed.
l Mount Points Without /etc/fstab Entry Indexed paths depend on how the cluster associates backup content with guest mount metadata. Runtime-only mounts or volumes that are not defined persistently (for example, no /etc/fstab entry on Linux or no drive letter on Windows) might not appear under their original paths in the UI. In such cases, content may be grouped under generic or synthetic prefixes (for example, lvol_N, where N is a unique number). Recommendation: Use clear and persistent mount definitions for volumes that must be browsable and recoverable.
l LVM Handling During Recovery For Linux guests using LVM, recovery relies on importing and activating volume groups so backup volumes can be mounted within the guest.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization

This requires LVM packages, vgimportclone, and activation using vgchange -ay. If these utilities are not available, recovery might fail. l No Cross-OS Recovery Cross-operating system file-level recovery is not supported. Windows Linux: Not supported Linux Windows: Not supported. l Windows Data Deduplication If Windows Data Deduplication is enabled, recovery to a VM without deduplication drivers might fail or result in incomplete recovery. Use Download Files, full VM recovery, or other supported workflows if recovery fails. l Storage Replica on Windows with GPT Disks If Storage Replica is enabled with GPT disks, original-location recovery might be unsupported or unreliable. Alternatives include recovering to another path, full VM recovery, or using download. l Long File Paths (Windows Targets) Paths longer than approximately 200 characters might fail during restore operations due to Windows limitations. Mitigation: Use shorter paths, restore smaller sets, or rename files after restore. l Hard Links, Reparse Points, and Alternate Data Streams Recovery does not guarantee preservation of NTFS features such as alternate data streams, reparse points, or hard link relationships. l Sparse File Support on Windows Sparse file handling is not supported during recovery. Sparse files may be restored as fully allocated files. l Copy Tools: rsync and robocopy Recovery relies on rsync on Linux and robocopy on Windows. If these tools are missing or fail, metadata such as ACLs and attributes may not be preserved. l Supported Operating System Versions Support for backup and file-level recovery follows Cohesity RHOV interoperability guidelines, including requirements for QEMU Guest Agent, guest-exec, and SELinux where applicable.

QEMU Guest Agent Not Connected
1. Check agent status inside the VM
sudo systemctl status qemu-guest-agent
2. Verify connectivity from KubeVirt:
oc get vmi <vm-name> -n <namespace> -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[? (@.type=="AgentConnected")].status}' ``` [1](https://cohesity-

guest-exec Still Blocked
1. Verify configuration. cat /etc/sysconfig/qemu-ga
2. Restart the agent: sudo systemctl restart qemu-guest-agent
Note: qemu-ga -b=help displays potential blocked commands, not the current active configuration.
Mount fails with "Permission denied"
Check current mode getenforce

The Cohesity cluster attempts to index all files and folders to a drive on both Windows and Linux systems. If the Cohesity cluster is unable to find mount point information about files or directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories in the lvol_N directory, where N is a unique number such as 1.
On Windows systems, if the Cohesity cluster finds the mount point information about files and directories, it indexes and displays these files and directories with a drive letter such as C:.
Linux LVM indexing supports the following LVM types only: Linear, Striped, Mirrored, Mirrored + Striped, Thin. On Linux systems, how files and directories are indexed and displayed is dependent on the conditions specified in the following table.

Character replacement explanation for : and \ in file and directory names in zip files
If the original file or directory name contains a `:' , it is replaced with `_COLON_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "a:b" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b" l The original name is "a:b:c" then the archived name is "a_COLON_b_
COLON_c"
If the original file or directory name contains a `\', it is replaced with '_BACK_ SLASH_' in the archive. Example:
l The original name is "x\y" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_y" l The original name is "x\y\z" then the archived name is "x_BACK_SLASH_
y_BACK_SLASH_z"

7. Optional. Edit the default settings of the following Recovery options:
l Overwrite Existing File/Folder: By default, this option is enabled to overwrite the existing files and folders. Disable this option to create the files and folders in the specified location. Any duplicate files are skipped.
Example for a Windows alternate location with Overwrite Existing File/Folder enabled and the target already exists:
Files to be recovered: "C:\foo\1.txt", "C:\foo\test\1.txt", "C:\bar", "C:\foo\bar". Specified alternate location: "C:\restore". At the end of the copy, the target folder looks like this:
l C:\restore\1.txt
l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_0\1.txt
l C:\restore\bar
l C:\restore\cohesity<taskid>_1\bar

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 21: Kubernetes

Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization

If Overwrite Existing File/Folder is enabled, recovering a file to source when the file is in use may cause the open file to be overwritten. Whether overwriting occurs depends on the application using the file.
l Preserve File/Folder Attributes: File attributes are preserved when rsync for (Linux) or robocopy (Windows) is available and functioning correctly. If these tools are not present, preservation of file attributes is not guaranteed.
By default, this option is enabled and the ACLs, permissions, and timestamps are preserved for all files and folders. If you disable this option, then ACLs and permissions are not preserved. If recovering both folders and files, then folders will receive the new timestamps, but files retain their original timestamps. If recovering only, files, then files will receive the new timestamps.
l Continue on Error: Enable this option if you want to continue the recovery even if one of the objects encounters an error. By default, this option is disabled and the recovery operation will fail if one of the objects encounters an error.
l Cluster Interface: By default, the Auto Select option is enabled and the recovery task automatically selects the correct VLAN. If you disable this option, then select a configured interface group from the Interface Group drop-down.
l Task Name: Change the default name of the recovery task.

The recovery task is initiated. You can monitor the recovery task from the Recoveries page.

If recovering both folders and files, then folders will receive the new timestamps, but files retain their original timestamps. If recovering only, files, then files will receive the new timestamps.
l Continue on Error: Enable this option if you want to continue the recovery even if one of the objects encounters an error. By default, this option is disabled and the recovery operation will fail if one of the objects encounters an error.
l Cluster Interface: By default, the Auto Select option is enabled and the recovery task automatically selects the correct VLAN. If you disable this option, then select a configured interface group from the Interface Group drop-down.
l Task Name: Change the default name of the recovery task.

Chapter 22: Private Cloud Platforms
A private cloud is a dedicated computing environment that offers greater security, control, and compliance. Cohesity provides data protection for modern applications deployed in private cloud environments.
VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Automation
Note: This is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
Cohesity supports data protection for VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Automation environments, enabling backup and recovery operations. VCF Automation is a full-stack cloud platform that delivers a consistent private cloud experience across on-premises data centers, edge environments, and public cloud deployments. It integrates compute, storage, networking, and lifecycle management into a unified software-defined platform supporting both traditional Virtual Machines and modern workloads. VCF Automation is the self-service automation layer of VMware Cloud Foundation.It turns the underlying vSphere infrastructure into a self-service private cloud that teams consume through declarative APIs and UIs, with policy-based governance and multi-tenancy. Considerations

Key Concepts for VCF Automation Source Protection Cohesity discovers the following VCF Automation entity hierarchy when you register a source:
Organization
An Organization represents the top-level tenant in VCF Automation. It can correspond to an end customer for a service provider or a department or line of business within an enterprise. An Organization:
l Acts as the primary administrative boundary. l Is mapped to one or more vSphere Supervisor clusters through Regions to provide
infrastructure resources. l Contains one or more Projects for logical resource organization.
Projects
A Project resides within an Organization and provides a logical grouping of resources based on teams, environments, or business units. A Project:
l Exists under a single Organization. l Can be created in multiples within an Organization. l Represents different teams or lines of business. l Manages user access, roles, and governance policies at the project level. l Contains one or more Namespaces for workload deployment.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 22: Private Cloud Platforms

VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Automation

Namespaces
A Namespace resides within a Project and acts as the execution and resource boundary for workloads. A Namespace:
l Exists under a Project, with multiple namespaces supported per project. l Is instantiated on the vSphere Supervisor cluster associated with the Organization. l Defines resource allocations such as CPU, memory, storage, and network. l Carves out a dedicated resource pool for quota management. l Serves as the deployment location for workloads, including virtual machines and
container-based applications.
Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) provides networking capabilities similar to public cloud environments, enabling secure and isolated communication for workloads. A VPC:
l Provides network isolation and connectivity for workloads. l Can be associated with one or multiple Namespaces. l Enables a cloud-like networking experience within VCF Automation.
Supervisor
A Kubernetes-style control plane embedded in ESXi and vCenter. VCF Automation creates VMs through the Supervisor (VM Service). Each workload-domain vCenter requires at least one Supervisor; one NSX instance supports up to 16 vCenters.
Region
Maps to a Supervisor. In the Cohesity entity hierarchy, each namespace shows the Region it runs on.
VM Service VM

Chapter 23: About Bare Machine Recovery
A Bare Machine Recovery (BMR) is the ability to recover a system, including the operating system, its configuration, applications running on the operating system, and its data back to a state it was at a given point. Cohesity integrates with Cristie software to protect your servers for bare machine recovery (BMR). Cohesity supports two types of BMR:
l Cristie Bare Machine Recovery (CBMR): In this integration, a separate schedule for BMR backup is required to be added to the protection policy. First, a block-based protection run is executed followed by a separate BMR run. The BMR run is always Full (no incremental). For more information, see CBMR.
l Cohesity Bare Machine Recovery (CoBMR): In this integration, CoBMR leverages Cohesity's file-based and block-based physical server protection. No separate BMR schedule or protection run is required. For more information, see CoBMR.
Note: l For BMR-based protection of a physical server, you must first install the Cohesity agent on the physical server followed by the BMR agent and register the physical server with the Cohesity cluster.
l You can also deploy the Cohesity agent on a virtual machine and protect the VM as a physical server to perform BMR. For more information, see Deploy Cohesity Agent on Virtual Servers.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Recovery Workflow

Initiate BMR recovery from Cohesity to fetch the recovery path (the SMB share has the "system.vtd" file, the Custom Virtual Device Driver file). Then mount the system.vtd file in the CBMR recovery wizard to complete the recovery.

Recovery is performed through CoBMR Recovery Environment.

CoBMR
Cohesity Bare Machine Recovery (CoBMR) is a licensed BMR software suite. Cohesity integrates with CoBMR to perform the bare machine recovery of the physical servers (Windows and Linux) by leveraging Cohesity's file-based backup and block-based backup for physical server protection. With CoBMR, the system state information of the physical server is captured first, followed by the file-based or block-based backup for all drives, volumes, and partitions. This way, CoBMR recovers the physical server's original state using the recovery image and the protected data. To obtain the CoBMR software and license, contact Cristie.

5. Set Timeout: Set Timeout (mins) to at least 45 minutes to account for script execution time.
6. Disable Script Failure Option: Uncheck Continue Backup if script fails.
For Linux Servers
1. Choose Backup Type: Select either a file-based or block-based Protection Group.
Note: Recovery steps vary by backup type. Refer to platform-specific documentation for details.
2. Include All Volumes: If backing up all system volumes, enable Protect all local volumes during server selection.
3. Add Pre-Script: Configure a pre-script that invokes cobmrcfg with the --cobmr_ boot_backup flag to ensure the /boot partition is backed up correctly. For guidance on adding scripts, see see Add Executable File in user_scripts Directory.

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

CloudArchive Direct

CloudArchive Direct
CloudArchive Direct lets you archive data directly to an external target without retaining a copy of the data on the Cohesity cluster. In CloudArchive Direct, the Cohesity cluster acts as a local cache to stream the dataset to the external target, eliminating the need to store a full backup copy on the Cohesity cluster first. This approach reduces the capacity requirements on the local Cohesity cluster to a small cluster footprint, as only the metadata and index, and not the dataset itself are stored on the local cluster. Storing the metadata and index on the local cluster enables much quicker search and recovery down the road. The external target also stores the metadata and index, in addition to the data itself. On the Cohesity cluster, you can register a cloud storage, S3compatible storage, or NFS-mounted servers as external targets.
Note: For the first archival, depending on the size of data, the Cohesity cluster might experience significant capacity utilization, because the data first gets stored on the local storage (Storage Domain) and then aggressively gets down tiered to the external target. During this time, the capacity utilization will increase till the data is garbage collected upon the successful transfer.
Important: The option to enable CloudArchive Direct (native mode - no dedupe, no compression) from the NAS Protection Group page is deprecated in the 6.7 version.

How CloudArchive Direct Works
When you run a Protection Group for a registered source with CloudArchive Direct enabled, then according to the policy set for the Protection Group, the file system from NAS is read and stored on the external target as a streaming backup using the Cohesity cluster as a temporary cache.

CloudArchive Direct

Differences Between CloudArchive Direct and Cloud Archive

Term CloudArchive Direct
Cloud Archive

Description
CloudArchive Direct copies the data from the supported source directly to any registered external target such as public cloud providers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform) or any S3-compatible external target to reduce storage costs and eliminate the need to store a full backup copy onpremises.
Cloud Archive sends a copy of the backup data (it contains the backup data, metadata, dedupe fingerprint, and index) stored on the Cohesity Cluster to any registered external target. To perform Cloud Archive, at least one full copy of the primary data needs to be stored on the cluster.

Figure X: CloudArchive Direct and Cloud Archive workflow

Considerations
l CloudArchive Direct is supported for both physical clusters and virtual clusters. CloudArchive Direct is not supported for Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy). Cohesity Cloud Edition (formerly known as NGCE cluster) uses a CloudArchive Direct architecture, in which backup data is directly down tiered to object storage, and only metadata is stored on the cluster's cache tier.
l If Encryption is enabled at the cluster level, you must also enable encryption while registering the external target for CloudArchive Direct. Archiving directly to an external target may fail if encryption is enabled at the cluster level but not at the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

CloudArchive Direct

external target level. l Review and understand the following considerations if you are performing
CloudArchive Direct of NAS sources: l When you upgrade the Cohesity cluster from 6.6 or below versions to the latest version, the existing Protection Group created with CloudArchive Direct native mode will not automatically switch to the new CloudArchive Direct format. Therefore, you must pause the existing Protection Group and then create a new Protection Group for the objects with CloudArchive Direct new format.
l Review and understand the following considerations if you are performing CloudArchive Direct of VMware VMs to Archive Storage tier (AWS S3-Glacier, AWS S3-Glacier-Deep-Archive, AWS S3-Glacier-Deep-Archive, AWS S3-Glacier-DeepArchive Gov): l File and folder recovery is not supported. l Instant recovery of VMware VMs is not supported. l Instant Volume Mount is not supported. l Test & Dev (Cloning) is not supported. l Virtual Disks (VMDK) recovery is not supported. l Indexing is not supported.

CloudArchive Direct

during weekdays but not on Saturdays or Sundays. Quiet Times only prevent new protection runs from starting during the specified time period. Protection runs that started before the quiet time period are not affected and will continue to run. For example, if a protection run starts at 12:45 AM on Saturday morning and there is a weekend quiet time period that starts at 1 AM on Saturday morning, the protection run will continue to run past 1 AM. No new protection runs are started during the quiet times.
You can add multiple quiet times. For example, you could define a quiet time period for Saturday and Sunday and another quiet time period every morning from 9:00 AM to 11:00 AM.
Note: If you update the Quiet Time periods in a policy for a running Protection Group, only new protection runs using the policy are affected and any existing Protection runs that have already started will use the original Quiet Time periods.
4. Retry Options: By default, the Cohesity cluster attempts to capture snapshots three times before the Job fails. The default time between retries is five minutes. You can optionally customize the number of retries and how long to wait between each attempt.
5. (Optional) Click the Primary Copy tile and configure the following Backup Options from the floating menu:
l Extended Retention: Select this option to retain a subset of snapshots (backups) for a longer time period than defined by the protection schedule. Specify when to take the first snapshot and how long to retain it.
l Data Movement: This option applies only when you have selected AWS Standard Storage Tier as the external target to store the primary copy. With this option, you can move the data (downtier) from the selected AWS Standard Storage Tier to an AWS Archive Storage Tier target after a specified time period. Data Movement helps in space reclamation on the external target. From the Move Data drop-down, you can select the data S3 target and specify after how many days, weeks, months, or years you want to move the data from the external target to the S3 bucket.
Note: As an AWS consideration, you cannot downtier from S3 Glacier to S3 Deep Archive. After downtiering to either S3 Glacier or S3 Deep Archive, you cannot perform any further downtiering.
6. Click Create.

CloudArchive Direct

Create a Protection Group and Attach the CloudArchive Direct Policy
A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured. For performing CloudArchive Direct on the supported sources, you must create a Protection Group and attach the policy created with the CloudArchive Direct settings.
l For information on creating a Protection Group for VMware VMs, see Add or Edit a Protection Group for Virtual Servers.
l For information on creating a Protection Group for NAS, see Protect NAS.
Use Cases for CloudArchive Direct
Use-Case 1: Perform CloudArchive Direct to a cold storage tier
1. On the AWS console, create an S3 bucket. Ensure that you do not set lifecycle management policy on the S3 bucket.
2. Log in to the Cohesity cluster, and perform the following steps: 1. Register the S3 bucket as an S3-Glacier or S3-Glacier-Deep-Archive as an external target. While registering: l Select the Archival Format as Incremental Forever. l Download and execute the CloudFormation template in your AWS account to create the required resources for Garbage collection. For more information, see Register an External Target for Archival. 2. Create a policy with the Primary Copy option set to the registered external target. For more information, see Create a Policy with CloudArchive Direct Settings. 3. Create a Protection Group and Attach the CloudArchive Direct Policy. For more information, see Create a Protection Group and Attach the CloudArchive Direct Policy.
Use-Case 2: Perform CloudArchive Direct to hot storage tier (S3) with tiering to a cold storage tier (S3-Glacier or S3-Glacier-Deep-Archive)
1. On the AWS console, create an S3 bucket. You must not set the lifecycle management policy on the S3 bucket.
2. Log in to the Cohesity cluster, and perform the following steps: 1. Register the S3 bucket as an S3-Glacier or S3-Glacier-Deep-Archive as an external target. While registering:

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

Archive Object Lock

Cohesity stores immutable data at both the source cluster and external target levels. By configuring Object Lock, you can lock archives on external targets to prevent data from being modified, deleted, or overwritten. Object Lock can be configured during external target registration. For registering an external target, see Register an External Target for Archival.
Prerequisites for Object Lock
Before registering an external target with Object Lock enabled, ensure the following:
l Confirm Object Lock support: Verify that the target you select supports Object Lock. For the list of targets that support Object Lock, see Supported Workflows and External Targets.
l For AWS external targets: The Object Lock-supported AWS external target must have versioning and Object Lock enabled. For more information, see Using S3 Object Lock.
l For Azure external targets: The Object Lock-supported Azure external target must have version-level immutability enabled on the storage container, which indicates that the storage account must also have version-level immutability. For more information, see Enable version-level immutability support on a container.
l For GCP external targets: The Object Lock-supported GCP external target must have versioning and Object Retention Lock enabled. For more information, see Object Retention Lock.
Note: l The above properties must be set at the time of target creation and cannot be enabled after creation.
l Avoid setting default retention on S3 buckets and Azure - this is not required as Cohesity locks the objects for the duration required. Large default retentions affect garbage collection and increase costs.
l For AWS and S3-compatible targets, by default, the archived objects will be locked in the Governance retention mode. Support for enabling Object Lock in Compliance mode via the Cohesity UI will be introduced in an upcoming release.
l For Azure targets, by default, the objects will be locked in the Locked mode.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

Archive Object Lock

Considerations for Object Lock
l If you registered an Object Lock-capable external target on a Cohesity cluster running version 6.8 or earlier and later upgraded the cluster to a version that supports Object Lock, you will not be able to enable Object Lock on those previously registered targets.
l When archiving data to versioned buckets, ensure that you do not edit the storage class of objects directly. Editing the storage class of objects directly will create a new version of the object while the original version remains in the previous storage tier. Object-level locks will not be carried over to the new version.
l The Cohesity Data Movement feature, which can enabled during protection policy creation cannot coexist with Object Lock. An archival target can only have one of the settings enabled.
l The expiry of the object lock will match the expiry set for archived snapshots. However, the object lock will not update if you modify the expiry for archived snapshots after the Protection Group has run.
l You cannot disable Object Lock once you enable it on a target.
l For archival with periodic full format:
l For the list of targets (S3-compatible, AWS, and Azure) that support Object Lock for archival with periodic full,
see Supported Workflows and External Targets.
l If Object Lock is not met for an archive, the archive is still considered successful and can be recovered.
l After archival, to view the Object Lock status, perform the following:
a. Click the Protection menu.
b. Select the required Protection Group.
c. Select the required run.
d. Click the Cloud Archive tab.
The Object Lock Compliance status and Archive Object Lock Expiry Time will be displayed.
l For archival with incremental forever format:
l For the list of targets (S3-compatible, AWS, Azure, and GCP) that support Object Lock for archival with incremental full, see Supported Workflows and External Targets.
l If Object Lock compliance is not met for an archive, then the archival will fail.
l For on-prem clusters, Cohesity does not support Object Lock for CloudArchive Direct. However, for Cohesity Cloud Edition clusters in AWS, GCP, and Azure, where the primary copy of data is down-tiered directly to an external target via

Archive Data Over AWS PrivateLink
AWS PrivateLink allows AWS users to access Amazon services (S3, EC2, etc) through a private network. With AWS PrivateLink, you can create an interface endpoint in your VPC. These endpoints are directly accessible from applications that are on premises over VPN and AWS Direct Connect, or in a different AWS Region over VPC peering. For archiving your data to AWS S3, you can configure AWS PrivateLink to securely connect to the AWS external target over your private network. The following diagram depicts how AWS PrivateLink is used to access Amazon S3 through a private network:

Configuring Amazon PrivateLink for Archive
Prerequisites Before configuring Amazon PrivateLink for archive, ensure to have:
l AWS Direct Connect or AWS Virtual Private Network (AWS VPN) connection between the on-premise data center and AWS.
l AWS Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), VPC subnet, and security group. To configure Amazon PrivateLink for archive, perform the following steps:
1. Create a PrivateLink Interface Endpoint for S3 in Your VPC. 2. Create an S3 Bucket in the AWS Console. 3. Register S3 Bucket as an External Target.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

Archive Data Over Azure Private Endpoints

Create a PrivateLink Interface Endpoint for S3 in Your VPC
To support on-premise traffic for S3, you must create an interface VPC endpoint. To create an interface endpoint for S3, see AWS documentation. Once you create an interface endpoint, Amazon S3 generates two types of endpoint-specific S3 DNS names that you can use to communicate with the AWS service from your VPC: Regional and zonal. Select Regional S3 DNS name to communicate with the AWS service.
Create an S3 Bucket in the AWS Console
To archive your data to Amazon S3, you must create an S3 bucket. While creating a bucket, Cohesity recommends you update the S3 bucket policy to restrict access only to the VPC endpoint. For more information on creating an SR bucket, see AWS documentation.
Register S3 Bucket as an External Target
Once you map the VPC endpoint IP address with the FQDN of the S3 bucket, for archiving your data over the private network, you can register the AWS S3 bucket with Cohesity as an external target. For more information, see Register an External Target for Archival. If you have configured Amazon PrivateLink interface endpoints with the Cohesity cluster to access the AWS S3 external targets for archival, then you must provide values for the following parameters while executing CFT:
l NetworkSecurityGroup: The network security group ID to use for the lambda function.
l VPCSubnets: One or more subnet IDs in the VPC to use for the lambda function.
For more information, see CloudFormation Template.

S3-Compatible Object Storage - Standard Tier
Cohesity supports any S3-compatible device as an S3-Standard tier (Regular as storage class) external target with similar capabilities to an AWS S3-Standard. Any S3-compatible targets that use S3-Standard must be registered as a regular storage class. The S3compatible uses S3-Standard APIs for archival and recovery. This Standard tier is supported for both incremental with periodic full and incremental forever archival formats. Compression and deduplication are supported for both archival formats.
With incremental forever archival format, the Cohesity cluster will download a portion of the data from the S3-compatible Standard tier external target for the space reclamation process and reupload it after compaction. This leads to increased network bandwidth usage. Cohesity recommends having sufficient network bandwidth between the cluster and the external target; for example, hosting the external target within the same data center or network as the Cohesity cluster.
Note: Any S3-compatible targets that use Tape storage in the backend are not supported with the Standard tier; instead, you must register them as S3compatible with the Tape-based Storage Class.

S3-Compatible Object Storage - Tape-Based
Cohesity supports any S3-compatible targets that use tape storage in the backend as an external target and have capabilities similar to those of AWS S3 Glacier. Any S3-compatible targets that use Tape storage in the backend must be registered as Tape-based Storage Class. The tape-based Storage Class uses S3 Glacier APIs for archival and recovery. This supports always full with compression enabled by default and does not support deduplication and incremental archives.
Note: S3-compatible Tape-based targets that deviate in their capabilities compared to AWS S3 Glacier tier are not supported. For the supported workflows of Tape-based, see Supported Workflows and External Targets.

S3 External Target Compatibility Tool
The S3 external target compatibility tool validates whether the provided S3 compatible configuration has all the necessary permissions to execute the required APIs for successful archive and restore operations. This tool can validate S3-compatible storage targets and Tape-based S3 targets. The S3 external target compatibility tool can be run from any linux environment and does not require a Cohesity cluster. The S3 external target compatibility tool validates the following features:
l Incremental with periodic full l Incremental with periodic full - versioning support l Incremental with periodic full - object lock support l Forever incremental l Forever incremental - versioning support l Forever incremental - object lock support
Install and Configure S3 Compatible Tool
To install the S3 compatibility tool:
1. Download the tool from the Cohesity Tools section on the Cohesity Download portal. 2. Run the following command to install the tool:
./s3_external_target_compatibility_tool_installer
The installer is a self-extracting package that installs all required files under the following directory:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

Register an External Target

/tmp/s3_external_target_compatibility_tool

Note: The dll_libs directory contains all dependent libraries. The installer automatically sets the correct interpreter and rpath.
3. Change the directory to /tmp/s3_external_target_compatibility_tool. 4. Run the following command to start the validation:
./s3_external_target_compatibility_tool --vault_config_file_path=<path_ to_vault_config_file> 5. Run the following command to view the list of available options in the tool: ./s3_external_target_compatibility_tool Configuration File Format The S3 External Target compatibility tool requires the external target configuration file in the following format: { "access_key_id": "<Provide access key id>", "secret_access_key": "<Provide secret access key>", "host_name": "<Enter the hostname>", "bucket_name": "<Enter the bucket name>", "port_number": "<Optional: Default is 443. Specify only if different>", "signature_version": <Optional: Default is 4. Values can be 2 or 4 (integer)>, "use_https": <Optional: Default is true. Values can be true or false (boolean)> "region": <Optional> } Parameters The following table describes the external target configuration file parameters.

Prerequisites and Considerations for Registering External Targets
Before registering an external target, read and understand the following points: l Ensure the external target is reachable. Verify by pinging the target from the Cohesity CLI. l Check the network infrastructure and confirm it is not blocking connectivity. l Check firewall policy settings. You may need to add the Cohesity node IP addresses to firewall rules. l For AWS S3 or Glacier external targets, add the DNS names for the S3 and Glacier endpoints for the region to the allow list. For more information, see AWS service endpoints. l For GCP, ensure that the Cloud Resource Manager API is enabled on the GCP project. l Before registering GCP as external targets, ensure the following endpoints are accessible to the Cohesity cluster: "www.googleapis.com", "accounts.google.com". l Cloud Tier targets cannot be unregistered currently. l The target type cannot be modified once you register the target.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

Register an External Target

l You can register an external target either for Cloud Archive, CloudArchive Direct, or for Cloud Tier. You cannot register the same external target for Cloud Archive, CloudArchive Direct, and Cloud Tier purposes.
l The external targets that are registered for Cloud Tiering must have low latency. Therefore, high latency storage classes like glacier vault etc are not supported for Cloud Tiering.
l The same bucket can be registered as different external targets depending on the storage class.
l If you are using an S3 bucket with object versioning enabled as the external target, you must set up a Lifecycle Management Policy on the bucket to permanently delete non-current versions of objects. This is required to garbage-collect object versions. If there is a malware attack on the bucket that overwrites object versions, this policy could result in data loss in the absence of WORM locks on the object versions.
l To configure an HTTP proxy server for outbound internet connectivity from a Cohesity cluster to an external target, see this KB article.
l From the Cohesity UI, you cannot unregister an external target registered for CloudTier.
l For Cloud Archive with incremental forever and for CloudArchive Direct, Cohesity cluster may download a portion of the data from the S3-compatible and NAS external targets during each garbage collection process and reupload it after compaction. This can potentially lead to increased network bandwidth usage. To prevent additional network usage, Cohesity recommends using S3-compatible and NAS targets hosted within the same data center or network as the Cohesity cluster.
l If an external target you want to register for archival has object lock with a default retention period configured, then you must not select "incremental forever" as the archival format while registering this external target with the Cohesity cluster.
Cohesity may require additional permissions to validate whether such a data lock policy is configured on the external target. For example, to validate the data lock configuration on AWS S3 targets, you must have the s3:GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration permission.
l If the Object Key Pattern of the S3 View is Object ID, then you must use the Incremental Forever archival format while archiving the S3 View. You cannot archive the S3 View using the Incremental with Periodic Full format.
l If you are planning to archive your data to Azure hot tier using the incremental forever archival format, then ensure that the storage account you create is accessible through a public network and not a private network.
l To avoid early deletion charges, garbage collection of objects archived to an external target is performed only after the minimum retention period is met. As a result, storage utilization at the target level may increase; however, the associated costs

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

Register an External Target

typically remain the same or may even be lower.
l For archiving data to S3 Compatible - Tape Based Storage Class: l The archival format is Always Full with compression enabled by default. l Cohesity does not support deduplication and incremental archive. l Cohesity does not support file-level recovery. l The S3 cache must have sufficient storage to hold the largest Protection Group while the cache is filled with the restored data. l The recovery workflow retains the restored data from the tape on the S3 cache for seven days. If you want to reduce the retention period of restored data on the S3 cache, contact Cohesity Support. l If multiple recoveries are triggered within a span of seven days, the cache size must be large enough to hold all the recovered snapshots. l By default, the number of parallel streams per cluster is set to 10. If you want to configure these values, contact Cohesity Support. l By default, the number of restore tasks per Tape Storage is set to 1. l Cohesity recommends not to add more objects in a Protection Group as the recovery workflow could hydrate the complete archive while restoring a single object. l To protect IBM Storage Protect S3 Compatible, you must contact IBM support.
l You must not set up a Lifecycle Management (LCM) Policy on the external target registered for Cloud Tier.
l If you are archiving data using Cloud Archive or CloudArchive Direct with the Incremental Forever archival format to Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering, ensure you do not explicitly configure a bucket lifecycle policy that down-tiers data to the Archive or Deep Archive tiers. Doing so will cause the external target registration to fail.
Additionally, if such a policy is configured after the S3 Intelligent-Tiering target has been registered with the cluster, any data archived to that bucket may become unrecoverable
l Prerequisites for Registering AWS S3 Buckts as External Targets Using IAM Roles Anywhere:
Before registering an AWS S3 bucket as an external target on the Cohesity cluster for archival using IAM Roles Anywhere, follow these steps:
1. Create a Certificate Authority (CA):
l Ensure that the certificates are X.509 v3 compliant.
l Set Basic Constraints to "CA" with the value "false".
l Include the key usage for Digital Signature.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

Register an External Target

l Use a signing algorithm such as SHA256 or stronger. Avoid MD5 and SHA1 algorithms.
2. Create a Trust Anchor in AWS: l Establish the relationship between the certificate authority and IAM Anywhere by creating a Trust anchor.
3. Create an IAM Role: l This role should have access to the AWS S3 bucket. l Implement a custom trust policy specifically for the IAM Anywhere service principal.
4. Create an IAM Anywhere Profile: l Specify which roles IAM Roles Anywhere can assume. This will define the permissions and restrictions associated with the roles used by IAM Roles Anywhere.
For more information about creating a Trust Anchor and Profile role, see the AWS documentation.

"s3:GetObjectVersionAttributes" is used to fetch metadata of objects in versioned objects.

Recommended Azure Storage Account Configuration for External Targets
When using Microsoft Azure as an external target with Cloud Archive or Cloud Archive Direct, we recommend specific Azure Storage Account settings to support reliable operation and cost effective storage.
Before estimating Azure storage costs, determine the required storage capacity for the external target by obtaining the total capacity from the Cohesity sales team, based on the internal sizing tools.
This topic describes the recommended Azure Storage Account configuration options and explains why those selections are typically used. With this information, you can

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

Register an External Target

independently use Microsoft's Azure Pricing Calculator to estimate storage costs based on their own capacity and retention requirements.
Note: Azure options and defaults may change over time. Always refer to the official Azure documentation and Azure Pricing Calculator for the most current information.
Recommended Settings for Azure Storage Account
We recommend the following settings when configuring an Azure Storage Account for use as an external target:
l Region: Select the Azure region where the cluster runs or where the external target data will be stored.
l Storage Type: Select Azure Blob Storage as the storage type. l Storage Account Type: Select General Purpose v2 as the storage account type so
that Hot, Cool, Cold, and Archive access tiers are available. l Performance Tier: Select Standard as the performance tier, because standard
performance is typically sufficient for Cloud Archive workloads. l Access Tier: Select Hot, Cool, Cold, or Archive based on access frequency and
retention requirements, accounting for Azure minimum retention and early deletion charges. l Redundancy: Select Locally Redundant Storage (LRS) as the redundancy option to keep storage and network costs low. Note that Geo-Redundant Storage (GRS) is selected by default. l Namespace: Select a flat namespace for the file structure, because hierarchical namespaces are usually not required. l Capacity: Enter the required storage capacity obtained earlier and review the estimated monthly and yearly storage costs shown by the Azure Pricing Calculator.
Additional Considerations
l Azure Pricing Calculator estimates reflect Azure storage costs only and exclude Cohesity licensing and Azure compute costs.
l Exact read, write, list, and delete operation costs vary; some teams account for approximately 5% additional cost beyond raw storage charges.
l Configure the actual Azure Storage Account using the Azure portal, CLI, or APIs after planning.
l Some Azure features (for example, immutability) are configured at account creation but do not affect pricing calculator inputs.

l If you want to use Cohesity Data Lock for immutability, you must enable the Object Lock on the Azure Storage Account.
Register an External Target for Archival
Before register an external target for archival, ensure you have:
l Met the pre-requirements to register an external target. l Reviewed the considerations. l The minimum permissions to register the external target.
To register an external target for Cloud Archive, perform the following steps:
1. Navigate to Infrastructure > External Target. 2. Click Add External Target located at the top right of the page. 3. Select Archival as the external target's Purpose. 4. From the Storage Type drop-down list, select the external target you want to
register with the Cohesity cluster for Cloud Archive. 5. From the Storage Class drop-down, select the storage class of the storage type you
selected.
Note: For Cloud Archive with incremental forever and for CloudArchive Direct, Cohesity cluster may download a portion of the data from the S3compatible and NAS external targets during each garbage collection process and reupload it after compaction. This can potentially lead to increased network bandwidth usage. To prevent additional network usage, Cohesity recommends using S3-compatible and NAS targets hosted within the same data center or network as the Cohesity cluster.

Reclamation option based on your optimization preference:

For information on configuring external KMS, see External Key Management Service.
If you have selected Internal KMS or KMIP Compliant as the Key Management Service (KMS) Type for encryption, then you can enable additional security for the external target. By enabling additional security, you can manage the key manually instead of Cohesity managing the encryption key for data that is transferred out. If you choose to manage the key manually, then after registering the external target with the Cohesity cluster, you must download the key from the external target's details page and store it in a secure location outside of the Cohesity cluster. With additional security, only the Cohesity clusters where you have explicitly provided the encryption key can download data from that external target. However, the source Cohesity cluster (the cluster that archived the data) does not require the encryption key of the external target.
Cohesity recommends you keep the Encryption option as enabled in almost all cases, except when the data is already encrypted.
Note: If Encryption is enabled at the cluster level, you must also enable encryption while registering the external target for CloudArchive Direct. Archiving directly to an external target may fail if encryption is enabled at the cluster level but not at the external target level.

16. Enable Bandwidth Throttling to limit the maximum data transfer rate from and to this External Target during a time window.
a. Traffic: Specify the direction of traffic to limit, by specifying a maximum bandwidth:
l Upload: Limit the data transfer rate from the Cohesity cluster to this External Target.
l Download: Limit the data transfer rate from this External Target to the Cohesity cluster.
b. Days: Specify the days of the week to apply the window.
c. Time: Specify all day or a time period for each day.
d. Throttle To: Specify the maximum data transfer rate.Optionally change the rate type.
e. Click Add.
f. Repeat these steps to add more upload throttling windows.
If overlapping windows are specified, the latest window that was created takes precedence. For example, if you first create a window from Monday 9 AM - 10 PM with a data rate of 50 Mbps and then a window from 5 PM to 12 PM with a data rate of 100 Mbps, during 5 PM -12 PM the data rate is limited to 100 Mbps.
If both cluster-level override throttling window and an external-target override throttling window is set during the same time period, the lowest Throttle To number specified is the maximum allowed data transfer rate. For example, if a cluster-level override throttling window of 8-11 AM is set to 250 Mbps and an External-level override throttling window of 9-10 AM is set to 200 Mbps, during 9-10 AM the maximum allowed data transfer rate is 200 Mbps. Specifying transfer rate limits at the External-target level is described at the end of this procedure. For information on setting up cluster-level bandwidth throttling, see Register an External Target for Archival.
17. Click Register.
The Cohesity cluster attempts to connect to the Target. A successful connection displays the External Targets page with the new Target included in the list.

Archival Formats
Cohesity supports the following formats for archiving the data to an external target:
l Incremental with Periodic Full: Performs an initial full archive and then incremental archival of data with a periodic full every 90 days from the Cohesity cluster to an external target.
l Incremental Forever: Performs a first full archival and then incremental forever archival of data from the Cohesity cluster to an external target.
Important: In version 7.2.2 and later, Cohesity enforces Incremental Forever as the default archival method for registering external target. If the target does not support Incremental Forever, Cohesity will automatically fall back to Incremental with Periodic Full. Note that if the target supports Incremental Forever, the option to switch to Incremental with Periodic Full is not available is not available.
Incremental with Periodic Full
An archived snapshot is referred to as an archive. The first archive of a Protection Group is always a Reference Full Archive. A Reference Full forms the basis for Incremental Archives. With incremental archives, the next archive after a reference full is an Incremental Archive. It designates the Reference Full Archive as its reference. The Incremental Archive contains only data that is different between its reference's snapshot and the snapshot being archived. Change blocks are computed and then changed data is compared to the reference, and the necessary data is sent to the external target. If deduplication is enabled and data did not change, only metadata is transferred. To reconstruct the snapshot of this incremental archive, both the incremental and the reference must be processed. Then, the next Incremental Archive constitutes an increment on top of the previous incremental archive, i.e. it designates the previous Incremental Archive as its reference. To reconstruct its snapshot, both Incremental Archives and the Reference Full Archive must be processed.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

Register an External Target

In this way, incremental archives form an "archival chain" that starts at the archive in question and ends with the Reference Full.

In order to limit the number of archives that must be processed to restore a snapshot, the chain is "broken" every 90 days. At that threshold, the next archive will not be an Incremental Archive, but rather a Full Archive. A regular, non-reference Full Archive is full in the sense that it covers all previous increments since the Reference Full Archive. However, it itself still refers to the Reference Full archive just like the first Incremental Archive.
The next Incremental Archive after a Full Archive will use the Full Archive as a reference.
The threshold is not configurable through the web interface, and is always 90 days regardless of how many archivals have been performed.

During incremental archives, if the Reference Full Archive becomes too inefficient, mainly if its utilization as a reference drops below 50%, the Reference Full Archive is retired.
Retiring a Reference Full Archive means that the next time a Full Archive needs to be created, it is created as a Reference Full Archive, rather than a regular, non-reference Full Archive. The next Incremental then uses that new Reference Full Archive as its reference.

Note: The web interface does not distinguish between Reference Full Archive and non-reference Full Archive.
Each archive, Whether Reference Full, Full, or Incremental, is retained as long as it is referred to by another archive, or as long as its own policy specifies.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

Register an External Target

For example, for a Protection Job with a 30-day retention policy on archives, on the 90th day, an Incremental Archive will be created, and set to expire on day 120. On day 119, it still refers to an entire archive chain going all the way to the Full Archive from day 1, and therefore even a 119-day old archive is not deleted from the external target.
Furthermore, if that Full Archive refers to a Reference Full Archive that is 6 months old, that Reference Full Archive is also not deleted.

Incremental Forever
Enable this option to perform a first full archival and then incremental forever archival of data from the Cohesity cluster to an external target. Incremental forever archival eliminates the need for periodic full archive and supports global deduplication, thereby improving the storage utilization of the target. This option is enabled by default while registering a new external target. For an existing registered external target, you must edit the registered target and enable this option. The migration from Incremental Archival to Incremental Forever Archival takes place in the next reference archive.
Note: l Ensure that the external target does not have WORM/Object Lock with a default locking period configured.
For the list of external targets and the Protection Groups that supports incremental forever archival, see Supported Workflows and External Targets.

Migrate External Targets with Incremental with Periodic full to Incremental Forever
If you want to migrate an existing external target registered with Incremental with Periodic Full archival format in version 7.2.1 or earlier to Incremental Forever, perform the following steps:
1. Confirm the external target supports incremental forever archival format. For the list of supported external targets, see Supported workflow and External Targets.
2. From the Cohesity UI, navigate to the registered external target (Infrastructure > External Target).
3. Click the Actions menu ( ) next to the target and select Edit. 4. Enable incremental forever as the archival format. 5. If you are enabling Incremental Forever on:
a. Azure hot tier, you must create Azure Function App. For more information, see Function App.
b. AWS S3 targets, you must run the CloudFormation Template on the AWS console using your AWS account. For more information, see CloudFormation template.
6. Click Save.

Add a New External Target for CloudTier
You can add a new external target for CloudTier while the existing external target registered for CloudTier is being removed.
Steps:
1. Verify whether the CloudTier is configured at the Cohesity cluster level or at the Storage Domain level.
a. If the CloudTier is configured at the Storage Domain level, verify if the Storage Domain has physical storage available to uptier the data back to the Storage Domain with the physical quota being set. If the storage space is less, you must extend the physical quota to uptier the data completely.
b. If the CloudTier is set at the cluster level, no action is required, proceed with step 2.
2. Remove the external target's disk if you want to remove the existing target from the entire Cohesity cluster. Skip this step if you want to remove the external target only from a set of Storage Domains as other Storage Domains might have data in this external target.
3. Contact Cohesity Support to remove the existing cloud_spill_vec depending on from where you want to remove the existing external target (from a set of Storage Domains or from the entire Cohesity cluster).
4. Wait until uptiering is complete. You can use the Advanced Diagnostics statistics (System > Advanced Diagnostics) on the Cohesity UI to confirm the status.

Kerberos Authentication Configuration Steps
Before you register an NFS volume as an external target with the Cohesity cluster using Kerberos authentication, you must perform the following steps:
1. Add Administrators to the Kerberos Database. 2. Add Administrators to the ACLs File. 3. Add Kerberos Provider to Cohesity cluster. Add Administrators to the Kerberos Database On the Kerberos database that you maintain, you must add an administrative principal (admin principal) with the required ACLs. You can also use an existing principal that has the required ACLs. This admin principal will be used by the Cohesity cluster during Kerberos provider registration.
Note: The steps for adding admin principal to Kerberos may vary depending on the Kerberos environment.
The following is an example of adding admin principal on a standard Linux environment:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

Kerberos Authentication for NAS External Target

You can use kadmin.local on the Kerberos admin server to create the administrative principal cohesity/admin
shell% /usr/local/sbin/kadmin.local kadmin.local: addprinc cohesity/admin@ENG.COHESITY.COM //ENG.COHESITY.COM is the Realm name// NOTICE: no policy specified for "cohesity/admin@ENG.COHESITY.COM"; assigning "default". Enter password for principal cohesity/admin@ENG.COHESITY.COM: <= Enter a password. Re-enter password for principal admin/admin@ENG.COHESITY.COM: <= re-enter the password. Principal "cohesity/admin@ENG.COHESITY.COM" created. kadmin.local:
Add Administrators to the ACLs File
The admin principal you created on the Kerberos database must be added to the Access Control List (ACL) file. The principal used during Kerberos provider registration must have the following minimum permissions:
l All permissions except extract password for NFS and host principals l All permissions including extract password for Cohesity principal
Note: The steps for adding admin principal to the ACL file may vary depending on the Kerberos environment.
The following is an example of adding an admin principal to the ACL file on the Linux server:
1. Edit the access control list for Kerberos administration.
$ sudo cat /etc/krb5kdc/kadm5.acl
2. Add the following:
cohesity/admin@ENG.COHESITY.COM xe cohesity@ENG.COHESITY.COM cohesity/admin@ENG.COHESITY.COM x nfs/*@ENG.COHESITY.COM cohesity/admin@ENG.COHESITY.COM x host/*@ENG.COHESITY.COM
Here, l cohesity/admin@ENG.COHESITY.COM is the admin principal that the Cohesity cluster uses to make changes to the Kerberos configuration. l cohesity@ENG.COHESITY.COM, nfs/*@ENG.COHESITY.COM, host/*@ENG.COHESITY.COM are the user principals.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 24: Manage External Targets

Kerberos Authentication for NAS External Target

l The user principal, cohesity@ENG.COHESITY.COM is shared among multiple clusters. The admin principal (cohesity/admin@ENG.COHESITY.COM) has read/write privileges (x) with respect to this user principal. The admin principal also has privileges to extract password (e) for this user principal. The reason to grant the admin principal the permission to extract the password for this user principal is that this user principal is shared among multiple Cohesity clusters in the same Kerberos realm. For example, in a multiple clusters environment, the first Cohesity cluster that registers with the Kerberos realm will create a user principal with a random password. This password is saved in its keytab. However, when the second cluster registers with the Kerberos realm, it does not know the password for the user principal that the first cluster created. Therefore, this password needs to be extracted and saved in the second cluster's keytab.
l nfs/*@ENG.COHESITY.COM, host/*@ENG.COHESITY.COM principals are not shared among clusters. These principles have more restrictive privileges but have wildcard associated with it. The names (nfs/* and host/*) of these principals are derived from the host alias provided during Kerberos provider registration with the Cohesity cluster and are assumed to be unique for each Cohesity cluster.
Add Kerberos Provider to Cohesity cluster
You need to add the Kerberos provider to the Cohesity cluster to authenticate the Cohesity user to access NAS volumes in a Kerberos environment. The Cohesity user is used for mounting the NFS volume onto the Cohesity cluster.
Prerequisites
l Realm name
Note: Realm is the domain over which a Kerberos provider can authenticate a user, host, or service. Realm name is the unique identifier of the Realm.
l KDC server name and credentials l Admin server

1. Type Realm Name. 2. Type Host Alias.

Once the Kerberos provider is added to the Cohesity cluster,
l The Cohesity cluster creates certain principals with the Kerberos provider depending on the provided host aliases:
l host/<host_alias>.<realm_name_in_lowercase>@<realm_name>
l nfs/<host_alias>.<realm_name_in_lowercase>@<realm_name>
l If you have provided multiple host aliases, multiple principals will be created. l Cohesity cluster additionally creates a Cohesity "user" principal, cohesity@<realm
name>, which is used by the NFS client when mounting a Kerberos-secured NFS volume. l The authentication of the principals created is restricted to AES-128/256 encryption types. These encryption types apply to the encryption applied to tickets and Kerberos client/server messages. l The principals are created with a randomly generated password using the "-randkey" kadmin option. l On each Cohesity node, a keytab is created containing the randomly generated passwords of each of the created principals.
l This is a standard way to store Kerberos client authentication details. l Access to the keytab files is protected from non-Cohesity users by access
control.

l The keytab contents are stored in the Cohesity cluster configuration and shared among nodes.

Unregister an External Target
Before you unregister an external target registered for archival, you must make sure that this external target is not used by any of the policies. To unregister an external target registered for archival from the Cohesity cluster:
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, navigate to Infrastructure > External Target. 2. Click the Delete icon.
If the external target is used by any of the policies, then a prompt is displayed to remove the external target from the policies before unregistering. 3. In the Unregister External Target prompt, type Unregister for confirmation and optionally, toggle on Delete Data. By enabling the Delete Data option, all the data available at the target will be deleted before unregistering. If this is not enabled, then only the metadata will be deleted. 4. Click Unregister. Depending on the number of archives in that external target, the status moves to Unregistering along with the percentage displayed. On success, the external target will not be displayed on the External Targets page.
Note: From the Cohesity UI, you cannot unregister an external target registered for CloudTier.
If you want to remove the external target registered for CloudTier from the cloud source, then you must:
1. Ensure to have enough storage space on the Cohesity cluster to uptier the data from the external target to the Cohesity cluster.
2. Gracefully remove the cloud disk. 3. Contact Cohesity Support to remove the external target from the Cohesity cluster.

Disaster Recovery Using CloudEdition

About Replication
Organizations can achieve enterprise-level resiliency with site-to-site replication between Cohesity clusters. Replication can be configured at multiple granularity levels for maximum flexibility, including job-level or Cohesity View level (similar to a storage volume). All data on a single Cohesity cluster can be replicated to one or more clusters through the use of Protection Groups. The Protection Group specifies the objects (like databases, physical servers, VMs, Cohesity Views etc) to be backed up and replicated. Full and partial fail-over functions are fully automated using the Cohesity Orchestration workflow engine for simple, seamless recovery.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 25: Disaster Recovery

About Replication

You specify a protection schedule in a Policy and that protection schedule defines how often a Protection Group using that Policy runs. In the example above, a Protection Group using a policy with an hourly protection schedule is capturing Snapshots of VM1 and VM2 and storing those Snapshots in the Dev Storage Domain. Another Protection Group using a policy with a daily protection schedule is capturing Snapshots of VM3 and storing those Snapshots in the QA Storage Domain.
You can optionally specify a replication schedule in a Policy. The replication schedule defines how often Snapshots are copied from a Storage Domain in the capturing Cohesity cluster and saved on a Storage Domain in the remote Cohesity cluster by a Protection Group using this Policy. In the example above, the Protection Group is making daily copies of the Snapshots in the Dev Storage Domain of the EngMain Cohesity cluster and storing those replicated Snapshots in the EngBackup Storage Domain of the remote Cohesity cluster called EngReserve. Another Protection Group with a different Policy is making weekly copies of the Snapshots in the QA Storage Domain of the EngMain Cohesity cluster and storing those replicated Snapshots in the QABackup Storage Domain of the remote Cohesity cluster called EngReserve.
The replication schedule for copying Snapshots cannot be more often than the protection schedule for capturing Snapshots. For example if Snapshots are captured hourly, the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 25: Disaster Recovery

About Replication

Cohesity cluster cannot replicate them every 30 minutes but it can replicate them hourly or any value over one hour.
Note: When replicating large files, if the replication process is slow for more than a day, contact Cohesity Support. For reference, see the KB Article.
Note: After Snapshots of Objects (such as VMs) are created by a Protection Group with replication schedules, copy tasks are immediately created to replicate the Snapshots to the remote Cluster. The Cohesity cluster does not wait until the Snapshots of all the Objects protected by the Protection Group are captured, before it starts replicating.

Using the Replicated VM Snapshots
After VM Snapshots are replicated (copied) to a remote Cohesity cluster you can use the Snapshots to complete the following tasks:
l Recover VMs from the replicated Snapshots to a new location. l Clone VMs from the replicated Snapshots. l Recover files from the replicated Snapshots. l Run the Analytics Workbench on these replicated Snapshots. l Download VMX files from the replicated Snapshots. The procedures for initiating these tasks are the same as initiating these tasks from Snapshots created by a Backup task of a Protection Group. You can also use the Snapshots and Inactive Protection Group that were replicated to the remote Cohesity cluster for disaster recovery. To learn more, see Active Protection Group Replicating to Remote Cohesity cluster.
Using the Replicated View Snapshots
After View Snapshots are replicated (copied) to a remote Cohesity cluster you can use the snapshots to complete the following task:
l Clone a View From a Snapshot.
Using the Replicated SQL Server Snapshots
After SQL Server snapshots are replicated (copied) to a remote Cohesity cluster you can use the snapshots to complete the following task:

l Recover Microsoft SQL Server.
Warning: For replicated MS SQL Server VM Snapshots, you can only restore MS SQL Server to a new location. (You cannot restore MS SQL Server to its original location.)

Object-based Replication
Object-based replication offers granular control by allowing replication at the individual object level. Instead of replicating all the runs in a protection group, you can replicate only the selected objects from a backup run to the target. Follow these steps to perform object-based replication:
1. In the Cohesity cluster, select Data Protection > Protection. 2. On the Protection page, select the required Protection Group. 3. On the backup run details page, click the Actions menu ( ) for the run and click Edit
Run. 4. In the Edit Run dialog, click Replication. 5. From the Replicate dropdown, select the subset of objects in the backup run and
click Continue. 6. From the Replication target dropdown, select the required target. 7. Toggle on Modify Retention if required.
1. Retention: From the dropdown, select one of the following: 1. Extend 2. Reduce
2. Retain for: Specify how many days, weeks, months, or years backups are retained on the cluster before they are deleted.
8. Click the save icon.
To add a new target to the backup run, click the plus icon.
About Replication Setup
Replication automatically makes copies of snapshots captured by a Protection Group on one Cohesity cluster and copies them to a second Cohesity cluster. To learn more about Replication, see About Replication. Before the Cohesity cluster can replicate Snapshots, you must register the Cohesity clusters with each other. For more information, see Replication and Remote Access Setup.

About Replication

Register Cohesity clusters for Replication
You must register the Cohesity clusters with each other and create at least one Storage Domain pairing between the Cohesity clusters. You can optionally specify a replication schedule in a Policy.

For more information on Replication Compatibility, see Replication Compatibility.

Cascaded Replication and Archival policy
Cohesity now supports Cascaded Replication. You can use this feature to not only replicate your Protection Groups from the source to the target cluster but also from the target cluster to another cluster. Also, protection objects can be archived from any of these targets.
Cohesity supports cascaded replication through scripts only. You have to create a cascaded replication policy that is non-cyclic. For example, replicating data from A to B to C is supported but Cohesity doesn't support the replication of data from A to B to C to A. For more information, see Cascaded Replication, Archival, and Vaulting Policy.
