About Replication

About Replication and Disaster Recovery
When a Protection Group with a replication schedule starts replicating snapshots from a primary Cohesity cluster to a remote Cohesity cluster, a Protection Group in Failover Ready state is created on the remote Cohesity cluster. If the original capturing Cohesity cluster and/or the original Source are down because there is a planned maintenance outage or a disaster destroys them, you can failover the Protection Group in Failover Ready state and deactivate the original task on the capturing Cohesity cluster. As part of the Failover, you are prompted to optionally recover the VMs from the replicated snapshots stored on the remote Cohesity cluster.
Warning: When you create a Protection Group on a Cohesity cluster with a replication schedule after the first snapshot is replicated, a Failover Ready copy of the Protection Group is created on the remote Cohesity cluster that is receiving the snapshot. For more information on Failover Ready, see About Failover Ready. You can failover the Protection Group of VMs. You cannot failover the Protection Group of Views or SQL Servers. You can, however, clone replicated Views and restore SQL Servers. For more information, see Failover a Protection Group.
The disaster recovery procedure consists of the following actions:
1. Active Protection Group Replicating to Remote Cohesity cluster. Protection Group on a Cohesity cluster is actively capturing Snapshots of VMs and replicating them to a remote Cohesity cluster. After the first Snapshot is replicated, an Inactive copy of the Job is also created on the remote Cohesity cluster.
2. Failover from Replicated Copies. Disaster strikes and you must recover from the replicated copies on the remote Cohesity cluster that received the Snapshots. This Failover activates the Job on the receiving (remote) Cohesity cluster. However, the Job is not running.
3. Deactivate Original VM Protection Group. If possible, deactivate the original Job on the Cohesity cluster that originally captured the Snapshots.
4. Restore Activated Protection Group. You can restore the state of the activated Job to running, by assigning a new Policy to the Job and selecting Objects (VMs) to back up.
Active Protection Group Replicating to Remote Cohesity cluster
A Protection Group on a Cohesity cluster is actively capturing Snapshots and replicating them to other remote Cohesity clusters. The Protection Group specifies Objects (such as VMs) to be backed up, replicated or archived. The Policy used by the Protection Group determines the protection schedule, the replication schedule and the archive schedule. The protection schedule determines when Snapshots of the Objects are captured. The replication schedule determines when the Snapshots are replicated to other remote Cohesity clusters. The backup Snapshots of the specified Objects are captured and saved on

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 25: Disaster Recovery

About Replication

a Storage Domain in the capturing Cohesity cluster as represented by the "Back Up" orange arrow in the figure below. The specified Snapshots are replicated from the Storage Domain in the capturing Cohesity cluster ("EngMain" below) to the Storage Domain in the remote Cohesity cluster ("EngReserve" below) as represented by the "Replicate" purple arrow in the figure below. After the first Snapshot is replicated, an Inactive copy of the Protection Group is created on the remote Cohesity cluster.
The example below shows the deactivation of a Protection Group protecting VMs. Deactivating a Protection Group protecting SQL Servers is similar but not all details are the same. For example, the transaction logs are not described or pictured.

About Replication

Failover from Replicated Copies
A disaster strikes the Source or there is a planned maintenance outage of the Source. The Cohesity cluster or the Source may be down or not available. From the Cohesity Dashboard, start the Failover procedure. For detailed instructions, see Failover a Protection Group. The example below shows the Failover of a task protecting VMs. Failover of a task protecting SQL Servers has transaction logs that are not pictured.
Note: When you create a Protection Group on a Cohesity cluster with a replication schedule after the first snapshot is replicated, a Failover Ready copy of the Protection Group is created on the remote Cohesity cluster that is receiving the snapshot. For more information on Failover Ready, see About Failover Ready. You can failover the Protection Group of VMs. You cannot failover the Protection Group of Views or SQL Servers. You can, however, clone replicated Views and restore SQL Servers. For more information, see Failover a Protection Group.
During Failover, the following actions occur:
1. Disaster at Source - On the primary Cohesity cluster, the backup job fails to capture the snapshots of the source.
2. Replication Fails - As the source is down or unreachable, the replication job fails to replicate the snapshots onto the remote Cohesity cluster. The Failover Ready for VMs on the remote Cohesity cluster is activated and causes the rejection of the incoming replicated snapshots created by the associated job on the primary Cohesity cluster.
3. Failover VMs - You are prompted to optionally recover the VMs from the replicated snapshots on the remote Cohesity cluster to a new source.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 25: Disaster Recovery

About Replication

Deactivate Original VM Protection Group
Only Protection Groups that are protecting VMs can be deactivated. Protection Groups that are protecting a view cannot be deactivated.
Note: If possible, deactivate the original Protection Group on the original capturing Cohesity cluster. If the original Cohesity cluster that captured the Snapshots is down or unreachable, you may be unable to deactivate the Protection Group.
The example below shows the deactivation of a Protection Group protecting VMs. Deactivating a Protection Group protecting SQL Servers is similar but not all details are the same. For example, the transaction logs are not described or pictured. During deactivation, the following actions occur:
1. Snapshots are no longer captured by the original Protection Group on the original capturing Cohesity cluster. However, the existing snapshots captured by the Protection Group remain in the storage domain. They are not deleted.
2. Snapshots created by the Protection Group are no longer replicated to the receiving (remote) Cohesity cluster. (If you have already initiated the failover procedure, the replication has already stopped.)
3. You can optionally choose that the VMs on the original source be powered off. The VMs and the VM files, however, are not deleted. (The Cohesity cluster may be unable to power off the VMs if the original source is down or unreachable.)

Cascaded Replication, Archival, and Vaulting Policy
By default, Cohesity supports site-to-site replication of the Protection Groups, which includes objects such as databases, physical servers, VMs, and Cohesity Views. Cohesity now supports Cascaded Replication. You can use this feature to not only replicate your Protection Groups from the source to the target cluster, but also from the target cluster to another cluster. Also, protection objects can also be archived from any of these targets. Prerequisites Make sure the following prerequisites are met before creating a cascaded replication policy:
l Install Python on the Virtual machine on the cluster with the following modules: l argparse l ast l copy l requests l logging l kson l sys l os l csv l time l re l datetime l subprocess l urllib3
Note: Python 3.10 must have all the modules except for requests.
Install the unavailable modules using the following command: pip install <modulename> Example pip command: pip install request For more information, see How to install pip on windows. l Storage Domains of the source cluster and the target cluster must be paired. l The Cohesity cluster version must be 6.8.1 and above. l Download the manage_cascaded_policy.py and sample inputs file here.

Before you Begin Cohesity provides the following files to create a cascaded replication policy:
l manage_cascaded_policy.py: The manage_cascaded_policy.py file contains the code and is used as the source file to create a cascaded replication policy. For more information, see Create a Cascaded Replication policy.
Warning: Do not edit the manage_cascaded_policy.py file.
l user_friendly_policy.json: The user_friendly_policy.json file contains the policy name, IP address, replication topology and other information required for the cascaded replication and archival. Topology is the connection between two nodes in a network and it represents the replication happening from the source cluster to the target cluster. In topology, where replication must be done from cluster A > B > C. While providing information for cluster A, mention the immediate cluster B and not C.

Considerations l Cohesity supports cascaded replication through scripts only. Replication and Remote Access Setup
On the Remote Cohesity clusters page, you can configure replication and remote access to another Cohesity cluster:
l Replication automatically makes copies of snapshots captured by a Protection Group on one Cohesity cluster and copies them to a second Cohesity cluster.You must register the Cohesity clusters with each other and create at least one Storage Domain

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 25: Disaster Recovery

Replication and Remote Access Setup

pairing between the Cohesity clusters. You can optionally specify a replication schedule in a Policy. A single Cohesity cluster can act as both a local and remote Cohesity cluster. For more information, see About Replication.
l Remote access lets you set up multi-cluster access and manage remote Cohesity clusters from the local Cohesity cluster. The Cohesity clusters must be the same version (6.0 or later). Once you add a remote Cohesity cluster to the local Cohesity cluster, you can switch to the remote Cohesity cluster by selecting its name from the drop-down list on the top left of the Cohesity Dashboard. The drop-down is not displayed until you add at least one remote Cohesity cluster. You can also display the consolidated statistics for all the remote access Cohesity clusters by selecting All Clusters Dashboard from the drop-down.
Note that replication and remote access are independent of each other; you can enable either or both for a remote Cohesity cluster. One does not require the other.
From the Remote Cohesity cluster's Dashboard page, you can begin setting up replication and remote access by clicking Register Remote Cluster. For detailed instructions, see Create a Connection to the Remote Cohesity Cluster.
To configure the Cohesity cluster's 1G interface for remote replication, see Set Up the Secondary Interface for Replication.
Note the following about replication:
l For information about using replication between Cohesity clusters running different versions, see Replication Compatibility.
For the latest notes about replication compatibility, prerequisites and limitations, see the Release Notes.
l If you have a Protection Group that is capturing and replicating Snapshots multiple times a day, Cohesity recommends configuring the replication schedule to copy Snapshots daily instead of replicating Snapshots after each protection run. If the replication schedule is too frequent, the replication may lag behind the capturing of Snapshots resulting in a backlog of replication tasks.
l If Snapshots of a VM are replicated to a remote Cluster and the VM is renamed in the vCenter Server, the Cohesity Dashboard on the remote Cluster displays the original VM name in the protection run Details page. However, you can search for new VM name while recovering or cloning and the search results display the new VM name. Replication is not affected by this issue.
l In production environments, Cohesity recommends not replicating from one single node Cohesity cluster Virtual Edition to another single node Cohesity cluster Virtual Edition. Cohesity recommends replicating from Cohesity cluster Virtual Editions to Cohesity clusters running directly on hardware.
Prerequisites:

l When registering a remote Cluster, log in to the local Cluster with a user in the default LOCAL domain that has an Admin Role such as the default Admin account. Do not use users or groups that were added to the Cohesity cluster for Active Directory principals to register a remote Cluster.
l Ensure that the required firewall ports (443, 11111, 20000, and 23335) are accessible for replication to a remote Cohesity cluster.
Note: If both the local and remote Cohesity clusters support TLS 1.3, port number 23335 is utilized for TLS communication during replication.
l Verify the IP reachability for both VIP and Node IPs between the Cohesity cluster capturing and replicating Snapshots and the Cohesity clusters receiving the replicated Snapshots.
l If the cluster replication is configured, verify that the network connectivity is functioning properly during the upgrade to ensure the cluster replication relationship is successfully upgraded to use AES-256-GCM for encryption.
l In a replication environment, if either the transmitting or receiving cluster is a multitenancy-enabled, both clusters must be running version 6.1 or later. Storage domain pairing must be set up on the source cluster. One or both clusters can be multitenancy-enabled.
Note the following about multi-cluster access:
l Both the local Cohesity cluster and the remote access Cohesity cluster must be running the same version (6.0 or later) of the Cohesity cluster software.
l On the local Cohesity cluster for which multi-Cluster access is configured, verify that firewall port 443 (TCP outbound) is open to all the remote access Cohesity clusters.
l If a Cohesity cluster is configured for multi-Cluster access and then the Cohesity cluster is re-imaged or re-installed, Cohesity recommends deleting and re-adding the remote access configurations to ensure that multi-Cluster access functions properly.

Create a Connection to the Remote Cohesity Cluster
If you are setting up replication on the Cohesity cluster that contains the original snapshots to replicate, you must register the connection to the remote Cohesity cluster that will store the replicated snapshots. The capturing (local) Cohesity cluster captures the snapshots and replicates them to the remote Cohesity cluster.
Note: A remote cluster is reachable by the source cluster only after the registration is complete because the firewall ports on the remote cluster are open after the registration.
To register a connection to a remote Cohesity cluster for replication and remote access: 1. Log in to the Cohesity cluster on which the original snapshots are stored. 2. Navigate to Infrastructure > Remote Clusters.

3. On the Remote Clusters page, click Register Remote Cluster.
The Register Remote Cluster dialog is displayed.
4. VIP or Node IP Addresses--Specify one of the following:
l One or more Virtual IP (VIP) addresses of the remote Cohesity cluster. Cohesity recommends specifying VIPs because of their ability to failover to other nodes in the Cohesity cluster if a node is down or unreachable.
l One or more node IP addresses of the remote Cohesity cluster.
If All Cluster Node IPs are Reachable is enabled for replication, a single node is specified in this field and the primary Cohesity cluster can establish an initial connection to the specified remote node, and the Cohesity cluster distributes the network traffic to other nodes in the remote Cohesity cluster. Cohesity recommends specifying VIPs. However, if you specify node IP addresses, Cohesity recommends specifying multiple node IP addresses. By specifying multiple node IP addresses, if the network traffic cannot reach a node, the Cohesity cluster can try a different node to establish the initial connection.
If network traffic is restricted in your environment, specify the VIP or node IP addresses of the Cohesity cluster that are configured to receive network traffic in your environment and turn off the All Cluster Node IPs are Reachable toggle.
Note: To add more IP addresses after the remote connection is configured, edit the remote connection, click Change, enter the addresses in the VIP or Node IP Addresses field, and click Connect to verify connectivity to the addresses.
5. Username--Specify a local or Active Directory user.
Authentication by Active Directory user is an Early Access feature. Contact your Cohesity account team to enable the feature.
l For remote access, Cohesity recommends you specify an admin user. Ensure you disable the MFA for this user.
l For replication, Cohesity recommends you specify a local user with only the Replication role on the remote Cohesity cluster. Ensure you disable the MFA for this user. For more information see Disable MFA for Local Users.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 25: Disaster Recovery

Replication and Remote Access Setup

a. Select a local storage domain. This storage domain contains the original snapshots that will be replicated.
Note: You cannot pair multiple storage domains on one Cohesity cluster to the same storage domain on the other Cohesity cluster. You cannot pair a storage domain to two different storage domains on the same remote cluster. You can pair a storage domain to two different storage domains if they are in different remote clusters. For more information, see Pair Storage Domains for Replication.
b. Select a remote storage domain. This storage domain is where the copies of the replicated snapshots are stored.
13. Outbound compression is enabled by default. Cohesity recommends keeping this option enabled so that this Cohesity cluster can compress the replication data before sending it to another Cohesity cluster.
14. All Cluster Node IPs are Reachable--Turn on the toggle if traffic can be distributed to all nodes. Turn off if your network environment requires restricting network traffic to the subset of IP addresses listed in the Node IP Address field. For example, if your environment has a firewall that is limiting the network traffic to the remote Cohesity cluster and if All Cluster Node IPs are Reachable is enabled, the Cohesity cluster automatically distributes the network traffic to other nodes in the remote Cohesity cluster.
Note: If there is Network Address Translation (NAT) between two clusters, ensure that the All Cluster Node IPs are Reachable option is disabled. This prevents communication issues due to translated IP addresses that may not be directly routable across the clusters.
15. Turn on the Encryption toggle to encrypt the replication data generated by this Cohesity cluster. Click Generate New Key. The encryption key is displayed. The Cohesity cluster that is receiving encrypted data must enable encryption and specify the same encryption key as the Cohesity cluster that sent the replication data. Copy the encryption key to the clipboard, so you can paste it while creating the connection from the capturing Cohesity cluster back to the remote Cohesity cluster as described in Create Connection Back to the Capturing Cohesity cluster.
16. Turn on the Throttle toggle to set a replication data transfer rate limit from this Cohesity cluster to another Cohesity cluster. Specify the data rate in Megabits per second. For this connection, this value limits the data transfer rate when copying replication data such as snapshots from this Cohesity cluster to another Cohesity

cluster. 17. Turn on the Quiet Times and Throttle Overrides toggle to specify one or more
replication override windows. These windows override the setting in the Data Transfer Rate Limit field during the time period specified for the window.
l You can optionally change the time zone that applies to all the override windows specified for the connection between the local Cohesity cluster and the remote Cohesity cluster.

l Throttle--A window when this data transfer rate overrides the Data Transfer Rate Limit value specified. This window sets the maximum data transfer rate between the local Cohesity cluster and the remote Cohesity cluster during the specified time period.

Note: If overlapping windows are specified, the latest one that was created takes precedence. For example, if you first create a quiet time window from Monday 9 AM to 10 PM and then a throttle window from 5 PM to 12 PM with a data rate of 100 megabits per second, from 5 PM to 12 PM the data rate is limited to 100 megabits per second.

On the remote Cohesity cluster that will store the replicated snapshots, you must register the Cohesity cluster that is capturing the original snapshots. Important: In this procedure, you are logged in to the remote Cohesity cluster and registering the capturing Cohesity cluster. Specify the IP address and user credentials of the local Cohesity cluster.

If All Cluster Node IPs are Reachable is enabled for replication, a single node is specified

in this field and this Cohesity cluster can establish an initial connection to the specified primary node, and the Cohesity cluster distributes the network traffic to other nodes in the capturing Cohesity cluster. Cohesity recommends specifying VIPs. However, if you specify node IP addresses, Cohesity recommends specifying multiple node IP addresses. By specifying multiple node IP addresses, if the network traffic cannot reach a node, the Cohesity cluster can try a different node to establish the initial connection. If network traffic is restricted in your environment, specify the VIP or node IP addresses of the Cohesity cluster that are configured to receive network traffic in your environment and disable All Cluster Node IPs are Reachable.

About CloudRetrieve
CloudRetrieve provides the ability to download data that was archived from a Cohesity cluster to an alternate (non-original) Cohesity cluster. For example: You have Cohesity cluster A, which archives data to a cloud external target, but you want to download that archived data to Cohesity cluster B.
Note: CloudRetrieve is not intended to be used to recover data to the original Cohesity cluster. To restore data to the original Cohesity cluster, see About Recovering VMs.
Download to an Alternate Cohesity cluster
The following example depicts one source Cohesity cluster archiving data to a cloud external target followed by an alternate Cohesity cluster retrieving the archived data from that external target. The action steps in the following procedure are represented in the figure
below with blue numbered time squares: . 1. Register the external target that contains the data you want to download to the alternate Cohesity cluster. 2. Submit a search for Protection Groups that contain the data you want to download from the cloud external target. The search may take a few hours to complete. If the job to be downloaded is from a particular Cohesity cluster, specify the job name and Cohesity cluster name to narrow the results. 3. If the external target's encryption key file is managed manually, upload the key file to the alternate Cohesity cluster before triggering the search. See Create a CloudRetrieve Search Task for more details.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 25: Disaster Recovery

About CloudRetrieve

4. Download a snapshot from any of the Protection Groups in the search results. You can also build a local index of Protection Groups that ran during a specified date range. Downloading can take a few hours to complete. See Create a CloudRetrieve Download Task for more details.
5. Recover or clone any downloaded objects using the Cohesity recovery or clone workflows. See CloudRetrieve Downloaded Protection Groups for more details.

Considerations
l It is recommended that the Cloud Retrieve cluster runs a newer software version than the source cluster. The version of archives performed increases across releases and the older clusters cannot retrieve newer versions.
l Cohesity recommends not registering the same AWS S3 bucket, Azure storage container, or GCP bucket more than once for CloudRetrieval, even if the storage class differs.
CloudRetrieve Searches
The Searches tab lists search tasks and their status. Click a search task name to set up a download task.

Create a CloudRetrieve Search Task
Note: CloudRetrieve is not intended to be used to recover data to the original Cohesity cluster.
In this section you create a task to search for Cohesity clusters and Protection Groups that were archived to the selected external target. To learn more, see About CloudRetrieve. Before you can submit a search, an external target must be registered. See Register an External Target.
Search Cohesity clusters and Protection Groups
1. Select an external target. You may need to register an external target if the one you want to search is not registered with the Cohesity cluster.
2. In the Task Name field, you can optionally change the default name for the task. 3. Change the Date Range by clicking the date range link (for example: 06/30/2017 -
07/06/2017), and adjusting the time period. A larger date range results in a longer search time. The default date range is one year. 4. Optionally provide a Cohesity Cluster Name to search for. This is the Cohesity cluster where the Protection Groups originated. 5. Optionally provide a Protection Group Name to search for.
Important: Wildcard characters (like `*') are NOT supported.
Note: l If you enter search terms for both Cohesity Cluster Name and Protection Group Name, your search must find matches for the Protection Group within clusters that match. l If your search is too narrow, try entering a search term for Cohesity Cluster Name or Protection Group Name, or leave one or both empty.
6. If the external target is protected by a manually managed key, click Attach to upload the encryption key file to the Cohesity cluster.
7. Click Search. The search can take up to several hours to complete.

Note: The success of a CloudRetrieve search does not guarantee that the search found any matches. It only means that the search operation was completed successfully. Create a CloudRetrieve Download Task
In this section, you can create a task to download data from an external target. To learn more, see About CloudRetrieve.
Download Data
1. If desired, filter search results by Protection Group type or Cohesity cluster. You can also narrow results by searching for a Protection Group or Cohesity cluster.
2. Select the Protection Groups to download. Selecting the check box adjacent to Protection Group selects all filtered jobs.
3. For each selected Protection Group, you can edit download options by clicking Edit ( ). Or click Edit Selected to set download options for all selected Jobs together. Select the Download Job Meta-Data check box to fetch and index Job meta-data for the specified range. After the Protection Groups are indexed, they are listed as inactive Protection Groups on the Manage Protection Groups page. Jobs protecting VMs can be activated using the failover action. For more information, see Failover a Protection Group. Select the Download Snapshot check box to download the specified snapshot to the Cohesity cluster. Selecting a specific Snapshot is not available when editing multiple Protection Groups together (you clicked Edit Selected); the latest snapshot is always downloaded for these Protection Groups.
Note: In addition to the selected archive, a download fetches job meta-data for all archives that the currently selected archive depends on. This results in all the dependent protection runs displaying on the Job Details page. Additionally, selecting only a snapshot for download also downloads job meta-data.
4. Select or create a storage domain to contain the downloaded objects.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 25: Disaster Recovery

About CloudRetrieve

Note: Selected archived Protection Groups that are linked to Protection Groups on this Cohesity cluster use the local Protection Group's storage domain for their download location. Selected archived Protection Groups without a known local Protection Group are downloaded to the selected storage domain.
5. Click Download. Downloads may take up to several hours to complete. (Applies only for cloud archive incremental with periodic full) Provisioned Capacity Units (PCU) are required for all file-level recoveries. Provisioned capacity ensures that your retrieval capacity for expedited retrievals is available when needed. Each unit of capacity guarantees that at least three expedited retrievals can be performed every five minutes and provides up to 150 MB/s of retrieval throughput. Glacier Expedited retrieval offers a significantly improved latency (1-5 minutes) over Standard/Bulk retrievals (3-12 hours). As part of this, AWS may fail expedited Glacier requests with a lack-of-resources response:

Option uri

Description

HTTP Status Code

Returned if there is insufficient capacity to process the expedited request. This error only applies to expedited retrievals and not to standard or bulk retrievals.

503 Service Unavailable

Client Server

The Cohesity Bridge warning logs will return the following error when the cloud provider cannot process the expedited request.
curl_http_rpc_executor.cc:226] Response for the failed RPC: 9173 is {"code":"InsufficientCapacityException","message":"There is insufficient capacity to process this Expedited request.","type":"Server"}
6. Go to Downloaded Jobs on the CloudRetrieve page and choose an action to perform from the actions menu.

About Failover Ready

About Failover Ready
The state of a Protection Group protecting VMs can be "Failover Ready" for any of the following reasons:
l When you create a Protection Group on a Cohesity cluster with a replication schedule after the first snapshot is replicated, a Failover Ready copy of the Protection Group is created on the remote Cohesity cluster that is receiving the snapshot.

l When an active Protection Group is deactivated ( ), the Protection Group becomes Inactive and the selected VMs and Policy are still associated with the Protection Group.
Warning: Cohesity recommends only deactivating a Protection Group as part of the failover process made possible by replication. Deactivate the original Protection Group running on the Cluster that captured the Snapshots before the failover and restoration of the Protection Group on the remote Cluster receiving the Snapshots. For more information, see Deactivate Original VM Protection Group and Failover from Replicated Copies.

l When the Protection Group meta-data is downloaded during CloudRetrieve, metadata for the specified range is fetched and indexed. After the Protection Groups in this range are indexed, they are listed as Inactive Protection Groups on the Manage

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 25: Disaster Recovery Protection Groups page.

Disaster Recovery Using CloudEdition

Note: Only Protection Groups that are protecting VMs can be deactivated. Protection Groups that are protecting a view cannot be deactivated.

Maintenance Mode
With your Cohesity cluster, you can easily enable Maintenance mode for registered sources. Enabling Maintenance mode for your Cohesity cluster's registered source will skip any scheduled activities or manually initiated operations, such as protection runs, restores, and upgrades. Ongoing backups will be canceled, but ongoing restores will continue without any interruptions.
Note: You can only apply the maintenance mode at the level at which you registered it with the Cohesity cluster. For example, if you registered a vCenter, the entire vCenter will be put into maintenance mode. You won't be able to place individual ESXi hosts or VMs within that vCenter exclusively into maintenance mode.
To place a registered source in maintenance mode:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. From the Action Menu ( ) of the source, select Maintenance.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

The Start Maintenance Now dialog displays the list of Protection Groups available in that source. b. Review the list of Protection Groups and enter yes to confirm. c. Optionally, you can enter a note. d. Click Confirm. To schedule the maintenance mode: a. Select Schedule. b. On the Schedule Maintenance dialog, enter the start date and time and the end date and time. c. Optionally, you can enter a note. d. Click Save.

Cancel Replication and Archive Copy Tasks of a Protection Run
A Protection Group with replication and/or archive schedules creates copy tasks that copy Snapshots to remote Cohesity cluster or External Targets. You can cancel these copy tasks for a specific protection run using the Cohesity Dashboard. Here are some example scenarios when you may want to cancel copy tasks:
l A protection run takes a lot of time to complete and you want to free the resources used by Runs of this Protection Group:
1. Pause the protection run.
2. Cancel the replication and archive tasks of past Runs of this Protection Group.
l You delete a Job that is replicating or archiving Snapshots and not all of the Snapshots captured by this Job have been copied to the remote Cohesity cluster or the External Target, the Cohesity cluster continues to replicate and archive the remaining captured Snapshots even after the Job has been deleted. Before or after deleting this Job, you may want to cancel the replicate and archive tasks of existing protection runs that copy the remaining captured Snapshots.
To cancel the copy tasks of a Protection Group Run:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection.
2. From the list of Protection Groups, click on the Protection Group that has replication or archival running to view that Protection Group's details.

Delete Protection Groups, Snapshots and Objects
You can delete a Protection Group from the local Cohesity cluster where the Protection Group is running. As part of the Protection Group deletion, you can optionally delete the snapshots captured by the Protection Group. You can also delete snapshots or individual Objects for protection runs (without deleting the Protection Group) as described in Deleting Snapshots or Objects. However, the deletion of snapshots is possible only if they're not protected by the DataLock policy or if the DataLock policy has expired.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 27: Manage Protection Groups

Delete Protection Groups, Snapshots and Objects

Note: DataLock policy can be changed at any time. After you change the policy, the snapshots that were taken earlier will continue to follow the previous policy time and only the new snapshots will follow the time defined in the updated policy. This means if you've set a 15-day DataLock policy for the snapshots and you change it to 7 days, then the old snapshots, which were taken before the policy change, will continue to be protected for 15 days from the day of its creation. However, any new snapshots that are taken after the policy change will be protected for 7 days.

Protection Group Run Issues

Protection Group Run Issues
If a protection run fails, additional information may be available below:
l If backing up MS SQL Server fails with the following error: Backup task failed with error: [kGuestOperationsError]: Error while pushing the agent file, it means Cohesity was unable to push its agent file to the VM. Possible causes: VMware Tools went into a bad state, VM was not running in high performance mode.
Possible fix - Restart VMware Tools and ensure the VM is running in high performance mode.
l Lingering VSS shadows on the VM can cause backups to fail with the following error: "Backup task failed with error: [kDatabaseBackupMismatch]: Incompatible LSN numbers for..." Running vssadmin list shadows in elevated mode in the CLI of the VM encountering issues shows the VM's existing shadows.
Workaround - If no other backup apps are running on that VM, you can delete all VSS shadows using this command:
PS C:\Windows\system32> vssadmin delete shadows /All
If the previous command does not work, open DiskShadow and use this command:
DiskShadow> delete shadows all
l If you encounter SOAP errors between Cohesity cluster and VMware vSphere, refer the Knowledge Base article, Troubleshooting SOAP errors between Cohesity cluster and VMware vSphere to troubleshoot the commonly seen errors during the SOAP exchange.
l If you encounter any VSS errors in a Cohesity environment, refer the Knowledge Base article, Troubleshooting VSS issues in a Cohesity environment. These error messages generally point to an environment issue and not a Cohesity protection or recovery issue.
Add or Remove a Legal Hold to a Snapshot
Users who are assigned the Data Security role can put a legal hold on existing Snapshots to preserve them for legal purposes. Legal hold Snapshots cannot be deleted until the legal hold is removed. Legal hold can be added to unlocked and DataLocked Snapshots. Cohesity recommends that their data security user enable Legal Hold for business-critical workloads after a ransomware attack is confirmed.
You can add a legal hold to Backup, Replication, and Archival targets in the protection run or individual objects in a protection run:
l If you add a legal hold to a protection run, it applies to all the Snapshot objects that were backed up by that protection run.
l You must manage the legal hold status on the remote replication Cluster manually.

Failover a Protection Group

When a Protection Group with a replication schedule starts replicating snapshots from a primary Cohesity cluster to a remote Cohesity cluster, a Protection Group in Failover Ready state is created on the remote Cohesity cluster. If the original capturing Cohesity cluster and/or the original Source are down because there is a planned maintenance outage or a disaster destroys them, you can failover the Protection Group in Failover Ready state and deactivate the original task on the capturing Cohesity cluster. As part of the Failover, you are prompted to optionally recover the VMs from the replicated snapshots stored on the remote Cohesity cluster.
Note: When you create a Protection Group on a Cohesity cluster with a replication schedule after the first snapshot is replicated, a Failover Ready copy of the Protection Group is created on the remote Cohesity cluster that is receiving the snapshot. For more information on Failover Ready, see About Failover Ready. You can failover the Protection Group of VMs. You cannot failover the Protection Group of Views or SQL Servers. You can, however, clone replicated Views and restore SQL Servers. For more information, see Failover a Protection Group.
During Failover, the following actions occur:
1. Disaster at Source - On the primary Cohesity cluster, the backup job fails to capture the snapshots of the source.
2. Replication Fails - As the source is down or unreachable, the replication job fails to replicate the snapshots onto the remote Cohesity cluster. The Failover Ready for VMs on the remote Cohesity cluster is activated and causes the rejection of the incoming replicated snapshots created by the associated job on the primary Cohesity cluster.
3. Failover VMs - You are prompted to optionally recover the VMs from the replicated snapshots on the remote Cohesity cluster to a new source.
The state of a Protection Group may also become "Failover Ready" when an active Protection Group is deactivated. For more information, see About Failover Ready. For more information about what happens during a Failover, see Failover from Replicated Copies. For more information on disaster recovery of VMs using the Cohesity Cloud Edition, see Back Up VMs to On-Prem, Replicate and Failover to AWS Cloud. To Failover a Protection Group on the remote Cluster:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Protection. 2. Find the Protection Group in the Failover Ready state in the list, click on the actions
menu , and select Failover.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 27: Manage Protection Groups

Recovery.

Cohesity Dashboard does not automatically deactivate the original task on the original cluster that captured the snapshots. To deactivate, you must follow the instructions in Deactivate Original VM Protection Group 7. Restore VM Protection Group to Running. The Failover of the Protection Group in the Cohesity Dashboard does not automatically restore the task to running on the new cluster. Deactivate Original VM Protection Group
Only Protection Groups that are protecting VMs can be deactivated. Protection Groups that are protecting a view cannot be deactivated.
Note: If possible, deactivate the original Protection Group on the original capturing Cohesity cluster. If the original Cohesity cluster that captured the Snapshots is down or unreachable, you may be unable to deactivate the Protection Group.
The example below shows the deactivation of a Protection Group protecting VMs. Deactivating a Protection Group protecting SQL Servers is similar but not all details are the same. For example, the transaction logs are not described or pictured. During deactivation, the following actions occur:
1. Snapshots are no longer captured by the original Protection Group on the original capturing Cohesity cluster. However, the existing snapshots captured by the Protection Group remain in the storage domain. They are not deleted.
2. Snapshots created by the Protection Group are no longer replicated to the receiving (remote) Cohesity cluster. (If you have already initiated the failover procedure, the replication has already stopped.)
3. You can optionally choose that the VMs on the original source be powered off. The VMs and the VM files, however, are not deleted. (The Cohesity cluster may be unable to power off the VMs if the original source is down or unreachable.)

You can optionally use the Wildcard * in any location in the search string. The following table shows some example searches.

Description
Note that this search does not find: vol1/usr/memtest.ext
When searching for file extensions, do not enter the period in the search string. For example if searching for all files that end in the .txt extension, enter *txt and not *.txt.

Description
Enter search* *xml with a space and not search*xml. However, when you add spaces between search terms, only files that match all the search terms are found, for example searching with the string: search* *xml does not find: usr/searchplugins Entering just search does not find usr/searchplugins/dsl.xml.
Only files that match all the search terms are found.

Note: Ensure to follow the standard regular expression rules. Specify a dot '.' before asterisk '*' to match all characters, for example, L:.*.ndf.

Cancel a Recovery
The recovery of any objects that have not yet been recovered is canceled. Note the following:
l Canceling a recovery might require some manual cleanup. For example, if you cancel a folder recovery, any files copied prior to the cancellation will not be deleted.
l When canceling a VMware VM recovery, the cancellation will occur after the VM is created, the datastore is mounted and the Storage vMotion migration process begins. You will need to manually clean up the VM that was created and unmount the datastore.
Cancel a Running Recovery
1. In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Data Protection > Recoveries. 2. Click the recover task you want to cancel. The task details page is displayed. 3. Click Cancel in the upper right corner of the details page. 4. Respond to the confirmation prompt.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 29: Cohesity Agents
Data protection is paramount in today's complex IT environments, whether for physical servers, virtualized infrastructure, or databases. Cohesity provides a comprehensive solution to safeguard data across different systems using specialized software components known as agents. These agents are crucial in streamlining the data protection process across various platforms, ensuring smooth backup and recovery operations tailored to each environment.
What are Cohesity Agents?
Cohesity agents are lightweight software applications installed on target machines running supported operating systems--whether to protect physical servers, virtual environments, or databases. In particular, when Cohesity agents are used to protect filesystem data, they are referred to as Cohesity Physical Agents. Once installed, these agents enable the Cohesity platform to manage backup and recovery through block-based or file-based Protection Groups. These Protection Groups determine how data is protected, while the agents facilitate interaction between the Cohesity cluster and the protected workloads. The Physical agents also contain modules to protect other data, such as MS SQL databases. Additionally, the agents protect other workloads, such as SAP HANA, in conjunction with other Cohesity modules described in the documentation for the respective integrations.
What Do Cohesity Agents Do?
The core purpose of Cohesity agents is to enable seamless data protection by performing key tasks specific to the environment in which they are deployed:
l Backup and Recovery: Agents handle the backup of system, application, and database data, securely storing it within the Cohesity platform for fast recovery when needed.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 29: Cohesity Agents

Cohesity Agents Deployment in Different Scenarios

l Block-Based or File-Based Protection: The Cohesity cluster can support blockbased and file-based backups, depending on the type of agent and the system it protects.
l Application Consistency: Cohesity agents capture application-consistent backups for critical workloads like databases, ensuring data is protected without the risk of corruption.
l Data Management: Agents manage the scheduling, execution, and monitoring of backups, integrating with the Cohesity platform for centralized control and reporting.
l Efficiency: Using technologies such as deduplication and compression, agents optimize data transmission, reducing storage consumption and bandwidth usage.
Cohesity Agents Deployment in Different Scenarios
Physical Server Environments
In physical environments, Cohesity Agents are installed directly onto the operating system. These agents ensure that all critical data from the server, including file systems, applications, and system state, is fully protected. Administrators can use block-based or file-based Protection Groups to define backup schedules and policies depending on the system's configuration. This is particularly useful for traditional systems or workloads that are not virtualized, as the agents protect the entire physical infrastructure. It is important to note that nothing precludes the agents from being used inside virtual environments, which are described in the next section.
Virtual Environments
In virtualized environments, such as VMware or Hyper-V, Cohesity supports both agentless and agent-based protection. When using agents, they are typically installed on virtual machines (VMs) requiring more granular control over backup operations, such as specific applications or critical data. Cohesity can also perform agentless protection by interacting with the hypervisor directly, to allow for better management of workloads at scale. In cases where the agent-based approach makes sense, the Cohesity agent ensures that the VM and its underlying applications are backed up in an application-consistent manner, providing the option for individual VM restores or more complex recovery scenarios.
Databases
Cohesity offers specialized agents for database environments, particularly for SQL Server, Oracle, and other enterprise databases. These agents are designed to work closely with database applications to ensure consistent and reliable backups. For example:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 29: Cohesity Agents

Install and Manage Cohesity Agents

l SQL Server: The agent interfaces with the SQL Server application to take application-consistent snapshots, enabling log truncation, point-in-time recovery, and rapid restoration of databases.
l Oracle Databases: Similarly, the Cohesity agent integrates with Oracle RMAN (Recovery Manager) to perform both full and incremental backups, ensuring fast recovery and minimal impact on performance.
For databases, ensuring data consistency is critical. Cohesity agents allow administrators to leverage granular control over backup policies, ensuring that the databases can be restored to a specific state without loss of data integrity. In summary, Cohesity agents are versatile tools designed to protect data in Physical, Virtual, and Database environments. They are essential for enabling tailored data protection strategies, ensuring that regardless of the infrastructure, backups are consistent, efficient, and easily recoverable. Whether protecting a traditional physical server, a modern virtual environment, or an enterprise-grade database, Cohesity agents provide the backbone for robust, reliable data protection.
Install and Manage Cohesity Agents
Installing the Cohesity Agent is required to protect physical servers and some hypervisor environments. The following topics discuss Agent installation and management.

Because of weaknesses in the SHA-1 algorithm and to align to industry standards, starting from the Cohesity version 6.7 onwards, sha1 signing of Cohesity artifacts is dropped. Windows Agent installer which was previously signed with sha1 and sha256 hashing algorithms is now signed with only sha256 algorithm. Due to this, legacy OS users will notice the following warning when installing the Cohesity Windows agent.

To avoid this warning, install sha2 code signing support on the system where you are installing the agent.
Note: This is only a warning, and you can click Run to continue with the installation.

Installing this component requires a reboot. Without a reboot, only full backups can be performed. Silently Install the Cohesity Agent on Windows Physical Servers
You can install the Windows Cohesity agent on multiple Windows servers by running the following command in an Administrator CMD shell or Administrator PowerShell. (The servers must have access to the agent file.)
<InstallerExeFile> [/type=<onlyagent|volcbt|fscbt|allcbt>] [/log="<absolute-path-to-log-file>"] [/dir="<absolute-path-to-installlocation>"] [/username=<value> [/password=<value>]] [/verysilent] [/suppressmsgboxes] [/norestart] [/firewallrule=<value>] [/configfile <value>] /deleteconfigfile <value>] [/enforceusecustomcert=<value>] [/cohesitycustomcertpath=<Value>] The default name for <InstallerExeFile> is Cohesity_Agent_<Version>_Win_x64_ Installer.exe. A sample command is shown below:
Cohesity_Agent_5.0.0.0_Win_x64_Installer.exe /log="C:\logs\install logs.txt" /verysilent /suppressmsgboxes /norestart /dir="F:\CohesityAgent"
The command parameters are described below.

Parameter
/type=<onlyagent|fscbt|allcbt|volcbt |onlyagent|volcbtwithsbt|fscbtwithsbt |agentwithsbt>

Description
Specifies the type of installation.
l volcbt - Installs the Windows Agent Service and Volume CBT component.
l fscbt - Installs the Windows Agent Service and File System CBT component. This parameter enables incremental backups of Windows Server 2012 R2 or individual databases hosted by MS SQL Server.
l allcbt - Installs the Windows Agent Service, Volume CBT component and File System CBT component. This parameter enables incremental backups of Windows Server 2012 R2 or individual databases hosted by MS SQL Server.
l onlyagent - Installs only the Windows Agent Service and not the Volume CBT or File System CBT components.
l onlyagent- Installs only the Windows Agent Service and not the Volume CBT or File System CBT components.
l volcbtwithsbt- Agent, Volume CBT and Oracle SBT Library
l fscbtwithsbt- Agent, File System CBT and Oracle SBT Library
l allcbtwithsbt- Agent, File System CBT, Volume CBT and Oracle SBT Library
l agentwithsbt- Agent and Oracle SBT Library

Note: The /type parameter is supported only for a fresh installation. It is not supported for upgrades. You cannot add or remove components during an upgrade.

/log="<absolute-path-to-log-file>"

Note: If the volcbt parameter is not specified, volume based backups will always be full. Similarly, if the fscbt parameter is not specified, SQL and exchange file based backups will be full.

Download and Install the Agent on Hyper-V Hosts
Ensure you install the Cohesity agent on any Hyper-V hosts that you want Cohesity to protect.
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click Download Cohesity Agent. Ensure the agent has been downloaded to the
appropriate hosts. 3. As an administrator with local system privileges, run the executable and complete the
installation wizard. For Hyper-V 2016 servers, install the agent without additional components. For incremental backups of individual VMs hosted by Hyper-V on Windows Server 2012 R2, install the File System CBT (Changed Block Tracker) component. 4. The agent starts automatically.
Guest Windows VM minimum recommended specifications: 2 GB RAM and the equivalent of a 1 GHz processor. Best practice: For Hyper-V 2016, configure all VMs' Automatic Stop Action to shut down or turn off, instead of save. This results in all powered-on VMs having minimal size .vmrs files. Because Cohesity does not back up .vmrs files that are greater than 10 MB (.vmrs file size, if set to save, scales to the amount of memory assigned to the VM). VMs in the saved state, by definition, generally have .vmrs files greater than 10 MB. This Cohesity Windows Agent registry value entry determines the maximum size of the .vmrs file supported per backup: agent_hyperv_max_vm_config_file_size_mb. Set it to zero to back up .vmrs files of all sizes.

Auto-upgrade of the Cohesity Windows Agent
Cohesity upgrade process supports auto-upgrade of the agents running on sources.

Uninstall the Agent
The following uninstallation methods are available: l Use the Add/Remove Programs in the Control Panel and Start Menu shortcuts in Windows versions where it is supported. l Use the uninstaller executable. The details of the uninstaller executable are available in the registry value "HKEY_LOCAL_ MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\{992469860300-4B21-9A1C-DE278D8EC715}_is1\UninstallString". The default value is "C:\Program Files\Cohesity\Installer\unins000.exe", assuming C: is the default operating system installation volume and "C:\Program Files\Cohesity" is the default Cohesity Agent install location.
Preserve registry settings when uninstalling the agent Uninstalling the Cohesity agent normally clears registration settings from the registry. You can preserve registration settings in the registry by using the /preservesettings flag when uninstalling from the command line. Preserving registry settings is not supported when uninstalling from the UI. Sample command: unins000.exe /preservesettings

Action
Install the agent as nonroot user

How to
To start the service as a non-root user, create a new user or use an existing user with sudo permission and run the following command:
l RPM: export COHESITYUSER=<username> ; rpm -i el-cohesity-agent7.4.1-1.x86_64
l Debian: COHESITYUSER=<username> dpkg -i cohesity-agent_7.4.1-1_amd64 l SUSE RPM: export COHESITYUSER=<username> rpm -i cohesity-agent-
7.4.1-1.x86_64 Where, <username> is the user name with sudo permission.

Note: By default, the installation uses the root user permission for all the files, and the service is started as root. Therefore, it is required to add non-root users to the sudoers list by making the following changes in the /etc/sudoers file:
<user_name> ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL
Defaults:<user_name> !requiretty

An example of the sudoers file is as given below:

dgoble ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL
Defaults:dgoble !requiretty cohbackup ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL Defaults:cohbackup !requiretty

How to

Note: You can add sudo privileges for non-root users using the syntax given below:
<user_name> ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:/path/to/command1, /path/to/command2, /path/to/command3
Remove NOPASSWD from the command above if you do not want to authenticate every sudo commands with password.

Agent Installation User type

Action required

As default cohesityagent user

The Cohesity Linux agent is installed using the cohesityagent user by default. For default installations, the cohesityagent is created by the installer. cohesityagent ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL Defaults:cohesityagent !requiretty

#includedir /etc/sudoers.d dgoble ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL cohbackup ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL Defaults:cohbackup !requiretty

Linux Script Installer Options
The Cohesity Linux agent installer has the following options available.

Option

Description

--agentoptions, -a [options]

Options to pass to the Cohesity agent. Used with single mode operation only.

--createuser, -c [0|1]

Whether to create --service-user or not. [Default: 1] Used with --install option only.

--debug, -d

Enable shell script debugging with set -x [Default: off]

--fulluninstall, -U

Uninstall the Cohesity Linux agent including service-user account and its home directory contents. Destructive operation. Use with care.

--help, -h

Print this help.

--install, -i Install/uninstall the Cohesity Linux agent.

--installdir, -I [dir]

Cohesity agent installation dir. [Default: /home/<username>/cohesityagent or /root/cohesityagent]

--installlog-file, -L [file]

Filename where installer logs should be saved. [Default: /tmp/cohesity_agent_installer_<time_in_ seconds>_<pid>.log]

--log-dir

Cohesity agent log installation directory. [Default: /home/cohesityagent/cohesityagent/logs]

--servicegroup, -G [group]

Groupname to use for service. [Default: cohesityagent]

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 29: Cohesity Agents

Install and Manage the Agent on Linux Servers

Option --serviceuser, -S [user] --singlemode, -s
--skip-lvmcheck

Description
Username to use for service. [Default: cohesityagent]
Install the Cohesity Linux agent for single mode operation. This installs the agent for one time usage/run only. It does not install the Agent to run as service or daemon to run continuously. This copies all required binaries/files to a location and runs the agent. Example use case: You want to recover files to a Linux VM. Cohesity pushes the Cohesity agent and starts it. After performing the usual file/folder recovery by talking to Cohesity Agent and file copying is done, the Agent is removed. The agent is not installed to run as service. It runs for the duration of the recover task only.
1 - Skip LVM related checks during installation and start the agent in non-lvm mode (only file-based backup will be supported). 0 - Flag is not set.
Note: The default value is 0.

--skipmountpointcheck

Skip checks performed on installation directory's filesystem mountpoint.

--target

Extract directly to a target directory. Directory path can be either absolute or relative. [Default: /tmp]

--updateuninstall, -u

Uninstall the Cohesity Linux agent. Preserve user, group and agent config. Useful when upgrading software.

--yes-all, -y

Accept 'yes' answer to all questions in installer. [Default: off] This is useful for performing silent install/uninstall.

Install the Cohesity Agent to run with the Root User
Follow the steps below to install the Cohesity agent to run with the root user:
Note: In the following command, replace the Cohesity agent version with the desired agent version.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 29: Cohesity Agents

Install and Manage the Agent on Linux Servers

For example, run the following command: sudo ./cohesity_agent_7.4.1_linux_x64_ installer -- --install -S root -G root -c 0 -I /opt -y
The above example does the following:
l -S root -G root sets user "root:root" user:group for the agent. l -c 0 instructs the installer that user root already exists on the system, so do not
create it. l -I /opt installs the agent in the /opt directory. If you do not specify the directory,
then the default home directory of the user will be used, /root/ in this case.

Sudo Privileges for Linux Users
The Linux system administrator can allowlist set of commands that do not need the root rights to be executed from the Cohesity agent deployed on the Linux servers.
The following tables list the commands that can be allowlisted for Oracle database, volume backups, and file restores for the Cohesity agent.
Oracle Database

Argument
--skip-oraclecheck

Default Behavior
The default value is 0. We will allowlist commands required by Oracle database.

If set to 1, we will not add any commands to the allowlist.

Allowlist Commands
mkdir rm tee stat cp srvctl (from Oracle home)

Volume Backup

Argument
--skip-lvmcheck

Default Behavior
The default value is 0. We will allowlist commands required by volume backup.
If set to 1, we will not add any commands to the allowlist.

Allowlist Commands
lvs vgs lvcreate vgcreate

File Restore

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 29: Cohesity Agents

Install and Manage the Agent on Linux Servers

Argument
--skip-restorecheck

Default Behavior The default value is 0. We will allowlist commands required by file restore.
If set to 1, we will not add any commands to the allowlist.

Allowlist Commands
blkid lsof ls losetup dmsetup rsync timeout

Note: During a Linux agent upgrade: If NOPASSWD:ALL entry is present in the sudoers file, then all commands can be executed without the root rights. If NOPASSWD:ALL entry is removed from the sudoers file, then you can add the commands listed in the table above for allowlisting.

Upgrade from the Cohesity UI
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources.
2. Click Download Cohesity Agent.
3. Stop the Agent service on the server.
4. Click Upgrade Agents. 5. Restart the Agent service.

Upgrade using CLI
1. Navigate to the Agent installation directory. 2. Run the following command to install the script installer package:
sudo cohesity_agent_7.4.1_linux_x64_installer -- -install 3. Run the following command to install the RPM package: rpm -U el-cohesity-agent-7.4.1-1.x86_64.rpm 4. Run the following command to install the Debian package: dpkg -i cohesity-agent_7.4.1-1_amd64.deb 5. Run the following command to install the SUSE RPM package: rpm -U cohesity-agent-7.4.1-1.x86_64.rpm 6. Run the following command to install the PowerPC RPM package: rpm -U cohesity-java-agent-7.0.1-1.ppc64le.rpm 7. To install the Linux on z/Architecture package on Linux variants running on the x64 platform: rpm -U cohesity-java-agent-0.0.0-1.s390x.rpm 8. To install the Linux on ARM (aarch64) package on Linux variants running on the x64 platform: rpm -U cohesity-java-agent-7.3.1-1.aarch64.rpm

Auto-upgrade of the Cohesity Linux Agent
Cohesity supports auto-upgrade of the Cohesity Linux Agent running on physical servers.
Note: The option to auto-upgrade Cohesity Agent is not available on the Cohesity cluster with multi-tenancy configured.
To enable auto-upgrade: 1. Navigate to Settings > Update, and select Upgrade tab. 2. Select the Upgrade Cohesity Agent on all servers in Sources checkbox.

Install and Manage the Agent on Hyper-V Linux VMs
To allow file-level recovery to a guest Linux VM running on Hyper-V, the guest VM must have the following installed:
l Cohesity Linux Agent l Linux Integration Services l Ubuntu l CentOS or RHEL
Limitations
l Efficient file-level recovery does not support recovering from multiple Linux volumes.
Free Space Requirement for block-based Backup
For each virtual machine backup, you'll need free space on the volume hosting the virtual hard disk files to allow Hyper-V enough room for differencing disks (AVHDs) during backup. The space must be at least equal to the calculation Initial disk size*Churn rate*Backup window time. If you're running multiple backups on a cluster, you'll need enough storage capacity to accommodate the AVHDs for each of the virtual machines using this calculation.

Follow these steps to download and install the agent. 1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click Download Cohesity Agent. The Download Agents window appears.

Minimum Permissions
Ensure you have the following permissions for deploying the Cohesity agent.
For Windows server
For deploying the Windows agent, you can either use the LOCAL SYSTEM account or an account that meets the following requirements to install the Cohesity agent:
l The account must be a member of the local Windows Administrators group. For example, qa01\tme-backup is an Active Directory user account in the data center. If the backup admin plans to use this account, qa01\tme-backup must be part of the local Windows Administrators group on the Windows server.
l The account must have Log on as a service in the User Rights Assignment on the Windows server to deploy the Cohesity agent.
For Linux Server
If you are deploying the Linux agent using an existing user, the user must have sudo permission. For sudo permission, you must add the user to the sudoers list by making the following changes in the /etc/sudoers file: <user_name> ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL
Defaults:<user_name> !requiretty

To deploy the Cohesity agent on multiple physical servers having different credentials:
1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources. 2. Click the plus icon on the top-right of the page and then select Deploy Cohesity
Agent. The Deploy Cohesity agent page appears. 3. From the Deploy Cohesity agent page, select Upload CSV as the option to deploy Cohesity agent. 4. Click Download sample file and download the CSV sample file to know the information and format in which the input must be provided in the CSV file. The following is the format in which the input must be provided in the CSV file:
#IP/Hostname,OS Type,Server Username,Server Password,Install Location,Volume CBT,File CBT,Service Account Username,Service Account Password,SSH Key,
Where, l IP/Hostname: The IP address or a valid hostname on which the Cohesity agent needs to be deployed. l OS type: The operating system of the server. l Server Username and Server Password: Credentials of the server on which the Cohesity agent needs to be deployed. l Install Location: (Optional) The path where the Cohesity agent must be deployed. If left blank, then the agent will be installed in the default location. l Volume CBT : (Optional) Applicable only for Windows OS types. If set to TRUE, the volume CBT driver will be installed. This field is ignored for non-Windows OS types. l File CBT: (Optional) Applicable only for Windows OS types. If set to TRUE, the file CBT driver will be installed. This field is ignored for non-Windows OS types. l Service Account Username and Service Account Password: (Optional) Credentials to register Cohesity agent as a service account. l SSH Key: (Optional) Use the SSH key to authenticate the server to deploy the Cohesity agent.
For example:

l #10.0.0.1,linux,admin,test_password,/var/agent_location/,,,,,, l #10.0.0.2,windows,admin,test_password,C:\\Program
Files\,,,service_admin,service_password,,
Note: l Each entry should end with a comma. l If no value is to be given for an optional field, it should be left blank between separating commas.
5. Click Browse to upload a CSV file and upload the CSV file in the format provided in the sample file.
6. Click Select. Cohesity will initiate the Cohesity agent deployment on the physical servers. You can view the status by clicking the notification icon on the top-right corner of the Source page.
Deploy Cohesity Agent on Virtual Servers
By deploying the Cohesity agent on a virtual machine, you can: l Perform efficient file-level recovery. l Protect VMs as physical servers. l Protect the applications running on the VMs.
This topic provides information on how to deploy the Cohesity agent on virtual machines from the Cohesity UI. Plan and Prepare Before you deploy the Cohesity agent on a virtual server, ensure the following prerequisites:
l The required firewall ports are open to enable communication between the Cohesity cluster and the physical server.
l Minimum permission required to deploy the Cohesity agent. l Disable the Windows UAC. l Understand the considerations. l VMware tool is installed and running on the VMs of the virtual server.
Ports Used for Communication
For deploying the Cohesity agent on a virtual server, port 50051 must be open.

Minimum Permissions
l The user account that is used for auto-deploying agents in a Windows VMware environment must have administrator privileges on the VM where the agent is deployed. The account must have the "sysadmin" Server Role if the virtual server has SQL Server installed.
l If Windows firewall is used, add an inbound rule to accept the Cohesity agent and TCP connections on local port 50051.
l The user account that is used for file recovery to a Windows VM must have administrator privileges on the target VM. The account must have the "sysadmin" Server Role if the virtual server has SQL Server installed.

Troubleshoot Cohesity Agent

Registering a Cohesity Agent on a new Cohesity cluster fails with the following error:
Host is already registered with another cluster: <old cluster-id>, <new cluster-id>

Agent is already registered to a different Cohesity cluster ID.

Installing or upgrading the Cohesity Agent either manually or automatically fails with the following error: WinHttpSendRequest() failed : 0x2ee7

This error indicates a DNS issue in Windows. While installing the Cohesity Agent, the Agent confirms that it can resolve the host name of the Cohesity cluster. If this check fails, this error is returned.

1. Navigate to Data Protection > Sources > Register > Physical Server.
2. cluster_ fqdn/protection/sources/new/physical ?forceRegister=true" to the end of the URL and press the Enter key. You will be redirected to a new registration page.
3. Enter the Agent information and ensure that the Force Agent Registration check box is selected.
Ensure DNS forward and reverse lookups are working on the server or VM.

Login to the Cohesity Support site to see more Knowledge Base Articles.

Upgrading the Cohesity Agent on a Windows Physical Server may Become Stuck
Under specific conditions, upgrading the Cohesity agent on a Windows physical server may become stuck. To identify if a server is affected by this issue, read the following:
Check if the agent logs (under %programdata%\Cohesity) contain "Cannot start the agent because the port 50051 is in use," indicating that the agent is in a crash loop.
The upgrade issue can occur if all of the following are true:
l The Cohesity agent is running under a specific user account (not the default Local System account).
l The Cohesity agent service is the only service in the running state at the time of upgrade using the specified account. l The specified user account has not been logged into through other means (such as RDP) at the time of the upgrade.
l The "Do not forcefully unload the user registry at user logoff" policy is "Not Configured" (the default) or set to "No."
To get the agent out of this state:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 29: Cohesity Agents

Troubleshoot Cohesity Agent

1. Open Windows Task Manager and click the Details tab. 2. Locate the "installer.exe" and "installer.tmp" processes (with the Cohesity icon). 3. Right-click "installer.tmp" and select "End Task". This stops both processes
("installer.exe" and "installer.tmp").
To avoid future occurrences: Use the Group Policy Editor (gpedit.msc) to enable the "Do not forcefully unload the user registry at user logoff" policy. The policy is located under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > User Profiles.

Chapter 30: NoSQL and Hadoop Service

NoSQL and Hadoop Service is an enterprise data management solution to protect Hadoop clusters and NoSQL distributed databases on a single web-scale platform. The NoSQL and Hadoop Service expands Cohesity's DataProtect coverage to support protection for Couchbase, MongoDB, Cassandra, Hbase, Hive, HDFS, all managed through a single policy framework and global user interface. Features

Application Cassandra Couchbase MongoDB Hadoop

Details See Supported Versions for Cassandra DataProtect Solution. See Supported Versions for Couchbase DataProtect Solution. See Supported Versions for MongoDB DataProtect Solution. See Supported Versions for Hadoop DataProtect Solution.

Features
l Supports protection of NoSQL databases such as Couchbase, MongoDB, Cassandra, and Hadoop (HDFS, Hive, and Hbase).
l Scalable backup and recovery architecture supporting petabytes of data. l Meet business RPOs/RTOs with parallel architecture to support rapid backup and
recovery. l Supports a simple agentless deployment. l Offers a unified and automated policy-driven model involving no manual steps. l Supports a flexible backup and recovery method from a database to a table or a
collection level. l Offers incremental forever backup. l Recovery is topology-independent. l Improved data resiliency with erasure coding. l Reduced data footprint with global variable-length deduplication, compression. l Native cloud integrations for simplified archival to the public cloud for long-term
retention. l One-click archival to public cloud for long term retention using native cloud
integrations. l An API-first architecture approach with RESTful API support. l Integration with Active Directory, LDAP, and Kerberos. l Encryption of data in-flight and at rest. l Customizable role-based access control. l Supports protection of NoSQL databases such as Cassandra and Couchbase
configured using IPv6 addresses.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 30: NoSQL and Hadoop Service

Prerequisites

Prerequisites
l The NoSQL and Hadoop service is designed to handle petabytes of data efficiently by scaling out to perform parallel backups and restores. As a result, the services require a higher amount of CPU and memory depending on the RPO & RTO needs. Compute Nodes in the Cohesity cluster provide CPU and memory resources to run resourceintensive apps and services. In order to install the NoSQL and Hadoop service, the Cohesity cluster must have compute nodes added. See Manage Compute Nodes for details.
l Data and Compute nodes on the Cohesity cluster must have connectivity to all the primary cluster nodes of your data source (Hadoop cluster nodes or Cassandra cluster nodes or MongoDB cluster nodes) for successful discovery, backup and recovery.
l For more information on managing apps and the prerequisites for apps management, see Manage Apps .
Process Overview
A quick overview of the process is as follows:

1. To use NoSQL and Hadoop service, you must first add a compute node. 2. Download the NoSQL and Hadoop Service from Helios, and Run App. 3. Configure the QoS Policy and Instant Size based on the business requirement and
run the application.
4. Ensure that the advanced configuration settings are enabled for NoSQL and Hadoop solutions. Contact Cohesity Support to enable this capability.

Run the NoSQL and Hadoop Service
1. Log in to the Cohesity cluster, and navigate to Marketplace > My Apps > My Apps tab.
2. If the app upload is successful, the NoSQL & Hadoop Service App is listed and the Run App button appears.
3. Click Run App to start running the app instance on your cluster.
Note: You can run only one instance of the app per cluster.
4. Based on the requirement, select QoS Policy, Views, and Instant Size. Enter a brief description (optional) and click Run App. An instance of the app will be initiated.

Parameters QoS Policy

Description
This decides how much % of resources of compute nodes are allocated to the NoSQL and Hadoop service.
Note: l You can set this value as Max if this is the only app instance running on your cluster. However, if you wish to use other apps at the same time, you can set a lower QoS policy. l Max QoS allows 80% of total allocatable resources for NoSQL App. l High QoS allows 50% of total allocatable resources for NoSQL App. l It is recommended that you allow maximum QoS for NoSQL app for better performance.

Description
This indicates the size of the container. It is recommended to use a large instance size. Each instance of nodemanager container will be of size
l 16GB/4core (small) l 32GB/8core (medium) l 40GB/10core (large) App nodes (compute only nodes) should have enough resources to fit at least 3 small instances of nodemanagers.
