Job Type
All

Error Codes kInvalid kUnsupported
kDisabled kIneligible kCancelled kPending kTransportError kTimeout kRejected

Description
The alert with the error code is raised when the snapshot on the primary Cohesity cluster is deleted before the Cohesity cluster can replicate the snapshot to the remote cluster.
The alert with the error code is raised when: l An older version of the Cohesity software is running on the remote cluster. l The remote cluster does not support the workload that is being replicated. l The remote cluster does not support cascaded replication, and you attempt to perform cascaded replication.
The alert with the error code is raised for Azure or AWS native workloads if their disaster recovery failback support is disabled
The alert with the error code is raised when no objects are copied to the remote cluster.
The alert with the error code is raised when replication is canceled on the source Cohesity cluster.
The alert with the error code is raised when an attempt to perform replication fails. After a backoff, the replication is retried.
The alert with the error code is raised when the RPC to the remote cluster to initiate replication fails.
The alert with the error code is raised when the RPC to the remote cluster to initiate replication timed out.
The alert with the error code is raised when the remote cluster rejects the replication request. This scenario can happen if the remote cluster has been rebuilt recently.

Upgrade Alerts
CE03301003 UpgradeFailed
Alert Description: Upgrade failure. Reason: This alert is triggered when an upgrade fails and is aborted. This is triggered once per failed upgrade. After the Cohesity cluster upgrade is initiated, if the first node is unable to download the upgrade package and install, then the upgrade is marked as failed and aborted. Downloading the upgrade package may fail for a number of reasons such as network failures, download checksum mismatch, or mismatched versions. Action: Investigate why the upgrade failed. After correcting any invalid input, initiate the upgrade again using the Cohesity UI or Cohesity CLI. Related Error Code:

Error Codes KUpgradeSoftwareDownloadError KUpgradeHealthCheckError KUpgradeDiskMarkedForRemoval KUpgradeFeatureCompatabilityError

Description
The alert with the error code is raised when the Cohesity cluster cannot download the upgrade package.
The alert with the error code is raised when the Cohesity cluster state is not healthy.
The alert with the error code is raised when a disk in the Cohesity cluster is marked for removal and the upgrade fails.
The alert with this error code is raised when the existing version's features matrix is incompatible with the upgrade version.

Fault Tolerance Alerts
CE03915005 MetadataCannotTolerateAnymoreFailures
Alert Description: Metadata fault tolerance level has been reached. Autohealing from an additional failure will not be possible. Reason: This alert is triggered when automatic healing of failed Nodes is stalled and any more failures would result in unavailability and possible data loss. This alert is triggered daily. The metadata server cannot tolerate any more failures because the automatic healing of failed nodes has stalled. Possible causes include an insufficient number of nodes online or a failed metadata server on available nodes. Action: Bring any failed nodes back online. Look for any metadata server failed Alerts and resolve them. If the problem persists, contact Cohesity Support. Related Error Code: Not Applicable Severity: Warning Dedup Interval: 86400 seconds SNMP OID: 1.3.6.1.4.1.47421.0.115 Platform: All

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Health Dashboard

Reason: This alert is triggered if a metadata fault tolerance factor change is stalled. The cluster does not have enough nodes for the metadata server to achieve the configured fault tolerance factor. This alert is triggered daily. Action: Make sure there are enough nodes in the cluster to support the configured metadata fault tolerance factor. Look for any metadata server failed Alerts and resolve them. Related Error Code: Not Applicable Severity: Warning Dedup Interval: 86400 seconds SNMP OID: 1.3.6.1.4.1.47421.0.116 Platform: All
CE03902123 NodeFailureIsNotTolerated
Alert Description: The effective usage space in the cluster is high. The cluster may not have enough space to heal if a node failure happens. Reason: This alert is triggered when the Cohesity cluster detects that a potential node failure could result in an effective Cohesity cluster disk usage of 99% or greater. This alert Cause field indicates the current actual disk usage, which is typically less than 99%. If a node in the Cohesity cluster fails, its contents need to be copied to the other nodes. If the Cohesity cluster detects that the contents of a potentially failed node cannot be copied to the remaining nodes due a lack of disk space, this alert is triggered to indicate that node failures cannot be tolerated. Action: Do one or more of the following:
l Add more nodes to your Cohesity cluster. l Clean up Snapshots that are no longer required. l Archive Snapshots to an External Target. l Configure Cloud Tier to hold rarely used data. l Consider changing Storage Domains to use Erasure Coding. Capacity utilization will be
reduced over time in the background. l See the Alert: CE03902123 Cluster Space Usage High KB article.
Related Error Code: Not Applicable Severity: Informational Dedup Interval: 86400 seconds SNMP OID: 1.3.6.1.4.1.47421.0.106 Platform: All
CE03901064 LowFaultTolerantStorageDomain
Alert Description: Low fault tolerant storage domain found for the cluster.

Reports
Important: Helios Reporting supports global reporting and has an enhanced library of built-in reports. You can find equivalent reports in the new and improved Helios Reporting. Please create new schedules with the equivalent reports in Helios Reporting to start using these new features.
In today's data-driven business environment, it is more important than ever to analyze your data and identify patterns and trends that help organizations make better decisions. With reporting, Cohesity extends its built-in reporting features to give you the flexibility to produce several reports to understand cluster capacity, usage metrics and help you address your organization's specific needs most effectively. For information about how long the cluster keeps audit data, see Data Retention for Audits.
Run Reports
1. Navigate to Reporting and click Proceed to cluster Reporting. 2. Select a report from the Select Report drop-down. 3. If the Filters panel is provided for the report, you can optionally filter your results by
the options listed. Select the options and click Apply Filters.
Email Reports
You can email most reports as needed or on a recurring basis.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Reports

Note: To email reports, an email address must be specified for the local System Admin account (admin) of the Cohesity cluster. Select Settings > Access Management and if necessary, edit the local admin user to provide an email address.
1. Navigate to Reporting and click Proceed to cluster Reporting. 2. Select a report from the Select Report drop-down. 3. If the Filters panel is provided for the report, you can optionally filter your results by
the options listed. Select the options and click Apply Filters.
4. Click the Email icon ( ) and type one or more email addresses in the Email Recipients field. (Not all reports can be emailed.)
5. Select a format for the report in the Format drop-down. A CSV format report is sent as an email attachment. An HTML format report is sent in the body of the email.
6. To email the report one time, toggle Schedule Recurring Email off. To send recurring emails, select one or more days in Email Every and set the time the emails should be sent.
7. Optionally, select the Time Zone that matches your mailing schedule. 8. The current report filters are displayed. You can use them as is or modify them. 9. Click Save Schedule. If you scheduled emails, click the Scheduled Emails tab to display all scheduled emails. If you did not provide schedule information, the report is emailed immediately.
Delete a Scheduled Email
1. Navigate to Reporting and click Proceed to cluster Reporting. 2. Click the Scheduled Emails tab.
This tab lists the scheduled emails for all reports.
3. To edit a scheduled email, click the edit icon ( ) and edit the recipients, format, filters and scheduling information and then click Save Schedule.
4. To permanently delete a scheduled email, click its delete icon ( ).
Download a Report as a CSV File
For most reports, you can download the data generated for the currently displayed report as described below. (You can also schedule an email that includes the report as a CSV

Reports

attachment as described previously in this topic.)
1. Navigate to Reporting and click Proceed to cluster Reporting. 2. Select a report from the Select Report drop-down. 3. If the Filters panel is provided for the report, you can optionally filter your results by
the options listed. Select the options and click Apply Filters.
4. Click the CSV icon ( ). The file is downloaded immediately to your device.

Cohesity Reports
Cohesity provides the following reports:

Report Name

Description

Available Local Snapshots Per Job

This report provides Snapshot summary statistics for a leaf Protection Source Object (such as a VM) for all Protection Groups or a specific Protection Group.
For detailed information about this report, see Available Local Snapshots.

Agent Status Summary

This report provides information about the Cohesity Agents installed on servers registered as Sources on the Cluster.
For detailed information about this report, see Agent Status.

Understanding Storage Metrics
The Cohesity UI and reports use the following terminology to describe storage metrics:

Metrics Logical Data Data In Data Written
Storage Consumed
Resiliency Impact Storage Consumed Local and Cloud

Description
The combined total of data in the objects that are protected by Cohesity.
Total unique logical data residing in Cohesity.
Data written on the Cohesity after the unique logical data has been reduced by data deduplication and data compression.
The total size of data stored on the Cohesity file system after all operations on the data (data deduplication, data compression, and data resiliency). This data can be stored either all locally or as a combination of local storage and in the Cloud Tier (if Cloud Tier is enabled).
The space required to honor resiliency settings (Erasure Coding / Replication Factor) in addition to the data written.
Data stored locally and in the Cloud Tier (if Cloud Tier is configured) including the space required for honoring the resiliency settings (EC/RF).

Custom Reporting
The Custom Reporting feature addresses the limitations of monitoring options for historical data. This feature helps in creating custom reports to capture the information outside of the built-in reports available on the Cohesity cluster.
The Custom Reporting in Cohesity is achieved by reading the data from a Custom Database (Postgres) that stores relevant performance metrics, stats, and information of a (standalone) Cohesity cluster.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Reports

Note: l In earlier releases, there was no firewall rule for custom reporting. After upgrading to the latest version, you may encounter connection failures to the Reporting Database because, starting from version 6.8, the new firewall rule is set to deny by default.
l To use custom reporting in a Cohesity cluster, you should edit the firewall rule for Reporting Database and set it to Allow. For more information, refer to the Configure Firewall Rule section in Manage Application-Based Firewall Rules.
l The IP address of the Reporting Database may change, as it can fail over to another node in the cluster during service restarts, patching, upgrades, or similar events.
l Contact your Cohesity account team to use the Custom Reporting feature.
The users can use the third-party SQL reporting tools, such as JasperSoft, TablePlus, Orange, DevArt plugin for Excel, Microsoft SSRS / Visual Studio, and Tableau for Desktop to access the Custom Database and build reports tailored to specific business requirements.

For more information, see the Cohesity Custom Reporting Solution Guide.
Limitations
l If you change the fault tolerance values of the Postgres database in the Cohesity Dashboard (Settings > Summary > Configure), the changes are not applied to the

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Reports

Postgres database. l Data archival is not supported for the Postgres database. l Custom Reporting does not track expired snapshot data for Protection Group runs. Connecting to the Postgres Database To avoid a single point of failure, the data is replicated across the nodes in the Cohesity cluster. A service manager manages redundant Postgres databases inside the cluster. This redundancy is set during cluster configuration. The number of replicas depends on the fault tolerance of the cluster. 1. Connect to the Cohesity CLI. For more information, see Using the Cohesity CLI and
List of Cohesity CLI Commands.
Note: The Cohesity Admin user should perform the steps listed in this section.
2. Execute the following command to get the default credentials to connect to the Postgres database. iris_cli custom-reporting database
Note: The default credentials returned by the command are those generated on the cluster, not the global default.
3. Connect to the Postgres database using any third-party SQL reporting tools with the following parameters. l IP: Node IP running Postgres l Port: 27999 l Database: postgres l User: reporting_read l Password: default password from the previous step
Note: The default password of the reporting database is changed after you upgrade a Cohesity cluster to the 6.7 release. You should update the password of the reporting database in your database clients. The connection to the reporting database will be broken after the upgrade if the connection is established using the default password provided in the previous releases.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Reports

l Schema: reporting Cohesity recommends changing the password after connecting to the Postgres database.
4. To change the password, connect to the Postgres database as described below and execute the following query: alter role reporting_read with encrypted password 'new_strong_pass_ here';
Note: This changes the password for the Postgres instance on the current node.
Repeat the above 4 steps on all Postgres instances. This changes the password for the Postgres instance on the current node. Repeat these steps on all Postgres instances. Understanding the Database The users can build reports by understanding the underlying database schema. The database schema is intuitive and user-friendly. The table names and the field names in the database are straightforward and self-explanatory. Click the link below to refer to the Entity Relationship diagram and the Data Dictionary for the Custom Reporting database.

Cluster Wide Storage
This report provides Cluster storage statistics that are useful for administrators to plan out disk space utilization.
This page provides the following data use statistics about the entire local Cohesity cluster. The disk space available from External Targets is not included in the reported statistics. For example, the value reported in the Cluster Storage Capacity field does not include the disk space available in the Cloud Tier.

Field
Cluster Storage Capacity

Field Description
The amount of total disk space on the Cohesity cluster available for storage of your data such as Snapshots of Protection Groups, files and directories.

Note:
l

Storage Domain settings such as number of failures tolerated and erasure coding affect how much data can be stored on the Cluster.

l On All Flash clusters, Cohesity reserves extra space for metadata. This space is automatically made available for data (cluster capacity) if the cluster usage exceeds 90%. Due to this behavior, cluster capacity would vary when the cluster usage is 90% or exceeds 90%.

Cluster Storage Used

The amount of disk space on the Cohesity cluster currently used for storing your data such as Snapshots of Protection Groups, files and directories.

Daily Growth Rate

Daily growth rate for the Storage Consumed value.
Where Storage Consumed is the total size of data stored on the Cohesity file system after all operations on the data (data deduplication, data compression, and data resiliency) have been accounted for.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Reports

Field

Field Description

Data Reduction Ratio

The data reduction ratio is calculated by dividing the Logical Data Managed by the Physical Data Used.
Logical Data Managed--Indicates the size of the data if the data is fully hydrated or expanded. The actual physical data stored on the Cohesity cluster is reduced by change-block tracking, compression and deduplication.
Physical Data Used--The size of the data physically stored on the Cohesity cluster, after the data has been reduced by change block tracking, compression and deduplication, including the disk space used for data resiliency (fault tolerance and erasure coding).

Utilization Ratio

Ratio of Storage Consumed to Raw Cluster Capacity.
Where Storage Consumed is the total size of data stored on the Cohesity file system after all operations on the data (data deduplication, data compression, and data resiliency) have been accounted for.

Date to Exceed 80% Utilization

Based on the current daily growth rate, what is the projected date that the Cohesity cluster is expected to be 80% full.

Raw Cluster Capacity

The total physical capacity of all storage devices. This is pre-reservation of capacity for Cohesity software operations.

Minimum Usable

The total physical capacity of all storage devices after subtracting the space reserved for Cohesity software operations.

Below the list of statistics is the following chart:
Cluster Storage Used Over 7 Days--This chart graphs the physical growth of the disk space used on the Cohesity cluster over the last seven days.

Logical Data Transferred

Data Protection:
The combined total of data in the objects that are protected by Cohesity. These metrics are different depending on workload type.
l VMs: The data size reported by VMware is the provisioned amount, not the actual data residing in the VM. For example, if a VM is provisioned for 1TB but contains only 100GB of data, VMware reports it as 1TB.
l All Other Workloads: The data size reported is the actual front end data residing on the server. If a server with 1TB capacity contains 100GB of data, the server reports 100GB.

Note: - These metrics do not include unprotected objects. - Currently, the logical data value shown on the UI is a sum of the logical data values captured across all the protection runs. For instance, if the source has 100GB of logical data, and assuming it remains at 100GB for the first 10 protection runs, Cohesity would report, after 10 runs, the Logical Data to be 1000GB (1TB).

Data written to the External Target after the unique logical data has been reduced by data deduplication and data compression.

Data Protection:
The combined total of data in the objects that are protected by Cohesity. These metrics are different depending on workload type.
l VMs: The data size reported by VMware is the provisioned amount, not the actual data residing in the VM. For example, if a VM is provisioned for 1TB but contains only 100GB of data, VMware reports it as 1TB.
l All Other Workloads: The data size reported is the actual front end data residing on the server. If a server with 1TB capacity contains 100GB of data, the server reports 100GB.

Note: - These metrics do not include unprotected objects. - Currently, the logical data value shown on the UI is a sum of the logical data values captured across all the protection runs. For instance, if the source has 100GB of logical data, and assuming it remains at 100GB for the first 10 protection runs, Cohesity would report, after 10 runs, the Logical Data to be 1000GB (1TB).

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Reports

Column Name Description / Action

Variance of Logical Managed

The percentage difference between the values of Logical (total) today, and Logical (total) x days ago, where x is a user input value.

Data In

Total unique logical data residing on the Cohesity cluster.
This is the sum of your first full backup and subsequent change data captured by Cohesity as measured in units of source-side bytes.

Data Written

Data written and retained on the Cohesity cluster, as measured in post-dedupe and post-compression bytes.

Storage Consumed

The total size of data stored on the Cohesity file system, as measured in bytes after all operations on the data (data deduplication, data compression, and data resiliency) have been accounted for. This data can be stored either all locally or as a combination of local storage and in the Cloud Tier (if Cloud Tier is enabled).
For example, if the Data Written is 100GB and resiliency is set to RF3, leading to the need for an additional 200GB of space, the resulting Storage Consumed is 300GB. If the Data Written is 100GB and resiliency is set to EC4:2, leading to the need for an additional 50GB (as for every 4 data fragments, 2 parity fragments are added), the resulting Storage Consumed is 150GB.

Note: If you have enabled Cloud Tiering, then Storage Consumed is the sum of space consumed on local storage and space consumed on the cloud tier. In such cases, the sum of Storage Consumed value and Capacity Available value for the cluster can exceed the cluster capacity.

Storage Consumed (<Num> days ago)

The total size of data stored on the Cohesity file system, as measured in bytes after all operations on the data (data deduplication, data compression, and data resiliency) have been accounted for over the number of days.

Growth Rate

Shown as a percentage, the increase in "storage consumed" over the time period specified in the report's filter.

Daily Growth Rate

Daily growth rate for the Storage Consumed value over the time window specified in the report's filter.
Where Storage Consumed is the total size of data as measured in bytes stored on the Cohesity file system after all operations on the data (data deduplication, data compression, and data resiliency) have been accounted for.

Storage Reduction

The ratio of Logical Data to Storage Consumed.

As of a past date, the total size of the logical data for all the files in this Category found in the last Snapshot of this Server created by the listed Protection Group. Variance

This field shows the difference between the total logical data size for all the files in this Category found in the last Snapshot of this Server created by the listed Protection Group as of today compared to the total logical data size for all the files in this Category found in the last Snapshot of this Server created by the listed Protection Group as of a past date.
The Variance is calculated using the following formula:
( (Total Logical Data Written as of Today - Total Logical Data Written on a Past Date)/ Total Logical Data Written on a Past Date) * 100

Audit Logs
Cohesity records all events and operations occurring on your Cohesity cluster in the form of Audit Logs. An audit log contains details about an event, such as date and time, category, type, and user. Audit logs help you as a cluster administrator to monitor and analyze the events that occurred if you need to troubleshoot issues and investigate unauthorized or suspicious activities.
Note: Cohesity captures the audit logs at the cluster level and file services-level (NFS and SMB Views).

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Settings for Cluster Audit Logs
Enable or Disable Cluster Audit Logs
By default, the Cluster Auditing setting is enabled. You can disable or enable it back from the Log Settings tab of the Audit Logs page. When you disable the option, the old logs continue to retain until the retention period ends. To enable or disable cluster auditing, complete the following in the Cohesity UI:
1. Select System> Audit Logs>Log Settings. 2. In the Log Settings tab, toggle the ClusterAudit button to enable or disable. After enabling the Cluster Audit, option the Log Retention Period option appears. Using this option you can set the audit logs retention period.
Set Log Retention Period for Cluster Audit Logs
You can set the retention period for cluster audit logs. When you set a retention period, the logs are retained on the cluster until the retention period ends.
Note: The default retention period is 90 days.
To set a retention period for cluster audit logs, complete the following in the Cohesity UI: 1. Select System> Audit Logs>Log Settings.
2. In the Log Settings tab, click the pencil icon ( ) for the Log Retention Period audit information option, type the desired number, and select retention period (Days, Weeks, Months, or Years).
3. The Log Retention Period is displayed in days as Cohesity converts weeks, months, or years into days.
4. Click Save. Monitor Cluster Audit Logs You can view cluster audit logs to know the activities on your cluster. To monitor cluster audit logs, complete the following in the Cohesity UI:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Audit Logs

1. Select System>Audit Logs>Cluster. 2. In the Cluster tab of the Audit Logs page, apply filters on the required fields (Date
Range, Users, Category, or Action) and monitor logs.
Download Cluster Audit Logs
You can download the cluster audit logs for analyzing the logs outside your cluster. Cohesity cluster allows you to download the logs in a .CSV format.
Note: The download .CSV file has more details than what the Cohesity displays. The file contains details about the IP addresses of the systems from which the cluster is accessed, tenants, impersonation, and so on.
To download a cluster audit log, complete the following in the Cohesity UI:
1. Select System>Audit Logs>Cluster.
2. In the Cluster tab of the Audit Logs page, click the icon.
The CSV file automatically downloads to your local system.

File Services Audit Logs
The File Services Audit Logs feature enables you to record and monitor events occurring on your SMB and NFS views. Unlike the cluster-level audit logs, the logs for views are not displayed in the Cohesity GUI. The file services audit logs are saved in an internal view called filesystem_audit. You can access these views by mounting the path COHESITY_AUDIT_VIEW\filesystem_audit. The File Services tab in the Audit Log page provides two mount paths for NFS and SMB. You can mount these paths to access and view the audit logs. You can set permissions for the view and restrict access only to required subnets or users. Only the subnet's IP addresses in the allowlist can access and view the audit logs.
Note:
By default, when you create a view, the Audit Log option is disabled. You must manually enable it when creating the view or after creation.

Add a Syslog Server
You can add a Syslog server to the Cohesity cluster and send cluster audit logs, filer audit logs, alert audit logs, and data protection events entries to that server. These logs are

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Audit Logs

identified by their respective audit tags as listed below: l Cluster audit log entries are identified with the tag cluster_audit. l Filer audit log entries are identified with the tag filesystem_audit. l Alert audit log entries are identified by the tag cohesity_alerts. l Data protection events are identified by the tag dataprotection_events.
Optionally, you can set custom tags or token IDs for these Syslog messages to aggregate and parse them based on the set tags and tokens. Add a Syslog server to the Cohesity cluster There are two ways you can add a Syslog server to the Cohesity cluster.
l Adding a Syslog server using the Cohesity CLI l Adding a Syslog server using the Cohesity UI
Adding a Syslog server using the Cohesity CLI
1. Start the Cohesity CLI remotely or locally as described in the Cohesity CLI Reference Guide. Specify the static IPv4 or IPv6 address of one of the Cohesity nodes. For example, if the CLI was downloaded to a Linux system, you might use the following command. Provide a Cohesity cluster username and password. ./iris_cli -server 172.16.3.101 -username=admin
2. Add a syslog server to the Cohesity cluster using the syslog create CLI command: admin>syslog create address=<IPAddressorHostname> port=<Port>

Adding a Syslog server using the Cohesity UI
1. Navigate to Settings > Summary and then select the Syslog tab. 2. Click Add located at the top-right of the page. 3. IP Address/Hostname: Specify the hostname or IP address of the syslog server. 4. Protocol: Specify the protocol used by the syslog server. The default is TCP, but UDP
is also supported. 5. Port: Specify the port where the syslog server listens. 6. Stream: Select the logs to be sent to the syslog server from the drop-down list.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Audit Logs

7. Facilities (Optional): Enable this option to send the logs of specific facilities to the syslog server.
8. Secure Connection: Toggle to configure the authentication method to securely connect to the syslog server. 1. Authentication Mode: Select one of two modes from the drop-down list. 1. anon: This method uses TLS encryption without server identity validation, suitable for trusted networks where authentication is not required. 2. x509/name: This method uses TLS with certificate-based authentication. The server's identity will be verified using a trusted CA certificate and an expected subject name. In Permitted Peer Identity field, enter the expected subject name of the syslog server's TLS certificate. For example, syslog.example.com.
Important: The connection will only be established when the server presents a certificate with this identity.
2. Trusted CA Certificate: Paste the PEM-encoded certificate text or click Select Certificate File to select the file containing the certificate text.
9. Enable Syslog Forwarding: Toggle to forward logs and events to the syslog server. 10. Click Add.
Optional. Click Manage Streams to set custom tags or token IDs for cluster audit logs, file system audit logs, alert audit logs, and data protection event entries to aggregate and parse them based on the set tags and tokens. You must set up an alert rule to get the logs for the Alert Audit Logs stream sent to the Syslog server. For more information, see Add Alert Notification Rule.
Enable or Disable Syslog Server
You can enable or disable the syslog server to the Cohesity cluster. To enable a syslog server:
1. Navigate to Settings > Summary and then select the Syslog tab. 2. Find the syslog server in the list, click the Edit button, and toggle on or off the Syslog
Server button to enable or disable the syslog server to the Cohesity cluster.

Capture Logs
Use the timecapsule command to capture a comprehensive log bundle of Cohesity services across a single or multiple Nodes in a Cohesity cluster for a specified time range. To capture logs: Use any of the following timecapsule command depending on your requirement:
l To capture logs from the cluster (all Nodes) for all components for a time range:
timecapsule --clusterip=<Cluster_Ip_address> -start_time_secs=<Seconds_ in_Unix_Time> -end_time_secs=<Seconds_in_Unix_Time>
For example, timecapsule --clusterip=198.51.100.1 -start_time_ secs=1549001025 -end_time_secs=1549173873 By default, the timecapsule command captures logs for all services. l To capture logs from the cluster (all Nodes) for specific components for a time range:
timecapsule --clusterip=<Cluster_Ip_address> -start_time_secs=<Seconds_ in_Unix_Time> -end_time_secs=<Seconds_in_Unix_Time> -service_ names=<Service_names_list>
For example, timecapsule --clusterip=198.51.100.1 -start_time_ secs=1549001025 -end_time_secs=1549173873 -service_names=genie, magneto
l To capture logs from a single or multiple nodes for all components for a time range:
timecapsule --hostips=<Nodes_IP_addresses> -start_time_secs=<Seconds_ in_Unix_Time> -end_time_secs=<Seconds_in_Unix_Time>
For example, timecapsule -hostips=198.51.100.1,198.51.100.2,198.51.100.3 -start_time_ secs=1549001025 -end_time_secs=1549173873 l To capture logs from a single or multiple nodes for specific components for a time range:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Audit Logs

timecapsule --hostips=<Nodes_IP_addresses> -start_time_secs=<Seconds_ in_Unix_Time> -end_time_secs=<SSeconds_in_Unix_Time> -service_ names=<Service_names_list>
For example, timecapsule --hostips=198.51.100.1 -start_time_ secs=1549001025 -end_time_secs=1549173873 -service_names=bridge,apollo

Advanced Diagnostics
Cohesity provides common pre-canned statistics in charts and graphs with pre-determined X and Y axes at the following locations in the Cohesity UI:
l Performance Statistics--Select System > Performance. For more information, see Performance.
l Storage Statistics--Select System > Storage. For more information, see Storage Statistics.
In addition, Cohesity provides an extensive set of reports. For more information, see Reports. Cohesity also provides advanced diagnostics that allow you to customize the plotted statistics. To use Advanced Diagnostics:
1. Navigate to System > Advanced Diagnostics. 2. From the Schema drop-down, select a Cohesity component that you are interested in
viewing statistics about. For example, if you want to learn more about physical disk

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Advanced Diagnostics

statistics on the Cohesity cluster, select Disk Physical Stats in the Schema dropdown. After selecting a Schema, the Metric and Entity drop-downs are populated with options specific to this Schema.
Note: Entity is equivalent to an Object in the Cohesity Dashboard.
3. Select a Metric to plot. The options available in the Metric drop-down are specific to the chosen Schema. The Metric drop-down provides data that can be plotted on a graph. For example, after selecting the Node Physical Stats Schema, you could select the Bytes Written Metric.
4. Select an Entity to report on. The options available in the Entity drop-down are specific to the chosen Schema. The Entity drop-down defines the specific Cohesity Object to report on such as a disk, node or storage domain. For example, after selecting the Node Physical Stats Schema and the Bytes Written Metric, you can select one of the nodes in the cluster from the Entity drop-down.
5. Select a Rollup Function to apply to the data points returned by the selected Metric and Entity for the specified time period. For example, you could select the Node Physical Stats Schema, the Bytes Written Metric, the Node:1 Entity and the Average Rollup Function.
The available Rollup Functions are listed in the following table.

Rollup Function Name Raw
Sum
Average
Count Max Min

Function Description
The data is not altered by a Rollup Function. All data points in the specified time interval are reported. The sum of all the data points over the specified time interval. Add all the data points together for the specified time period. The mean of the data points over the specified time period. Sum of the data points divided by the number of data points. The number of data points for the specified time interval. The largest value of all the data points for the specified time interval. The smallest value of all the data points for the specified time interval.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 32: Monitoring

Advanced Diagnostics

Rollup Function Name

Function Description

Median

The middle value of all the data points if all the data points in the specified time interval are sorted by value. (50 Percentile)

Rate

The sum of the data points divided by the specified time interval in seconds. For example if the Bytes Read Metric is specified for the Cluster Physical Schema, the Rate Rollup Function and an interval of 10 Minutes, the number of bytes per second read by the cluster is reported. This is the throughput of the cluster. In this example, the rate of bytes per second is calculated by dividing the number of bytes read in 600 seconds by 600 seconds (10 Minutes).

95 Percentile

The data point that is 95% greater than all the other data points if all the data points in the specified time interval are sorted by value.

Latest

Is the last data point that was recorded during the specified interval.

Warning: Not all Rollup Functions are appropriate for all metrics. For example, reporting the bytes read every hour on the cluster using the Latest Function is probably not very informative. However, reporting cumulative statics about the number of bytes read during a time period on the cluster is more informative. For example, you can report on the average number of bytes read on the cluster in one hour using the Average function or you can report on the total number of bytes read on the cluster during one day using the Sum function.
6. Select a time interval from the drop-down or choose Custom to specify your own time interval in seconds. For example, you could select the Node Physical Stats Schema, the Bytes Written Metric, the Node:1 Entity, using the Average Rollup Function over a 10 Minutes Interval.
7. Click Plot and either a new graph displays with the plotted data or a line of the plotted data is added to an existing graph. For this example, a new graph showing the average number of bytes written per ten-minute interval to a node is plotted as shown in the following figure.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Advanced Diagnostics

Plot lines that have the same Y-axis are plotted on the same graph with different colors. For example, all plot lines that report on bytes are plotted on the same graph. (The X-axis is always time.) A plot line with different Y-axis are plotted in a new graph. A graph showing Critical (Red) and Warning (Yellow) Alerts can be found along the bottom of the page. You can click an Alert in the graphic to drill down to more information about the Alert. A detail page about the Alert is displayed in a new Browser tab. 8. Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 33: Virtual Edition

Cohesity Virtual Edition

Cohesity Virtual Edition
Cohesity Virtual Edition is a single-node Cohesity cluster (ROBO) or multi-node Cohesity cluster that is hosted on a Virtual Machine that is hosted on VMware vCenter Server, Microsoft Hyper-V server, Nutanix AHV, RHEL KVM, AlmaLinux, or OCI Linux KVM. You can use a single-node Virtual Edition if your environment has smaller offices with reduced workloads that do not require the full computing power of a Cohesity cluster running on multiple nodes. In addition, Cohesity Clustered Virtual Edition is a multiple node Cohesity cluster that can support larger workflows and is hosted on multiple Virtual Machines in VMware vCenter Server, Nutanix AHV, RHEL KVM, AlmaLinux, or OCI Linux KVM. For information on the hypervisors and their support for single-node and multi-node clusters, see Virtual Edition.
A single Node Virtual Edition is appropriate for the following reduced workflow example. A company has San Jose and Las Vegas remote offices that require backing up of a small number of VMware Virtual Machines. However, the company wants to centralize the backups on a central Cohesity cluster located in the Datacenter of the Corporate Headquarters. These two smaller remote offices can use Cohesity cluster Virtual Editions to capture Snapshots of the VMs and replicate the Snapshots to the central Cohesity cluster located in the Chicago Corporate Datacenter. This central Cohesity cluster is running directly on hardware supported by Cohesity.
In addition, other remote offices can also replicate Snapshots to the central Cohesity cluster using Cohesity clusters running directly on supported hardware as shown by the following examples:
l At the Cincinnati remote office, a Cohesity cluster captures and then stores Snapshots of a physical server.
l At the Des Moines remote office, a Cohesity cluster captures and then stores Snapshots of Virtual Machines.
These Snapshots are then replicated to the central Cohesity cluster located in Chicago.

Extend the Capacities of a Virtual Edition for VMware

Extend the Capacities of a Virtual Edition for VMware
Extending the node capacities of a Virtual Edition(VE) for VMware is predefined by the cluster configuration, either SMALL or Large.
Note: For multi-node cluster, - you can add or extend the disk for individual nodes or all nodes. - you can add multiple disks to a node. - you must add or extend the disk on only one node at a time.
This section assumes that the node to be extended is part of the cluster and is healthy with no cluster operation running on the node. To check the cluster operations, run iris_cli cluster status and ensure the cluster status is as below: SERVICE STATE SYNC: DONE
CLUSTER ACTIVE OPERATION: <this field must be empty>
CLUSTER HEAL STATUS: NORMAL
Small Configurations (8TB VE) Small configurations support a maximum of 8TB data disk space on each node accumulating all data disks on the node. The node to be extended must satisfy the following conditions before and after the capacity extend:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 33: Virtual Edition

Extend the Capacities of a Virtual Edition for VMware

Review the following prerequisites and warnings before starting the process to extend the capacities of the Virtual Edition VMware VM:
l You must have a vCenter Server account that has been granted administrator privileges for the ESXi host that is hosting the Virtual Edition.
l During this process, the Cohesity cluster services must be stopped and the cluster must be powered off. Therefore, during this process, the cluster is unable to run workflow tasks such as Protection Groups, Recover tasks, Replicating Data tasks, etc. Cohesity recommends stopping all tasks on the cluster before starting this process.
l If the ESXI host reboots, power cycles or powers off during this extension process, data loss may occur. If this occurs, contact Cohesity Support.
l The ESXi Datastores that are hosting the Virtual Edition VM must have enough capacity to support the disk size expansion of the VM. A new Datastore cannot be used to extend the size of the existing disks on the VM. It can be used only to expand the capacities of an existing VM by adding a new disk with a restriction on the total number of disks attached to the VM.
l All disks must be attached to different SCSI controllers.
You can extend the node capacities of a Virtual Edition VMware in two ways:
l Add a new disk to Virtual Edition VMware. l Extend an existing disk on the Virtual Edition VMware.
Note: Cohesity recommends adding multiple disks each from different datastore to the Virtual Edition VMware as it provides better disk bandwidth.

Add a New Data Disk or Metadata Disk
1. Run the Cohesity CLI locally or remotely on the Virtual Edition. For more information, see Using the Cohesity CLI and List of Cohesity CLI Commands.
iris_cli admin>
2. Verify the capacities of the existing Metadata and Disk Tier disks. For a Metadata disk, STORAGE TIER is set to PCIeSSD. For a Data Tier disk, STORAGE TIER is set to SATAHDD.
admin> disk ls
Sample Output In the following sample output, the capacity of the Data disk is 7.99 TiB and the capacity of the Metadata disk is 500 GiB.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Extend the Capacities of a Virtual Edition for VMware

5. If the VM is running, right-click the VM and select Power Off. 6. Right-click the VM and select Edit Settings. 7. Click the Add hard disk tab > New hard disk. 8. Update the size of the new hard disk.
Warning: Do not change the size of existing data disks.
Note: If the newly added disk is for the data tier, the data tier size after extension must be at most 16 times than the size of the metadata tier. If this is not the case, you need to extend the metadata disk tier capacity either by updating the size of the existing metadata disk or adding one more disk for the metadata tier. For example if the Virtual Edition VM was originally a configuration with a 500GB Metadata disk and a 8000GB Data Tier disk and you increase the disk sizes to a 1000 GB Metadata disk and a 16000 GB Data Tier disk, you must also increase the number of vCPUs to 8 and the memory to 64000. Ensure that the Data Tier disk size does not exceed 16 times the Metadata disk size. In addition, the total Data Tier disk capacity per node must not exceed the supported upper limits of 8 TB or 16 TB, depending on the configuration. The Metadata drive size must be smaller than the Data Tier drive size.
9. Click OK to save the changes. Wait until this operation is completed. 10. Right-click the VM and select Power On. 11. Run the Cohesity CLI locally or remotely on the Virtual Edition. For more information,
see Using the Cohesity CLI and List of Cohesity CLI Commands. iris_cli admin> 12. Stop the cluster services. admin> cluster stop
Wait for 2 minutes for the cluster services to stop. 13. Find and copy the node ID of the cluster.
admin> node list 14. Based on the requirement, perform the following:
Adding a Data Disk to the Node

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 33: Virtual Edition

Extend the Capacities of a Virtual Edition for VMware

Note: You must be on the same VM node where the new disk is added. If the data-to-metadata tier ratio is not maintained after adding a new data disk, you must add a new metadata disk or extend the existing one before adding a new data disk to maintain the ratio.
Perform the following steps: 1. Run lsblk on bash on the node to see the new disk added and copy its disk path. 2. Run the following command: iris_cli admin> disk assimilate disk-paths=<disk_path_of_new_disk_on_node> node-id=<node ID>
Adding a Metadata Disk to the Node Perform the following steps:
1. Run lsblk on bash on the node to see the new disk added and copy its disk path.
2. Run the following command: iris_cli admin> disk assimilate disk-paths=<disk_path_of_new_disk_on_node> node-id=<node ID> is-metadata=true
15. View the current disk size admin> disk ls Keep repeating this command until the MAXIMUM PHYSICAL CAPACITY field settings for both the Metadata disk and the Data Tier disk are equal to the new sizes you specified. For a Metadata disk, STORAGE TIER is set to PCIeSSD. For a Data Tier disk, STORAGE TIER is set to SATA-HDD.
Note: It can take up to 10 minutes for the size to be increased.
16. After the sizes are equal to the new sizes you specified, start the cluster services. admin> cluster start Wait for 2 minutes for the cluster services to start.

18. Wait for the Cohesity Dashboard to report the updated storage capacity.
It can take about 10 minutes for the Cohesity Dashboard to report the updated storage capacity.
19. Resume running the workflow tasks on the cluster such as Protection Groups, Recover tasks, Replicating Data tasks, etc.

: 5.00 GiB

3. Using a VMware vSphere Web Client, log in to a vCenter Server that hosts Virtual Edition VM: 1. Enter the URL of your vCenter Server in the address bar of a web browser in the following format: https://<vcenter_server_ip_address_or_fqdn>. 2. On the vSphere Welcome page, click Launch vSphere Client (HTML5).
3. On the vSphere login page, enter the username and password of the vCenter Server and click Login.
4. The vSphere Client home page opens. The left panel displays the hosts, clusters, and VMs in the vSphere inventory. From the left pane, find the Virtual EditionVM to extend capacity.
5. If the VM is running, right-click the VM and select Power Off.
6. Right-click the VM and select Edit Settings.
7. Select the hard disk that you want to extend and update its size.

Note: If you are extending the Data disk, the disk size must be extended to a size that is at most 16 times the size of the Metadata disk. If this requirement is not met, you need to extend the Data disk capacity by increasing the size of the existing Data disk or by adding an additional Data disk. To add a new disk, see Add a New Data Disk or Metadata Disk.

8. Click OK to save the changes. Wait until this operation completes. 9. Right-click the VM and select Power On.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 33: Virtual Edition

Extend the Capacities of a Virtual Edition for VMware

10. Run the Cohesity CLI locally or remotely on the Virtual Edition. For more information, see Using the Cohesity CLI and List of Cohesity CLI Commands. iris_cli admin>
11. Stop the cluster services. admin> cluster stop Wait for 2 minutes for the cluster services to stop.
12. Disable Secure Shell admin> cluster secure-shell enable=false
Note: After disabling the secure shell, the current session will exit, wait a few minutes and log back in again.
13. Stop the containerd service. [support@virtual-node-1 ~]$ sudo systemctl stop containerd
14. Check for any Cohesity services that are still actively using the disk. Ensure the output of this command is empty before you proceed. Update the sdc2 value according to the disk that needs to be extended (refer to the output from Step 2). [support@virtual-node-1 ~]$ sudo lsof | grep /home_cohesity_ data/disks/sdc2
15. Find and copy the node ID of the cluster. admin> node list
16. Extend the size of the disks admin> disk extend node-id=<node ID of node where disks are extended>
Note: If you are extending the Data disk or Metadata disk size by adding a new disk, follow the steps in Add a New Data Disk or Metadata Disk.
17. View the current disk size admin> disk ls Keep repeating this command until the MAXIMUM PHYSICAL CAPACITY field settings for both the Metadata disk and the Data Tier disk are equal to the new sizes you specified. For a Metadata disk, STORAGE TIER is set to PCIeSSD. For a Data Tier disk, STORAGE TIER is set to SATA-HDD.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 33: Virtual Edition

Extend the Capacities of a Virtual Edition for VMware

Note: It can take up to 10 minutes for the size to be increased.
18. Start the containerd service. [support@virtual-node-1 ~]$ sudo systemctl start containerd
19. Start Secure Shell admin> cluster secure-shell enable=true
Note: Enabling the secure shell will disconnect the current session, wait a few minutes and login again.
20. After the sizes are equal to the new sizes you specified, start the cluster services. admin> cluster start Wait for 2 minutes for the cluster services to start.
21. Log in to the Cohesity Dashboard: a. Start a browser and enter the Cohesity cluster domain name in the browser address bar. b. Log in to the Cohesity Dashboard. The default System Admin account is admin and the default password is administartor.
22. Wait for the Cohesity Dashboard to report the updated storage capacity. It can take about 10 minutes for the Cohesity Dashboard to report the updated storage capacity.
23. Resume running the workflow tasks on the cluster such as Protection Groups, Recover tasks, Replicating Data tasks, etc.

Chapter 34: Cohesity Cloud Edition
Cohesity simplifies data management for organizations, allowing them to experience the benefits of the cloud without giving up control over their data. Cohesity Cloud Edition is a Cohesity cluster deployed in a cloud service, designed to offer high performance and greater cluster capacity. Cohesity supports the following Cohesity Cloud Edition:
l Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS l Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure l Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP l Cohesity Cloud Edition on OCI For information on the Cohesity Cloud Edition supportability, seeCohesity Cloud EditionCohesity Cloud Edition Supportability.

Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS is a Cohesity cluster deployed in AWS, designed to offer high performance and greater cluster capacity. CloudFormation

UpdateStack ListStackResources CreateStack GetTemplate DeleteStack DescribeStacks DescribeStackEvents ValidateTemplate

Description
Cohesity uses the access key and the secret access key provided to validate the IAM user. IAM permissions are required to get the user, the policy for the user and to validate the credentials. To create a cluster by using Helios, Cohesity uses System Service Manager (SSM). A role is created for SSM and passed onto the service. These IAM permissions are required to create a policy, create a role for SSM operation, attach the policy to this role and pass the role onto the SSM service for performing operations to create a cluster using Helios. Delete role and delete role policy permissions are required to delete the role and policy created for the SSM operation after the task is complete.
Cohesity creates a CloudFormation template using the information provided on the UI for cluster creation, and creates a CloudFormation stack. The stack is deleted when destroy cluster command is used from the control VM. Validate cluster validates the Cloud Formation template which requires the permission "cloudformation:ValidateTemplate". "cloudformation:DeleteStack" is required while executing destroy cluster.

AttachNetworkInterface AttachVolume AuthorizeSecurityGroupEgress AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress CreateLaunchTemplate CreateNetworkInterface CreateSecurityGroup CreateTags CreateVolume DeleteNetworkInterface DeleteSecurityGroup DeleteTags DeleteVolume DescribeAvailabilityZones DescribeIamInstanceProfileAssociations DescribeInstanceStatus DescribeInstances DescribeNetworkInterfaces DescribeRegions DescribeSecurityGroups DescribeSubnets DescribeVolumes DescribeVpcs DetachNetworkInterface DetachVolume ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute ModifyVolumeAttribute ReplaceIamInstanceProfileAssociation RevokeSecurityGroupEgress RevokeSecurityGroupIngress RunInstances StartInstances StopInstances TerminateInstances

Creating a cluster requires creating AWS EC2 instances. Network Interface and volumes are created and attached to the instance to create a cluster node in a particular region. Tags are created and added to these EC2 services. Permissions to start/stop these instances are required while executing commands to start/stop cluster from the control VM. Permissions to delete all the EC2 services created while creating cluster are required while executing destroy cluster/delete VMs from the control VM. While creating a cluster using Helios, users can create a new security group and deploy the cluster using that security group instead of using the existing security group. Therefore, Cohesity needs permission to create the security group, delete the security group, authorize the security group ingress and egress, and revoke the security group ingress and egress.

Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS Object Lock
For Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS, you can configure Object Lock to secure the backed-up data. Enabling Object Lock prevents data from being modified, deleted, or overwritten on the object storage. You can configure Object Lock while registering the object storage as an external target to store the data.
Prerequisites for Object Lock
Before registering an object storage as an external target with Object Lock enabled, ensure the following:
l For AWS external target (AWS S3 Bucket): The AWS external target must have versioning and Object Lock enabled. For more information, see Using S3 Object Lock. This property must be set at the time of target creation and cannot be enabled after creation.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 34: Cohesity Cloud Edition

Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS

Note: Avoid setting default retention on AWS target- this is not required as Cohesity locks the objects for the duration required. Large default retentions affect garbage collection and increase costs.
Considerations for Object Lock
l For the AWS target, the objects will be locked in the Governance retention mode by default. To use the Compliance mode, contact Cohesity Support.
l When backing up data to versioned buckets, ensure that you do not edit the storage class of objects directly. Editing the storage class of objects directly will create a new version of the object while the original version remains in the previous storage tier. Object-level locks will not be carried over to the new version.
l The expiry of the object lock will match the retention of the backup snapshots. However, the object lock will not update if you modify the expiry for archived snapshots after the Protection Group has run.
l Once enabled, Object Lock cannot be disabled. l With Object Lock enabled, the storage utilization of external targets may be higher. l If Object Lock compliance is not met for a backup, then the backup will fail.
Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS Considerations
Review the following considerations for Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS:
l Cohesity does not support the following features on Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS: l Direct migration from Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS to Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS. As an alternative, you can deploy a new Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS cluster and then replicate the data from Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on AWS to the newly deployed Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS. l CloudArchive with periodic full. l CloudTier workflow. l Data movement policy to move data to archive tiers. l Policy-based Cloud Spin.
l Cohesity Cloud Edition on AWS supports Write Once Read Many (WORM) for CloudArchive with incremental forever format. The WORM model ensures that the objects written to the WORM-supported AWS targets cannot be tampered with (deleted or overwritten). The archives created are immutable for the duration configured. For the list of WORM supported AWS external targets, see AWS External Targets.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 34: Cohesity Cloud Edition

Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure

l You cannot unregister an external target associated with a cluster's Storage Domain for down-tiering protected data (primary copy). Only external targets registered for archival (secondary copy) can be unregistered from the cluster.

Notes
Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure configured with Hot Tier and Cold Tier support SmartFiles for SMB, NFS, and S3 protocols, with functionality limited to View Snapshots and Replication.
You can install Marketplace Apps on Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure configured with Hot Tier. For more information on Marketplace App, see Apps

The multitenancy feature enables you to configure the multitenant environment on your Cohesity Platform and securely isolate each tenant in your environment. Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure Object Lock
For Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure, you can configure Object Lock to secure the backed-up data. Enabling Object Lock prevents data from being modified, deleted, or overwritten on the object storage. You can configure Object Lock while registering the object storage as an external target to store the data.
Prerequisites for Object Lock
Before registering an object storage as an external target with Object Lock enabled, ensure the following:
l For Azure external targets (Azure Hot Blob Storage): The Azure external target must have version-level immutability enabled on the storage container, which indicates that the storage account must also have version-level immutability. This property must be set at the time of target creation and cannot be enabled after creation.For more information, see Enable version-level immutability support on a container.
Note: Avoid setting default retention on Azure target- this is not required as Cohesity locks the objects for the duration required. Large default retentions affect garbage collection and increase costs.
Considerations for Object Lock
l For the Azure target, the objects will be locked in the Locked mode by default. l When backing up data to versioned buckets, ensure that you do not edit the storage
class of objects directly. Editing the storage class of objects directly will create a new version of the object while the original version remains in the previous storage tier. Object-level locks will not be carried over to the new version. l The expiry of the object lock will match the retention of the backup snapshots. However, the object lock will not update if you modify the expiry for archived snapshots after the Protection Group has run. l Once enabled, Object Lock cannot be disabled. l With Object Lock enabled, the storage utilization of external targets may be higher. l If Object Lock compliance is not met for a backup, then the backup will fail.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 34: Cohesity Cloud Edition

Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP

Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure Considerations
Review the following considerations for Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure:
l Cohesity does not support the features on Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure: l Direct migration from Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on Azure to Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure. As an alternative, you can deploy a new Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure and then replicate the data from Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on Azure to the newly deployed Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure. l CloudTier workflow. l Data movement policy to move data to archive tier s. l Policy-based Cloud Spin.
l Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure backend APIs are only V2 compliant; to automate workflows against Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure ensure to call the V2 APIs and not V1 APIs.
l From 7.2 version onwards, Cohesity Cloud Edition on Azure supports Write Once Read Many (WORM) for CloudArchive with periodic full. The WORM model ensures that the objects written to the WORM-supported Azure targets cannot be tampered with (deleted or overwritten). The archives created are immutable for the duration configured. For the list of WORM supported Azure external targets, see Microsoft Azure External Targets.
l You cannot unregister an external target associated with a cluster's Storage Domain for down-tiering protected data (primary copy). Only external targets registered for archival (secondary copy) can be unregistered from the cluster.
Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP
Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP is a Cohesity cluster deployed in GCP, designed to offer high performance and greater cluster capacity. This solution employs advanced data deduplication and compression techniques to significantly reduce data footprints and storage costs. This section provides the following information on Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP:
Supported Regions for Deploying Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP
You can deploy Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP in all regions supported by the GCP cloud. For the list of supported regions, see Regions.

Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP Object Lock
On Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP, you can enable Object Lock for GCP cloud storage buckets while registering them as external targets. A GCP external target with Object Lock enabled can be:
l Used as the main backup location by associating with the Storage Domain (primary copy).
l Used for archiving (secondary copy).
Object Lock protects backup or archive data from accidental or malicious deletion or modification. It helps meet compliance requirements by making backed-up or archived data read-only for a specified period. You can configure Object Lock while registering the cloud storage bucket as an external target.
Prerequisites for Object Lock
Before registering a GCP cloud storage bucket as an external target with Object Lock enabled, ensure the GCP cloud storage bucket has versioning and Object Retention Lock enabled. For more information, see Object Rentention Lock. The Object Retention Lock property must be set at the time of the GCP cloud storage bucket creation and cannot be enabled after creation.
Considerations for Object Lock
l Object Lock is supported only if the GCP Cloud Storage bucket and the cluster are located in the same region.
l When creating the Protection Policy, avoid setting a long retention period, as Cohesity locks the objects for the entire duration. Longer retention periods can delay garbage

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 34: Cohesity Cloud Edition

Cohesity Cloud Edition on OCI

collection and increase costs. l For the GCP target, the objects will be locked in the Governance retention mode by
default. To use the Compliance mode, contact Cohesity Support. l When backing up data to versioned buckets, ensure that you do not edit the storage
class of objects directly. Editing the storage class of objects directly will create a new version of the object while the original version remains in the previous storage tier. Object-level locks will not be carried over to the new version. l The expiry of the object lock will match the retention of the backup snapshots. However, the object lock will not update if you modify the expiry for archived snapshots after the Protection Group has run. l Once enabled, Object Lock cannot be disabled. l With Object Lock enabled, the storage utilization of external targets may be higher. l If Object Lock compliance is not met for a backup, then the backup will fail.
Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP Considerations
Cohesity does not support the following features on Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP:
l Direct migration from Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on GCP to Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP. As an alternative, you can deploy a new Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP and then replicate the data from Cohesity Cloud Edition (legacy) on GCP to the newly deployed Cohesity Cloud Edition on GCP.
l CloudArchive with periodic full. l Write Once Read Many (WORM) for CloudArchive. l CloudTier workflow. l Data movement policy to move data to archive tiers. l Policy-based Cloud Spin. l You cannot unregister an external target associated with a cluster's Storage Domain
for down-tiering protected data (primary copy). Only external targets registered for archival (secondary copy) can be unregistered from the cluster.

Using the Cohesity CLI
You can use the Cohesity Command Line Interface (CLI) locally or remotely to manage your Cohesity cluster.

Run the Cohesity CLI Locally
Before you begin:
Cohesity restricts SSH access to the host operating system shell, which means you can run custom scripts and private tools only on Secure Shell and not on Cohesity CLI (iris CLI). Cohesity recommends evaluating the security enhancements mentioned in the Secure Shell Considerations section and deciding whether to enable Secure Shell or leverage the Cohesity Cluster and Helios APIs.
Follow these steps to run the CLI commands on Secure Shell:
1. Get the IP address for any node of the Cohesity cluster. You can get the list of IP addresses from the Cohesity Cluster UI by selecting Settings > Summary and then selecting the Nodes tab.
2. Use the IP address to log into the node as the support user.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 35: Tools

Using the Cohesity CLI

Note: Make sure that you have enabled the Support user on the Cohesity cluster. For more information, see Enable Support User for Local Shell Access.
Command ssh support@<node IP address> Example ssh support@111.1.1.1 3. When prompted, enter the password of the support user account. support@111.1.1.1's password: Once your password is successfully authenticated, the prompt changes, and the support@restricted prompt is displayed. [support@restricted-cluster-1-node-4 ~]\> 4. Run the command to start the Cohesity CLI console as a local user. [support@restricted-cluster-1-node-4 ~]$ iris_cli You are prompted to enter the username and password. Enter the credentials of the local user account you use to log into the Cohesity cluster's User Interface. Sample Output [support@restricted-cluster-1-node-4 ~]$ iris_cli Username: john Password: ..... 5. Once the local user account's password is successfully authenticated, the Cohesity CLI console opens. You can now run any CLI command. Sample Output john@111.1.1.1>cluster status Username: john Password: ..... If you only enter the CLI commands at the prompt and then enter your credentials when prompted (as shown in the example above), you're in the Interactive Mode.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 35: Tools

Using the Cohesity CLI

Login with Active Directory User
You can log in to iris_cli with an Active Directory (AD) user by specifying the AD domain using the -domain flag. Prerequisites The cluster must be joined to one or more Active Directory domains. For more information, see Active Directory (AD) and Join Active Directory. Steps to Log In with an AD User
1. After starting the iris_cli, use the -domain switch to specify the AD domain: iris_cli -domain <AD-domain-name>
2. When prompted, provide the username (in the format <username>) and the password for the AD user. Example Username: john
Password: .....
Note: Usernames must be provided as-is, as iris_cli does not support the NetBIOS (DOMAIN\username) or UPN format (username@domain). iris_cli also does not support login for SSO-based users (SAML).

Enable Support User for Local Shell Access
You need to use the support user account to log into the Cohesity bash shell using SSH.
By default, the support user account is disabled on the Cohesity node that is part of a Cohesity cluster. You need to enable the support user account by setting a password for the user account in the Cohesity Dashboard. Also, you can enable Linux sudo access for the support user account.
Set the Support User Password for the First Time
Using the Cohesity Dashboard or Cohesity CLI, you can set the password for the support user. You cannot retrieve the password once it is set. Therefore, ensure that you set a strong password that is longer and easy to remember. In case, if you want to reset the support user password and have forgotten the existing password, then contact Cohesity Support.
To set the support user password:
In the Cohesity Dashboard, select Settings > Access Management. In the Support user section, under Password, click Set Password and define the new password for the support user account.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 35: Tools

Using the Cohesity CLI

Also, from the Cohesity CLI, you can use the following iris_cli command to change the support user password: iris_cli user linux-user linux-username=support linux-password=<password> Enable Linux Sudo Access When operating within the Host OS, without sudo access, the support user has read-only access privileges and limited read-write access privileges. To perform advanced operations within the Host OS that require privileged access, you need to enable Linux sudo access for the support user account. Use the following iris_cli command to enable Linux sudo access for the support user: iris_cli user linux-sudo-access enable=true duration-in-hours=xxx
Note: You can enter a duration within the range of 1 to 720 hours.
To disable Linux sudo access for the support user, use the following iris_cli command: iris_cli user linux-sudo-access enable=false
Note: Apart from the admin user, if you use a local user account to enable Linux sudo access for the support user, ensure that you configure the local user account with the Manage Linux user sudo access privilege.

Update cohesity_console User Password
By default, the root user account is disabled on the Cohesity cluster. For operations that require root access, you can use the cohesity_console user account. To update the cohesity_console user password, use the following iris_cli command: iris_cli user linux-user linux-username=cohesity_console linux-password=<password>
Explore the Cohesity CLI
To view the top-level Cohesity CLI commands and help about the commands, enter help. admin>help To view the operations available for a command and help about the operations, enter the command, a space, and help. admin>node help

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 35: Tools

Using the Cohesity CLI

To view the parameters of an operation and get help about the parameters, enter the command, a space, the operation, and help. admin>node list help
To list the top-level commands that start with specified characters using command-line completion, enter some characters, and a tab. For example: admin>vie<tab> view view-box
To list the operations available for a command using command-line completion, enter the command, a space, and a tab. For example: admin>node <tab>
To list the operations using command-line completion, enter the command, a space, one or more characters of the sub-command, and a tab. admin>node l<tab> list list-packages ls ls-free-nodes ls-pkgs
To list the parameters using command-line completion, enter the command, a space, the operation, a space, and a tab. For example: admin>node list<tab> list list-packages admin>node list
To see a list of available Nodes on the Cohesity cluster. admin>node list
To see the status of the Cohesity cluster. admin>cluster status
To get details about the Cohesity cluster. admin>cluster info
Note: This is a small sample of the commands available from the Cohesity CLI. Explore the Cohesity CLI help for more options.

Use the Bash Shell on a Cohesity Node
This section describes how to access the Cohesity bash shell for troubleshooting and configuration.
1. To log into the Cohesity cluster, use the DNS Name or IP that is used to browse into the Cohesity Dashboard. The bash shell can also be accessed from the IPMI remote console (IPMI, iLO, CIMC, or iDRAC, depending on the hardware vendor) of the node.
2. Use PuTTY (shown below), an SSH client, or IPMI remote console to log in to the cluster. Use the username support to log in to the cluster and specify the IP address. On a Mac, Unix, or Linux computer, use the ssh command:
ssh support@<hostname>
Example:
ssh support@192.168.1.100

3. When prompted, enter the password.
Note: This password refers to the console password and not the Cohesity UI credentials. You can provide the default password if the node is not part of a Cohesity cluster. For the default password of the support user account, contact Cohesity Support.

Run the Cohesity CLI Remotely
You can also run the Cohesity CLI on a Windows, macOS, or Linux system and remotely connect to the Cohesity cluster.
Note: The user using a Mac with Apple Silicon needs to install Rosetta 2 to run the Cohesity CLI.
To download and start the remote version of the Cohesity CLI:

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 35: Tools

Using the Cohesity CLI

1. Download the appropriate CLI executable for your Operating System using one of the following methods: l Download from the Cohesity UI:
a. Click Help ( ) in the top right corner and click Download CLI. b. Find the appropriate CLI for your Operating System and click Download (
). l Download over HTTP:
Download a Cohesity CLI executable from one of the following URLs on the Cohesity cluster:

Windows macOS Linux

On Windows, you can download the Cohesity CLI using the following command in PowerShell or CMD: wget http://<nodeIP>/files/bin/cli/windows-x86_64/iris_cli.exe, where <nodeIP> is the IP address of one of the Nodes in the Cohesity cluster. Example: wget http://192.168.1.100/files/bin/cli/windows-x86_64/iris_cli.exe
On Mac, perform the following steps to download the Cohesity CLI: 1. curl http://<nodeIP>/files/bin/cli/darwin-x86_64/iris_cli -o iris_cli, where <NodeIP> is the IP address of one of the nodes on the Cohesity cluster. Example: curl http://198.51.100.12/files/bin/cli/darwin-x86_64/iris_cli -o iris_cli 2. chmod 755 iris_cli
On Linux, perform the following steps to download the Cohesity CLI: 1. wget http://<nodeIP>/files/bin/cli/linux-x86_64/iris_cli, where <NodeIP> is the IP address of one of the nodes on the Cohesity cluster. Example: wget http://198.51.100.12/files/bin/cli/linux-x86_64/iris_cli 2. chmod 755 iris_cli

2. Start an Operating System terminal or command prompt. 3. Change directories to the location of the CLI executable. 4. Start the CLI with the -help option to view all the start-up options.

Windows macOS Linux

.\iris_cli.exe -help ./iris_cli -help ./iris_cli -help

./iris_cli -server=198.51.100.12

./iris_cli -server=198.51.100.12 Username: admin Password: *****

Array of mode for protocols in the view. Valid values are ReadOnly (or 'r') and ReadWrite (or 'w') and are specified in a comma separated string. Number of items in the string should be equal to items in 'protocol' options or should be empty. Empty denotes that all protocols will be taken as ReadWrite mode.

Cluster Health Check
hc_cli is a Cohesity support-automation tool which checks for commonly seen issues on a Cohesity cluster. The output of the verbose command includes links to a knowledge base article which describes how to resolve the error. After using hc_cli to perform the initial checks, you need to open a case with Cohesity Support to review your cluster's health.
Run hc_cli
To run hc_cli, run the hc_cli run command. To view results, run the hc_cli show --failed command. To view the built-in help, run the hc_cli command without any arguments or append -h at the end of the command:
$ hc_cli usage: hc_cli.py [-h] {debug,ls-tests,show,run,version,generate-doc,status} ... hc_cli.py: error: too few arguments
See the following table for a list of hc_cli commands and description.

l get_magneto_vm_protection_flags.py l get_job_hierarchy.py l For the Cluster Manager service: l top_cpu.py l services_memory_check.py l network_errors.py l For the Indexing service: l yoda_persistent_queue.py
l Lists available lists.
l Prints the most recent results. l Available flags include:
l -h/--help: Prints help output. l -C/--current-node: Prints output from only the current node. l -F/--failed: Prints only failed checks. l -v/--verbose: Prints verbose output.
