Support Toolbox
The support toolbox and its cli interface, hc_cli, are a set of tools built to enable self service of a cluster by identifying issues and providing documentation with the goal of resolution, or if escalation is needed, a more targeted support case. The support toolbox and its constituent components are all designed to assist in identifying known issues, validating cluster health, and to certify a cluster is prepared for an upgrade. As Cohesity keeps this tool in constant development and updates are constantly being built, refer to the following Knowledge Base article to get the latest data on the toolbox, execution, and how to use new features:
l Support Toolbox overview l Updating the support toolbox to the latest version l Running hc_cli health checks l Preupgrade checks (recommended to review prior to an upgrade) l List of checks with links to their KBs l Showing verbose output post check
Using the Secure Shell
The Secure Shell restricts SSH access to the host operating system shell, further tightening access to the Cohesity cluster while still providing users with the ability to execute CLI commands, run diagnostic tools, and access logs. In previous releases, support users could log on to Cohesity nodes using SSH and access the host operating system shell. Access to the host operating system is now restricted through SSH. The Secure Shell can be accessed using only the support user account. To enable the support user account, see Manage Support User.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 35: Tools

Using the Secure Shell

Using the Secure Shell, you can perform the following: l Run iris_cli commands l View the logs (read-only) l Basic connectivity checks
Note: The basic connectivity checks can be performed using the following utilities: l ping and curl will be available from 6.8.1 and later versions. l dig/host, nping, tcptraceroute, and elinks will be available from 6.8.1_u7 and later versions.

Considerations
After upgrading to the 6.8 or later releases, the secure shell might have the following impact on your existing Cohesity deployments:
l If you run custom scripts using ssh on your Cohesity cluster, the scripts might fail. In this case, Cohesity recommends the following: l Verify if there is an alternate method to use Cohesity CLI commands or REST API and update your scripts accordingly. l Verify if a corresponding Cohesity CLI command is available in the supported list of CLI commands; if so, use the supported CLI command. For more information, see Using the Secure Shell. If the CLI command is not available in the supported list of commands, contact Cohesity Support to enable the CLI command.
l The private binary or tools running on the Cohesity nodes might fail. Contact Cohesity Support for options to install private binaries or tools.
l Sudo access is disabled by default. For support channel access, you need to enable sudo access for the support user to the host shell using the following command:
iris_cli user linux-sudo-access enable=true duration-in-hours=xxx
Note: You can enter a duration within the range of 1 to 720 hours.

Secure Shell Prompt
To identify whether you are running the secure shell, once you log into the shell using the support user account, the shell prompt displays the term "restricted," this suggests that

Enable Host Shell Access
You can access the host shell on port 2222 using the support user account. To enable host shell access:
1. Log on to the node's secured shell using the support user. Use the following command: $ ssh support@<node_IP> Where node_IP is the IP address of the node in your Cohesity cluster.
2. Log on to the iris_cli and generate a support token using the following command: $ iris_cli support host-access-token
Note: By default, the support token is only valid for an hour. You can extend the support token validity for up to 12 hours using the following command: iris_cli support host-access-token validity-in-hours=12
3. Obtain the Cohesity cluster information using the following command: $ iris_cli cluster info
4. Share the following details with Cohesity Support to generate an access code: l Host Access Token generated in step 2 l Cluster ID obtained in step 3

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 35: Tools

Cohesity REST API

l Cohesity Software Version obtained in step 3 l The number of hours you require the host shell access 5. After you receive the access code from Cohesity Support, enable host shell access using the following command in iris_cli: $ iris_cli support host-access ssh-enable=true access-code=<access_ code>
Where access_code is the access code you received from Cohesity Support.
Important: Ensure that you enable host shell access before the support access token you generated in Step 2 expires.
6. Access the host shell of the node on port 2222 using the support user. Use the following command: $ ssh support@<node_IP> -p 2222
Cohesity REST API
Cohesity provides a REST API that supports programmatically interfacing with a Cohesity cluster, for example:
l Send a GET /public/protectionJobs REST API request that returns all the Protection Groups found on a Cohesity cluster.
l Send a GET /public/protectionSources/virtualMachines REST API request that returns all the VMs found in a protected Source (vCenter Server) that are registered on a Cohesity cluster.
Complete REST API documentation is available on the Cohesity Developer Portal. Cohesity provides ready-to-use integrations with the automation and orchestration tools of your choice to streamline your operations. Under the hood, all integrations are powered by the Cohesity REST API. For more information, see API Integrations.
View and Run the API Directly on a Cluster
Cohesity also provides a REST API interface directly on the Cohesity cluster which provides documentation and the ability to run operation requests directly against the Cohesity cluster and view the response.
1. Log in to the Cohesity Dashboard from a browser by entering a Node IP Address or VIP IP address of a Cohesity cluster into the browser address bar.
2. Click the icon in the upper right corner and select REST API.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 35: Tools

Cohesity REST API

A new browser tab opens and the Cohesity REST API operations are displayed as nested under group tags such as AccessTokens and Active Directory.
Note: By default, AccessTokens are used. Sessions will be used if session management is enabled.
3. To view the documentation on the response: a. Click Model next to Example Value.

b. Keep clicking to expand the documentation hierarchy.

4. To run an operation: a. Click on the operation to expand it. b. Click Try it out.
Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 35: Tools

Cohesity REST API

c. Enter any required parameters. d. Click Execute. The operation is run against the Cohesity cluster you are logged in to and the results are displayed under the Response body.
Specifying Access Credentials
When you run Cohesity REST API operations from the browser, the Cohesity cluster uses the Login credentials you specified to log in to the Cohesity Dashboard. You can run the Cohesity REST API operations programmatically in two ways:
1. Access tokens 2. Sessions Access Tokens
Note: By default, AccessTokens are used.
From your REST client program, you must make a POST /public/accessTokens request to supply the valid Login credentials before calling other Cohesity REST API operations. This POST request returns an access token and type in the response that is generated by the Cohesity cluster. Subsequent requests to other Cohesity REST API operations must specify the returned access token and type by setting Authorization in the http header in the following format: Authorization: <token_type> <access_token>
The generated token is valid for 24 hours. If a request is made with an expired token, the Token expired error message is returned. Add code to your REST client to check for this error and request another access token before reissuing the request. Sessions
Note: Sessions will be used if session management is enabled.
From your REST client program, you must make a POST /public/v2/users/sessions request to supply the valid Login credentials before calling other Cohesity REST API operations. This POST request returns the session id in the response that is generated by the Cohesity cluster. If session management is enabled, the subsequent requests to other Cohesity REST API operations must specify the returned session id by setting the session-id header in the http header in the following format: session-id: "oxxx0yyyyy81Rzzzz//aaaaaO7qbbbbbAcccccc="

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 35: Tools

Cohesity REST API

The session id is valid till the Inactivity Timeout (1 hour) or Absolute Timeout (24 hours). If a request is made with an expired session id, the expired error message is returned. Add code to your REST client to check for this error and request another session id before reissuing the request.
Generate an API Key
To generate an API key: 1. Navigate to Settings > Access Management and click API Keys.
Note: By default, the API Key is disabled. Contact Cohesity Support to enable the feature.
2. Click Add API Key. 3. Select the user for which the API key should be generated. 4. Enter a Name for the API key. 5. Click Add to generate the API key. 6. Copy the API key to use with the application.

Glossary

Support/Service Assistance
First, contact the Service Provider that you have contracted for service and support. If you work directly with Cohesity and have a product warranty/entitlement, repair pricing, or technical support-related question, see your options below:
l To find solutions to your product issues or for suggestions or best practices, visit the Cohesity Knowledge Base.
l Log in to the Cohesity Support Portal to create a new case. l To monitor your open cases, log in to the portal and click the Cases tab on the home
page. This page should have all the case statuses and updates. You can also view individual case status.
Cohesity Software Running on Partner Hardware
For Cohesity software running on qualified third-party hardware, the following support workflow applies:
1. The customer may contact Cohesity Support first if the issue cannot be determined as a hardware issue.
Note: Cohesity cannot process hardware replacement requests for partner hardware.
2. Cohesity Support triages the issue. If it is a software issue, Cohesity Support continues to work on it.
3. If it is a hardware/firmware issue or is suspected to be a hardware/firmware issue, Cohesity provides information about the issue to the customer and requests that the customer open a support ticket with the appropriate partner.
4. If needed, Cohesity Support can join a three-way call with the partner and the customer.
5. The customer informs Cohesity Support on the progress of the partner's case.
Glossary
A
Agent A lightweight software that is installed on Operating systems like Windows, Linux, AIX, Solaris, HP-UX etc running on a Physical Server or a Virtual machine enabling communication between OS and Cohesity to protect data.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 36: Supplemental Information

Glossary

B
Backup A recoverable snapshot of a registered source, such as a physical or virtual server, database or storage array, created by a Protection Group, used to protect against data loss or corruption.
C
Clone The ability to clone objects from snapshots created by a Protection Group. The cloned objects are copied to a new location, rehydrated and restored to a running state.
Cloud Tier The process of moving rarely used and inactive data to the cloud when HDD usage on the Cohesity cluster exceeds a certain threshold.
CloudArchive The process of copying snapshots created by Protection Groups from the Cohesity cluster to a registered external target.
CloudArchive Direct The process of archiving data directly to an external target without retaining a copy of the data on the cluster. Only the metadata and indexes, required for quick search and recovery, are stored on the cluster.
CloudRetrieve The process of retrieving an archived Protection Group and its run details from an external target to a different cluster. Used for geo-redundancy and disaster recovery.
Cluster An instance of Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-Managed).
D
Data In Data sent from a protected source to Cohesity.
Data Written Data to be written post-deduplication.
Deduplication The process of eliminating redundant copies of data to reduce storage usage on the cluster. The Inline Deduplication process deduplicates data as it is written to the cluster and the Post-process deduplication deduplicates data after it is written to the cluster.
E
External Target Any storage location outside the Cohesity cluster where data is stored. They can be for cloudarchive, cloudarchive direct, or cloud tier.

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 36: Supplemental Information

Glossary

F
Firewall Attachment An active Cohesity rule that includes a profile and multiple ipsets.
Firewall Profile A group of TCP or UDP ports.
Full Archive A full copy of a Protection Group that is archived.
I
Incremental Archive An archive that records just the changed data since the most recent archive.
Inline Deduplication The process of eliminating redundant copies of data as the data is written to a Cohesity view.
Instant Mount A fast and reliable way to access data via the instant volume mounting feature. Some benefits include granular recovery of Microsoft Exchange, SQL and SharePoint data.
L
Logical Data Data residing in a protected source.
N
Node A physical or virtual appliance that runs the Cohesity software. One or more nodes comprise a Cohesity cluster.
P
Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-Managed) The Cohesity software consolidates secondary data and applications, including backups, files, objects, test/dev, and analytics, on a single, software-defined platform.
Protection Policy Business mapping on reusable settings that define how often to protect (RTO), how long to retain, how many copies to create like, archive, replication, tape, and where to store the data.
Protection Group A backup job that runs repeatedly, based on an associated policy, to back up data from a source and store it on the cluster. A Protection Group uses the schedules and

Cohesity User Guide 7.4.1

Chapter 36: Supplemental Information

Glossary

settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, archived or replicated, the operational management of data to be protected etc.
R
Registration The process of registering a source with the Cohesity cluster so the source can be protected.
Remote Adapter Protection Group A backup job that runs scripts or executables on a remote Linux machine, typically for sources that are not supported by Cohesity.
Replication The process of automatically copying Protection Group snapshots from one Cohesity cluster to another Cohesity cluster for data resiliency purposes.
S
Source An object in the IT infrastructure of your company that you want to protect, such as a VM, physical server, Pure Storage volume, MS SQL Server, and NAS files.
Storage Consumed Data written with all copies required for honoring the resiliency setting.
Storage Domain A named storage location on a cluster. A storage domain defines deduplication, compression, erasure coding, fault tolerance and more. Views are created in storage domains. Storage domains were formerly known as View Boxes.
T
Test&Dev The process of cloning a VM, database, or view from a backup or existing file share for test and development purposes.
V
View A named storage location in the storage domain in a Cohesity cluster, which has NFS, SMB, and S3 mount paths.
